sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-muwail.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the IB Diploma and both main IGCSE boards at the levels Muwaileh students sit. Each profile lists subjects, levels and session availability in Gulf Standard Time, so you can match a slot to your own evening before you speak to anyone.

intro.heading: What a tutor near Muwaileh really costs, and what you are buying
paragraphs: Start with the monthly number, because that is the one a household budget feels. A single weekly hour of qualified online subject tuition sits inside Bestimate's mid band of roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month in its Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, and its specialist exam-year band runs from about AED 1,000 to over AED 2,000 a month. Two sessions a week with a named IB Diploma or IGCSE specialist crosses into that upper band quickly. Knowing that before you start means you choose a plan you can hold for two terms rather than one you abandon in week five.

The hourly figures behind those monthly totals are public if you look. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to AED 52, which is the university-student and budget-platform end of the market. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists about AED 270. BartyED quotes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Bestimate's in-home band runs AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors in Sharjah and Dubai are quoted anywhere from AED 200 to AED 500 once travel is priced in. Those are market rates from the providers named, not IB Gram's price list.

The gap between AED 45 and AED 650 is not a quality ladder with clean rungs. It is mostly three things: how much subject-specific examining experience the tutor has, whether a company is carrying office and sales costs, and whether somebody is sitting in a car. A parent in Muwaileh who books an in-home tutor is paying for the second half of a round trip along University City Road at the exact hour that road is at its worst. That premium is real and it is not teaching.

This is why IB Gram delivers tuition to Muwaileh as one-to-one online lessons over live video rather than as home visits. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service offered only in India. The practical consequence for your child is the one that matters: the Chemistry HL tutor who has marked that paper style for years is available to a Muwaileh family at 7pm on a Tuesday, instead of whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of Muwaileh Commercial.

There is a second cost nobody itemises, which is wasted hours. A tutor who has not read the right syllabus spends the first three sessions finding out what the student is studying. On Cambridge IGCSE Maths that means knowing whether the entry is Core, with Papers 1 and 3 and a grade ceiling of C, or Extended, with Papers 2 and 4 and access to A*. On the IB side it means knowing whether the student sits Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, because the Paper 3 at Higher Level and the whole feel of the Exploration differ. Three misdirected sessions at market rate is AED 450 to AED 900 of nothing, and the page below shows how to avoid spending it.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-muwail.programmesIntro: Muwaileh sits beside University City and Al Zahia, and the households in it send children into British, Indian, American schools and schools licensed to run the IB, often on the same street. These are the programmes tutoring around Muwaileh is actually asked for, with the cost consequence of each stated plainly.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The diploma is awarded from 24 points to a maximum of 45, with up to three bonus points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Most of the tutoring demand concentrates in Mathematics, the three sciences and Economics, and most of it arrives in DP2 when two Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay land in the same eight weeks.
programmes.countryNote: For a Muwaileh household the DP is the most expensive programme to support badly. Market specialist rates of AED 200 to AED 450 an hour mean a two-subject rescue in DP2 costs more than two years of steady single-subject support started in DP1. The cheapest DP plan is almost always the early one: one hour a week in the weaker Higher Level subject from the first term, with the Internal Assessment timeline mapped against the school's own internal deadlines rather than the May session.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge reports grades A* to G and offers Core and Extended tiers in subjects such as Maths 0580 and Physics 0625. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1 and runs untiered papers in most subjects, with codes like 4MA1 for Maths and 4PH1 for Physics. The board and the tier decide the paper set, the grade ceiling and therefore the sensible number of tutoring hours.
programmes.countryNote: Families around Muwaileh often discover the board only when the first mock paper comes home. It is worth checking, because an Edexcel 4MA1 past paper is poor practice for a Cambridge 0580 Extended candidate and the two mark schemes reward different working. Market IGCSE rates of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour online make that mismatch expensive: a term of practice on the wrong paper style is the single most common waste in the local market.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment in eight subject groups, with marks awarded against criteria A to D rather than as percentages. The Personal Project runs in MYP 5. Students move from MYP into either the Diploma or an IGCSE pathway, and the step into formal external papers is where most families first ask for help.
programmes.countryNote: MYP support is the cheapest intervention available to a Sharjah family and the least bought. One hour a fortnight in MYP 4 and 5, aimed at the criteria wording and at writing to a command term, costs a fraction of DP1 remediation at AED 200 an hour and removes the most common reason students struggle in the first Diploma term: never having written to a mark scheme.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-muwail.subjectsIntro: Subject choice drives cost more than level does, because the thin-supply subjects carry the premium. These are the IB Diploma subjects Muwaileh families request most, with what each one assesses and where marks leak.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Standard Level, Papers 1 and 2 carry 40% each and the Exploration 20%. At Higher Level the split is 30%, 30%, 20% for Paper 3 and 20% for the Exploration. Marks go on unjustified steps in proof and on calculator-paper arithmetic in Paper 2, which is where a weekly hour pays for itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same weighting structure as Analysis and Approaches, different content: statistics, modelling and technology use dominate. Students lose marks by writing conclusions a dataset does not support and by skipping the interpretation sentence after a correct calculation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is 36% of the grade across its multiple-choice and data sections, Paper 2 is 44% and the Internal Assessment 20%. The common leak is the extended-response question that asks for an explanation and receives a formula. Tutoring targets command terms and the data-analysis skills the Internal Assessment is graded on.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same 36 / 44 / 20 structure as Physics. Organic mechanisms and the quantitative chemistry at the start of the course are the two places Sharjah students most often need rebuilding, usually because the MYP or IGCSE foundation was stronger on recall than on calculation.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Weighted 36% Paper 1, 44% Paper 2, 20% Internal Assessment. Long-answer marks are lost on command terms: distinguish, outline and explain each want a different shape of answer, and a well-memorised paragraph that answers the wrong verb scores nothing.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: At Standard Level Paper 1 is 30%, Paper 2 40% and the Internal Assessment 30%. Higher Level adds Paper 3 and reweights to 20 / 30 / 30 / 20. The Internal Assessment is three commentaries on published news articles, and the marks go on diagram accuracy and on applying one key concept properly, not on summarising the article.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Paper 1 is 35%, Paper 2 40% and the Internal Assessment 25%. Students lose marks by describing a tool instead of using it on the case: a SWOT with no conclusion earns far less than a shorter answer that reaches a judgement supported by the data provided.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen text, Paper 2 a comparative essay, plus the Individual Oral; Higher Level adds the HL Essay. Marks are lost on Paper 1 by paraphrasing the text instead of analysing how it builds meaning for a specific audience.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Written papers plus a solution-development Internal Assessment. The frequent gap is between coding fluency and the documented design cycle the Internal Assessment is marked against, which is a process skill rather than a programming one.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and Internal Assessment supervision
subjects.description: Coaching only: question framing, research planning, structure, referencing and feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor may read, question and comment. A tutor may not write, complete or edit the work to a finish, and IB Gram does not do so, because that is malpractice under IB academic-honesty rules.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-muwail.igcseSubjectsIntro: At IGCSE the syllabus code decides everything about the work, so each entry below names it. Rates in the Sharjah market for IGCSE tuition run below IB Diploma rates, which is why starting in Year 10 rather than Year 11 is the cheapest decision available.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge Core sits Papers 1 and 3 with a C ceiling; Extended sits Papers 2 and 4 and reaches A*. Edexcel 4MA1 is untiered across two papers. Checking which of those three a student is entered for is the first thing any honest tutor does.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Edexcel 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge candidates sit a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper at their tier, and either Paper 5 practical or Paper 6 alternative to practical. Electricity and the moments-and-equilibrium topics generate most of the requests for help in Sharjah.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Edexcel 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Mole calculations and the qualitative-analysis tables are the two reliable mark earners and the two most reliably skipped in revision. Paper 6 candidates need deliberate practice at reading other people's experimental methods.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Long-answer marks hinge on command terms and on using the correct unit and scale in graph work. Transport in plants and human physiology are where recall-based revision tends to collapse under a six-mark question.

igcseSubjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 or 0510, Edexcel 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: 0500 First Language and 0510 English as a Second Language are different qualifications with different mark schemes, and being entered for the wrong one is more common than parents expect. Directed-writing tasks reward audience and form before they reward vocabulary.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 and 0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Both reward diagram accuracy and a conclusion that answers the question asked. Data-response questions are where students who have revised definitions still lose half the available marks.

regions.name: Al Zahia

regions.name: Aljada
regions.note: Arada's mixed-use district on the Muwaileh side of Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, still adding phases. New arrivals here often change school mid-year, which is when board and tier mismatches surface.

sections.heading: The monthly arithmetic before the hourly rate
paragraphs: An IB or IGCSE tutor around Muwaileh costs between roughly AED 240 and AED 2,000 a month depending on how many hours you buy and from which tier of the market. That range comes from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for weekly one-hour sessions: around AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to over AED 2,000 for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in the UAE market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Reading it monthly changes the decision. Most families who ask about an hourly rate are really asking whether they can run tuition for two terms, and the honest answer depends on the monthly figure, not the hour. One hour a week for a full academic year at a mid-market rate costs less than a panic block of three hours a week for the last two months, and produces a different result, because content gaps close slowly and exam technique closes fast.

sections.heading: Hourly bands and who publishes them
paragraphs: The UAE tutoring market publishes less about price than almost any other consumer category, which is why three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches show no figure at all and the two that do quote US dollars. A Muwaileh parent deserves AED. The bands below are each attributed to the provider or survey that published them, read in October 2026, so you can check them rather than take them on trust.

Two patterns are worth naming. First, the in-home band sits consistently above the online band for the same level of tutor, and the gap is travel. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 while independent home tutors are quoted at AED 200 to AED 500. Second, the premium end of the market is not a different subject expertise so much as a different scarcity: BartyED's AED 650 buys a named individual with a waiting list.

What this means for a tutoring decision near Muwaileh is simple. If a budget stretches to one subject at the qualified-tutor band, buy that rather than two subjects at the budget band. A student with a specific Paper 4 problem in Cambridge 0580 Extended needs somebody who knows that mark scheme; two cheaper hours a week with somebody who does not will cost more over a term and change less. The same logic applies to the premium end: paying AED 650 an hour for a named tutor makes sense only if the scarce thing is that individual's experience of the exact paper, and for most Sharjah students it is not. The mid band is where the syllabus knowledge starts and the overhead has not yet taken over, which is why most sensible plans in this part of the emirate sit inside it.

sections.heading: Where tutoring money is wasted around Muwaileh
paragraphs: Waste in a tutoring budget is rarely the hourly rate. It is hours that produce nothing, and there are five reliable sources of those. The first is a board or tier mismatch: practising Edexcel 4MA1 papers for a Cambridge 0580 Extended entry, or working at Extended difficulty with a Core candidate who cannot be awarded above a C. Two or three sessions of this is AED 300 to AED 900 gone.

The second is travel paid as teaching. A tutor who drives from central Sharjah to Muwaileh at 5pm has priced that journey into the hour. The third is the diagnostic period: a tutor who starts without seeing the student's last mock paper and school report spends the first two sessions discovering what a ten-minute document review would have shown. The fourth is paying for content delivery that the school already provides well, when the real gap is timed-paper technique. The fifth, and the most expensive, is starting in the last month before a series.

Each of these has a cheap fix, and the table sets them against what they cost. None of the fixes requires buying more hours, which is the point. The useful question is not how much a tutor near Muwaileh charges but how many of the hours you buy will be spent on the thing your child is actually losing marks for. A sixth source of waste deserves a mention because it is invisible on an invoice: paying for two subjects when the student only has the attention for one. Two hours a week on top of a Sharjah school day with Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies already in the timetable is a real load, and a tired student learns slowly at any hourly rate.

sections.heading: Online or in-home, priced honestly for this part of Sharjah
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real market in Sharjah and plenty of families use it. The fair comparison is not quality against quality, because a good tutor is good in either format. It is cost, tutor pool and reliability over a term, and in eastern Sharjah those three favour online clearly enough that IB Gram built its UAE service that way.

Cost first. The same tutor costs more in your living room because the travel is in the rate. Pool second, and this is the bigger factor: an in-home arrangement limits you to tutors willing to drive to Muwaileh at a specific hour, which for a subject like Physics at Higher Level or Economics Higher Level Paper 3 may be a very short list. Online removes the radius, so the constraint becomes the tutor's calendar rather than the map.

Reliability third. A 5pm in-home session that depends on University City Road or the Al Ittihad Road corridor will be cancelled or shortened several times a term, and those are hours paid for and not taught. A video session starts when it is meant to. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so this comparison is about the market rather than a menu, and it is published here because a parent weighing the two deserves the arithmetic. One honest point for the in-home format: a younger child who will not sit still at a screen may genuinely do better with somebody in the room, and for a Muwaileh family with a child in the primary years that is a fair reason to choose it. From Year 10 upwards, when the work is past papers, mark schemes and annotated scripts, the screen stops being a compromise and starts being the better tool.

sections.heading: What the exam calendar does to your spending plan
paragraphs: Tutoring spend should follow the calendar, not the panic. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a Muwaileh candidate sits June, with November as the resit or staged route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge also places every centre in one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

The dates that matter to a budget are the ones months before the papers. Entry deadlines sit with the school's exams officer well ahead of the series, internal Internal Assessment and Extended Essay deadlines sit earlier still, and results arrive long after. The Pearson November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results for the November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Those are published, checkable dates for past and current series, which is the point of citing them.

Spread across that calendar, a year of tuition costs less and does more than a block at the end. The plan below works backwards from a series rather than forwards from today. Always confirm the live timetable with the school's exams officer or on the board's own site, because provisional timetables are revised, and no IB session date is published here: ibo.org is the only source to trust for those, and the May session is the one UAE schools sit.

sections.heading: SPEA, the Ministry and what a Sharjah parent is actually paying into
paragraphs: Private schooling in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate. Its powers go beyond inspection: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a different arrangement from Dubai, where the Knowledge and Human Development Authority oversees quality, and from Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, where the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools. In Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools, and Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge.

This matters to a tutoring budget in two practical ways. A fee increase at a Sharjah school is not a unilateral decision by the school, and the curriculum a school may offer is approved rather than assumed, which is why it is worth checking the current programme list rather than relying on what a school offered three years ago. Federal rules also require private schools to teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, so a child on an IB or IGCSE pathway in Muwaileh is carrying those subjects too, and they are a frequent and under-bought tutoring need.

Tutors themselves are regulated separately. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here. IB Gram holds no SPEA, Ministry or examination-board approval and claims none.

sections.heading: Coursework support: what you may pay for and what nobody may sell you
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake available in this market is not overpaying for a tutor. It is buying work the student must produce themselves. One page ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. Under IB academic-honesty rules that is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller: a withheld grade or a withdrawn diploma after two years of work.

What legitimate support looks like is narrow and genuinely useful. A tutor can help a student choose a researchable question, explain what the criteria letters actually reward, read a draft and ask the questions a supervisor would ask, show how to reference properly, and give written feedback the student then acts on alone. A tutor can teach the statistics a Mathematics Exploration needs or the data-handling a science Internal Assessment is graded on. A tutor cannot write a sentence of it, cannot edit it to completion, and cannot supply a model answer to be adapted.

This boundary also saves money. Coursework coaching at fortnightly intervals costs roughly half a weekly plan, and it is the highest-value spend in the Diploma because the Internal Assessment is 20% to 30% of a subject grade depending on the subject, and the Extended Essay feeds the three bonus points through the matrix. Word and page limits are fixed, published and worth knowing before a first draft rather than after: the Extended Essay runs to a 4,000-word maximum, the Theory of Knowledge essay to 1,600 words, and a Mathematics Exploration is expected in the 12 to 20 page range.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the cost of finding out late
paragraphs: Families in Sharjah planning on a UAE university place need the Ministry of Education's equivalency of the school certificate, and the subject count is where parents are most often misinformed. For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page ranking for UAE tutoring queries tells parents six IGCSE subjects are required; the sourced rule is five.

On the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold is published here: that figure must be read on moe.gov.ae or confirmed with the attestation authority, and publishing an unsourced number would be worse than publishing nothing.

The cost connection is direct. A student who discovers in Year 11 that they are one accredited subject short has to find an extra entry, often as a private candidate in a November series, with the tutoring that implies. A student who checks the requirement in Year 9 chooses their options around it and spends nothing extra. Equivalency is a Ministry process; IB Gram does not perform it, guarantee it, or claim any role in it, and tutoring is not required for it.

faqs.question: What does an IB or IGCSE tutor near Muwaileh actually cost per month?
faqs.answer: Budget on the month, not the hour. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to over AED 2,000 for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in the UAE include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are market figures from the sources named, read in October 2026. IB Gram's own arrangement begins with a free trial lesson and a plan, and the cost is discussed once a tutor has seen the student's work.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book an online tutor or a home tutor in this part of Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Online is cheaper for the same calibre of tutor, because travel sits inside every in-home rate. Published market bands put online qualified tutoring at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, while in-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's figures and AED 200 to AED 500 for independent home tutors. The second difference is reliability: an evening visit across eastern Sharjah is exposed to University City Road traffic, and lost minutes are paid minutes. IB Gram delivers UAE tuition online only; in-home visits are offered in India, not here.

faqs.question: Why does the hourly rate for Sharjah tutoring range from AED 45 to AED 650?
faqs.answer: Three things move the number. Examining depth in the specific subject and paper, the overhead the provider carries, and travel. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists about AED 270, Bestimate puts specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and BartyED quotes AED 650 for a named premium tutor. The top of that range is scarcity more than extra syllabus knowledge, which is why one subject at mid-band usually beats two at the bottom.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Muwaileh family start with?
faqs.answer: One hour a week in the single weakest subject, for a full term, is the plan that works most often and costs least. It gives a tutor time to repair content rather than only drill papers, and it survives a busy school calendar. Two subjects at once is justified when both are Higher Level and both are below the student's target by two grades. Three or more sessions a week should be a bounded block of six to eight weeks before a series, with a stop date agreed in advance, rather than an open-ended arrangement that quietly becomes the family's largest monthly bill.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both an IB subject and an IGCSE subject for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because it reduces coordination for you. A tutor who teaches Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level can usually also handle Cambridge 0580 Extended for a younger sibling, and a Physics specialist can cover 0625 and Diploma Physics. The limit is paper-specific experience. Economics Higher Level Paper 3 and the IGCSE 0455 data-response questions reward different skills, so a tutor strong in one may not be strong in the other. Ask which specific papers and codes they have taught, and judge the answer rather than the claim.

faqs.question: My child has mocks in six weeks. Is paying for tutoring now still worth it?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the money goes to technique rather than content. Six weeks is enough to change how a student reads a question, allocate time across a paper, and stop losing marks on command terms, and those are often three to six grade-boundary marks per paper. Six weeks is not enough to rebuild two years of missing foundations, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling. The sensible shape is two sessions a week built entirely around timed questions with written feedback against the mark scheme, then a taper in the final fortnight so the student is resting rather than cramming.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE board does my child sit, and why does it change the price of help?
faqs.answer: It changes what the hours are spent on. Cambridge IGCSE reports A* to G and tiers several subjects: Maths 0580 Core sits Papers 1 and 3 with a grade ceiling of C, Extended sits Papers 2 and 4 and reaches A*. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1 and is untiered in most subjects, with codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Practising the wrong board's papers is the most common waste in this market, worth AED 300 to AED 900 over two or three sessions. The school's exams officer will confirm board, code and tier in writing.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working with families in Sharjah need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is covered by a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Asking a prospective tutor about their permit is reasonable and cheap.

faqs.question: Where does the money go in an in-home tutoring rate around University City Road?
faqs.answer: Into the journey. An in-home rate has to cover the tutor's travel in both directions at the hour you want them, which in eastern Sharjah is the hour the road is busiest. Bestimate's in-home band of AED 180 to AED 350 against an online qualified band of AED 150 to AED 300 is roughly the size of that premium, and independent home tutors quoted at up to AED 500 are pricing a narrow radius. The premium buys a physical presence, not better teaching, and it also buys exposure to cancellations. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: How much does Internal Assessment or Extended Essay supervision cost, and what can a tutor legally do?
faqs.answer: Fortnightly coursework coaching costs roughly half a weekly plan, so in market terms around AED 300 to AED 600 a month. What it buys is narrow and valuable: help choosing a researchable question, an explanation of what the criteria reward, questions on the student's own draft, referencing practice and written feedback. What nobody may sell you is the work itself. Writing, completing or editing an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay to a finish is malpractice under IB rules and the penalty falls on the student. IB Gram does not do it.

faqs.question: Are online science lessons any use when my child has a practical paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, because of how the practical component is assessed. Cambridge candidates sit either Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and Paper 6 is a written paper about experimental method, data and error. That is exactly what a video session with screen-shared data sets and past-paper method questions can teach. Hands-on technique belongs in the school laboratory, and good tutoring does not pretend otherwise. For a Paper 6 candidate in Sharjah, deliberate practice at reading somebody else's method and spotting the weakness is usually worth more than extra bench time.

faqs.question: Does the exam calendar change when we should start spending?
faqs.answer: It should. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so a Sharjah candidate plans around June with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Entry deadlines, internal coursework deadlines and mock windows all sit months before the papers, and spreading one hour a week across that span costs less than a block at the end. Confirm the live timetable with the school's exams officer, and note that Cambridge allocates centres to six zones with different timetables.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor before paying for a first session near Muwaileh?
faqs.answer: Five questions, in this order. Which board, code and tier have you taught for this subject? What are the paper weightings at this level? Where do students most often lose marks in it? What will the first four sessions cover? And do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit? A tutor who answers the first three precisely is worth the mid-market rate. A tutor who answers generally will spend your first sessions finding out what your child is studying, and at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour that is an expensive way to share information you already have.

faqs.question: Can sessions fit around a Sharjah school day and family routine?
faqs.answer: That is the main reason online works here. Sessions are booked in Gulf Standard Time and the common slots are 5.30pm, 7pm and 8pm on weekdays, plus weekend mornings, because a 4pm start rarely survives a school run through Muwaileh. Sharjah's government sector moved to a Friday-to-Sunday weekend, so households with a parent in a Sharjah government role often use Friday mornings, while families commuting from Dubai usually need the later evening slots. During Ramadan sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar time, and a slot can move during mock weeks without changing the tutor.

faqs.question: What are we told if nobody is available for a thin-supply Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You are told, rather than matched to somebody approximately suitable. The thin-supply requests are usually Higher Level sciences, Economics Higher Level Paper 3, Computer Science and occasionally a second language at Diploma level. Where no suitable tutor has availability in the slot you need, the options are an alternative time, a place on the list when a slot opens, or a different tutor whose relevant experience is explained to you honestly so you can judge it. Taking a booking that cannot be served properly wastes your money and the student's term, which is the opposite of the point.

intro.heading: The useful question is which course, not which neighbourhood
paragraphs: Parents in Sharjah Garden City type 'near me' because that is how search works, not because distance is what they care about. What they care about is whether the person teaching their child understands the course in front of them. Those are different questions, and only one of them has a good answer on this corridor.

Consider how specific the courses actually are. 'IB maths' is two different subjects: Analysis and Approaches, which is proof and calculus heavy, and Applications and Interpretation, which is modelling and statistics heavy. Each runs at higher and standard level. 'IGCSE maths' is at least two more: Cambridge 0580, tiered Core and Extended across its own paper pattern, and Pearson 4MA1, with two equally weighted papers and a different question style. That is six distinct teaching jobs behind one word, and a tutor is good at some of them and not others.

The same is true in the sciences, and worse. A Cambridge science candidate sits a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and an alternative-to-practical paper, each with its own failure modes. An IB science student sits terminal papers and submits an internal assessment marked against criteria by letter. A tutor who has spent five years on IB chemistry internal assessments may never have taught a student to answer an alternative-to-practical question, and vice versa. Neither is a weakness; both are specialisations.

Sort a list of tutors by distance from Sharjah Garden City and you get people whose specialisation is unknown and whose availability is set by traffic on the southern corridor. Sort by course and level and you get somebody who can tell you, in the first conversation, which three topics are costing your child marks. We think the second sort is the one worth doing, which is why we match on syllabus and teach over live video rather than sending anybody to an address.

This page is therefore unusually technical for a tutoring page. It sets out the maths routes side by side, the places where science mark schemes punish loose language, what each command term demands, how to use past papers without burning them, what the English courses actually reward, and where a tutor's work stops and the student's own work begins.

A warning about how specialisation is advertised. Listings in this market say 'all subjects, all levels' because that maximises enquiries, and the phrase tells you nothing about whether the person has taught your child's course. The useful credential is not a degree title or a photograph of a certificate; it is the ability to describe the paper structure and the common mark losses in the specific course, unprompted, in under a minute.

If you only take one habit from it, take this one: when you contact any tutor, lead with the course and the level or code. 'Year 11 science' gets you a generalist. '0625 Extended, Paper 6 is the problem, mocks in three weeks' gets you somebody who can start work in session one.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at higher or standard level, plus Theory of Knowledge, an extended essay and creativity, activity, service. Each subject combines terminal examinations with an internal assessment marked against published criteria and moderated by the IB. Teaching has to serve both halves, and they reward different work: criteria-driven precision in the assessment, exam technique in the papers.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah has a small number of schools authorised for the Diploma Programme, so students from the southern corridor often travel a long way to school. That is the practical reason a subject specialist is easier to reach by video than by car, and why most of our Diploma work in this emirate is delivered online.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria by letter with task-specific descriptors issued per assignment, and no external papers in most subjects. Good teaching here is descriptor-literate: it practises the thing the criterion rewards, which is usually precision with command terms, investigation structure and conclusions justified from the evidence collected.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah these years also carry mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies lessons alongside the international curriculum, so the week is full. Short sessions aimed at one criterion work; long general homework supervision competes with the school's own workload and loses.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written examinations with published mark schemes, tiered at Cambridge into Core and Extended. Because the grade is made in the examination room, the most valuable tutoring activity is timed paper work marked against the official mark scheme, with errors logged by question type rather than by topic.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the February/March Cambridge series is offered in India only. Entries go through the school's centre, and each centre belongs to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, so only the exams officer's copy should be trusted.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-sharja.subjectsIntro: IB subjects first, described by what the course actually assesses and where Sharjah students most often lose marks. The level - higher or standard - changes the answer, so it is part of the match.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic technique, proof and calculus carry the papers. Students arriving from a secure Extended IGCSE background still lose marks because method must be written and justified rather than implied. At higher level the proof content and the depth of calculus are the usual pressure points.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use dominate. It is not the easy route: higher level statistics is demanding, and some engineering degree routes expect Analysis and Approaches instead, so the choice has consequences beyond the next two years.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are where marks concentrate. Extended responses are marked for precision: naming an observation rather than asserting a conclusion, and giving conditions rather than gesturing at them. The internal assessment needs controlled variables more than an ambitious topic.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields, with sign conventions and unstated assumptions causing most avoidable losses in multi-step problems. Uncertainty treatment is rewarded in the investigation and is almost always underdone, which makes it an efficient thing to coach early.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, so the grade turns on command terms and on data-based questions. Students who revise by rereading plateau quickly; students who answer past data questions under timing and check against the mark scheme move. Statistical treatment in the investigation is a recurring weakness.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams and evaluation earn the marks. A labelled diagram with correctly drawn shifts is quick to teach and routinely sloppy. Higher level adds quantitative work that surprises students who chose the subject expecting essays, and the commentaries need one syllabus section applied tightly to one article.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis and the individual oral decide most of the grade. Orals fail when the global issue is too broad to anchor in two extracts. The higher level essay needs a text chosen early enough to reread, which is a scheduling decision disguised as a literary one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The toolkit must be applied to the case rather than described. Students lose marks writing everything they know about a concept instead of using it to reach a judgement about the organisation in front of them.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-sharja.igcseSubjectsIntro: The Cambridge and Pearson side, with the structural detail that decides which tutor is right. Send the code; it is the single most useful thing in an enquiry.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge tiers the papers and Pearson sets two equally weighted ones, so the pacing strategy differs. Confirm the current structure and weighting in the syllabus document your school issues rather than from a tutoring page, then practise to that shape under timing.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Edexcel
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge candidates face a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and an alternative-to-practical paper. The last of those is a separate skill: describing method, identifying variables, spotting a source of error. It can be taught in three or four sessions and is frequently ignored until the week before.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Mole ratios taken from the wrong species, electrolysis products guessed rather than reasoned, and organic conditions written approximately. The mark scheme wants state symbols and precise observations, so sloppy writing costs marks a student has genuinely earned.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Marks sit in command words and in diagram work rather than in recall. Transport in plants, genetic crosses and experimental design are the questions where a tutor's hour converts directly into marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
igcseSubjects.description: The bridge to A Level mathematics or higher level IB maths. Calculus notation, radian measure and the factor theorem expose the gap between comfortable and merely competent algebra within the first month.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (0500)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and the reading passages carry the grade. The commonest loss is summarising when the question asks for analysis of effect, closely followed by an unvaried register across both papers. Timed writing annotated against the mark scheme moves this subject quickly.

sections.heading: Four maths courses behind one search term
paragraphs: A family in Sharjah Garden City looking for maths help is looking for one of at least four different things, and the differences are large enough that a tutor strong in one can be actively unhelpful in another. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency, proof and calculus, with method written out and justified. Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling, statistics and intelligent use of technology. Cambridge 0580 rewards accuracy and speed across a tiered paper structure. Pearson 4MA1 rewards the same arithmetic competence with a different question style and two equally weighted papers.

The choice between the two IB routes has consequences beyond the classroom. Some engineering and mathematics degree routes expect Analysis and Approaches, and a student who takes Applications and Interpretation because it sounds gentler can find a prerequisite missing two years later. The reverse error is equally common: a student who takes Analysis and Approaches at higher level on ambition alone and spends DP2 underwater. The sensible method is evidence - attempt questions from both courses, with somebody who knows both, and decide from the scripts.

On the British side, the tier decision has the same structure. Core caps the grade; Extended carries the full range but demands content a Core candidate never meets. The test is whether the student can access the Extended-only topics and finish the harder paper in the time available, and two sessions of past-paper questions answer it better than a term of impressions. Changes have to go through the school before its internal entry deadline.

What all four courses share is that the paper structure should shape practice from early on. Confirm the current structure and weighting from the syllabus document your school issues - it is the authoritative version and it does change between syllabus cycles - then practise to that shape under timing rather than doing untimed exercises from a textbook.

sections.heading: Where science mark schemes punish loose language
paragraphs: Science marks are lost in two places: things the student does not know, and things the student knows but writes imprecisely. The second category is larger than most families expect, and it is the faster of the two to fix, which makes it the obvious place for a tutor to start.

Chemistry is the clearest example. A mark scheme asking for an observation wants 'a white precipitate forms', not 'it goes cloudy', and certainly not the conclusion 'so it is a sulfate'. Equations want state symbols. Organic questions want conditions - temperature, catalyst, concentration - rather than a reaction arrow and optimism. None of that is difficult chemistry; all of it is a writing habit, and habits respond quickly to marking against the real mark scheme.

In physics the equivalent is the unstated assumption. A multi-step problem answered with a number and no working earns little when the method carries the marks. A graph question answered by reading a value rather than calculating a gradient over a large interval loses the technique mark. On the alternative-to-practical paper, candidates who have never narrated a method aloud produce vague answers about 'measuring carefully' where the scheme wants a named instrument, a repeat and a control.

Biology concentrates its losses in command terms and in data questions. 'Describe' asks for what happens; 'explain' asks why; 'suggest' invites a reasoned possibility from unfamiliar context. A candidate who answers all three the same way caps their long-answer marks regardless of how well they know the content. In IB sciences the same discipline applies to extended responses, with the added expectation that uncertainty and limitation are addressed honestly in the internal assessment.

sections.heading: What each command term actually demands
paragraphs: Both systems publish command terms, and both expect students to treat them as instructions. In practice most candidates treat them as a general invitation to write about the topic. This is the single most common avoidable mark loss we see in scripts from Sharjah schools, across subjects and across boards.

The fix is mechanical and quick. Take a past paper, cover the content, and sort the questions by command term. Ask the student what each term requires before attempting any of them. Most students can state the difference between describe and explain when asked directly and then fail to apply it under time pressure, which tells you the problem is habit rather than understanding.

There is a second layer in the IB. Internal assessment criteria use their own language - evaluation, limitation, justification - and each criterion's descriptors spell out what a higher level of achievement looks like. Students who read those descriptors in the first week of the project write differently from students who read them after the first draft comes back. Reading them together is one of the highest-value hours a tutor can spend.
The table below is the version worth keeping beside a student while they work. It is deliberately practical rather than exhaustive: a handful of terms that cover most of the damage.

One more habit is worth building alongside it. Before writing anything, a student should underline the command term and the number of marks, then decide how many distinct points the answer needs. A four-mark explain question wants four linked statements, not one statement written four ways, and that single piece of arithmetic recovers marks across every paper in both systems.

sections.heading: Using past papers without wasting them
paragraphs: Past papers are the most valuable resource a candidate has and the most frequently squandered. There are only so many of them, and a paper done untimed, unmarked and half-completed teaches almost nothing while using one up. The protocol matters more than the quantity.

Our method is consistent across both systems. Early in a course, use individual questions by topic, untimed, to check whether a topic is secure. Mid-course, use sections under timing. In the final block, use whole papers under full exam conditions, marked against the published mark scheme between sessions, with the review session spent only on the question types the error log identifies. Never mark a paper leniently to protect a student's feelings - the paper is the only honest feedback mechanism available before the real one.

Two practical constraints. Papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents belong to the boards, so we reference the official sources and point families to them rather than distributing copies. Your child's school is the proper route to current material, and a tutoring service offering a drive full of 'exclusive' board documents is distributing somebody else's copyright. For unreleased material, the exposure is worse than copyright: it is a malpractice question attached to your child.

The other constraint is honesty about marking. A tutor who marks generously produces a student who is confident and unprepared. We would rather deliver an uncomfortable mark in March than a surprise in June, and the error log exists so that the discomfort has somewhere useful to go.

sections.heading: English in both systems: what actually earns the grade
paragraphs: English is the subject where families most often assume a general tutor will do, and the subject where course-specific knowledge is most quickly visible. The IB's English A: Language and Literature assesses unseen textual analysis and an individual oral built around a global issue anchored in two extracts. Cambridge First Language English 0500 assesses directed writing and reading analysis across its papers. English as a Second Language 0510 assesses a formulaic set of exercises with specific word limits and register expectations.

Each of those rewards something different. The IB oral fails when the global issue is too broad - a student who chooses 'inequality' will produce generalities, where 'the treatment of domestic workers in these two extracts' produces analysis. Cambridge directed writing fails when the student summarises the passage instead of analysing the effect of its language, or writes both papers in the same register. The second-language exercises fail on word limits and on missing the audience, both of which are entirely coachable.

What all three share is that improvement comes from writing under timing and then annotating against the mark scheme or criteria, rather than from reading more. Students are often asked to read more and rarely asked to write the same task three times and compare the versions. The second activity is where marks move, and it is uncomfortable enough that most students avoid it without a tutor sitting there.

For students whose home language is not English - common across Sharjah schools - there is a further point. Fluency in conversation does not predict performance on an analysis paper, and a student can be entirely comfortable speaking while losing marks for register, structure and precision in writing. Those are specific, teachable things, not a general language problem to be worried about.
bullets: A global issue must be narrow enough to anchor in two extracts
Directed writing is assessed on effect, not on summary
Register and audience are marks in every one of these courses

sections.heading: Why the specialist is rarely the nearest person
paragraphs: Everything above describes a fairly narrow kind of expertise: knowing a particular course, its paper structure, its command terms and its mark scheme. The population of people with that expertise for any given course is small, and it is distributed by where those people chose to live rather than by where demand appears.

Sharjah Garden City is on the emirate's southern corridor, away from the older tutoring districts. The practical consequence is that a distance-sorted list contains generalists and, in the IB subjects especially, very few people who have taught the specific course at the specific level. Insisting on proximity in that situation means accepting a generalist, which is a real trade-off rather than a neutral one.

The money makes the same argument. Across published UAE rate cards, a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, while an in-home visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed, and named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 and above. For an address on this corridor the in-home premium sits high in that range, and what it buys is a drive. It does not buy knowledge of a command term.

So the arrangement we offer is a specialist matched to the course, teaching one to one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses - home visits are a service we run only in India - and the free trial lesson is how a family tests whether the format works for their child before committing to anything.

sections.heading: What course-specific teaching costs, and what it replaces
paragraphs: Specialist teaching is not the most expensive thing in this market, which surprises families who assume subject depth carries a premium. The premium in the UAE tutoring market attaches to travel and to branding, not to syllabus knowledge, and that is worth knowing before a quote lands.

Across published UAE rate cards, budget online tutoring starts around AED 45 an hour and is generally delivered by university students. A qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300. An in-home visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed. Named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 and above, and examiner status is rarely evidenced and never transfers to your child's paper. Bestimate's Dubai cost estimates, read in October 2026, put a single weekly session at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at budget level and AED 600 to 1,200 with a qualified tutor.

What course-specific teaching replaces is the diagnosis period. A generalist spends three or four sessions working out what the course requires and where this student is failing; a specialist does that from one marked script before the first lesson. At market rates those saved sessions are worth several hundred dirhams, which usually exceeds any difference in the hourly rate. That is the honest economic argument for specialism, and it is unrelated to anybody's enthusiasm.

These are market figures published so that any quote - ours included - can be judged against something checkable. There is no IB Gram price list on this page: ask us directly, and start with the free trial lesson, which costs nothing and produces a marked script you keep either way.

sections.heading: Where a tutor's work stops
paragraphs: A page this focused on syllabus detail should be equally precise about limits. There are things a subject specialist can do, things they cannot, and things they must not, and families are entitled to know which is which before they book anybody.

A tutor can teach content, diagnose from a script, drill command terms, mark to a mark scheme, plan an investigation's method and uncertainty treatment, read a draft and explain which criterion it fails, and rehearse an oral to time. A tutor cannot guarantee a grade - nobody can, and anybody who offers a number is selling confidence. A tutor cannot replace two years of teaching in a short block, and should say which topics are being left alone when time is short.

What a tutor must not do is produce assessed work. No writing, no redrafting, no editing to completion of an internal assessment, extended essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or coursework. IB Gram does not sell completed assessments of any kind. This market contains operations that do, at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the malpractice consequence lands on the student's diploma rather than on the seller's invoice.

Nor do we describe ourselves as approved, licensed or accredited by any education authority, because we are not. IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no UAE premises. A service claiming regulator approval should be asked for the permit number, and in our experience the request ends the conversation.

faqs.question: Does a subject specialist really matter more than a tutor nearby in Sharjah Garden City?
faqs.answer: For anything assessed by a published mark scheme or a set of criteria, yes. The marks sit in course-specific behaviour: command terms, method written out, observations rather than conclusions, uncertainty handled honestly. A generalist can keep a student company through homework; a specialist can tell you in one marked script which three habits are costing the grade. Proximity matters for attendance, and we solve attendance with live video instead - lessons are one-to-one online, and IB Gram sends nobody to a UAE address.

faqs.question: Should my child take IB Maths Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Decide from evidence rather than reputation. Analysis and Approaches is algebra, proof and calculus heavy and is expected by some maths-heavy degree routes; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics heavy and is not an easy option at higher level. The reliable method is to attempt questions from both with somebody who teaches both, then look at the scripts. Check the prerequisites of the degree subjects your child is considering before the choice is locked, because reversing it later is disruptive and sometimes impossible.

faqs.question: What is an alternative-to-practical paper and how do you prepare for it?
faqs.answer: In Cambridge sciences it is the paper that tests practical skills in writing: identifying variables, describing a method precisely, naming instruments, spotting sources of error and suggesting improvements. Candidates who have done plenty of laboratory work still lose marks here because they have never had to narrate a method. It is one of the most coachable components in either system - three or four focused sessions with past questions, marked against the published scheme, usually produce a visible change in the next mock.

faqs.question: Why do my child's science answers lose marks when the content is right?
faqs.answer: Almost always because of precision. The mark scheme asks for an observation and gets a conclusion: 'it goes cloudy' instead of 'a white precipitate forms'. Equations arrive without state symbols. Organic reactions arrive without conditions. Multi-step calculations arrive as a number with no method, in a question where the method carries the marks. None of that is difficult science, and all of it is a writing habit that changes within a few sessions once somebody marks the work strictly against the real scheme.

faqs.question: How do command terms differ between IB and Cambridge papers?
faqs.answer: Less than you would expect, which is good news. Both publish command terms and both treat them as instructions: state asks for a fact, describe for what happens, explain for why with a mechanism, suggest for a reasoned possibility in unfamiliar context, evaluate for both sides plus a judgement. The IB adds criterion language in internal assessments - evaluation, limitation, justification - with descriptors spelling out what higher achievement looks like. Students who read those descriptors in week one of a project write differently from those who meet them after a first draft.

faqs.question: How should past papers be used across a two-year course?
faqs.answer: In three phases, because the supply is finite. Early on, individual questions by topic, untimed, to test whether a topic is secure. Mid-course, sections under timing to build pace. In the final block, whole papers under exam conditions, marked against the published mark scheme between sessions, with review limited to the question types your error log names. Papers done untimed, unmarked and half-finished teach nothing while using up a resource you will want in the final ten weeks.

faqs.question: Can you supply past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents?
faqs.answer: We reference them and point you to the official sources, and we do not distribute copies. Those documents belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and your child's school is the proper route to the current versions - syllabuses change between cycles, so the school's copy is also the correct one. Any tutoring service offering a shared drive full of board material is distributing somebody else's copyright, and where material is unreleased it creates a malpractice question that attaches to your child rather than to the seller.

faqs.question: My child speaks English fluently but loses marks in English papers. Why?
faqs.answer: Because conversational fluency and analytical writing are different skills, and the papers assess the second. Marks go on register, structure, precision and - in Cambridge directed writing - analysis of effect rather than summary of content. In the IB oral, the commonest failure is choosing a global issue too broad to anchor in two extracts. All of those are specific and teachable. The method that works is writing the same task two or three times and annotating each version against the mark scheme, which almost nobody does without a tutor present.

faqs.question: Is Core or Extended the right entry for my Cambridge candidate?
faqs.answer: Test it rather than argue about it. Extended carries the full grade range and includes content a Core candidate never meets; Core caps the grade but a secure top Core grade beats a scraped Extended one. The question is whether the student can access the Extended-only topics and finish the harder paper in the time, and two sessions of Extended past-paper questions will tell a specialist that. Any change must go through the school before its internal entry deadline, so the conversation needs to happen early rather than after the mocks.

faqs.question: How much does subject-specialist tuition cost around Sharjah Garden City?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours: budget online tutoring starts around AED 45 an hour across published UAE rate cards, a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit is quoted at AED 180 to 500 once travel is absorbed, and named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 and above. Bestimate's Dubai estimates, read in October 2026, put one weekly session at AED 600 to 1,200 a month with a qualified tutor. Ask us directly and begin with the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do about an IB internal assessment, exactly?
faqs.answer: Read the criteria with the student, narrow the research question until the available data can answer it, teach the statistics or technique the investigation needs, plan the method and uncertainty treatment, and read drafts to explain which criterion is not being met. What a tutor cannot do is write, redraft or edit any part of the submitted work, or hand over a topic with the analysis already done. IB Gram does not sell completed assessments. The malpractice consequence falls on the student's diploma, which settles the argument.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both my children if they are on different courses?
faqs.answer: Only where the courses are genuinely close - two Cambridge sciences, or IGCSE and IB maths at the lower levels. Across a Diploma higher level subject and a Year 10 IGCSE course, the honest answer is that one of the two children gets the weaker teaching, and it is usually the older one. We would rather give you two specialists in consecutive slots on the same evening, with one point of contact and two written plans, than a single tutor whose second course is approximate.

faqs.question: How soon does course-specific coaching show up in a mark?
faqs.answer: Technique changes - command terms, precision of language, timing - usually show up in the next timed assessment, which is often three to six weeks away. Content gaps take longer because they need teaching and then practice. What we will not do is quote a grade improvement or a timeline for one: nobody can know what a particular candidate will score, and a tutor who offers a number is describing a sales position rather than an educational one. The honest measure is movement on timed scripts, reviewed at session six.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free for our exact course and time?
faqs.answer: We say so. Narrow combinations - a higher level language, Additional Mathematics 0606, a specific board's business paper at a peak evening hour - occasionally have nobody available, particularly in the weeks before a series. The options we will offer are a different hour with the right specialist, or a named date when one becomes free. We will not substitute a generalist and leave a family to discover the mismatch over six weeks, because for course-specific work that substitution is the whole problem.

intro.heading: What 'near me' can and cannot give a family in Tilal City
paragraphs: Proximity solves exactly one problem: getting a competent adult into the same room as a teenager, reliably, every week. That is a real problem and it used to be the only one worth solving, which is why 'tutor near me' is still the phrase everybody types. From Tilal City, on the southern Sharjah corridor, the map returns a short list, and the short list is the issue.

What proximity cannot give you is syllabus knowledge. The IB Middle Years Programme assesses against criteria A to D in most subjects, with command terms and task-specific clarifications that a tutor has to have read. The Diploma Programme adds internal assessments, Theory of Knowledge and an extended essay, each with its own rules about what help is permitted. Cambridge IGCSE splits into Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings. Pearson Edexcel uses different codes and paper structures again. Those four systems demand four different kinds of expertise, and none of them is distributed by neighbourhood.

The mismatch bites hardest in households running two systems at once, which is common here. An older child in Diploma Programme maths analysis and approaches and a younger one working towards Cambridge 0580 need genuinely different teaching, and a single local generalist hired for convenience will usually be stronger with the younger one and vague with the older. Families discover this in the second term, after a year's budget is committed.

Our answer is to match the syllabus first and remove distance from the equation. Teaching is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, so a family on the Mleiha road can work with a Diploma Programme chemistry teacher and an Edexcel maths specialist in the same week without either of them driving anywhere. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE - that service exists only in India - and saying so plainly is more useful than implying a car is coming.

There is a cost dimension too, and it is worth stating before the detail. An in-home visit on this corridor carries a travel premium that buys travel. Nothing in that premium makes the tutor better at reading a criterion descriptor or at marking a Cambridge paper to its mark scheme. For an address this far from the older tutoring districts, the premium is at the top of the market range, and it is the single largest avoidable line in a family's tutoring budget here.

The rest of this page deals with the practical consequences: how to identify which system your child is actually on, how IB and IGCSE assessment differ in ways that change tutoring, how UAE Ministry of Education equivalency treats each qualification, how the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons in Sharjah schools shape a weekday timetable, how to verify a tutor's permit, and what we do when nobody suitable is free.
