programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed against criteria rather than papers, with achievement levels converted to a 1-7 grade by the school. Because assessment is internal and criterion-based, a student can look secure while being weak at the thing the criteria actually reward: using command terms accurately, structuring an investigation, and justifying a conclusion with the evidence collected rather than with an opinion.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah, MYP students sit the same mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies lessons as every other private-school pupil in the emirate, which compresses the evening. Tutoring that works here is short, criterion-specific and scheduled after the school run rather than open-ended homework supervision.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at higher or standard level, plus Theory of Knowledge, an extended essay and creativity, activity, service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked against published criteria by letter. The common failure is not subject difficulty but load management: three higher level subjects, an extended essay and an internal assessment all peaking in the same weeks of DP2.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah has a small number of schools authorised for the Diploma Programme, so Tilal City families with a DP student frequently commute some distance to school. That makes a weekday in-home slot hard to place and an online slot straightforward, which is the practical reason most of our DP work in this emirate is video-based.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written examinations, with Cambridge offering Core and Extended tiers and Pearson using its own two-paper structures under codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. The grade is decided almost entirely in the examination room, which makes timed past-paper work with mark-scheme marking the highest-value use of tutoring hours in Years 10 and 11.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the February/March Cambridge series is offered in India only. Entries are made by the school as part of its centre registration, and each Cambridge centre belongs to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, so the only reliable schedule is the one your exams officer issues.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-tilal-.subjectsIntro: IB subjects first, because they are the harder ones to staff locally. Each entry names what the course assesses and where Sharjah students most often drop marks, since that is what decides whether a tutor is the right match.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry the paper. Students arriving from a strong IGCSE Extended background still struggle with the expectation that method is written out and justified. The internal assessment, a mathematical exploration, needs a question narrow enough to analyse properly - the single most common DP maths problem we are asked to fix.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-heavy work. It is not the easy option: the higher level course includes demanding statistical content, and some university engineering routes expect analysis and approaches instead. Choosing between the two is a decision worth making with evidence rather than reputation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields dominate the lost marks, usually through sign conventions and unexamined assumptions in multi-step problems. The internal assessment rewards a controlled variable set and honest uncertainty treatment far more than an ambitious topic, which is where tutoring saves the most time.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are the recurring difficulties, and higher level adds depth rather than breadth. Precision of language in extended responses decides a surprising share of marks - naming an observation rather than stating a conclusion, as at IGCSE, only more strictly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where the grade turns on command terms and on data-based questions. Students who revise by rereading notes plateau; students who answer past data questions under time and check against the mark scheme move. Statistical treatment in the internal assessment is a common weak point.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation are the mark earners. Higher level adds quantitative work that catches students who chose the subject expecting essays only. The three commentaries require a current article and disciplined application of one section of the syllabus, not a general discussion of the news.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen textual analysis and the individual oral carry the grade. The oral fails when the global issue is too broad to anchor in two extracts. Practice here is structural: choosing the issue, selecting the extracts, and rehearsing to the time limit with the criteria visible.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Taken by many Sharjah students who are fluent but not first-language English users. The productive skills are coachable to a formula: register, text type conventions, and a paper 1 task that must match its audience. Listening practice is routinely neglected and routinely costs marks.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools such as the business management toolkit must be applied to the case, not described. The internal assessment needs a real organisation and genuine data, which is where students in a hurry create problems for themselves that no amount of writing skill repairs.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-tilal-.igcseSubjectsIntro: The British-track side of a mixed household, with the codes that decide which tutor fits. Ask your child's school for the code if the report does not show it; it takes one email and it changes the match.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Most requested subject in Years 10 and 11 across Sharjah. Bounds, rearrangement under time pressure and multi-step problems abandoned early are the standard mark losses, and all three respond to timed papers with immediate marking rather than to topic revision.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Edexcel
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and graph-gradient work account for most of the gap between a 6 and an 8. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards students who can narrate a method, which is a skill a tutor can teach deliberately in three or four sessions.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Mole ratios, electrolysis products and the precise language of observations. The extended paper marks wording strictly, so a student who knows the chemistry can still lose marks by writing loosely about what they saw.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Memorisable content, so the marks sit in command words and diagram work. Transport in plants, genetic crosses and experimental design questions are where tutoring earns its hour.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: Widely taken in Sharjah schools where English is the language of instruction but not of the home. Note-making, summary word limits and register shifts are formulaic enough to coach precisely.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
igcseSubjects.description: The bridge subject for students heading to A Level mathematics or a higher level IB maths course. Calculus notation and radian work expose the gap early, and it is a hard subject to staff locally at a weekday hour.

sections.heading: First, work out which syllabus your child is actually on
paragraphs: A surprising number of enquiries from this corridor begin with a sentence that does not identify the course: 'she's in Year 11 doing sciences', 'he's in grade 10 IB'. Neither is enough to match a tutor, and both are easy to resolve. The school report names the programme. For IB, it will say Middle Years Programme or Diploma Programme and give criterion grades or subject levels. For the British track, there is a code - 0580, 0620, 4MA1, 4PH1 - on the statement of entry or in the exam information the school circulates.

The distinction matters because the teaching is different in kind, not degree. A Middle Years student is assessed against criteria by letter, with task-specific descriptors, and good tutoring there means practising against those descriptors. A Cambridge IGCSE candidate is assessed by terminal papers, and good tutoring means timed papers marked to a mark scheme. A Diploma student needs both: internal assessment coaching against criteria and paper technique for the terminal examinations.

There is a third case, common in Sharjah: a student moving between systems. A Year 11 IGCSE candidate heading into the Diploma Programme faces a genuine step in independent writing and in mathematical justification. A Middle Years student entering Year 10 at a British-curriculum school meets terminal examinations for the first time. Both transitions benefit from a few sessions aimed at the new system's demands rather than at subject content, and both are usually left until the first disappointing report.

Send the programme and the code when you contact us. It takes a line, and it is the difference between a tutor who starts teaching in session one and a tutor who spends three sessions working out what the course requires.
bullets: IB report language: criteria A-D, achievement levels, subject level HL or SL

sections.heading: How IB and IGCSE assessment differ, and why one tutor rarely covers both
paragraphs: The two systems reward different behaviour. IGCSE grades are decided almost entirely in the examination room, on papers with predictable question styles and published mark schemes. Preparation is therefore repetitive and measurable: do the paper, mark it honestly, log the error type, repeat. A student can lift an IGCSE grade substantially in eight weeks without learning much new content, purely by learning what the examiner rewards.

IB grades are built over two years. Internal assessments carry a defined share of the subject grade and are marked against criteria by letter, with the school marking and the IB moderating. An extended essay and Theory of Knowledge sit outside subject teaching and contribute points of their own. The work is less recoverable late, because deadlines pass and cannot be re-sat, which changes what tutoring is for: it is scheduling and standards as much as teaching.

That difference explains why a single local tutor hired for both children usually disappoints one of them. Someone fluent in mark-scheme marking for Cambridge papers may never have read an internal assessment criterion. Someone who has supervised Diploma internal assessments may be rusty on the mechanics of a tiered Core and Extended entry. Neither is a bad tutor; they are differently specialised, and the specialisation is invisible on a listing that says 'maths and science, all levels'.
The table below sets out the differences that actually change a tutoring plan. It is worth reading before you book anybody, local or online, because it tells you what to ask them.

sections.heading: Why distance stops being the useful filter in southern Sharjah
paragraphs: In a dense district, filtering by distance is a rough but workable proxy for availability: there are enough tutors nearby that some of them will be good. Tilal City does not have that density, and neither do the communities around it. Filter to a twenty-minute radius and the list is short; filter again to a single programme and subject and it frequently empties.

The arithmetic is worth making explicit. A Diploma Programme chemistry teacher is a rarer person than a maths graduate. Sharjah has a limited number of schools authorised for the Diploma Programme, so the pool of adults in this emirate who have taught DP chemistry is small, and the subset willing to drive to the Mleiha corridor at six o'clock on a Tuesday is smaller still. Requiring both proximity and specialism usually means accepting neither.

Travel also costs money that buys nothing academic. In-home visits in the Sharjah market are quoted between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour once the drive is absorbed, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor teaching online. The difference is a car, not better teaching, and for an address this far out the premium sits at the top of the range.

So the sensible filter is the syllabus. Match on programme, subject and level, pick from the whole country, and solve the presence problem with video rather than with a windscreen. That is what we do: lessons one to one, online, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with no tutor travelling to any UAE address.

sections.heading: Equivalency: what the UAE Ministry of Education asks of each qualification
paragraphs: Families in Sharjah planning a UAE university application eventually meet the equivalency process, and it is poorly explained almost everywhere. For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects.

That five-subject rule is worth repeating because a ranking competitor page states UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong and could change a family's subject choices for no reason. For the American track, the published requirements include an English proficiency score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in SAT mathematics.

For the IB Diploma there is no points figure published in the source material available to us, and we will not invent one. If your child is on the Diploma Programme and you need the equivalency threshold, read it on the Ministry of Education's own site or ask the emirate attestation authority directly. A tutoring page is not a source for a regulatory number that affects a university application.

Two further points of hygiene. Equivalency is a process families complete themselves through the official channel; IB Gram does not perform it, guarantee it or speed it up, and nobody who offers to should be trusted with it. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression - any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency.

sections.heading: The mandatory subjects nobody factors into the evening timetable
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why your child's international programme shares its week with lessons that have nothing to do with the Diploma Programme or Cambridge.

Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed version of these requirements, and it is instructive even for Sharjah families because the federal baseline is the same. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory regardless of the licensed curriculum. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated in forty-minute lesson units, with schools able to vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met.

For a parent, this has two consequences. The first is timetable load: an international curriculum plus mandatory subjects fills the day, and an evening tutoring slot competes with homework for both. Short, specific sessions beat long general ones here. The second is that the mandatory subjects themselves sometimes need support, particularly for students who arrived in the UAE mid-school and are placed in Arabic as an additional language several years behind their year group.

Where we can help with those subjects we say so, and where we cannot we say that too. Content for the mandatory subjects is tightly controlled - using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited - so the honest offer is support with language and study skills rather than an alternative syllabus.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor is legally permitted to teach in the UAE
paragraphs: This is the question families most often skip and most easily ask. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18.

Because the permit is free and the application takes about two working days through MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, a tutor who works regularly has no practical reason not to hold one. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, and anybody quoting you a figure is guessing.

A second check is worth making. Do not arrange tuition with your child's own class teacher. Abu Dhabi's regulator has published professional-ethics rules prohibiting private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct points the same way. Press-reported rules should be verified against the current policy document, but the direction of travel is unambiguous and the conflict of interest is obvious even without a rule.

On our own position, plainly: IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform and holds no approval, licence or accreditation from any UAE education authority. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a specific educational services permit for a training institute; we do not run premises here, and we do not describe ourselves as approved by anybody. Treat any service claiming regulator approval as a claim to be evidenced.

sections.heading: Scheduling around the school run, Ramadan and the exam term
paragraphs: A tutoring plan that ignores the calendar fails quietly. For a Tilal City family, the weekday constraint is the drive home from school, which for an IB student can be long because Diploma provision in this emirate is concentrated in a few schools. A slot that starts when the student walks in is realistic; one that assumes a tutor has also finished their own commute is not.

Ramadan reshapes the week rather than pausing it. School days shorten, afternoons are low-energy, and families commonly move sessions to after Iftar or to late morning at the weekend. Diploma Programme students with internal assessment deadlines in that period need the plan rewritten in advance, not improvised in week two. Because our teaching is online, a slot can move by two hours without anybody renegotiating a journey.

The exam term has its own shape. For IGCSE candidates, the final eight to ten weeks should be timed papers, marked against the published mark scheme, with the error log deciding what gets reviewed. For Diploma students, the same weeks are usually a collision between internal assessment deadlines and examination revision, and the useful intervention is sequencing: finish the assessed work, then free the revision time, rather than doing both badly in parallel.

Where a specialist is not available at the hour you need - a common problem for narrow subjects at peak season - we tell you rather than filling the slot. A clear answer about availability lets a family make another plan; a vague one costs them a term.

sections.heading: Coursework help that is actually permitted
paragraphs: Both systems a Tilal City household might be running carry assessed work that must be the student's own, and both treat breaches as malpractice. The permitted zone is wide and worth knowing, because families who do not know where the line sits either over-ask or avoid asking for help they are entitled to.

A tutor may explain the criteria, question a research question until it is answerable, suggest how to collect usable data, teach the statistics the investigation needs, read a draft and say that the evaluation does not address the criterion, and model the same move on a different piece of work. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit any part of the submitted work, supply a topic with the analysis already done, or produce text the student then adapts.

IB Gram does not sell completed internal assessments, extended essays, Theory of Knowledge essays or coursework of any kind. This needs saying because the search results for these queries include operations that do, at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the consequence of using one falls on the student as a malpractice finding rather than on the seller. Nor do we distribute boards' syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; those belong to the boards and the school is the proper route to the current version.

The practical form this takes in a lesson is unglamorous. We read the criteria in the first session, agree what evidence the student needs to produce, and set deadlines earlier than the school's. Most assessed-work problems are scheduling problems wearing a writing-quality costume.

process.description: At six sessions we look at scores on timed work and at criterion feedback, not at effort. A wrong match is replaced without restarting the plan. If no specialist is free for a narrow subject at your hour, we say so plainly instead of substituting a generalist.

whyPoints.description: A Diploma Programme student and an IGCSE candidate under the same roof need different specialists. Matching both through one platform means two written plans, one contact and one review conversation, rather than two separate arrangements that never align with the school calendar.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus is the filter, not the map
whyPoints.description: We match on programme, subject and level first. For southern Sharjah that is the only way to reach a subject specialist at all, because the local pool within a short drive of Tilal City is small and weighted towards generalists.

whyPoints.title: Honest about delivery
whyPoints.description: All UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. You will not book expecting a car and discover a video call.

whyPoints.description: The equivalency rules, the permit position and the mandatory-subject requirements on this page come from official UAE sources, and where a figure is not published - the IB equivalency threshold - we say so instead of filling the gap with a guess.

whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback against published criteria. They do not write or edit assessed work, and we do not sell it. That boundary protects the student, which is the only party who carries the consequence of crossing it.

faqs.question: Does a tutor near me in Tilal City actually matter more than subject expertise?
faqs.answer: Proximity solves attendance; expertise decides the grade. In a dense district you can often have both, but Tilal City sits on the southern Sharjah corridor where the local pool is small and weighted towards generalists. Filter by distance and then by programme and subject, and the list frequently empties. Our view is to match on syllabus and solve attendance with live video, which is why we teach one-to-one online and do not send anybody to a UAE address. The free trial lesson exists so you can test that this works for your child before committing.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both my IB and my IGCSE child?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and only when the subject is the same and the tutor has genuinely taught both systems. The two reward different work: IGCSE is terminal papers marked to a published mark scheme, while IB adds criterion-marked internal assessment over two years. A tutor fluent in one often has never read a criterion descriptor or never timed a Cambridge paper. We would rather give you two specialists with consecutive slots on the same evening than one compromise who is strong with one child and vague with the other.

faqs.question: How do I find out which syllabus and code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: The school report names the programme - Middle Years Programme, Diploma Programme, or a year group on the British track. For Cambridge or Pearson, there is a code on the statement of entry or in the exam information the school circulates: 0580 and 0620 are Cambridge, 4MA1 and 4CH1 are Pearson Edexcel. If neither document is to hand, the exams officer can confirm it in one email. Send us that code and the subject level, and the match is made on evidence rather than on a guess about what Year 11 usually means.

faqs.question: What are the UAE equivalency requirements for a British-curriculum student?
faqs.answer: The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking tutoring site states six subjects are needed, which is incorrect. Verify your own case on the Ministry of Education's site or with the emirate attestation authority - equivalency is a process families complete themselves, and no tutoring service performs it for you.

faqs.question: Is there an IB equivalency points score I should be working towards?
faqs.answer: Not one we will publish. The sources available to us carry the British and American track requirements in detail but no IB Diploma points threshold, and an unsourced number on a tutoring page could change a family's university plans for the worse. Read it on the Ministry of Education's own site, or ask your school's IB coordinator, who deals with this annually for a whole cohort. Treat any tutoring site that quotes a confident IB figure without a government source with the scepticism you would apply to any other unsourced claim about your child's future.

faqs.question: Which exam series do Sharjah students sit, and what about resits?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs June and November series, and UAE candidates sit those two - the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. November is the standard resit route for a June candidate. For Pearson, the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 and results from that series reach students in January; the November 2025 cohort received theirs on 22 January 2026. Use the timetable your school's exams officer issues, since each Cambridge centre belongs to one of six zones.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect tutoring time?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than most families expect. Private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum under federal regulations, and schools organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of those subjects. Instructional time is counted in forty-minute units. The practical effect is a full school day and homework across two curricula, so an evening tutoring slot needs to be short and specific. We also support Arabic as an additional language where a student arrived mid-school and sits well below their year group.

faqs.question: How much does one-to-one IB or IGCSE tuition cost in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Across published UAE rate cards, budget online tutoring starts around AED 45 an hour, a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed, and named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 and above. Bestimate's Dubai cost estimates, read in October 2026, put one weekly session at AED 600 to 1,200 a month with a qualified tutor. Those are market figures for comparison; ask us for ours and start with the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: What internal assessment help may a tutor give a Tilal City student?
faqs.answer: With the thinking, the criteria and the feedback - yes, and early help is the useful kind. A tutor can narrow a research question until it is answerable, teach the statistics an investigation needs, read a draft and explain which criterion is not being met, and model the same move on a different task. A tutor cannot write, redraft or edit the submitted work. IB Gram does not sell completed internal assessments, extended essays or Theory of Knowledge essays. The consequence of buying one lands on the student as a malpractice finding, not on the seller.

faqs.question: Does somebody tutoring in Tilal City need a MoHRE permit, and can I verify it?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is free of charge, valid two years, and issued through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service in about two working days, so a working tutor has no practical reason to be without one. Those operating without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so ignore any figure quoted at you. Also avoid arranging tuition with your child's own class teacher - that conflict is explicitly discouraged.

faqs.question: Why is Diploma Programme tutoring harder to find locally than IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Because the teaching population is smaller. Sharjah has a limited number of schools authorised for the Diploma Programme, so the number of adults in this emirate who have taught a specific DP subject to final-grade standard is low, and the number willing to drive to the Mleiha corridor on a weekday evening is lower still. British-curriculum provision is far broader, which is why local lists are thicker for IGCSE. Teaching over video dissolves the problem by letting a Tilal City family work with a DP subject teacher wherever that person happens to live.

faqs.question: What happens during Ramadan and the school holidays?
faqs.answer: Sessions move rather than stop. School days shorten during Ramadan and afternoons are low-energy, so families commonly shift lessons to after Iftar or to late morning at the weekend; because the lesson is online, moving it by two hours costs nothing. Holidays are often the best time for transition work - an IGCSE candidate heading into the Diploma Programme, or a Middle Years student meeting terminal examinations for the first time - because there is time to teach the new system's demands without competing with term-time homework.

faqs.question: My child says they will not learn from a screen. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Test it rather than argue about it. The free trial lesson is one-to-one, with a shared screen and a writing tablet so the tutor can work through a problem rather than talk at a camera, and most students who object are picturing a recorded class or a group webinar. Some genuinely do better in a room, and for those families the honest answer is that IB Gram does not provide UAE home visits, so a local arrangement may suit them better. We would rather you found that out in a free trial than after a term.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is available for the subject and time we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you. Narrow requests - Additional Mathematics 0606, a specific board's business studies paper, a higher level language at a peak evening hour - sometimes have no specialist free, especially in the weeks before a series. The alternatives we will offer are a different time with the right specialist, or a wait with a named date. What we will not do is put a generalist in the slot and let a family spend six weeks finding out. A clear no is worth more than an optimistic yes.

intro.heading: The district where supply is not the constraint
paragraphs: Most "tutor near me" pages exist to tell a parent that supply is scarce. In University City that would be dishonest. The district holds Sharjah's higher-education cluster — the American University of Sharjah, the University of Sharjah, Al Qasimia University, the Higher Colleges of Technology and the Sharjah Institute of Technology among them — and the result is a large resident undergraduate population within walking distance, much of it entirely capable of explaining calculus or titration to a Year 11.

That abundance is why Sharjah's budget tutoring band is real. Published rates in this market start at AED 45 to AED 65 an hour on EdFlik and AED 33 to AED 52 on Tutopiya, and in University City those numbers are not marketing. They reflect a genuine local labour supply of undergraduates teaching between lectures.

So the honest version of the question changes. It is not "is there anyone near me". It is "can the person near me teach the paper my child is actually sitting". Those are different skills, and the gap between them is not about intelligence or effort. A chemistry undergraduate knows more chemistry than the examiner needs. What they usually have not seen is a Cambridge 0620 mark scheme, or the lettered criteria an IB Diploma Internal Assessment is judged against, and those two documents are where IGCSE and Diploma marks are won.

One framing worth holding onto. A tutor cannot be judged on proximity, on years of experience or on a list of schools, because none of those is checkable from a parent's side of the conversation. A tutor can be judged on whether they have read the document that awards the marks, and that is checkable in five minutes by anyone, including a parent who never studied the subject.

This page is therefore built differently from most tutoring pages. It spends its length on how to evaluate a tutor whose strength is subject knowledge and whose gap is assessment knowledge — because in University City that is the most likely candidate you will meet, and because a well-chosen undergraduate tutor working on the right task is genuinely good value.

It also covers the permit position properly, because it applies directly here. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and its eligible applicants explicitly include university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A student tutor in University City can hold one, and since it costs nothing there is no reason not to ask.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. In-home visits are offered only in India. University City students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. The claim is not that we are closer. It is that for a Higher Level Diploma science or a 0606 Additional Mathematics entry, choosing on syllabus rather than on walking distance is the choice that matters.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-univer.programmesIntro: University City's own school catchment spans both systems, and households here often hold both at once. These are the programmes behind the search, with the specific thing each one asks of a tutor beyond subject knowledge.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment marked against lettered criteria with their own descriptor bands, and the marks are added criterion by criterion rather than pooled. This is the single piece of knowledge a subject-strong tutor most often lacks, and it is the one that decides Internal Assessment grades.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No IB exam or results date appears on this page because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than none — take every Diploma date from your school's IB coordinator. What is locally fixed is that Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the Diploma in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two separate qualifications that school reports blur into one word. Cambridge uses four-digit codes — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry — with Core and Extended tiering. Pearson codes start with 4 — 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 — with Foundation and Higher tiering on Mathematics Specification A. Papers, weightings and question styles all differ, and so does which past-paper archive is worth working through.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November, and its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January. Cambridge assigns every centre to one of six timetable zones and cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong version.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria per subject scored 0–8 and converted to a 1–7 grade. The programme credits process, communication and reflection explicitly, which is why a capable student can sit at a 4 with correct work and a thin justification criterion. A tutor who cannot name the four criteria is teaching the subject rather than the assessment.
programmes.countryNote: The step from the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma is the most common reason families in this part of Sharjah start tutoring in Year 11. The useful intervention is a short diagnostic on the specific algebra, functions and proof the Diploma mathematics courses open with, done before Year 12 rather than after the first assessment comes back.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route in several Sharjah schools, and often what a family is weighing the Diploma against. Three or four subjects in depth, no Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge. Subject entry usually assumes an A or B at IGCSE Extended, and the step up in mathematics and the sciences is steep because A Level assumes algebraic fluency IGCSE only samples.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 — Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five — plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. A ranking competitor states six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-univer.subjectsIntro: Below, the subjects most requested in this catchment and the specific assessment behaviour each one rewards. These lines double as interview questions for any tutor, undergraduate or otherwise.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended investigation, not a question set, and it is the most common reason a predicted grade falls. The exploration is marked on communication, presentation, reasoning and personal engagement, and strong mathematicians routinely lose the last of those entirely.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-permitted work throughout. Frequently misread as the easier route rather than the different one. The exploration rewards genuine collected data, which is a decision made in the first week and not fixable later.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the grade, with marks for state symbols, conditions and the reasoning between steps. The Internal Assessment credits the student's own research question and method design, and a tidy textbook result earns nothing by itself.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth on shared topics and that extra material separates candidates. Extended responses reward stating the physical principle before the calculation. The Internal Assessment credits design and uncertainty handling rather than getting the accepted value.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: Command terms do the damage: outline, describe, explain, distinguish and discuss expect different structures and mark counts. A student answering all of them the same way settles near a 5 regardless of content knowledge. Data questions on unfamiliar experiments are trainable and rarely trained.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics — 0580 / 4MA1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended Paper 4 decides most grades through structured multi-mark questions, and unshown method on a four-mark item typically scores one. Pearson splits the marks evenly across two papers, which makes pacing errors unrecoverable.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics — 0625 / 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism take most of the lost marks, usually when a potential divider is read as a plain series circuit. Which practical route the centre uses — timetabled practical or alternative-to-practical — changes half the revision plan.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry — 0620 / 4CH1
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic and organic pathways carry the grade. Units dropped mid-titration cost marks, and a product named without its functional group scores nothing. Cambridge examines qualitative analysis tables in detail and they are the cheapest marks on the paper.

subjects.name: IGCSE Additional Mathematics — 0606
subjects.description: Calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities 0580 never reaches. Reading it as harder 0580 revision is the standard error. Students who do well have drilled differentiation and the factor theorem deliberately, and the tutor pool for it is thin everywhere.

subjects.name: IGCSE Computer Science — 0478 / 4CP0
subjects.description: Pseudocode is marked against the syllabus's own conventions rather than Python, which costs marks on every trace table — a trap an undergraduate programmer walks into faster than anyone. Theory on data representation and networks is learnable and chronically under-revised.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.levels: First language and additional language routes
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools. Separate streams exist for Arab and non-Arab students because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, so material does not transfer between them.

sections.heading: Why the cheapest tutor in Sharjah lives here
paragraphs: Rate bands in a market are set by supply, and University City has an unusual amount of it. Several thousand undergraduates live inside or immediately around the district, a good number of them in subjects that map directly onto IGCSE and Diploma content, and many of them want a few paid hours a week that do not require a car.

That is why published budget rates in this market are not fiction. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, and in this district those figures are achievable in person. Compare the AED 150 to AED 300 band that a qualified subject tutor commands online, or the AED 180 to AED 500 range for in-home visits where Bestimate's Dubai table puts the typical case at AED 180 to AED 350.

A parent should take the saving seriously rather than dismiss it. For a student who missed three weeks of mechanics through illness, or who needs someone to sit alongside them while they work through a problem set, a capable undergraduate at AED 60 an hour is excellent value and probably better value than a specialist at four times the price.

The mistake is assuming the saving scales to every task. It does not, and the reason is specific rather than snobbish. Mark schemes and criterion descriptors are professional documents that undergraduates have no reason to have read. A tutor who has never seen how a Cambridge six-mark item is credited, or how an Internal Assessment's evaluation criterion is banded, cannot diagnose a loss in those places however well they know the content.

So the question to carry into this district is not whether to pay less. It is which of your child's problems is a content problem and which is an assessment problem, because the first is cheap here and the second is not.

sections.heading: A test that works on a nineteen-year-old tutor
paragraphs: Asking an undergraduate about their experience is useless, because the honest answer is that they have little and it does not follow that they will be bad. Ask about the documents instead. These four questions take five minutes and they work on anyone.

First: have you read the mark scheme for this paper, and what does it credit that a student would not guess? A good answer names something concrete — method marks awarded independently of the final answer, a specific vocabulary requirement in a science extended response, the structure of a six-mark item. Second, for a Diploma student: name the criteria for this Internal Assessment and say what each one rewards. Those descriptors are lettered and published, and someone who has taught the course can list them.

Third: here is a marked paper, what went wrong? Not "they need more practice" — the useful answer is a named behaviour. The student writes answers without working on any question worth three or more marks. The student describes where the question asked them to explain. The student labels no axes on economics diagrams. That is a diagnosis, and it tells you what the next four sessions will do.

Fourth: what will you refuse to do with my child's coursework? A tutor who has thought about the boundary answers immediately. One who has not will hesitate, and that hesitation matters more with an inexperienced tutor than with an experienced one, because an undergraduate under pressure to be helpful is exactly the person most likely to rewrite a paragraph themselves.

A candidate who answers the first three well and the fourth cleanly is worth hiring at any age. One who cannot answer the first two can still be useful for content, at content prices, on content tasks.

sections.heading: The permit rules that apply directly in this district
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the rules are unusually relevant in University City because they explicitly cover student tutors. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years.

The eligible categories are set out in the official guidance and include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. So a University of Sharjah undergraduate tutoring a Year 11 is within a recognised category, provided they hold the permit.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, so a figure quoted to you as the penalty is unverified and should be treated as such. The application route is MoHRE's own service for private tutor licensing, through the smart app, website and e-services system.

Because the permit is free, the question is easy to ask and the answer is informative. A tutor who holds it has done a two-day administrative process at no cost. A tutor who has not either did not know or decided not to, and both are worth knowing before they teach your child weekly in your home.

One related rule, press-reported rather than taken from the policy document itself: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE code of conduct carries a similar bar. Verify against the current policy before relying on the exact wording, but the principle is clear enough — a teacher tutoring their own student is not a shortcut to take.

sections.heading: IB and IGCSE ask for two different skills
paragraphs: A household in this catchment often has one child on each system, and parents reasonably assume a good tutor covers both. Sometimes true, but the two qualifications test different things and reward different training, and a tutor strong in one can be mediocre in the other without anybody noticing for a term.

IGCSE is terminal and paper-based. Grades come from written papers sat under time, and marks are won by precision: method shown, units carried, mark-scheme vocabulary used, the command term answered as asked. Training for it is mechanical in a good way — marked papers, an error log, targeted repetition of the behaviour that keeps costing marks.

The Diploma puts a substantial share of the grade in the student's own extended work and marks it against lettered criteria added separately. Training for it is editorial: reading descriptors, questioning an argument, pushing a student to evaluate rather than describe. The failure modes are structural rather than careless — an empty evaluation criterion, a research question too broad to answer, a commentary built on an article with no economics in it.

The practical consequence for a University City family is to stop looking for one tutor for both children. Ask instead which document each tutor has worked from. A tutor who talks fluently about mark schemes is probably your IGCSE answer. A tutor who talks about criteria and command terms is probably your Diploma answer. Someone who talks about neither is a content tutor, which is a real and useful thing at a lower price.

The transition between the two systems is its own job again. A student arriving in Diploma Year 1 from a strong IGCSE record frequently drops two grades in a term, and the cause is almost always that speed and accuracy stop being the skill being measured.

sections.heading: Coursework: the line an inexperienced tutor most often crosses
paragraphs: This section is here specifically because of who tutors in this district. An undergraduate wants to help, is good at writing, is being paid by a parent who wants results, and is sitting next to a student with a deadline. That is the exact set of pressures under which a sentence gets rewritten for the student rather than discussed with them.

The rule is not a matter of style. IB academic-honesty rules treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and a malpractice finding affects the candidate's diploma. The tutor carries no consequence at all. Neither does the operator in this market that sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price.

So the boundary needs stating before the first session, in words a nineteen-year-old can apply under deadline pressure. A tutor may explain the criteria, question the argument, point at a weak paragraph and say why it is weak, and teach the skill the task needs. A tutor may not write a sentence that will be submitted, redraft to completion, or supply model text to work from.

The same applies to materials. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are their copyright and are available free through the school. Working through them together with the source cited is the legitimate version; a shared drive of them is not.

A practical safeguard: ask that feedback be given verbally or as comments rather than as edits in the document. It is a small procedural change and it removes the ambiguity entirely, for the student's protection as much as anyone's.

sections.heading: When a session fits around a University City evening
paragraphs: Scheduling kills more tutoring arrangements than teaching quality does. A slot that does not survive the real school day gets moved, then moved again, and then the arrangement quietly ends with the family concluding tutoring does not work.

This district's constraint is the Muwaileh and Maliha Road dismissal window, where several large campuses release into the same roads within a narrow period. A household twenty minutes away by map is thirty-five minutes away at 2.45pm, and with a sibling at a second school it is rarely settled before 4.30pm. That makes a 4pm session fiction and 5pm the earliest honest option for a single-child household.

University schedules add a wrinkle unique to this area. An undergraduate tutor's availability moves with their own timetable and collapses entirely during their exam weeks, which do not align with school exam weeks. A family that has built its revision plan around a local student tutor can lose that tutor precisely in the month before the school mocks.

Live-video sessions remove the travel variable and make the slot a fixed commitment rather than a negotiation, which is most of what families want from them. The slot is booked in Gulf Standard Time and held weekly, including the later windows for students commuting back from Dubai schools.

Ramadan is planned around rather than through. Study patterns shift and evenings run later, so lighter sessions during the month and the intensive work either side of it is the arrangement that survives, and most families here move to a post-Iftar time.

sections.heading: What a parent in this district can verify in a day
paragraphs: Most claims a tutoring service makes about itself cannot be checked. A short list can, and in a district where you will be choosing between several plausible local candidates, that list is worth an afternoon.

The board, code and tier come from the school's exams officer in one email, along with the centre's own timetable. That last item matters: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

The permit comes from asking the tutor, and the honest answer is informative either way given that it is free. The school side comes from knowing your regulator: the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods — a wider remit than inspection alone.

Two claims cannot be checked and should be read as warnings. Examiner status should not be asserted for an individual whose current position cannot be shown, and should never be used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content. Regulator approval is the other: a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and a claim of regulator endorsement over a platform's tutors is the most misleading thing available in this market.

For the avoidance of doubt about us: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed by or partnered with SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and holds no educational services permit. Naming a regulator on this page describes the system a Sharjah student studies inside.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what the thin spots are
paragraphs: Begin with the last marked piece of work rather than the report card. A grade says something is wrong; marked work shows which marks went and why, and it is the only basis on which any tutor can say something useful before being paid.

Then the free trial over live video, at a time that survives the dismissal window — usually six o'clock or later for a household with children at two schools. Judge it on whether the tutor named a specific behaviour and said what the next four sessions would address. Vagueness here becomes billed hours later.

Coverage is not uniform and should be stated rather than concealed. Content help is abundant in this district. Assessment technique at IGCSE Extended is moderately available. Diploma Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Economics evaluation coaching, Theory of Knowledge support, Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 pseudocode and Accounting 0452 are all thin pools, locally and generally.

When the match is not available, the honest options are a different slot with the right specialist, that specialist over live video from another time zone, or a plain statement that it is not available this term. A general science tutor in front of a Higher Level Chemistry candidate is not a match whatever label is put on it.

Finally, agree the review point before the first paid session. Six weeks later, read the next marked piece for the loss you started with. If it has moved, continue. If it has not, change the plan or the tutor — a mismatch is common and says nothing about either party.

faqs.question: Are there really more tutors available in University City than elsewhere in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is not a marketing claim. The district holds Sharjah's higher-education cluster, including the American University of Sharjah, the University of Sharjah, Al Qasimia University, the Higher Colleges of Technology and the Sharjah Institute of Technology, so several thousand undergraduates live within walking distance of each other. That supply is why published budget rates of AED 33 to AED 150 an hour are achievable here in person. The constraint is not availability. It is whether a given tutor has read the mark scheme for your child's paper.

faqs.question: Can a university student actually tutor my child for IGCSE or the IB?
faqs.answer: Legally yes, and often usefully. The MoHRE private tuition work permit explicitly lists university students among its eligible applicants, alongside school and government-sector teachers, private-sector employees, unemployed individuals and school students aged 15 to 18. It is granted free of charge for two years. Practically, an undergraduate is usually strong on content and weak on assessment documents, so the arrangement works best for re-teaching missed material rather than for mark-scheme or criterion technique.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying four times more for a specialist when a student tutor is nearby?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which problem you have. If your child missed three weeks of mechanics, a capable undergraduate at AED 60 an hour is excellent value and a specialist at AED 270 is an overpayment. If your child knows the content and keeps losing method marks because working is not shown, no amount of cheap content teaching will move it. Diagnose first from a marked paper, then buy the matching thing. Many families here sensibly buy both for different tasks.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to homes in University City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Sharjah or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. University City students are taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Given that this is the one district in Sharjah where local supply is genuinely abundant, the honest case for online is narrow and specific: it is how you reach a Higher Level Diploma science or Additional Mathematics 0606 specialist that nobody nearby teaches.

faqs.question: What exactly should I ask a tutor who has never taught professionally?
faqs.answer: Four things, and none of them about experience. What does the mark scheme for this paper credit that a student would not guess? For a Diploma student, name the criteria for this Internal Assessment and say what each rewards. Here is a marked paper — what went wrong, in terms of a behaviour rather than a feeling? And what will you refuse to do with my child's coursework? Good answers to the first three plus a clean answer to the fourth is a hire worth making at any age.

faqs.question: Why would a tutor who knows the subject still not help my child's grade?
faqs.answer: Because marks are awarded by a document the tutor may never have read. Mark schemes credit method independently of the answer, require specific vocabulary in science extended responses, and structure six-mark items in a particular way. IB Internal Assessments are marked criterion by criterion, each lettered and added separately, so a mathematically perfect exploration with no personal engagement loses those marks outright. Subject knowledge cannot diagnose a loss in a place the tutor has never looked.

faqs.question: Will a student tutor still be available during my child's mock exams?
faqs.answer: Often not, and this catches families here specifically. An undergraduate's availability follows their own university timetable, and their exam weeks do not align with school ones — which means a tutor recruited in October can disappear in the month before the school mocks or before the June series. If you are building a revision plan around a local student tutor, ask for their exam dates at the start and plan the cover, or hold a specialist slot in parallel.

faqs.question: My child has one sibling on IGCSE and one on the Diploma. Can one tutor do both?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it is worth testing rather than assuming. The two systems reward different training: IGCSE is terminal and paper-based, so the work is marked papers, an error log and targeted repetition. The Diploma puts a large share of the grade in criterion-marked internal work, so the work is editorial — reading descriptors, questioning arguments, pushing a student from describing to evaluating. Ask each tutor which document they work from. The answer sorts them quickly.

faqs.question: How late can a session start for a household near University City?
faqs.answer: Six o'clock works for most, and 5pm only where there is a single child at a nearby school. Dismissal congestion along the Maliha Road corridor is sharp because several large campuses release into the same roads in a narrow window, and a household with children at two schools is rarely settled before 4.30pm. Students commuting back from Dubai schools are looking at 7.30pm. Slots are booked in Gulf Standard Time and held weekly, with a post-Iftar time during Ramadan.

faqs.question: How do I make sure a tutor does not end up writing part of my child's coursework?
faqs.answer: Set the rule in words before the first session and ask for a procedural safeguard: feedback as spoken comments or margin notes, never as edits inside the document. A tutor may explain criteria, question an argument, point at a weak paragraph and teach the underlying skill. A tutor may not write submitted text, redraft to completion or supply model answers. IB rules treat work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student.

faqs.question: What does SPEA regulate, and does it cover private tutors?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and its remit is broader than inspection — Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. It does not license individual tutors; that sits with the MoHRE private tuition work permit. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge, and naming them here describes the system rather than implying endorsement.

faqs.question: Which subjects will I struggle to find locally even in this district?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 marked against the syllabus's own pseudocode conventions rather than Python, and Accounting 0452 on the IGCSE side. On the Diploma side, Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Economics with proper diagram and evaluation coaching, and Theory of Knowledge support. International Baccalaureate students were 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school population in 2024-25 against 37 per cent on UK curricula, which is why DP specialists are thin regionally.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge exam timetable should we be working from?
faqs.answer: The one your school's exams officer issues, and only that one. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. A tutor quoting dates from a generic download may be working from a document that does not apply to your child's centre. UAE candidates sit the June and November series; February/March is India-only.

faqs.question: How will I know in six weeks whether I chose the right tutor?
faqs.answer: By reading marked work for the loss you named at the start. Get the failure mode in writing before the block begins — working not shown on multi-mark questions, an evaluation criterion left empty, command terms answered identically, diagrams unlabelled. Six weeks later, look at the next marked paper or assessment for that same loss specifically. If it has shifted, continue. If not, change the plan or the tutor; a mismatch is common and says nothing about either side.

intro.heading: One grade on the report, four numbers behind it, and only one of them usually needs work
paragraphs: A Middle Years Programme mathematics report shows a grade from 1 to 7. Behind that grade sit four separate criterion levels, each marked out of 8, and they measure genuinely different things. Criterion A is knowing and understanding. Criterion B is investigating patterns. Criterion C is communicating. Criterion D is applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student can be level 7 on A and level 3 on C and receive a middling overall grade that tells a parent almost nothing about what to do next.

That is why a page about an IB MYP Mathematics Tutor in Sharjah has to start with evidence rather than with a sales argument. The first thing worth doing is free: ask the school for the four criterion levels separately, and ask for a recent marked task with the teacher's annotations on it. Those two documents will usually show, in ten minutes, which criterion is dragging the grade and whether the problem is mathematical knowledge, written communication, or the discipline of a sustained investigation.

The pattern we see most often in Sharjah is not what parents expect. Students arrive described as weak at maths and turn out to be competent on criterion A and losing most of their ground on criterion C, where notation, labelled working and the use of correct mathematical forms are assessed. That is a presentation and language problem sitting inside a maths grade, and it responds quickly — often within a term — because the mathematics was never the obstacle.

The second pattern is criterion B. Investigating patterns asks a student to find a general rule, describe it, justify it and, in the higher bands, prove it. It is the criterion schools assess least often during a term and the one that most reliably separates a 5 from a 7. Students who have never been shown what a justification looks like, as opposed to an example, cannot reach the top bands however strong their arithmetic is.

Everything below is organised so a Sharjah family can check progress rather than trust it: what the bands actually ask for, what a twelve-week record should contain, and what you should be able to see by week four. One operational fact first. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and we do not sell home visits in Sharjah or anywhere else in the country; our in-home service exists only in India. Delivery here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with work submitted before each session so the tutor has already read it.

A note on what this page deliberately does not do. It carries no claim about how fast a grade moves, because criterion levels are frequently best-fit judgements across a reporting period and no honest tutor can put a date on one. It quotes no price of ours. Every dirham figure further down is a published market rate attributed to whoever published it, so you can check it yourself before you speak to anybody at all, including us.

subjects.name: Number
subjects.description: Integers, fractions, decimals, ratio, percentage, indices and standard form. Criterion A territory for most students, and the branch where errors are usually arithmetic habits rather than gaps in understanding, which makes them cheap to fix with drilling.

subjects.name: Algebra
subjects.description: Expressions, equations, inequalities, sequences and functions. The extended route adds further manipulation and more demanding rearrangement. This is where criterion C losses concentrate, because students who can solve an equation often cannot set out the steps in acceptable mathematical form.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, transformations, Pythagoras, right-angled trigonometry, perimeter, area and volume, with the extended route reaching non-right-angled triangles. Diagram labelling is assessed under criterion C, and unlabelled diagrams quietly cost marks a student thinks they earned.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Data collection, representation, averages, spread and probability including combined events. The most natural home for criterion D, because a real-life context with real data is easy to construct and hard to fake.

subjects.name: Patterns and generalisation
subjects.description: Not a content branch but the strand criterion B examines: finding a rule, describing it in words and in algebra, testing it and justifying why it holds. Schools assess it in set investigation tasks, often only once or twice a term.

subjects.name: Mathematics, extended route
subjects.description: An additional body of content on top of the standard route, taken by students heading towards Higher Level Analysis and Approaches or a demanding IGCSE tier. Moving onto it late is harder than moving onto it early, which is why the decision belongs in MYP 4.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Generates usable maths evidence that parents overlook: graph plotting, units, significant figures and the processing of experimental data. A student whose science graphs are unlabelled is showing the same criterion C weakness that is costing them in maths.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The design cycle with measurement, tolerance and specification. Strong overlap with criterion D, because a design brief is a real-life context with constraints, and students who handle it well often do better on applied maths than their maths grade suggests.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Data interpretation, population figures, index numbers and graph reading. A useful source of evidence when a student claims to dislike maths but handles quantitative material comfortably in another subject.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project with a process journal and a report. Where mathematics is used in it, the project shows whether a student can select an appropriate method without being told which one to use — which is exactly what criterion D asks.

sections.heading: What the four criteria actually measure, in the language of the bands
paragraphs: The four criteria are not four names for the same thing, and a parent who can state what each one wants is immediately better equipped than one who cannot. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, asks the student to select and apply mathematics to solve problems in both familiar and unfamiliar situations, and the top band requires success in unfamiliar ones. Criterion B, investigating patterns, asks them to select and apply techniques to find a general rule, describe it and, at the top, prove or justify it.

Criterion C, communicating, is the one most often mistaken for neatness. It is not about handwriting. It assesses the use of appropriate mathematical language, the use of different forms of representation, moving between those forms, communicating complete and coherent lines of reasoning, and organising information logically. A student who writes a correct answer with no visible reasoning scores in the lower bands on C while being entirely correct on the mathematics, which is why the overall grade confuses parents.

Criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, asks the student to identify the relevant elements of an authentic situation, select an appropriate strategy, apply it, explain the degree of accuracy of the solution and explain whether the solution makes sense in the context. The last two are where almost all the losses sit. Students solve the problem and stop. The band descriptors want a judgement about the answer, not just the answer.

The practical consequence is that a single overall grade of 5 can mean four completely different situations, and the tutoring that helps differs in each. So the first request to the school is specific: not 'how is she doing in maths' but 'what were her four criterion levels in the last reporting cycle, and may we see a marked task for each'. Schools provide this readily when asked precisely, and it is the cheapest diagnostic available to a Sharjah parent.

sections.heading: Reading your child's own marked task before hiring anybody
paragraphs: A marked Middle Years mathematics task carries more diagnostic information than any conversation, and most parents have never been shown how to read one. Start with the criterion the task was marked against, which is usually printed on the task sheet. A single task is rarely marked against all four; schools assess one or two at a time. Knowing which criterion a task targeted tells you what the level on it does and does not mean.

Then read the annotations rather than the level. Teacher comments on a maths task fall into three recognisable types. Comments about the mathematics itself — a wrong method, a misread question — point to criterion A. Comments about presentation, missing steps, unlabelled axes or notation point to criterion C. Comments asking why, or asking whether the answer is reasonable, point to criterion B or D. A task covered in the third type with correct answers throughout is a very specific and very fixable profile.

Next, compare two tasks a few weeks apart. Movement on criterion A across two tasks is normal progress. Flatness on criterion C across a term, with correct answers in both, means nobody has told the student what the criterion wants. That is the single most common finding, and it is also the reason some students make visible progress within three or four sessions: the mathematics was never the problem, and the fix is a habit rather than a body of knowledge.

Finally, ask one question of the school that parents rarely ask: is this level a single judgement or a best-fit across several tasks. MYP reporting practice varies, and criterion levels are often a best-fit judgement over a reporting period rather than an average. That matters when you are measuring whether tutoring is working, because a best-fit level moves slowly by design and a parent expecting a number to jump in a fortnight will conclude wrongly that nothing is happening.

sections.heading: A twelve-week ledger: what gets marked, what gets recorded, what you see
paragraphs: If progress is going to be judged on evidence then the evidence has to be written down somewhere, and the thing we keep is deliberately boring. Each week has a named criterion focus, a piece of the student's own work that was marked, and one line stating what changed. Over twelve weeks that produces a document a parent can read in two minutes and a school can be shown. It also makes the uncomfortable weeks visible, which is the point: a ledger that only records progress is marketing, not evidence.

The early weeks are deliberately unglamorous. Weeks one and two are diagnosis from the student's existing marked work, with no new content taught at all, because teaching before diagnosis is how a term gets spent on the wrong criterion. Week three is the first intervention on whichever criterion the evidence named. Week four is where a parent should expect to see something: not a grade change, but a before-and-after pair of the student's own solutions with the difference visible to a non-mathematician.

The middle weeks are where criterion B work happens, because investigations need a long uninterrupted block and a run of them to build the habit. By about week eight there should be a student-written justification of a general rule that would have been impossible in week one. That artefact is the clearest single piece of evidence in the whole twelve weeks, and it is worth asking any tutor, including ours, to produce something equivalent before you commit to a second term.

The last weeks turn to whatever the school is assessing next, with timing and method presentation drilled under conditions that match the real task. Then the ledger is read end to end with the parent, and the honest version of that conversation sometimes concludes that weekly tutoring has done its job and a monthly check-in is enough. We would rather say that than extend a block because it is already booked.
