process.title: Say which subject and which component
process.description: The useful first message names the subject, the level, and the component where marks are going, plus the school and whether the commute crosses into Dubai. That is enough to say which fault types are likely and which tutor matches the component rather than the subject label.

process.title: One free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A single sixty-minute session at no charge with the tutor you would keep, before any payment is taken. It is one lesson rather than a trial period, and it is used to set the first timed section and to check the component match is right.

process.title: Two timed sections, marked and categorised
process.description: Your child attempts two timed sections unaided and both are marked against the published scheme. The losses are then sorted into the five fault categories, and the resulting note names the fault to work on first and the weeks it needs.

process.title: A fault-targeted block with a counted outcome
process.description: Six to eight weeks on one named fault, with the fault counted in marked work each week rather than described. The block ends when the fault stops appearing, which is sometimes earlier than the block was booked for, and that shortening is reported rather than absorbed.

process.title: Re-diagnose before renewing
process.description: At the end of a block the scripts are re-categorised. Where the fault has gone, the next one on the list is named. Where it has not, the plan changes instead of continuing: a different match, fewer subjects more intensively, or a recommendation to stop.

whyPoints.title: The fault is named before the hours are sold
whyPoints.description: Two timed sections are marked and categorised before a teaching plan exists. That ordering means a family is sometimes told the gap is content and will take months, which is a less attractive sale than a six-week block and a more accurate one.

whyPoints.title: Progress is counted, not asserted
whyPoints.description: The named fault is counted in marked work each week. A grade is not promised, no point improvement is quoted, and no satisfaction statistic appears anywhere on this page, because none of those could be produced with a method you could check.

whyPoints.title: The schedule is built on the real school run
whyPoints.description: Al Nahda households crossing into Dubai cannot start at 17:00 in term time, and a plan that pretends otherwise collapses in a fortnight. Slot timing is agreed against the actual commute, Ramadan and study leave before any content is planned.

whyPoints.title: The regulator is explained, not borrowed
whyPoints.description: SPEA regulates private education in Sharjah and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is described because it is useful. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from SPEA or any other authority and claims none.

whyPoints.title: The mandatory subjects are treated as a real load
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit alongside the Diploma rather than inside it, and the published rules on separate classes, instructional time and approved content constrain what support can legitimately be. A plan that ignores those hours asks for time the week does not contain.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage are stated up front
whyPoints.description: Sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits in the UAE and no Sharjah centre to attend, and where the right specialist is not free in your window you are told so with a named alternative rather than matched to whoever had the slot.

faqs.question: How do I work out what is actually going wrong before I hire an IB tutor in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Get a marked script rather than a grade and ask four questions of it. Did your child know the content on the questions they lost marks on? Did the answer do what the command term asked? Where on the paper did the marks stop? And in internally assessed work, which criterion is capping the mark? Those four answers separate missing content, which takes months, from command-term drift, timing collapse and unfinished analysis, which are habits and move in weeks. Buying hours before answering them usually buys the wrong product at the right price.

faqs.question: Which of these faults can realistically be fixed in six weeks?
faqs.answer: Three of the five. Command-term misreading usually settles in two to three weeks and then improves every written paper your child sits, not just the one it was diagnosed in. Timing collapse takes a similar window and is fixed by building and rehearsing a question order. Description instead of analysis takes three to four weeks of drilling the final move in isolation. Missing content does not fit in six weeks and should not be sold as if it does. Capped internally assessed structure sits in between and runs alongside other work.

faqs.question: Does SPEA regulate private tutors in Sharjah as well as schools?
faqs.answer: SPEA regulates private education in the emirate and, with Ras Al Khaimah's authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for schools. Individual private tutoring is regulated separately, by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone giving private lessons without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. No tutoring company is approved or accredited by SPEA, and IB Gram claims no such status.

faqs.question: My child is in a Dubai school but we live in Al Nahda. Which regulator matters for us?
faqs.answer: Both, for different things. The school answers to the regulator of the emirate it sits in, so a Dubai school answers to KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education there, while you live under SPEA's jurisdiction for local matters. For tutoring purposes the practical consequence is not regulatory at all, it is timing: the return journey from a Dubai school in term time usually makes 18:00 the earliest workable session slot, and a plan booked for 17:00 will be renegotiated within a fortnight.

faqs.question: How do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect how much tutoring my child can take?
faqs.answer: They reduce the hours available more than families expect. Private schools in the Emirates must include Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed international curriculum rather than instead of part of it, and the published Dubai guidance calculates mandatory instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab groups. A UAE school week is therefore genuinely fuller. A plan assuming four spare weekly hours often has two, and building for two that actually happen beats building for four that do not.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with Arabic if it is one of my child's assessed subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a language acquisition or language A subject within the Diploma, where the work is frequent short productive practice with correction rather than vocabulary revision. Where Arabic is being taken as a mandatory school subject rather than as an IB course, support means practising the school's own assessed tasks using the school's material, because the published guidance prohibits using different or additional content for the mandatory subjects without prior permission from the Ministry. Ask the school which of the two situations applies, since the right support differs.

faqs.question: What does a session look like when the fault is timing rather than knowledge?
faqs.answer: Short and uncomfortable, by design. The candidate attempts a timed section with a visible clock, stops at the bell wherever they are, and the two of you then look at where the marks stopped rather than at whether the answers were right. From that, a question order is built: which questions to attempt first, how many minutes each is worth, what to do with a question that resists after two minutes. Then it is rehearsed weekly until the paper gets finished. Two to three weeks is a normal window.

faqs.question: Will marked evidence from a tutor change the predicted grade my child's school submits?
faqs.answer: No tutor can change a prediction, because it belongs to the school. What marked evidence does is give a teacher material of the kind they produce themselves, which is more likely to prompt a second look than a parent's report of improvement. The timing matters: evidence has to exist before the school's own forecast deadline, so ask the Diploma coordinator when that falls. Anything arriving afterwards has no route into the decision, however good it is.

faqs.question: How many points can my child realistically gain across a Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Nobody can answer that honestly in advance, and a provider who gives you a figure is quoting a sales number. The Diploma is reported out of 45, with up to 7 in each of six subjects and up to 3 from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination, so movement depends on how many marks shift in how many subjects and where the grade boundaries happen to fall. What can be promised is a counted fault, marked scripts and a written statement of what the remaining weeks can address. Confirm the current award conditions with your school's coordinator.

faqs.question: Is one tutor for two Higher Level subjects a good idea or a false economy?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the components are related. Mathematics with Physics is a workable pairing because the techniques overlap and the shared context genuinely helps. Economics with Business Management works for similar reasons. Pairing two subjects with unrelated assessment shapes saves coordination and loses match quality on both, which is the wrong trade at this level. Where the faults differ between the two subjects, two specialists sharing one progress record is the better structure at the same total hours, even though it looks less tidy on an invoice.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do with my child's internal assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Explain what each criterion rewards, discuss a plan, ask questions about the draft your child wrote, and name the criterion a given paragraph is currently failing. What a tutor does not do is supply text, edit a piece to completion or hand over a model to be adapted. Your child chooses the topic, runs the investigation, writes every word and reaches the conclusions. Every version is kept with its date, so if the coordinator asks how the work was supported there is a folder rather than an assurance.

faqs.question: We are on the east coast in Kalba. Is any of this practical for us?
faqs.answer: More practical than it is for a household in the city, in one specific sense: distance stops mattering entirely. Kalba and Khor Fakkan sit under the same regulator as the city but a long way from it, and a visiting arrangement with a Higher Level specialist is not realistic from there at any price. Over video the match is about the component rather than the drive. The scheduling difference is that east coast families usually prefer one longer weekend morning session with marked work midweek, rather than two weekday evening slots.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the sessions for a Diploma candidate in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: School days shorten and the usable window for many households moves to after Iftar, so sessions typically run from around 21:00, shorter and more frequent. For fault-targeted work that is often an improvement, since habits change through repeated correction rather than long exposure. Study leave then inverts the pattern, with mornings becoming the right slot because papers are sat in the morning and practising then is itself rehearsal. We ask which weeks are genuinely available, counting Ramadan, travel and public holidays, before the content plan is written.

faqs.question: What happens if the first month shows no change in the named fault?
faqs.answer: The plan changes rather than renews. Three explanations are worth testing in that order: the fault was misdiagnosed and the scripts need re-categorising, the tutor match is wrong at component level, or the candidate is spread across too many supported subjects to change anything in one. Each has a different remedy, and one of them is to stop and reallocate. A block that is quietly continued after a month of no movement is the most expensive outcome available, which is why re-diagnosis is scheduled rather than offered.

sharjah/ib-tutor.closingHeading: Start with a marked script, not a grade
sharjah/ib-tutor.closingBody: The thing worth doing first is not choosing a tutor. It is getting two timed sections marked and sorted into the five categories on this page, so that the next decision is made against evidence rather than against a number from a report. Send the subject, the level, the component where marks are going, and whether the school run crosses into Dubai. You will get back a categorised list of losses, the fault to work on first, the weeks it needs, and an honest note where the answer is that the gap is content and the plan should be longer than you hoped.

sharjah/ib-tutor-near-me.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach IB subjects to Sharjah students over live video and work from marked evidence rather than from a general sense of how the term is going. Each session produces something you can read afterwards.

intro.heading: The question behind the search is: how will I know?
paragraphs: Four weeks into a tutoring arrangement, most parents cannot answer the only question that matters. The sessions happen. The tutor seems competent. The child says it is helping. The next report is eight weeks away and will arrive too late to act on. Nothing in that picture distinguishes a tutor who is changing the way the student writes under timed conditions from one who is pleasantly going over work the student already understood.

This is not a problem of trust. It is a problem of instrumentation. Tutoring is bought in hours and judged by grades, and the gap between the two is a term long. By the time the signal arrives, the money is spent and the decision about whether to carry on has already been made by default. The families who get the most from tutoring are the ones who set up a way to read the signal early, and who ask for it before the first invoice rather than after the third.

The IB makes the instrumentation available, which is the useful part. Internally assessed work is marked against published criteria, lettered rather than numbered, each with its own band descriptors. That means a draft can be scored before it is submitted, and the score can be compared with the one it got last time. Externally examined papers come back from mocks with annotations. A Middle Years Programme report gives four criterion scores per subject rather than one percentage. All of it is evidence, and most of it goes unexamined.

Searching by proximity does not help with any of this, which is the first thing worth saying about the search itself. A tutor fifteen minutes away and a tutor on the other side of the Gulf produce identical evidence trails or identical silence. Distance decides how you meet. It decides nothing about whether anybody can tell you what changed. In Sharjah specifically, where the pool of people who have actually taught a particular Higher Level subject is modest and a large share of families run a cross-border school commute, insisting on proximity narrows the choice without improving the information.

None of the instruments described here require you to understand the subject. A parent who could not mark a Higher Level Physics paper can still read a criterion descriptor and check whether the last draft met it, still notice that a session note names a mood rather than an error, and still see that the same mistake appears in week two and week ten. The work is in setting the instruments up at the beginning, when nobody is defending anything, rather than in operating them later.

What follows is an audit, in the order you would actually use it: the three documents to ask for up front, the criterion letters behind the marks, how to read a grade against a markband, the draft rule and the trail it should leave, five checkpoints across a Sharjah term, and the point at which the evidence tells you to change the plan rather than buy more of it.

sharjah/ib-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: What counts as evidence depends on which programme your child is in, because the three IB programmes report progress in quite different units. Confusing them is the most common reason a parent misreads a report.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject group is assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, scored 1 to 8, and the four are added to a total out of thirty-two before being converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using boundaries the school publishes in its assessment policy. There is no percentage anywhere in the system. A student can hold a strong total and a weak single criterion, which is precisely the information a tutoring plan needs and precisely what a summary grade hides.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah MYP cohorts include a high proportion of students who transferred in from a British, American or Indian curriculum, where marks arrive as percentages. Those families often read a criterion score of 5 out of 8 as a failure when it is mid-band, and miss the criterion sitting at 2 that is actually dragging the total down.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects each graded 1 to 7, plus up to three points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Most subjects combine externally examined papers with one internally assessed component marked by the teacher against published criteria and then moderated. The evidence a parent can actually inspect is therefore split: mock scripts with annotations on the external side, and criterion-scored drafts on the internal side.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma cohorts in the emirate are smaller than Dubai's, so a student is often one of a handful taking a given Higher Level subject at their school. That makes internal comparison unreliable and makes the criterion descriptors, which are the same everywhere, the only stable reference point a Sharjah family has.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed continuously through portfolios, observation and student reflection rather than by examination, and organised around inquiry rather than subject syllabuses. The evidence here is a portfolio and a conversation, and the useful thing to track is whether a child can explain their own reasoning in writing, since that is the capability the Middle Years Programme will shortly start scoring formally.
programmes.countryNote: Primary enquiries from Sharjah are usually about written explanation rather than content, particularly from families whose child moved into a PYP school from a curriculum where the answer alone earned the mark.

sharjah/ib-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the note names the component where evidence is easiest to collect and the loss pattern that shows up in it. That is what makes a six-week review possible rather than theoretical.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The cleanest evidence is a marked non-calculator paper, because method marks are awarded or withheld visibly. The recurring loss is working that the examiner cannot follow, which is a presentation habit rather than a mathematical weakness and shows measurable change within a month.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Look at the interpretation sentences rather than the calculations. Students produce a correct statistical result and then write nothing about what it means in context, which is where the available marks sit. Count those sentences across two papers and the trend is obvious.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The internal investigation gives the most readable evidence, because uncertainty treatment is either present or absent. On papers, track whether derivation questions are being answered with derivations. Both are countable, which makes them good instruments.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mark the structured questions and count three specific failures: unbalanced equations, missing state symbols, and correct chemistry written in a form the markscheme cannot credit. All three fall quickly once named, and the count is the measurement.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The evidence to collect is whether answers form a causal chain or a list. Take two marked extended-response items and underline the linking words. If there are none, the content is not the problem and revision will not move the grade.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are the fastest evidence in the Diploma: axes labelled, initial equilibrium stated, shift drawn and explained. Then check whether evaluation paragraphs reach a verdict. Both are visible on a photograph of the script.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ratio of analysis to paraphrase, measured by highlighting. A guided analysis that is two-thirds summary cannot reach the upper bands however fluent it reads, and the highlighting makes that visible to a parent in a way a comment does not.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Check whether the named tool is applied to the company in the stimulus or merely described. Count applications per answer across two marked case studies; it is a crude instrument and it works.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Each study cited should be followed by a sentence connecting it to the command term. Count the studies and count the connecting sentences. The gap between those two numbers is usually the whole problem.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay evidence is whether the student is arguing about knowledge or about the topic. A draft that discusses climate science rather than how we know things about climate science is off-task, and that is diagnosable from a single paragraph.

sharjah/ib-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: These notes cover where Sharjah families live and what it does to the practicalities, since the search that brought you here was a proximity search. The academic argument for video delivery comes later on the page.

regions.name: Al Qasimia
regions.note: Central and long settled, with several established schools inside a short radius. Families here often have more than one child at the same campus, which helps with scheduling but means a single bad evening affects both plans at once.

regions.name: Al Zahia
regions.note: Newer housing with a young population and a short run to the Muwaileh school cluster. Enquiries from here are mostly Middle Years Programme, where criterion scores rather than percentages are the evidence to track.

regions.name: Tilal City
regions.note: Set back from the coastal districts with longer drives to the main school corridors. The distance makes a fixed online slot considerably more reliable than any arrangement that depends on someone travelling.

regions.name: Al Suyoh
regions.note: Expanding residential area within reach of the Muwaileh and University City campuses. Afternoon sessions are more workable here than in the districts that feed Dubai schools.

regions.name: Maryam Island
regions.note: Waterfront development close to the Al Majaz and Al Khan districts, with families commuting in both directions across the emirate boundary. Evening slots dominate for the same reason they do in Al Taawun.

regions.name: Al Juraina
regions.note: Established residential district with a mix of Sharjah and Dubai school attendance. Where siblings are split across emirates, two separate tutoring evenings tend to work better than one shared one.

regions.name: Kalba
regions.note: On the east coast beyond the mountain road, where private international provision is limited. Specialist IB support here is realistically only available over video, and that is how it is delivered.

regions.name: Al Ramtha
regions.note: Close to the Wesgreen and Muwaileh campuses, so the school run is short. Families here can use earlier slots, which suits younger Middle Years Programme students who fade after seven o'clock.

schoolClusters.city: Muwaileh, Al Ramtha and University City
schoolClusters.note: Where most of the emirate's international school capacity sits. Programme authorisations and curricula are revised from year to year, so check directly with the school or with SPEA rather than relying on any third-party summary, including this one.

schoolClusters.city: Al Qasimia, Al Majaz and Al Nahda
schoolClusters.note: The older central and border districts, where a substantial share of households hold places at Dubai schools and the family calendar is set by two different emirate frameworks at once.

sharjah/ib-tutor-near-me.modesIntro: Each of the three arrangements below produces a different evidence trail, and it is worth choosing with that in mind rather than on price alone.

modes.title: Weekly slot with a written note
modes.description: A fixed one-to-one session each week on one subject, with a short written note afterwards naming what was covered, what the student got wrong and what they are to do before the next session. Over a term the notes become the record that makes a review possible.
bullets: Same tutor and same time each week
Session built from the most recent marked work
Written note sent after every session
Formal review at six weeks against the stated target

modes.title: Criterion-scored draft review
modes.description: Sessions arranged around an internally assessed piece, in which the student submits work they have written and the tutor returns a criterion-by-criterion score with reasons. The same piece is scored again after the student revises it, so the movement is measured rather than asserted.
bullets: Student writes; tutor scores and explains
Scores recorded against each criterion letter
Second scoring after the student's own revision
Nothing drafted, rewritten or edited by the tutor

modes.title: Timed-paper diagnostic block
modes.description: A short block that opens and closes with the same kind of timed paper under the same conditions, with the sessions in between spent on whatever the first attempt exposed. The comparison at the end is the deliverable, and it is a comparison rather than an impression.
bullets: Baseline attempt marked before any teaching
Four to eight sessions on the exposed weakness
Closing attempt under identical conditions
Both scripts returned to the family

sections.heading: What a proximity search returns, and what it leaves you unable to check
paragraphs: A search for an IB tutor near me in Sharjah returns a list sorted by distance from a point. That sorting tells you who can reach your district and nothing else. It does not tell you whether anyone on the list has taught the Higher Level course your child is taking, whether they can score a draft against the published criteria, or whether they will put anything in writing. Those are the three things that determine the outcome, and none of them is correlated with how close somebody lives.

The distance filter also actively costs you something in this emirate. Sharjah has fewer Diploma cohorts than Dubai, so for any given Higher Level subject the number of people locally who have taught it to IB candidates is small. Filtering that already-small group by driving distance from your villa can reduce it to nobody. Families then take the nearest person who covers the subject in general, which is how an examination-year student ends up with a tutor learning the course alongside them.

The useful substitute for the distance filter is a document filter. Ask for three things before any money changes hands, and judge the answers rather than the proximity. The table below sets out what each document proves, which matters because each one has a limit, and a tutor who offers only the first is offering the least informative of the three.

None of this requires expertise in the subject. A parent who cannot mark a Physics paper can still read a criterion descriptor, still check that a session note names a specific error rather than a general attitude, and still notice that the same weakness appears in week two and week ten.

sections.heading: Criterion letters: the marks behind the mark
paragraphs: Internally assessed IB work is not marked out of a hundred. It is marked against criteria identified by letter, each with its own band descriptors and its own maximum, and the letters are the single most useful piece of information a parent can learn to read. A Middle Years Programme subject reports four of them per subject per reporting cycle. A Diploma internal assessment is scored against a published set specific to the subject.

The practical value is that criteria separate problems that a single grade merges. A student scoring well on knowledge and understanding and poorly on the criterion covering analysis or evaluation has a technique gap, which is fixable in weeks. A student scoring uniformly in the middle of every band has a different and slower problem. Those two students receive the same overall grade and need entirely different plans, and no amount of looking at the grade will distinguish them.

It also gives a tutor something honest to be measured against. If the agreed target is the criterion covering critical thinking, then the deliverable at six weeks is a draft scoring higher on that criterion, with the reasoning written down. That is a claim that can be checked. Compare it with the usual alternative, which is a tutor reporting that the student is more confident.

The table below maps the internally assessed work by subject area to what each criterion family actually rewards. The exact letters, names and maxima differ by subject and are revised periodically, so take the authoritative version from the subject guide or assessment policy your school holds and use this as the orientation rather than the reference.

sections.heading: Reading a 1 to 7 against a markband rather than against a percentage
paragraphs: Families arriving from percentage-based systems read a 5 as a middling result, because 5 out of 7 looks like seventy per cent. It is not a percentage and the conversion does not work that way. The 1 to 7 scale reports a band of performance described in words, and the distance between adjacent bands is not uniform. Moving from a 4 to a 5 is a different quantity of work from moving a 6 to a 7, and in most subjects the second is considerably harder.

This matters when a target is being set. A parent who asks for a 7 in a Higher Level subject that is currently a 4, eight weeks before final papers, is asking for something no tutor should promise. A parent who asks what the markband above the current one actually requires, and whether the student's last script showed any of it, is asking a question with a usable answer. The first conversation produces a sales pitch. The second produces a plan.

There is a further wrinkle specific to internally assessed work. The criterion score a teacher awards is subject to moderation by the IB, which can move a cohort's marks in either direction. A draft scored generously in November is not a result. It is a working estimate, and the honest way to use it is as a comparison against the same student's earlier draft rather than as a prediction of the final grade.

The one number that is genuinely informative early is the gap between a student's performance on internally assessed work and on timed papers. A large gap in either direction tells you where the hours should go, and it is visible by the end of the first term of DP1.

sections.heading: What a marked script shows that a Sharjah school report cannot
paragraphs: School reports are written to a template and describe a student across a reporting period. They are useful for what they are, and they are structurally incapable of telling you where marks went. A report says a student needs to develop evaluative skills. A marked script shows the exact sentence where the evaluation stopped and the mark was not awarded. One of those can be acted on this week.

There is also a timing problem. Sharjah schools report on their own cycle, which for families with children in both Sharjah and Dubai means two cycles that do not align. By the time a report confirms a problem, a term of sessions has already been bought. The script is available continuously and costs nothing.

Getting hold of scripts is easier than parents assume. Schools return mock papers, and most will let a student photograph an internally marked piece. Four marked artefacts across a term is enough to see a pattern, and a pattern is what a tutor should be working against. Where nothing is available, a tutor can set a timed past question in the first session and mark it, which creates the baseline that was missing.

What to look for does not require subject knowledge. Are the lost marks clustered at the end of the paper, which is a timing problem? Are they spread evenly through the extended-response questions, which is usually a command-term problem? Are they concentrated in one topic, which is a content gap? Those three patterns point at three different plans, and distinguishing them is the whole value of looking.
bullets: Losses clustered at the end of the paper point to timing
Losses spread across extended answers point to command terms
Losses in one topic point to a content gap the school can help close
Losses on presentation and working point to habit, which moves fastest

sections.heading: The draft rule, and the trail a legitimate feedback process leaves
paragraphs: Coursework is where tutoring is most valuable and most abused. A student's internally assessed work has to be their own, and the IB treats breaches as malpractice with consequences that land on the candidate. A family buying coursework help should therefore be interested not only in whether it works but in what trail it leaves, because the trail is what protects the student if the question is ever asked.

A legitimate process looks like this. The student produces work. The tutor reads it and returns written feedback that names criteria and asks questions. The student revises it themselves. The tutor scores the revision. Every stage is dated, the student's own versions are kept, and the feedback is identifiable as feedback rather than as text that has migrated into the submission. Keep all of it in one folder.

What that process never includes is the tutor writing, rewriting, restructuring or editing the work to completion, supplying the research question, or producing a model answer for the student to adapt. Those are not cautious policies; they are the line itself. A service that offers a finished investigation is selling a risk and charging for it.

The table below sets out the stages and who does what at each. It is worth agreeing this explicitly at the start, because the pressure to cross the line arrives late at night four days before a deadline, and the right time to have settled it is months earlier.

sections.heading: Five checkpoints across a Sharjah term
paragraphs: A term is long enough to waste and short enough to run out. Setting checkpoints at the start, with a named artefact at each, turns a vague arrangement into something that can be judged halfway through rather than at the end. The dates below follow the rhythm of a typical Sharjah academic year rather than any particular school's calendar, so adjust them to your own.

The principle behind each checkpoint is that something physical must exist. Not a conversation about how it is going, which will always be positive, but a document: a marked baseline, a scored draft, a second attempt at the same kind of paper. If the artefact does not exist on the agreed date, that is itself the finding, and it is a more useful finding than any verbal reassurance.

The second principle is that the review happens whether or not anybody is worried. A review scheduled only when a parent becomes uneasy arrives late and feels adversarial. One scheduled in week one is routine, and both sides prepare for it. It is also the moment to change the plan without anybody feeling that a judgement has been passed.

The last checkpoint matters most and is skipped most often. At the end of the term the question is not whether to continue but whether to continue with the same target. A problem that has been fixed should release the hours to something else, and a problem that has not moved in twelve weeks is unlikely to move in the next twelve under the same plan.

sections.heading: Why the nearest specialist is usually in another emirate, and why that stops mattering
paragraphs: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Sessions for Sharjah families are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. On a page answering a proximity search, that deserves an argument rather than an announcement.

The argument begins with supply. The emirate's Diploma cohorts are smaller than Dubai's, and the number of people who have taught a specific Higher Level subject to IB candidates and happen to live near your district is correspondingly small. The search that brought you here sorts by distance, which puts that constraint at the top of the list of things deciding your child's tutor. Sorting by component instead puts the thing that affects the grade at the top.

Then there is the Sharjah evening. A substantial share of households here run a daily crossing into Dubai for school, and the inbound journey in the late afternoon is the least predictable hour of the week. Any arrangement that depends on a second person also completing a journey inherits that unpredictability twice over. A video session starts when the clock says so, which over a term is worth more than it sounds.

The last part of the argument is the one this whole page is about. A video session produces a shared whiteboard, an annotated script and a written note. A session in a living room produces whatever ends up on paper and a general impression. For a parent trying to answer the question of whether this is working, the first is evidence and the second is not, and that difference has nothing to do with the tutor's ability.

sections.heading: When the evidence says change the plan rather than buy more hours
paragraphs: The hardest thing a tutoring arrangement has to do is end at the right time. Most do not, because continuing is the default and nobody wants to have the conversation. Setting the review point early makes the conversation routine, but it still needs a rule for what the answer means, and the rule is worth writing down before anybody is invested.

Three patterns justify stopping or changing. If the targeted problem has not moved after six weeks of weekly sessions with work completed between them, the plan is wrong; more of it will not help, and either the target or the tutor should change. If the student's difficulty turns out to be attendance, sleep, anxiety or something else outside the academic question, another academic hour is the wrong purchase and will make the week worse. If the subject itself is the problem in DP1, the conversation belongs with the school's Diploma coordinator, because a level change may be the better answer than any amount of support.

There is a fourth, happier pattern. Sometimes the problem is genuinely fixed in eight sessions, and the right move is to stop rather than to roll the slot into something vaguer. Hours released from a solved problem are worth more spent on the next one, and a tutor who says the work is done has told you something useful about how they operate.

What none of these decisions should rest on is how the sessions felt. Felt is the least reliable instrument available and it points in the same direction almost regardless of what is happening, which is why the folder exists.
bullets: No movement in six weeks means the plan changes, not the hours
A non-academic cause is not treated by academic hours
A level decision in DP1 belongs with the school's coordinator

sections.heading: Getting started, and the first three sessions
paragraphs: You send the subject, the level, the programme year and whatever marked work exists. We match a tutor who teaches that component and arrange a free trial lesson over live video, with no card details taken beforehand. If no one suitable is free at the time you need, we say so and give a realistic date rather than substituting a general tutor into an examination-year subject.

The first session establishes the baseline. If marked work was sent, it is read and worked through; if not, a timed past question is set and marked. By the end of it there should be a named target component and a stated reason for choosing it. The second session works on that target and produces the first written note. The third repeats it, and by then you can see whether the notes are naming specific errors or describing the weather.

From there the checkpoints above take over. Week six is the first real decision point, and it is an easier decision because the baseline from session one is sitting in the folder to compare against. Families who skip the baseline almost always end up arguing about memory instead of looking at paper.

If you want to see how the same approach reads elsewhere in the country before committing, the equivalent pages for Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain cover the same ground with the local detail changed.

process.title: Send the component and one artefact
process.description: The subject, the level, the programme year, and one piece of marked work. That is enough to match a tutor to the actual problem. A long description of how the term has been going is less useful than a photograph of a script with an examiner's marks on it.

process.title: Agree the target and the review date
process.description: Before the first paid session, name the component being targeted and the date on which the plan will be judged. Six weeks is a reasonable first point. Agreeing it early makes the review routine rather than a complaint, and it makes changing course easy.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full one-to-one session over live video with the matched tutor, with no card details taken first. The useful test is whether the tutor can name, at the end, a specific thing that is costing marks and a specific plan for the following month.

process.title: Collect the notes in one place
process.description: Keep every session note, every draft and every marked script in a single folder, dated. It takes no effort during the term and it is the entire basis of the review at the end of it. It also protects the student if the authorship of coursework is ever questioned.

process.title: Review against the baseline, not against memory
process.description: At six weeks, compare a second attempt at the baseline task with the first. The comparison is the finding. If nothing has moved, change the target or the tutor rather than adding sessions to a plan that is already not working.

whyPoints.title: Everything is written down
whyPoints.description: A note after each session naming what was worked on, what went wrong and what the student is to do next. It is the only instrument available to a parent who was not in the room, and it costs nothing to insist on from the first week.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-referenced, not impressionistic
whyPoints.description: Internally assessed work is scored against the published criteria and the score is explained, so movement can be compared between drafts instead of described. That makes a six-week review a measurement rather than a conversation about confidence.

whyPoints.title: A review date set in advance
whyPoints.description: The plan is judged on an agreed date whether or not anyone is worried. Reviews that happen only when a parent becomes uneasy arrive late and feel adversarial, and by then a term of hours has usually been spent.

whyPoints.title: A boundary stated to the student
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on work the student has written, and the student is told this in the first session. The pressure to cross that line arrives days before a deadline, and the time to have settled it is months earlier.

whyPoints.title: Matched by component, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: Sessions run over live video, so the choice is not limited to the people who can drive to your district. In an emirate with modest Diploma cohorts, that is what makes a genuine Higher Level specialist available at all.

faqs.question: Does it matter that my IB tutor is not physically near us in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: For the things that decide the grade, no. A session consists of marked work, a worked solution and a conversation about why a mark was not awarded, and all three move to a shared screen without losing anything. What proximity costs you here is choice: the number of people who have taught a specific Higher Level course and live near your district is small, and filtering by distance can leave nobody. The evidence trail a tutor produces is identical whether they are fifteen minutes away or in another time zone.

faqs.question: What should a session note actually say for me to trust it?
faqs.answer: It should name a specific error, a specific cause and a specific next step. Something like: lost four marks across two evaluation questions by not reaching a judgement, practised writing the verdict sentence first, three past questions to complete before Thursday. What it should not say is that the student worked hard and is growing in confidence, which is true of almost every session and tells you nothing. Ask to see an anonymised example before you commit, and judge the level of detail rather than the tone.

faqs.question: How do criterion letters work in the Middle Years Programme, and why does my child have no percentage?
faqs.answer: Each subject group is assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, scored 1 to 8, and the four are added to a total out of thirty-two which is then converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using boundaries your school publishes in its assessment policy. There is no percentage in the system at any point. The value of the letters is that they separate problems a single grade merges: a strong total with one criterion at 2 is a different situation from a flat score across all four, and the two need different plans.

faqs.question: Can I ask a tutor to score my child's internal assessment draft before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most useful things to buy. The criteria and their descriptors are published, so a draft can be scored against them and the reasons explained. What the tutor must not do is change the document: no writing, rewriting, restructuring or editing to completion, and no supplying the research question. The student revises their own work, the tutor scores it again, and the comparison between the two scores is the evidence that the hours did something. Keep both versions, dated.

faqs.question: My child has a 4 in a Higher Level subject and wants a 7. Is that realistic in one term?
faqs.answer: It is not something any tutor should promise, and a tutor who does has told you something about how they operate. The 1 to 7 scale is not a percentage and the bands are not evenly spaced; moving a 6 to a 7 is far harder than moving a 4 to a 5. The useful version of the question is what the markband above the current one actually requires and whether the last script showed any sign of it. That has an answer, and the answer produces a plan rather than a sales pitch.

faqs.question: How many marked scripts do I need before a pattern is visible?
faqs.answer: Four across a term is usually enough, and two is often enough to see the obvious. What you are looking for is where the lost marks cluster. Losses at the end of the paper point to timing. Losses spread across the extended-response questions point to command terms. Losses concentrated in one topic point to a content gap, which is the school's work more than a tutor's. Losses on working and presentation point to habit, which moves fastest of all. You do not need subject knowledge to see any of this.

faqs.question: What happens if nothing has improved after six weeks of sessions?
faqs.answer: The plan changes. If the targeted problem has not moved in six weeks of weekly sessions with the work completed in between, buying more of the same is unlikely to help, and either the target or the tutor should change. Occasionally the finding is different again: the real difficulty is attendance, sleep or anxiety rather than the subject, in which case another academic hour makes the week worse rather than better. The reason the baseline from session one matters is that it makes this decision a comparison rather than an argument.

faqs.question: Will a tutor talk to my child's school in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Only with your agreement, and in practice it is rarely necessary. What is useful is that the tutor works to the school's own assessment calendar and to the criteria the school is using, which means asking you for the dates and the assessment policy rather than contacting anybody. Where a decision involves subject level or a predicted grade, that conversation belongs between you and the school's programme coordinator. A tutor can tell you what the evidence shows; the school holds the decision.

faqs.question: Is a predicted grade a reliable measure of where my child actually is?
faqs.answer: It is a professional judgement from the evidence available at the time, produced mainly for university applications, and it moves in both directions before final results. Where internally assessed work is unfinished, a prediction is partly a forecast of effort rather than a measurement. Treat it as a signal about where attention is needed, not as a reading. The more informative early number is the gap between how a student performs on internally assessed work and on timed papers, which tells you where the hours should go.

faqs.question: We live in Al Nahda and our children are at schools in two different emirates. How should we schedule?
faqs.answer: Usually as two separate plans on two separate evenings, rather than one shared slot. Schools in Sharjah and Dubai report on different cycles and run different term dates, so a single arrangement built around one child's calendar fits the other badly. The second point is to pick each slot from the worst traffic week rather than the best one: the late-afternoon crossing is unpredictable enough that an early slot will slip, and a session that keeps moving stops working as a fixed point in the week.

faqs.question: Do you keep anything after the tutoring ends?
faqs.answer: You keep the folder, which is the part that matters: the baseline, the session notes, the drafts in the student's own versions, and the scored comparisons. That record is useful beyond the tutoring itself. It is what lets you brief the next tutor in five minutes instead of starting again, it is what makes a conversation with the school concrete, and it is what demonstrates authorship of coursework if that is ever questioned. Keep it in one place and keep everything dated.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with Theory of Knowledge, or is that only the school's job?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help, and the help is mostly about staying on task. The commonest failure in a Theory of Knowledge essay is arguing about the topic rather than about how we come to know things about it, and that is diagnosable from a single paragraph. A tutor can read the student's own draft, point at where the argument slipped from knowledge to subject matter, and ask the questions that pull it back. The student writes it. The prescribed title and the school's internal deadlines come from the school.

faqs.question: How long before final exams is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: It is rarely too late to improve technique and frequently too late to close content gaps, and the honest answer depends on which one you have. Six weeks out, a student losing marks to command terms or timing can still make real gains, because those habits change quickly. A student with four subjects two grades below target does not have a problem that more hours solve; they have a triage problem, and the useful conversation is about which two subjects to protect. A tutor whose answer is always more tutoring is not giving advice.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson tell me that a phone call would not?
faqs.answer: Whether the tutor can diagnose. A call establishes manner and availability. A full session over live video with the actual marked work in front of them shows whether they can look at a script and name what is costing marks, and whether they can explain it to your child in a way the child can repeat afterwards. At the end you should be able to write down one sentence about the problem and one about the plan. If you cannot, that is the result of the trial, and no money has been taken.

faqs.question: Are Sharjah schools and tutors regulated by the same body?
faqs.answer: No, and the distinction matters. Private schools in the emirate are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education and approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods for the schools it oversees. Individual private tutors sit under a different route: a private tuition work permit through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. No tutoring service should describe itself as approved by a schools regulator, and IB Gram does not.

sharjah/ib-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Set the review date before the first invoice
sharjah/ib-tutor-near-me.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB tutor near me in Sharjah, the single change that most improves the outcome has nothing to do with distance. Name the component being targeted, collect one piece of marked work as a baseline, and fix the date on which the plan will be judged, all before any money is spent. Send us the subject, the level and the artefact, and we will match a tutor who teaches that component and arrange a free trial lesson over live video. If we cannot cover it properly, we will say so and tell you when we can.

intro.heading: The number in the quote is mostly about distance
paragraphs: An in-home tutoring quote in Sharjah is three things bundled into one hourly figure: the teaching, the travel, and the risk that the traffic makes the journey longer than planned. Parents see one number and compare it against another number, which is why the market looks confusing. Published UAE rates run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the student-tutor end to AED 650 at the named-examiner end, and most of that spread has nothing to do with how well the person knows Cambridge 0580.

The second thing in the quote is the size of the pool it was drawn from. A parent in Tilal City asking for someone who can teach Extended chemistry on a Tuesday at 17:00 is not choosing between every good chemistry teacher in the UAE. They are choosing between the ones who can reach Tilal City by 17:00 and still get home. That filter is applied before any question about teaching quality, and it is the single biggest reason in-home matching produces a generalist at a specialist rate.

The third thing is what actually arrives. A 60-minute slot where the tutor leaves at 16:20 to beat the Maliha Road queue and arrives at 17:10 is not a 60-minute lesson, and nobody writes that down. Families on the Sharjah-Dubai corridor know the pattern: the session shortens quietly over a term, the tutor starts rescheduling, and the arrangement ends without anyone deciding to end it. The parent is rarely told that the reason is the road rather than the child, so the next tutor is hired on the same terms and the same thing happens again in a different living room.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Sharjah address. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and that is stated the same way on every country page on this site rather than buried here. For UAE families the lesson is one-to-one over live video, at the hour it was booked for, with a shared screen and a shared document. The trade is simple and worth stating plainly: you give up a person in the room, and you get a person who has taught the exact paper your child is entered for.

The rest of this page is the arithmetic rather than the argument. What the market charges by tier and format, what a monthly package usually contains, what the permit position is for anyone you hire privately, which cheaper options are worth trying before paying for one-to-one hours at all, and how the Sharjah week and Ramadan change when sessions can realistically happen. Every AED figure here is attributed to whoever published it, and none of them is our price list. Where the cheaper option is the right one, it is named before the expensive one, because a parent who has not asked the school what support is already inside the fee may be paying for an hour that was available at three in the afternoon for nothing.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Sharjah schools licensed by the Sharjah Private Education Authority run several routes to a 16-plus qualification, and the route changes both the hours a subject needs and what a tutor can usefully do in them.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of teaching assessed at the end by externally marked papers. Mathematics and the separate sciences are tiered into Core and Extended, and the tier the school enters a candidate for changes what hours are worth buying: on the Core route the Extended-only topics are not examined, so paying to teach them is money spent on content that will not be tested.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a timetable per zone, cautioning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong version. Before you commit to a block of sessions timed around a series, ask the Sharjah school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in and work from that timetable.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Graded 9-1 and untiered in most subjects, which means no ceiling is set by the entry and no hours are wasted on content outside the paper. Mathematics A is tiered into Foundation and Higher. Practical skills are examined inside the written papers rather than in a separate component, so revision hours go into written method and data handling.
programmes.countryNote: Two series a year, in May/June and November, changes the economics of a block of sessions. A Sharjah family facing a disappointing June grade can plan a November resit a few months later rather than funding a repeat year. The November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Some schools in the emirate sit Cambridge O Level rather than IGCSE in particular subjects, and the two are not interchangeable in revision terms even where the content overlaps. Cambridge runs O Level in the same June and November series as IGCSE, so the entry deadlines and the timetable logic are identical.
programmes.countryNote: If a Sharjah school's entries mix O Level and IGCSE across a candidate's subjects, the statement of entry will show it and a tutor needs to know which is which. Paying for IGCSE past papers to prepare an O Level entry is a quiet waste of an hour a week.

programmes.name: Post-16 routes after IGCSE
programmes.description: Sharjah IGCSE leavers go on to International A Levels, the IB Diploma, or a school's own post-16 programme, often moving to a different school and sometimes to a different emirate. Each route assumes content from the harder tier, which is why the tier decision in Year 10 has a price attached two years later.
programmes.countryNote: For budgeting, this is the argument for spending on the Extended or Higher tier content in Year 11 rather than economising. A student who arrives at Higher Level sciences without the Extended foundations needs catch-up hours in Year 12 at a higher specialist rate, which costs more than the Year 11 sessions would have.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Subjects differ in how many hours they typically absorb, and in whether those hours buy content or technique. That is the figure to weigh against a rate, rather than the rate on its own.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The highest-volume request in the emirate and usually the best value per hour, because most of the lost marks sit in a short list of Extended topics plus the discipline of showing method. A defined topic list can be worked through in a countable number of sessions, which makes the spend predictable.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two equally weighted calculator papers, so breadth matters more than depth and revision hours spread across the specification rather than concentrating. Ratio, proportional reasoning and the long unstructured questions at the end of each paper absorb the most time.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Hours divide into calculation technique, which is drillable, and organic pathways, which need repetition over weeks. Families who book a short block for chemistry usually get the calculation marks and should expect the pathway work to run longer.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The cheapest marks in the subject sit in the practical component, because students prepare for it last and it rewards knowing how a method is written rather than new content. A block of four to six sessions aimed only at that paper often moves more marks than a term of general physics.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content-heavy rather than conceptually hard, so hours go into definitions, data interpretation and structuring extended answers. This is the subject where independent work between sessions changes the cost most, because the recall can be done without a tutor present.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Marking is the expensive part. Progress comes from a tutor reading and annotating full responses against the published criteria, which takes time outside the session, so ask whether marking is included in the hourly rate or charged separately.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus case is the whole grade, and it is a technique rather than a body of knowledge. Short blocks work well here: four sessions of marked case-study practice shifts more than a term of content revision.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455
subjects.description: Diagram work and evaluation paragraphs are the two cost centres. Students who can draw a diagram but not use it in an argument need modelling rather than content, which is quick; students missing the micro foundations need longer.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Unusually predictable in hours. Binary and data representation, trace tables and pseudocode discipline account for most lost marks and each is drillable, so a tutor should be able to quote a realistic session count at the start.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Untiered, so no hours are spent on content outside the paper and the full 9-1 range stays open. Equation selection, unit conversion and the longer written explanations absorb the time, particularly for students arriving from a tiered Cambridge course.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: A narrow specialism and the subject where Sharjah availability is thinnest at short notice. Budget for a longer search and expect a specialist rate rather than a general maths rate, because the calculus and trigonometric identity work needs someone who teaches it regularly.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, so this runs alongside an IGCSE timetable rather than inside it. Hours here are usually about keeping a mandatory subject from eating revision time, not about a target grade.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Travel time is the hidden line in every in-home quote, and in Sharjah it varies more by hour than by distance. These are the areas IGCSE enquiries come from, with what the journey does to a weekday session.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Pressed against the Dubai border, with a heavy share of children at Al Qusais and Mirdif schools. A visiting tutor crossing at 16:30 can lose 40 minutes each way, and that cost sits inside whatever hourly figure gets quoted.

regions.name: Al Taawun
regions.note: Short distances, unpredictable timings. Journeys here fail by minutes rather than by miles, so an arrangement that cannot absorb a half-hour shift tends not to survive a term.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Lagoon-side apartment blocks where parking is the specific obstacle for a visiting tutor. Families here are often the first to try a video slot simply because the logistics are easier.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: A schools cluster, so journeys are short but pick-up congestion is concentrated into a narrow window. A 16:30 start works; a 15:45 start rarely does.

regions.name: Tilal City
regions.note: Newer villa plots on the southern side where in-home rates come in higher because the journey is long in both directions. This is where the distance premium in a quote is most visible.

regions.name: Al Suyoh
regions.note: Expanding residential land with limited nearby schooling, so children travel further to school and arrive home later. Sessions here work better after 18:00 or at the weekend.

regions.name: Al Rahmaniya
regions.note: Villa communities with a long run to the central Sharjah schools. Families often ask for two subjects on one evening, which usually works less well than two shorter sessions on separate days.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan
regions.note: On the east coast, where the in-home tutoring market thins out almost completely and a visiting tutor from the city is not a realistic weekly arrangement. Live video removes the geography entirely.

schoolClusters.note: Schools with large Year 10 and Year 11 cohorts sitting Cambridge or Pearson papers. Enquiries from these families are usually about a specific subject and a specific tier rather than about general support, and they come with marked work attached.

schoolClusters.city: Central and northern Sharjah
schoolClusters.note: Long-established private schools near the old city and the lagoon, with mixed curricula and some O Level entries alongside IGCSE. Price sensitivity is highest in this group, which makes the cheaper options worth exhausting first.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs in this market, in AED
paragraphs: Nobody ranking for this search publishes a rate table, which is why parents in Sharjah end up phoning five providers to build one. The figures below are the published rates of named UAE providers, with the tier each belongs to. They are the market, not our price list, and they are useful mainly as a sanity check: a quote well outside these bands needs explaining before it is accepted.

At the bottom of the market, EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. At those rates the tutor is typically a university student or an early-career teacher, which can be entirely adequate for Year 9 consolidation and is not adequate for Extended chemistry eight weeks before a series. The middle band, a qualified subject tutor working online, runs roughly AED 150-300; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200.

In-home one-to-one sits higher because the travel is inside the number. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home sessions at roughly AED 180-350, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500. Specialist IGCSE, IB and A-Level tutors are quoted at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and the premium end reaches AED 650, where BartyED sits. The whole spread is a factor of nearly twenty, and most families are choosing inside the middle third of it.

Two warnings go with any table like this. First, these figures were published by the providers named and carry their framing, not ours; rates change and should be checked at source. Second, an hourly rate is not a cost. Six sessions of a specialist at AED 300 that close a named gap is cheaper than a term of AED 100 sessions that do not, and that comparison is the only one worth making.

sections.heading: The travel arithmetic hidden inside an in-home quote
paragraphs: Take a tutor living in central Sharjah and a family in Tilal City. The drive is 25 minutes at 11:00 and can be 45 at 17:00, each way. For a 60-minute session the tutor is committing somewhere between two and two and a half hours. That is why in-home rates sit above online rates: the second hour is being paid for whether or not anyone mentions it. The honest version of an in-home quote is an hourly rate for the teaching plus an unwritten fee for the road.

The consequence is not only financial. A tutor with three in-home clients in one evening has to fit them geographically rather than pedagogically, which is why in-home slots are offered as take-it-or-leave-it times. Families in Al Suyoh and Al Rahmaniya hear this most: the only slot available is the one that fits the route, not the one that fits the student's energy or the school bus.

It also sets a hard limit on who is available at all. A specialist in Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 may live in Dubai, in Abu Dhabi, or outside the country. For an in-home arrangement that person is simply not an option, however well they teach the subject. The parent is left choosing between a general maths tutor who can drive to the villa and no tutor at all, and the choice is usually made without anyone naming it.

On the east coast the arithmetic stops working entirely. A weekly drive to Khor Fakkan or Kalba from the city is not a sustainable commitment at any sensible rate, which is why families there have historically had the thinnest options in the emirate. Removing the journey is the only thing that changes that, and it changes it completely: the same shortlist becomes available on the coast as on the corniche.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context for a Sharjah family
paragraphs: An hourly rate means little without the annual picture. School fees are the dominant number in any UAE education budget, and the tutoring decision is usually a small percentage change on top of a fee that was already set. Worth knowing for context: the Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Fees in Sharjah are approved by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for the emirate.

Against that, weekly tutoring in one subject is a known quantity. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Two subjects doubles it. A short exam-season intensive concentrates the same money into six weeks rather than spreading it over a year, which is often the better purchase for a Year 11 student and a worse one for a Year 9.

There is a cost most families forget: entry fees if a candidate sits a paper privately rather than through their school. A resit arranged outside the school's entry is paid for separately and booked through a centre, with its own deadlines. Before planning a November resit as the cheap option, ask the school whether it will enter the candidate and what that costs, because the answer changes the budget more than the tutoring rate does.

The useful habit is to decide the total before choosing the rate. A family that knows it can spend a fixed amount this term can ask a sensible question: what is the best use of this budget? Sometimes the answer is twelve sessions in one subject. Sometimes it is four diagnostic sessions and a reallocation. It is almost never thirty sessions spread thinly across four subjects, which is the pattern panic produces.

sections.heading: Hiring privately in Sharjah: the permit and the questions
paragraphs: If you engage a tutor directly rather than through a platform, you are the one checking the paperwork. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

Two details are worth holding onto. The permit costs nothing, so a tutor charging you for the administrative cost of holding one is charging for air. And no fine schedule has been published: a figure circulating online as the penalty could not be verified, so treat any specific amount quoted at you as unverified. The official application route is MoHRE's own service, "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a stated completion time of two working days.

There is one arrangement to avoid regardless of paperwork. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. Treat the ADEK detail as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document, but the direction is clear: paying your child's own class teacher for private lessons is the arrangement most likely to create a problem for everyone, including the child.

Beyond the permit, the questions that actually predict a good term are mundane. What have you taught of this exact paper? What will you send me after each session? What happens if we cancel? Is marking of full papers included? What would make you tell me to stop paying for this? A tutor who answers all five crisply is usually worth more than one who answers none of them and quotes less.

sections.heading: Cheaper things to try before buying one-to-one hours
paragraphs: One-to-one tutoring is the most expensive intervention available, and for a reasonable number of Sharjah students it is not the first one needed. Schools licensed by the Sharjah Private Education Authority generally run subject clinics, catch-up sessions or departmental support, and those are already paid for inside the fee. A parent who has not asked the head of department what support exists is often paying for an hour that was available free at 15:00.

Past papers and mark schemes are published by the awarding bodies on their own sites, and a student who works through them with the mark scheme beside them picks up a surprising amount of the technique a tutor would otherwise teach. We reference and link those official sources rather than reproducing them, because reproducing an awarding body's papers or mark schemes is a copyright matter. The point for a budget is that the raw material costs nothing.

Group teaching is the middle option. A small group at a tuition centre divides the hour between students and the rate per student falls accordingly, which suits consolidation and does not suit a student who needs the pace set to them. Where a group works, it works well for the price; where the student's problem is specific, the group's pace becomes the problem.

Where one-to-one is genuinely the right purchase is narrow and recognisable: a named gap that classroom teaching keeps missing, a tier or entry decision that needs expert input, a component paper nobody has taught properly, or an exam-season technique problem with a deadline attached. If your situation is one of those, buy the hours. If it is not, the diagnostic block is the honest first spend.
