sections.heading: The Sharjah week, Ramadan and when sessions can actually happen
paragraphs: A tutoring plan that ignores the shape of the local week fails quietly. Sharjah's school week and the Dubai commute together compress the usable evening into a narrow band, and the band is different for a child at a school five minutes away in Muwaileh and a child crossing to Al Qusais from Al Nahda. The first can start at 16:00; the second often cannot start honestly before 18:00. Booking the wrong one produces a tired student and a cancelled session on the third week.

Ramadan changes it again. School hours shorten, family routines move towards the evening, and the sensible pattern for many households is sessions after Iftar or earlier in the afternoon rather than in the late-afternoon slot that works the rest of the year. Families who plan this in advance keep continuity through the month; families who do not usually lose three or four weeks and then try to buy them back closer to the series at a worse rate.

The academic calendar matters as much as the daily one. Mock examinations, school internal deadlines and the entry deadlines for a series all land before the papers do, and the useful tutoring weeks are the ones before those milestones rather than after. A block booked immediately after mock results is reacting; a block booked eight weeks before them is preparing, and costs the same.

Travel disrupts the rest. Families moving between Sharjah and another country during school holidays can keep a video slot running from wherever they are, with the hour adjusted for the time difference. That continuity is worth real money in an exam year: the alternative is pausing in December, resuming in January and paying to recover ground that was never lost in the first place.

sections.heading: Why we deliver this on live video rather than at your address
paragraphs: This is the part of the page that needs saying without hedging. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and that position is stated identically on every country page on the site. The search term you used is the phrase parents type, and it describes a real market with real prices, set out above. What we sell into that market is a one-to-one lesson over live video.

The case for it is not that video is as good as a person in the room. It is that the thing a family is actually buying is a specialist in a component, and distance is what prevents them having one. A parent in Al Rahmaniya who wants someone who teaches Pearson 4CH1 written practical questions every week is choosing from a handful of reachable people, or from everyone. That is the trade, and for IGCSE work it is a favourable one.

There is also a transparency argument. Two of the providers researched for this page route UAE parents to a non-UAE phone number without saying where the teaching happens; one shows a Dubai address on an Abu Dhabi page. Saying plainly that delivery is online, from wherever the right specialist sits, is a smaller claim than those pages make and a true one. We would rather be judged on it than hide it behind a local-sounding number.

What the format gives you in practice is evidence. The marked paper is on screen for both people, the working is on a shared surface, the session leaves a document you can read afterwards, and a written note follows. A parent who was not in the room can still see what happened. That is harder to get from a tutor who worked in a closed study for an hour and left.

sections.heading: Getting started when the budget is fixed
paragraphs: Start by naming the number. A family that knows it can spend a set amount this term gets better advice than one that asks what things cost, because the question becomes a plan rather than a price list. Tell us the budget, the subject, the board and the tier, and the answer should be a recommendation about how to spend it, including the option of spending less than offered.

Then send the two documents that make the first session useful: the statement of entry from the school's exams officer, which carries the board, the syllabus code and the tier, and one piece of marked work. Those two things remove a paid hour of guesswork. Parents frequently send a school report instead, which describes the symptom without showing where the marks went.

Take the free trial lesson next. One session, one subject, at no charge, before any schedule or block is agreed. The test of a trial is specificity: at the end of it the tutor should be able to name what is costing marks, estimate the sessions a named gap needs, and say what the first three weeks will cover. Warmth without specifics is not a diagnosis.

Then hold the arrangement to a review date set in advance, and be willing to stop. If three reviews pass with no movement in the marks, adding hours is rarely the answer; changing the plan or the tutor usually is. Where no suitable specialist is available for a narrow subject, we say so and offer a date, an alternative time zone, or the advice that the money is better spent on a different subject this term.

process.title: Name the budget before the subject
process.description: Say what you can spend this term and we will say what it buys, including the option of a short diagnostic block rather than a term of sessions. A fixed figure produces a plan; an open question produces a price list.

process.title: Send the statement of entry and one marked paper
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier and paper numbers sit on one page from the school's exams officer. With a marked paper beside it, the first session starts on teaching rather than on working out what your child is entered for.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One session, one subject, at no charge, before any block or schedule is agreed. Judge it on whether the tutor names the gap and estimates the sessions it needs, not on how reassuring the half hour felt.

process.title: Choose the slot the week can survive
process.description: For Dubai-schooled children in Al Nahda or Al Taawun that usually means 18:00 or a weekend morning. Picking the ideal hour rather than the robust one is why arrangements fail in week three.

process.title: Review on a date fixed in advance
process.description: Agree when you will look again and what you will look at: a marked paper, the session notes, a topic list closed off. Reviewing against a baseline is what stops a term of spending drifting unexamined.

process.title: Stop or redirect when the evidence says so
process.description: If the marks have not moved across three reviews, more hours is the least likely fix. Changing the plan, the subject priority or the tutor is usually the cheaper and more honest response.

whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one on live video. No tutor is sent to a Sharjah address, and home visits are a service we run only in India. The same sentence appears on every country page on this site.

whyPoints.title: The cheaper option gets mentioned first
whyPoints.description: School subject clinics, official past papers and small-group teaching are all cheaper than one-to-one. Where one of them fits your situation better, we say so before quoting for hours.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Tutors are shortlisted against the specification code and the paper your child is entered for. Removing the drive is what makes that possible rather than aspirational.

faqs.question: What does an in-home IGCSE tutor cost per hour in Sharjah compared with online?
faqs.answer: Published UAE figures put in-home one-to-one, with travel included, at roughly AED 180-500 an hour: Bestimate's rate table shows AED 180-350 and independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500. A qualified subject tutor working online is published at roughly AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. The gap is largely travel and traffic risk rather than teaching quality. Those are other providers' published rates as of October 2026, not IB Gram's price list; check them at source before relying on them.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our villa in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For Sharjah families every lesson is one-to-one over live video, at the hour you book, with a shared screen and a shared working document. The reason is the tutor pool: removing the drive means your child can be matched with someone who teaches their exact syllabus code and component rather than with whoever can reach your address at 17:00 on a Tuesday.

faqs.question: Should we buy a monthly IGCSE package or pay by the session?
faqs.answer: Only if you divide it. Packages seen in this market include online plans from around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home plans at AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour sessions. Dividing gives you the real hourly figure, which is the only number comparable with an hourly quote. Then ask the questions packages tend to obscure: what happens to an unused session, whether marking of full papers is included, and whether the rate holds if you reduce to one subject.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home tutor in Tilal City or Al Suyoh quoted higher than one in Al Majaz?
faqs.answer: Distance. A tutor driving to the southern communities is committing two hours or more for a 60-minute session once the return journey is counted, and that time is inside the hourly figure whether or not it is itemised. The same effect decides which slot you are offered: a tutor with three visits in an evening arranges them by route rather than by what time suits your child. On live video neither the premium nor the route constraint applies.

faqs.question: What should I ask a private tutor before paying for a block of sessions?
faqs.answer: Five questions predict the term better than the rate does. What have you taught of this exact paper, not just this subject? What will I receive after each session? Is marking of full past papers included or charged separately? What is the cancellation position? And what would make you tell me to stop paying for this? A tutor who answers all five crisply is usually worth more than a cheaper one who answers none. Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit too.

faqs.question: Do I need to check a permit if I hire a tutor directly in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it costs you nothing to ask. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so be wary of any specific amount quoted at you as the penalty.

faqs.question: Is there anything cheaper than one-to-one worth trying first?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. Ask the head of department what subject support the school already runs inside the fee, because catch-up clinics and departmental sessions are commonly available and commonly unused. Awarding bodies publish past papers and mark schemes on their own sites, and a student working through them with the scheme alongside picks up much of the technique a tutor would teach. A small group at a centre lowers the rate per student. One-to-one earns its price on a named gap, a tier decision or an exam-technique problem with a deadline.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE sessions should I budget for one weak topic?
faqs.answer: Ask for a number, and be suspicious if you do not get one. A single named topic, such as moles or vectors or trace tables, is usually a small countable block followed by practice. Exam technique across a paper is a few weeks. Two years of accumulated gaps across a whole specification is a termly project and should be described as one. Any tutor who has seen one marked paper should be able to tell you which of the three you are in and roughly what it costs.

faqs.question: Does the quoted rate include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, and ask for the answer in writing on the quote. We do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general fact on these pages, because that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority and the provider's own tax position rather than for a tutoring page. What matters to you is whether the figure you were given is the figure you pay, and that is a fair question to put to any tutor or agency before a block is booked.

faqs.question: How should tutoring be scheduled during Ramadan in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Plan it before the month starts. School hours shorten, household routines move later, and the late-afternoon slot that works the rest of the year often stops working. The patterns that hold are a session after Iftar or one earlier in the afternoon, agreed in advance and kept. Families who leave it until the first week usually lose three or four weeks of continuity and then pay to recover the ground closer to the series, which costs more than planning around it would have.

faqs.question: Can my child keep lessons going while we travel over the holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, which is one of the practical advantages of video delivery in an exam year. The slot moves with the time difference rather than stopping, so a family spending December abroad does not come back in January needing to recover a month. For a Year 11 student, continuity through the holidays is often worth more than the same number of sessions bought in a rush in April, and it costs the same.

faqs.question: We are on a tight budget and three subjects are weak. What do we buy?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic block, then a decision. Get one marked paper in each subject and look at where the lost marks sit rather than at the grades. A subject losing marks to technique or unshown method can move quickly and is worth the hours. A subject missing two years of content will not move much this term, and funding it costs you the grade you could have saved elsewhere. Spreading a small budget thinly across three subjects is the one approach that reliably buys nothing.

faqs.question: Where does a tutor stop on an IGCSE coursework piece in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Within a clear boundary, yes. A tutor can teach the skills the task assesses, question the plan, point out an unsupported argument and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor must not produce material that will be submitted, rewrite a draft into its finished form, or supply content to copy. The student writes and submits the work. A tutor who offers anything more than that is creating a malpractice risk for your child, not a shortcut.

faqs.question: What do you do when no specialist covers my child's IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date or an alternative, rather than placed with a generalist. Narrow subjects are where this bites: Additional Mathematics 0606 at short notice, Accounting, a minority language, or a specification a school has just switched to. The options we offer are a wait with a named date, a tutor in another time zone whose hours work from Sharjah, or honest advice that the hours are better spent on a subject where the marks are more movable this term.

faqs.question: Does the free trial lesson have conditions attached?
faqs.answer: It is one lesson, in one subject, at no charge, and it happens before any schedule, block or payment plan is agreed. There is no obligation to continue afterwards. What we ask for beforehand is the statement of entry and one piece of marked work, because without those the hour goes on working out what your child is entered for instead of on teaching. If the trial ends without a specific diagnosis, that tells you something useful about the tutor.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Tell us the budget, not just the subject
sharjah/igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: Most families who arrive on this page are weighing an hourly figure against another hourly figure with no way to judge either. The figures above are what the UAE market publishes, attributed to whoever published them. What we provide is one-to-one IGCSE teaching on live video for Sharjah families, matched on the syllabus code and component rather than on the drive radius, with a written note after every session. Send the statement of entry, one marked paper and the amount you can spend this term, and we will come back with a plan and a free trial lesson in one subject.

intro.heading: Availability is not the problem. Verification is
paragraphs: Al Juraina is in the older, central-southern part of Sharjah, off the Maliha Road, with schools nearby and a tutoring market that has existed for decades. A parent here can find somebody to teach their child within a day. What they cannot easily find out is whether that person knows the examination their child is sitting, and this district makes the problem harder than most.

The reason is the school mix. Schools around here run British, Indian and mixed curricula, and a student can attend a school whose principal curriculum is one thing while being entered for Cambridge or Pearson papers in some subjects. So the first question - which syllabus is my child on - is genuinely uncertain for many families, and every later question depends on it.

The codes resolve it. Cambridge subjects carry four-digit codes: 0580 mathematics, 0620 chemistry, 0625 physics, 0610 biology, 0500 first language English. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses its own: 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1. They appear on the statement of entry and in the exam information a school circulates, and the exams officer can confirm them in one email. Until you have them, any tutoring conversation is approximate.

Then comes verification, which is where this market is weakest. Listings say 'all subjects, all levels' because that maximises enquiries. A photograph of a degree certificate proves a degree. Years of experience prove longevity. None of those tell you whether the person has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended to a cohort and marked their papers against the published scheme. The information a parent needs is specific, and it is obtainable in a five-minute conversation if you know what to ask.

Our answer to all of this is structural rather than rhetorical. We ask for the board, the code and the tier first, match a tutor who has taught that exact course, read a marked script before anybody meets, and deliver the lesson one-to-one over live video so the match is not restricted to people who will drive to the Maliha Road. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE - that service exists only in India.

One cost note before the detail, because it affects the verification decision. Across published UAE rate cards an in-home visit is quoted between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor teaching online. The premium is the drive along the Maliha Road. Spending it narrows your choice of tutor at the same time as raising the price, which is an unusual combination and not one in your favour.

What follows is the practical version: how to identify the syllabus, what 'knows the syllabus' means subject by subject, what your child's school can and cannot tell you, how to use a trial lesson as a test rather than a sales call, where local supply genuinely exists, and what we do when nobody suitable is free.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, pre-IGCSE
programmes.description: No external examinations, so syllabus knowledge matters less than general teaching skill. What to verify here is simply whether the tutor can diagnose: can they look at a piece of work and name the underlying weakness - algebraic fluency, unit handling, writing that does not answer the question - rather than marking it and moving on.
programmes.countryNote: In this part of Sharjah, where tuition centres are plentiful, families often buy long-running homework support at this stage. The useful test is whether the specific gap you started with has closed. If nobody can tell you, the arrangement is not being measured and the stage does not need it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written papers with published mark schemes, tiered into Core and Extended in most subjects. Here syllabus knowledge is decisive: a tutor should be able to name the papers, their weightings, the Extended-only content and the three topics where candidates most often lose marks, without being prompted.
programmes.countryNote: Entries run through the school's centre, and each Cambridge centre belongs to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after using the wrong zone timetable, so the exams officer's copy is the only one worth holding.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other route, with different codes, different paper structures and a recognisably different question style. Edexcel maths sets two equally weighted papers rather than Cambridge's tiered pattern. A tutor who has only taught Cambridge will give confident and wrong guidance about these papers, which is why the code is the first thing we ask for.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the next day, and the November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026. Work from the live official timetable.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-juraina.subjectsIntro: What 'knowing the syllabus' means in each subject, subject by subject. Use these as the questions you put to any tutor, local or online - the answers are audible even if you have no subject knowledge yourself.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: A specialist can say which paper is non-calculator, what the Extended tier adds, and that bounds, rearrangement under time pressure and multi-step problems abandoned early are where marks go. A generalist says the content is similar to other curricula, which is true and useless.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Edexcel
subjects.description: The test here is the alternative-to-practical paper. A tutor who has taught 0625 will mention it unprompted and describe what it asks for - named instruments, variables, sources of error. One who has not will talk about experiments in general terms.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Ask what the mark scheme wants when a question asks for an observation. The right answer is the observation itself - 'a white precipitate forms' - not the conclusion. A tutor who has marked these papers answers immediately; one who has not finds the question odd.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: The giveaway is command words. A specialist distinguishes describe, explain and suggest and can say what each earns on a long-answer question. A generalist treats them as synonyms, which is exactly the mistake their students will go on to make.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into two grades. The useful tutor asks which strand is dragging before agreeing to anything, because there is no time to treat all three equally and triage is the whole intervention.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Ask how they would raise a mark on directed writing. The answer should involve timed writing annotated against the mark scheme and a discussion of register. If it involves reading more books, the hours will be pleasant and the marks will not move.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A specialist knows the exercises are formulaic and will name them - note-making, summary with a word limit, register shift - and knows whether your child's entry carries the speaking endorsement. That last detail is frequently missed.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (0450 / 0455)
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward define, apply, evaluate with a judgement. Ask how marks are lost: the right answer is writing everything known about a concept rather than using it on the case in front of the candidate.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions and trace tables cost more marks than programming ability. A tutor who codes professionally but has not taught this syllabus will teach the wrong thing competently, which is a particular trap in this subject.

sections.heading: Step one: find out what your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: In a district where schools run several curricula, this is not a formality. We regularly receive enquiries that describe a student as 'doing IGCSE science' when the school has entered them for Cambridge Coordinated Sciences, or as 'on the British system' when the papers are Pearson Edexcel. Neither parent was careless; the information simply never reached them in a usable form.

The statement of entry is the primary document. It lists each subject with its code and tier, and it is issued well before the series. If it has not reached you, the exam information the school circulates usually carries the same detail, and the exams officer can confirm it in a sentence. Ask for three things: the board, the code, and the tier for each subject.

While you are asking, add a fourth: the school's internal deadline for changing an entry. That date sits earlier than the board's and is the one that constrains a tier change from Core to Extended. Families who discover a tier problem after a mock frequently find the internal deadline has passed, and the remaining option is the November series.

With those four facts, you can brief any tutor in one sentence - 'Cambridge 0620 Extended, Paper 4 is the weak one, mocks in January, internal entry deadline passed' - and the quality of responses you get will change immediately. A specialist will react to the detail. A generalist will reply to the subject name.
bullets: Statement of entry: board, code and tier per subject
Ask the exams officer if the document has not arrived
Ask for the internal entry-change deadline at the same time
Brief every tutor with the code, not the subject name

sections.heading: Step two: what 'knows the syllabus' sounds like
paragraphs: Parents are rarely in a position to assess subject knowledge directly, and confidence is easy to mistake for competence. The reliable approach is to ask questions whose answers only a person who has taught the paper can give, and then listen for specificity rather than reassurance.

The strongest single question is about where marks are lost, because the answer is a list and lists are hard to fake. In chemistry it should include mole ratios taken from the wrong species, electrolysis products guessed rather than reasoned, and observations written as conclusions. In physics, parallel circuits, gradients read instead of calculated, and vague answers on the alternative-to-practical paper. In maths, bounds, rearrangement under time pressure, and multi-step problems abandoned one step early.

The second strongest is about the final six weeks. A specialist describes a shift to complete papers under timing, marked against the published mark scheme, with errors logged by question type. A generalist says there will be more revision and more past papers, without a protocol for either.

The third is a request rather than a question: ask them to mark a recent script before you meet. A tutor who has taught the course will do it willingly, because the annotated paper argues their case better than any conversation. One who prefers to talk about rapport is telling you which of the two they are stronger at - and rapport matters, but it is not what is failing in most Year 11 subjects.

sections.heading: What your child's school can and cannot tell you
paragraphs: Schools are the best source of information about the entry and a poor source of information about tutoring, and it is worth knowing which questions belong where.

What a school can give you: the board, the code and the tier; the internal entry-change deadline; the mock window; the marked mock script; the head of department's view of which topics are weak; and in many cases a frank answer about how many teachers have taught the current cohort. All of that is useful and most of it is simply not asked for.

What a school cannot properly do is recommend a private tutor, and you should be cautious if one does. Abu Dhabi's regulator has published professional-ethics rules barring private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tutor permit carries a code of conduct pointing the same way. Hiring the person who marks your child's work creates a conflict in both the marking and the reporting.

Schools also cannot tell you how your child compares with candidates elsewhere, only with their own cohort. A strong set in a weak year group and a middling set in a strong one look identical on a report. That is one of the few genuine arguments for an outside opinion: a specialist who marks scripts from many schools has a wider reference point than any single department does.

There is one more thing worth asking the school, and it is the most awkward: whether the department considers your child's current tier correct. The answer shapes everything a tutor should do. If the school believes Extended is a stretch and the family believes otherwise, that disagreement needs resolving with past-paper evidence before anybody spends a term teaching towards the wrong target.

sections.heading: Why local supply thins exactly where you need it
paragraphs: Al Juraina sits in a well-supplied part of Sharjah, so it is reasonable to ask why a specialist is still hard to find locally. The answer is in the arithmetic of narrow expertise.

A tutor who teaches maths across several year groups has a large addressable market and fills their week easily. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended for years, marks to the scheme and knows the Paper 6 technique has a much narrower market, and their availability is consumed by whoever found them first. There are not many such people in any emirate, and they are distributed by where they happen to live.

Seasonality makes it worse. Demand concentrates in the eight to ten weeks before a series, which is exactly when families start looking. At that point the specialists are committed and the local list skews to generalists and awkward hours. The quality decision has effectively been taken by the calendar.

It is worth noticing that the summer is the inverse of the peak: many local tutors travel, so neighbourhood supply thins, while the national online pool is at its most available. For a family planning a bridge block before Year 11, that is the cheapest access to a specialist available all year.

Two practical responses. First, book the scarce course early, even at a low frequency - a fortnightly slot held from the start of the year converts easily into a weekly one in the final block. Second, stop filtering by distance. Over video, the pool is national rather than local, which is the difference between a short list of generalists and a real choice of specialists. For families here, the second response is the one that changes the outcome.

sections.heading: Using the trial lesson as a test
paragraphs: Almost everybody offers something free, and the variety is wide. A trial is only useful if it answers the question you actually have, which is whether this tutor knows this course and can work with this child.

To make it a test, do three things. Send a marked script in advance and ask for it to be read. Ask who will teach the trial and whether they are the tutor who would be assigned afterwards - a senior demonstrator followed by a different allocated tutor is a common and unhelpful pattern. And listen to the first ten minutes: a specialist opens with what the script shows, not with an introduction.

Things that should make you pause. A grade prediction at the end of a free lesson - nobody can know what a candidate will score, and a number offered that early is a sales instrument. A request for card details for something described as free. A condition on the word 'free' that was not stated on the same screen. And an unwillingness to say which specific courses the tutor has taught.

Our trial is a full one-to-one lesson over live video, with no payment and no card details, taught by the tutor who would be assigned. The marked script and the tutor's written view of what the remaining weeks can realistically change are yours whether or not you continue. That is deliberately a low-risk way to resolve a question this market usually resolves only after money has changed hands.

sections.heading: The permit question, and the one conflict to avoid
paragraphs: Verification has a legal dimension as well as an academic one, and both questions are easy to ask.

Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service is the application route, with a stated completion time of two working days.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so ignore any figure quoted at you - including by a tutor explaining why they would rather not discuss it. Because the permit costs nothing and takes days, a working tutor has no practical reason to be without one, and the answer to the question is informative either way.

The conflict to avoid is hiring your child's own teacher. Beyond the published ethics rules in Abu Dhabi and the permit's code of conduct, the problem is structural: the person marking your child's work should not be on your payroll. An independent specialist gives you something a school-based arrangement cannot - an outside opinion on where your child actually stands. For our part, IB Gram holds no approval, licence or accreditation from SPEA, KHDA or any other UAE authority, and we have no premises in this country.

sections.heading: When the answer is honestly 'nobody right now'
paragraphs: Every page in this market implies infinite availability. It is not true anywhere, and pretending otherwise is how families lose a term.

Some requests are genuinely hard to fill. Additional Mathematics 0606 at a peak evening hour. Computer science 0478 with somebody who has taught the pseudocode conventions rather than just programming. A specific board's business studies paper in the fortnight before a series. For these, the honest set of options is a different hour with the right person, a named date when a slot opens, or a referral to a different kind of provision.

What we will not do is fill the slot with a generalist and let the family discover the mismatch over six weeks. In a ten-week block that substitution costs exactly the weeks the family came to buy, and it is the single most damaging thing a matching service can do. A clear no, delivered early, leaves a family able to make another plan.

There is a version of this that works in a family's favour. If we cannot fill a weekday slot but can offer a weekend morning, that is often the better arrangement anyway for a student with a long school day, so a refusal sometimes produces a better plan than the original request would have.

The same honesty applies to what tutoring can achieve. Eight weeks changes technique, timing and repeated errors. It does not reteach two years of content, and a provider who says otherwise is selling hours. We would rather tell you which topics are being abandoned, early, than produce a schedule that quietly assumes a student can cover everything.

sections.heading: Coursework, materials and the limits that do not move
paragraphs: A page about verification should be explicit about the things a parent should never need to verify, because they are fixed commitments rather than variables.

A tutor may teach the content, diagnose from a script, drill command terms, mark to a published mark scheme, and give feedback on the student's own work. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit any part of assessed coursework, and we do not supply completed coursework. Operations that do appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams; the malpractice consequence lands on the student rather than the seller.

On materials: syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. We cite the official sources and point families to the school for current versions, which is also the correct route because syllabuses change between cycles. A provider offering a shared drive full of board material is distributing somebody else's copyright, and where the material is unreleased the exposure is a malpractice question attached to your child.

These limits are not negotiable under deadline pressure, which is the only time anybody tries to negotiate them. Agreeing them before a term starts means the awkward conversation never happens at eleven o'clock the night before a submission, which is when families make decisions they later regret.

And on outcomes: no tutor can know what a particular candidate will score, so there are no grade guarantees here, no promised improvements and no refund tied to a result. What we will commit to is a written plan, marking against the real mark scheme, a review at six sessions on timed scores, and a straight answer when something is not working.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor has really taught my child's IGCSE syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask three things and listen for specifics. Which topics do candidates lose most marks on in this subject - a specialist answers with a list, naming topics and question types. What changes in the final six weeks - the right answer involves full papers under timing, marked against the published mark scheme, with errors logged by question type. And will you mark a recent mock before we meet - somebody who has taught the course says yes immediately, because the annotated script makes their case better than any conversation can.

faqs.question: My child's school teaches an Indian curriculum but enters them for IGCSE. Who do we need?
faqs.answer: Somebody who has taught that board's papers, not somebody who knows the content. The mathematics and science overlap between systems is substantial, so the gap is examination behaviour: question phrasing, the expectation that method is shown, and command terms treated as precise instructions. Two to four board-specific sessions working through past papers, marked against the published scheme, usually close that gap faster than more content teaching. Get the code from the statement of entry first - it decides which board's papers to practise.

faqs.question: Where exactly do I find the syllabus code?
faqs.answer: On the statement of entry, which lists each subject with its code and tier, and usually in the exam information your school circulates. Cambridge codes are four digits - 0580 maths, 0620 chemistry, 0625 physics, 0610 biology, 0500 first language English. Pearson Edexcel codes begin with a 4: 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1. If neither document is to hand, the exams officer can confirm board, code and tier in one reply, and it is worth asking for the internal entry-change deadline in the same email.

faqs.question: Is a degree in the subject enough to teach the IGCSE paper?
faqs.answer: It is necessary and not sufficient. A chemistry graduate knows more chemistry than the syllabus requires and may not know that the mark scheme wants an observation rather than a conclusion, or how Paper 6 differs from Paper 4, or which organic conditions candidates habitually omit. Teaching a specified examination is a particular skill built by teaching it repeatedly and marking it against the scheme. Ask what they have taught and how recently, rather than what they studied.

faqs.question: Can the school recommend a private tutor for us?
faqs.answer: Schools can give you a great deal - board, code, tier, internal deadlines, the marked mock, a head of department's view of weak topics - and you should be cautious about taking a tutor recommendation, particularly if it is a member of staff. Abu Dhabi's regulator has published professional-ethics rules barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct pointing the same way. The person who marks your child's work should not be on your payroll.

faqs.question: Why is it so hard to find a single-subject specialist in central Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Because narrow expertise has a narrow market. A tutor who teaches maths across several year groups fills their week easily; one who has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended for years and marks to the scheme is a rarer person whose hours are taken by whoever found them first. Demand then concentrates in the eight to ten weeks before a series, which is when most families start looking, so the local list skews to generalists. Removing the distance filter is what turns a short list into a real choice.

faqs.question: What should I send when I first make contact with a tutoring service?
faqs.answer: Five things, and it fits in a short message: the board, the syllabus code and tier, the year group, the next dated assessment, and a marked script if one exists. That is enough for a specialist match and for an honest answer about what the available weeks can change. Enquiries that say 'Year 11 science, needs help' get a generic reply from everybody in this market, because there is nothing in them to respond to specifically.

faqs.question: Should the trial lesson be with the tutor who will actually teach?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth asking explicitly, because a trial taught by a senior demonstrator followed by a different allocated tutor is a common pattern and answers the wrong question. A trial exists to establish whether this tutor knows this course and can work with this child. Ours is a full one-to-one lesson over live video with the assigned tutor, no payment and no card details, and you keep the marked script and the tutor's written view either way.

faqs.question: A tutor predicted a grade in the first session. Is that a good sign?
faqs.answer: It is a reason for caution. Nobody can know what a particular candidate will score: the paper, the day, the boundaries and the student's own performance are all outside anybody's control. A number offered in a first or free session is a sales instrument rather than a professional judgement, and a provider comfortable making it will be comfortable making other claims. What a good tutor will give you after reading a script is a list of what is recoverable and what is not, which is more useful and less flattering.

faqs.question: Do we need the same tutor for two IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and often not ideally. Chemistry and physics at Extended level have different failure modes and different papers, including the alternative-to-practical technique, and a tutor strong in one is frequently approximate in the other. Where a tutor has genuinely taught both, one person is convenient. Where they have not, two specialists in consecutive slots will produce better teaching for a similar total. Ask what each has taught rather than assuming science is one subject.

faqs.question: Does a tutor in Al Juraina need a permit, and can I ask to see it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. The private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service handles applications in about two working days. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Which series will my child sit, and what if June goes wrong?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs June and November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. November is the standard resit route, and results from a November series reach students in January - the November 2025 cohort received theirs on 22 January 2026. Before entering, confirm that the receiving sixth form or university accepts a January result and confirm the entry route with the school or a registered centre.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework in IGCSE subjects that still have it?
faqs.answer: With the teaching and the feedback, yes; with the writing, no. A tutor may explain what the task requires, question a plan, teach the skill involved, and explain why a paragraph does not answer the question asked. A tutor may not write, redraft or edit any part of the submitted work, and IB Gram does not supply completed coursework. Services that sell finished assessments appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

faqs.answer: We tell you, and we offer a different hour with the right specialist or a named date when one frees up. Narrow requests - Additional Mathematics 0606, computer science 0478, a specific board's business paper in peak weeks - sometimes have nobody available. What we will not do is put a generalist into a deadline block and leave a family to discover the mismatch over six weeks, because that substitution costs exactly the weeks they were trying to buy.

intro.heading: The third bill, in context
paragraphs: Al Khan runs along the Sharjah lagoon between Al Majaz and Al Taawun, a dense residential strip with the Dubai boundary a short drive west and schools on both sides of it. Households here are typically paying substantial school fees, often for more than one child, and a tutoring enquiry arrives as a third bill rather than as a first one. That is the right way to think about it, and almost no page in this market does.

So this page sets the numbers side by side. School fees, which are approved by a regulator and are the largest education cost a family carries. Examination entry fees, which arrive quietly through the school and are rarely itemised in a parent's mental budget. And tutoring, which is the only one of the three a family actually controls, and therefore the one most often cut, delayed or over-bought in a panic.

The published tutoring market, read in October 2026, gives the frame. Entry-level online sessions are advertised from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified online subject tutors publish from about AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Specialist IGCSE and IB tutors are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase at around AED 270. In-home visits including travel run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table placing the usual band at AED 180 to 350.

Against school fees those figures look different from how they look in isolation. A short diagnostic block of three sessions at qualified rates is a small fraction of a term's fees. A year of weekly specialist sessions is not, and is a decision that deserves the same scrutiny a school choice gets. The distinction most families need is between those two purchases, and the evidence that tells them apart is free.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. In budget terms that removes the travel component from the rate and removes the waste that a visiting arrangement produces on a corridor where afternoon arrival times are genuinely unpredictable.

The rest of this page costs tutoring in context, explains who approves school fees and why that matters, puts examination and resit entry fees into the picture, sets out what to cut first when a budget is fixed, and ranks the free and low-cost options that should come before anybody is paid. It also says plainly where the honest answer is to spend nothing at all, which is a conclusion we reach with families more often than a page selling tutoring would normally admit.

paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Khan, as the phrase is used here, is one-to-one teaching for one child on the specification that child is entered for. IB Gram provides that over live video to Sharjah families and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. The question this page answers is not what an hour costs but what that hour costs relative to the education bills a household is already carrying.

Those bills are large and mostly fixed. School fees are the biggest and are set by the school within a regulatory framework rather than negotiated by a parent. Examination entry fees arrive through the school and are frequently bundled into a term's invoice without a parent ever seeing the per-subject figure. Transport, uniform and activity costs sit alongside them. Against that background, tutoring is the one discretionary line, which is why it tends to be either skipped entirely or bought in an expensive hurry.

The useful reframing is to separate the small purchases from the large ones. Three diagnostic sessions at published qualified rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour is a modest number against a term of fees, and it produces a written list of what is actually going wrong. A year of weekly specialist sessions at AED 200 to AED 450 and above is a serious commitment that deserves the same scrutiny as a school choice. Treating those two as the same kind of decision is how families overspend.

IB Gram publishes no tariff on these pages, because the right figure depends on subject scarcity, tier and session length and is quoted after a free trial lesson. Every dirham figure here belongs to the named provider or rate survey that published it, read in October 2026.

sections.heading: Who approves school fees, and why a tutoring budget should care
paragraphs: Fee regulation is not a detail for a tutoring page; it is the context in which a family decides whether a third bill is affordable. The frameworks differ by emirate and they are not symmetrical.

In Sharjah, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge operates on the same model. That is a broader remit than inspection: fee levels and curriculum approval both sit with the emirate authority rather than with the school alone.

In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education. It confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a Sharjah family with children at a Dubai school, that is directly relevant to what the household can afford elsewhere.

The scale of the market matters too, because it is what sets the local supply of tutors. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, and its 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools creating 16,846 new places. A market that size is why the online tutoring pool is deep, and why a family on the Sharjah side of the boundary can access it at the same rates as one inside Dubai.

sections.heading: Examination entries and resits: the line nobody budgets
paragraphs: Ask most parents what their child's IGCSE entries cost and the answer is a shrug, because the figure arrives inside a school invoice. That invisibility has a consequence: the cost of getting an entry decision wrong is also invisible, and so the decisions that generate resits are made with no price attached.

The sequence is worth seeing in cost terms. Entries are submitted by the school's examinations officer months before the papers, with a fee per subject. A tier that caps a grade below what a sixth form or an equivalency requirement needs leads to a November entry, which means another fee, a term of tutoring and a student still working on a subject the cohort has finished. A review of marking, requested through the centre within a short window after results, carries its own fee and its own risk.

Against all of that, a three-session evidence block in Year 10 that supports a tier conversation is a small, early purchase with an unusually clear return. It is also the purchase least often made, because in Year 10 nothing feels urgent and no bill has yet arrived.

For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the November window has run from late October into November, with the November 2026 final timetable finishing on 19 November 2026 and results reaching students in January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Those past dates are cited because they are checkable; confirm current timings against the official timetable and ask your school whether it enters November candidates at all.

sections.heading: What to cut first when the budget is fixed
paragraphs: Most households here are not choosing between everything and nothing; they are choosing what to keep. So the useful advice is an explicit cutting order rather than an argument that tutoring is valuable.

Cut, in this order. Anything bought before marked work was read, because it is a guess. Sessions in a subject the student dislikes but passes, which is motivation rather than teaching. Sessions spread thinly across three or four subjects, which produce no visible movement in any. Any arrangement whose sessions are repeatedly missed because the hour does not suit the commute, since those are being paid for twice. And finally, length: a term bought where the evidence supported three sessions.

Keep, in this order. The diagnostic block, because without it everything else is guesswork. Technique work in the subject nearest a grade boundary, where a small intervention converts into a grade. English Language technique, because planning and structure transfer to five other subjects at once. And the tier-evidence block if entries are still open, because the ceiling matters more than any topic.
The table below sets that out as a decision list. It is deliberately blunt, because a fixed budget rewards bluntness more than it rewards a balanced view in which everything has some merit.

One more cut worth naming, because families resist it. A block that is not working should be ended rather than extended, even when the tutor is likeable and the student has grown comfortable. Comfort is a real benefit and it is not what the fee was for. Agreeing the stopping condition at the outset makes that decision administrative rather than personal, which is the only way it reliably gets made.

sections.heading: The free and low-cost options, ranked
paragraphs: Before a third bill is added, there is a ladder of cheaper options that families on this corridor consistently under-use. Ranked by cost, starting at nothing.

Free, from the school: the marked script rather than the grade sheet, read with four labels — blank, attempted and abandoned, partially credited, completed but wrong. The subject teacher's answer to which three topics they would prioritise, a question they are rarely asked and answer well. Any departmental revision clinic, which on both sides of this boundary is often under-attended purely because families do not know it exists. And the code, tier, study-leave date and November entry deadline in writing from the examinations officer.

Free, from the boards: Cambridge and Pearson publish specification documents, support material and the official timetables on their own sites, including the zone-specific Cambridge timetable a centre must use. We link those rather than reproducing them, because the material belongs to the boards and copying it is a copyright problem. Anybody offering a download library of mark schemes is advertising that problem rather than a service.

Low cost: a group revision class at a local centre, which retells a specification with structure at the lowest supervised rate available and is a reasonable purchase for a student who has fallen behind across a whole subject. It cannot examine your child's own script, so it will not find an error pattern, and on this corridor it also adds a round trip at the worst hour of the day. After all of that, a three-session diagnostic block is the first thing worth paying a one-to-one rate for.

sections.heading: Permits, claims and the questions to ask before paying
paragraphs: A conspicuously low rate sometimes means a regulatory question has not been asked, and asking it costs nothing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, any page quoting an amount has invented it.

The permit also carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, which matters in a district where a family and a teacher may well live in the same tower. The school regulator is a separate matter: private schools in Sharjah answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Dubai's to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, and no tutoring provider, including IB Gram, holds approval, accreditation or a licence from either.

Four questions are worth asking any provider before money moves. What happens to a missed session, which on this corridor will happen. What the smallest useful purchase is, and whether it is offered without an argument. What evidence would justify stopping, agreed in advance. And what the provider will refuse to do with coursework, where a subject has it.

And the claims to refuse outright: a guarantee of a grade, any claimed regulator or board approval, any school described as a partner or client, any satisfaction figure or rating without the number, date and method behind it, and any offer to complete assessed work. We make none of them, publish no ratings, and do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables.

faqs.question: How does IGCSE tutoring compare in cost with a term of school fees in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: A three-session diagnostic block at published qualified rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour is a few hundred dirhams, which is a small line against a term of fees. The distinction matters: families who treat those two purchases as the same kind of decision usually overspend on the second and skip the first.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE examination entries actually cost?
faqs.answer: Most parents do not know, because the figure arrives bundled in a school invoice. Ask the examinations officer for the per-subject entry fee once. It is worth doing because it makes the cost of a resit concrete: a capped tier leads to a November entry with another fee, plus a term of tutoring, plus a student still working on a subject their cohort has finished. That in turn makes the Year 10 tier conversation feel as consequential as it really is.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to an apartment in Al Khan?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time. In budget terms that removes the travel component that published in-home rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour include, and it removes the waste when an unpredictable afternoon on this corridor cuts a visit short or cancels it.

faqs.question: Who approves the fees at my child's school?
faqs.answer: It depends on the emirate the school sits in. In Sharjah the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. In Dubai the Knowledge and Human Development Authority oversees private education quality, and it confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year under a AED 1.5 billion incentives package. For a Sharjah family with a child at a Dubai school, that is relevant context.

faqs.question: If the budget is fixed, what should we cut first?
faqs.answer: In this order: anything bought before marked work was read, because it was a guess; sessions in a subject the student dislikes but passes, which is a motivation issue; sessions spread thinly across three or four subjects, which move nothing; any arrangement whose sessions are repeatedly missed because the hour does not suit the commute; and finally length, where a term was bought and three sessions would have done. Keep the diagnostic block, the boundary subject and English Language technique.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest thing that actually tells us what is wrong?
faqs.answer: The marked script, and it is free. Ask the subject teacher for it rather than the grade, then go through it with four labels: blank, attempted and abandoned, partially credited, and completed but wrong. The distribution is the diagnosis. Blanks at the end mean timing; scattered blanks mean avoided topics; partial credit everywhere means method and command terms; completed but wrong means a genuine content gap. Only the last needs teaching rather than training.

faqs.question: Is a group revision class a reasonable way to keep the third bill small?
faqs.answer: For one purpose. A class retells a specification with structure at the lowest supervised cost per hour, which suits a student who has fallen behind across a whole subject. It cannot examine your child's own script, so it cannot find an error pattern, and on this corridor it adds a round trip at the worst hour of the day. If the marked paper shows two marks a question going missing on units and method, no number of classes will address it.

faqs.question: Why is a Year 10 tier conversation described as a cost saving?
faqs.answer: Because the alternative is a resit. Cambridge Core accesses grades C to G while Extended accesses A* to E; Pearson Foundation accesses 5 to 1 while Higher accesses 9 to 4 with a grade 3 safety net. If a sixth form or an equivalency requirement needs a grade the tier cannot award, no preparation produces it, and the remedy costs an entry fee plus a term of tutoring. A three-session evidence block in Year 10 is a fraction of that and is bought when nothing feels urgent.

faqs.question: How much should a Sharjah family expect to spend across both IGCSE years?
faqs.answer: Less than most do, if it is placed well. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour-long sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support. The pattern that wastes money is nothing in Year 10 and a concentrated burst between the mock and study leave. Moving part of the same total into Year 10, while content is still being taught, buys considerably more.

faqs.question: Does the deep Dubai school market affect what we pay in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Yes, favourably. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with seven new schools and 16,846 new places added for 2026-27. A market that size supports a deep pool of subject specialists, and because specialist tutoring is priced regionally and delivered online, a family on the Sharjah side of the boundary reaches that pool at the same published rates as one inside Dubai.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if a session is missed because of traffic?
faqs.answer: Ask any provider this before signing anything, because on this corridor it will happen. The answer tells you how the arrangement behaves in week five, which matters more than the hourly rate. Our own structural answer is to set the slot late enough to survive a bad crossing and to put the most important session at the weekend, because a cancellation policy is a worse solution than a time that works. A session repeatedly missed is being paid for twice.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a student in Al Khan need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Because it costs nothing there is no good reason not to hold one, and tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can we get mark schemes and past papers included in the fee?
faqs.answer: No, and be wary of anybody offering them. Specification documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are published on their own sites. We cite and link them rather than reproducing or hosting copies, because copying is a copyright problem and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Your school can tell you what your child is entitled to access, and that access is part of the fees you already pay.

faqs.question: What should make us stop paying rather than renew?
faqs.answer: Agree it at the start. A reasonable standard is a second timed paper at the midpoint, marked against the published scheme and compared with the first by topic, plus your child being able to name their own weakest area unprompted. If neither has moved after four weeks, the plan or the match is wrong and continuing is paying for hope. A provider who cannot describe a stopping condition is selling a subscription, which is exactly what a discretionary third bill should not become.

intro.heading: A Sharjah address, a Dubai timetable, a board deadline
paragraphs: Al Majaz sits along the Khalid Lagoon and the Buheirah Corniche, in the part of Sharjah that is closest to Dubai in both distance and daily rhythm. A large share of the children living in these towers are schooled across the emirate boundary, which means their household runs on one calendar and their education on another. Add a board examination timetable on top and there are three clocks in play, none of which was set by the family.

That is a different problem from the one most tutoring pages describe. The question is rarely whether a child understands the material; it is when, in a week shaped by a cross-border commute, there is an hour in which they can do anything useful with it. A tutor who ignores that produces a plan that looks sensible on paper and collapses in its third week.

The examination side of the calendar is the fixed part. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two a candidate in this country works to. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Entries are submitted by the school's examinations officer months ahead of the papers, and that submission fixes the board, the code and the tier.

The school side is the variable part, and it depends on which emirate the school sits in. A Sharjah school answers to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A Dubai school answers to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Term dates, mock windows and study-leave dates are set by the school rather than by either authority, which is why a family with children on both sides of the border can have two different school calendars in one house.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. On this corridor that is the practical answer to the timing problem: a session can be set for the hour the student is actually home and functioning, including a later slot than any visiting tutor would offer, and two children on two different school calendars can be taught on the same evening.

The rest of this page works through those three clocks in order: what the two school calendars do to each other, how the mock-to-paper sequence runs in a commuting household, why the hour everybody wants does not exist on this road, and how to use the November series as a plan rather than a rescue. Everything in it is written to be used alongside your own school's published dates rather than instead of them, because those dates differ by school and a page that invented them would be wrong within a term.

programmes.name: Year 9: the cheap window
programmes.description: No board deadlines, no tier, and the lowest cost per unit of improvement in the whole pipeline. Algebraic fluency and written-answer structure built here remove work that otherwise costs several times as much in Year 11. Fortnightly across two terms is normally enough for a student who is coping but careless.
programmes.countryNote: In a commuting household Year 9 is also when a family should decide whether the cross-border school run is sustainable for two more years. A child who loses ninety minutes a day to a boundary crossing has fewer usable evening hours than a classmate living in the same school's catchment, and that gap compounds.

programmes.name: Year 10: evidence while it still counts
programmes.description: Most of the specification is taught, usually once, and the internal examination at the end of the year generally becomes the tier recommendation. Support here closes coverage gaps and produces marked evidence for a tier conversation, which is a benefit available at this point and not later.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the school whether the Year 10 result is the final input into the tier decision or whether it is revisited in the autumn of Year 11. Schools on either side of the boundary differ, the answer is free, and it decides whether later evidence will even be looked at.

programmes.name: Year 11: the ceiling is set
programmes.description: The board, code and tier are fixed, teaching runs to study leave, and the remaining work is recovering marks the student can already earn: method lines, command terms, units, timing and question order. Narrow, diagnosable and quick-moving when the diagnosis comes from a marked script rather than from conversation.
programmes.countryNote: The November series stays open as a route rather than only as a consolation. For a student on a capped tier, or one who has lost teaching to illness or a mid-year move, raising November with the examinations officer in the autumn can be worth more than a whole spring of sessions.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-majaz.subjectsIntro: Requests from Al Majaz lean towards mathematics and the sciences, with English and Business behind them. Each entry names the component where the marks are actually decided.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Two written papers and no coursework, so every mark stays recoverable until the paper itself. Losses concentrate in non-calculator arithmetic, unwritten method lines and the combined-topic final parts of long questions. The tier sets the ceiling, so confirm it in writing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and practical-skills work decide most grades. Cambridge candidates sitting the practical-skills paper need a written method precise enough for a stranger to repeat, which is a writing skill built over several marked attempts rather than explained once.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and organic pathways separate the upper grades. The recurring loss is a correct calculation written without units or significant figures, which quietly costs two marks per question.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Highest content load and the subject most sensitive to command terms. An explain question answered with a description earns nothing however accurate it is, and that is a training problem rather than a revision one.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition carry the paper. Students who read widely still lose marks for not planning, so a response drifts from the audience and purpose the question specified. Timed writing with criteria annotation moves this fastest.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate qualification from First Language English with different recognition later. Worth confirming which one is on the entry long before a sixth form asks the question.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Application to the case insert is most of the paper. Definition-led revision plateaus in the middle grades; practising three concepts applied to an unfamiliar business moves a grade in a term.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy plus explicit evaluation. Unlabelled axes and answers that explain without weighing one effect against another are the two reliable sources of lost marks.

subjects.name: Computer Science

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Al Majaz can change this term
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Majaz, in the sense families here use the phrase, is a subject specialist working one-to-one with one child on the specification that child is entered for. IB Gram supplies that over live video to Sharjah families and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. On this corridor the online format solves a specific problem rather than a general one: it decouples the session from the road.

What a term can change depends on where it sits. With two terms left before a June paper, content teaching is genuinely possible: a topic can be rebuilt, a habit changed, a specification gap closed. With one term left, content teaching is largely over and the work becomes recovering marks the student is already capable of earning. With four weeks left, the honest answer is paper technique, and anybody promising more is selling comfort rather than teaching.

That distinction decides what a family should buy, and families on this corridor are particularly prone to buying the right thing at the wrong time. The pattern we see is a household that defers because the evenings are already difficult, then buys intensively in the spring when the evenings are no easier and the window has narrowed. Three sessions in October are worth more than six in April, and they are also easier to fit.

The first conversation should therefore cover three things in order: the dates from the school, the code and tier on the entry, and a marked script. All three are free to obtain, and together they turn a general worry into a specific, costed plan.

sections.heading: Two calendars in one household
paragraphs: A family living in Al Majaz with a child at a Dubai school is running two institutional calendars, and they are not aligned. The school's term dates, mock windows, internal deadlines and study-leave date are set by the school, and schools on either side of the boundary make those decisions independently. A household with children at a Sharjah school and a Dubai school can have two mock seasons, two study-leave dates and two holiday patterns.

On top of that sits the regulatory difference, which matters less for dates than families assume but matters for other things. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai's are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education there. Inspection frameworks and published reports differ accordingly.

The third calendar is domestic. Sharjah government employees work a four-day week, which for some households changes which days are genuinely available and makes a Friday morning session a real option rather than an odd one. A family where one parent works a Sharjah public-sector pattern and the other a Dubai private-sector pattern has a weekly rhythm that no generic tutoring schedule will match.

The practical response is to put all of it on one page before buying anything: both schools' term and study-leave dates, both mock windows, the board entry deadline, and the days the household is actually free. The table below is the comparison most families here find useful.

sections.heading: The mock-to-paper sequence in a commuting household
paragraphs: The stretch between a marked mock and the first paper is where most tutoring money in this market is spent, and where it is most often spent badly. In a household with a boundary commute the problem is compounded, because the plan has to survive evenings that are unpredictable through no fault of anybody in the family.

A sequence that works has a shape and some slack. The first session is the marked mock, gone through question by question with four labels: blank, attempted and abandoned, partially credited, and completed but wrong. The distribution is the diagnosis. The next sessions take the dominant pattern and attack it one at a time, with short homework that produces evidence. The midpoint is a second timed paper on the same specification. The last third is timing and question order across a whole paper.

The slack is the part a commuting family needs and rarely gets. A plan built on eight consecutive weekday evenings will lose two of them to traffic, illness or a school event, and a student who falls behind a plan tends to abandon it rather than adjust. Building in a weekend anchor and one deliberately empty week produces a plan that still works in week six, which matters more than theoretical efficiency.
