sections.heading: Why four o'clock does not exist on this corridor
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider offers a four o'clock slot and almost no family on the Sharjah boundary can use one. A child leaving a Dubai school at half past two or three is not home at four, and on a bad afternoon is not home at half past four either. The slot gets booked anyway, missed twice, and then the family concludes that tutoring does not work for them.

The fix is unglamorous: find out the real arrival time on three ordinary weekdays, then set the session fifteen minutes after the latest of them. That single piece of arithmetic removes most of the scheduling failure we see on this corridor, and it costs nothing. It usually produces a 5pm or 5.30pm start, which is later than parents would like and earlier than the alternative of not happening.

The second lever is the weekend. For a commuting household the weekend session is not a compromise; it is the best session of the week, because the student arrives rested and the road is irrelevant. Where only one quality hour a week is realistic, it belongs on a Saturday or Sunday morning with a short midweek slot used only to mark work and set the next piece.

The third lever is sibling sequencing. Two children at two schools arrive at two times, and online delivery is what makes two slots on one evening possible without anybody driving. That is also why a household on this corridor usually ends up with one heavily used weeknight rather than three lightly used ones, which is both cheaper and more sustainable.

sections.heading: The November series, used deliberately
paragraphs: Both main boards run a November series and candidates in this country can use it. Most families only learn that after a disappointing August, which turns a planning option into a consolation. Treated deliberately it is a legitimate route, and on this corridor it is particularly useful because the spring evenings are the hardest ones to work with.

Three situations make it worth raising early. A student on a tier that caps the grade below what they need, where sitting June as a baseline and targeting a focused November entry produces a better final result. A student who has lost substantial teaching to illness or a mid-year move between schools, which on a cross-border corridor happens more often than average. And a student carrying a large number of subjects, where spreading the load protects the grades that matter most.

The costs are real and belong in the conversation. Entry fees, a summer and autumn still spent on a subject the cohort has finished, and a sixth-form application timetable that may want results before November grades exist. Those are questions for the examinations officer, and they should be asked before the June entry rather than after the result.

For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE the November window has run from late October into November, with the November 2026 final timetable finishing on 19 November 2026 and results reaching students in January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Those past dates are cited because they are checkable, and current timings should be confirmed against the official timetable.

sections.heading: SPEA, KHDA and which rules apply to your child
paragraphs: Families on the boundary ask this constantly, and the answer is simpler than it sounds: the regulator that matters is the one for the emirate where the school sits, not the one where the family lives. A child living in Al Majaz and attending a Dubai school is in a KHDA-regulated school, and their inspection report, curriculum approval and fee framework come from there.

Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and, like Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader remit than inspection alone. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, while Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education.

One federal rule applies everywhere and surprises families regularly. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. So a child on a British or IB curriculum carries those subjects alongside it, with schools running separate streams for Arab and non-Arab students. Those subjects are also excluded from the five that the Ministry counts for British-track equivalency, which catches out families reading the requirement for the first time.

What no family should ever see claimed is regulator approval for a tutoring provider. IB Gram holds no SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, and claims none. A KHDA educational services permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and implying one without holding it is a misrepresentation.

sections.heading: Permits, coursework and the claims to refuse
paragraphs: Private tutoring in this country is regulated and a parent is entitled to ask about it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any page quoting an amount has invented it.

Because the permit costs nothing, there is no reasonable excuse for an independent tutor not to hold one, and asking is the simplest due diligence available. A rate far below the market sometimes means the question has never been put. The permit also carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, which is worth knowing in a dense residential area where a family and a teacher may well be neighbours.

On coursework, where a subject has it, the boundary is firm. A tutor teaches the skill the component assesses, explains the published criteria and what their command words mean, questions the student about their own reasoning, and gives feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write the work, does not rewrite sentences and does not supply material for submission. The consequence of crossing that line falls on the student, which is why it is stated before any coursework support starts.

And the claims to walk away from: any guarantee of a grade, any claimed regulator or board approval, any school described as a partner or client, any satisfaction figure or star rating without the number, date and method behind it, and any offer to complete assessed work. Each of those appears somewhere in this search result. We make none of them, and we do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, because those belong to the boards and are published on their own sites.

faqs.question: My child lives in Al Majaz but attends school in Dubai. Which calendar should a tutoring plan follow?
faqs.answer: The school's, for term dates, mocks and study leave, and the board's for the examination series. Term dates and study-leave dates are set by schools individually rather than by either regulator, so a household with children on both sides of the boundary can have two mock seasons and two leave dates. Hold both on one page along with the board entry deadline. The one element that is shared is the examination series itself: June, with November available as the resit route.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start for a family on the Buheirah Corniche?
faqs.answer: Later than most providers offer. A child leaving a Dubai school in the early afternoon is frequently not home and settled before five, and on a bad afternoon not before half past. The fix is to measure the real arrival time on three ordinary weekdays and set the session fifteen minutes after the latest one, which usually produces a 5pm or 5.30pm start. That single step removes most of the missed-session problem families on this corridor report.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to an apartment in Al Majaz?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for working through paper questions. On this corridor that solves the specific problem the commute creates: the session is decoupled from the road, a later start is available, and two children arriving at two different times can both be taught on the same evening.

faqs.question: Is a weekend session better than a weekday one for a commuting Sharjah student?
faqs.answer: Usually, and it deserves to be the main session rather than an extra. On a weekend the student arrives rested and the boundary crossing is irrelevant, which makes it the best hour of the week for timed-paper work that needs real concentration. Where only one quality hour a week is realistic, put it on a weekend morning and use a short midweek slot purely to mark what was set and set the next piece. Many Sharjah households also have a four-day public-sector week, which opens up Friday.

faqs.question: Which exam series will a Sharjah candidate sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE and O Level candidates sit the June series, with November available as the resit route. Cambridge offers its spring sitting in February and March to India only, so any page quoting those dates to a family in this country has the wrong calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, so confirm which applies with your school's examinations officer.

faqs.question: How should we plan six weeks from the mock to study leave?
faqs.answer: With slack in it. Start with the marked mock gone through using four labels — blank, attempted and abandoned, partially credited, completed but wrong — because the distribution is the diagnosis. Attack the dominant pattern one week at a time, keep one week deliberately light, take a second timed paper at the midpoint, and spend the final week on timing and question order. On this corridor a plan assuming eight perfect weekday evenings will lose two and then be abandoned, which is worse than a shorter plan that holds.

faqs.question: Does SPEA or KHDA set my child's mock and study-leave dates?
faqs.answer: Neither. Those are school decisions. The regulator that applies is the one for the emirate where the school sits: Sharjah's private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods, while Dubai's answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. That determines which inspection framework and published report apply to your child, not when they go on study leave. For dates, ask the school in writing.

faqs.question: Should we plan for a November resit before June even happens?
faqs.answer: If your child is on a tier that caps the grade below what they need, or has lost substantial teaching to illness or a school move, yes. Sitting June as a baseline and targeting a focused November entry often produces a better final result than a compressed spring, and the spring evenings on this corridor are the hardest ones to use. Ask the examinations officer about entry costs, whether the school enters November candidates, and whether sixth-form applications will need results before November grades exist.

faqs.question: When do Pearson Edexcel results actually reach students?
faqs.answer: For the summer series, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. For the autumn series, November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Those are past dates, cited because they are checkable. Current and future timings should be taken from the official Pearson timetable rather than from any tutoring page, since provisional timetables are revised.

faqs.question: Can a tutor produce evidence to change my child's tier?
faqs.answer: A tutor can produce evidence; only the school can change the tier, and only before entries are submitted to the board. Two timed sections and a diagnostic session, marked against the published scheme, show whether a student can access the harder paper, and a conversation backed by that is different from one backed by a parental impression. After the entry deadline the question is closed, and the honest plan becomes using the available ceiling fully, with November considered where it genuinely helps.

faqs.question: Do my children have to take Arabic alongside their IGCSE subjects in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under the federal position, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Schools run separate streams for Arab and non-Arab students, with different expectations in each. These subjects also sit outside the five that the Ministry of Education counts for British-track equivalency, which is the detail families most often discover late and occasionally plan around incorrectly.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a student in Al Majaz need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Because it costs nothing, there is no good reason not to hold one. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher tutor them privately in these towers?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid. The MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK applies a comparable rule to school staff in Abu Dhabi. Beyond the regulation it is poor practice: the person marking the work should not also be paid to prepare it. In a dense residential area where families and teachers are often neighbours the arrangement is easy to fall into, and an independent specialist gives you a separate read on the marks.

faqs.question: How will we know in four weeks whether the block is worth continuing?
faqs.answer: By comparing two marked papers rather than two impressions. The first session should produce a script with the error types written down; the fourth or fifth should produce a second timed paper on the same specification, marked the same way and compared by topic. Movement should be visible in the areas the diagnosis named. You should also hear your child name their own weakest topic unprompted. If neither has happened, the plan or the match is wrong and should change rather than continue.

intro.heading: Your child sits papers, not subjects
paragraphs: An IGCSE grade is not awarded for knowing Chemistry. It is awarded for marks earned on named papers, each testing a different set of skills, each with its own timing pressure and its own mark scheme conventions. A student can know the subject well and still lose a grade because the paper that tests experimental reasoning was never practised, or because they wrote four minutes of answer for a one-mark question. Those are paper-level problems and they need paper-level work.

Al Mamsha is a walkable mixed-use district in Sharjah, close to Muwaileh and University City, so students here live near schools and no nearer than anyone else to somebody who has marked a Cambridge Paper 4. The constraint across this emirate is not distance but how few people have taught a given syllabus code at a given tier through a full two-year cycle. Those people are not distributed by development, which is why we do not sort tutors by address.

IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE. Home tuition is a service we offer only in India, and every Sharjah lesson is live, one-to-one, over video, in a slot held in Gulf Standard Time. Paper-level work survives that format intact, because what it consists of is a question attempted under timing, a mark scheme opened and an answer corrected phrase by phrase. None of that improves by having somebody in the room.

This page is organised by paper rather than by subject. There is a table of what each component tests across the main subjects, a marks-per-minute table that settles how long an answer should be, a topic-to-paper map for Mathematics, a proper account of the alternative-to-practical paper, and an honest explanation of what grade boundaries are and why nobody can tell you next series' in advance. Verify every syllabus code on your child's statement of entry, because that is the only document that is reliably current.

One correction to make early, because it affects dates families act on. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Any page quoting a February exam window to a Sharjah parent has handed them a deadline that belongs to another country, and that error appears more often in these search results than you would expect. Ask the school one more thing while you are checking: which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre sits in, because Cambridge states plainly that using the correct timetable for the zone is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after working from the wrong one.

sections.heading: What each paper actually tests
paragraphs: Revision planned without knowing what each paper tests produces a student who is well prepared for the component they were already good at. The table below sets out, subject by subject, what the components assess and where marks are lost, which is the information a specialist session should establish in the first ten minutes and which most students reach Year 11 without.

The pattern worth seeing is that the components test genuinely different things rather than the same thing at different lengths. A multiple-choice paper rewards speed and the elimination of distractors. A structured paper rewards precise phrasing against a mark scheme. A practical or data paper rewards experimental reasoning that cannot be revised from notes at all. Treating them as one body of revision is the commonest planning error in this market.

The tier interacts with all of this. Core and Extended candidates sit different papers in most Cambridge subjects, so a student practising the wrong set is not merely under-prepared but prepared for questions they will not see. This is why the tier has to be confirmed from the statement of entry before any paper-level work begins rather than assumed from the textbook in use.

Confirm the structure for your child's specific syllabus and series on the board's own site, because specifications are revised and component patterns change between versions. We are describing the general shape to make the planning argument, not publishing a specification. A provider who presents paper structures as permanent facts has not checked recently.

sections.heading: Marks per minute, and how long an answer should be
paragraphs: This is the most mechanical improvement available in the IGCSE years and almost nobody teaches it. Each paper has a total mark and a total time, which gives a rate. A student who does not know their rate will write a paragraph for a one-mark question and then find there are eleven minutes left for the last fifteen marks, which is how able candidates end up with unfinished papers and a grade below their ability.

The rule we teach is blunt because blunt rules survive exam pressure: one mark, one line. Two marks, two distinct points. Six marks, six separate creditable statements, not one idea expressed six ways. Students resist this because it feels like under-answering, and the mark scheme is entirely indifferent to how much was written beyond the points it credits.

The second half of the discipline is pacing against the clock on the page. Work out the halfway mark in minutes and write it on the paper at the start. A student who reaches that point behind can make a deliberate decision about what to abandon, which is a far better outcome than discovering the problem in the final five minutes and panicking through the heaviest questions.

This block takes four to six sessions and does not require knowing any more content. It is also the intervention families are least willing to pay for, because it does not feel like teaching. It is, reliably, worth more marks per hour spent than almost anything else available in Year 11.

sections.heading: The alternative-to-practical paper, properly
paragraphs: Cambridge science candidates sit a practical component, and most Sharjah centres enter students for the alternative-to-practical written paper rather than a laboratory examination. It is the single largest recoverable loss in IGCSE science for students in this emirate, and it is routinely treated as something that will take care of itself because the student does experiments at school.

It will not take care of itself, because the paper does not test whether a student can do an experiment. It tests whether they can reason about one on paper: identify independent, dependent and controlled variables, judge the precision of an instrument, read and construct graphs with correct scales and best-fit lines, identify specific sources of error rather than general ones, and suggest improvements that address those specific errors.

Those are learnable, discrete skills with highly predictable mark scheme phrasing, and six to eight dedicated sessions typically move a student from guessing to competent. The mistake is to fold this paper into general revision, where it receives a tenth of the attention it needs and the student continues to write human error as a source of error, which earns nothing in any series.

Ask the school which practical route your child is entered for. If it is the alternative-to-practical paper, give it its own sessions. If it is a laboratory examination, the preparation is different again and needs the school's own equipment list. Either way it is one question to the school and it changes what a third of the science preparation should contain.

sections.heading: Topic to paper, using Mathematics as the worked example
paragraphs: Students revise topics and sit papers, and the mapping between the two is rarely made explicit. The table below does it for Mathematics, which is the subject most Al Mamsha families ask about, and the same exercise is worth doing with your child for every subject because it immediately shows where revision time should go.

Two things usually become visible when the mapping is drawn. First, that several topics the student finds comfortable carry relatively few marks, while the ones they avoid carry many. Second, that the supplementary Extended content concentrates in the harder questions late in each paper, which is exactly where the student was already running out of time. Those two facts together explain most unexpected Mathematics grades.

The practical use of the mapping is to order revision by weight rather than by chapter. A student with eight weeks should spend the first three on the heavily weighted topics they cannot do, not on working through the textbook from page one. This sounds obvious written down and is almost never what happens, because revision follows the order material was taught in.

Draw the same map for the sciences and it reveals the practical paper sitting there carrying a substantial share of the grade and receiving almost no preparation. That is the single most common finding when we do this exercise with a Sharjah family in Year 11, and it is also the easiest to fix. Do the mapping on one sheet of paper with your child rather than for them, because the point is partly that they see it. A student who has worked out for themselves that a topic they avoid carries three times the marks of a topic they enjoy will revise differently without being told to.

sections.heading: Grade boundaries, and why nobody can tell you next series'
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask what mark is needed for an A, and the honest answer is that nobody knows until after the papers are sat. Boundaries are set by the awarding body for each series, after the papers have been marked, to account for how difficult that particular paper turned out to be. A provider quoting a fixed boundary for a future series is either guessing or repeating an old figure as though it were current.

What is useful is the shape of the thing rather than the number. Boundaries move between series and between subjects, sometimes by several marks, which has two consequences for planning. A student sitting a few marks under a boundary in a mock might be above it in a real series, or further below. And the marks closest to any boundary are the mechanical ones: method shown, units given, terminology precise, the last question attempted at all.

This is why we push timing discipline and method marks so hard rather than chasing additional content. A student who recovers five mechanical marks a paper has moved further towards a boundary than one who learns an extra topic they may or may not be asked about. Mechanical marks are available in every question on every paper, which is a much better bet than any single topic.

We also do not reproduce or supply grade-boundary tables, past papers or mark schemes as downloads. Those are Cambridge and Pearson materials and reproducing them is a copyright matter. We reference them, teach from them in session and point to the official source so you can obtain what you need through your school.

sections.heading: The three sciences compared, because they are not one subject
paragraphs: Families routinely ask for a science tutor and are surprised that we will not supply one person for all three. Physics, Chemistry and Biology fail in different places, demand different habits and reward different revision, and a tutor strong in one is usually ordinary in the others. The distinction is practical rather than territorial.

Physics loses marks in written explanation, where a correct idea phrased loosely earns nothing because the mark scheme names a chain of cause and effect. The remedy is to collect standard explanations from mark schemes and learn the phrasing until it is automatic. It is memorisation of wording, which is not what most people expect physics revision to involve.

Chemistry loses marks cumulatively and quantitatively. Moles and stoichiometry carry the heaviest weight and the highest failure rate, and a weakness there damages every subsequent topic. The qualitative-analysis tables, by contrast, are pure recall, appear reliably and are usually left unlearned, which makes them among the cheapest marks in the whole examination.

Biology loses marks terminologically. The mark scheme frequently names the exact word required, and the student who revised from their own notes writes their own words. Revising from mark schemes rather than notes is the correction, and it is the single most effective change a Biology candidate can make. Three subjects, three different problems, three different tutors.

There is a budget consequence worth stating. Three specialists cost more than one generalist, and most households cannot fund three weekly hours. The sensible structure is to take the science that is doing the most damage, work it properly for a term, and leave the others to school. One science moved from a 5 to a 7 is worth more than three sciences nudged by half a grade, and it is the only version of this plan that is affordable.

sections.heading: What paper-level work costs in Sharjah
paragraphs: Specialist knowledge of a paper is priced at the top of the market and it is worth knowing where the bands sit. Read in October 2026, a qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. An IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table in the same range.

The budget band of roughly AED 33 to 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, is supplied largely by university students, and University City adjoins Al Mamsha. For Year 9 consolidation that is often the right purchase and we will say so. For six dedicated sessions on the alternative-to-practical paper it is not, because what you are buying is somebody who knows what that paper's mark scheme credits.

The useful way to cost this work is per block rather than per hour, because paper-level interventions are short. Six sessions on one component at the qualified band is roughly AED 900 to 1,800; at the specialist band, roughly AED 1,200 to 2,700. Compare that with Bestimate's monthly estimate of AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, and the short targeted block starts to look like the better-value purchase it usually is.

In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to 500 with independent tutors. For this kind of work the travel premium buys nothing at all, because a timed attempt, an open mark scheme and a line-by-line correction work identically on a shared screen. Every figure is published by the provider named; none is an IB Gram price, and for ours take the free trial and ask.

sections.heading: Coursework, practical write-ups and the line a tutor holds
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry school-assessed components, and this market contains providers who will simply produce them. One page in this research advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. For a Sharjah student, submitting purchased work converts a grade worry into a malpractice finding against the qualification, which is not recoverable by resitting anything.

The boundary, plainly. A tutor may teach the skills the task requires, explain how the mark scheme awards them, model the approach on a different example, read a draft the student has written and say where it is unclear, unsupported or off-brief, and teach referencing, data handling and experimental write-up conventions properly.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, complete or edit the work to a finished state, and may not produce a worked version of the student's own task. This matters more rather than less in paper-level tutoring, because the work is close to the mark scheme and the temptation to demonstrate by doing is real. Demonstration happens on a different question, never on the student's own.

One further rule concerns teachers. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document. We will not arrange it either way.

The last boundary is about materials. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them, teach from them within a session and link the official source. If a provider offers you a bundle of official papers and mark schemes to keep, that tells you what else they consider negotiable.

sections.heading: Starting at paper level from Al Mamsha
paragraphs: Three documents before you contact anybody. The statement of entry, which gives the board, the code and the tier for every subject. One recent marked paper, ideally a mock. And, for a science, the answer to one question put to the school: which practical route is my child entered for. With those, a specialist can be specific in the first hour.

In the trial lesson, ask the tutor which component carries the practical skills in your child's subject and what the mark scheme accepts as a source of error. A specialist answers immediately and precisely. A general tutor talks about building confidence. That single exchange sorts the market faster than any credential, and asking it costs you nothing at all.

Expect the trial to end with a written list rather than an impression: the specific marks being lost, named by paper and by operation. Method marks on late multi-topic questions. Human error written where a named source was required. Paragraph answers to one-mark questions. Everything afterwards aims at that list, and the list is how you judge whether the work is landing.

Then review at four weeks. Items should be gone from the list. If the list is unchanged, the diagnosis was wrong and we change the plan or the specialist rather than running the term on it. Ask any provider what their answer to that is before you pay them, and notice whether they have one ready. It is the obvious question, the honest answer costs a serious provider nothing, and the hesitation is itself the information you were looking for.

Grade boundaries are set by the awarding body for each series, after marking, to account for how difficult that paper proved. They move between series and between subjects, sometimes by several marks. The planning consequence is useful though: the marks nearest any boundary are mechanical ones, so method shown, units given, precise terminology and attempting the final question are the cheapest route upward.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Physics, Chemistry and Biology?
faqs.answer: They can and we will not arrange it, because the three fail in different places and need different habits. Physics loses marks in written explanation and needs mark-scheme phrasing learned verbatim. Chemistry loses them cumulatively in moles and stoichiometry. Biology loses them to imprecise terminology, and the fix is revising from mark schemes rather than from notes. A tutor strong in one of the three is usually ordinary in the others, and in the term before a series that difference is expensive.

faqs.question: Which practical route is my child entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, because it is their entry decision and they will answer immediately. Cambridge science candidates sit a practical component which can be a laboratory examination or the alternative-to-practical written paper, and most Sharjah centres use the written route. The preparation differs completely between them: the written paper needs reasoning practice on past questions, while a laboratory examination needs familiarity with specific apparatus and procedures from the school's own equipment list. It is one question and it shapes a third of the science plan.

faqs.question: How do we know whether the problem is content or technique?
faqs.answer: Look at a marked paper rather than at the grade. If the student starts every question and loses marks in parts c and d, in method shown, in terminology and in the final unfinished question, that is technique and it responds quickly. If they cannot begin questions on particular topics, that is missing content and no amount of timed practice will supply it. A trial lesson on a real question, marked against the scheme, will tell you which within the hour, and the two need opposite plans.

faqs.question: Why do the sciences need sessions on terminology?
faqs.answer: Because the mark scheme frequently names the exact word, especially in Biology, and an answer that is loosely correct earns nothing. The mechanism behind most under-performance is that students revise from notes written in their own words and then produce those words under examination conditions. The correction is to revise from mark schemes: read what the scheme credits, learn that phrasing, and use it. It feels like rote learning, it is unglamorous, and it moves Biology grades more reliably than any other single change.

faqs.question: Does working through whole past papers help?
faqs.answer: In the last fortnight, yes, because what you are then practising is stamina and pacing. Before that it is inefficient. A student losing marks on data interpretation should do the data questions from six papers rather than six whole papers, which concentrates correction on the failing operation instead of spreading it thinly. Then redo the same question type from scratch, which is the step almost everyone skips and the step that turns a correction into a habit that survives pressure.

faqs.question: How much does a six-session block on one paper cost?
faqs.answer: At published October 2026 rates, roughly AED 900 to 1,800 at the qualified online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, and roughly AED 1,200 to 2,700 at the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and TutorChase quotes AED 270. Compare that against Bestimate's monthly estimate of AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, and a short targeted block is usually the better-value purchase.

faqs.question: Is the February IGCSE series available to students in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. This matters because several pages ranking for these searches quote February dates and autumn deadlines to Gulf families, which is a date a parent books around and loses an entry over. Also ask your school which of Cambridge's six administrative zones it sits in, because the zone timetable is the one that applies.

faqs.question: My child writes too much and runs out of time. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the quickest fixes available because it requires no new content. Four to six sessions on answer-length discipline and pacing typically resolve it. The method is mechanical: time-box every answer to its mark value, write the halfway time on the paper before starting, and attempt a paper in reverse order occasionally to expose where the pacing collapses. Families are least willing to pay for this work because it does not feel like teaching, and it is worth more marks per hour than most alternatives.

faqs.question: Should revision follow the textbook order?
faqs.answer: No, and following it is one of the commonest planning errors. Revision should be ordered by mark weight: the heavily weighted topic the student cannot do comes before the lightly weighted topic they also cannot do. Textbook order reflects the sequence material was taught in, which has nothing to do with where the marks are. Map your child's topics against where they appear in the papers and how much they carry, and the right order usually becomes obvious in twenty minutes.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an IGCSE practical write-up for assessment?
faqs.answer: They can teach the conventions, explain how the mark scheme credits them, demonstrate on a different experiment and read what your child has written to say where it is unclear or unsupported. They cannot write it, rewrite it, complete it or edit it to a finished state, and cannot produce a worked version of your child's own task. The temptation to demonstrate by doing is real in paper-level work, which is why demonstration always happens on a different question.

faqs.question: Should a Sharjah student add Additional Mathematics 0606 to their subject list?
faqs.answer: If your child is heading towards A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level mathematics, it is the most useful signal available. It covers calculus and trigonometry beyond the 0580 syllabus, so coping with 0606 suggests the next step is realistic and struggling with it is information worth having in Year 11 rather than in the second term of a Diploma. Take it even where the school presents it as optional. Be aware that the local specialist pool for 0606 is thin, so allow longer to match a tutor.

faqs.question: What single question should I ask a prospective IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: How many full two-year cycles have you taught of this exact syllabus code at this exact tier. It is specific, checkable and sorts the market quickly. A tutor who answers with a degree, with years of general experience or with rapport has not answered it. Follow it with a mark-scheme question in your child's subject, such as what the scheme accepts as a source of error, and with two practical ones: do they hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and what happens if the match is wrong in week two.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mamsha.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE home tutor in Al Mamsha, the useful first step is paperwork rather than conversation. intro.heading: Nine subjects, two usable evenings, one budget
paragraphs: Al Nahda in Sharjah is a dense block of residential towers on the Dubai boundary, with schools on both sides of it and a large, cost-conscious expatriate population. Families here are typically paying substantial school fees already, often for more than one child, and the tutoring question arrives with a number attached: how much will this cost, and is it worth it?

That deserves a real answer rather than a brochure. The published market in this country runs from roughly AED 33 an hour at the entry level to AED 650 for premium examiner-led provision, which is a twentyfold range for something sold under the same word. Three of the six strongest pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and two quote United States dollars at families who transact in dirhams. So the first thing this page does is put the figures down with the names of whoever published them.

The second thing it does is widen the question. For a household in these towers, cost is not only the hourly rate. It is the number of subjects a candidate is entered for, which here is frequently eight, nine or ten. It is the value of an evening hour, which is scarce because of the crossing. It is the cost of a missed session, which is not zero. And it is the cost of a tier error, which is paid in a resit a year later rather than in a fee this term.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. In cost terms that removes the travel component of the rate — published in-home figures run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included — and it removes the scheduling waste that a visiting arrangement produces on a corridor where arrival times are unpredictable.

The rest of this page is arithmetic rather than argument. The published rates and what each tier buys. What a missed session actually costs. How to split a limited budget across nine subjects, which is the decision nobody writes about. The economics of a tier error. Three free things worth doing first. And whether to pay monthly or by session when the schedule itself is variable.

One honest caveat throughout. IB Gram does not publish a tariff on these pages, because the right figure depends on subject scarcity, tier and session length, and it is quoted after a free trial lesson. Every dirham figure below belongs to the named provider or rate survey that published it, read in October 2026. Where a figure could not be verified it is left out entirely rather than rounded into something plausible.

sections.heading: What IGCSE support actually costs a household here
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Nahda, Sharjah, in the sense families here mean, is one-to-one teaching for one child on the specification that child is entered for. IB Gram provides that over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. The published market, read in October 2026, sets the frame for what any of it costs.

At the entry level, Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified online subject tutors sit considerably higher: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IGCSE and IB tutors are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at around AED 270, and premium named or examiner-led provision advertised as high as AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits including travel run from about AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table placing the usual band at AED 180 to 350.

Monthly framing is more useful to households in these towers, because school fees are already a monthly line. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour-long sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work. Advertised packages in this market have included AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

What those numbers do not show is the part specific to this corridor: the cost of the evening itself. A household where children arrive home after half past four has roughly two usable weekday evenings a week, which means every hour bought is competing with homework rather than adding to it. That is why this page spends as much time on allocation as on rates.

sections.heading: The cost of a missed session is not zero
paragraphs: Every tutoring arrangement on this corridor eventually meets a bad afternoon: a longer crossing, a late bus, an unexpected school event. Most families treat a missed or rescheduled session as a neutral event, and it is not. It has three costs, and together they are the main reason tutoring arrangements here quietly stop working.

The first is the fee, depending on the cancellation terms. The second, larger cost is the homework cycle: work set at the previous session goes unmarked, so the next session starts by catching up instead of moving forward, and two weeks produce one week of progress. The third and largest is behavioural. A student who sees a slot move twice stops treating it as fixed, stops preparing for it, and the arrangement decays into a conversation.

The structural fix is to set the slot late enough that it survives a bad afternoon, which on this corridor usually means half past five or six rather than four. The secondary fix is to put the most important session at the weekend, where the road is irrelevant. Both are free, and both are more effective than any cancellation policy.

It is also worth asking any provider what happens to a missed session before signing anything. The answer tells you how the arrangement will behave in week five, which matters more than the hourly rate. The table below sets out what each kind of disruption actually costs a family in practice.

sections.heading: Splitting a budget across eight or nine subjects
paragraphs: This is the decision nobody writes about and every family here faces. A candidate entered for nine subjects cannot be tutored in nine, so a budget has to be allocated, and the allocation rule most families use — fund the subject with the lowest grade — is usually wrong.

Three better rules. First, fund the subject where a small amount of work converts into a whole grade, which is usually a subject sitting just below a boundary rather than the weakest one. Second, fund the subject whose skill transfers: English Language planning and argument structure improve answers in Business, Economics, History and the sciences at the same time, which makes it the highest-leverage single purchase in a large entry. Third, fund the subject where the loss is mechanical rather than conceptual, because mechanical losses are cheap to fix.

Against those, the rules that waste money. Funding the lowest grade regardless of distance from a boundary. Funding the subject the student dislikes most, which is usually a motivation problem rather than a teaching one. And spreading sessions thinly across three or four subjects, which reliably produces no visible movement anywhere and is the single commonest error in this district.

sections.heading: The price of a tier error, paid a year later
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake available in IGCSE is not a tutoring purchase at all. It is a tier entry that caps a grade below what a student needed, and it is paid for in a resit a year later rather than in a fee this term.

The mechanics are simple. On Cambridge Mathematics 0580 the choice is Core or Extended, and Core accesses grades C to G while Extended accesses A* to E. On Pearson 4MA1 it is Foundation, accessing grades 5 to 1, or Higher, accessing 9 to 4 with a grade 3 safety net. If a sixth form or a Ministry equivalency requirement needs a grade the tier cannot award, no amount of preparation produces it.

Costed out, that error means a November entry at minimum: an entry fee, a term of a tutor's time, and a student still working on a subject their cohort finished. In the worst case it means a delayed sixth-form place. Against that, a three-session block in Year 10 producing marked evidence for a tier conversation costs a few hundred dirhams at published qualified rates. Few purchases in this market have a clearer return.

The constraint is timing. Entries are submitted months before the papers, and the school decides on evidence. After the deadline the question is closed and the honest plan becomes using the available ceiling fully and considering November deliberately. Which is why the tier conversation belongs in Year 10, when nobody feels any urgency about it at all.

sections.heading: Three free things to do before paying anybody
paragraphs: A page that sells tutoring should be clear about the free support that comes first, because a family that uses it sometimes needs to buy nothing, and always buys less.

The first is the marked script. Ask the subject teacher for it rather than for the grade, and go through it with four labels: blank, attempted and abandoned, partially credited, and completed but wrong. The distribution is the diagnosis, and it is free. Blanks at the end mean timing; scattered blanks mean avoided topics; partial credit everywhere means method and command terms; completed but wrong means a genuine content gap.

The second is the subject teacher's own view. Ask which three topics they would prioritise if they had your child for an extra hour a week. Teachers answer that question well and are almost never asked it. Ask also whether the department runs a revision clinic, because many schools on both sides of this boundary do and attendance is often poor simply because families do not know it exists.

The third is the examinations officer: the syllabus code, the tier, the study-leave date and the November entry deadline, all in writing. Those four facts determine which practice material is correct, what grade is available, how many usable weeks a plan has, and whether a resit is a planned route. All free, all obtainable in a week, and all of it is material any competent tutor would ask for anyway.

A fourth item is free but less obvious: ask the school whether your child's set or tier can still be reviewed. The answer costs nothing, and it determines whether a paid evidence block is worth buying at all.

sections.heading: Monthly or per session, when the schedule is variable
paragraphs: Monthly packages are common in this market and they look like a discount. Advertised examples have included AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Whether they represent value for a household on this corridor depends almost entirely on whether the sessions will actually happen.

On a corridor where arrival times are unpredictable, a package that assumes eight sessions in a calendar month is a package that will lose one or two, and the discount rarely compensates for paying for hours that did not run. The questions to ask about any package are: what happens to a missed session, does unused credit carry forward, and can the arrangement be ended at the midpoint if the evidence says stop.

The second consideration is information. A package bought before anybody has read marked work is a commitment made without evidence, and the discount is being paid for with your ability to change course. A sensible sequence is a short diagnostic block first, then a package only if the diagnosis supports a block of that length, with a stated stopping condition.

IB Gram publishes no tariff on these pages. The rate depends on subject scarcity, tier and session length and is quoted after a free trial lesson. What we will always state is the number of sessions, the finish date and the review point, because an arrangement without those is a subscription rather than a plan.

sections.heading: Permits, approvals and the claims to refuse
paragraphs: A conspicuously low rate sometimes means a regulatory question has never been asked. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any page quoting an amount has invented it.

Because the permit costs nothing, there is no reasonable excuse for an independent tutor not to hold one, and asking is free. The permit also carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, which matters in a district this dense, where a family and a teacher are often neighbours in the same tower.

Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. For a child schooled across the boundary the applicable body is Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority. No tutoring provider, including IB Gram, holds approval, accreditation or a licence from either, and a KHDA educational services permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai.

And the claims that should end a conversation: a guarantee of a grade, any claimed regulator or board approval, a school described as a partner or client, a satisfaction figure or star rating without the number, date and method behind it, and any offer to write or complete assessed coursework. We make none of them, we publish no ratings, and we do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, because those belong to the boards and are published on their own sites.

faqs.question: What should a family in Al Nahda, Sharjah expect to pay for IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 give the range. Entry-level online sessions are advertised from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, qualified online subject tutors from about AED 150 to 300, and specialist IGCSE and IB tutors from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with premium examiner-led provision as high as AED 650. In-home visits including travel run from around AED 180 to 500. Those are other providers' figures. IB Gram quotes after a free trial, because scarcity, tier and session length all affect it.

faqs.question: My child is entered for nine subjects. Which should we actually pay for help in?
faqs.answer: Not the one with the lowest grade, usually. Fund the subject sitting just below a boundary, where a small amount of work converts into a whole grade. Then fund English Language technique, because planning and argument structure improve answers in Business, Economics, History and the sciences simultaneously. Then fund any mechanical loss — units, method lines, an avoided topic — because those are cheap to fix. And deliberately leave subjects alone: spreading sessions across three or four produces no visible movement in any of them.

faqs.question: Does a missed session really cost us anything beyond the fee?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the indirect costs are larger. Work set at the previous session goes unmarked, so the next session is spent catching up and two weeks produce one week of progress. Worse, a student who sees a slot move twice stops treating it as fixed and stops preparing for it, which is how arrangements on this corridor quietly decay into conversations. The fix is structural rather than contractual: set the slot late enough to survive a bad crossing, and put the hardest subject at the weekend.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to an apartment in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time. In cost terms that removes the travel component that published in-home rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour include, and it removes the scheduling waste a visiting arrangement produces on a corridor where arrival times are genuinely unpredictable.

faqs.question: Is a tutor at AED 50 an hour worth trying first?
faqs.answer: It depends on the diagnosis. Entry-level rates in this market, advertised from around AED 33 to 65, buy supervision, structure and company, which genuinely helps a disorganised student who works better with somebody present. They do not buy a diagnosis against a published mark scheme, so if the marked script shows partial credit spread across long questions, this tier will not move it. Ask also whether the tutor holds the MoHRE permit, which is free to obtain and therefore reasonable to expect.

faqs.question: How much does a tier error end up costing?
faqs.answer: A resit, a year later. Cambridge Core accesses grades C to G while Extended accesses A* to E; Pearson Foundation accesses 5 to 1 while Higher accesses 9 to 4 with a grade 3 safety net. If a sixth form or an equivalency requirement needs a grade the tier cannot award, no preparation produces it, and the remedy is a November entry with its fee, a term of tutoring and a student still working on a finished subject. A three-session evidence block in Year 10 costs a fraction of that.

faqs.question: What free help should we exhaust before paying anyone on this corridor?
faqs.answer: Three things. The marked script rather than the grade, read with four labels: blank, attempted and abandoned, partially credited, completed but wrong. The subject teacher's answer to which three topics they would prioritise, a question they are rarely asked and answer well. And any departmental revision clinic the school runs, which on both sides of this boundary is often under-attended purely because families do not know about it. Then get the code, tier and study-leave date in writing.

faqs.question: Should we pay monthly or by session given how often the evenings go wrong?
faqs.answer: Be careful with packages on this corridor. Advertised monthly plans in this market have included AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, and a plan assuming eight sessions in a month will usually lose one or two here. Ask what happens to a missed session, whether unused credit carries forward, and whether the arrangement can end at the midpoint. And never buy a package before marked work has been read.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to use a tutor based on the Sharjah side?
faqs.answer: For informal and centre-based options, often yes, because those are priced against local overheads. For specialist one-to-one work, no: that is priced by a regional online market where the boundary is irrelevant, so published qualified rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour apply on either side. What does differ is willingness to travel across the boundary at five in the afternoon, which shows up as waiting time rather than as a discount.

faqs.question: What is the smallest amount we can spend and still learn something useful?
faqs.answer: Three sessions. One reading a marked paper and naming the recurring error types, two fixing the largest, ending with your child attempting the same question type unaided. At published qualified rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour that is a few hundred dirhams, and the written diagnosis is yours whatever you decide next. Most families are quoted a term instead, so it is worth asking for the smallest option and noting whether it is offered.

faqs.question: Can a cheaper group class replace one-to-one for an IGCSE student here?
faqs.answer: For one purpose. A class retells a specification with structure at the lowest cost per hour, which suits a student who has fallen behind across a whole subject. It cannot examine your child's own script, so it cannot find an error pattern, and on this corridor it also adds a round trip at the worst hour of the day. If the marked paper shows two marks a question going missing on units and method, no number of classes will address it.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a student in these towers need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Its code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

faqs.question: Should we expect a tutoring provider here to hold SPEA or KHDA approval?
faqs.answer: No, and we will not imply otherwise. IB Gram holds no SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licence or partnership. You may see that claim on competing pages; it is the most dangerous sentence available in this market and it is checkable. A KHDA educational services permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. What you can verify about us is whether a tutor knows your child's specification.

faqs.question: What evidence should make us stop spending rather than spend more?
faqs.answer: Agree it before the first session. A reasonable standard is a second timed paper at the midpoint, marked against the published scheme and compared with the first by topic, plus your child being able to name their own weakest area unprompted. If neither has moved after four weeks, the plan or the match is wrong and continuing is paying for hope. A provider who cannot describe a stopping condition is selling a subscription with a tutor attached.

intro.heading: What actually fits into a Sharjah afternoon in Years 10 and 11
paragraphs: The IGCSE years are the first time a Sharjah student's evening is genuinely full. In Years 7 to 9 there is slack in the week. From September of Year 10 there is coursework, there are mocks, there is a two-year content load that nobody can cram, and there is the same fixed afternoon there always was. The question is not whether your child needs a tutor. It is how many usable hours exist in the week, and the honest answer in Al Nouf is fewer than you think.

Al Nouf lies inland, in Sharjah's residential belt, with no major school inside the district. Its students travel out to the Muwaileh and University City clusters or into central Sharjah, and a few go further into Dubai. Release falls between roughly 1.30pm and 2.45pm. The drive back at pick-up time runs thirty to fifty minutes, longer if there is a second collection at a second school. Arrival home at 3.30pm is normal; arrival at 2.45pm is not.

From that arrival, build forwards rather than backwards. A Year 10 student needs food, a change and twenty minutes of nothing before anything useful happens, which puts the first real slot at around 4.30pm. School-set work in Year 10 runs to ninety minutes on an ordinary day and considerably more in Year 11. A tutoring session has to sit in front of that work, not after it, because a session that starts at 7.30pm after two hours of homework is a session the student attends rather than uses.

This is where a home visit struggles in this district specifically. A tutor driving in for 4.30pm is in the same traffic that delayed your own journey, so the hour starts at 4.45pm and ends on time anyway. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE regardless; home tuition is an India-only service for us. Every Sharjah lesson is live, one-to-one, over video, in a slot held in Gulf Standard Time and movable within the week when a school deadline lands badly.

The rest of this page is practical. There is a table of what session length and frequency suit each year group, a map from school cluster to first workable slot, the Sharjah market rates expressed as cost per contact hour rather than cost per hour, and the June and November series read as a set of deadlines. The IB page for this neighbourhood takes the same timetable question from the Diploma side; the combined page answers the bare near-me phrasing. Read the rate table with one question in mind that almost nobody asks: not what an hour costs, but what an hour that actually happened at full attention costs, because in this district those are two different numbers and the gap between them is where tutoring budgets quietly disappear.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-nouf.programmesIntro: Three entry points lead into the IGCSE years in Sharjah, and each one changes how much of the first term is repair work. It is worth being clear which applies before anybody books a session, because the three need different starting plans.

programmes.name: Lower secondary, before the IGCSE course begins
programmes.description: Cambridge Lower Secondary or a school's own key-stage-3 scheme. No external examinations, which is exactly why gaps form here unnoticed. Algebraic manipulation, scientific notation and extended writing are the three that cost marks two years later, and they are cheap to fix now and expensive to fix in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one stage where an Al Nouf family has real afternoon flexibility, because Year 7 and 8 homework is light and a 4pm slot works. Families who use Year 9 for a single weekly hour on algebra and written explanation arrive in Year 10 needing far less support, and a budget-band tutor is often entirely adequate at this stage.

programmes.name: The two-year IGCSE course, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Seven to nine subjects, tiered as Core and Extended with Cambridge or Foundation and Higher with Pearson. Assessment is largely by terminal examination in the June or November series, with some subjects carrying coursework or practical components. The content is paced across two years and cannot be compressed into the final term.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah the tier decision is usually taken by the school at the end of Year 9, and parents frequently do not learn the outcome until a report arrives. Ask the subject teacher directly. A Core-tier student drilled on Extended material and an Extended-tier student fed Core questions both waste the same sessions, and the error only surfaces in the exam hall.

programmes.name: Joining an IGCSE course mid-stream
programmes.description: Students arriving from a CBSE, Ministry-curriculum or American school part-way through the course face a different problem from their classmates: not weak understanding but a different coverage order. Topics the class met last term may be entirely new, and the student's apparent weakness is actually a gap in sequence.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah sees a lot of this because families move between school systems within the emirate and across from Ajman and Dubai. The first job is an audit of what has and has not been covered, subject by subject, against the syllabus. Done properly that takes one session and saves a term of guessing at what the student does not know.

programmes.name: What the IGCSE grades are actually for
programmes.description: Most Sharjah British-curriculum students continue to AS and A Level in three or four subjects, and entry requirements are set on IGCSE grades. The step up in depth is larger than the step into IGCSE was, so a borderline Extended grade in a subject your child intends to continue is a Year 12 problem rather than a Year 11 one.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students submit five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Check the current rule on the Ministry's own channel before dropping any subject for timetable reasons.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-nouf.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Sharjah families ask about, with the syllabus code where that is what decides the match. Each note says where the marks go, since that is what a weekly hour should be spent on.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers, no coursework. Extended candidates lose marks to algebra under time pressure and to multi-topic problems. Timed papers with the mark scheme open beat more worked examples every time.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Theory papers plus, for Cambridge, the alternative-to-practical paper. That paper tests experimental reasoning rather than recall and is where Sharjah Extended candidates most often underperform. It needs its own sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry carry the heaviest weight and the heaviest failure rate. The qualitative-analysis tables and organic nomenclature are memorisable and routinely left unlearned until April.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: Large content volume with marks tied to exact terminology. A loosely correct answer scores nothing where the mark scheme names a term. Transport in plants, genetics and homeostasis recur as weak points.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading comprehension, a disciplined summary task and directed writing with a stated purpose and audience. Students lose summary marks by lifting sentences from the passage rather than reformulating them.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450 / 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study led, with the marks in application and evaluation rather than definition. A student who knows every term and cannot apply it to the stimulus material stalls around a C and stays there.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Theory of computer systems plus algorithms and programming. Pseudocode conventions and trace tables are mechanical marks students throw away, and binary and hexadecimal conversion rewards straightforward drill.

subjects.name: ICT (0417)
subjects.description: Practical papers assessed on exact software behaviour: formatting, file handling, spreadsheet functions. Technologically confident students still lose marks for not following the instruction literally, which is a teachable habit.

subjects.name: Economics (0455 / 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks: axes labelled, curve shifted correctly, new equilibrium identified. Data-response answers must quote figures from the extract rather than reason generally.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: Sat alongside the international curriculum because Arabic is mandatory in UAE private schools. It does not count towards the five subjects required for Ministry equivalency, which surprises families, and it still needs preparation.

sections.heading: Session length and frequency by year group, not by budget
paragraphs: Start with the shape of the session rather than the price of it. A Year 9 student can use ninety minutes. A Year 11 student in March, three hours into an evening of school work, cannot, and buying them ninety minutes is buying forty-five minutes of learning and forty-five minutes of fatigue. The table below is what works in practice for Sharjah students at each stage.

The frequency column is the one families get wrong in both directions. Booking three sessions a week in Year 10 crowds out the independent practice that actually consolidates learning, and a student who never works alone never builds exam stamina. Booking one session a month achieves nothing at all, because the gap is long enough for the previous session to evaporate. Weekly is the floor that works.

Session length should also shrink as the year progresses rather than grow. In September there is content to teach and ninety minutes is justified. By April the job is timed papers and correction, and two focused forty-five minute slots beat one long one because the correction happens while the attempt is still fresh in the student's mind.

One caveat for Al Nouf specifically. If the arrival home is genuinely 3.30pm and there is a sibling collection after that, the honest number of weekly slots your household has is two, and one of them is probably a weekend morning. Planning for three will produce two attended sessions and a quiet resentment about the third.

sections.heading: From school cluster to the first slot that holds
paragraphs: Al Nouf imports its timetable from wherever its children study, so the school cluster is the real input to any schedule. The table maps cluster to release time, journey back and the earliest session that will reliably happen. Find your own row instead of working from an average, because the spread between the best and worst case here is nearly three hours.

The Muwaileh and University City rows are the ones that apply to most Al Nouf families. They are close in kilometres and slow in practice. Families who use a school bus for the older child, or who can shift their own collection twenty minutes later, consistently report a calmer afternoon and a session that actually starts on time.

The Dubai rows deserve particular attention, because a surprising number of Sharjah families drive south for school. A Deira or Al Barsha finish plus the northbound return puts arrival home after five and often after six. For those households the weekday slot is realistically a single evening hour, and the weekend morning stops being an alternative and becomes the main session.

Test the last column against your own week before you commit. Five days of recorded arrival times will tell you more than any table, and most parents find they are later than they believed. If the real figure is worse than the row suggests, take the later slot honestly rather than booking the earlier one and missing it twice a month.

sections.heading: Coursework, mocks and the weeks when the slot has to move
paragraphs: The IGCSE year has four or five weeks in it when the normal schedule cannot hold, and planning for them in September is the difference between an arrangement that survives and one that lapses. Coursework and practical deadlines are school-set and cluster together. Mocks occupy a fortnight. The week before a school report, everything is due at once.

Our answer is a primary slot plus one agreed alternative day, fixed at the start. When a coursework deadline lands on the usual Tuesday, the hour moves to Thursday that week and returns afterwards. That sounds trivial and it is the single most load-bearing piece of administration in the whole arrangement, because the alternative is a cancellation, and cancellations are what actually end tutoring relationships in Sharjah.

Mock fortnight should change the content of the sessions, not just the timing. The useful work during mocks is not revision for the next paper; it is going through the paper just sat, question by question, against the mark scheme, while the student still remembers what they were thinking. That post-mortem is worth more than three sessions of general revision and almost nobody books it.

A home visit cannot absorb any of this well, and that is a structural point rather than a criticism. Moving an in-home session means a second journey for the tutor, so in practice it gets cancelled instead. Over a Year 11 that is four or five lost sessions at exactly the moments when they mattered most.

sections.heading: Cost per contact hour, not cost per hour
paragraphs: The number families compare is the hourly rate. The number that decides value is the cost of an hour that actually happened at full attention. Those two diverge fast in a district like Al Nouf. An in-home session at the Bestimate band of AED 180 to 350 that starts ten minutes late and finishes on time is not an hour; it is fifty minutes at an hour's price, and across thirty weeks that is five hours bought and not received.

The market bands themselves, read in October 2026, are these. Budget online tutors run roughly AED 33 to 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. A specialist runs AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

Now apply the attendance arithmetic. A monthly in-home package at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions is eight contact hours. An online package at AED 799 for eight sessions is eight contact hours. If two of the in-home sessions are cancelled across a term because they could not be moved, the effective cost per received hour rises by a third while the online figure does not move at all.

None of these are IB Gram prices. They are the published figures of the providers named, cited so you can check them, and they are here to let you work out your own cost per received hour rather than per advertised hour. For our pricing, take the free trial lesson and ask against your child's actual subject list.
