sections.heading: A 4.30pm video slot against a 4.50pm arrival
paragraphs: The comparison deserves to be made on its merits. In-home tuition has real strengths: physical presence, easier handling of a distractible student, independence from a connection. Those are genuine and we will not pretend otherwise. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the in-home column below describes what the Sharjah market sells, not something we are offering you.

The decisive difference in this district is not quality of attention, it is who is available. An in-home arrangement in Al Nouf draws from the people willing to drive inland in the late afternoon. For Mathematics 0580 that pool may be adequate. For Computer Science 0478 or ICT 0417 it may contain nobody who has taught the specification, and the family ends up with a competent generalist and a disappointing August.

The second difference is what happens in a disrupted week, which in Years 10 and 11 is one week in six. An online slot moves. A journey-dependent slot gets cancelled. That is not a small operational detail; it is the mechanism by which an arrangement that looked fine in October has quietly stopped by February.

If a home visit genuinely is right for your child, book it from a provider who offers it, and ask two questions before you do: the tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit, and how many full cycles they have taught of the exact syllabus code your child is sitting. Both are reasonable questions and the answers are informative.

sections.heading: Two years, paced properly, counted back from the series
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so disregard any page that quotes a February window to a Sharjah family. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

Counting backwards from a series makes the pacing obvious. Entry deadlines are handled by the school months ahead. Mocks sit a term before. Coursework and practicals land earlier still. The revision peak belongs in the eight to twelve weeks before the papers, which means the content has to be learned by then, which means Year 10 cannot be the year nothing happened.

One Cambridge administrative point is worth naming because Cambridge names it itself: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your school which zone it sits in and work from that timetable, not a generic one.

The resit decision is the one most often made too slowly. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The autumn entry window closes not long after August results. Decide the rule in advance: which grade in which subject triggers a November entry, written down before results day rather than debated afterwards.

sections.heading: SPEA, mandatory subjects and the timetable space they take
paragraphs: Al Nouf's private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and, in Sharjah's case, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That breadth is why timetable shape is more uniform across Sharjah schools than families arriving from Dubai expect.

It also explains something parents often misread as their school being awkward. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in UAE private schools whatever international curriculum is licensed, and they occupy real timetable space alongside eight or nine IGCSE subjects. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time in forty-minute lesson units and advises that no such lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes, which gives a sense of the load.

Two further KHDA requirements shape what tutoring can legitimately do here. Separate classes are required for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes not permitted because curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. And for the mandatory UAE subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is not allowed. A tutor cannot substitute their own syllabus here.

What no regulator does is check your tutor. SPEA regulates schools. Private tutoring sits with MoHRE under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; the permit is granted free of charge for two years, is open to school teachers, public and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app and e-services system. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with IGCSE coursework
paragraphs: Several subjects carry school-assessed components, and that is where the integrity line matters. This market contains providers selling completed assessed work; one page in this research advertises finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. For a Sharjah student the consequence of buying assessed work is not a lower grade, it is a malpractice finding against the qualification.

The boundary in plain terms. A tutor may teach the skills the task requires, explain how the mark scheme awards them, model the approach on a different example, read a draft the student has written and say where it is unclear, unsupported or off-brief, and teach referencing, data handling and experimental write-up conventions properly.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, complete or edit the work to a finished state, and may not produce a worked version of the student's own task. We also do not reproduce or supply Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter rather than a judgement call.

One more boundary. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and check the current policy document. Either way, we will not arrange for a child to be privately tutored by the teacher who marks their school work.

sections.heading: Booking a slot in Al Nouf that is still running in April
paragraphs: Measure before you book. Record for five days the time your child actually came through the door and which afternoons carry an activity. That gives you the number of workable slots your household genuinely has, which in this district is usually two, one of which may be a weekend morning. Everything else follows from that number.

Then take the earlier of the two. Attention is better, school homework has not started, and an overrun of ten minutes costs nothing. A 4.30pm slot that holds every week outperforms a 7pm slot that moves twice a month, and in Year 11 the difference is roughly six sessions across the spring term.

Use the free trial as a diagnosis. Send the subject, the board, the syllabus code, the tier and one recent piece of marked work. A specialist should tell you within the hour whether the gap is content, technique or sequence from a transfer, and those three need three different plans. A trial that produces warmth and no diagnosis has told you something about the provider.

Then review at four weeks against evidence you set in advance: which errors have stopped recurring, what is happening on timed questions, whether the work between sessions is being done. If it is not there, we change the specialist rather than defend the match. Ask any provider you are considering what their answer to that question is, and listen for whether they have one. One last thing, and it is the part only your household can do. The sessions that work here are the ones where the room is quiet, the connection was checked before the slot rather than during it, and the hour is treated as fixed when something else comes up. That is not a lecture, it is the difference between thirty sessions and twenty-two across a Year 11.

faqs.question: How long should an IGCSE session be for a Year 11 student in Al Nouf?
faqs.answer: Forty-five minutes twice a week beats ninety minutes once, particularly after January. By Year 11 the student is already two or three hours into school work by the time an evening session starts, and the back half of a long session is fatigue rather than learning. Two shorter contacts also catch a misunderstanding before it sets, and the small task set between them is more likely to be done than one large one. In the final four weeks, two or three short sessions a week on past papers is the right shape.

faqs.question: Why does IB Gram teach Sharjah students online rather than visiting Al Nouf?
faqs.answer: Home visits are something IB Gram offers only in India. Across the UAE every lesson is live, one-to-one and over video. The reasoning is specific to districts like this one. An in-home arrangement in inland Sharjah selects a tutor by who will drive there after four o'clock, which tells you nothing about whether they have taught Cambridge 0620 at Extended tier. And a 4.30pm visit starts when the car arrives, so you buy an hour and receive fifty minutes, thirty times a year.

faqs.question: What is the real cost per hour once sessions get cancelled?
faqs.answer: Higher than advertised, and this is where in-home arrangements lose their apparent advantage. Published in-home rates run AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table and AED 200 to 500 with independent tutors, read in October 2026. If two sessions a term cannot be moved and are cancelled, the cost per received hour rises by roughly a third. A monthly in-home package at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for eight contact hours can exceed AED 250 per hour actually received, against about AED 100 for an AED 799 online package.

faqs.question: My child joined a Sharjah IGCSE course halfway through. Is that a content problem?
faqs.answer: Usually it is a sequence problem rather than a weakness, and treating it as weakness wastes a term. Schools cover the syllabus in different orders, so a transferring student may never have met topics the class did last year while being ahead on others. The first job is an audit: go through the syllabus content list subject by subject and mark what has and has not been taught. That takes one session and replaces three months of guessing about what the student does not know.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge series do Sharjah candidates sit, and when are entries?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting a February window to a Sharjah parent is giving a date that is wrong for this country. Final entries are handled by the school months before the papers. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise.

faqs.question: How do you handle the fortnight of mock examinations?
faqs.answer: We change what the sessions are for rather than pausing them. During mocks the valuable work is not revising for the next paper, it is going through the paper just sat, question by question, against the mark scheme, while the student still remembers their reasoning. That post-mortem produces a specific list of fixable habits. Book it before the mocks start, because the window closes fast once the next topic begins, and almost no family thinks to schedule it in advance.

faqs.question: Do you cover both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel for the same student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Sharjah it is common to need both. Several schools run Cambridge for some subjects and Pearson for others, so one student can sit two boards in the same year. We match a separate specialist per subject and per board rather than giving you one tutor who knows one specification and is guessing at the other. Find the codes on the statement of entry: Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended tiers, Pearson Specification A is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher.

faqs.question: Is a group class cheaper in a useful way, or only on paper?
faqs.answer: Only on paper, for the problem most Year 11 families are trying to solve. A group of three at a reduced per-student rate is genuinely good value for content revision, where everyone needs the same material explained. It is close to useless for correcting the individual technical habits that cost a specific student six marks a paper, because the tutor is managing three error patterns at once. If your child's content knowledge is sound and the marks are leaking elsewhere, pay for one-to-one.

faqs.question: What does SPEA regulate, and does it cover private tutors in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and its powers are broad: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. It does not regulate private tutors. That sits with the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which introduced a private tuition work permit granted free of charge for two years. Ask any tutor for theirs. No tutoring provider in this market, including us, holds approval or accreditation from SPEA or KHDA, and a claim of that kind is the point at which to ask for a document.

faqs.question: How much timetable space do Arabic and Islamic Education take alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: More than families expect, and it is a federal requirement rather than a school preference. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in UAE private schools whatever international curriculum is licensed. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time in forty-minute lesson units and advises that no such lesson is shorter than twenty-five minutes. Those lessons sit alongside eight or nine IGCSE subjects, which is part of why Year 11 feels crowded. Arabic as a First Language 0508 also does not count towards the five subjects required for Ministry equivalency.

faqs.question: Can a tutor check my child's IGCSE coursework before submission?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read what your child has written and tell them where it is unclear, unsupported or does not answer the brief, explain how the mark scheme awards marks, and teach referencing and write-up conventions. That is useful and legitimate. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it, complete it or edit it to a finished state, and cannot produce a worked version of your child's own task. Providers in this market sell finished assessed work outright; buying it converts a grade problem into a malpractice problem.

faqs.question: Should a Year 9 student in Sharjah start tutoring, or is that early?
faqs.answer: Year 9 is the cheapest year to fix anything. There are no external examinations, homework is light enough that an afternoon slot is easy, and the three things that cost IGCSE marks later are all addressable now: algebraic manipulation, written explanation under a command term, and the habit of checking work. A single weekly hour in Year 9 reduces how much support Year 11 needs, and a budget-band tutor is often entirely adequate at this stage. It is also the year nobody books, because nothing feels urgent yet.

faqs.question: What happens when a coursework deadline lands on our usual tutoring day?
faqs.answer: The session moves to the alternative day we agreed at the start, then returns to its normal slot. That fallback day is the most load-bearing piece of administration in the whole arrangement, because the alternative is a cancellation. Every IGCSE year contains four or five weeks where the normal schedule cannot hold, between coursework, practicals, mocks and report deadlines. An arrangement that can only be cancelled rather than moved loses all five, and it loses them at the worst moments.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match an IGCSE tutor for a Sharjah student?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Extended-tier subjects such as Mathematics 0580, English as a Second Language 0510 or the separate sciences, usually within two to four days and often inside forty-eight hours. For thinner subjects such as Computer Science 0478 or ICT 0417, expect five to ten days, and expect us to tell you whether the specialist is UAE-based or teaching into your evening from another timezone. Families willing to take a weekend-morning slot are matched faster across every subject, because the Sharjah weekday evening is the most contested window there is.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting if the June papers are ten weeks away?
faqs.answer: Ten weeks is enough to change a grade if the problem is technique and not enough to rebuild two years of content. The distinction matters because the two need opposite plans. If content is broadly known and marks are going to timing, command-term misreading and presentation, ten weeks of timed papers with mark-scheme correction works and works reliably. If the content was never learned, consider whether a November entry is the better decision and use the ten weeks to build properly rather than to panic.

intro.heading: Does the district actually change the answer?
paragraphs: Al Qasimia sits in the middle of old Sharjah, minutes from Al Majaz, Al Khan, Abu Shagara and Al Nahda. Search for an IGCSE tutor from any of those addresses and you will notice something: the results are largely the same people. Central Sharjah is one tutoring market with several postcodes, and a family comparing districts is mostly comparing drive times.

That matters because the drive is what the premium pays for. Across published UAE rate cards, an in-home visit is quoted between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, while a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300. The difference is a car. It is not better knowledge of Cambridge 0580's paper structure, and it is not a better understanding of why a candidate loses marks describing an observation as a conclusion.

There is a second thing worth comparing, and almost nobody does it: what each district's schools actually enter their students for. Al Qasimia and the streets around it carry a dense mix of Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum schools, which means plenty of IGCSE candidates sit their papers at schools whose main curriculum is something else. Their mock calendars, their teaching pace and their entry patterns differ from a purely British school's, and a tutor needs to know which one they are dealing with.

Then there is the part that does not change at all. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates. The mark scheme for 0620 is the same in Al Khan as in Al Qasimia. The command-term traps are identical. The permit a private tutor needs is federal. Your child's grade is decided by a script marked against a published scheme, and no district has a local edition of that scheme.

So the honest comparison runs like this: districts differ in commute, school mix and local supply density, and they do not differ in what the examination demands. Which is why we match on the board and the code rather than on the address, and teach one to one over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE - that service exists only in India - so the same specialist is available whether you are in Al Qasimia, Al Majaz or across the boundary in Al Nahda.

One caveat before the comparison. Local supply does matter for one group: younger children who need an adult beside them to stay on task. If that is your situation, the in-home premium may be worth paying and we are not the right provider, because we do not offer UAE home visits. For a Year 10 or 11 candidate working through papers, the specialist match matters more than the presence, and that is who this page is written for.
The sections below compare the districts properly, then compare provider models, then set out what is fixed regardless of where you live.

subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Edexcel
subjects.description: Electricity and graph-gradient work dominate the losses. The alternative-to-practical paper is a separate skill - naming instruments, identifying variables, suggesting improvements - and it is coachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole ratios, electrolysis products and organic conditions, plus the language problem: the scheme wants the observation, not the conclusion. Precision here recovers marks the student has already earned.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content is memorisable, so the marks go on command words and diagrams. Genetic crosses, transport in plants and experimental design are where an hour converts most directly into marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics for Indian-curriculum crossovers
subjects.description: Students moving from a CBSE or ICSE school into an IGCSE entry meet different question phrasing and a different expectation about showing method. The content overlap is large; the examination behaviour is not, and that gap is quick to close with board-specific practice.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading analysis carry the grade. Summarising when asked to analyse effect is the standard loss, and timed writing annotated against the mark scheme moves this subject faster than almost any other.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Common across central Sharjah schools where English is the language of instruction but not of the home. Note-making, summary word limits and register shifts are formulaic enough to coach precisely.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (0450 / 0455)
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward structure: define, apply to the case, evaluate with a judgement. Economics diagram accuracy is cheap to fix and frequently left to the student to work out alone.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions and trace tables cause more lost marks than programming ability. It is also one of the harder subjects to staff locally at a weekday hour, in any district.

sections.heading: Four central Sharjah districts, compared honestly
paragraphs: A family in Al Qasimia asking whether they would do better searching from an Al Majaz or Al Khan address deserves a straight answer: marginally, and not in the way they expect. Local supply density does vary. Al Majaz has the deepest pool because it has been the emirate's tutoring district longest. Al Khan benefits from short school runs. Al Nahda has the largest share of families commuting into Dubai schools, which changes the hour more than the supply.

What does not vary much is the quality distribution. The same generalist-heavy pattern appears in every district: plenty of people who will teach maths across several year groups, fewer who know one board's paper structure in detail, and very few who have taught a specific syllabus code to grade standard for years. That shape is a property of the market, not of the postcode.

The second real difference is the school mix, and it is the one worth paying attention to. Districts with a heavier Indian-curriculum school presence produce IGCSE candidates whose school is primarily teaching something else for most cohorts. Their mocks land at different times, their teaching sequence differs, and the question of which board they are entered for is genuinely uncertain until somebody checks. In a predominantly British-curriculum catchment, that question answers itself.

The third difference is the commute, which decides the hour rather than the tutor. From Al Qasimia, a school in Muwaileh or across the Dubai boundary turns a five o'clock slot into a five-forty slot. That is worth knowing before a time is agreed, and it is the one variable an online arrangement removes entirely.

sections.heading: What the travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: The in-home premium is the single largest avoidable line in a central Sharjah tutoring budget, and it is almost never itemised. A tutor driving to your building spends real time doing it, and that time is priced into the rate whether or not anybody says so.

Compare the published bands. A qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour across UAE rate cards. An in-home visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed. Monthly packages seen in the market include about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. The arithmetic is not subtle: the same teaching hour costs materially more when somebody drives to deliver it.

What the premium does buy is genuine, and worth stating fairly. A person in the room can see a student's exercise book, can watch them work without a camera angle problem, and can be harder to ignore than a screen. For some students, particularly younger ones and those with attention difficulties, that is worth paying for. For a Year 11 candidate working through timed papers, it is worth much less than having the right specialist.

What the premium never buys is subject knowledge. A longer drive does not make a tutor better at 0625 Paper 6. If a family in Al Qasimia is paying the top of the in-home band, the right question is what else that money could have bought - and the usual honest answer is more hours with somebody who knows the paper.

sections.heading: Why the board matters more than the neighbourhood
paragraphs: If you take one practical step from this comparison, take this one: find out which board and code your child is entered for before you talk to any tutor. In a district with a mixed school population, this is not obvious, and families frequently get it wrong.

The codes are the giveaway. 0580, 0620, 0625 and 0500 are Cambridge. 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4EB1 are Pearson Edexcel. They appear on the statement of entry and in the exam information the school circulates, and the exams officer can confirm them in one email. A tutor who does not ask for the code is not going to use it, which tells you something.

Why it matters so much: the paper structures differ, the question phrasing differs, and the preparation differs accordingly. Cambridge maths uses a tiered pattern; Pearson sets two equally weighted papers. A tutor fluent in one board will give confident, well-meant and wrong advice about the other's papers. For a student who has been practising the wrong board's past papers for a term, the discovery usually arrives in a mock.

This is also where an Indian-curriculum crossover needs care. A student with solid CBSE mathematics can be entirely competent and still lose marks on an IGCSE paper because the expectation about showing method and the phrasing of questions differ. That is examination behaviour rather than mathematics, and two or three board-specific sessions usually fix it.

Ask for the tier as well as the code. Core and Extended at Cambridge, or Foundation and Higher on an Edexcel paper, change both the content a student must cover and the grade available to them. A family who knows the code and the tier can brief any tutor in one sentence, which is more than most enquiries in this market manage.

sections.heading: Comparing provider models instead of districts
paragraphs: Once you accept that the districts are broadly similar, the useful comparison is between kinds of provider. There are five in this market and they differ on things that matter more than location: who the tutor is, what happens if they leave, whether a trial exists, and whether a rate is published at all.

Agencies and platforms carry a pool, so a tutor who leaves can be replaced without the family starting again. An independent tutor found through a neighbour offers continuity and local knowledge, and no fallback. A tuition centre offers structure and group economics, and cannot keep an individual error log. A university student offers a low rate and limited course-specific experience. And some well-known international marketplaces quote in dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in.

A striking feature of this market is how little is published. Three of six ranking competitor pages in our research set carry no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. One asks the price in its own FAQ and declines to answer it. Reading six pages and learning nothing about cost is a poor experience and an unnecessary one, which is why the AED bands appear on this page with their source and the month they were read.

Our own model, stated plainly so it can be compared: a matching platform with a pool of subject specialists, online one-to-one delivery, a free trial lesson before payment, tutor replacement without restarting the plan, and no UAE premises. We hold no approval, licence or accreditation from any UAE education authority, and we do not describe ourselves as approved by one.

sections.heading: Looking across the boundary: Dubai and Ajman options
paragraphs: Families in this part of Sharjah routinely look over two boundaries. Dubai is minutes away from Al Nahda and Al Taawun, and Ajman is a short drive north. Both change the calculation in ways worth knowing.

Dubai has more tutors, more specialists and higher prices. Its private school sector is substantially larger - Dubai recorded 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25 - so the tutoring market is deeper too. An in-home tutor travelling from Dubai to Al Qasimia will price the journey accordingly, which usually makes it the most expensive option on the table. Online, the same Dubai-based specialist costs no more to reach than a Sharjah-based one.

Ajman is the reverse: fewer schools, thinner local supply, and a regulatory difference worth noting. Private schools in Ajman, along with Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate authority, while Sharjah's private schools fall under the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Families with children at Ajman schools and a home in Sharjah are therefore dealing with two different regulators, which affects school processes rather than tutoring.

The neat conclusion is that crossing a boundary changes price and supply but not the examination. A Pearson 4CH1 candidate in Al Qasimia, Al Nahda or Ajman sits the same paper, marked to the same scheme, in the same series. Which is the argument for choosing the best specialist rather than the nearest one, and for a format that makes that possible.

sections.heading: What is identical in every district
paragraphs: Having compared what varies, it is worth being precise about what does not, because this is where families waste the most effort. The examination is national and international, not local.

Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two - the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Entries are made by the school's centre, and each Cambridge centre belongs to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, which is a property of the centre rather than the neighbourhood.

The permit position is federal too. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so ignore any figure quoted at you, in any district.

And the academic-honesty boundary is identical everywhere. A tutor may teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work. A tutor may not write, draft or edit assessed coursework, and IB Gram does not supply completed coursework of any kind. Essay mills appear in these search results charging thousands of dirhams, and the malpractice consequence attaches to the student, wherever the student lives.

sections.heading: So what should a family in Al Qasimia actually do?
paragraphs: The comparison leads somewhere specific. Since the districts are similar, the supply is generalist-weighted everywhere, and the examination is identical, the decision that remains is about matching and format rather than geography.

Step one is the code. Email the exams officer, confirm the board and syllabus code for every subject, and ask for the school's internal entry-change deadline in writing. Those three facts shape everything else and cost one message. Step two is a marked script: a recent mock, marked against the published scheme, which tells you whether the problem is content, technique or timing. Those are different problems with different fixes and different costs.

Step three is choosing a format deliberately rather than by habit. If your child is nine and needs somebody sitting beside them, the in-home premium may be worth paying, and we are not the right provider for that - we do not offer UAE home visits. If your child is fifteen, working through papers, and needs somebody who knows 0625 Paper 6, then paying for a drive is paying for the wrong thing.

Step four is a trial. Ours is free, one-to-one over live video, and it produces a marked script you keep whether or not you continue. That is a low-cost way to answer the question this whole page has been circling: not which district has better tutors, but which tutor knows your child's paper.

If you do decide to hire locally, the same four steps still apply, and the four questions in the first conversation are the same. Nothing on this page depends on choosing us; it depends on leading with the code and the script rather than with the postcode, because that is the order in which the decision actually gets better.

faqs.question: Would we find better IGCSE tutors by searching from Al Majaz instead of Al Qasimia?
faqs.answer: Marginally more of them, not better ones. Al Majaz has the deepest local pool in central Sharjah because it has been the emirate's tutoring district longest, but the quality distribution is the same everywhere: many generalists, fewer board-specific teachers, very few who have taught one syllabus code to grade standard for years. The districts share one market and largely the same names. What does change by district is the commute, which sets the hour a session can start, and that is the variable an online arrangement removes.

faqs.question: Do tutors charge more to visit Al Qasimia than nearby districts?
faqs.answer: In-home quotes track the journey, so an address further from a tutor's base costs more, and a tutor travelling from Dubai costs most of all. Across published UAE rate cards, in-home visits are quoted between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor teaching online. The premium is real and it pays for driving. It does not improve anybody's knowledge of a Cambridge paper, which is why we do not sell it.

faqs.question: Al Qasimia schools run several curricula - how do I identify my child's board?
faqs.answer: Look for the code. 0580, 0620, 0625 and 0500 are Cambridge; 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1 are Pearson Edexcel. The code appears on the statement of entry and in the exam information the school circulates, and the exams officer can confirm it in one email. This matters most in districts like this one where schools run more than one curriculum, and a child can be at an Indian-curriculum school while sitting a British board's papers in some subjects.

faqs.question: My child moved from a CBSE school into IGCSE entries. What changes?
faqs.answer: Less content than you fear and more examination behaviour than you expect. The mathematics and science overlap is substantial, but IGCSE questions are phrased differently, the expectation about showing method is stricter, and command terms are treated as precise instructions. A capable student can lose marks for reasons that have nothing to do with knowledge. Two or three board-specific sessions working through past papers, marked against the published scheme, usually closes that gap faster than any amount of additional content teaching.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in central Sharjah better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It is cheaper per hour and it cannot do the thing that matters most in Year 11. A group class covers content on a fixed schedule; it cannot keep an individual error log, mark one student's timed papers against the scheme every week, or decide that this particular candidate should skip a topic and drill another. For a confident student wanting structure, a centre works. For a candidate underperforming on paper, the individual script analysis is the whole intervention, and it is not available in a group.

faqs.question: Can we use a Dubai-based tutor while living in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Online, easily, and at no travel premium. Dubai's market is deeper - the emirate recorded 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25 - so more specialists are based there. In-home, a Dubai tutor driving to Al Qasimia will price the journey, which usually makes it the most expensive option available. Since the examination is identical, the sensible approach is to choose the specialist on course experience and let the format remove the geography. That is precisely what we do.

faqs.question: Does it matter that Ajman schools have a different regulator?
faqs.answer: For school processes, yes; for tutoring, almost not at all. Private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, while Sharjah's are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods. If you live in Sharjah and your child attends school in Ajman, you deal with both. The examination board, the series, the mark scheme and the tutor permit are the same either way.

faqs.question: What should a first conversation with any tutor cover?
faqs.answer: Four questions, none of which need subject knowledge from you. Which board and code is my child entered for, and how do you know? How many papers are there and what is each worth? Name the three topics where candidates lose the most marks in this subject. What will you do differently in the last six weeks? A specialist answers in specifics and often corrects your premise. A generalist answers with reassurance about confidence, which is pleasant and not what you are buying.

faqs.question: Are the dirham figures quoted here IB Gram's own prices?
faqs.answer: No. They are market bands drawn from published UAE rate cards and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table, read in October 2026, and they are here so you can judge any quote against something checkable - including ours. Three of six ranking pages in our competitor research publish no price at all, and two of the remaining ones quote in US dollars, which UAE families do not transact in. Ask us directly for our own figure, and start with the free trial lesson, which costs nothing.

faqs.question: What happens if our tutor becomes unavailable mid-term?
faqs.answer: We match another specialist in the same course and carry the written plan across, so the student does not restart from a diagnostic conversation. This is the practical advantage of a pool over an individual arrangement: a family who found a tutor through a neighbour has to begin the whole search again, usually in the term when they can least afford the disruption. We also change tutors on request if the fit is wrong, which we check deliberately at session six.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Al Qasimia need a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is federal rather than local. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Since it costs nothing, asking is reasonable.

faqs.question: When are the exams, and is a resit possible if June goes badly?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, and results from a November series reach students in January - the November 2025 cohort received theirs on 22 January 2026. A resit is therefore a real option, provided the receiving sixth form or university accepts a January result and the entry route is confirmed with the school or a registered centre first.

faqs.question: How many hours should we budget for one subject before the papers?
faqs.answer: A ten-week block at two sessions a week is about twenty hours and is the pattern with the clearest relationship to marks: roughly four hours closing the largest gaps, twelve hours of timed papers marked between sessions, and four hours reviewing the error log. At market online rates of AED 150 to 300 an hour, that is in the region of AED 3,000 to 6,000 per subject. Fewer hours in two subjects usually beats the same money spread across four.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework if a deadline is close?
faqs.answer: With the thinking and the feedback, yes; with the writing, never. A tutor can explain the criteria, question a plan, teach the skill the task needs and explain why a paragraph misses the question asked. A tutor may not write, redraft or edit any part of assessed work, and IB Gram does not supply completed coursework. Services selling finished assessments appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the malpractice consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

intro.heading: The honest answer to "is there an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Rahmaniya?"
paragraphs: There probably is someone within a few minutes' drive of Al Rahmaniya who tutors school subjects. Whether that person has taught Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 through a full two-year cycle, marked against the Paper 4 mark scheme, and can tell you why your child keeps losing the final two marks on a titration calculation is a different question. Proximity and syllabus expertise are two separate things, and the search phrase quietly assumes they arrive together. They usually do not.

Al Rahmaniya is a residential district on the inland edge of Sharjah city, close to the Maliha Road and the Sharjah-Dubai inland routes. It is a family area rather than a teaching hub. The schools that serve it sit several kilometres away in Muwaileh, Al Zahia and University City, and the teachers who work in them live scattered across Sharjah, Ajman and Dubai. A parent who insists on a tutor who can physically arrive in Al Rahmaniya on a Tuesday at 5pm has narrowed the field to whoever happens to be free and nearby, which is a transport constraint masquerading as a quality filter.

IB Gram answers the question the other way around. We do not operate home visits in the UAE at all; home tuition is a service we run only in India. For Sharjah families, every lesson is delivered live, one-to-one, over video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. That decision is not a cost-saving dodge. It is what allows a student in Al Rahmaniya to be taught Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics by someone who has taught the 4MA1 specification repeatedly, rather than by the nearest available graduate.

This page is built around supply. It sets out, subject by subject, how deep the specialist pool actually is, what the Sharjah market charges for each delivery model, which syllabus your child is most likely sitting, and what happens when no specialist is free. If you want the school-run timing version of this argument, the IB page for the same neighbourhood covers it; if you want the direct "near me" phrasing, the combined IB and IGCSE page does. This one is about whether the expertise exists and how you verify it.

One more thing worth saying up front. Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated. Under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, individuals giving private lessons need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years, and those who tutor without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Anybody who treats that as paperwork you need not mention is telling you something about how they operate. The permit applies to the individual giving the lesson, it is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation directly, and it is the one credential a parent in Sharjah can actually ask to see before a first session. Ask for it early, before money changes hands and before a term has gone by, because it is far easier to raise in week one than in week twelve.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rahmaniya.programmesIntro: Al Rahmaniya families reach IGCSE by several routes: a Cambridge lower-secondary programme, a Pearson key-stage-3 programme, or a transfer in from a CBSE or MoE-curriculum school. The entry point changes what the first eight weeks of tutoring have to repair, so it is worth naming which one applies to your child.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Core tier
programmes.description: The Core tier covers the extended-syllabus content minus the harder topics and caps the available grade at C in most subjects. It suits a student who needs a secure pass across five subjects for equivalency rather than a science or maths route at A Level. The papers are shorter, the command terms are narrower, and the arithmetic load in subjects such as Physics is reduced.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah the tier decision is usually made by the school at the end of Year 9, and parents in Al Rahmaniya often do not learn which tier their child was placed in until a report arrives. Ask the subject teacher directly, because a Core-tier student being tutored on Extended material wastes sessions, and an Extended-tier student being drilled on Core questions will meet unfamiliar question types in the June series.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended opens the full grade range to A*, adds the supplementary content, and sets the longer, more analytical papers. It is the tier a student needs for AS and A Level sciences, for most engineering routes, and for the stronger university applications. The step up is not volume alone; the questions ask for explanation and justification rather than recall.
programmes.countryNote: Extended tier is where most Al Rahmaniya tutoring enquiries land, and specifically on Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625 and Chemistry 0620. The supply problem is concentrated here too: plenty of people can help with Core arithmetic, far fewer can mark an Extended Paper 4 answer the way a Cambridge examiner does and explain the difference between a method mark and an accuracy mark.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE runs parallel to Cambridge with its own codes, papers and tiering. Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1, taken at Foundation or Higher tier across two papers of equal weight. Some subjects can be sat in a modular pattern, which changes revision planning substantially compared with the Cambridge linear model.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run Edexcel for some subjects and Cambridge for others, which means a single Al Rahmaniya student can be sitting two boards in the same academic year. A tutor who assumes one board will give confidently wrong advice about paper structure. Check the board on the statement of entry, not on the textbook cover, because schools change board without changing their resources.

programmes.name: Progression to AS and A Level
programmes.description: After IGCSE most Sharjah British-curriculum students continue to AS and A Level, taking three or four subjects. The jump is steeper than the IGCSE step was: content doubles in depth and the papers reward structured argument. IGCSE grades act as the gatekeeper, which is why Year 11 tutoring is a decision about Year 12 options rather than about one report card.
programmes.countryNote: For MoE equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE subjects. That requirement is published by the Ministry and is worth reading before a child in Al Rahmaniya drops a subject in Year 11 for timetable reasons.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rahmaniya.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Sharjah families ask about most, with the syllabus code where it is the thing that decides whether a tutor is the right match. The description in each case says what the assessment actually demands, because that is where sessions should be spent.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers, equally weighted, no coursework. Extended students lose marks in algebraic manipulation under time pressure and in the multi-step problems that combine topics. The fix is timed past-paper work with the mark scheme open, not more worked examples.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Theory papers plus the alternative-to-practical paper, which is where Extended candidates in Sharjah most often underperform. It tests experimental reasoning: variables, precision, sources of error, graph work. It cannot be revised by reading notes.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry carry the heaviest mark weight and the heaviest failure rate. Organic chemistry nomenclature and the qualitative-analysis tables are both memorisable and routinely under-revised. Paper 6 rewards precise experimental description.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: High content volume with marks awarded for exact terminology. Students who write a loosely correct answer score nothing where the mark scheme names a specific term. Transport in plants, genetics and homeostasis are the recurring weak points.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading comprehension, summary writing, and directed writing against a stated purpose and audience. The summary question has a strict word discipline and students lose marks by lifting whole sentences from the passage rather than reformulating.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition in one paper, reading passages in the other. Analytical marks depend on quoting precisely and commenting on effect rather than restating content. Strong Sharjah bilingual students often plateau here on technique, not vocabulary.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study driven. The marks sit in application and evaluation, not definition, so a student who knows every term and cannot apply it to the stimulus material will stall at a C. Structured answer frameworks move grades quickly.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks: axes labelled, curves shifted in the right direction, the new equilibrium identified. Data-response questions require quoting figures from the extract rather than general reasoning.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Theory of computer systems plus algorithms and programming. Pseudocode conventions and trace tables are the mechanical marks students throw away. Binary, hexadecimal and data-representation questions reward drill.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Sharjah candidates as a bridge to A Level Mathematics, covering calculus and trigonometry beyond 0580. It is the clearest early signal of whether a student will cope with A Level Maths, and worth tutoring for that reason alone.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: Sat alongside the international curriculum because Arabic is a mandatory subject in UAE private schools. It does not count towards the five subjects required for MoE equivalency, which surprises many families, and it still needs real preparation.

subjects.name: ICT (0417)
subjects.description: Practical papers assessed on software skills with a precise mark scheme: exact formatting, exact file handling, exact spreadsheet functions. Students who are comfortable with technology still lose marks for not following the instruction literally.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rahmaniya.regionsIntro: Al Rahmaniya sits in a ring of Sharjah districts whose families ask us for the same subjects for slightly different reasons. The notes below are about distance, traffic and school access, because those are the real constraints on an in-person arrangement and the reason an online slot holds.

regions.name: Al Rahmaniya
regions.note: Inland Sharjah, off the Maliha Road, largely villa and townhouse housing with young families. Few tutoring centres within the district itself, so an in-person arrangement almost always means someone driving in from Muwaileh or Dubai.

regions.name: Al Zahia
regions.note: The nearest master-planned community with school provision, a short drive from Al Rahmaniya. Families often have children at the same schools, and the two districts compete for the same handful of locally available tutors.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: Dense school cluster and the destination for much of the Al Rahmaniya school run. Sessions here slip later because the afternoon pick-up queues on University City Road push arrival home past 4pm.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: Home to the Sharjah university campuses, which makes undergraduate tutors plentiful and specialist IGCSE examiners rare. This is the source of the AED 45-150 budget band and its real limits.

regions.name: Aljada
regions.note: Newer mixed-use development with a growing school-age population. Travel between Aljada and Al Rahmaniya at 5pm is unpredictable, which is why families here were early adopters of fixed online slots.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Older central Sharjah district on the lagoon, with many families commuting to Dubai schools. Evening schedules run late and weekend-morning sessions are often the only reliable window.

regions.name: Tilal City
regions.note: Inland and still filling out, with limited nearby provision of any kind. The nearest specialist for a subject like Additional Mathematics 0606 is realistically not nearby at all.

regions.name: Sharjah Garden City
regions.note: Another inland community with an Al Rahmaniya-like profile: residential, villa-based, no tutoring infrastructure within walking distance, and the same reliance on whoever is willing to drive.

schoolClusters.city: Muwaileh and University City
schoolClusters.note: The closest substantial school cluster to Al Rahmaniya and the one most of its British-curriculum students attend. Pick-up congestion here is the single biggest reason a 4pm in-person session does not start at 4pm.

schoolClusters.city: Central Sharjah and Al Zahia
schoolClusters.note: Serves families on the Al Majaz, Al Khan and Al Zahia side, including a number of Al Rahmaniya households that chose a school near a parent's commute rather than near home.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai-side schools on the Sharjah border
schoolClusters.note: A meaningful share of Al Rahmaniya and Al Nahda families drive into Dubai for school. Those students finish later and need evening slots, which is exactly where locally available tutors are already booked.

This is the default for a Year 10 student in Al Rahmaniya who is coping but drifting in one subject, and it is the pattern that produces steady change because the tutor sees the same errors recur and can attack the cause.

sections.heading: What "IGCSE home tutor in Al Rahmaniya" actually returns
paragraphs: Typed into a search bar, the phrase produces three kinds of result: agencies that will send whoever is free, marketplaces listing tutors by distance, and content pages that answer a different question. Almost none tell you how many people within reach of Al Rahmaniya have actually taught the syllabus your child is sitting. That number is the only one that matters, and it is small.

The reason is structural. Al Rahmaniya is residential. Its school-age population is served by schools in Muwaileh, Al Zahia and University City, and the teachers in those schools are spread across three emirates. A tutor filtered by driving distance from Al Rahmaniya is a tutor filtered by where they chose to live, which has no relationship at all to whether they can teach Cambridge 0620 Chemistry.

IB Gram's answer is to drop the distance filter entirely. We do not run home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service. Every Sharjah lesson is live video, one-to-one, at a fixed time in Gulf Standard Time. The practical consequence is that the pool your child is matched from is the whole specialist pool rather than the subset that can drive to Al Rahmaniya by five o'clock.

It is a trade, and it is worth stating what you give up. You give up a tutor sitting at the same table. You gain a tutor who has marked the paper your child is about to sit. For most families in this district that exchange is obviously worth making, but you should make it knowingly rather than have it sold to you.

sections.heading: How deep the specialist pool really is, subject by subject
paragraphs: No competitor in this market publishes a coverage table, because a coverage table admits limits. We publish one. The figures below describe how quickly a match is typically made for a student in Sharjah, where the constraint sits, and what happens when nobody suitable is free. This is the table to read if your question is really about availability.

Two patterns show up repeatedly. Mainstream Extended-tier subjects at Years 10 and 11 are well covered and match quickly. Narrow subjects, second-board variants and the subjects that only a handful of Sharjah schools offer are slower, and in those cases a specialist outside the UAE teaching in your evening window is the realistic answer rather than a local generalist.

The fallback matters more than the headline. If a student in Al Rahmaniya needs Additional Mathematics 0606 and no UAE-based specialist has a free slot, we say so and offer a specialist in another timezone whose availability overlaps the Sharjah evening. What we do not do is accept the booking and hand the student to someone who will learn the syllabus alongside them.

Read the pool-depth column with one more thing in mind. Depth describes how many specialists exist, not how many are free on a Tuesday at five o'clock. The Sharjah evening is the busiest window in the whole schedule, because that is when almost every family in Al Rahmaniya, Al Zahia and Muwaileh wants a lesson. A family willing to take a weekend-morning slot will see shorter match times across every row in that table, and will usually get a stronger tutor as well. That is the single cheapest piece of leverage a parent in this district has, and almost nobody uses it.

sections.heading: Which board is your child sitting, and why it changes the tutor
paragraphs: Parents in Al Rahmaniya routinely tell us their child does "IGCSE Maths" and are surprised that this is not enough information to make a match. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are separate awarding bodies with separate specifications, separate paper structures and separate mark schemes. A tutor fluent in one and guessing at the other will give advice that is sincerely wrong.

The table below sets out the codes for the subjects Sharjah families ask about most. Find the one on your child's statement of entry, not the one on the textbook spine; schools switch board more often than they switch resources, and a Cambridge revision guide on the shelf of an Edexcel student is a common sight in this district.

The practical differences are concrete. Cambridge tiers Mathematics as Core and Extended; Pearson tiers it as Foundation and Higher within Specification A. Cambridge sciences include an alternative-to-practical route; Pearson structures practical assessment differently. Some Pearson subjects allow a modular entry pattern, which changes when revision has to peak. None of that is detail a parent should have to discover in April.

There is a related trap with the sciences. A Sharjah student may sit Cambridge Physics 0625 and Pearson Chemistry 4CH1 in the same year, which means two different approaches to practical assessment running in parallel. The revision strategy for the Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper is not the revision strategy for the Pearson equivalent, and a tutor who treats them as interchangeable will spend sessions on the wrong skills. Write the board next to every subject on a single sheet of paper before you book anything. It takes five minutes and it prevents the commonest mismatch in this market.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Al Rahmaniya, cheapest first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most Sharjah families start and where the disappointments happen. University City sits a short drive away and supplies a large number of undergraduate tutors. Published budget rates in this band run from roughly AED 33 to 65 per hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For a Year 9 student who needs supervision and structure, that can be entirely adequate.

It stops being adequate at the Extended tier in the term before a series. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A specialist in IGCSE, IB or A Level runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium named or examiner-led tutors go further again, with BartyED at AED 650.

The in-home premium is the figure parents in Al Rahmaniya should look at hardest. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Part of that premium is teaching and part of it is a car on the Maliha Road. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 per month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 per month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Every figure here is published by the provider named, as read in October 2026; none is an IB Gram price.

sections.heading: Where the money gets wasted, and how to avoid it
paragraphs: The commonest waste in this market is paying specialist rates for generalist work. A student who has not learned the content does not need an examiner-level tutor; they need thirty hours of ordinary teaching. A student who knows the content and loses eight marks a paper to command-term misreading does not need more teaching at all; they need mark-scheme correction. Families frequently buy the wrong one of those two and conclude tutoring does not work.

The second waste is paying for travel without noticing. At the Bestimate in-home band of AED 180 to 350 against an online qualified band of AED 150 to 300, the gap is partly geography. If the arrangement means the tutor arrives at 5.20pm for a 5pm session, tired from the Maliha Road, you have paid a premium for a worse lesson. This is the specific failure mode that makes families in inland districts such as Al Rahmaniya and Tilal City switch to online slots.

The third is starting too late and buying too much at once. Twenty hours bought in the fortnight before a paper cannot replace content that was never learned, and the price per hour tends to rise as the series approaches. A single weekly hour from October onwards costs less in total than an emergency block in April and does considerably more. If you can only do one thing with this page, do that.

The fourth waste is quieter and harder to see: paying for hours that are not really one-to-one. A small group of three at a reduced per-student rate looks like value until you notice that your child's specific error pattern is never addressed, because the tutor is managing three error patterns at once. Group sessions have a legitimate place in content revision. They are close to useless for correcting the individual technical habits that cost a student six marks a paper, and that is usually what a Year 11 family is actually paying to fix.

sections.heading: Online against a tutor driving into Al Rahmaniya
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search phrase deserves, laid out honestly. In-home tuition has real advantages: physical presence, easier engagement with a younger or distractible child, no dependence on a connection. Those advantages are genuine and we are not going to pretend otherwise. IB Gram simply does not offer home visits in the UAE, and the reasons are set out in the table rather than asserted.

The decisive column is tutor pool. An in-home arrangement in Al Rahmaniya selects from people willing to drive to an inland Sharjah district in the late afternoon. An online arrangement selects from everyone teaching that syllabus whose working hours overlap your evening. For mainstream Mathematics the two pools may both be adequate. For Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478, the first pool may be empty.

The second decisive column is reliability. A fixed online slot at 5pm starts at 5pm. An in-home slot at 5pm starts when the car arrives, and over a thirty-week year the accumulated loss is substantial. Families who moved for this reason rarely move back, which is worth knowing before you spend a term testing it yourself.

One column in the table deserves a direct statement rather than a cell. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so nothing on this page should be read as an offer to send a tutor to an Al Rahmaniya address. The in-home column describes what the wider Sharjah market sells and what it costs, so that you can weigh it against what we actually do. If a home visit is genuinely the right answer for your child, you should book one from somebody who provides it, and you should still ask them for the tutor's permit and their syllabus experience.

sections.heading: SPEA, the Ministry and what a regulator does not do for you
paragraphs: Al Rahmaniya's private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate. SPEA's remit goes beyond inspection: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider grip on school practice than many parents assume, and it is why school-level decisions such as tier placement follow emirate-level patterns.

The emirate map matters when families move. Dubai private schools fall under KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, Sharjah under SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. A child moving from Al Rahmaniya to a Dubai school has changed regulator as well as school, and the mandatory-subject requirements they meet will be the ones KHDA publishes.

What no regulator does is vet your tutor. SPEA regulates schools. The private-tutoring permit is a MoHRE matter, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time. Nobody can call themselves SPEA-approved or KHDA-approved as a private tutor, and IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. If a provider implies otherwise, that is the moment to ask for the permit number.

The distinction between an individual tutor and a tutoring business is also worth knowing, because providers blur it. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. That is a specific licence issued to a specific kind of organisation. It is not something a private tutor holds, and it is not something an online matching platform holds either. Phrases like approved tutors are doing work that no document behind them supports.

sections.heading: The IGCSE calendar counted backwards from the next series
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series. UAE candidates sit those two. The February/March series is offered to India only, and any page quoting a February window to a Sharjah parent has given them a date to act on that is wrong for their country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

Counting backwards is the useful direction. Final entry deadlines sit months before the papers, mocks land a term earlier, and the decision about whether a resit is needed is made before the previous results arrive. The table below is built from the published pattern: the Pearson November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

One administrative trap is worth naming because Cambridge names it itself. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential that the correct version of the timetable for the zone is used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your school which zone it sits in and work from the zone timetable, not from a generic one. Always check the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than relying on restated dates.

For a Year 11 student in Al Rahmaniya the resit decision is the one most often made too slowly. Results arrive in August for the June series, and the entry window for the November series closes not long afterwards. Families who spend three weeks deciding whether to resit frequently discover the decision was made for them by a deadline. Agree the rule in advance instead: decide now what grade in which subject would trigger a November entry, write it down, and act on it within days of the results rather than debating it from scratch in late August.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor may and may not do with your child's work
paragraphs: This market contains providers who sell completed coursework. One competitor page reviewed in this research advertises finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is not tutoring, it is a malpractice trigger, and for the student the consequence is far worse than a poor grade. We state the boundary plainly because being explicit about it is a genuine difference rather than a slogan.

A tutor may teach the content, explain the mark scheme, model how a strong answer is constructed from a different example, read a draft the student wrote and say where it is unclear or unsupported, and teach referencing and data handling. A tutor may not write, rewrite, complete, substantially edit or supply any part of assessed work. On the IGCSE side that covers coursework components, practical write-ups and any school-assessed element; the same rule governs IB Internal Assessments, Extended Essays and TOK essays.

There is a second boundary worth knowing. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter. If a provider offers you a bundle of official papers and mark schemes to keep, ask yourself what else they are relaxed about.

A third boundary applies to teachers. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on the exact wording. The principle is clear enough regardless: we will not arrange for a child to be privately tutored by a teacher who also grades their school work.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Rahmaniya without losing a term
paragraphs: The first week should be diagnostic, not motivational. Before any session is booked, find three things: the board and code for each subject, the tier your child was placed in, and one recent piece of marked work. With those, a specialist can tell you in a single trial lesson whether the problem is content, technique or confidence, and those three problems need three different plans.

Then choose frequency honestly. One hour a week from October, held consistently, outperforms a crash block in the spring at a lower total cost. If two subjects are in trouble, two specialists are better than one generalist, even though one generalist is simpler to schedule. If money is the constraint, take one subject properly rather than three subjects thinly; the thin version is the most common way a tutoring budget disappears without a grade moving.

Finally, agree what failure looks like. Ask what you should expect to see by week four, what evidence will show it, and what happens if it does not appear. A provider who cannot answer that is selling hours rather than outcomes. We would rather tell you in week two that the match is wrong and change the tutor than collect thirty weeks of fees for a relationship that is not working.

Last, be realistic about your own part in it. The sessions that work in this district are the ones where a parent has cleared a quiet room, checked the connection before the slot rather than during it, and does not treat the hour as negotiable when something else comes up. That is not a lecture, it is the practical difference between thirty lessons and twenty-two. A tutor can carry the subject knowledge and the mark-scheme fluency. Only the household can protect the slot, and the household that protects it gets a different result.

process.title: A free trial lesson, used as a diagnosis
process.description: The trial is a working session. The tutor sets a question from a past paper, marks it against the mark scheme, and tells you whether the gap is content, technique or exam timing. You get that read in writing, and no payment is taken before it happens.

process.description: We set a weekly time in Gulf Standard Time that accounts for when your child genuinely gets home from Muwaileh, University City or a Dubai-side school. A slot that looks neat on paper and is missed twice a month is worse than a later one that holds.

Knowing the limit before you pay is worth more than a promise.

Distance filtering is how an inland Sharjah family ends up with a generalist, and it is the single biggest cause of tutoring money spent without a grade moving.
