They do not write coursework, Internal Assessments, Extended Essays or TOK essays, and we do not supply official papers or mark schemes as downloads. In a market where completed IAs are openly sold, that boundary protects your child's qualification.

whyPoints.title: Permit-aware, not permit-silent
whyPoints.description: We explain the MoHRE private tuition work permit, name the resolution that created it, say that it is free and valid for two years, and point to the official application route. We claim no regulator's approval for ourselves, because we hold none.

whyPoints.title: Lessons that survive a move
whyPoints.description: Families leave Sharjah for the summer, travel at Eid, and sometimes relocate emirate mid-year. An online slot follows the student; a home arrangement ends at the city limit. Continuity through those gaps is often what decides a November resit.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Rahmaniya who knows the syllabus?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly there is someone nearby who tutors school subjects. Whether they have taught your child's exact specification through a full cycle is a separate question, and in an inland residential district such as Al Rahmaniya the specialist pool within driving distance is small. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE, so we do not filter by distance at all. We match on the syllabus code and teach live one-to-one over video in a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, which means the pool your child is drawn from is every specialist whose hours overlap your evening.

faqs.question: Why does IB Gram not send a tutor to our villa in Al Rahmaniya?
faqs.answer: Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. Across the UAE, including Sharjah, every lesson is delivered live and one-to-one over video. The reason is not cost. It is that an in-home arrangement in Al Rahmaniya selects a tutor from the people willing to drive to an inland district in the late afternoon, which has nothing to do with whether they can teach Cambridge 0620 Chemistry at Extended tier. We would rather hand you a subject specialist on a screen than a generalist at your table.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for IGCSE tuition around Al Rahmaniya?
faqs.answer: Published market rates, read in October 2026, run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour for budget online and university-student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IGCSE specialist. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are figures the named providers publish, not IB Gram prices. For ours, take the free trial lesson and ask for a quote against your child's actual subject list.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE board does my child's Sharjah school use, Cambridge or Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Check the statement of entry rather than the textbook. Several Sharjah schools run Cambridge for some subjects and Pearson Edexcel for others, so one student can sit two boards in the same year. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended tiers; Pearson Specification A is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher tiers. The paper structures and mark schemes differ, and a tutor working from the wrong board will give advice that is confidently wrong about timing, tiering and question style.

faqs.question: My child is Extended tier in Physics 0625 and keeps failing the practical paper. Can that be fixed?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the more fixable problems because it is a technique gap rather than a content gap. The alternative-to-practical paper tests experimental reasoning: identifying variables, judging precision, spotting sources of error, reading and drawing graphs. It cannot be revised by rereading notes. Sessions should be spent attempting the paper cold, then working through the mark scheme line by line to see exactly which words earn marks. Most students improve measurably within six to eight focused sessions on that paper alone.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams happen for a candidate in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so ignore any page that quotes it to a Sharjah parent. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Final entry deadlines sit months before the papers and are handled by the school. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the wrong zone timetable is the candidate's risk, so ask your school which zone it is in.

faqs.question: How quickly can you find a tutor for a Year 11 student in Al Rahmaniya?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Extended-tier subjects such as Mathematics 0580, English as a Second Language 0510 or the three separate sciences, a match is usually made within two to four days and often inside forty-eight hours. For thinner subjects such as Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 or ICT 0417, expect five to ten days, and expect us to tell you whether the specialist is UAE-based or working from another timezone into your evening. We publish that coverage table on this page rather than making you discover it after paying.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Sharjah need a permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask the tutor directly for their permit; the application runs through the MoHRE smart app and e-services system and completes in about two working days.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IGCSE coursework or write-up?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills the task requires, explain how the mark scheme rewards them, model the approach on a different example, and read a draft your child has written and say where it is unclear or unsupported. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it, complete it or edit it to a finished state. That boundary is not a policy preference, it is what keeps the qualification valid. Providers in this market openly sell completed Internal Assessments; buying one risks the student's whole diploma, not just one grade.

faqs.question: Is online tuition really as effective for a fourteen-year-old as someone sitting beside them?
faqs.answer: For a focused fourteen-year-old, yes, provided the session is genuinely one-to-one and the tutor uses a shared board so the work is visible. For a younger or very distractible child, physical presence has real advantages and we will say so. What online reliably wins on is who teaches: a fixed video slot draws from every specialist in the syllabus, while an in-home slot in Al Rahmaniya draws from whoever will drive inland after four o'clock. For Extended-tier sciences that difference usually outweighs the presence.

faqs.question: Which Sharjah schools do the students you support in this area attend?
faqs.answer: Students we support near Al Rahmaniya attend schools across the Muwaileh and University City cluster, including Wesgreen International School, the American School of Creative Science in Muwaileh and The Westminster School Sharjah, as well as central Sharjah schools such as Sharjah English School and Victoria International School of Sharjah. A number travel into Dubai schools instead. We name these as context for the local landscape; IB Gram has no affiliation or partnership with any of them and none is implied.

faqs.question: Will five IGCSE grades from a Sharjah school satisfy the Ministry equivalency rule?
faqs.answer: On the British track the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Students also submit one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One competitor page in this market states six IGCSE subjects are required, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel before acting; IB Gram does not perform equivalency.

faqs.question: We travel between Sharjah and abroad during term. Will the schedule survive that?
faqs.answer: It will, because nothing in the arrangement depends on a journey. The slot is held in Gulf Standard Time and the lesson follows the student, so a fortnight in another country does not break the sequence. If the time difference makes the usual slot impossible, we move it for the duration and move it back. This is one of the practical reasons families in inland Sharjah districts switch from a home arrangement: a tutor who drives to you cannot follow you anywhere.

faqs.question: What do you do if the tutor we start with in Al Rahmaniya is the wrong match?
faqs.answer: We change them. At the start we agree what week four should look like: which errors should have stopped recurring, what should be happening on timed questions, whether homework is being completed. If that evidence is not there, or if the relationship is simply not working, we move the student to another specialist in the same subject rather than defending the original match. You do not restart from the beginning, and you do not need to justify the request beyond telling us it is not working.

faqs.question: Do you teach Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and students often sit something like Arabic as a First Language 0508 alongside their IGCSE set. We can support Arabic language work, and it is worth knowing two constraints: KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in these subjects, and for the mandatory UAE subjects the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is not allowed. That limits what any tutor can legitimately substitute.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start if the series is only two months away?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which problem you have. If the content was never learned, two months of tutoring will raise some marks but will not rebuild two years, and you should consider whether a November entry is the better plan. If the content is broadly known and marks are going to technique, timing and command-term misreading, eight weeks of timed-paper work with mark-scheme correction can move a grade. Ask for a diagnostic trial lesson first; a provider who sells you twenty hours without diagnosing is guessing with your money.

Send us those and we will tell you honestly how deep the specialist pool is for that exact combination, how long a match will take, and whether the tutor would be UAE-based or working into your evening from elsewhere. Then take the free trial lesson and judge it on the diagnosis you get, not the warmth. Lessons are live, one-to-one and online, in your Gulf Standard Time slot, every week.

intro.heading: Comparing addresses when the examination is the same everywhere
paragraphs: Al Ramtha is an older residential district in the central-western part of Sharjah, with Abu Shagara, Al Nud and Al Qasimia close by and schools in most directions. Families here often start by wondering whether a neighbouring district would give them better options. It is a reasonable question and the answer is narrower than expected: the names overlap, the quality distribution is the same, and the examination your child sits is set in Cambridge and London rather than in any neighbourhood.

Three things do genuinely differ by district. The type of school nearby, which in this part of Sharjah skews towards Indian-curriculum provision with British-board entries for some cohorts. The depth of local tutoring supply, which is greatest around Al Majaz and thins towards the outer corridors. And peak-season availability, which collapses everywhere in the eight to ten weeks before a series but collapses first where demand is densest.

Four more things differ and have nothing to do with geography at all. Which board your child is entered for. Which tier. Which paper is weak. And how the hours before the series are spent. Those four decide the grade, and they are the comparison worth making. A family that runs them properly from Al Ramtha will do better than a family that moves its search two streets and ignores them.

The board comparison in particular is almost never explained to parents. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers, use different codes, tier differently and phrase questions differently. A tutor fluent in one gives confident, well-meant and wrong guidance about the other, and a student who has spent a term on the wrong board's past papers usually finds out in a mock. There is a table below setting the two side by side.

The cost comparison resolves similarly. Across published UAE rate cards an in-home visit is quoted between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor teaching online. Choosing by district, then paying a premium for somebody to drive within it, raises the price and narrows the choice at the same time. We teach one-to-one over live video and do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE - that service exists only in India.

It is worth saying why the district question feels so important even though it is not. House moves, school choices and tutoring decisions arrive in the same conversations, so geography gets attached to all three. For the first two it matters a great deal. For the third it decides who can drive to you, and once nobody has to drive, it decides nothing at all.

What follows compares the districts honestly, then the boards, then Sharjah against Dubai and Ajman, then three ways of buying the same preparation - and finishes with the list of things that are identical whatever your address.

sections.heading: What actually differs between these districts
paragraphs: Start with the real differences, because there are some. The first is school type. The area around Al Ramtha, Abu Shagara and Al Nud has a heavy concentration of Indian-curriculum schools, several of which enter some cohorts or subjects for Cambridge or Pearson papers. That produces a specific local situation: a large number of IGCSE candidates whose school is primarily teaching a different system, whose teaching sequence differs from a British school's, and whose families often do not know which board they are entered for.

The second is supply depth. Al Majaz has the deepest tutoring pool in the emirate because it has been the tutoring district longest; Al Qasimia and Al Khan are well supplied; the outer corridors are thin. Al Ramtha sits in the comfortable middle, which means the local problem here is not scarcity but selection - plenty of names, little information about which of them has taught your child's paper.

The third is peak behaviour. Demand across central Sharjah concentrates in the eight to ten weeks before a series, and the densest districts fill first. A family searching from Al Ramtha in that window will find the Al Majaz specialists committed and the remaining local list skewed towards generalists at awkward hours. That is a timing problem rather than a geography problem, and the remedy is to book early rather than to search further afield.

What does not differ is the quality distribution. In every district the pattern is the same: many people who will teach several subjects across several year groups, fewer who know one board's paper structure in detail, and very few who have taught a specific syllabus code to grade standard for years. That shape is a property of the market, and moving your search two streets does not change it.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel for the same subject
paragraphs: This is the comparison that changes outcomes, and almost nobody explains it to parents. Both boards award an International GCSE in the same subject, and the two qualifications are not interchangeable for the purpose of preparing a candidate.

Codes first, because they are how you identify which you have. Cambridge uses four digits: 0580 mathematics, 0620 chemistry, 0625 physics, 0610 biology, 0500 first language English, 0510 English as a second language. Pearson Edexcel codes begin with a 4: 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1. They appear on the statement of entry and in the exam information the school circulates.

Structure next. Cambridge tiers most subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capping the available grade, and its sciences include an alternative-to-practical paper that tests practical skills in writing. Pearson's mathematics uses two equally weighted papers rather than a tiered four-paper pattern, which changes how a candidate should allocate effort across the two sittings. Confirm the current structure and weightings from the syllabus document your school issues, since these change between syllabus cycles and the school's copy is authoritative.

Then question style, which is the part a tutor feels rather than reads. The phrasing, the typical length of a structured question and the way marks are distributed within one differ enough that practising the wrong board's papers teaches partly wrong habits. For a student transferring schools mid-course - common in this part of Sharjah - two or three sessions explicitly comparing the two styles is usually enough to reset expectations.

sections.heading: Sharjah against Dubai and Ajman
paragraphs: Families in central Sharjah compare across emirate boundaries as readily as across streets, and the comparison is worth making properly because the differences there are real.

Dubai has more schools, more tutors and higher prices. The emirate recorded 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, so the tutoring market behind it is deeper, including more single-subject specialists. In-home, a Dubai tutor travelling to Al Ramtha prices the journey and usually becomes the most expensive option available. Online, the same specialist costs no more to reach than somebody in Al Qasimia, which is the practical argument for the format rather than for the emirate.

Ajman is the reverse: fewer schools, thinner local supply, and a regulatory difference worth knowing. Private schools in Ajman, along with Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, while Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods. Families whose children attend school in one emirate and live in another deal with two sets of published information.

Crossing a boundary therefore changes price, supply and school administration. It does not change the examination. A Pearson 4CH1 candidate in Al Ramtha, Al Nahda or Ajman sits the same paper, marked to the same scheme, in the same series - which is the whole argument for choosing the best available specialist rather than the nearest one.

sections.heading: Three ways to buy the same preparation
paragraphs: Having established that the examination is fixed, the remaining comparison is between methods of preparing for it. There are three realistic routes, and the right one depends on the student rather than on the address.

Self-study with honest marking is the cheapest and works for a disciplined candidate. Past papers exist, mark schemes exist, and a student who completes a paper under timing and marks it strictly against the scheme learns most of what a tutor would teach about technique. The failure modes are generous self-marking and avoiding the papers that feel hardest, both of which are human and both of which a parent can partly police.

Group classes at a centre are the cheapest paid teaching per student and suit a shared content weakness. What they cannot do is run an individual error log, review the script a particular student wrote, or decide that this candidate should abandon one topic and drill another. That is why group revision courses before a series frequently feel productive and move little.

One-to-one with a board-matched specialist is the most expensive per hour and the only route that does diagnosis, triage and technique for a specific candidate. Across published UAE rate cards that is roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour online, against AED 180 to 500 for the same thing delivered in person with travel absorbed. For most candidates the sensible combination is self-study for volume plus a small number of specialist hours for direction - which costs less than a term of weekly sessions and usually achieves more.

sections.heading: What is identical wherever you live
paragraphs: Having compared what varies, the longer list is what does not - and this is where families expend the most unnecessary effort.

The examination. Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level papers in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February/March series is offered in India only, so any page telling Sharjah parents to prepare for a February sitting is describing another country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Entries are made by the school's centre, and the zone timetable belongs to that centre rather than to your district.

The mark scheme. There is no local edition of the 0620 mark scheme. Command terms mean the same thing in Al Ramtha as in Al Majaz. The three topics where candidates lose the most marks in each subject are the same across the emirate, which is why a tutor's course experience is the variable worth optimising and their postcode is not.

The permit. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. And the academic-honesty boundary is federal and universal: a tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work, and never writes any part of it.

sections.heading: Choosing between two tutors: a short checklist
paragraphs: Most families reach a point where they have two or three plausible options and no way to separate them. Price and proximity are the easy comparators and the least informative. Here is a better list.

First, which board and code have they taught, and how recently? A specific answer with a year attached beats 'all boards'. Second, will they mark a recent script before the first session? A tutor who has taught the paper says yes because the annotated script argues their case; one who prefers to meet the student first is choosing the ground they are stronger on. Third, what will change in the last six weeks? The right answer involves full timed papers marked against the published scheme and an error log by question type.

Fourth, what is written down? A target list for the next six sessions and a note after each lesson are what make an arrangement reviewable. Fifth, what happens if the match is wrong - a provider with a pool can replace a tutor and carry the plan across, while an individual arrangement means starting the search again mid-term. Sixth, do they hold the MoHRE permit? It costs nothing, so the answer is informative either way.

Finally, a negative test. Anybody who predicts a grade, offers to handle assessed coursework, claims approval from a regulator or board, or shows a star rating with no countable dated reviews behind it has told you something important. Those four appear in this market and each is a reason to keep looking, whatever the district and whatever the price.

sections.heading: Limits, stated once
paragraphs: A page built on comparisons should be straightforward about the things we do not offer, so they are not discovered later as a disappointment.

We do not send tutors to UAE addresses. All teaching here is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. If what your family needs is an adult physically supervising a younger child, a local in-home arrangement is the better fit and we will say so.

We do not guarantee grades, because nobody can know what a particular candidate will score. We do not write, draft or edit assessed coursework, and we do not sell completed work - services that do appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the malpractice consequence falls on the student. We do not distribute boards' syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; we cite the official sources and point families to the school for current versions.

And we hold no approval, licence or accreditation from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no premises in this country. A tutoring service claiming otherwise should be asked for the permit number, and that request usually ends the conversation.

Nor do we handle the Ministry of Education equivalency process, which some families ask about at the same time as tutoring. Equivalency is completed by families through the official channel, and describing it is the most any tutoring service should do. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression, and a page suggesting otherwise is manufacturing urgency rather than offering information.

faqs.question: Would searching from Abu Shagara or Al Nud give us better IGCSE options than Al Ramtha?
faqs.answer: Hardly at all. These districts share one tutoring pool, and the quality distribution is the same in each: many generalists, fewer board-specific teachers, very few single-code specialists. What varies is school type - this area has a heavy Indian-curriculum presence, so board identification matters more here - along with supply depth and how fast local availability disappears before a series. Moving a search two streets changes the names slightly and changes nothing about the examination your child sits.

faqs.question: How different are Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel in the same subject?
faqs.answer: Different enough that practising the wrong board's papers teaches partly wrong habits. Cambridge uses four-digit codes and tiers most subjects into Core and Extended, with sciences including an alternative-to-practical paper. Pearson codes begin with a 4 and its maths uses two equally weighted papers rather than a tiered pattern. Question phrasing and mark distribution within structured questions also differ. Confirm the current structure from the syllabus document your school issues, since these change between cycles.

faqs.question: Our school teaches an Indian curriculum but enters IGCSE papers. Who should teach my child?
faqs.answer: Somebody who has taught that board's papers rather than somebody who knows the content. The subject overlap between systems is substantial, so the gap is examination behaviour: question phrasing, the expectation that method is shown, and command terms treated as precise instructions. Two to four board-specific sessions working through past papers, marked against the published scheme, usually close that gap faster than more content teaching. Get the code from the statement of entry first - it decides which papers to practise.

faqs.question: Is it worth looking for a tutor in Dubai instead of Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Online, there is no reason not to: Dubai's market is deeper - the emirate recorded 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25 - so more specialists are based there, and over video the distance costs nothing. In-home, a Dubai tutor travelling to Al Ramtha prices the journey and usually becomes the most expensive option on the table. Since the examination is identical in both emirates, the sensible approach is to choose on course experience and let the format remove the geography.

faqs.question: Can a disciplined student prepare without a tutor at all?
faqs.answer: For many candidates, substantially yes. Past papers and mark schemes exist, and a student who completes a paper under timing and marks it strictly against the scheme learns most of what a tutor teaches about technique. The two failure modes are generous self-marking and avoiding the papers that feel hardest, both of which a parent can partly police. The cheapest effective combination for most Year 11 candidates is self-study for volume plus a small number of specialist hours for direction.

faqs.question: Do group revision courses work as well as one-to-one before a series?
faqs.answer: For a shared content weakness they are good value, and they are the cheapest paid teaching per student. For an individual problem they cannot help: a group cannot keep one candidate's error log, review the script they wrote, or decide that this student should abandon one topic and drill another. That is why group courses often feel busy and change little - the candidate who needed three sessions on electrolysis sat through six hours covering everything else as well.

faqs.question: Which exam series will a Sharjah candidate sit, and what about a resit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs June and November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. November is the standard resit route, and results from a November series reach students in January - the November 2025 cohort received theirs on 22 January 2026. Before entering, confirm the receiving sixth form or university accepts a January result and confirm the entry route with the school or a registered centre.

faqs.question: Why do in-home quotes differ so much between neighbouring districts?
faqs.answer: Because they price the journey. The teaching inside the hour does not change, but a tutor based in Muwaileh quoting for Al Ramtha adds the Maliha Road drive, while one from Al Nud adds almost nothing. Across published UAE rate cards the in-home band runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online for a qualified subject tutor. If two quotes for the same tutor differ sharply by address, you are looking at the cost of fuel and time rather than quality.

faqs.question: How do I choose between two tutors who both sound competent?
faqs.answer: Ask six questions. Which board and code have you taught, and how recently? Will you mark a recent script before the first session? What changes in the last six weeks? What gets written down? What happens if the match is wrong? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition permit? Specific answers to the first three and a replacement policy for the fifth separate candidates far better than price or distance do, and none of the questions requires subject knowledge from you.

faqs.question: Does my child's tier matter as much as the board?
faqs.answer: Nearly. At Cambridge, Core caps the grade available while Extended carries the full range and includes content a Core candidate never meets; Pearson tiers some subjects as Foundation and Higher. The test is whether the student can access the harder content and finish the harder paper in the time, which two sessions of past-paper questions will establish. Any change goes through the school before its internal entry deadline, so the conversation has to happen early rather than after the mocks that prompt it.

faqs.question: Are the regulators different for schools in Sharjah and Ajman?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it matters for school administration rather than tutoring. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education; Dubai has KHDA and Abu Dhabi has ADEK. The examination boards, series, timetables and mark schemes are identical across all of them, as is the federal tutor permit requirement.

faqs.question: What does ten weeks of exam preparation cost around here?
faqs.answer: A ten-week block at two sessions a week is about twenty hours, which at the published qualified-online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour is in the region of AED 3,000 to 6,000 per subject. The in-home equivalent, quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel absorbed, reaches AED 3,600 to 10,000 for the same hours. Those are market figures read in October 2026 and published for comparison rather than as our price list - ask us directly, and the trial costs nothing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework where a subject still has it?
faqs.answer: With the teaching and the feedback, yes; with the writing, no. A tutor may explain what the task requires, question a plan, teach the skill involved and explain why a paragraph does not answer the question asked. A tutor may not write, redraft or edit any part of the submitted work, and IB Gram does not supply completed coursework. Services selling finished assessments appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

faqs.question: What if the specialist we want has no slot at our preferred hour?
faqs.answer: We will offer a different hour with the right person, or a named date when one frees up. Demand concentrates in the eight to ten weeks before a series and narrow courses - Additional Mathematics 0606, computer science 0478, a specific board's business paper - sometimes have nobody free. What we will not do is substitute a generalist into a deadline block and leave a family to discover the mismatch over six weeks, because that costs exactly the weeks you were trying to buy.

intro.heading: The hour that decides whether tutoring works
paragraphs: Families looking for an IGCSE home tutor in Al Suyoh usually discover the real constraint in week two. The teaching was fine. The slot was not. A Year 11 student who gets home at half past three, eats, deals with school homework and then faces a tutor at four is not in a state to work on Cambridge 0580 Paper 4 technique. A student sitting down at seven, having decompressed, is. The difference between those two bookings is often a grade, and it has nothing to do with the tutor's subject knowledge.

Al Suyoh makes this sharper than most Sharjah districts. It is an inland plotted residential area off the Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road corridor, with Al Tai immediately north, Muwaileh and University City a short run away, and the Maliha Road heading south. Almost every child here travels out to school, and the schools are spread across three directions rather than concentrated in one catchment. Two neighbours on the same street can have children finishing forty minutes apart at schools eight kilometres from each other.

That spread breaks the in-home model quietly. A tutor driving to Al Suyoh can realistically fit two students in an evening, so they schedule around their own route rather than around either family's day, and the parent takes whichever slot is left. With online delivery that constraint disappears: there is no route, so the slot is chosen by when the student can actually concentrate. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, since in-home visiting is an India-only service, and this page is written on that basis rather than around it.

The rest of this page is the scheduling information nobody publishes. When Sharjah school days typically end and what that leaves. What the drive does to a four o'clock lesson. How mock season reshapes a term and why the tutor should know the dates before the school does anything about them. How Ramadan moves the week, and why a post-Iftar slot is straightforward online and awkward for anyone driving. And which IGCSE board your child sits, because a Cambridge entry and a Pearson entry do not need the same weekly rhythm.

One practical note before the detail. The single most useful thing an Al Suyoh parent can send with an enquiry is not a report card but a timetable: the school's finish time, the days with after-school commitments, and the dates of the next mock window. A tutor who has that can propose a slot that survives the term. A tutor who does not will propose whatever is free in their diary, and that is the booking that quietly fails by half-term. A timetable costs nothing to send and saves a term of friction.

Tutoring here is best kept short and early in the evening, because attention is the limiting factor rather than content, and a tired Year 8 gains nothing from a nine o'clock session.

It is also the cheapest point to fix arithmetic fluency and written structure, both of which decide the Core or Extended tiering conversation two years later.

Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended with different grade ceilings; Pearson Edexcel uses its own codes, such as 4MA1 for Mathematics and 4PH1 for Physics, and structures papers differently. Weekly rhythm matters most here because mock windows and the real series both have fixed dates.

The realistic pattern is one subject at a fixed later slot through the autumn and spring, raised to short frequent sessions in the weeks before the June series.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-suyoh.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Suyoh enquiries concentrate in. Each note includes the practical timing point: how long a session needs to be useful in that subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Needs a full sixty minutes minimum, because a worked paper question cannot be rushed and marked in twenty. Extended candidates lose marks on transformations, bounds and non-calculator arithmetic. The tier decision belongs in Year 10, not Year 11, and reviewing it takes two sessions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the widest mark spread. Works well in ninety-minute blocks because a circuit problem plus the alternative-to-practical technique fills that time naturally. Shorter sessions tend to cover only one of the two.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and the qualitative analysis observations carry the Extended marks. The six-mark extended answers need a taught structure. A sixty-minute slot handles one topic plus its paper technique; attempting two leaves both half-done.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume rather than conceptual difficulty, which makes it the most forgiving subject for a later evening slot: recall and command-term practice survive tiredness better than multi-step calculation does.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response both improve fastest through marked practice rather than teaching, so sessions are short and frequent rather than long. A thirty-minute timed piece plus feedback is a complete and genuinely useful session.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline carries marks that prose cannot recover, and the data-response paper rewards students who answer the command word used. Works well in a single weekly hour across a term, with no need for intensity until the final weeks.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole paper. Students who revise definitions and not application plateau at a middle grade. Sessions need the case material in front of both parties, which is straightforward on a shared screen and awkward on a kitchen table.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken by a small minority and consequently the hardest subject to staff locally in Sharjah at any price. Needs a long session, usually ninety minutes, because the questions are long. This is the clearest case where distance matching beats a local search.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode and the theory paper are separable, and most students need only one of them. A diagnostic first lesson saves weeks of generic coverage. Later evening slots work well because the practical thinking is less fatigue-sensitive than calculation.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Runs alongside the international curriculum as a mandatory UAE subject and is often the one left to the last fortnight. Short, frequent sessions beat long ones, and the material must be the school's own prescribed content rather than an imported syllabus.

sections.heading: The Al Suyoh school day, and what it leaves
paragraphs: Work backwards from the exam rather than forwards from the school bell and the scheduling becomes obvious. A Year 11 student needs a weekly hour in which they can hold a full Paper 4 question in their head. The question is simply when that hour exists. Most international schools serving this part of Sharjah finish in the early to mid afternoon, which sounds generous until the drive, the meal, the school homework and any after-school commitment are subtracted. What remains is usually a single viable window, and it is later than parents expect.

The table below sets out the shape for the school clusters Al Suyoh children actually attend. It is deliberately expressed in windows rather than exact minutes, because finish times vary by year group and by day, and a page quoting a precise bell time for a named school would be wrong somewhere within a term. What does not vary is the pattern: the nearer the school, the earlier the realistic slot, and the more the family depends on the E311 or the Maliha Road, the later it moves.

Two scheduling errors recur. The first is booking the slot that is available rather than the slot that works, which happens whenever the tutor's route sets the time. The second is booking too early in the day for a Year 11 student and then concluding that tutoring does not help, when what actually failed was the hour. Both disappear when there is no drive to accommodate on either side, which is the practical argument for online delivery in a district laid out like this one.

sections.heading: What the drive does to a four o'clock lesson
paragraphs: Consider the two sides of the same booking. On the tutor's side, a visit to Al Suyoh from Sharjah city means leaving well before the lesson, arriving at a plotted suburb where the junctions are busiest, teaching for an hour, and driving back. That is close to three hours of commitment for sixty minutes of teaching, which is why in-home rates in the UAE are quoted at AED 180-350 in Bestimate's 2026 table and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The parent funds the car either in the rate or in reduced availability.

On the student's side, a four o'clock booking means the lesson lands in the worst hour of their day. They have been in school since morning, they have just completed a drive of their own, and they have school homework still waiting. A tutor who arrives into that is teaching against the clock and the student's energy at once. Nothing in the subject knowledge compensates for it, and a parent watching from the next room usually concludes the tutoring is not working when what is not working is the hour.

Removing the drive fixes both sides simultaneously, which is unusual in a trade-off. The tutor's three hours become one, so their availability widens and late slots become ordinary rather than a favour. The student's lesson moves to the point in the evening where they can actually think. Nobody has to be anywhere, so a session can start at eight and finish at nine without a return journey hanging over it.

The honest limit is worth naming. If your child will not sit and work without an adult physically present, online delivery will not solve that, and we say so at the enquiry rather than after a month. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE; home visiting is offered only in India, so there is nothing to gain here by talking a family out of what they actually need.

sections.heading: Mock season, and planning the term backwards
paragraphs: Every Sharjah British-curriculum school runs internal mock examinations, usually in the winter term and often again in the spring, and those weeks reshape a tutoring schedule more than any other single factor. A student in a mock window should not be meeting new content. They should be working through the papers they have just sat, with the marks in front of them. A tutor who does not know the dates will be halfway through a new topic when the mocks arrive and will lose the most valuable diagnostic opportunity of the year.

The right sequence is to get the mock dates from the school as soon as they are published and build the term around them. Before the window, the work is syllabus coverage and timed practice. During it, the work pauses or becomes revision triage. Immediately afterwards, the marked papers become the agenda for the next month, because a mock paper is the closest thing available to the real one and the mark scheme is the same. Families who send their child's mock papers to the tutor get a term's worth of targeting for free.

The series the mocks are rehearsing matters too, and this is where UAE parents are frequently misinformed. Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series; the February/March series is offered to India only, so any date given for it does not apply to a candidate in Sharjah. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

So the practical instruction for an Al Suyoh family is narrow and important: get the timetable version your child's centre actually uses, from the school's exams officer or the board's own site, and work the schedule backwards from it. Provisional timetables get revised, which is why this page links the official source rather than restating dates that will move.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and the post-Iftar slot
paragraphs: The UAE academic calendar and Ramadan interact with tutoring in a way no competitor page in this market addresses. School hours shorten during Ramadan, the rhythm of the day inverts, and a student who was working well at five in the afternoon may be far better served at nine in the evening after Iftar. For a family in Al Suyoh this is a straightforward adjustment online and an awkward one for anybody driving, since a tutor's post-Iftar availability is competing with their own family's evening.

The practical pattern that works is to agree the Ramadan arrangement before Ramadan starts rather than during it. Some students keep the existing slot and shorten it. Some move the whole session to a post-Iftar window. Some pause for the month and return with the same tutor, which is only possible if the tutor is not filling the gap with somebody else. Saying which of the three you want in advance is the difference between a month of continuity and a month of cancellations.

Prayer times matter on ordinary weeks too, and the fix is simply to schedule around them rather than pretending the calendar does not exist. A fixed slot that habitually collides with Maghrib will be moved every week by one party or the other until it collapses. One conversation at the start about which times genuinely work removes a recurring friction that otherwise gets blamed on the tutor.

The same flexibility applies to travel. Families in this part of Sharjah often spend part of the summer or a winter break abroad, and an online schedule follows them with only a time-zone adjustment to negotiate. That is not a small benefit for a Year 11 student in the spring, when a three-week absence at the wrong moment can cost a topic that will not be retaught.

sections.heading: The travel maths, set out plainly
paragraphs: It helps to see the comparison as time rather than money, because time is what an Al Suyoh evening is short of. The table below counts the minutes each option consumes from the household's day for a single sixty-minute lesson, alongside the published rate bands so the two can be weighed together. The figures for rates are market figures with their sources; none is a price of ours.

The result is not close. An in-home visit consumes the tutor's travel, which the parent funds, and constrains the start time to suit the route. A tuition centre consumes the family's own travel in both directions, which for a plotted suburb means a parent driving twice in an evening. Online consumes the lesson and nothing else. For a household with two children at different schools, that difference compounds across a week into several hours.

The second column of the comparison matters as much as the first. Travel does not only cost time, it narrows the pool, because the only tutors available are those willing to make the trip. For Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics or Pearson 4PM1, the number of specialists prepared to drive to Al Suyoh on a weekday evening may genuinely be zero, and a family paying the in-home premium can end up with a generalist at specialist prices.

None of this is an argument that in-home tutoring is bad. It is an argument that in an inland plotted district with scattered school destinations, the format's costs fall hardest and its benefits are thinnest. Where a student needs physical presence, that calculation changes entirely, and the honest answer is to hire locally for it.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson, and why the week looks different
paragraphs: Parents in Al Suyoh are often surprised to learn their child's school uses different boards for different subjects, and the distinction changes both what is taught and how the term should be paced. Cambridge International tiers many IGCSE subjects into Core and Extended, with different grade ceilings and different papers. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE does not tier in the same way and uses its own syllabus codes, such as 4MA1 for Mathematics, 4PH1 for Physics and 4CH1 for Chemistry. A tutor who does not establish which applies is guessing at the paper your child will sit.

The scheduling consequence is concrete. A Cambridge Extended candidate has a tier decision that should be settled in Year 10, and reviewing it properly needs a session with real work in front of the tutor, in the term the school is deciding. A Pearson candidate does not have that decision but does have a different paper structure to build technique for. The same subject, the same year group, two different term plans.

The exam windows differ as well. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with November functioning as the resit route; the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and for the November 2026 series the final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with November 2025 results having reached students on 22 January 2026 and June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. Those past dates are quoted because they are checkable; future windows are given as the series month only, since provisional timetables are revised.

The actionable version for a parent: find the syllabus code on your child's exam entry or subject report, send it with the enquiry, and the schedule can be built from the right calendar on the first attempt rather than the second.

sections.heading: SPEA, and the Sharjah school year a tutor has to work with
paragraphs: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, so an Al Suyoh child at a Sharjah school sits under SPEA rather than Dubai's KHDA or Abu Dhabi's ADEK. UAE government guidance also records that the Sharjah authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is a broader remit than inspection alone. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge holds comparable powers; Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the federal Ministry of Education.

For scheduling purposes the relevance is that term dates, holiday patterns and assessment calendars are set at school and emirate level rather than nationally, which is why a neighbour whose child commutes to a Dubai school can be on a different half-term from yours. Two children in the same Al Suyoh household at schools in two emirates genuinely can have mismatched holidays, and a tutoring schedule has to accommodate that rather than assume a single calendar.

A tutoring service cannot borrow any regulator's authority, and this one does not. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument for training institutes with premises in Dubai, requiring initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An online matching service does not hold one, and any site advertising regulator-approved tutors is describing something that does not exist in that form.

What is worth verifying is the individual tutor's position. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and UAE government guidance states it is granted free of charge for two years. People tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Since the permit is free, there is no cost reason for a tutor to lack one.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with IGCSE coursework
paragraphs: Most IGCSE subjects are assessed by terminal written papers, but several carry coursework or a practical component, and the boundary there is the same one the IB enforces on an Internal Assessment. The work must be the student's own. A tutor teaches the assessment criteria, explains what each one rewards, models the method on a different example, and reads what the student produced. A tutor does not write, redraft or supply text, and does not complete a practical write-up on the student's behalf.

The practical-science question comes up constantly from families considering online tuition, and deserves a direct answer. Where a school assesses practical work internally, the apparatus and the supervision are the school's responsibility and a tutor's role is to teach the technique, the uncertainty handling and the write-up structure. Where the board uses an alternative-to-practical written paper, that paper rewards students who have genuinely handled apparatus, so the honest advice is to take every laboratory session at school seriously rather than assume tutoring substitutes for it.

English coursework options, where a school offers them, are a related case. Marked feedback on a student's own draft is legitimate and valuable: the criterion that is not met, named, with an instruction to go back and rewrite. An edit that changes the voice is not, and an experienced marker can tell. The slower route is the only safe one, and it is also the one that teaches something transferable.

On timing, which is this page's theme: coursework blocks should be booked in the term before the school deadline, not the fortnight before it. A student who needs to write their own material needs time in which to write it, and a schedule that leaves none has already decided what kind of help it will be asking for.

faqs.question: When can an IGCSE home tutor in Al Suyoh realistically start a session?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the school is. Children at schools in Al Tai or Muwaileh are home early enough for a late-afternoon slot, though Year 11 students usually work better in the early evening once homework has cleared. Children travelling to Sharjah city, Al Hoshi or across the Dubai border are realistically looking at after seven, and after eight for the longest runs. Because lessons are online with no travel on either side, a slot at eight is as straightforward as one at five, which is rarely true of an in-home booking.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to a house in Al Suyoh?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Al Suyoh families are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In a plotted inland district with school destinations in three directions, that is also the format that solves the actual problem, which is finding an hour in the student's day rather than finding somebody nearby. If your child needs an adult physically present to work, the honest recommendation is to hire that locally.

faqs.question: Which exam series does an IGCSE student in Sharjah sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a date quoted for it does not apply in Sharjah. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Confirm with your school's exams officer.

faqs.question: Should a Year 11 student in Al Suyoh have lessons straight after school?
faqs.answer: Usually not. A four o'clock session lands in the weakest hour of a Year 11 day: school has just finished, a drive has just been completed, and school homework is still waiting. Paper 4 technique needs a student who can hold a multi-step question in their head, which is an early-evening activity for most teenagers. The exception is Years 7 to 9, where homework volumes are lower and attention fades later in the evening, so a late-afternoon slot genuinely works better for them.

faqs.question: How should mock examinations change the tutoring schedule?
faqs.answer: They should drive it. Send the mock dates to the tutor as soon as the school publishes them. Before the window, the work is coverage and timed practice. During it, new content stops. Immediately afterwards, the marked papers become the agenda for the next month, because a mock uses the same mark scheme as the real series and shows exactly which marks were available and left behind. Families who hand over the marked mocks get a term of targeted work out of them, which is better than any revision plan built from a syllabus list.

faqs.question: Can an Al Suyoh session move to a post-Iftar time during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth agreeing the arrangement before the month begins. Three patterns work: keep the slot and shorten it, move the whole session to a post-Iftar window, or pause for the month and resume with the same tutor. Online delivery absorbs any of the three without a tutor rearranging a drive, which is the practical reason a post-Iftar slot is easy here and awkward in person. Prayer times on ordinary weeks are worth scheduling around at the outset too, rather than moving the lesson every week.

faqs.question: How do I find out which board my child's Al Suyoh school uses?
faqs.answer: Look at the exam entry slip or the subject page of the school report, both of which carry the syllabus code. Cambridge codes look like 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look like 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. Schools commonly use different boards for different subjects, so check each one rather than assuming the school has a single board. Send the codes with your enquiry and the match is made against tutors who teach those exact papers.

faqs.question: Is a weekend block better than a weekday evening for Al Suyoh families?
faqs.answer: For households running two or three school runs on different schedules, often yes. A ninety-minute weekend session covers a topic and its paper technique in one sitting, where a rushed weekday hour tends to cover one of them. It also makes consecutive sibling sessions straightforward. The trade-off is that a single weekly weekend block gives less contact with the school week, so it suits steady coverage better than it suits reacting to a problem that surfaced on Tuesday.

faqs.question: How long should an IGCSE session be for each subject?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and Physics reward ninety minutes, because a full paper question plus its mark-scheme technique does not compress into twenty minutes of working. Chemistry works well in sixty if the session covers one topic rather than two. English improves fastest in shorter sessions built around a timed piece and feedback. Additional Mathematics and Further Pure need the longer block because the questions themselves are long. Matching length to subject is a cheap decision that most families make by accident rather than deliberately.

faqs.question: What happens to the schedule if we travel from Al Suyoh during term?
faqs.answer: An online schedule follows the family with only a time-zone adjustment to negotiate, which matters more than it sounds for a Year 11 student in the spring. A three-week absence at the wrong point in the syllabus can cost a topic that will not be retaught, and keeping the weekly session running through a trip prevents that. Tell the tutor the dates and the destination's time difference in advance so the slot is agreed rather than improvised while you are away.

faqs.answer: Where a school assesses practical work internally, the apparatus and supervision are the school's responsibility; a tutor teaches the technique, uncertainty handling and write-up structure around it. Where the board uses an alternative-to-practical written paper, that paper rewards candidates who have genuinely handled equipment, so the honest advice is to take every school laboratory session seriously rather than assume tutoring substitutes for it. What online tuition does well here is the data analysis, the graph work and the structured answer, which is where the marks are actually distributed.

faqs.answer: It is one of the best-value sessions available and almost nobody buys it. Cambridge tiers many IGCSE subjects into Core and Extended with different grade ceilings, so a student entered for Core has a limit placed on their result before any revision happens. Reviewing that decision properly means a tutor looking at real marked work in the term the school is deciding, not at predicted grades. Two sessions in Year 10 can change the ceiling; no amount of work in Year 11 can lift it once the entry is made.

intro.heading: The price question, answered before anything else
paragraphs: A parent in Al Taawun typing "IGCSE home tutor in Al Taawun" into Google is almost always carrying two numbers in their head: the grade their child came home with, and the figure they are willing to spend each month to change it. Most tutoring pages answer neither. Three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Sharjah family transacts in. So this page starts with AED and stays with AED.

Al Taawun sits on the Al Khan lagoon, a dense band of residential towers between Al Majaz and the Al Mamzar crossing into Dubai. That geography is the reason a home-tutor search here behaves differently from the same search in a villa community. A tutor driving to a tower in Al Taawun does not park and walk in. They queue on Al Ittihad Road, find visitor parking, clear building security, and reach the apartment door somewhere between fifteen and forty minutes after they intended to. Every one of those minutes is paid for, either in a travel surcharge or in a rate that quietly absorbs it.

The market bands are real and they are wide. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by a university student, advertises from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45–65 and Tutopiya AED 33–52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one visits, with travel inside the figure, run AED 180 to AED 500, Bestimate's Dubai rate table placing the usual range at AED 180–350. Specialist IGCSE and A-Level tutors are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above; TutorChase publishes AED 270. The top of the market is named-examiner work at AED 500–650, with BartyED at AED 650.

Read those five bands side by side and the pattern is obvious. The jump from online to in-home is roughly AED 60 to AED 150 an hour for the same tutor teaching the same syllabus. That is the travel premium, and in a tower district it buys travel, not teaching. A family paying it in Al Taawun is paying for the Al Ittihad Road queue and the lift, and the student gets exactly the same sixty minutes of 0580 practice they would have had on screen.

IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Al Taawun students are taught one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and the past paper on screen. The honest case for that is not that it is cheaper, although it usually is. It is that the pool stops being whoever lives within a twenty-minute drive of the Al Khan lagoon and becomes whoever actually teaches Cambridge Extended Additional Maths 0606 well.

What follows is the full cost picture: rate tables, the monthly arithmetic, the three ways Sharjah families most often waste tutoring money, the Cambridge-versus-Edexcel decision that quietly changes what you are buying, and the June series counted backwards so you know which weeks matter.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-taawun.programmesIntro: An IGCSE search in Al Taawun covers more than one qualification. Sharjah schools run Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and in some cases both inside the same year group for different subjects. The route a student is already on decides which papers matter, which is why the first conversation is about codes rather than subject names.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year Cambridge course most British-curriculum schools in Sharjah run, assessed by terminal written papers at the end of Year 11. Subjects are tiered: Core entry caps the grade at C, Extended reaches A*. Syllabus codes matter more than titles — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English. Practical science is assessed either by an alternative-to-practical paper or a timetabled practical, and which one a school uses changes the revision plan completely.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A Sharjah school and a Dubai school may not share a zone, so the timetable to work from is the one the school's exams officer issues, not a version downloaded from a search result. UAE centres sit the June and November series only.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's international qualification, codes beginning 4 — 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Mathematics Specification A is tiered Foundation and Higher, with two papers each. Pearson's science papers carry no separate coursework component for most routes, which concentrates the whole grade into written papers and makes timed practice the entire preparation strategy for a weak candidate.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results reached students in January — November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live PDF is the only version worth planning around.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, ending in Checkpoint tests that schools use for setting decisions. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint in March, May and October. Families in Al Taawun often arrive at tutoring in Year 9 because a Checkpoint result put a child into Core rather than Extended Maths, and that single decision shapes the grade ceiling two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Tier placement made in Year 9 in a Sharjah school is rarely revisited without a parent asking. A Core entry caps the Cambridge Mathematics grade at C, which is above the MoE equivalency floor of grade E but below what most UAE and overseas universities want for an engineering or medical route. Tutoring aimed at a tier appeal is cheaper and more effective in Year 9 than remediation in Year 11.

programmes.name: AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: Where most Sharjah IGCSE students go next. AS and A Level subject entry usually assumes a grade A or B at IGCSE Extended in that subject, and the step up in Mathematics and the sciences is steep because A Level assumes algebraic fluency IGCSE only samples. Families planning this route use Year 11 tutoring differently: the target is not a pass but the specific topics AS builds on directly.
programmes.countryNote: MoE equivalency on the British track asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject rule; the sourced figure is five.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-taawun.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Sharjah families request most for Al Taawun students, with the specific place each one leaks marks. A tutor who cannot name that place in the first conversation is being paid to find out at your expense.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended Paper 4 is where the grade is decided: structured multi-mark questions on functions, transformations, vectors and probability trees. Marks are lost to method rather than arithmetic — unshown working on a four-mark question scores one. Pearson 4MA1 splits the same content across two equally weighted papers, so pacing matters more than on Cambridge.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Maths. Introduces calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities that 0580 never touches. The common failure is treating it as harder 0580 practice; it is a different syllabus with its own command terms, and students who do well have drilled differentiation from first principles.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism account for most dropped marks, specifically circuit calculations where students read a potential divider as a series chain. The six-mark extended-response items reward structured reasoning, not recall. Which practical route the school uses — Paper 5 practical or Paper 6 alternative-to-practical — changes half the revision plan.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and organic reaction pathways carry the grade. Students lose marks on titration arithmetic by dropping units mid-calculation and on organic questions by naming a product without the functional group. Qualitative analysis tables are examinable in full and are the cheapest marks on the paper to secure.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem, not difficulty. Transport in plants, homeostasis and genetics crosses between papers, and extended-response marks go to students who use the mark-scheme vocabulary — active transport, partially permeable, selective reabsorption — rather than paraphrase. Data-analysis questions on unfamiliar experiments are where strong students separate.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 0990 / 4EA1)
subjects.description: The directed-writing task is marked on audience, register and form as much as on content, and Sharjah students who write fluent but generic prose sit at grade C. Reading questions on 0500 Paper 1 require quotation plus explanation; a quotation alone scores nothing. Pearson 4EA1 carries a different anthology, so the texts are not interchangeable.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Widely taken in Sharjah schools where English is an additional language. The reading-and-writing paper rewards precise information transfer; students lose marks by copying whole sentences into a note-taking grid. Speaking is separately assessed and often under-prepared because it carries no written revision material.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450 / 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole paper. A textbook-correct definition with no reference to the named business in the stem scores at the bottom band. Evaluation questions carry the top marks and require a judgement with a reason, which is the single most trainable skill in the syllabus and the one most tutoring ignores.

subjects.name: Economics (0455 / 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides grades. Axis labels, shift direction and a stated new equilibrium are all separately credited, and students who draw from memory without labelling lose three marks before the explanation starts. UAE-context data questions appear regularly, which makes Gulf examples genuinely useful revision rather than colour.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478 / 4CP0)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory on data representation and networks is learnable and routinely under-revised; students spend their time on programming and lose the easier marks. Pseudocode questions are marked against the syllabus's own pseudocode conventions, not Python, and that mismatch costs marks on every trace-table question.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.levels: First language and additional language routes
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools, and examinable at IGCSE in its own right. Grammar accuracy and comprehension of unseen passages carry the marks. Separate streams exist for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and material from one stream does not transfer to the other.

subjects.name: Accounting (0452 / 4AC1)
subjects.description: Format marks are free and routinely thrown away: a correctly balanced trial balance with the wrong headings loses presentation marks. Adjustments for accruals, prepayments and depreciation are the recurring failure point, and the fix is repeated full-question practice under time rather than topic revision.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-taawun.regionsIntro: Al Taawun does not stand alone. It belongs to a band of dense Sharjah districts whose families share schools, traffic and session timing. These are the neighbourhoods an Al Taawun tutoring plan is really competing with for a 5pm slot.

regions.name: Al Taawun
regions.note: Residential towers along the Al Khan lagoon, close to the Al Mamzar crossing. Apartment living means visitor parking and building access add real minutes to any home visit, and sibling sessions often run back-to-back in the same flat.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: The waterfront district immediately south, sharing the lagoon and much of Al Taawun's school catchment. Families here face the same Al Ittihad Road congestion northbound in the evening, which pushes realistic session starts past 5.30pm.

regions.name: Al Khan
regions.note: Between Al Taawun and the Sharjah Aquarium, a mix of towers and older villas. Shorter school runs than the Muwaileh side of the emirate, so Al Khan students often manage a 4.30pm start that Al Zahia families cannot.

regions.name: Al Nahda, Sharjah
regions.note: The densest residential block on the Dubai border, with a large share of children attending Dubai schools. A Dubai school day plus the Al Nahda return journey means tutoring here is a post-7pm activity on weekdays.

regions.name: Al Qasimia
regions.note: Central Sharjah, close to the older British and Indian curriculum schools. Short commutes but heavy local traffic around school gates, and a cluster of CBSE schools alongside the IGCSE ones, which mixes the tutoring demand.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: Inland towards University City, with several large British and bilingual schools. The commute out to Muwaileh from the lagoon districts is long enough that families who moved across the emirate usually keep the same online tutor.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: Sharjah's higher-education corridor. A large pool of university students tutor here, which is why Sharjah's budget tutoring band is genuinely cheaper than Dubai's — and why checking who is actually teaching matters more.

regions.name: Aljada
regions.note: A newer master-planned community south of Muwaileh with its own schools opening progressively. Families moving in from the lagoon districts carry their tutoring arrangements with them, and an online arrangement survives the move intact.

schoolClusters.city: Al Taawun, Al Majaz and Al Khan
schoolClusters.note: The lagoon-side catchment. Students here attend a mix of British-curriculum and Indian-curriculum schools within Sharjah, with a significant share crossing to Dubai schools through Al Mamzar. Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE both appear in this cluster, sometimes within one year group.

This is what most Al Taawun families start with and what the market's AED 150–300 online band is quoting for. It works when the gap is a named topic or a technique, and the student is doing the homework between sessions.
