sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor in Al Taawun costs, by tier and format
paragraphs: A qualified IGCSE subject tutor working online in this market charges between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour. An in-home visit for the same subject, with travel inside the figure, runs AED 180 to AED 500. Those are market bands collected from published competitor pricing and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate table, not IB Gram's own price list.

The table below splits the market the way a parent actually shops: by level, by format, and by what a month of it costs. Monthly figures assume one session a week unless the row says otherwise, and they are the market's own package arithmetic — AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits both appear as advertised packages in this market.

Two things are worth noticing before the numbers. The first is how little the online band moves between Core and Extended tier for the same subject; the tier changes what is taught, not what an hour of teaching costs. The second is that the in-home column is consistently AED 60 to AED 150 higher for identical teaching, and in a tower district that gap is funding a car and a lift, not a better lesson.

One more thing the table will not say out loud. The widest band on it is the budget row, and that width is the whole risk. AED 45 and AED 150 buy very different hours from the same advertised tier, and the only way to tell them apart before paying is a trial lesson where the tutor reads a marked paper in front of you.

sections.heading: The travel premium in a tower district, worked out in minutes
paragraphs: The in-home premium is not a mystery charge. It is the tutor's travel time, priced. A tutor who teaches four students a day and drives between them is selling perhaps five billable hours out of an eight-hour working evening, and the rate has to cover the other three.

In Al Taawun the arithmetic is worse than in a villa community, which is counter-intuitive until you have done the drive. A villa visit in Al Zahia or Tilal City means gate security and a driveway. A tower visit in Al Taawun means the Al Ittihad Road approach at the exact hour it is slowest, then visitor parking that may be full, then a security desk, then a lift in a building with several hundred apartments. Fifteen minutes is a good run. Forty is normal on a Sunday or Monday evening.

Set against that, a live-video session starts when it says it starts. The student is at the kitchen table at 5.30pm with the paper open; the tutor is on screen at 5.30pm. Nothing is lost to the lagoon or the lift. The table prices the difference across a term so the comparison is in dirhams rather than adjectives.

There is a second cost hidden in the travel column, and it is the student's. A session that starts twenty minutes late either runs twenty minutes short or pushes dinner and the rest of the homework back. Over a term that erosion is not small, and it falls hardest on the exam-year student who has least slack in the evening to give away.

sections.heading: Three ways Sharjah families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: The expensive mistakes in this market are not about choosing the wrong hourly rate. They are structural, and all three are avoidable before the first invoice.

The first is buying hours against the wrong diagnosis. A student failing Extended Maths Paper 4 because they do not show method needs technique work, which is four to six sessions. The same student put onto a full syllabus re-teach will take thirty sessions and still lose the method marks. Any tutor should be able to name the failure mode after reading one marked paper; if the answer is "we will start from the beginning and build confidence", you are buying hours, not diagnosis.

The second is paying for the wrong board. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 cover overlapping content with different papers, different tiering and different question styles. A tutor fluent in one will teach the other adequately, and "adequately" is what costs a grade in a timed paper. Ask which board the school enters and which code; a school's exams officer will confirm both in a sentence.

The third is starting in Year 11 term two. The content gap that takes six sessions in Year 10 takes fifteen in March of the exam year, because the student is simultaneously revising eight other subjects. The cheapest IGCSE tutoring in Al Taawun is early tutoring, and it is cheaper by a factor, not a margin.

A fourth mistake is quieter than the other three: paying for hours nobody is checking. Tutoring that is never measured against the school's own marked work can run for two terms on goodwill alone. Set the review point before the first session, name the mark you expect to recover, and look at it on paper after six weeks.
bullets: Ask for the failure mode in writing after one marked paper, before booking a block
Confirm the syllabus code with the school, not the subject name
Six sessions in Year 10 routinely do the work of fifteen in Year 11
Decline any plan that cannot say what the next four sessions will cover

sections.heading: Online, in-home or group: priced against what each actually fixes
paragraphs: Format is a cost decision and a pedagogy decision at once, and the two answers do not always agree. Group tutoring is genuinely cheaper per hour and genuinely worse for a student whose problem is a specific misconception, because the group moves at the syllabus's pace rather than the student's.

In-home visits earn their premium in two situations. One is a young student who cannot hold attention on a screen without an adult in the room. The other is a household where the study space is shared and a physical tutor enforces the hour. Neither applies to most Year 10 and Year 11 students in Al Taawun, who already do homework on a laptop.

Online one-to-one wins on the thing that actually decides IGCSE grades: who is teaching. Sharjah's local tutor pool is real but thin at the specialist end — Additional Maths 0606, Computer Science 0478 pseudocode, Economics diagram technique. A family restricted to tutors who will drive to Al Taawun is choosing from a short list. A family on live video is not.

One practical note on the group option. Two friends at the same school, the same board and the same tier can genuinely share a tutor well, and the saving is real. Two students at different tiers cannot, because Core and Extended questions diverge sharply by the second half of the syllabus and one of the pair will spend the hour watching.
Centre group classes carry a hidden logistics cost too: they are a second school run, in the evening, on the same roads the first one used.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: what guessing wrong costs you
paragraphs: Sharjah schools do not all enter the same board, and some enter different boards for different subjects within the same year group. Parents rarely know which, because the school report says "Mathematics", not "0580 Extended". That gap is where tutoring money leaks quietly for a full term.

The practical differences are not cosmetic. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended, with Extended Paper 4 carrying the structured long questions that decide the grade. Pearson 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher, with two papers of equal weight, so a student who mismanages time on Paper 1 cannot recover it on a shorter second paper. Science practical assessment differs again: a Cambridge centre may use Paper 5 practical or Paper 6 alternative-to-practical, and the revision required is not the same.

The table sets the two boards side by side for the subjects Al Taawun families ask about most. Confirm the row that applies with the school's exams officer before the first paid session. It takes one email and it is the highest-return question a parent can ask.

There is one more reason to confirm the code early. Past papers are board-specific, and a term of practice on the wrong board's papers is worse than no practice, because the student learns question shapes that will not appear. Pearson and Cambridge both publish their materials free through the school, so there is no cost to getting this right.
Finally, check whether the school enters the same board for every subject. Several in this cluster do not, and a split entry is easy to miss from a report card.

sections.heading: The June series counted backwards from today
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what determines whether tutoring money is well spent. Eight sessions in February do different work from eight sessions in November, and the price is the same.

Work backwards from the June series. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, mocks land in the preceding term, and the window where timed full-paper practice actually changes a grade is roughly the eight weeks before the first exam. Before that window, the money should be buying content and technique. Inside it, the money should be buying marked papers.

Dates below are the structure of the year, not a timetable. Cambridge and Pearson both revise published timetables, and Cambridge warns explicitly that it cannot take responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong zone version. Take the live PDF from the exams officer and plan against that.

Ramadan deserves its own line in this plan. Study patterns shift, evenings run later, and a timed-paper block scheduled straight through the month tends to be rescheduled anyway. Families who plan around it — lighter sessions during, the intensive block either side — lose nothing, while families who plan through it lose the sessions and the momentum.

Results day deserves planning as well. A June grade that misses an AS requirement has a November resit route, but the entry for it closes quickly, so the decision window is days rather than weeks. Families who have already asked the exams officer what a resit entry involves make that call calmly; families who have not spend the week guessing.

sections.heading: SPEA, the MoHRE permit, and what a cheap tutor might be skipping
paragraphs: Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate. SPEA's remit goes further than inspection: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is why a Sharjah school's IGCSE offer can differ from a Dubai school's, and why the emirate matters when you are reading a school report.

Private tutoring itself sits under a different rule. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

This is where the bottom of the AED 45–150 band deserves a question. The permit is free, which means there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one. Ask. And note the separate restriction in Abu Dhabi, press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE code of conduct carries a similar bar. A tutor who offers to teach their own enrolled student is not a bargain.

IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge, and holds no such permit or partnership. Naming a regulator on this page describes the system your child studies inside; it does not imply any endorsement of us.

sections.heading: What a tutor may never do, at any price
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but the boundary still matters, and in this market it is routinely crossed. One operator in the researched set sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for the student, who carries the consequence, not the seller.

The line is simple to state. A tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria, reads the student's own draft and says where it falls short against the published descriptors. A tutor does not write, redraft to completion, or supply model answers for submission. Coursework and controlled-assessment components across IGCSE subjects — English coursework routes, Business and Computer Science projects where a centre runs them — all sit under that rule.

Nor should a tutor be supplying syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those are Cambridge's and Pearson's copyright, available free from the boards and from the school. A tutor's job is to work through them with the student, cite the source, and link to the official page.
Ask any prospective tutor in Al Taawun what they will not do. The answer separates teaching from the essay-mill end of this market faster than any rate table.

A related question worth asking: what does the tutor do when they do not know an answer? The honest reply is that they look it up in the board's published material and come back with the reference. Anyone who invents an answer in front of a student is teaching them to do the same in an exam, which costs marks the mark scheme will not forgive.

sections.heading: What happens if no specialist is free for your subject
paragraphs: Availability is the thing nobody in this market discloses, and it is a cost question too, because a badly matched tutor is the most expensive tutor there is. Common IGCSE subjects — Maths, the three sciences, English — have depth. Additional Maths 0606, Computer Science 0478, Accounting 0452 and Arabic first-language at IGCSE level are thinner, and so is any subject at a specific tier in a specific exam window.

When a specialist is not free for the slot an Al Taawun family needs, there are three honest answers and one dishonest one. The honest ones are: offer a different time with the right tutor, offer a tutor at the same level teaching from a different time zone over live video, or say the match is not available this term. The dishonest one is putting a general science tutor in front of a 0606 candidate and calling it a match.

This is also where the free trial lesson does real work. It is not a sales device; it is the point where a parent finds out whether the tutor can name the failure mode in the student's marked paper. If they cannot, the trial has saved a term's fees. If they can, the rate stops being the main question.

Availability also moves with the calendar. The eight weeks before the June series are the busiest hours in this market, and a specialist who was free in October may not be free in April at 5pm Gulf Standard Time. Families who book the slot early hold it; families who wait until the mocks come back take whatever is left.

process.title: Send the marked paper, not the report card
process.description: Share the most recent marked IGCSE paper or mock, the syllabus code if you have it, and the school name. A report grade says there is a problem. A marked paper says which four marks were lost and why, and that is what a tutor needs to say anything useful before being paid.

process.title: Confirm board and tier with the school
process.description: One email to the exams officer gets you the board, the code and the tier — Cambridge 0580 Extended, Pearson 4MA1 Higher, whichever it is. This is the single question that most often changes which tutor is right, and it costs nothing to ask.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A one-to-one session over live video at a time that works after the Sharjah school run. Judge it on one thing: did the tutor identify the specific failure mode and say what the next four sessions will cover? Vagueness at this stage becomes billed hours later.

process.title: Agree a block with a stated target
process.description: Weekly, twice weekly or an exam-window intensive, with a written note of what each block is meant to fix. Market monthly packages run from around AED 799 for eight online sessions upward; agree what you are buying before the first invoice rather than after the third.

process.title: Review against the school's own assessments
process.description: Six weeks in, compare the next marked paper with the first one. If the named failure mode has not moved, the plan changes or the tutor changes. Progress is measured on school marks, not on how the sessions felt.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the competitor or rate table it came from, with the month it was read. Three of the six strongest pages in this market publish no price at all, and one of them asks the price in its own FAQ and declines to answer it.

whyPoints.description: Not to a subject name. A tutor who teaches Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 4 well is a different hire from one who teaches Pearson 4MA1 Higher well, and a different hire again from an Additional Maths 0606 specialist. The code is the match key.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is offered only in India. That is on this page because a parent should not have to discover it after booking.

whyPoints.description: A tutor reads the student's own work and says where it falls short of the published criteria. A tutor does not write it. That is stated here because an operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments, and a parent deserves to know which side of that line they are buying from.

whyPoints.description: No guaranteed grades, no satisfaction percentages, no star ratings we cannot evidence. Competitors in this market publish contradictory review counts on the same page. A figure without its source and date is a liability, not reassurance.

whyPoints.title: A free trial before any payment
whyPoints.description: One session, no payment, no card. The purpose is for you to test whether the tutor can diagnose from a marked paper. If they cannot, you have lost an hour instead of a term's fees, and that is the trial doing its job.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for an IGCSE tutor in Al Taawun?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified IGCSE subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and in-home visits with travel included run AED 180 to AED 500. Budget tutoring, usually a university student, advertises from AED 45 upward — EdFlik publishes AED 45–65 and Tutopiya AED 33–52. Specialist IGCSE work is quoted higher: TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED's examiner tier AED 650. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram's price list. For our own costs, take the free trial and the consultation that follows it.

faqs.question: Why does an in-home tutor in Al Taawun cost more than an online one for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Because you are paying for travel. A tutor driving to a tower in Al Taawun loses fifteen to forty minutes each way to the Al Ittihad Road approach, visitor parking, building security and the lift, and the hourly rate has to cover the hours that are not billable. Across a twelve-week term at one subject, that premium works out at roughly AED 1,800 in this market — close to the full cost of a second subject taught online. The teaching inside the hour is identical.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to my apartment in Al Taawun?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Al Taawun students are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run, with the past paper and a shared whiteboard on screen. The practical gain is the tutor pool: instead of choosing from people willing to drive to the lagoon at 5pm, you are choosing from whoever teaches your child's syllabus code best.

faqs.question: Is cheap tutoring in Sharjah worse than expensive tutoring?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, but it buys something different. The AED 45–150 band generally buys content explanation and homework supervision, which genuinely helps a student who has missed topics. It rarely buys mark-scheme technique, which is what moves a grade from C to A on an Extended paper. If the problem is unshown method on 0580 Paper 4, a cheaper tutor who does not read mark schemes will not fix it however many hours you buy. Match the tier to the diagnosis, not to the budget.

faqs.question: Which exam board does my child's Sharjah school use, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer, and ask for the subject code rather than the subject name. Sharjah schools enter both boards, and some use different boards for different subjects inside one year group. The answer changes your tutoring: Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended with a heavily weighted Paper 4, while Pearson 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher with two equally weighted papers. A tutor fluent in one teaches the other adequately, and adequately costs marks under time.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams actually happen for students in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only and does not apply to UAE candidates. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January — November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. Always work from the live timetable your school's exams officer issues, because Cambridge allocates centres to six zones and the wrong version can cost a paper.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an Al Taawun IGCSE student usually need?
faqs.answer: Most families start with one weekly session on one subject and adjust after the first marked assessment. One session a week closes a named topic gap or trains a technique if the student does the work between lessons. Two subjects usually means two separate specialists rather than one tutor covering both, because Physics marks lost to electromagnetism reasoning and Maths marks lost to unshown method are different teaching problems. In the eight weeks before the June series, families often switch to a compressed block of timed papers instead.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring if my child is already in Year 11?
faqs.answer: No, but it is more expensive, and the plan has to change. A content gap that takes six sessions in Year 10 can take fifteen in the spring of Year 11, because the student is revising seven or eight other subjects at the same time. Starting late means prioritising: pick the two subjects where marks are most recoverable, work from marked papers rather than the syllabus, and accept that full re-teaching is not possible. An error log across timed papers does more in eight weeks than topic revision does.

faqs.question: Is a tutor charging AED 60 an hour in Al Taawun likely to hold a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted figure with caution. Because the permit is free, there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one.

faqs.question: What is SPEA and how does it affect my child's IGCSE course?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate. Its remit is wider than inspection: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is why a Sharjah school's IGCSE subject offer can differ from a Dubai school's a few kilometres away, and why a report or a subject list has to be read in the context of the emirate the school sits in. IB Gram is not approved, licensed or endorsed by SPEA or any other UAE regulator.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework or a project my child has to submit?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills the task needs, explain the published assessment criteria, read the student's own draft and say where it falls short. A tutor cannot write it, redraft it to completion, or supply a model answer for submission. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that is an integrity breach and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. Ask any prospective tutor what they will not do — the answer tells you which end of this market you are dealing with.

faqs.question: Does my child need five or six IGCSE passes for UAE equivalency in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Alongside that, equivalency asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One competitor page states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. Verify your own case with the Ministry, since equivalency is a process IB Gram describes rather than performs.

faqs.question: Can sessions be scheduled around the Al Taawun school run and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the timing question is real in this district. Lagoon-side families often manage a 4.30pm or 5pm start, while households whose children attend Dubai schools through Al Mamzar are usually looking at 7pm or later once the return journey is done. Sessions are booked in Gulf Standard Time and the slot is held weekly. During Ramadan most families move to a post-Iftar slot, and an exam-window intensive is better planned around the month than driven through it.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is available for my child's specific subject and tier?
faqs.answer: Then you should be told that rather than offered a substitute. Mathematics, the three sciences and English have real depth in this pool. Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478, Accounting 0452 and IGCSE Arabic first language are thinner, and a specific tier in a specific exam window can be thinner still. The honest options are a different time slot with the right specialist, a tutor teaching from another time zone over live video, or a wait. Putting a general science tutor in front of an 0606 candidate is not a match.

faqs.question: How do I know after one month whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Compare marked work, not impressions. Before the block starts, get the named failure mode in writing — unshown method on structured questions, mark-scheme vocabulary missing from extended responses, circuit calculations misread. After four to six sessions, look at the next marked paper or school assessment for that specific loss. If it has not moved, the plan changes or the tutor changes. Sessions that feel productive while the same marks keep disappearing are the most common way tutoring money is wasted in this market.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-taawun.closingHeading: Start with the marked paper and a trial lesson
sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-taawun.closingBody: If you are weighing an IGCSE home tutor in Al Taawun against an online specialist, the deciding question is not the hourly rate. It is whether the tutor can look at your child's last marked paper and say exactly which marks went and why. Send that paper, tell us the board and code if the school has confirmed them, and take a free trial session over live video at a time that fits the Sharjah school run. You will know within the hour whether the diagnosis is real — and that is a far cheaper test than a term of invoices.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-zahia.tutorsIntro: Tutors are listed against the component they teach, not the subject alone — 0580 Extended Paper 4, 0625 Paper 6 alternative-to-practical, 4CH1 written papers. A tutor who can name what a component rewards before the first session is a tutor who has marked against it.

intro.heading: The paper, not the subject
paragraphs: A school report says your child is a grade C in Physics. That sentence contains almost no information you can act on. The useful version is narrower: on Cambridge 0625 at Extended tier, they are losing marks on Paper 4 extended-response items about potential dividers and electromagnetic induction, and on the alternative-to-practical paper they are describing results instead of explaining anomalies. That version tells you what to buy.

Getting to that version is what this page is for. It sets out, subject by subject, which components your child actually sits, where marks are lost in each, and what kind of practice recovers them — because those three things are what a competent tutor should be able to state in the first conversation, and most cannot.

There are two reasons families in Al Zahia end up with vague tutoring. The first is that the report card never names a component. The second is that most tutoring enquiries are answered with reassurance rather than detail, and reassurance is easier to produce than a diagnosis. A page that gives you the detail lets you tell the difference.

The structure to hold onto is this. Cambridge science subjects give Extended candidates a multiple-choice paper and a theory paper, plus either a timetabled practical or an alternative-to-practical written paper depending on what the centre runs. Cambridge Mathematics gives Extended candidates a short-answer paper and a structured paper, with the structured one carrying the long multi-mark questions where method marks live. Pearson's International GCSE equivalents concentrate most routes into written papers, usually two of equal weight, which changes the pacing risk entirely.

Al Zahia itself is villa and townhouse housing immediately west of Muwaileh, with City Centre Al Zahia alongside and established routes into the main campuses. Those routes feed the Maliha Road corridor at the hour several large schools release, so a household here is typically settled around half past five, later with two school runs. That sets the session window and nothing else about the teaching.

A parent does not need the subject to use any of this. The published mark scheme and the paper sit side by side, and reading one against the other for twenty minutes produces a list of specific losses. That list is what turns a tutoring enquiry from a request for reassurance into a brief.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. In-home tutoring is offered only in India, and there is no UAE office or centre. Al Zahia students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and the published mark scheme open on a shared screen — which is, for this kind of work, the format that makes most sense anyway.
What follows is the subject detail: Mathematics, the three sciences, English, and the traps that appear in every one of them, followed by the practice method that actually changes a mark.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-zahia.programmesIntro: Two boards, two tiering systems and one progression route sit behind this search. Establish which applies before anything else, because the components differ and so does the practice archive.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit codes and tiered entry. Core candidates sit one set of components with the grade capped at C; Extended candidates sit a different set reaching A*. In the sciences, Extended candidates take a multiple-choice paper and a theory paper, plus either a timetabled practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper. In Mathematics 0580, Extended candidates take a short-answer paper and a structured paper, and the structured one is where multi-mark method is credited.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only and is not available to Sharjah candidates. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, says it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes beginning with 4. Mathematics Specification A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher with two papers of equal weight, so a pacing failure on the first paper cannot be made up later. The sciences — 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1 — concentrate most routes into written papers, with practical skills examined within them rather than in a separate practical test. Grades are reported 9 to 1 rather than A* to G.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January — November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the next day. Provisional timetables are published ahead of each series, so plan from the live official PDF.

programmes.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics, and Extended-tier only. It introduces differentiation, integration, logarithms, the factor theorem and trigonometric identities that 0580 never reaches. The standard failure is treating it as harder 0580 revision, when it is a separate syllabus with its own command terms and its own question shapes, and it rewards deliberate drilling of calculus technique.
programmes.countryNote: The tutor pool for 0606 is thin across the whole emirate, which matters more than it would for a common subject: a student entered for it in a school that offers it to a small set may have limited support at school as well. If the school does not offer it at all, the private-candidate route through a centre that accepts external entries exists, and the exams officer can explain what it involves.

programmes.name: AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: The destination that explains why specific IGCSE topics matter more than others. A Level Mathematics assumes algebraic fluency that 0580 only samples, and A Level sciences assume the quantitative work IGCSE treats lightly. Year 11 tutoring aimed at progression weights the topics AS builds on directly — algebraic manipulation, functions, moles and energetics, electricity — rather than spreading evenly across the syllabus.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor states six subjects; the sourced figure is five.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-zahia.subjectsIntro: Each entry below names the component where the grade is decided and the behaviour that loses marks there. These are the lines to put to a prospective tutor — the answers tell you whether they have read a mark scheme.

subjects.name: Mathematics — 0580 Extended
subjects.description: The structured paper carries the long multi-mark questions on functions, transformations, vectors, probability trees and compound measures. Method marks are awarded independently of the final answer, so a correct answer with no working on a four-mark item typically scores one. Non-exact answers without the required rounding instruction lose accuracy marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics — 4MA1 Higher
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, so running out of time on the first is unrecoverable. Content overlaps 0580 Extended but question phrasing differs, and the Pearson style leans more on multi-step problems set in context. Practice has to be board-specific; a term on the wrong archive teaches question shapes that will not appear.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics — 0606
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, logarithms, the factor theorem, trigonometric identities and kinematics. Marks go to technique executed cleanly rather than to insight, which makes it unusually responsive to deliberate drilling. Students who struggle usually have an algebra weakness underneath rather than a calculus one.

subjects.name: Physics — 0625 Extended
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism take most of the lost marks, especially potential dividers read as plain series chains and induction questions answered without naming the changing flux. Extended-response items reward stating the principle before the calculation. The practical route — timetabled test or alternative-to-practical — decides half the revision plan.

subjects.name: Chemistry — 0620 Extended
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic and organic pathways carry the grade. Units dropped mid-titration cost accuracy marks; a product named without its functional group scores nothing. Qualitative analysis — the ion tests and their observations — is examinable in detail and is the cheapest set of marks on the paper to secure.

subjects.name: Biology — 0610 Extended
subjects.description: Volume rather than conceptual difficulty. Extended-response marks go to candidates using the mark scheme's own vocabulary — active transport, partially permeable, selective reabsorption — rather than paraphrasing it. Questions on unfamiliar experiments with data are where strong candidates separate, and they are trainable.

subjects.name: English First Language — 0500
subjects.description: The reading paper requires quotation plus explanation of effect; a quotation alone scores nothing, and so does an assertion with no textual anchor. The writing paper is marked on audience, register and form as well as content, which is why fluent but generic prose settles at C regardless of accuracy.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language — 0510 / 0511
subjects.description: The reading-and-writing paper rewards precise information transfer, and lifting whole sentences into a note-taking grid loses marks the mark scheme awards for selection. Speaking is separately assessed, carries no written revision material, and is consequently the least prepared component in the subject.

subjects.name: Economics — 0455
subjects.description: Diagram marks are awarded separately for axis labels, correct shift direction and a stated new equilibrium, so a remembered sketch loses three marks before any explanation. Evaluation questions need a judgement with a reason attached, and the judgement sentence is the single most trainable thing in the syllabus.

subjects.name: Business Studies — 0450
subjects.description: Every answer is marked against the named business in the stem. A textbook-correct definition with no application sits in the bottom band however accurate it is. Evaluation carries the top marks and is where candidates who revise content but not technique stall at a B.

subjects.name: Computer Science — 0478
subjects.description: Pseudocode is marked against the syllabus's own conventions rather than Python, which costs marks on every trace table and on algorithm-writing questions. Theory on data representation, networks and security is learnable and chronically under-revised because students prefer to code.

subjects.name: Accounting — 0452
subjects.description: Presentation marks are free and routinely discarded: a balanced trial balance with incorrect headings loses them. Accruals, prepayments and depreciation adjustments are the recurring failure point, and the fix is repeated full timed questions rather than topic-by-topic revision.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 Extended: where the marks actually sit
paragraphs: Extended Mathematics candidates sit a short-answer paper and a structured paper. The short-answer paper rewards accuracy and speed across a wide spread of topics. The structured paper carries the long multi-mark questions, and it is where grades are decided because it is where method marks exist.

Method marks are awarded independently of the final answer, which is the single most valuable thing a student can understand about this syllabus. A candidate who sets out a correct method and makes an arithmetic slip at the end can score three out of four. A candidate who writes the right answer with no working on the same question typically scores one. That is not a rule about neatness; it is how the marking works.

The topics that recur in the lost-mark list are consistent: transformations described without naming the type and the parameters, vectors where the position and direction are conflated, probability trees where the second branch is not conditioned, functions where composite and inverse notation are swapped, and compound measures where units are not carried through the calculation.

Rounding is its own quiet thief. Questions specify the degree of accuracy required, and an answer given to the wrong number of significant figures loses the accuracy mark even when the mathematics is right. Students who have never been shown this lose a mark or two on every paper for two years.

The practice that fixes all of this is narrow: structured-paper questions, worked with the mark scheme visible afterwards, with the student annotating where each mark was available. Four sessions of that changes more than a term of topic revision in a student whose content is already broadly present.

sections.heading: 0625 Physics: electricity, induction and the practical route
paragraphs: Physics loses marks in a small number of places with great reliability, and electricity is first among them. The potential divider is the clearest example: students read a divider as a plain series circuit, apply a single current to the whole arrangement and lose the question before they start calculating.

Electromagnetic induction is second. The marks require a changing magnetic flux to be named as the cause, and answers that describe the wire moving without connecting it to flux change score below the top band however physically sensible they sound. Extended-response items in general reward stating the principle first and then calculating — a structure that can be taught in one session and practised in three.

Third is the treatment of graphs and gradients. Questions asking what a gradient represents are answered with a value rather than a quantity, and the mark is for the quantity. Similarly, questions about an area under a graph expect the physical meaning, not an arithmetic result alone.

Then the practical route, which is a centre-level decision and changes half the revision plan. A centre running a timetabled practical test needs apparatus handling, observation recording and the discipline of repeating a reading. A centre running the alternative-to-practical written paper needs something quite different: interpreting someone else's method, identifying the variable that was not controlled, and explaining an anomalous result rather than noting it.

Both are teachable over live video, and the alternative-to-practical route arguably better, because it is entirely a written skill. What is not acceptable is a revision plan built without knowing which one the centre uses, and that is a question for the head of science rather than for a tutor.

sections.heading: 0620 Chemistry: moles, mechanisms and the free marks
paragraphs: Chemistry divides neatly into the part that is calculation and the part that is recall-with-precision, and marks are lost differently in each.

On the calculation side, mole arithmetic carries the grade. The recurring failure is not conceptual — most students can state the relationship — but procedural: units are dropped halfway through a titration calculation, concentrations and amounts are mixed, and the answer emerges with no indication of what it is. The mark scheme awards the setting-out as well as the number, so the fix is a fixed procedure practised until it is automatic.

On the organic side, the loss is naming without the functional group. A question asking for the product of a reaction wants the compound identified in a way that shows the group formed, and a bare name or a partially drawn structure does not do it. Reaction conditions are separately credited and routinely omitted, which is a free mark discarded on nearly every organic question.

Then there is qualitative analysis, which is the cheapest set of marks in the subject and the most under-revised. The ion tests and their observations are examinable in detail — reagent, observation, conclusion — and they are pure recall. A student who learns the table properly picks up marks on every paper for a few hours of work, and almost nobody does it because it feels less important than the calculations.

The practice that works here is split: timed calculation sets with the procedure enforced, and a learned observation table tested cold. Those are different activities and mixing them into general revision is why neither gets done.

sections.heading: 0610 Biology and the vocabulary the scheme pays for
paragraphs: Biology is where students who revise hardest are most often disappointed, and the reason is linguistic rather than conceptual. The content volume is large but not difficult; the marks go to precise terms.

Extended-response items credit the mark scheme's own vocabulary. Active transport, partially permeable, selective reabsorption, limiting factor, antagonistic — each of these is the word the scheme lists, and a paraphrase that means the same thing to a biologist does not always earn the mark. Students who write fluent explanations in their own words consistently score below students who write shorter answers using the listed terms.

Command terms do the second layer of damage. Outline, describe, explain, distinguish and discuss expect different structures and mark counts, and a candidate who answers all five the same way settles around a C or a B regardless of knowledge. This is a technique problem, it is diagnosable from any marked paper in twenty minutes, and it responds to four to six sessions.

The third area is data interpretation on unfamiliar experiments. These questions are deliberately about something the student has not studied, which makes them feel unfair and makes them highly trainable: the skills are reading axes, identifying the controlled variables, describing a trend with figures quoted, and distinguishing a correlation from a cause. None of that requires content knowledge.

The practice is specific: extended-response questions rewritten using the scheme's terms, command-term sorting exercises, and a block of data questions from topics the student has not covered. Each of those is a different session, and a general revision hour does none of them.

sections.heading: English 0500: two papers, two different skills
paragraphs: English First Language is often left out of tutoring plans on the grounds that a fluent child does not need it. Fluent children sit at grade C in this subject regularly, and the reason is that neither paper rewards fluency on its own.

The reading paper wants quotation plus explanation of effect. A student who quotes without explaining has given the examiner half an answer; a student who explains without quoting has given an assertion. The directed-response task on the same paper is assessed on how well the student uses the source material rather than on how well they write, so inventing detail — however elegantly — loses marks.

The writing paper is marked on audience, register and form as well as content and accuracy. A letter that reads like an essay loses form marks. An article with no headline convention loses them too. These are learnable conventions and they are the reason a fluent writer can be stuck: nobody has told them that the form itself is credited.

Where the board matters: Pearson's 4EA1 carries a different anthology and different set material, so a student moving between schools cannot carry revision across. That is worth confirming before buying any literature-adjacent support, because the texts are not interchangeable even when the skills are.

The practice that moves this subject is short and unglamorous: three timed writing tasks in different forms, marked against the criteria with the form marks pointed out, and a block of reading questions where every answer is checked for the quotation-plus-explanation pattern.

sections.heading: The traps that appear in every subject
paragraphs: Beyond the subject-specific losses, four behaviours cost marks across every IGCSE paper a student sits, and fixing them once improves every subject at the same time. This is the highest-return tutoring available and it is rarely sold, because it does not look like a subject.

First, working not shown on multi-mark questions. Method marks exist and are awarded independently of the answer. A student who writes only answers is discarding marks in Mathematics, the sciences, Economics and Accounting simultaneously.

Second, the command term unread. Calculate, state, describe, explain, suggest, compare and evaluate expect different things, and the first word of the question is the instruction. Students who answer the topic rather than the instruction lose marks in every written subject.

Third, the instruction inside the question ignored — the required accuracy, the number of points asked for, the demand to use the data provided. "Give two reasons" scores two marks and a student offering one has left a mark on the table no matter how good the reason is.

Fourth, time collapsing in the final third of the paper. If marks drop sharply at the end of every paper, the problem is pacing, not knowledge, and no amount of content teaching touches it. The fix is full papers to time with a written pacing plan, and it is visible within three attempts.

All four are visible in a single marked paper and none of them requires subject knowledge to spot. That is why this is the work to do before hiring anybody: a parent who arrives with the four checked has already done the diagnosis that a tutor would otherwise charge two sessions to reach.

sections.heading: Past-paper work that actually changes a mark
paragraphs: Most families buy past-paper practice and most past-paper practice does nothing, because it is done in the way that feels productive rather than the way that works.

Three papers marked properly against the published scheme beat twenty papers skimmed. The marking is the active ingredient: a paper that is completed and then compared against answers teaches the student which questions they got wrong. A paper marked against the scheme teaches them where the marks were available and why they did not get them, which is a different and far more useful lesson.

The deliverable from the process is not a score. It is a one-page error log, kept across papers rather than per session, written in the student's own words. "Careless mistakes" is useless. "I write the answer without working on anything worth three or more marks" is actionable the next morning and checkable on the next paper.

Self-marking is the skill to teach early, because it makes practice between sessions count. A student who can mark their own work against a scheme converts every spare hour into useful hours; a student who cannot needs a tutor present for practice to mean anything, which is an expensive way to live.

On sourcing: syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are available free through your school and the boards' own channels. The legitimate approach is working through official material in session with the source named. A tutoring service hosting a download library of board material is distributing someone else's copyright, and for unreleased material the exposure is considerably worse.

sections.heading: Al Zahia logistics, the permit and the regulator
paragraphs: The practical and the regulatory, both briefly, because neither changes what is taught but both change what you should agree before starting.

Timing first. Al Zahia sits immediately west of the main Muwaileh campuses, and the routes in feed the Maliha Road corridor at the hour several large schools release. A household twenty minutes away by map is thirty-five minutes away at 2.45pm, and with children at two schools it is rarely settled before 5.15pm. Half past five is the earliest honest start and six o'clock the reliable one, with later slots better suited to technique work than to new content.

Cost next. Market rates for a qualified IGCSE tutor online run AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to AED 500 with travel inside the figure, Bestimate's Dubai table placing the usual range at AED 180 to AED 350. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

Regulation. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Private tutoring is separately regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school and government-sector teachers, private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published.

And the disclosure: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed by or partnered with SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE. In-home tutoring is an India-only service; Al Zahia students are taught over live video.

faqs.question: Which Mathematics papers does my child sit at Extended tier?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge 0580, Extended candidates take a short-answer paper and a structured paper. The short-answer paper rewards accuracy and speed across many topics; the structured paper carries the long multi-mark questions and is where the grade is decided, because method marks are awarded there independently of the final answer. On Pearson 4MA1 Higher there are two papers of equal weight, which means time lost on the first cannot be made up on the second. Confirm which board applies with your exams officer.

faqs.question: Do method marks really matter if the answer is right?
faqs.answer: Because method marks are awarded separately from the answer. On a four-mark structured question, a clear method with an arithmetic slip at the end can score three; the right answer with no working shown typically scores one. Students who believe only the answer is marked discard marks in Mathematics, the sciences, Economics and Accounting at the same time. It is a habit rather than a knowledge gap, and two to four sessions of annotating mark schemes usually fixes it.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and does it change how we revise?
faqs.answer: It changes about half the science revision plan. A Cambridge centre assesses practical work either through a timetabled practical test or through an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the skills differ: one needs apparatus handling, repeat readings and observation recording, the other needs interpreting someone else's method, spotting the variable that was not controlled and explaining an anomaly rather than describing it. Ask your head of science which route the centre uses before buying any science tutoring.

faqs.question: Does a tutor come to our home in Al Zahia?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits in Sharjah or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and there is no UAE office or centre. Al Zahia students are taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and the published mark scheme open on a shared screen. For this kind of component-level work that format is arguably better suited anyway, because both documents are visible to tutor and student at once.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE Chemistry marks are the easiest to recover?
faqs.answer: Qualitative analysis, almost always. The ion tests and their observations — reagent, observation, conclusion — are examinable in detail on Cambridge 0620 and are pure recall, so a student who learns the table properly picks up marks on every paper for a few hours of work. Almost nobody revises it because it feels less important than mole calculations. The second-cheapest set is reaction conditions in organic questions, which are separately credited and routinely left out entirely.

faqs.question: My child writes good explanations in Biology but scores in the middle. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually because the mark scheme credits its own vocabulary and a good paraphrase does not always earn the mark. Active transport, partially permeable, selective reabsorption and limiting factor are the listed terms, and shorter answers using them routinely outscore fluent answers that avoid them. The second cause is command terms: outline, describe, explain, distinguish and discuss expect different structures, and a candidate who answers all five identically plateaus whatever they know.

faqs.question: What loses marks most often in IGCSE Physics?
faqs.answer: Electricity first, specifically potential dividers read as plain series circuits with one current applied to the whole arrangement. Electromagnetic induction second, where the scheme wants a changing magnetic flux named as the cause and answers that only describe the wire moving score below the top band. Third, graph questions answered with a numerical value where the mark is for the physical quantity the gradient or area represents. All three are narrow, diagnosable and responsive to targeted question sets.

faqs.question: How many past papers should my child work through?
faqs.answer: Fewer than you think, done properly. Three papers marked against the published scheme beat twenty completed and skimmed, because the marking is the active ingredient — it shows where marks were available and why they were missed, rather than which answers were wrong. The output should be a one-page error log, kept across papers, in the student's own words. "Careless mistakes" is useless; "I give one reason when two are asked for" is actionable the next morning.

faqs.question: Why does it matter whether the school enters Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: Because the practice archive, the tiering language and the paper structure all differ. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended with a heavily weighted structured paper; Pearson 4MA1 is Foundation and Higher with two papers of equal weight. Cambridge science centres choose between a practical test and an alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson concentrates most routes into written papers. English set texts and anthologies differ entirely. A term on the wrong board's papers teaches question shapes that will not appear.

faqs.question: Is English First Language worth tutoring for a fluent child?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because neither paper rewards fluency by itself. The reading paper credits quotation together with explanation of effect, so quoting alone or asserting alone each lose half the answer. The writing paper is marked on audience, register and form as well as content, which is why a letter written as an essay loses form marks regardless of quality. Three timed tasks in different forms, marked against the criteria with the form marks pointed out, usually moves a stuck grade.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's problem is content or pacing?
faqs.answer: Look at where in the paper the marks disappear. If losses are spread evenly with blank spaces, that is content not reached or not known. If marks fall away sharply in the final third of every paper while the opening sections score, that is pacing, and no amount of content teaching will touch it. Pacing is fixed with full papers sat to time and a written plan for minutes per mark, and the improvement is usually visible within three attempts.

faqs.question: Can a tutor teach Additional Mathematics 0606 as part of 0580 sessions?
faqs.answer: It should not be treated that way. 0606 is a separate Extended-only syllabus introducing differentiation, integration, logarithms, the factor theorem and trigonometric identities that 0580 never reaches, with its own question shapes. Treating it as harder 0580 revision is the standard mistake. Students who struggle with it usually have an algebra weakness underneath rather than a calculus one, which is worth diagnosing first. The tutor pool for it is thin across the emirate, so book early.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give us the mark schemes to work from at home?
faqs.answer: They should point you to the official source rather than host copies. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are available free through your school and the boards' own channels, which is also why there is no reason for a tutoring service to be distributing them. The legitimate approach is working through official material in session with the source named so a family can find it again themselves.

faqs.question: What time can IGCSE sessions start from Al Zahia?
faqs.answer: Half past five at the earliest and six o'clock reliably. Al Zahia sits immediately west of the main Muwaileh campuses, but the routes in feed the Maliha Road corridor exactly when several large schools release, so a twenty-minute journey by map takes thirty-five at 2.45pm, and households with two school runs are rarely settled before 5.15pm. Later slots are better used for technique and timed practice, which need less fresh energy than new content does.

intro.heading: What the comparison actually turns up
paragraphs: Families in Aljada run this comparison constantly, because the community is new enough that nothing is settled by local habit. Is tutoring easier to arrange in Al Zahia? Are the Muwaileh families getting something we are not? Is the group class in the next development worth the drive? These are sensible questions and they deserve a direct answer rather than a page that pretends every neighbourhood is special.

Three things genuinely differ across these communities. The first is what a home visit costs to execute: a villa in Al Zahia with gate security and a driveway is a simpler visit than an apartment block, and a tutor's travel time from the city into Aljada or out to Tilal City is longer than a hop within Muwaileh. The second is group provision, which clusters around established schools and leisure centres and is genuinely thinner where a community is still being built. The third is session timing, because dismissal congestion and distance from the Muwaileh campuses set when a household is actually settled.

One thing does not differ. The supply of people who can teach Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, or mark a 0478 pseudocode trace table the way the syllabus does, or coach Economics diagram technique at Extended tier, is the same small number whether you search from Aljada, Al Zahia or Muwaileh. That supply is set by how many people have ever taught those specific syllabuses in this emirate, and moving house does not change it.

This matters because the natural response to a thin search result is to widen the radius. Widening the radius in inland Sharjah adds commute and adds content tutors — University City's undergraduate supply is real, and published budget rates of AED 33 to AED 150 an hour reflect it — while adding almost no specialists. It is the wrong lever.

There is a second reason the answer converges. IGCSE content and assessment are set by Cambridge and Pearson, not by the emirate or the community. Your child sits the same 0625 paper as a candidate in Al Zahia, marked by the same scheme. Nothing about the street changes what has to be taught, which is why a tutor should be chosen on the code rather than on the drive.

So this page compares the things that really vary, prices them, and then spends its length on the parts of IGCSE a parent can act on: establishing the code and tier, reading a marked paper yourself, the entry and resit decisions, and the subject-availability question including the private-candidate route when a school does not offer something.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. In-home tutoring is offered only in India, and there is no UAE office or centre. Aljada students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper on a shared screen.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years ending in terminal written papers, with tiered entry in several subjects: Core caps the grade at C, Extended reaches A*. programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to Sharjah candidates. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, says it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes beginning with 4 — 4MA1 Mathematics Specification A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Mathematics Specification A is tiered Foundation and Higher, with two papers of equal weight, so a pacing error on the first paper cannot be made up on a shorter second one. Grades are reported 9 to 1 rather than A* to G, which trips up parents comparing reports across boards.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, ending in Checkpoint tests schools use for setting. A result that places a student in Core rather than Extended Mathematics sets the grade ceiling two years before the exam. In a community where families arrive mid-course from other systems, this placement is often made on limited evidence and is worth questioning early with marked work rather than opinion.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving into a new Sharjah community frequently transfer schools and systems at the same time, and a tier placement made in the first term after a transfer carries the least evidence behind it. Ask the school what marked work would support a change, produce it, and have the conversation in Year 9 or early Year 10 while the entry has not yet been made.

programmes.name: AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: Where most Sharjah IGCSE students go next, and the reason a Year 11 grade matters beyond itself. Subject entry usually assumes an A or B at Extended, and the step up in mathematics and the sciences is steep because A Level assumes algebraic fluency IGCSE only samples. Tutoring aimed at that progression targets the specific topics AS builds on rather than the pass mark.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor states six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-aljada.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects families in these communities request most, with the specific place marks go. Use any line as an interview question — a tutor who knows the code can expand it without notes.

subjects.name: Mathematics — 0580 / 4MA1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended Paper 4 decides most grades through structured multi-mark questions on functions, transformations, vectors and probability. Working unshown on a four-mark item typically scores one. Pearson splits marks evenly across two papers, making pacing errors unrecoverable.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics — 0606
subjects.description: Calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities that 0580 never reaches, taken alongside it by students heading for A Level Maths. Reading it as harder 0580 revision is the standard error, and the tutor pool for it is thin across the whole emirate.

subjects.name: Physics — 0625 / 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism take most lost marks, usually when a potential divider is read as a plain series circuit. Six-mark items reward structured reasoning rather than recall, and the centre's practical route decides half the revision plan.

subjects.name: Chemistry — 0620 / 4CH1
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic and organic pathways carry the grade. Units dropped mid-titration cost marks and a product named without its functional group scores nothing. Cambridge examines qualitative analysis tables in detail and those are the cheapest marks on the paper.

subjects.name: Biology — 0610 / 4BI1
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty. Extended-response marks go to candidates using mark-scheme vocabulary — active transport, partially permeable, selective reabsorption — rather than paraphrase. Data questions on unfamiliar experiments separate the strong candidates.

subjects.name: English First Language — 0500 / 0990 / 4EA1
subjects.description: Directed writing is marked on audience, register and form as well as content, so fluent generic prose sits at C. Reading questions need quotation plus explanation. Set texts and anthologies differ by board, so revision does not transfer across a school move.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language — 0510 / 0511
subjects.description: Common across Sharjah schools. The reading-and-writing paper rewards precise information transfer, and copying whole sentences into a note-taking grid loses marks. Speaking is separately assessed and usually the least prepared component.

subjects.name: Business Studies — 0450 / 4BS1
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole paper: a correct definition with no reference to the named business sits in the bottom band. Evaluation questions carry the top marks and need a judgement with a reason — the most trainable skill in the syllabus.

subjects.name: Economics — 0455 / 4EC1
subjects.description: Diagram marks are awarded separately for axis labels, shift direction and the new equilibrium, so a remembered sketch loses three marks before the explanation starts. Gulf-context data questions appear regularly, which makes local examples useful revision.

subjects.name: Computer Science — 0478 / 4CP0
subjects.description: Pseudocode is marked against the syllabus's own conventions rather than Python, which costs marks on every trace table. Theory on data representation and networks is learnable and chronically under-revised while students spend their time coding.

subjects.name: Accounting — 0452 / 4AC1
subjects.description: Format marks are free and routinely discarded: a balanced trial balance with the wrong headings loses presentation marks. Accruals, prepayments and depreciation adjustments are the recurring failure, and the fix is full timed questions rather than topic revision.

sections.heading: What a home visit costs in a villa, an apartment and a new development
paragraphs: This is the first of the three real differences, and it is worth pricing rather than describing. The in-home premium is a tutor's travel time converted into an hourly rate, and travel time is a function of distance plus the friction at the other end.

In Al Zahia, a villa or townhouse with gate security and a driveway is the cheapest friction available: the tutor arrives, is let through, and parks. In an apartment district, the same visit adds visitor parking that may be full, a security desk and a lift. In Aljada or Tilal City, the friction is lower but the distance is greater, because most tutors are coming from the established parts of the emirate.

The market numbers reflect all of it. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, Bestimate's Dubai rate table placing the usual range at AED 180 to AED 350, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor working online. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Across a twelve-week term at one subject, the premium is roughly AED 1,500 to AED 2,000 — close to the full cost of a second subject taught online. And the erosion is not only financial: a session that starts twenty minutes late either runs short or pushes the rest of the evening back, which in an exam year is the scarcest thing in the house.

For completeness, IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; in-home tutoring is an India-only service. The comparison is here because it is the comparison parents are running, and it deserves real numbers rather than a dismissal.

sections.heading: Group classes: the one option that really does depend on where you live
paragraphs: Group tuition is the genuine exception to this page's argument. Unlike specialist one-to-one supply, group provision is physical: it needs a room, a timetable and enough students within a short drive to fill it. That clusters around established schools and commercial districts, and it is thinner where a community is still being built.

In practice that means a Muwaileh family has walkable or short-drive options, an Al Zahia family has a drive, and an Aljada or Tilal City family is often looking at a journey that turns a 90-minute class into a three-hour evening commitment. That journey is a second school run, in the evening, on the roads the first one used.

Group tuition is also genuinely cheaper, at AED 90 to AED 180 per student per hour in this market against AED 150 to AED 300 one-to-one, and genuinely effective for a particular job: broad revision across a syllabus for students who are roughly together in ability, board and tier.

Where it fails is individual misconceptions, because the group moves at the syllabus's pace rather than the student's. If your child's problem is that they do not show working on multi-mark questions, a group will not catch it. And mixing tiers wastes one student's hour entirely, because Core and Extended questions diverge sharply by the second half of the course.

Online small groups remove the geography from this trade-off, which is the useful part for a family in a newer community: two or three students at the same school, board and tier can share a tutor and a rate without anyone driving. The condition is the match — same code, same tier, no exceptions worth making.

sections.heading: How to read your child's marked paper without knowing the subject
paragraphs: This is the most useful skill a parent in any of these communities can acquire, and it takes twenty minutes. It is also the thing that makes every subsequent conversation with a tutor shorter and cheaper.

Take the marked paper and ignore the total. Go to each place where a mark was lost and note the first word of the question: calculate, describe, explain, state, suggest, compare, evaluate. Then note whether the student wrote something and got it wrong, or wrote nothing, or wrote an answer with no working.

Patterns appear quickly and they point at different problems. Losses clustered on explain and suggest while calculate and state scored means the content is present and the command terms are not being answered — a technique problem, four to six sessions. Losses spread evenly with blank spaces means content gaps, which is what a cheaper content tutor is genuinely good for. Correct final answers with no working on multi-mark questions means method marks are being thrown away, which is a habit, not a knowledge gap.

One more pass: look for repeated topics. Three losses in electricity on a 0625 paper is a topic problem. One loss each across six topics is not. This single distinction changes whether you should be buying topic teaching or paper technique, and it is the distinction most tutoring arrangements get wrong at the start.

Bring that reading to the first conversation. A tutor who agrees with your diagnosis and adds detail to it is worth hiring. A tutor who replies that your child needs more practice and more confidence has not looked at the paper.

sections.heading: Entry, tier and the November resit decision
paragraphs: Three decisions in the IGCSE year are made by adults rather than by revision, and all three are easier to get right with notice. They are tier of entry, the subjects entered at all, and whether to resit.

Tier is the largest. Cambridge Core entry caps the grade at C, which clears the Ministry of Education equivalency floor of grade E or 3 on the British track but usually falls short of what AS and A Level courses expect in mathematics and the sciences. The entry is made months before the papers, so a tier conversation has to happen before that deadline, supported by marked work at the higher standard rather than by a request.

Subject entry matters where a school does not offer something a student needs. Equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five, so a student short of five accredited subjects has a real problem to solve rather than a preference. In that situation the private-candidate route exists, through a centre that accepts external entries, and the school's exams officer is the person who can explain what it involves.

The resit decision arrives suddenly. A June grade that misses an AS requirement has a November route, but the entry window is short — days rather than weeks after results. Families who have already asked the exams officer what a resit entry involves make that call calmly; families who have not spend results week guessing while the deadline moves.

All three conversations are with the school, not with a tutor. What a tutor contributes is the marked evidence that makes the tier conversation possible, and the plan that makes a resit worth entering.
