sections.heading: Subject availability, and what happens when a school does not offer one
paragraphs: Availability has two faces in a community like this. One is tutor availability, which is emirate-wide and thin for specific syllabuses. The other is school availability — whether your child's school teaches the subject at all — and that genuinely does vary between campuses.

Smaller schools and newer ones run narrower IGCSE offers. Additional Mathematics 0606, Accounting 0452, Computer Science 0478 and Economics 0455 are the usual casualties, because each needs a specialist teacher and a viable class size. A student who needs one of those for a university route may find it is not on the school's list.

There are three routes from there and only one of them is quick. The school may add the subject if enough students want it, which is a multi-term conversation. The student may sit it as a private candidate through a centre that accepts external entries, which the exams officer can explain and which requires the teaching to be arranged separately. Or the student plans around the gap, which is sometimes the right answer and should be a decision rather than a default.

Tutor availability for those same subjects is the thin part of this market. Cambridge 0606, 0478 taught to the syllabus's own pseudocode conventions, 0452, and IGCSE Arabic as a first language are narrow pools anywhere in the emirate, and in the eight weeks before a series almost every specialist slot is taken.

When a match is not available at the hour you need, the honest options are a different slot with the right specialist, that specialist over live video from another time zone, or a plain statement that it is not available this term. A general science tutor in front of an 0606 candidate is not a match, whatever it is called on the invoice.

sections.heading: Past papers, mark schemes and what a tutor may hand over
paragraphs: Past-paper work is the centre of effective IGCSE tutoring and the place where a careless provider creates a real problem for themselves and for you.

Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge and Pearson. They are available free through your school and through the boards' own channels. The legitimate approach is to work through official material in session with the source named, so a family can find it again. A tutoring service hosting a download library of board material is distributing someone else's copyright, and for unreleased material the exposure is worse than copyright.

The useful version of past-paper work is narrower than most families expect. Three papers marked against the published scheme, with a one-page error log naming the recurring loss, beats twenty papers skimmed. The log is the deliverable, and it should be in the student's own words — "I write the answer without working on anything worth three or more marks" is actionable the next morning; "careless mistakes" is not.

On coursework, where a centre runs a component with one: a tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria and gives feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor does not write it, complete it or supply model text. One operator in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright at a published price, and the consequence of using that falls on the candidate rather than the seller.
A practical safeguard for either system: ask for feedback as spoken comments or margin notes rather than as edits inside the document. It removes the ambiguity entirely and it costs nothing.

sections.heading: SPEA, the permit and the mandatory subjects
paragraphs: Three pieces of local context a parent in Aljada should have, none of which any competitor page in this market supplies.

First, the regulator. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate, and its remit extends past inspection: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is why a school's subject offer in this emirate can differ from a Dubai school's a short drive away.

Second, the permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so treat a quoted figure as unverified. Because it is free, there is no innocent reason for a working tutor to be without it.

Third, the mandatory subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools. KHDA's guidelines require separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibit combined classes because expectations and the language of instruction differ, so material for one stream does not serve the other. Substituting content for these subjects without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited.

And the disclosure this page owes: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed by or partnered with SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Students we support attend schools across these communities; that is the extent of the relationship.

sections.heading: Starting from Aljada
paragraphs: Four steps, in this order, and the first two are free.

Email the school's exams officer for the board, the syllabus code, the tier and — for science — the practical route, plus the centre's own exam timetable. Then read the last marked paper using the method in this page: command terms on the lost marks, blank spaces against wrong answers, repeated topics against scattered ones. Those two pieces of work together tell you what you are buying before you talk to anybody.

Then take a free trial session over live video, at a time that survives an inland Sharjah evening — 5.30pm or later from Aljada, 6pm with children at two schools. Judge the session on whether the tutor agreed with or improved on your reading of the paper and said specifically what the next four sessions would cover.

Then agree a bounded block with a written target and a review date. Market monthly packages start around AED 799 for eight online sessions; agree what the block is meant to fix before the first invoice rather than after the third. Six weeks later, read the next marked paper for the same loss.

And agree in advance what happens if the match is wrong, because mismatches are common and say nothing about either the student or the tutor. An arrangement that changes the tutor without argument is worth more than a slightly cheaper rate.

One last practical point for a household that has recently moved in. If the school change and the tutoring enquiry are happening in the same term, keep them separate in your own mind. A worse report after a transfer is often unfamiliarity with a new board's question style rather than a learning problem, and the two need different responses.

faqs.question: Would we get better IGCSE tutoring if we lived in Muwaileh instead of Aljada?
faqs.answer: For group classes and for content help, marginally — provision clusters around established schools and University City's undergraduate supply is real, which is why published budget rates of AED 33 to AED 150 an hour are achievable there. For specialist syllabus teaching, no. The pool of people who can teach Additional Mathematics 0606 or mark 0478 pseudocode the way the syllabus does is the same small number across the whole emirate, and moving house does not change it.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor come to our apartment or villa in Aljada?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Sharjah or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we provide only in India, and there is no UAE office or centre. Aljada students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper on a shared screen. In a community still filling, the practical benefit is that the tutoring does not depend on local supply arriving first.

faqs.question: Is a group IGCSE class worth the drive from Aljada?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the maths is worth doing honestly. Group tuition runs AED 90 to AED 180 per student per hour against AED 150 to AED 300 one-to-one, so the saving is real. Against it, the journey turns a 90-minute class into a three-hour evening commitment and amounts to a second school run on the same roads. Groups are good at broad revision and poor at individual misconceptions, so the saving is only a saving if broad revision is what your child needs.

faqs.question: Can my child share a tutor with a friend to cut the cost?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one firm condition: the same board, the same syllabus code and the same tier. Two students at Core and Extended cannot share an hour usefully, because the questions diverge sharply in the second half of the course and one of the pair spends the time watching. Where the match holds, an online small group of two to four at AED 90 to AED 180 each is genuinely good value, and nobody has to drive anywhere for it.

faqs.question: How do I read my child's marked IGCSE paper if I never studied the subject?
faqs.answer: Ignore the total and look at where marks went. Note the first word of each question that lost marks — calculate, describe, explain, suggest, evaluate — and whether the space was blank, wrong, or right with no working shown. Blank spaces point at content gaps; wrong answers point at understanding; correct answers without working point at a habit throwing away method marks. Then check whether losses cluster in one topic or scatter across many. That distinction decides what to buy.

faqs.question: What happens if my child's school does not offer a subject they need?
faqs.answer: There are three routes and only one is quick. The school may add it if enough students want it, which is a multi-term conversation. The student may sit it as a private candidate through a centre that accepts external entries, with the teaching arranged separately — your exams officer can explain what that involves. Or you plan around the gap, which is sometimes right but should be a decision rather than a default. Additional Mathematics, Accounting, Computer Science and Economics are the usual casualties.

faqs.question: How many accredited IGCSE subjects does my child need for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five, on the British track: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five. Alongside those, equivalency asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor page states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. Verify your own case with the Ministry, since this is a process to describe rather than one a tutoring service performs.

faqs.question: When is the deadline to decide on a November resit?
faqs.answer: Days after August results rather than weeks, which is why the decision should be researched before results day. A June grade that misses an AS or university requirement has a November route — Cambridge runs June and November series and the February/March series is India-only, so November is the Sharjah resit option. Ask your exams officer in advance what a resit entry involves at your centre. Families who do that make the call calmly; families who do not spend results week guessing.

faqs.question: Does a Core tier entry cause a problem later?
faqs.answer: It caps the Cambridge grade at C. That clears the Ministry of Education equivalency floor of grade E or 3, so it does not block a UAE university application by itself, but it usually falls short of what AS and A Level courses expect in mathematics and the sciences, where an A or B at Extended is the normal ask. If the entry has not yet been made, a tier conversation supported by marked work at the higher standard is worth having with the school in Year 9 or early Year 10.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give us the mark schemes and past papers to keep at home?
faqs.answer: They should not host a library of them. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are Cambridge's and Pearson's copyright and are available free through your school and the boards' own channels. The legitimate approach is working through official material in session with the source named so you can find it yourself. A service distributing board material is handling someone else's copyright, and for unreleased material the exposure is considerably worse.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge timetable applies to a Sharjah candidate?
faqs.answer: Only the one your centre issues. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. A tutor quoting dates from a generic download may be working from a document that does not apply to your child. Sharjah candidates sit the June and November series; February/March is India-only.

faqs.question: Is a tutor in Sharjah required to hold a permit, and can I check?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you can simply ask. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school and government-sector teachers, private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts is published, so treat quoted figures as unverified.

faqs.question: What does SPEA mean for my child's subject choices?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and its remit is wider than inspection: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is part of why a Sharjah school's IGCSE offer can differ from a Dubai school's a short drive away, and why a subject list has to be read in the emirate's own context. IB Gram is not approved, licensed or endorsed by SPEA or any other UAE regulator.

faqs.question: What should I do if the tutor turns out to be the wrong match?
faqs.answer: Change them, early, and agree before you start that this is how it works. A mismatch between a student and a teacher is common and says nothing about either of them, and an arrangement that treats a change as a complaint is one you will stay with too long. Practically: name the loss in writing before the block begins, review the next marked paper after four to six sessions, and if that specific loss has not shifted, change the plan or the person.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-aljada.closingHeading: Compare the real differences, then get the code
sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-aljada.closingBody: If you are comparing an IGCSE home tutor in Aljada against the same search in Al Zahia, Muwaileh or Tilal City, the honest summary is that home-visit costs, group options and session times differ while specialist supply does not. So start with the things you control. Email the exams officer for the board, code, tier and practical route, read the last marked paper using the method on this page, and take a free trial over live video at a time that survives an inland Sharjah evening.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-kalba.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE courses to Year 10 and Year 11 students, including the Extended tier and the Alternative to Practical papers. Each one works to your child's own school scheme of work and the dated entry deadlines their exams officer is holding.

intro.heading: Start with the date, not the tutor
paragraphs: An IGCSE course is a two-year run at a fixed set of papers, and almost every decision a Kalba family makes about tutoring is really a decision about timing. A Year 10 student in October has roughly twenty teaching months left. A Year 11 student in the same month has eight or nine, minus a mock fortnight, minus the Eid and winter breaks, minus the fortnight around Ramadan when nobody revises well. Counting those weeks honestly usually changes the plan more than choosing a different tutor would.

Cambridge International runs its IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in a May/June window and in November. Those four points are the structure your child's year hangs from, and they are what a tutor should be planning against. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers themselves, because a school has to submit candidate data, order components and allocate an exam room before anything is printed. The deadline your child's exams officer is working to, not the exam date, is the one that constrains you.

Kalba adds a geographical fact to the calendar. The town sits on the Gulf of Oman, south of Khor Fakkan, and the drive over the Hajar mountains to Sharjah city takes well over an hour in normal traffic. Families who want a subject specialist who genuinely knows the 0620 organic chemistry papers face a choice that has nothing to do with money: either accept whoever happens to live within a short drive, or stop treating distance as a constraint at all. Live online lessons remove the drive, which is the reason most of our east-coast families chose them.

To be plain about what is being offered: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India. Every Kalba lesson runs over live video with a shared whiteboard, a past paper on screen and a recording your child can rewatch. The phrase "home tutor" is what parents type into Google, so it is the phrase this page uses, but it would be dishonest to let it imply a doorbell.

What follows is the year counted backwards. The exam calendar with its real milestones, an eight-week plan with the evidence each block should produce, the AED rates the east-coast market actually charges, the marks Kalba students most often lose, and what a tutor is permitted to do with coursework. Read the calendar section first if you only read one.

One more thing worth settling early: tutoring is not a regulatory requirement. Nobody needs a tutor to sit a Cambridge paper, to attest a certificate, or to apply to a UAE university. It buys teaching time on specific weaknesses, and that is all it buys.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-kalba.programmesIntro: Kalba students sit one of a small number of British-track qualifications, and the entry route differs between them. The four below cover almost every case we see on the east coast, with the scheduling consequence of each spelled out.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE (Core and Extended)
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE courses are examined in a June series and a November series. Most subjects are tiered: a Core paper set caps the grade at C, an Extended set reaches A*. The tier is chosen by the school on the entry form, which means a tier decision is really a deadline decision. Coursework components exist in some subjects and are marked internally against published criteria before external moderation.
programmes.countryNote: Kalba students are almost always entered through their own school as internal candidates, so the dates that matter are the ones the school's exams officer holds rather than anything published for private candidates. Ask for the final entry date in writing at the start of the term, then plan the tutoring blocks backwards from it.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE suite is examined in a May/June window and in November. Several subjects are modular in effect, with separate paper codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics A and 4PH1 for Physics, and results carry forward differently from Cambridge. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which is a useful illustration of how long a November series actually lasts.
programmes.countryNote: The practical difference for a Kalba family is the resit rhythm. A student who misses a grade in the May/June window can re-sit in November without waiting a full year, so a disappointing June result is not a lost year. Check the live Pearson timetable before assuming a particular paper is available in both windows.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Some schools still enter candidates for Cambridge O Level in particular subjects, usually where a coursework-free route suits the cohort. O Level is examined in the same June and November series as IGCSE and uses overlapping subject content, but the paper structures and grade descriptors are not identical and past papers are not interchangeable between the two.
programmes.countryNote: If your child's timetable mixes IGCSE and O Level subjects, say so before the first lesson. Working a student through an IGCSE past paper for an O Level entry wastes the session, and on the east coast a wasted session is harder to replace than it sounds.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson AS and A Level
programmes.description: The sixth-form route most Kalba IGCSE students move into. AS and A Level examinations also fall in June and November series, and the step up in algebraic fluency between IGCSE Extended Mathematics and AS Pure Mathematics is the single most common reason a Year 12 student asks for help in their first term.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-kalba.subjectsIntro: These are the Cambridge and Pearson subjects Kalba families ask about most, with the syllabus code and the specific place marks go missing. A tutor who cannot name the paper your child is weak on is guessing.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two written papers, no coursework. Extended candidates lose most marks on the non-calculator algebra, on compound-interest and reverse-percentage problems, and on the three-mark questions that ask for a reason rather than a number. Working shown badly costs method marks even when the answer is right.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Year 11 cohorts as a bridge to AS Mathematics. Calculus arrives early and the differentiation questions assume fluent surd and index manipulation. Students who coped with 0580 by pattern-matching usually stall here, and that stall is diagnosable in one session with a past paper.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and the moments questions are where Extended candidates leak marks, along with any question asking for an experimental method. Paper 6, the Alternative to Practical, rewards precise apparatus description and sensible precautions, and it is almost always under-practised relative to the theory papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis half-equations and organic reaction conditions account for most lost Extended marks. The command terms matter: a question that says state wants a word, one that says explain wants a mechanism, and students who write a paragraph for a one-mark state question run out of time.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The content volume is the problem rather than the difficulty. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance diagrams are the reliable mark-losers, and data-response questions that ask a student to use the graph are answered from memory instead, which scores nothing.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653, 0654)
subjects.description: A single award covering biology, chemistry and physics content at reduced depth. Students entered here sometimes revise from single-science past papers and spend hours on material that is not on their syllabus. Checking the correct code at the first session routinely saves a fortnight.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the composition paper reward structure over vocabulary. Reading responses lose marks when a student summarises instead of selecting and commenting, and the time split between the two reading questions is a technique problem a tutor can fix quickly.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.description: Exercise by exercise, the reading paper is winnable with technique: note-making needs short precise points, the summary has a word ceiling, and the writing tasks are marked against a fixed register. Many east-coast students are stronger in spoken English than their paper marks suggest.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455, 0450)
subjects.description: Both subjects are won on the extended-response questions, where marks come from applying a concept to the stimulus case rather than defining it. Diagram accuracy in Economics, especially shifts versus movements along a curve, is the other reliable gap.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, and Arab and non-Arab groups are taught in separate classes under different expectations. Support here has to match the stream the school has placed the student in.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (Cambridge 0417)
subjects.description: Two practical papers plus theory. Marks disappear in the document production and data-handling tasks, where instructions are long and precise and a single unformatted field loses the mark. Timed practice on the real task files is the only approach that moves the grade.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Kalba can actually fix this term
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Kalba is, for almost every family who searches that phrase, a request for one specific thing: somebody who knows the papers their child is entered for and has time in the week to work on them. The honest answer is that IB Gram covers this as live one-to-one online tuition rather than a visit to your address, and that for a subject specialist on the east coast this is an advantage rather than a compromise. A Kalba family looking for a tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended chemistry to exam classes is choosing from a national pool online, and from a very short local list otherwise.

What tutoring fixes well inside a single term is technique and specific topic gaps. A student who understands moles but loses marks because they never write the unit, or who can balance equations but freezes on electrolysis half-equations, is a tractable problem: identify it from a marked paper, teach the method, drill it, re-test under timing. Eight weeks is enough for three or four gaps of that size, and the evidence shows up in paper marks rather than in reassurance.

What tutoring does not fix in a term is two years of absent foundations across every science, or a Year 11 student who has not opened a past paper by March. It also cannot change a tier decision after the entry has been submitted, which is why the entry deadline matters more than the exam date. If your child is sitting Core papers and aiming at a grade the Core tier cannot award, that is a conversation to have with the school in the first weeks of the course, not in the revision period.

Before any of that, settle what format you are buying. Lessons run over live video with a shared whiteboard, screen-shared past papers and a recording afterwards. Nobody travels to Kalba. If a provider in this market promises a visiting specialist on the east coast at a city rate, ask who exactly is driving over the mountains twice a week, and what that does to the hourly figure.

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes the calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what parents are actually trying to plan around. The table below walks the sequence in reverse from a results day back to the point where tutoring still changes the outcome. Treat the windows as the shape of the year and always confirm the specific dates against the live official timetable and your child's exams officer, because series timetables are revised and schools set their internal deadlines independently.

Two sourced reference points anchor the Pearson side. The November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the June window, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Cambridge publishes zone-specific timetables and warns that centres must use the version for their administrative zone, as it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper because the wrong zone timetable was used. That is worth checking rather than assuming.

The practical reading of the table for a Kalba family is this: the useful tutoring window closes long before the papers start. By the time the exam timetable is pinned to the kitchen wall, the decisions that mattered have been taken. Entry tier, subject count, coursework submission and mock performance are all upstream of the exam, and all of them are places where teaching time changes the result.

sections.heading: Eight weeks, planned: what the block has to produce
paragraphs: An eight-week block is the unit most Kalba families buy, usually once the mocks have come back. It works when it is planned as four blocks of two weeks with a piece of evidence at the end of each, and it fails when it becomes eight weeks of going over things. The difference is whether anything is marked.

Week one is diagnostic and it is not negotiable. The student sits a full past paper for the weakest subject under timed conditions, the tutor marks it against the published mark scheme, and the two of them read the mark scheme together. That one session usually reorders the entire plan, because the paper rarely shows what the family expected. A student assumed to be weak at trigonometry turns out to be losing eleven marks on units and rounding across the whole paper.

The middle four weeks are rebuild and technique, in that order. Rebuild means teaching the two or three topics the diagnostic exposed, properly, from the definition up, with practice questions grouped by topic rather than by paper. Technique means the transferable marks: reading command terms, showing method, allocating time by mark value, and answering the question that was asked. Technique is where the fastest gains sit for a student who already knows the content, and it is routinely skipped because it feels less like studying.

The last two weeks are whole papers at exam timing, marked and reviewed, with no new content introduced. If a topic is still broken at week seven, it stays broken: the marginal mark is cheaper elsewhere. Families find this hard, and it is the single most useful piece of discipline in the block.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs on the Sharjah east coast
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of those that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Kalba family transacts in. Here are the market bands in dirhams, attributed, so you can tell whether a quote you have been given is normal. These are market figures gathered from published provider pages and from the Bestimate Dubai tutoring rate table, not an IB Gram price list.

Read it from the bottom first. Budget online tuition, typically delivered by a university student, starts around AED 45 to 65 an hour on EdFlik's published rates and from roughly AED 33 to 52 on Tutopiya's. A qualified subject tutor online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Exam-board specialists run AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and a named premium tutor can reach AED 650, as BartyED's published rate does. The spread between the bottom and the top of that range is a factor of fourteen for a product described in almost identical words.

In-home visiting rates are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, and that gap over the online band is the travel premium. On the east coast it would be larger still, because an hour-plus mountain drive each way is unpaid working time somebody has to price in. Monthly packages seen in this market include online plans around AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home plans at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one hour a week run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Context helps. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are the fixed cost in a family budget; tutoring is the variable one, and it is the one worth timing. Two concentrated sessions a week for eight weeks before a series usually buys more than one session a week spread thinly across a year, at a similar total.

sections.heading: Online lessons against the Kalba drive to a tutor
paragraphs: This is the comparison that decides it for most east-coast families, and it is worth doing with the real distances rather than in the abstract. Kalba to Sharjah city is a mountain crossing of well over an hour each way. Kalba to Khor Fakkan is around half an hour. Fujairah city is closer than Sharjah city by road. Any plan involving a tutor travelling to a Kalba address has to absorb two of those journeys per session, and somebody pays for them either in money or in a smaller choice of tutor.

The tutor pool is the real variable. Within a short drive of Kalba, the number of people who have taught Cambridge 0580 Extended to exam classes and can mark a Paper 4 script against the scheme is small. Nationally, online, it is not small. For a single subject at Core tier the local option may well be adequate; for Extended physics or Additional Mathematics, the gap in available expertise is the whole argument.

Scheduling is the second variable. A 17:00 online session can start at 17:00. A visiting tutor arriving from Sharjah city after their own working day cannot realistically be at a Kalba address before 19:00, and a 19:00 start on a school night is a worse lesson regardless of who is teaching it. Recordings matter here too: an online session leaves a rewatchable artefact, and east-coast students use them on the school run.

To restate the position plainly, because it is the question behind the search: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at a Kalba address. Home tutoring as a service exists in this market, the rates above show what it costs, and families who want it will find it. What we offer instead is the same one-to-one teaching over live video, with a wider choice of specialist and no drive.

sections.heading: SPEA, the Sharjah school year and Ramadan scheduling
paragraphs: Private schools in Sharjah, including the east-coast towns, are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. SPEA regulates private education in the emirate and, as the federal portal records for both Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah, the emirate authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone, and it is worth understanding that your child's curriculum is approved locally even though the examination is set in Cambridge or London. Families in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain sit under the federal Ministry of Education instead, which matters if a move is on the cards.

The federal baseline for curriculum is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind the mandatory subjects every UAE private school teaches alongside its international programme, and it is why your child's week contains lessons that do not appear on any Cambridge timetable. Tutoring plans that ignore those periods tend to overestimate how much study time actually exists in a school day.

Ramadan is the scheduling fact nobody plans for and everybody is affected by. School days shorten, energy in the late afternoon drops, and revision quality in the hour before iftar is poor regardless of discipline. The workable answer on the east coast has been to move sessions to a post-iftar slot, keep them shorter, and shift the heavy diagnostic work to the weeks either side. A tutor who treats the month as a four-week gap in the plan is planning badly; a tutor who moves the slot keeps the momentum.

The two remaining calendar facts to hold are the school's own internal deadlines and the public holidays around Eid. Internal coursework and practical-component deadlines are set by the school within board rules, and they land months before the written papers. Ask for them in writing in the first fortnight of the course, put them in the same calendar as the entry deadline, and plan the tutoring blocks into the space that is left.

sections.heading: Where Kalba students lose IGCSE marks, paper by paper
paragraphs: Marks are lost in patterns, and the patterns repeat across cohorts to a degree that surprises parents. Four causes account for most of the gap between a predicted grade and an awarded one: misreading the command term, not showing method, running out of time on the back pages, and revising content that is not on the syllabus code the student is entered for. None of those is about intelligence and all of them are teachable.

Command terms first. A Cambridge question that says state wants a short factual answer and awards one mark. Describe wants what happens; explain wants why. Calculate wants working. Students who answer every question in a paragraph lose time on the one-mark questions and then have none left for the six-mark ones at the end. In Chemistry 0620 this shows up most sharply in the organic and electrolysis questions, where a mechanism is wanted and a definition is given.

Method marks are the second pattern, and they are pure arithmetic in the mark scheme. A Mathematics 0580 Extended Paper 4 question worth four marks typically awards three of them for method. A student who writes only the final answer and gets it wrong scores zero where a student who showed three lines of working and slipped at the end scores three. Working shown badly is the most expensive habit in the subject, and it takes about two sessions to change.

The third and fourth patterns are structural. Timing is fixable by practising at mark-per-minute pacing rather than by working faster. Revising the wrong syllabus is fixable in one conversation: confirm whether your child sits 0625 Physics or the Pearson 4PH1 equivalent, Core or Extended, Combined Science 0653 or the single sciences, and whether a practical or Alternative to Practical paper applies. Every year a student on the east coast arrives for a session having spent a fortnight on material their paper does not assess.
bullets: Command terms: state, describe, explain and calculate each want a different answer shape
Method marks usually outnumber answer marks in multi-mark questions
Pace by mark value, not by stopwatch, and leave the long questions readable

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: Some of what is sold in this market crosses a line that gets students disqualified. One provider in the competitor set openly offers completed Internal Assessments for a fee. Buying that work is malpractice under board rules, the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller, and it is not a service IB Gram will provide at any price. The boundary is worth stating precisely rather than gesturing at, because parents are rarely told where it sits.

A tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain the published assessment criteria, talk through a plan, give feedback on a draft the student wrote, and point out where an argument is unsupported or a method is unsound. A tutor may not draft the work, rewrite it, supply paragraphs, or edit it into something the student could not have produced. If a piece of coursework is internally assessed, the school also has its own supervision rules and submission records, and a sudden change in a student's written voice is precisely what those records exist to catch.

There is a related rule about materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the boards. We reference them and link to the official source rather than reproducing or distributing them, and a provider offering a drive full of papers and mark schemes is usually telling you something about how it treats rules in general.

The permit position is the last piece of the honesty picture. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so anybody quoting you a figure is guessing. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.
bullets: A tutor teaches, explains criteria, and gives feedback on the student's own draft
A tutor does not draft, rewrite or supply assessed work in any form
Board materials are linked to at source, never redistributed
The MoHRE private tuition permit is free and valid for two years

sections.heading: If no specialist is free for your subject and week
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider has availability limits and almost none of them say so. The honest version matters more on the east coast than in the city, because a Kalba family who is told to wait has fewer fallbacks. Here is how it actually goes. Common subjects at Core and Extended tier, in early-evening Gulf Standard Time slots, are usually matched quickly. Narrow combinations are slower: Additional Mathematics 0606, ICT practical coaching, Arabic as a first language, and anything needing a specific board variant at short notice.

When a specialist is not free for the slot you want, there are three honest options and we will say which applies. The first is a different slot with the right tutor, which is nearly always better than the right slot with the wrong one. The second is a short bridging block with a strong generalist to stabilise technique while the specialist frees up, declared as exactly that. The third is to tell you we cannot cover it well and to say so before you pay, which is rarer but does happen for unusual board variants late in a series.

The practical advice for a Kalba family is to book the diagnostic session early in the term rather than after the mocks. Demand concentrates in the weeks following mock results and in the month before a series, and the specialists with exam-class experience are the first to fill. A plan started in the quiet part of the term gets a better tutor at a better time for the same money, which is the least glamorous and most reliable advantage available in this market.

process.title: Tell us the series and the deadline
process.description: Start with the facts that constrain everything else: which board and syllabus codes, Core or Extended, which series your child is entered for, and the final entry date the school is working to. A screenshot of the subject list from the school portal is more useful than a long description of the problem.

process.title: Send one piece of marked work
process.description: A marked mock paper or a returned class test tells a tutor more in two minutes than a phone call does in twenty. It shows where marks were actually lost rather than where the student feels weak, and those two things disagree more often than they agree.

process.title: Free trial lesson, 45 minutes
process.description: One lesson at no charge, with the tutor who would continue, using your child's own material. No card details are taken beforehand. The point of the trial is to find out whether your child will talk to this particular adult about things they do not understand, which is most of what makes tutoring work.

process.title: Agree the block and its evidence
process.description: Before the second lesson, agree what the block is for, how many weeks it runs, and what marked evidence will exist at the end of it. An open-ended arrangement with no checkpoint is how families end up paying for months of going over things.

process.title: Review at the halfway point
process.description: Halfway through, look at the marked work rather than at the reports. If the diagnosed gaps have closed, continue. If they have not, change the tutor, the frequency or the plan. Changing a tutor at week four is a normal thing to do and costs nothing but a conversation.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is on the page
whyPoints.description: Every other provider in this cluster leaves parents to work out the entry deadlines and the results windows themselves. The milestones are set out above in reverse order, with the sourced Pearson dates named, so you can see where in the year you currently stand before you buy anything.

whyPoints.description: Kalba is not a Dubai neighbourhood with a different name. The drive over the mountains, the thin local supply of Extended-tier specialists and the later realistic start time for a visiting tutor all change the answer, and this page starts from those facts.

whyPoints.title: One tutor, one slot, recorded
whyPoints.description: The same tutor each week in the same slot, with lesson recordings your child can rewatch. Continuity does more for a Year 11 student than a rotating roster of better-qualified strangers, because the tutor remembers what was broken last month.

whyPoints.title: Honest about coursework limits
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains the published criteria and gives feedback on the student's own draft. Nobody here will write a piece of assessed work, and the reason is that the student carries the consequence when a board investigates, not the person who sold it.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: If no specialist covers your subject, tier and slot, we say so and name the alternatives rather than filling the hour with whoever is free. That is a slower sale and a better lesson, and on the east coast it is the difference between help and a placeholder.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our house in Kalba for IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every Kalba lesson runs live online, one to one, over video with a shared whiteboard and screen-shared past papers, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The search phrase is "home tutor" because that is what parents type, and the page uses it honestly rather than implying a doorbell. The practical trade is a wider choice of subject specialist and no mountain drive, against the loss of a person in the room.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam series do Kalba students actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two your child will be entered for. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in a May/June window and in November. The February and March series that circulates in some tutoring material is offered in India only and does not apply to a UAE candidate. Confirm the specific paper dates on the live official timetable, and ask your child's exams officer which administrative zone the school sits in, because Cambridge publishes zone-specific timetables.

faqs.question: How many weeks before a series should a Year 11 student in Kalba start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do. The term before the series is the useful window, because the first session should be a full diagnostic paper and the plan that follows needs four to six weeks of teaching before it turns into whole-paper practice. Eight weeks works. Three weeks buys technique and timing but not content repair. The other reason to start early is competition for tutors: demand concentrates after mock results, and the specialists with exam-class experience fill first.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tutoring cost for a family on the Sharjah east coast?
faqs.answer: The market in dirhams runs from roughly AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik's published budget online rate, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, to AED 200 to 450 and above for exam-board specialists, where TutorChase publishes AED 270. Visiting in-home rates are quoted at AED 180 to 500. Those are market figures from published provider pages, not an IB Gram price list. Ask for the free trial lesson and a quote for a defined block rather than an open-ended hourly arrangement.

faqs.question: Is the premium for a tutor who drives to the east coast worth paying?
faqs.answer: It buys a car journey, not better teaching. The gap between the AED 150 to 300 online band and the AED 180 to 500 in-home band is travel time somebody has to price in, and from Kalba that journey is well over an hour each way to Sharjah city. The second cost is invisible: a visiting tutor must live within range, so the pool shrinks to whoever is nearby and free. For Extended-tier sciences or Additional Mathematics, that constraint usually costs more in expertise than the money saves.

faqs.question: Which syllabus code is my child sitting, and why does it matter in Kalba?
faqs.answer: It matters because revision material is code-specific and the wrong material wastes weeks. Cambridge Physics is 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Mathematics 0580, Additional Mathematics 0606, Combined Science 0653. Pearson equivalents carry codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Core and Extended tiers sit different papers with different grade ceilings. Ask the school for the code and tier of every subject in writing at the start of the course. Students on the east coast arrive at sessions every year having revised a syllabus they are not entered for.

faqs.question: Can online lessons prepare a student for the Alternative to Practical paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that paper is usually the most neglected part of a science entry. It assesses experimental reasoning on paper: describing apparatus, identifying variables, naming precautions, reading scales, spotting the flaw in a method and suggesting an improvement. All of that is taught and drilled from past papers on a shared screen. What online lessons cannot replace is time handling equipment in a school laboratory, which your child's school provides. The two are complementary, and the paper marks come from the reasoning.

faqs.question: How should we handle tutoring through Ramadan on the east coast?
faqs.answer: Move the slot rather than pausing the plan. School days shorten, and the hour before iftar is poor study time no matter how disciplined the student is. Families here have had better results with a post-iftar session, kept shorter than the usual length, with heavy diagnostic work scheduled into the weeks either side of the month. Treating the month as a four-week hole in an eight-week plan is what causes the scramble afterwards. Agree the revised timing before the month starts, not during it.

faqs.question: Who regulates my child's school in Kalba, and does it affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: Private schools in Sharjah, including the east-coast towns, come under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate. For Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. If your child moves to a school in Fujairah, Ajman or Umm Al Quwain, federal Ministry of Education oversight applies instead. None of this changes how a Cambridge paper is marked, but it does affect fees, curriculum approval and the inspection reports you can read.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with internally assessed IGCSE coursework?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor may teach the underlying skills, explain the published assessment criteria, discuss a plan, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not draft the work, rewrite it or supply paragraphs. One provider in this market sells completed assessed work outright; buying it is malpractice and the student carries the consequence. Your child's school also keeps supervision records, and an abrupt change in written voice is exactly what those records exist to detect.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching a Kalba student from elsewhere in the UAE need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with suspicion. Applications go through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does a Kalba student need for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track the Ministry of Education requires a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. At least one ranking competitor page states six subjects, which is wrong. Verify the current requirement with the Ministry or your emirate's attestation authority before acting on it.

faqs.question: My child missed a grade in the June series. What happens next?
faqs.answer: A June result is not a lost year. Both boards run a November series, so a resit entry is usually possible in the same calendar year, and November results reach students the following January: November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. Before entering, get the component breakdown from the statement of results, because it shows which paper lost the grade. A student who dropped the grade on one practical-style paper needs a different eight weeks from one who was short across every component.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for my child's subject and slot?
faqs.answer: We say so before you pay. Common subjects in early-evening Gulf Standard Time slots are matched quickly; narrow combinations such as Additional Mathematics 0606, ICT practical coaching or Arabic as a first language take longer. The alternatives are a different slot with the right specialist, a short declared bridging block with a strong generalist while the specialist frees up, or an honest decline. Booking the diagnostic session early in the term rather than after mock results is the reliable way to avoid the question.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two or three subjects for a Kalba student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is usually worth resisting. A mathematics and physics pairing is common and genuinely held by many tutors. A three-science pairing at Extended tier is rarer than the adverts suggest, and the subject where the tutor is weakest is the one your child will quietly stop asking about. If the budget forces a choice, concentrate the hours on the subject where the marked evidence shows the largest gap rather than spreading one hour each across three.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-kalba.closingHeading: Start from the deadline your school is working to
sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-kalba.closingBody: If you are searching for an IGCSE home tutor in Kalba, the most useful thing you can do before booking anything is to get two dates in writing from your child's school: the final entry deadline and the internal deadline for any coursework or practical component. With those in hand, the plan writes itself backwards, and you will know whether you are buying an eight-week exam block or a term of rebuilding. Send the subject list, the syllabus codes and one piece of marked work, and we will tell you which of the two we think it is before the free trial lesson rather than after it.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-khor-fakkan.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE courses to Year 10 and Year 11 students, including tiered entries and the practical and alternative-to-practical components. Each names the board and code they have taught to examination classes rather than listing subjects.

intro.heading: Which board, which code, which tier
paragraphs: Almost every wasted hour of IGCSE tutoring traces back to one of three unanswered questions: which board, which syllabus code, which tier. A family in Khor Fakkan buys a popular revision guide, a tutor works through a past paper that looks right, and nobody notices for a month that the school entered the student for a different board with a different paper structure. This is not a rare mistake. It is the normal one.

The two boards that matter here are Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel. Cambridge runs its IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson's International GCSE runs in a May/June window and in November. The content overlaps heavily. The papers do not: numbers of components differ, the balance between structured and extended answers differs, and the code on the front of the paper is the only reliable guide to what will be asked.

Cambridge adds a wrinkle that catches schools rather than families. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. If your child's exams officer cannot tell you the zone, that is worth pursuing before anything else on this page.

Tiering is the third decision and the one with teeth. Many Cambridge subjects are entered at Core or Extended. A Core entry caps the grades available; an Extended entry opens the top of the scale and asks for more content. The tier goes on the entry form months before the examination, and a student entered at Core cannot reach a top grade however well they are taught. Settle it in writing with the school early, because no amount of tutoring works around it.

On delivery, the position is plain. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India. Khor Fakkan lessons are one to one over live video, with the past paper or marked script on a shared screen and a recording kept. "Home tutor" is the search phrase and this page uses it, but nobody is driving the coast road to your address.

What follows is the board comparison in detail, a code map for the subjects families here ask about, how private and school entries differ, what the resit route looks like, where the marks actually go, and what tutoring costs in dirhams on this coast. If you read only one part, read the tier section, because it is the decision that bounds everything a tutor can achieve for your child this year.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE: May/June window and November

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-khor-fakkan.programmesIntro: Four routes cover the Khor Fakkan enquiries we receive. Each is described by what the board does differently, because that difference is what a tutor has to work with.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Examined in a June series and a November series. Many subjects are tiered between Core and Extended, with separate paper sets and different grade ceilings. Science subjects carry either a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical written paper, decided by the centre. Syllabus codes are four digits and they are the reference point for everything: 0580, 0625, 0620, 0610, 0500, 0510, 0455, 0450, 0417, 0606.
programmes.countryNote: Khor Fakkan candidates are entered through their school, so the centre's administrative zone and the exams officer's deadline are the operative facts. Ask for the zone and the final entry date in writing in the first weeks of Year 10, then plan the teaching inside what those allow.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Examined in a May/June window and in November, with paper codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry and 4BI1 for Biology. Several subjects have a tiered or optional-paper structure of their own, and the extent to which a subject can be taken in parts differs from Cambridge. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.
programmes.countryNote: The resit rhythm is the practical difference for an east-coast family. A missed grade in the May/June window can be re-entered in November rather than a year later, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Check the live Pearson timetable before assuming a given paper runs in both windows.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Still entered by some schools in particular subjects, usually where a coursework-free route suits the cohort. Examined in the same June and November series as IGCSE with overlapping content, but the paper structures and grade descriptors differ and past papers are not interchangeable between the two qualifications.
programmes.countryNote: If your child's entry list mixes IGCSE and O Level, say so at the first session. Working an O Level candidate through IGCSE papers wastes the hour, and on this coast a wasted hour is harder to replace than in the city because specialists are booked further ahead.

programmes.name: AS and A Level, the next step
programmes.description: The sixth-form route most IGCSE students take, examined in June and November series by both boards. The step up in algebraic fluency between Extended Mathematics and AS Pure Mathematics is the commonest reason a Year 12 student asks for help in their first term, and it is a technique gap rather than a content one.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or above or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-khor-fakkan.subjectsIntro: Subject by subject, with the code from each board and the component where marks actually go missing. Ask your child's school which of each pair applies before buying any resource.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Both are two-paper qualifications without coursework. Extended candidates lose marks on non-calculator algebra, reverse percentages and the questions that want a reason rather than a value. Method marks usually outnumber answer marks, so working shown badly is the most expensive habit in the subject.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: A bridge to AS Mathematics taken by stronger Year 11 groups. Calculus arrives early and assumes fluent index and surd work. Students who passed 0580 by recognising question types tend to stall here, and the stall is visible in a single diagnostic session.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and anything requiring an experimental method are the reliable mark-losers. The Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper rewards precise apparatus description and sensible precautions and is almost always under-practised relative to the theory papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis half-equations and organic reaction conditions account for most lost Extended marks. Command terms decide the length of the answer: state wants a word, explain wants a mechanism, and a paragraph written for a one-mark question costs time at the back of the paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume rather than difficulty. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance are the recurring gaps, and data questions are answered from memory instead of from the graph on the page, which scores nothing at all.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Reduced-depth science across all three disciplines in one or two awards. Students entered here routinely revise from single-science papers and spend weeks on material their syllabus does not assess. Confirming the code at session one is the cheapest fix available.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition reward structure and register over vocabulary. Reading responses lose marks when a student retells the passage instead of selecting and commenting, and the time split between the reading questions is a technique problem fixable in two sessions.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Exercise by exercise this paper is winnable on method: note-making wants short precise points, the summary has an enforced word ceiling, and the writing tasks are marked against a fixed register. Many students here speak better English than their marks suggest.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Extended-response marks come from applying a concept to the stimulus case rather than defining it. In Economics, diagram accuracy decides several marks a paper, and the shift-versus-movement error is the most frequent single loss in the subject.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology
subjects.description: Practical papers plus theory. Marks disappear in document production and data handling, where the instructions are long and exact and one unformatted field loses the mark. Timed practice on the real task files is the only approach that shifts the grade.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies
subjects.description: Taught alongside the licensed international curriculum in every UAE private school, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Any support has to match the stream the school has placed the student in.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel, for the same subject
paragraphs: This comparison is the thing a Khor Fakkan family most needs and the thing no page in this market provides. The two boards are not rivals in a parent's life; they are two different sets of papers your child might be sitting, and only one of them is relevant. The content overlap is large enough that a tutor can teach either, and the assessment differences are large enough that teaching one while the student sits the other loses marks.

The headline differences are these. Cambridge uses four-digit syllabus codes and tiers many subjects into Core and Extended paper sets with different grade ceilings. Pearson uses paper codes beginning with a digit and a subject abbreviation, such as 4MA1 and 4PH1, and structures several subjects with optional or staged papers rather than a Core and Extended split. Cambridge science entries involve either a practical examination or a written alternative to practical, chosen by the centre. Session availability differs too: Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates, Pearson a May/June window and November.

For tutoring, three consequences follow. Past papers must match the code, not the subject name, because the structure of the questions differs. Revision guides must match the board, and many on sale locally do not state which. And the tier or optional-paper decision has to be confirmed before a plan is built, because a plan aimed at content the entry does not allow is a plan that cannot work.

Khor Fakkan has a particular version of this problem. With few local schools, families compare notes across different schools and sometimes across different boards, so advice passed between neighbours is less reliable here than it would be in a city neighbourhood where everyone's children attend the same two schools. Check with your own school's exams officer, in writing, and treat everything else as rumour.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and why it precedes everything
paragraphs: A Cambridge Core entry is not an easier version of the same qualification. It is a different paper set with a lower grade ceiling, and that ceiling is fixed by the entry rather than by performance. The decision is made by the school, appears on the entry form months before the papers, and is the single most consequential administrative act in a British-track school year. Families are often not consulted and frequently discover it when results arrive.

The sensible sequence is to settle the tier first and buy teaching second. Ask the school, in writing, which tier each subject is entered at and when the final entry deadline falls. If the marked evidence shows a student consistently at the top of the Core range, that is the case for an Extended entry and it has to be made before the deadline, not after a good mock. If the evidence shows a student well below the Core ceiling across papers, an Extended entry risks a worse outcome than a Core one.

Where tutoring genuinely changes a tier decision is in the weeks before the deadline. Eight weeks of focused teaching can move a borderline student far enough that the school is comfortable entering them at Extended, and that is a decision with two years of consequences. Eight weeks of the same teaching after the entry closes produces a better Core grade and nothing more.

Pearson's structures differ by subject and the logic still holds: find out which papers your child is entered for, in writing, before a tutor plans anything. On this coast the commonest story is not a bad tutor but a good tutor teaching to the wrong entry.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, component by component
paragraphs: Four causes account for most of the gap between a predicted grade and an awarded one, and none of them is about ability. Misreading the command term. Not showing method. Running out of time on the final pages. Revising content the entry does not assess. Each is teachable and each shows up plainly on a marked past paper, which is why the first session of any block is a diagnostic rather than a lesson.

Command terms set the length of an answer. A one-mark question asking a student to state wants a word or a short phrase; a six-mark question asking them to explain wants a chain of reasoning. Students who write a paragraph for every question lose time at the back of the paper, where the heavy marks sit. In Chemistry this shows up in the organic and electrolysis questions, in Physics in anything about method, in Biology in the data questions that are answered from memory.

Method marks are arithmetic. A four-mark calculation typically awards three marks for method and one for the answer. A student who writes only a wrong answer scores nothing; a student who shows three lines and slips at the end scores three. Changing that habit takes about two sessions and is worth more than a term of extra content for most borderline candidates.

The last cause is administrative and the most galling. Every year a student on this coast arrives for a session having spent a fortnight revising single-science material for a Combined Science entry, or Cambridge material for a Pearson paper. Confirm the board, the code, the tier and whether a practical or written alternative applies. It takes one email and saves weeks.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys on this coast
paragraphs: Start with the gap rather than with the rates. Published in-home visiting rates in this market are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour. Published online rates for a qualified subject tutor run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. The difference between those two bands is not teaching quality. It is a car journey, and on the Sharjah east coast that journey is longer than anywhere the published figures were gathered.

What the premium buys is an adult in the room, which is a real thing worth real money for a younger child. What it also buys, without being advertised, is a smaller choice of tutor, because a visiting tutor must live within range of Khor Fakkan. That is the hidden cost, and for an Extended-tier science or Additional Mathematics 0606 it is the expensive one.

The rest of the market, for reference. Budget online tuition runs from about AED 45 to 65 an hour on EdFlik's published rates and from roughly AED 33 to 52 on Tutopiya's, generally delivered by university students. Board specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and a premium named tutor can reach AED 650 as BartyED publishes. Monthly packages in this market include online plans around AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home plans at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. These are market figures published by those providers, not an IB Gram price list.

One cost check a parent can make without asking anyone: work out the implied hourly rate of any monthly package by dividing by the number of sessions and the session length. Packages quoted in sessions rather than hours are the easiest place in this market for a rate to look cheaper than it is.

sections.heading: If the grade came back short: the November route
paragraphs: A missed grade in the summer window is not a lost year, and the mechanics are worth knowing before the results arrive. Both boards run a November series, so a re-entry inside the same calendar year is usually possible. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which gives a realistic sense of how long the wait for a result is.

The first step is not revision. It is reading the statement of results properly. The component breakdown shows which paper lost the grade, and that changes the plan completely. A student who dropped the grade on one practical-style component needs a different six weeks from one who was a few marks short across every paper. Families who start revising before reading the breakdown usually revise the thing that was already fine.

The second step is the entry itself, which your child's school handles and which has its own deadline well before the papers. Ask the exams officer to confirm the entry in writing, including the code and the tier, because a resit is exactly the moment a code or tier gets changed by accident. If the student has left the school, the private candidate route runs through an approved examination centre rather than through us, and the centre sets its own deadlines and fees.

A resit block is shorter and sharper than a first-time block: six to eight weeks, aimed at one or two named papers, with whole papers at exam timing in the last fortnight. It is the one situation where buying a specialist for the specific component clearly beats buying general support, because the diagnosis has already been done by the board.

sections.heading: The permit question, and what to verify about any tutor
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated and most pages in this market avoid saying so. The private tuition work permit was introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The official application route is the ministry's own private tutor licensing service, listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount quoted to you is unverified, including figures that circulate on tutoring sites. A provider who tells you the permit costs money is wrong about something easy to check, which is useful information about the rest of what they say.

There is a separate category worth understanding. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs an educational services permit for a training institute from the Dubai authority, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. That permit belongs to organisations with a physical centre. No tutoring provider should describe itself as approved by an education authority on the strength of anything else, and IB Gram holds no such approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any UAE authority or examination board.

For a teacher at your child's own school, there is one more rule. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as the authority's exact wording, and verify it against the current policy document, but do not go looking for your child's own teacher as a paid tutor.
