sections.heading: How lessons run, and the limits worth knowing
paragraphs: A session is live video with a shared digital whiteboard. The past paper, the marked script or the practical write-up sits on screen and both tutor and student can write on it. A wrong line of working gets rewritten next to the mark scheme. A circuit diagram gets annotated. The session is recorded and kept, which matters on this coast because students spend hours a day on the school run and a recording is the one form of study that survives a moving car.

The practical requirements are small: a laptop or tablet rather than a phone, headphones, and a quiet hour. A phone propped against a textbook is the single arrangement that does not work, because the shared document is the lesson rather than an illustration of it. Connection quality on the east coast is adequate for this in our experience, and a dropped minute costs a minute rather than the session.

The honest limits are two. A student who will not talk to a screen is better served by an adult in the room, and a trial lesson reveals that in twenty minutes rather than after a month of paying. And laboratory handling is school work: what online teaching covers is the written reasoning the practical or alternative-to-practical paper assesses, which is where the marks are.

To close the loop on the search phrase: no tutor arrives in Khor Fakkan. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE, and a provider promising a specialist on this coast at a city hourly rate should be asked who is making the drive and how long they will keep making it.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE board my child's Khor Fakkan school uses?
faqs.answer: Email the exams officer and ask for the board, the syllabus or paper code and the tier for each subject, plus whether science entries use a practical examination or the written alternative. Cambridge codes are four digits such as 0580 and 0625; Pearson codes look like 4MA1 and 4PH1. Do not infer the board from a neighbour's child, because east-coast families often attend different schools on different boards. Ask for it in writing, because a verbal answer is not something you can check later.

faqs.question: Does it matter to a Khor Fakkan student whether the entry is Cambridge or Edexcel?
faqs.answer: They cover overlapping content and are treated comparably by universities, but they are not the same papers. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended with different grade ceilings and uses four-digit codes; Pearson structures several subjects differently and uses codes such as 4CH1. Session availability differs: Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates, Pearson a May/June window and November. For tutoring the difference is practical, because past papers and revision material must match the code your child sits.

faqs.question: Does a Core entry limit what tutoring can do for a Khor Fakkan student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the most important sentence on the page. A Cambridge Core entry caps the grades available, so a student entered at Core cannot reach the top grades however well they are taught. The tier is fixed on the entry form months before the papers. Ask the school which tier each subject is entered at, in writing, before buying any teaching. If a tier change is warranted by the marked evidence, it has to be requested before the entry deadline.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our address in Khor Fakkan?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons here run live online, one to one, over video with a shared whiteboard and the past paper on screen, and the session is recorded. The phrase "home tutor" is the search term parents use, so the page uses it honestly. What you get instead of a visit is a tutor chosen for the exact board and code rather than for living within driving range.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam series can my child sit from the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson's International GCSE runs in a May/June window and in November. The February and March examination series that appears in some tutoring material is offered in India only. Cambridge also allocates centres to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, so ask your school which zone it sits in.

faqs.question: My child missed a grade in the summer. How does a November resit work?
faqs.answer: Start by reading the component breakdown on the statement of results, because it names the paper that lost the grade and a plan built without it usually targets the wrong one. The school handles the re-entry and its deadline falls well before the papers, so confirm the code and tier in writing at the same time. Pearson's November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which shows the realistic wait for a result.

faqs.question: If my child studies with an online tutor, who covers the practical science component?
faqs.answer: Cambridge centres choose between a practical examination and a written alternative to practical, and Pearson assesses practical skills through written papers. What the written components test is reasoning on paper: apparatus choice, variables, precautions, scale reading, identifying a flaw in a method and suggesting an improvement. All of that is taught from real papers on a shared screen. Handling equipment happens in your child's school laboratory, where it belongs, and the marks come from the reasoning.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should a Khor Fakkan student have tutoring in?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with. Hours spread across three subjects usually move none of them, because each gets too little contact to rebuild anything. The better approach is to use the marked evidence to find the one or two subjects where the gap is largest and the grade is most at risk, concentrate there for a dated block, then reassess. If the real problem is organisation across every subject rather than content in one, that is a different purchase entirely.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tutoring cost in Khor Fakkan compared with the city?
faqs.answer: The published market bands are the same wherever you sit, because the online tutor pool is national: roughly AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik's budget rate, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and AED 200 to 450 or more for board specialists where TutorChase publishes AED 270. Visiting in-home rates are quoted at AED 180 to 500. On this coast the in-home premium would be larger, because the journey is longer.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching a Khor Fakkan student need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so quoted amounts are unverified.

faqs.question: Can my child take different IGCSE subjects with different exam boards?
faqs.answer: Schools do sometimes enter candidates across both boards, and in some subjects alongside O Level. It is legitimate and it creates a practical trap: the family buys one set of revision material and uses it for everything. Ask for the entry list by subject with the board and code against each one. For tutoring, say which is which at the first session, because a tutor working an O Level candidate through IGCSE papers is teaching the wrong structure with the right content.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying more for an examiner-marketed tutor on this coast?
faqs.answer: Only if the claim can be evidenced. Published premium rates in this market reach AED 650 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Examiner status for an individual is easy to assert and hard to verify, and it implies nothing about access to marking standards or unreleased paper content. A tutor who knows the published mark scheme in detail and will show you a marked script is more useful than a title on a profile. Ask to see the script.

faqs.question: Which authority oversees private schools on the Sharjah east coast?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, including the east-coast towns, and for Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A Khor Fakkan student enrolled in Fujairah comes under federal Ministry of Education supervision instead. No UAE education authority approves or accredits private tutoring providers, so a provider claiming otherwise is making a checkable claim that does not hold.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Khor Fakkan family start lessons?
faqs.answer: Common subjects in early-evening Gulf Standard Time slots are usually matched quickly. Narrow combinations take longer: Additional Mathematics 0606, ICT practical coaching, Arabic as a first language, or an unusual board variant late in a series. If the right specialist is not free for your preferred slot we say so and name the alternatives, which are a different slot with the right tutor, a short declared bridging block, or a decline. Booking outside the post-mock rush is the reliable way to get both the tutor and the time.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both Cambridge and Pearson versions of a subject?
faqs.answer: In mathematics and the sciences, many can, because the content overlap is substantial and an experienced tutor knows both paper structures. Ask the specific question: which codes have you taught to examination classes, and in which series? A tutor who answers with named codes and components is telling you something verifiable. One who answers with the subject name is telling you they will learn the structure while teaching your child, which you are paying for either way.

intro.heading: Compare the models, not the postcodes
paragraphs: Maryam Island is a waterfront apartment development on the Sharjah lagoon, between Al Khan and Al Majaz and minutes from the Dubai border. Families here routinely begin the search for IGCSE support by comparing their district with the one next door, and it is the wrong comparison. These lagoon neighbourhoods share one tutoring market. The difference between them is the view, the age of the building and the service charge, not the depth of the pool of people who have taught Cambridge 0620 Chemistry at Extended tier.

The comparisons that do change a grade are three, and none of them is geographic. The first is between provider models: an agency, an international marketplace, a freelance tutor, a tuition centre and a platform are genuinely different products at genuinely different prices with genuinely different failure modes. The second is between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, which are separate awarding bodies with separate codes and papers. The third is between Core and Extended tier, which decides the ceiling your child is working towards.

Most pages ranking for these searches compare themselves with an unnamed set of other platforms, which tells a parent nothing. This page compares the models by what they charge, what they include, whether a permit can be verified and what happens when a match goes wrong, with every rate attributed to whoever published it and the month it was read. You can check each figure, and you should.

IB Gram's own model is worth stating at the outset so the comparison is honest. We are a matching service that teaches live, one-to-one, over video. We do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, because home tuition is a service we offer only in India. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and neither does any other tutoring provider in this market.

The rest of the page works through those three comparisons in order, then covers the June and November series for a Sharjah candidate, the tuition-centre permit question that nobody explains, and the boundary on coursework. If you want the housing-and-neighbourhood version of the comparison, the IB page for this development takes that line; the combined page reads the year as a calendar. One practical note first: find the statement of entry before you read the board table, because almost nobody knows which board their child is sitting until they check. It is a five-minute job, it costs nothing, and it removes the single most common source of wasted sessions in this market: a competent tutor working carefully from the wrong specification, giving advice about paper structure and timing that is specifically and confidently wrong for the papers your child will actually sit in the summer.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-maryam-islan.programmesIntro: Three things get compared under the heading of IGCSE and they are not the same thing. The board, the tier and the progression route each change what tutoring should be doing, and all three are decided before a parent usually finds out.

programmes.name: Cambridge Core tier
programmes.description: Core covers the main syllabus content without the supplementary material, sets shorter papers with narrower command terms, and caps the achievable grade at C in most subjects. For a student who needs five secure passes for equivalency rather than a science route at A Level, it is the sensible placement rather than a demotion.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah the tier is usually set by the school at the end of Year 9 and communicated badly. A Maryam Island parent should ask the subject teacher outright, because a Core-tier student being drilled on Extended material will meet unfamiliar question types in the exam hall, and an Extended-tier student fed Core questions will be under-prepared for the supplementary content that carries the top grades.

programmes.name: Cambridge Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended opens the full grade range to A*, adds the supplementary content and sets longer, more analytical papers. It is the requirement for AS and A Level sciences and for most competitive university routes. The step up is in the kind of question rather than only the quantity: explanation and justification replace recall.
programmes.countryNote: Extended tier is where the local tutor pool thins out across every Sharjah district equally. Many people can help with Core arithmetic. Far fewer can mark an Extended Paper 4 response the way an examiner does and explain the difference between a method mark and an accuracy mark, and the few who can are not distributed by neighbourhood.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE runs parallel to Cambridge with its own specification codes, papers and tiering. Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1, tiered Foundation and Higher across two equally weighted papers. Some subjects can be entered modularly, which changes when revision has to peak compared with a linear course.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools use Cambridge for some subjects and Pearson for others, so one child can sit two boards in a single year. The statement of entry is the only reliable source; textbook covers and school websites both lag behind actual entries, and a tutor working from the wrong board gives advice that is confidently and specifically wrong.

programmes.name: What the grades are being collected for
programmes.description: Most Sharjah British-curriculum students continue into AS and A Level with three or four subjects, and entry is set on IGCSE grades. The depth increase is larger than the step into IGCSE was, so a marginal Extended grade in a subject the student intends to continue is a Year 12 problem being deferred rather than solved.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students submit five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One competitor page in this market publishes six as the subject count, which is wrong; verify the rule on the Ministry's own channel.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-maryam-islan.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Sharjah families ask about, with codes where the code decides the match. Each note says where marks are actually lost, because that is what a weekly hour is for.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers, no coursework. Extended candidates lose marks to algebra under time pressure and to problems combining topics without signalling it. Timed papers with the mark scheme open outperform further worked examples.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Theory papers plus, for Cambridge, the alternative-to-practical paper, which tests experimental reasoning rather than recall. It is the paper Sharjah Extended candidates most often underperform on, and it needs sessions of its own.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry carry the heaviest weight and the highest failure rate. The qualitative-analysis tables and organic nomenclature are learnable by drill and are usually left until April, which is late enough to hurt.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: High content volume with marks tied to precise terminology: a loosely correct answer scores nothing where the mark scheme names a term. Transport in plants, genetics and homeostasis recur as the weak areas year after year.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Comprehension, a strictly disciplined summary task and directed writing against a stated purpose and audience. Summary marks are lost by lifting sentences from the passage rather than reformulating them properly.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition in one paper, reading passages in the other. Analytical marks depend on quoting precisely and commenting on effect rather than restating content, which is a technique problem rather than a vocabulary one.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450 / 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study led, with marks sitting in application and evaluation rather than definition. A student who knows every term and cannot apply it to the stimulus material stalls around a C until the answer structure changes.

subjects.name: Economics (0455 / 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks: axes labelled, correct shift, new equilibrium identified. Data-response answers must quote figures from the extract rather than reason in general terms.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Theory of computer systems plus algorithms and programming. Pseudocode conventions and trace tables are mechanical marks students throw away, and binary and hexadecimal conversion rewards plain drill.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: Sat alongside the international curriculum because Arabic is mandatory in UAE private schools. It does not count towards the five subjects required for Ministry equivalency, which surprises most families, and it still needs preparation.

regions.name: Al Taawun
regions.note: Coastal towers nearest the Dubai border, popular with families working in Deira and Bur Dubai. Border proximity shapes the school choice far more than it shapes who can teach 0625 Extended.

regions.name: Al Nahda, Sharjah
regions.note: Dense residential district straddling the border with a very high daily commute into Dubai. Another neighbourhood where comparing it with Maryam Island changes nothing about tutoring.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: The inland school cluster, twenty-five to forty minutes away depending on the hour. A lagoon-district child schooled here faces the longest afternoon of any Sharjah-schooled student.

regions.name: University City

sections.heading: The six provider models, compared on what they actually publish
paragraphs: This is the comparison that matters and almost nobody makes it. The IGCSE tutoring market in Sharjah contains at least six distinct models, and they differ in price, in what is included, in whether a tutor's permit can be verified and in what happens when a match goes wrong. Competitor pages compare themselves to an unnamed set of other platforms. The table below compares the models themselves, with sources.

Read the replacement-policy column carefully, because it is the one that predicts your experience six weeks in. A marketplace hands you a list and leaves the selection risk with you. An agency chooses for you and may or may not change the choice without charge. A freelance tutor is a single relationship with no fallback at all, which is fine when it works and expensive when it does not.

The permit column is the one nobody writes about. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Any model can be compliant. The difference is whether you, as a parent, can actually check.

Our own row is in the table and is not flattered. We teach online only, we have no UAE premises and we offer no home visits, and we hold no regulator's approval because no tutoring provider in this market holds one. What we do publish is the rate bands other people charge, the coverage limits on our own matching, and what happens if the first tutor is wrong.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel, subject by subject
paragraphs: The second comparison is between awarding bodies, and it is the one that most often produces a mismatched tutor. Parents in the lagoon districts tell us their child does IGCSE Maths, which is not enough information to make a match. Cambridge and Pearson are separate bodies with separate specifications, paper structures and mark schemes, and fluency in one is not fluency in the other.

Find the codes in the table below on your child's statement of entry rather than on the textbook spine. Schools change board more readily than they replace their resources, so a Cambridge revision guide on an Edexcel student's shelf is an ordinary sight in Sharjah and a reliable source of confusion. It is a five-minute check that prevents the commonest error in this market.

The differences are concrete rather than cosmetic. Cambridge tiers Mathematics as Core and Extended; Pearson tiers Specification A as Foundation and Higher. Cambridge sciences include an alternative-to-practical route; Pearson handles practical skills differently. Some Pearson subjects permit modular entry, which changes when revision has to peak. None of that should be discovered in April.

A single Sharjah student can be sitting both boards in the same year, with Cambridge Physics 0625 and Pearson Chemistry 4CH1 running in parallel. That means two different approaches to practical assessment at once, and a tutor who treats them as interchangeable will spend sessions on the wrong skills. Write the board next to every subject on one sheet before you book anything.

sections.heading: Core against Extended, and what each ceiling implies
paragraphs: The third comparison is the tier, and it is the one with the clearest consequence. Core caps most subjects at grade C. Extended opens the range to A*. That single fact determines whether a student can take the subject at AS and A Level, which determines a large part of what they can study at university, and it is decided by a school in Year 9 on the basis of Year 9 performance.

The table sets out what changes between the tiers. The row worth dwelling on is the tutoring-hours row, because it is the practical question. Extended requires the supplementary content and a different question style, so a student moving up a tier has both more material and a new skill to acquire, and that is a two-term job rather than a half-term one.

This matters particularly for a lagoon-district family weighing whether to push for a tier change. It can be the right decision and it is not free. A student moved to Extended in the middle of Year 10 without support will meet the supplementary content cold in Year 11, and the outcome can be worse than a secure C would have been. Ask the school what evidence they want before they will move a student, then decide.

The reverse case is worth naming too. A student placed at Extended who is not coping is sometimes better served by a managed move to Core, a secure pass and five solid subjects for equivalency, than by two years of distress and a D. Schools are often reluctant to discuss it. A parent can raise it, and it is a legitimate question rather than giving up.

sections.heading: A tuition centre against one-to-one, honestly
paragraphs: There are tuition centres within reach of the lagoon districts, and for some families they are the right answer. A group class at a lower per-student rate is genuinely good value when everybody in the room needs the same content explained, which is most often true in the autumn of Year 10 and in the weeks after a topic has been taught badly at school.

It is close to useless for the problem most Year 11 families actually have. If your child knows the content and loses six marks a paper to command-term misreading, presentation and timing, those are individual habits. A tutor managing six students cannot see or correct one student's specific habit, and the session is spent on material your child already has.

There is also a regulatory distinction worth knowing, because providers blur it. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific licence for a specific kind of organisation. An individual private tutor holds a MoHRE permit instead, which is a different document entirely.

So the honest comparison is this: use a centre for content, use one-to-one for technique, and do not pay one-to-one rates for content a group class would cover as well. We would rather you spent six sessions with us on paper technique and did your content revision elsewhere than bought thirty hours of general support from anyone.

sections.heading: What the lagoon districts pay, cheapest band first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because that is where most Sharjah families start. University City supplies a large number of undergraduate tutors, and published budget rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. For Year 9 consolidation and Core-tier support that is often entirely adequate and we will say so rather than talk you upwards.

The band stops being adequate at Extended tier in the term before a series. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. A specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED, which is rarely justified and almost never verifiable.

In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to 500 with independent tutors. On a waterfront development the visit also costs you visitor parking, building access and the quiet of a shared living room for the hour, which is a cost that never appears in a rate card. Monthly packages show the gap plainly: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, the same eight contact hours at roughly double the price.

sections.heading: The June and November series for a Sharjah candidate
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, which means any page quoting a February exam window or an autumn entry deadline to a Sharjah parent has given them a date that is wrong for their country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

Entry deadlines sit months before the papers and are handled by the school. Mocks fall a term earlier. Coursework and practical deadlines are earlier still and school-set. The revision peak belongs in the eight to twelve weeks before the papers, which means the content has to be learned before then, which means the autumn of Year 11 is not a planning period but a working one.

One Cambridge administrative point is worth naming because Cambridge names it itself: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your school which zone it sits in and work from that timetable.

The resit decision is the one families take too slowly. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The autumn entry window closes shortly after August results arrive. Agree the trigger rule in advance: which grade in which subject would mean a November entry, written down before results day rather than argued about afterwards. Always check the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than relying on restated dates.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Several IGCSE subjects carry school-assessed components, and this market contains providers who will simply produce them. One page in this research advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. For a student in Sharjah the consequence of submitting bought work is not a lower grade; it is a malpractice finding against the qualification, and it is not recoverable.

The boundary stated plainly. A tutor may teach the skills the task requires, explain how the mark scheme awards them, model the approach on a different example, read a draft the student has written and say where it is unclear, unsupported or off-brief, and teach referencing, data handling and write-up conventions.

Where that list stops is the more useful half of the boundary, and it is also where the six models in section one separate from one another. A tutor may not write, rewrite, complete or edit the work to a finished state, and may not produce a worked version of the student's own task, however carefully the task has been paraphrased first. The same line runs through materials. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter rather than a judgement call. A provider that hands over a folder of all four has told you, before you have asked, how it will treat every other boundary on this page.

There is a further rule about teachers. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and check the current policy document; the principle stands either way and we will not arrange it.
bullets: Teaching, mark-scheme explanation and feedback on the student's own draft: yes
Writing, completing or finishing assessed work: never
Official papers and mark schemes as downloads: no, we link the source
A tutor who also marks your child's school work: no

sections.heading: Making the three comparisons in one evening
paragraphs: All of this is actionable in about an hour. Find the statement of entry and write down, per subject, the board, the code and the tier. That settles two of the three comparisons immediately and it is information most parents in these districts do not have to hand, which is why so many first sessions are spent establishing it.

Then decide which problem you are buying a solution to. If content is missing, a group class or a budget-band tutor may be the efficient answer and we will tell you so. If the content is there and six marks a paper are leaking to technique, that is one-to-one work and a short block of it rather than a year. The trial lesson exists to tell you which of those two you have.

Then make the model choice with the table above open. Ask any provider three questions: what the rate is and whether it is per hour or per session, whether the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and what happens if the match is wrong in week two. A provider who answers all three without hesitation is a different proposition from one who answers none.

Finally, agree the week-four evidence before anything starts. Which errors should have stopped recurring, what should be happening on timed questions, whether the work between sessions is getting done. We change the specialist if that evidence is missing rather than defending the first choice, and you should expect the same of anybody you pay.

process.title: Send the statement of entry details
process.description: Board, syllabus code and tier for each subject in difficulty, plus the school. Those four facts decide the match and they are the information least often available at first contact, which is why so many first sessions elsewhere are spent discovering them instead of teaching.

process.title: We say which model suits the problem
process.description: If the issue is missing content, we will tell you a group class or a budget-band tutor may be the efficient answer. We would rather give you six useful sessions than thirty unnecessary ones, and saying that up front is cheaper for us than a cancellation in week five.

process.title: A free trial that diagnoses
process.description: The tutor sets a real past-paper question, marks it against the mark scheme and tells you in writing whether this is a content gap, a technique problem or a coverage-sequence issue from a school transfer. Nothing is paid before the trial and the diagnosis stands regardless of what you do next.

process.title: Fix the slot and a fallback day
process.description: A weekly time in Gulf Standard Time chosen around the real afternoon, plus one agreed alternative day for coursework and mock weeks. Sessions that can move survive the four or five disrupted weeks every IGCSE year contains; sessions that can only be cancelled do not.

process.title: Four-week review, change if needed
process.description: We check the evidence agreed at the start: recurring errors, timed-question performance, work completed between sessions. If it is not there we move the student to another specialist in the same subject rather than arguing for the original match.

whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit the Cambridge June and November series; the February and March series is India only. Several pages ranking for these searches publish the February dates to Gulf parents, which is a date a family acts on and gets wrong.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE tutoring easier to find in Al Khan than in Maryam Island?
faqs.answer: No. These two districts are adjacent, share the same school access and draw on the same tutor market, and the difference between them is housing age and service charge rather than tutoring supply. The real constraint is how few people have taught a given Extended-tier syllabus through a full two-year cycle, and those people are not distributed by neighbourhood. If you have been considering whether a different lagoon district would solve the problem, it will not, and the month spent checking is better spent on the board and tier.

faqs.question: Which provider model gives the best value for an Extended-tier student?
faqs.answer: It depends on the problem, which is why the comparison table on this page is organised by model rather than by brand. For missing content, a tuition centre group class or a budget-band online tutor at AED 33 to 65 an hour is efficient. For individual technical habits costing six marks a paper, one-to-one is the only model that can address them, and a short block of six to ten sessions usually beats a year of general support. Diagnose first, then choose the model.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a tutor in Sharjah is permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask them directly for their MoHRE private tuition work permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because it is free and completes in about two working days through the MoHRE smart app and e-services system, there is no good reason for a working tutor not to hold one. A hesitant answer is itself informative.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a tuition centre permit and a tutor permit?
faqs.answer: They are different documents for different things, and providers blur the distinction. An individual giving private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained through initial approval, with a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. Neither document makes anyone KHDA approved as a tutor, and no tutoring provider in this market, including us, holds a regulator's endorsement.

faqs.question: My child is at Core tier. Does that limit university options?
faqs.answer: It limits the subject route rather than the student. Core caps most Cambridge subjects at grade C, which generally rules the subject out at AS and A Level, and that in turn narrows some degree options. Five secure Core passes still satisfy the Ministry of Education's British-track requirement of five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. If a particular A Level is the goal, the tier conversation needs to happen with the school in Year 10, not Year 11.

faqs.question: Should we push the school to move our child up to Extended tier?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and not without planning. Moving up means covering the supplementary content from scratch plus adopting a different question style, which is realistically a two-term job rather than a half-term one. A student moved mid-Year 10 without support meets the supplementary material cold in Year 11 and can end up worse off than a secure C. Ask the school what evidence they want before they will move a student, get it, and then decide with a plan for the extra content rather than hoping.

faqs.question: Can a tutor cover both Cambridge and Pearson for the same child?
faqs.answer: In Sharjah you may need exactly that, because several schools run Cambridge for some subjects and Pearson for others, so one child can sit two boards in a year. We match a separate specialist per subject and per board rather than giving you one tutor who knows one specification and is guessing at the other. Read the codes from the statement of entry: Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended tiers, Pearson Specification A is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher. The textbook on the shelf is not evidence.

faqs.question: Why do some pages mention a February IGCSE exam series?
faqs.answer: Because they are repeating Cambridge's February and March series, which is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. A page that quotes a February exam window or an autumn entry deadline to a Sharjah parent has handed them a date to act on that is wrong for their country, and that is the kind of error that costs a family an entry. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with its November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026.

faqs.question: Does the quoted hourly rate include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing, because practice varies across this market and we are not going to state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees without a Federal Tax Authority citation. The practical questions for a parent are three: whether the figure is per hour or per session, whether it includes any tax, and whether there is a minimum commitment. Several providers quote a session price against an hourly comparison, which makes their rate look lower than it is when you compare it with a published hourly band.

faqs.question: Is a group class ever better than one-to-one for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more often than one-to-one providers admit. When everybody in the room needs the same content explained, which is most of the autumn of Year 10 and any time a topic has been taught badly at school, a group class at a lower per-student rate is good value. It fails for individual technique: a tutor managing six students cannot see that your child misreads the command term in part c of every structured question. Use a centre for content and one-to-one for habits.

faqs.question: How soon before the June series is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Ten to twelve weeks is enough to change a grade if the problem is technique, and not enough to rebuild two years if the content was never learned. Those two situations need opposite plans, which is why the trial lesson is diagnostic. If the content is broadly there and marks are going to timing, command-term misreading and presentation, timed papers with mark-scheme correction work reliably in that window. If it is not, a November entry with a proper build is the better decision than a panic block in April.

faqs.question: What happens if we need to change tutor after two weeks?
faqs.answer: We change them, and you do not restart the arrangement or justify the request beyond telling us it is not working. At the outset we agree what week four should show: which errors have stopped recurring, what is happening on timed questions, whether work between sessions is being done. If that evidence is absent, or the relationship simply is not productive, the student moves to another specialist in the same subject. Ask any provider what their version of this answer is before you pay anything.

faqs.question: Are tuition centres near the lagoon districts worth travelling to?
faqs.answer: For the right purpose, yes. A centre within fifteen minutes is a reasonable way to buy content revision in a group at a lower per-student cost, particularly in Year 10. Weigh the journey honestly though: two trips a week into central Sharjah traffic for a student who also has school homework is a real tax on the week, and it is the reason many lagoon families who start at a centre end up online. Decide on the basis of what the sessions are for rather than on the rate alone.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count in the five subjects for equivalency?
faqs.answer: No, and this catches families out. The Ministry of Education's British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. They are still mandatory in UAE private schools and still take timetable space. One competitor page in this market states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel; IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: Which single question should I ask every provider I contact?
faqs.answer: How many full two-year cycles has the proposed tutor taught of this exact syllabus code at this exact tier. It is a specific, checkable question, and the answers sort the market quickly. A provider who answers with the tutor's degree, their years of experience in general or their rapport with students has not answered it. The follow-up questions worth asking are whether the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit and what happens if the match is wrong in week two.

intro.heading: The code, not the subject
paragraphs: Your child's school report says Mathematics. What they actually sit is Cambridge 0580 at Core or Extended tier, or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 at Foundation or Higher tier, and those four possibilities are four different exam experiences with four different grade ceilings. A tutor who does not establish which one applies in the first conversation will teach the subject rather than the paper, and the gap shows up in a timed mock rather than in a session.

Muwaileh is a good place to see why this matters. The district sits inland next to University City, on the Maliha Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed corridor, with several large campuses releasing into the same dismissal window. Those campuses do not all enter the same board, and some enter different boards for different subjects inside one year group. A tutor working across three Muwaileh schools without checking codes is working on averages.

There is a second variable nobody mentions in a tutoring enquiry: practical science. A Cambridge centre may assess practical work through a timetabled practical paper or through an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the revision those two require is substantially different. A parent who does not know which route the school uses cannot judge whether a revision plan makes sense, and most tutors will not ask.

The tier decision is the third. Cambridge Core entry caps the grade at C. That clears the Ministry of Education equivalency floor on the British track, which asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, but it sits below what most universities want for engineering, medicine or mathematics. Tier placement is usually made in Year 9 on a Checkpoint result and then rarely revisited unless a parent asks.

None of this requires a parent to understand the subject. It requires four facts, all of which the school holds and will share on request, and a willingness to insist on them before money changes hands rather than after a disappointing mock. The four facts are the board, the code, the tier and the practical route, and they are what the first section of this page is about.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. In-home visits are a service offered only in India. Muwaileh students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper on a shared screen. Set against the local option, the trade is honest — you lose a person in the room and gain a tutor chosen for the code rather than for the drive.

What follows: how to establish the code and tier in one email, what the two boards actually differ on, the two practical routes, the revision timetable that works backwards from the June series, and where the local pool is thin.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-muwaileh.programmesIntro: Three qualifications sit behind an IGCSE search in this catchment, plus the progression route families are usually planning towards. The codes below are the ones to confirm with the school before any tutoring is booked.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, terminal written papers, and tiered entry in several subjects: Core caps at grade C, Extended reaches A*. The codes are four digits — 0580 Mathematics, 0606 Additional Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English, 0510 English as a Second Language. On Extended Mathematics, Paper 4 carries the structured long questions that decide most grades, and method marks there are won by showing working.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November series. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to Sharjah candidates. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Take the timetable from your school's exams officer.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes beginning with 4 — 4MA1 Mathematics Specification A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Mathematics Specification A is tiered Foundation and Higher, with two papers of equal weight, so a candidate who mismanages time on the first paper has no shorter second paper to recover on. Science is concentrated in written papers for most routes, which makes timed practice the whole preparation strategy for a weak candidate.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results reached students in January — November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the next day. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official PDF.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and the tier decision
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, ending in Checkpoint tests that schools use for setting. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint in March, May and October. A Checkpoint result that puts a student into Core rather than Extended Mathematics sets the grade ceiling two years ahead of the exam, and that decision is cheap to challenge in Year 9 and expensive to work around in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Muwaileh frequently reach tutoring at the point where a Year 10 report reveals a Core entry nobody discussed. The honest route is to ask the school what evidence would support a tier change and work towards it with marked papers, rather than buying remediation hours in the exam year. A tier appeal supported by real marked work is a different conversation from a parental request.

programmes.name: AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: Where most Sharjah IGCSE students go, and the reason the Year 11 grade matters beyond itself. AS and A Level subject entry usually assumes an A or B at Extended in that subject, and the step up in Mathematics and the sciences is steep because A Level assumes algebraic fluency that IGCSE only samples. Year 11 tutoring aimed at that progression targets the topics AS builds on directly, not just the pass.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. A ranking competitor page states six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-muwaileh.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Muwaileh families request most, each with the specific place marks go. Use them as test material: a tutor who knows the code can expand any of these without notes.

subjects.name: Mathematics — 0580 / 4MA1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended Paper 4 decides the grade: structured questions on functions, transformations, vectors and probability. Unshown method on a four-mark question typically scores one. Pearson splits the marks evenly across two papers, so pacing matters more there.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics — 0606
subjects.description: Calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities 0580 never reaches. Treating it as harder 0580 revision is the standard mistake; students who do well have drilled differentiation and the factor theorem deliberately. A thin pool of tutors in Sharjah.

subjects.name: Physics — 0625 / 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism take most of the lost marks, usually when a potential divider is read as a plain series circuit. Six-mark items reward structured reasoning. The centre's practical route changes half the revision plan.

subjects.name: Chemistry — 0620 / 4CH1
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic and organic pathways carry the grade. Units dropped mid-titration cost marks, and naming a product without its functional group scores nothing. Cambridge examines qualitative analysis in detail — the cheapest marks available.

subjects.name: Biology — 0610 / 4BI1
subjects.description: Volume, not difficulty. Extended-response marks go to candidates using mark-scheme vocabulary — active transport, partially permeable, selective reabsorption — rather than paraphrase. Data questions on unfamiliar experiments separate the strong candidates.

subjects.name: English First Language — 0500 / 0990 / 4EA1
subjects.description: Directed writing is marked on audience, register and form as well as content, so fluent generic prose sits at C. Reading questions need quotation plus explanation. The Pearson anthology differs, so revision material does not transfer between boards.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language — 0510 / 0511
subjects.description: Widely taken in Sharjah schools. The reading-and-writing paper rewards precise information transfer, and copying whole sentences into a note-taking grid loses marks. Speaking is assessed separately and is usually the least prepared component.

subjects.name: Business Studies — 0450 / 4BS1
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole paper: a correct definition with no reference to the named business sits in the bottom band. Evaluation questions carry the top marks and need a judgement with a reason — the most trainable skill in the syllabus.

subjects.name: Economics — 0455 / 4EC1
subjects.description: Diagram marks are awarded separately for axis labels, shift direction and the new equilibrium, so a remembered sketch loses three marks before the explanation starts. Gulf-context data questions appear regularly, which makes local examples genuinely useful.

subjects.name: Computer Science — 0478 / 4CP0
subjects.description: Theory on data representation and networks is learnable and chronically under-revised while students spend time coding. Pseudocode is marked against the syllabus's own conventions, not Python, which costs marks on every trace table.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools and examinable in its own right. Separate streams exist for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ, so material does not cross between them.

sections.heading: One email that fixes the whole tutoring plan
paragraphs: Write to your school's exams officer and ask four things: which board each subject is entered with, the syllabus code, the tier, and which practical route the science subjects use. The reply usually arrives inside a day and it is the highest-return ten minutes available to a Muwaileh parent.

Here is why each one changes the plan. The board decides which past papers are useful, and a term spent on the wrong board's papers is worse than no practice because the student learns question shapes that will not appear. The code pins the content: 0580 and 0606 are different syllabuses sat by the same student in the same year, and a tutor told only "maths" will cover the wrong one.

The tier decides the ceiling and the strategy. A Cambridge Core candidate working through Extended material is wasting hours on content they will never be asked; an Extended candidate drilled on Core material arrives at Paper 4 unprepared for the structured questions that carry the grade. The practical route decides whether lab technique or written interpretation of experiments needs the attention.

Ask for the centre's own timetable in the same email. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone version. A tutor quoting dates from a generic download is working from a document that may not apply to your child.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson are not the same qualification
paragraphs: Parents and even school reports treat IGCSE as one thing. It is two separate qualifications from two separate boards, with different papers, different tiering language and different question styles, and a tutor's fluency does not transfer automatically between them.

Mathematics is the clearest case. Cambridge 0580 runs Core and Extended, with Extended Paper 4 weighted heavily towards structured long questions. Pearson 4MA1 Specification A runs Foundation and Higher, with two papers of equal weight — which means pacing errors cannot be recovered and a student who freezes on Paper 1 has lost half the marks before the second sitting.

Science diverges on assessment rather than content. Cambridge centres choose between a timetabled practical paper and an alternative-to-practical written paper, and those demand different preparation: one needs apparatus handling and observation recording, the other needs the ability to interpret somebody else's experiment on paper. Pearson concentrates most routes into written papers, which makes timed practice the whole strategy.

English is the trap that catches families moving schools. The set texts and anthology differ between boards, so a student arriving from a Pearson school into a Cambridge entry cannot reuse a year of literature revision. Confirm the row that applies to your child before the first paid session, not after it.

One more practical consequence. Grade scales differ too: Cambridge reports A* to G while Pearson International GCSE reports 9 to 1, and a parent comparing two children's reports across boards is comparing different scales. Universities and the Ministry read both, but a family should know which scale they are looking at before drawing conclusions about progress.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and how to challenge one properly
paragraphs: Tier is the quietest decision in a British-curriculum school and one of the most consequential. Cambridge Core entry caps the grade at C. That is above the Ministry of Education equivalency floor of grade E or 3, so it does not block a UAE university application outright, but it sits below the entry requirement for most engineering, mathematics, medical and economics routes.

The decision is usually made in Year 9, often on a Checkpoint result, and then it travels forward without discussion. Many parents in this catchment discover it from a Year 10 report that mentions Core, and by then a year of teaching has already been pitched at that level.

Challenging it is possible and it works better with evidence than with pressure. Ask the school what evidence would support a change — typically marked work at Extended standard across several assessments. Then produce that: a short block of tutoring aimed at Extended-standard questions, with the marked outcomes shared with the subject teacher. That is a specific, bounded piece of work, usually six to ten sessions.

What does not work is buying general tutoring and hoping the grade argues for itself, or leaving it until Year 11 when the entry has been made. The honest advice is that a tier conversation belongs in Year 9 or early Year 10, and a parent who reads this in March of Year 11 should put the energy into maximising the Core grade instead.

sections.heading: The year counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, which is odd, because the calendar is what decides whether tutoring money does any work. Eight sessions in October buy content. The same eight sessions in April buy pacing. Both cost the same.

Work backwards. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers and the tier is fixed at that point. Mocks land in the preceding term and are the best diagnostic a family will get for free. The window in which timed full-paper practice actually moves a grade is roughly the eight weeks before the first exam, and before that window the hours should be buying content and technique instead.

Ramadan deserves a line of its own in the plan. Study patterns shift, evenings run later, and an intensive block scheduled straight through the month tends to be rescheduled anyway. Families who plan lighter sessions during it and put the intensive work either side lose nothing; families who plan through it lose the sessions and the rhythm.

Dates below are the structure of the year, not a timetable. Both boards revise published timetables and Cambridge warns explicitly about zone versions, so the only version to plan against is the one your exams officer issues.

There is also a decision that arrives suddenly in August. A June grade that misses an AS requirement has a November resit route, but the entry window for it is short, so the call is made in days rather than weeks. Families who have already asked the exams officer what a resit entry involves make it calmly; families who have not spend results week guessing.

sections.heading: Past papers: what a tutor may use and what they may not
paragraphs: Past-paper work is the core of effective IGCSE tutoring, and it is also where a careless provider creates a real problem. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge and Pearson. They are available free through the school and through the boards' own channels.

What a tutor should do is work through official material with the student, in session, citing where it came from. What a tutor should not do is host or supply a download library of board material, and a tutoring service that advertises one is distributing someone else's copyright. For unreleased material the exposure is worse than copyright — it crosses into malpractice territory.

The useful version of past-paper work is narrower than most families expect. It is not working through twenty papers. It is working through three, marking them against the published scheme, and building an error log that names the recurring loss — unshown method, dropped units, mark-scheme vocabulary missing, a command term misread. Then attacking that loss specifically.

On coursework, where a centre runs a component with one: a tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria and gives feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor does not write it, complete it or supply model text. One operator in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright; the consequence of using that falls on the candidate.

A note on the error log, because it is the part families skip. It should be one page, kept across papers rather than per session, naming the loss in the student's own words. A log that says "careless mistakes" is useless. A log that says "I write the answer without the working on any question worth three or more marks" is actionable the next morning.

sections.heading: Where the Muwaileh tutor pool is deep and where it is not
paragraphs: This district has a genuine local supply, and University City next door is the reason. Three universities on the doorstep produce a real pool of capable subject help at the lower end of the market — the band that advertises from about AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45–65 and Tutopiya AED 33–52.

That pool is good at content. A student who missed three weeks of trigonometry is well served. It is thinner on mark-scheme technique, which is a different skill: reading a marked paper, naming the loss, and training the specific behaviour that recovers it. The market's qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to AED 300 online is pricing that difference, and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 500 is pricing travel on top.

The genuinely thin specialisms are consistent: Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 marked against the syllabus's own pseudocode conventions, Accounting 0452, IGCSE Arabic as a first language, and any subject at a specific tier in the eight weeks before a series when every slot is taken.

Using both is often the best value. A local or budget tutor for content catch-up and a specialist over live video for technique is a common and sensible split in this catchment. What fails is buying one and expecting it to do the other's job.

Price is part of this picture and worth stating plainly. The market's qualified-tutor band runs AED 150 to AED 300 an hour online, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work, against in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 500 where Bestimate's Dubai table puts the usual range at AED 180–350. Those are market figures read in October 2026.

sections.heading: The permit, SPEA, and what a parent can check
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so a figure quoted to you as the penalty is unverified and should be treated that way. What matters practically is that the permit costs nothing, so a working tutor has no innocent reason not to hold one. Ask.

The school side sits with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate. Its remit is wider than inspection: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is why a Muwaileh school's subject offer can differ from a Dubai school's a short drive away, and why a report has to be read in the emirate's own context.

For clarity: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed by or partnered with SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. Any tutoring service describing itself as regulator-approved should be asked to show the number.

sections.heading: Starting from the marked paper
paragraphs: The useful first document is the last marked paper, not the report card. A grade says a problem exists; a marked paper shows which four marks went and why, and that is the only basis for saying anything worth paying for before being paid.

Send it with the school name, and with the board, code and tier if the exams officer has replied. Then take a free trial session over live video, at a time that survives the Muwaileh dismissal window — in practice six o'clock or later for a household with children at different schools. Judge the session on one thing: did the tutor name the specific loss and say what the next four sessions would cover?

If the answer was vague, you have spent an hour rather than a term's fees finding out. If it was specific, agree a block with a written target and a review point. Six weeks later, read the next marked paper for the same loss. If it has moved, continue; if not, change the plan or the tutor.

And if no specialist is free for a thin subject at the hour you need, you should be told that plainly. The honest options are a different slot with the right tutor, the right tutor over live video from another time zone, or a wait. A general science tutor in front of an 0606 candidate is not a match whatever it is called.

One last thing to agree up front: what happens if the match is wrong. A reasonable arrangement changes the tutor without an argument, because a mismatch between a student and a teacher is common and says nothing about either of them. A provider that treats a change as a complaint is a provider you will stay with too long.

process.description: The most recent marked assessment or mock, with the school name. That document shows which marks went and why. A report grade shows that something is wrong without saying what, which is not enough for a tutor to be useful on.

process.description: Compare the next marked paper with the one you started from, looking for the named loss specifically. If it has shifted, continue. If it has not, the plan changes or the tutor does. Progress is read from school marks, not from how the sessions felt.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE syllabus code my child in Muwaileh is sitting?
faqs.answer: Email the school's exams officer and ask for the board, the code and the tier for each subject. Report cards say "Mathematics", which could be Cambridge 0580 at Core or Extended or Pearson 4MA1 at Foundation or Higher — four different exams with four different grade ceilings. Schools in this catchment enter both boards and sometimes split boards across subjects in one year group. Ask for the centre's own timetable in the same email, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones.

faqs.question: Does a Cambridge Core entry limit what my child can do afterwards?
faqs.answer: It caps the grade at C. That clears the Ministry of Education equivalency floor on the British track, which asks for five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, so it does not block a UAE university application outright. It usually does fall short of what AS and A Level courses want in mathematics and the sciences, where an A or B at Extended is the normal expectation. If the entry has not yet been made, a tier conversation with marked evidence is worth having.

faqs.question: Do you send an IGCSE tutor to homes in Muwaileh?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Sharjah or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Muwaileh students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper on a shared screen. The trade is explicit: you lose a person in the room and gain a tutor chosen for the syllabus code rather than for willingness to drive out past University City at six o'clock.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE actually different?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the differences change tutoring. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended with Paper 4 heavily weighted; Pearson 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher with two papers of equal weight, so a pacing error on the first paper cannot be recovered. Cambridge science centres choose between a practical paper and an alternative-to-practical written paper. English set texts and anthologies differ entirely, so a year of literature revision does not transfer between boards.

faqs.question: How is science practical work assessed if my child studies with an online tutor?
faqs.answer: The assessment is set by the board and the centre, not by the tutor. A Cambridge centre uses either a timetabled practical paper or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and that choice decides what preparation is needed: apparatus handling and observation recording for one, interpreting someone else's experiment on paper for the other. Online tutoring prepares both — the second particularly well, since it is a written skill. Ask your head of science which route the centre uses.

faqs.question: When are the IGCSE exam series for students in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only and is not available to UAE candidates, so any plan built around it is wrong for your child's country. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with results in January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Work from the live timetable your exams officer issues.

faqs.question: How many past papers should my child actually do?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families expect, done properly. Three papers marked against the published scheme, with an error log naming the recurring loss, beats twenty papers skimmed. The log is the deliverable: unshown method on multi-mark questions, dropped units in titration arithmetic, mark-scheme vocabulary replaced by paraphrase, a command term misread. Once the loss is named, the work becomes specific. Papers worked through without marking against the scheme mostly rehearse the same error.

faqs.question: How much cheaper is starting IGCSE support in Year 10 than in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and the arithmetic is not close. A content gap that takes six sessions in Year 10 takes around fifteen in the spring of Year 11, because the student is then revising seven or eight other subjects in the same evenings. Year 10 is also the only point at which a tier conversation is still live, and a tier change supported by marked work is worth more than any amount of Year 11 remediation. Early tutoring is cheaper by a factor, not a margin.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 already. What is the best use of the time left?
faqs.answer: Prioritise ruthlessly: two subjects at most, chosen by where marks are recoverable rather than where the grades look worst. Work from marked papers instead of the syllabus, because a full re-teach is not available and pretending otherwise burns the term. Keep an error log across papers and attack the recurring loss specifically. In the last eight weeks switch to full papers sat to time. Accept that some subjects will be managed rather than improved.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 taught to the syllabus's own pseudocode conventions rather than Python, Accounting 0452, and IGCSE Arabic as a first language. Beyond subject, timing creates its own scarcity: in the eight weeks before a series almost every specialist slot is taken, so a tutor free in October may not be free in April at six o'clock Gulf Standard Time. Families who book the exam-season hour in the autumn keep it.

faqs.question: Should a Muwaileh tutor be handing us mark schemes to download?
faqs.answer: They should not host a download library of them. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and are available free through your school and the boards' own channels. The legitimate approach is working through official material in session, with the source named, so you can find it yourself. A service distributing board material is handling someone else's copyright, and for unreleased material it is worse than that.

faqs.question: Does a tutor in Sharjah need a MoHRE permit, and can I check?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you can ask. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school and government-sector teachers, private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts is published. Because the permit is free, there is no innocent reason for a working tutor to be without it.

faqs.question: What should a tutor do about Arabic alongside my child's IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Establish the stream first. KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines require separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibit combined classes because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Material for one route does not serve the other. Work goes through the school's own material, since for mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited.

faqs.question: How will I know in six weeks whether this is working?
faqs.answer: By reading marked work for the loss you named at the start. Before the block begins, get the failure mode in writing — unshown method, dropped units, mark-scheme vocabulary missing, a command term misread. Six weeks later, look at the next marked paper or school assessment for that specific loss. If it has shifted, the match is right. If it has not, change the plan or the tutor. Sessions that feel useful while the same marks disappear is the costliest pattern in this market.
