intro.heading: Counting weeks, not shopping for a tutor
paragraphs: Nobody searches for an IGCSE tutor in a calm week. The search happens after a mock result, after a parents' evening, or in the fortnight when the exam timetable finally becomes real. So the first useful thing a page like this can do is replace vague urgency with dates, because the dates decide what help is worth buying.

Here is the part most families in Sharjah Garden City have never been told clearly. The deadline that binds your child is not the board's; it is the school's internal entry deadline, which falls months before the papers and is usually announced once, in an email, during a busy term. Changing a tier from Core to Extended, adding a subject or switching a board all have to happen before that internal date. After it, the options narrow to the November series.

The second thing worth knowing is which series your child can actually sit. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two open to UAE candidates - the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. If you have read a page telling Sharjah parents to prepare for a February sitting, it was written for a different country.

Sharjah Garden City adds a practical constraint to all of this. The district sits on the emirate's southern corridor, away from the older tutoring belt around Al Majaz and Al Qasimia, so the supply of tutors willing to drive out here is thin and weighted towards generalists. In the ten weeks before a series, a late or cancelled session is expensive in a way it is not in September. Online lessons start when the student is at the desk, which is the unglamorous reason the format holds up better under deadline pressure.

There is one more reason to work from dates rather than from a weekly habit. Tutoring sold as an open-ended hour has no way of proving its worth, so it gets renewed out of hope. A block with a start, an end and a marked script at each end can be judged. If the second script is no better than the first, something in the arrangement is wrong, and a family deserves to know that in six weeks rather than in August. We review at session six for exactly that reason, and we would rather recommend stopping than let a block roll quietly into another term.

What follows is the whole calendar laid out: the year counted backwards from a written series, the ten-week shape that works, how Year 10 differs from Year 11 in what tutoring buys, when the Core or Extended decision closes, how a November resit decision should be made, what the market charges by period rather than by hour, and how Ramadan and the holidays change the arithmetic.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-sharjah-gard.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by where it sits in the calendar - when the content lands, when the marks are won - because that is what a family counting weeks needs to know.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Content finishes earlier than in most subjects, so the final term is pure technique. Bounds, rearrangement under time pressure and multi-step problems abandoned early are the standard losses, and all three respond to timed papers with immediate marking rather than to topic revision.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Edexcel
subjects.description: Electricity usually arrives in Year 11 and is the single most common reason a predicted grade slips late. The practical-style paper rewards students who can narrate a method aloud, a skill that can be taught deliberately in three or four sessions near the end of the course.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Organic chemistry tends to be taught last, which means it is the least rehearsed topic in the examination. Mole ratios and electrolysis products are the other two persistent losses, and the extended paper marks the precision of an observation strictly.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content accumulates across two years, so students who revise only before school tests arrive at the final term with a great deal unconsolidated. Command words and data questions are where a late block of work moves marks fastest.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences in two grades, with less teaching time per strand. In a ten-week block the first job is triage: identify which strand is dragging the grade and work only on that, since there is not time to treat all three equally.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: The one subject where a late block is often transformative, because directed writing and reading analysis respond quickly to timed practice annotated against the mark scheme. Students lose marks by summarising when asked to analyse effect.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Formulaic enough to coach precisely: note-making, summary word limits and register shifts. The speaking component is a scheduled event rather than a written paper, so rehearsal has to be booked into the calendar.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (0450 / 0455)
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward structure: define, apply to the case, then evaluate with a judgement. Diagram accuracy in economics is a cheap, late-available source of marks that schools often leave to the student to sort out.

sections.heading: The deadline that binds your child, and the one that does not
paragraphs: Two different deadlines get confused in almost every conversation about IGCSE entries. The board publishes dates for final entries from centres. The school publishes an internal date, earlier, by which it needs decisions from families so it can meet the board's. A parent who plans around the board's date has already missed the one that matters.

This is not a trivial administrative point. The tier decision - Core or Extended at Cambridge, Foundation or Higher on an Edexcel paper - is made in that window, and the tier caps the grade. So does adding or dropping a subject. A family that gets a worrying mock result in the second term and decides to move a child to Extended may find the school's internal deadline has passed, and the only remaining route is a November entry.

So the first action after reading this page is an email to the school's exams officer asking for two things in writing: the internal deadline for entry changes, and confirmation of the board and code for each subject. Both are facts the school already holds. Having them changes a tutoring plan from guesswork into arithmetic, and it takes one message.

The third date worth having is the mock window, because mocks are the first honest timed evidence most candidates produce. A ten-week block that begins before the mocks is planned on school reports; one that begins after them is planned on a marked script. The script is a far better basis, which is an argument for starting the conversation early and the block itself at the right moment.
bullets: Ask for the school's internal entry-change deadline in writing

sections.heading: The written series counted backwards
paragraphs: Working backwards from a written series produces a shape that holds for any subject and either board. The final fortnight reviews known errors and nothing else. The eight weeks before that are timed papers with honest marking. The fortnight before those closes the two or three largest content gaps. Anything earlier is ordinary teaching, which is the school's job and is where a tutor should be supplementing rather than replacing.

The administrative milestones sit further back still. Entries are made by the school's centre months before the papers. Each Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and Cambridge states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. For Pearson, provisional timetables are published ahead of each series and can be revised, which is why the only sensible instruction is to use the live official timetable your school confirms.

Results come back on published dates and they are the one part of the calendar families usually get right. For Pearson, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while the November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026. That January return is the reason a November resit is a genuine option for a student applying to a sixth form or a university route with a later deadline - but it needs checking against the receiving institution, not assumed.
The table below is the version to keep. It names each milestone, who controls it, and what should already be true when it arrives.

sections.heading: What a ten-week block does, hour by hour
paragraphs: Ten weeks at two sessions a week is about twenty hours. Spent badly, that is twenty hours of rereading notes with a sympathetic adult. Spent well, it is enough to change a grade in most written subjects, and the difference is almost entirely in the structure rather than in the tutor's brilliance.

The first four hours establish a baseline and close the largest gaps. That means a full past paper under timing, marked against the published mark scheme, and an honest conversation about what the script shows. Most scripts show a mixture: two topics genuinely not understood, a handful of command-word errors, and time lost on questions worth few marks. Those three problems have different fixes and should not be treated as one problem called revision.

The middle twelve hours are papers. One paper per session, marked between sessions, with the review targeted at the question types the error log identifies. Students resist this because it is uncomfortable, and it is also the only part of the process with a reliable relationship to marks. A tutor who lets a student talk through topics instead of writing under timing is making the hour pleasant at the student's expense.

The final four hours review the log and rehearse the mechanics: reading the paper, allocating minutes to marks, choosing which question to leave until last. Nothing new goes in. A block that is still introducing content in its final fortnight was planned badly, and the honest thing to say at that point is which topics are being left alone.

sections.heading: Year 10 against Year 11: where the same money does more
paragraphs: Families almost always buy tutoring in Year 11, and almost always wish they had bought some in Year 10. The reason is that the two years offer different things. In Year 10 there is time to teach content properly and to fix the underlying weaknesses - algebraic fluency, writing structure, graph work - that limit the grade in every subject. In Year 11 there is time to convert existing knowledge into marks, which is valuable but narrower.

The economics are worth seeing plainly. Twenty hours in Year 10 aimed at two or three structural weaknesses frequently removes the need for a panic block later. Twenty hours in the final term, after the content has been rushed, can only do so much: no tutor can reteach two years in ten weeks, and a tutor who says otherwise is selling the family the hours rather than the outcome.

That does not mean Year 11 support is wasted. For a candidate who knows the material and underperforms on paper, the late block is the single highest-value intervention available, because command-word confusion and timing problems are fast to fix. The question a parent should ask is which of the two students they have, and the answer is in the marked mock script rather than in the grade.
The table sets out what each year buys, so a family can decide deliberately rather than by panic.

One caveat for parents of younger children on this corridor. Years 7 to 9 carry no external papers, so nothing feels urgent and almost nobody buys support. Yet that is where the structural weaknesses form, and twenty hours there is worth more than forty hours in a final term. The constraint at that stage is motivation rather than money, which is why the sessions should be short, specific and finite.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, and the point at which the choice closes
paragraphs: At Cambridge, most subjects are tiered. Core covers less content and caps the grade available; Extended covers more and carries the full range. Pearson uses its own tiering in some subjects, notably Foundation and Higher in mathematics. The decision is made by the school, usually with a conversation involving the family, and it is reversible for longer than most parents realise - but not indefinitely.

The practical sequence is this. The school teaches towards a tier from early in the course. A mock result prompts a question about whether the tier is right. If a change is wanted, it has to be processed before the school's internal entry deadline, which is why that date matters so much. After it, the realistic alternative is entering the other tier in the November series.

How should the decision be made? Not on ambition and not on anxiety. A candidate should sit Extended if they can access the Extended-only topics and complete the harder paper within the time. Both of those are testable: two sessions with Extended past-paper questions will tell a specialist more than a term of classroom impressions. If the answer is no, Core with a secure top grade is a better outcome than Extended with a scraped one, and that is a legitimate choice rather than a failure.

What a tutor should never do is tell you the answer without evidence. Ask for the marked questions. A page cannot make this decision for a particular child, and neither can a tutor who has not seen them attempt the harder paper.

sections.heading: The November series: when a resit is the right call
paragraphs: A November entry is a real option, not a consolation. Cambridge runs the November series alongside June, and Pearson runs November alongside May/June, with results reaching students in January - the November 2025 Pearson cohort received theirs on 22 January 2026. For a candidate whose June grade blocks a sixth-form or university route, that January return can arrive in time, provided the receiving institution accepts it. Check that first; everything else depends on it.

The decision should be made from the script rather than from the grade. A candidate who missed a grade boundary by two marks because of one poorly answered structured question is a different case from one who was thirty marks short across all papers. The first needs a short, targeted block. The second needs to ask whether a resit in the same subject is the best use of the autumn at all.

Logistics come next. Entries for November are made through a centre, and a student who has left the school that entered them in June may need to enter as a private candidate through a registered centre, with its own earlier deadlines and its own fee. This is the part families discover late and it can remove the option entirely, so the sequence is: confirm acceptance, confirm the entry route, then start work.

A resit block is usually six to eight weeks of papers rather than a reteaching course, because the content was covered once already. We start from the June script, identify the question types that cost the marks, and work through papers under timing until those types stop costing marks.

sections.heading: What the market charges, by period rather than by hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are easy to compare and hard to budget from. The question a family on this corridor actually faces is what a term costs, or what the whole Year 11 costs, because that is the commitment. So the figures below are arranged by period.

Market hourly bands first, since the period figures derive from them. Across published UAE rate cards, budget online tutoring starts around AED 45 an hour, a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed, and named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 and above. Published packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's Dubai estimates, read in October 2026, put a single weekly session at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at budget level and AED 600 to 1,200 with a qualified tutor.

What those numbers mean over a period is the useful part. A ten-week block at two sessions a week with a qualified online tutor is about twenty hours - in the region of AED 3,000 to 6,000 at market rates. A full Year 11 of weekly support in one subject is nearer thirty-five hours. Two subjects doubles it, which is the point at which families should be deliberate rather than hopeful about how many subjects really need paid support.

These are market figures published so you can judge any quote, including ours, against something. They are not an IB Gram price list. And the gap between the online and in-home bands is worth naming: on the southern corridor it is mostly a car, and a car does not know the mark scheme.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the long summer and the weeks families lose
paragraphs: Any plan written in this country has to survive Ramadan, and most tutoring plans pretend it is not there. School days shorten, afternoons are low-energy, and the productive hours move to late morning at the weekend or to after Iftar. For a Year 11 candidate with a June series ahead, losing three weeks to improvisation is a material loss. Writing the month into the plan in advance keeps the block intact, and an online slot can move by two hours without anybody renegotiating a drive.

The summer before Year 11 is the other underused window. Nothing is due, and three or four sessions can close the content gap that will otherwise surface in the final term - electricity in physics, organic chemistry, algebra under time pressure. Families on this corridor often travel for part of the break, and because lessons are delivered over video the slot follows the student rather than ending at the airport.

Mock season has its own trap. Many Sharjah schools hold mocks earlier than parents expect, which means a January enquiry is frequently already inside the ten-week window for a June series. That is not a disaster, but it changes the plan: there is no longer time for a leisurely content phase, and the first session should be a timed paper rather than an introduction.

Finally, a word on school dates generally. Private schools in Sharjah operate within a regulated framework - the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private schools in the emirate and, with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Your school's assessment calendar is therefore a documented thing, and asking for it in writing is an ordinary request rather than an imposition.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to a villa in Sharjah Garden City for IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: Tutors in the Sharjah market do travel to homes, at rates quoted between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour once the drive is absorbed. IB Gram does not: we run no home visits anywhere in the UAE, since that service exists only in India. On this southern corridor the online format is an advantage rather than a compromise, because the local pool of board-specific specialists is small. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and the free trial lesson lets you test the format at no cost.

faqs.question: Which entry deadline should a Sharjah parent actually diary?
faqs.answer: The school's internal one. The board publishes a final entries date for centres, but your school needs decisions earlier so it can meet that date, and the school's internal deadline is the one that constrains your choices. Changing from Core to Extended, adding a subject or switching a board all have to happen before it. Email the exams officer and ask for the internal deadline and the confirmed board and code for each subject in writing. Both are facts the school already holds, and having them turns planning into arithmetic.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE candidates in the UAE actually sit their papers?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February/March series is offered to India only, so any page telling Sharjah families to prepare for a February sitting is describing another country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November - the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Each Cambridge centre belongs to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, so use only the one your exams officer issues.

faqs.question: How long before the exams should a ten-week block start?
faqs.answer: Ten weeks out, which usually means starting the conversation twelve or thirteen weeks out so the first session lands on time. The block has a shape: roughly four hours closing the largest gaps, twelve hours of full timed papers marked between sessions, and four hours reviewing the error log with no new content. If you are inside eight weeks, the plan compresses rather than shortens each phase proportionally - the paper work is what gets protected, because it has the most reliable relationship to marks.

faqs.question: My child's mock was poor. Does that mean the tier is wrong?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. A mock tells you three separate things: which topics are missing, which errors are technique, and whether the paper was finished. Only the first points towards a tier problem. The test for Extended is whether the candidate can access the Extended-only topics and complete the harder paper in the time, and two sessions on Extended past-paper questions will answer that more reliably than a term of classroom impressions. If a change is wanted, it must go through the school before its internal entry deadline.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth it, and when would results arrive?
faqs.answer: It can be, and the sequence matters. First confirm that the receiving sixth form or university accepts a January result, because everything else depends on it - the November 2025 Pearson series results reached students on 22 January 2026. Then confirm the entry route with the school, or with a registered centre if your child has left, since private-candidate entry carries earlier deadlines. Then read the June script. A candidate two marks short needs a short targeted block; one thirty marks short should reconsider whether the same subject is the right use of the autumn.

faqs.question: How much does a ten-week IGCSE exam block cost in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: At market rates rather than ours: a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour across published UAE rate cards, so a twenty-hour block sits in the region of AED 3,000 to 6,000. The in-home equivalent, quoted between AED 180 and 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, reaches AED 3,600 to 10,000 for the same hours. Bestimate's Dubai estimates, read in October 2026, put a single weekly session at AED 600 to 1,200 a month with a qualified tutor. Ask us directly and start with the free trial.

faqs.question: Would Year 10 support have been better value than Year 11 support?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, and it is worth knowing for a younger sibling. Year 10 hours can fix the structural weaknesses that limit every subject - algebraic fluency, writing structure, graph work - because there is time to teach rather than to patch. Year 11 hours convert existing knowledge into marks, which is valuable but narrower: no tutor can reteach two years in ten weeks. If you have a Year 10 student now, twenty well-aimed hours this year often removes the need for a panic block next year.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the run-up to a June series?
faqs.answer: It moves the working hours rather than cancelling them. School days shorten, afternoons are low-energy, and most families shift sessions to after Iftar or to late morning at the weekend. For a Year 11 candidate, the risk is losing two or three weeks to improvisation at exactly the point the block should be dense with timed papers. Write the month into the plan before it starts. Because lessons are online, a slot can move by two hours without renegotiating anybody's drive, which is why the format holds up better here.

faqs.question: Do we need to know whether the school uses Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it takes one email to find out. The codes give it away: 0580, 0620 and 0625 are Cambridge, while 4MA1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 are Pearson Edexcel. The paper structures differ - Cambridge maths uses a tiered four-paper pattern, Edexcel two equally weighted papers - and question style differs enough that a tutor fluent in one board will give confident but misleading guidance about the other. Send us the code with your enquiry and the match is made on the right basis from the first session.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with assessed coursework close to a deadline?
faqs.answer: With the thinking and the feedback, yes; with the writing, never. A tutor can explain the criteria, question a plan, teach a skill the task needs, and explain why a paragraph does not answer the question asked. A tutor may not write, redraft or edit any part of assessed work, and IB Gram does not supply completed coursework. Operations selling finished assessments appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the malpractice consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Sharjah need a permit from anybody?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Since the permit costs nothing, asking a prospective tutor whether they hold it is entirely reasonable.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we actually pay for support in?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with. Twenty focused hours in the two subjects that are genuinely blocking a progression route usually outperform ten hours spread across four. Look at the mock scripts and ask which grades change the next decision: a sixth-form entry requirement, a subject choice, a university prerequisite. Support those. For the rest, school teaching plus timed past papers at home is often enough, and we will say so rather than encouraging a larger package than the evidence supports.

faqs.question: What if nobody is free for our subject in the weeks before the series?
faqs.answer: We tell you straight away. Demand concentrates in the eight to ten weeks before a series, and narrow requests - Additional Mathematics 0606, computer science, a specific board's business paper at a peak evening hour - sometimes have no specialist available. We will offer a different time with the right specialist, or a named date when one frees up. We will not put a generalist in the slot during a deadline block, because that is precisely the arrangement that costs a family the weeks they came to buy.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near Tilal City who actually knows the IGCSE syllabus?
paragraphs: Tilal City is a planned residential district on the Sharjah-Mleiha corridor, and most of its families moved in recently. That matters for tutoring in a way nobody writes about: the informal network a parent relies on in an older neighbourhood - the neighbour whose daughter used the same chemistry tutor, the WhatsApp group with three names in it - has not had time to form here. So the search starts cold, on Google, with the words 'IGCSE home tutor in Tilal City'.

The literal version of that search has a short answer. There are tutors who will drive out to the Tilal City villas. Most of them are generalists: a graduate who can cover maths across several year groups, a science teacher who knows biology well and physics approximately, somebody who learned the Indian or American curriculum and is now reading an IGCSE syllabus for the first time. A smaller number know one board and one subject to examination depth, and those people are almost never within a twenty-minute drive of any particular address. They are wherever they happen to live.

This is the part worth being blunt about. A Year 11 student who needs Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Paper 4 does not need a chemistry tutor in general. They need somebody who knows that the extended paper asks for ionic half-equations with state symbols, that the examiner wants the word 'anhydrous' rather than 'dry', and that a candidate loses the mark for describing a test for a gas without naming what the positive result looks like. Geography cannot supply that. Subject depth and postcode are unrelated variables, and treating them as the same thing is why so many families pay for a term and see nothing move.

IB Gram works the other way round. We match on the board, the syllabus code and the paper, then deliver the lesson over live video so the match is not limited by the Mleiha road at five o'clock. A Tilal City family gets the tutor who has taught 0620 Paper 4 for years, not the tutor who lives closest to Tilal City. Lessons are online, one to one, and scheduled around the school day rather than around traffic.

One more thing is worth saying before the detail. Nobody on this corridor should pay a premium rate for general revision. If a tutor cannot name, in the first session, the three topics that are costing your child the most marks, you are funding diagnosis rather than teaching, and diagnosis should take one marked paper and twenty minutes of a specialist's time.

What follows is the detail a parent needs to make that decision properly: what in-home tutoring actually costs in this part of Sharjah, five questions that reveal within two minutes whether a tutor knows the syllabus, where marks are genuinely lost in the subjects Sharjah candidates struggle with, how the Cambridge and Pearson exam routes work for a candidate in this emirate, what SPEA does and does not regulate, and the line a tutor must not cross with coursework.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE choices are made. Content is broad and assessment is internal, which is exactly why weakness hides here: a student can pass school tests on topic-by-topic recall and arrive in Year 10 unable to rearrange an equation or write a conclusion that refers to evidence. Algebraic fluency, unit handling and structured scientific writing are the three things worth fixing at this stage, because Year 10 assumes all three.

Families new to Tilal City are frequently surprised by the timetable load, and it is a reason evening tutoring slots here need to be short and specific rather than long and general.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: A two-year course assessed by terminal written papers, with Core and Extended tiers in most subjects. Core caps the available grade; Extended carries the harder paper and the full grade range. The decision between them is usually made in Year 10 on the basis of one set of mock results, and it is reversible for longer than most parents are told. Grades run 9 to 1 or A* to G depending on the subject's reporting scale.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah candidates are entered by their school as part of a Cambridge centre, and every centre sits in one of six administrative zones with its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam because the wrong zone timetable was used, so the only timetable worth reading is the one the school's exams officer issues.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other British-track route, with its own codes - 4MA1 for maths, 4PH1 for physics, 4CH1 for chemistry - and its own paper structures. Edexcel maths uses two equally weighted papers rather than a four-paper tiered pattern, and its Higher tier covers content a Cambridge Core candidate never sees. A tutor who has only taught Cambridge will mislead an Edexcel student about what the question style demands, which is why we ask for the code before the subject.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November each year. The November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from that November series reach students in January - the November 2025 series results landed with students on 22 January 2026. Always work from the live official timetable your school confirms rather than a date copied off a tutoring page.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most requested subject on this corridor. Marks go on algebraic manipulation under time pressure, on bounds and rounding, and on multi-step problems where candidates stop one operation early. Tutoring works best when it is paper-timed from the start rather than topic-by-topic revision that never meets a clock.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Mathematics or an IB higher level course. Calculus notation, radian work and the factor theorem are where the gap between a confident 0580 candidate and a comfortable 0606 candidate shows up, usually in the first term.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Edexcel
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and anything involving a graph gradient account for most lost marks. Candidates can recite definitions and still fail to extract a value from a distance-time graph. Practical-style questions on the alternative-to-practical paper reward students who have actually handled apparatus, so a tutor needs to narrate method, not just equations.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis products and organic reaction conditions are the recurring three. The extended paper wants precise language - state symbols, 'anhydrous', the observation rather than the conclusion - and candidates who write loosely lose marks they understood perfectly well.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: The content is memorisable, so the marks are lost in command words. 'Describe' and 'explain' are different instructions, and a candidate who answers both the same way caps at about half the available marks on long-answer questions. Transport in plants and genetics crosses need diagram practice, not reading.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into two grades. Students who chose it to lighten the load often discover the physics content is the same difficulty with less teaching time. Tutoring here is triage: find which of the three strands is dragging and work only on that.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the two reading passages decide the grade. Students lose marks by summarising when the question asks for analysis of effect, and by writing in an unvaried register across both papers. Timed writing with annotation of the mark scheme moves this subject faster than almost any other.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.levels: Reading and writing · with or without speaking endorsement
subjects.description: Common in Sharjah schools where English is the language of instruction but not the home language. The exercises are formulaic enough to be coached precisely: note-making, summary word counts, and the register shift between an email to a friend and a report for a head teacher.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward structure over content. A candidate who defines, applies to the case, then evaluates with a judgement outscores one who writes everything they know. Diagram accuracy in economics - axes labelled, shift arrows drawn - is a cheap source of marks that schools often leave to the student.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: Home to the Sharjah universities, and the source of most budget tutoring supply in this part of the emirate. University students may hold a private tuition work permit, and plenty are capable, but very few have taught a specific IGCSE paper to grade standard.

sections.heading: What a Tilal City parent is actually asking
paragraphs: The phrase typed into Google is 'IGCSE home tutor in Tilal City'. The question underneath it is almost never about geography. It is: can somebody competent sit with my child regularly, understand the course they are on, and tell me honestly whether the current grade is fixable. Proximity gets attached to that because, historically, regular meant physically present.

It is worth separating the two needs, because they pull in different directions. Regularity needs a slot that survives homework, Arabic lessons, football and a sibling's exams. Competence needs a person who has taught the exact paper. In Tilal City, a tutor who is physically close is more likely to be a generalist, because the specialist population is small and spread across the whole country. Insisting on both usually means quietly dropping the second one.

There is also the drive itself. A tutor travelling out to the Tilal City villas spends real time on the road, and that time is priced into the rate whether or not it appears as a separate line. The travel premium in the Sharjah market is substantial - and it buys travel. It does not buy a better understanding of Cambridge 0625 Paper 6 or Edexcel's two-paper maths structure.

So the honest answer to the search is this: there are people who will come to the villa, and there are people who know the syllabus to examination depth, and the overlap in this district is small. IB Gram chooses the second and removes the distance problem by teaching online, one to one, over live video. That is not a workaround dressed up as a benefit; it is the only way a family on the Mleiha road gets the tutor who actually teaches the paper.

sections.heading: Five questions that reveal whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Parents are rarely in a position to assess subject knowledge directly, and a confident manner is easy to mistake for expertise. These five questions do not require you to know any chemistry or maths. They require the tutor to say something only a person who has taught the paper can say.

Ask them in a trial lesson, or on the phone before one. A specialist answers in specifics and often corrects the premise of the question. A generalist answers in reassurance. The difference is audible within a minute, and it is a far better signal than years of experience, a degree subject or a photograph of a certificate.

The point of the exercise is not to catch anybody out. It is that IGCSE is a precisely specified qualification, and the person teaching it should be able to talk about it precisely. A tutor who cannot name the papers in the subject they are about to teach for a year is being asked to do a job they have not done before, and your child's Year 11 is the wrong place to find that out.

Two answers should end the conversation. The first is a promise about the grade: no tutor can know what a candidate will score, and anybody who offers a number is selling confidence rather than teaching. The second is an offer to handle any piece of assessed work on the student's behalf. Both appear in this market, and both are reasons to keep looking.

If you want a shortcut, ask for a marked paper. A specialist will happily mark a recent mock before the trial lesson and bring the annotated script to the conversation, because the script makes their case for them. Somebody who would rather talk about rapport than about question 17 is telling you which of the two they are better at.
bullets: Which board and which code is my child entered for, and how do you know?
How many papers are there in this subject, and what is each one worth?
What is the difference between Core and Extended in this subject specifically?
Name the three topics where candidates in this subject lose the most marks.
What will you do differently in the last six weeks before the series?

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs around Tilal City, and what each rate buys
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number that decides whether a family can sustain support to the end of Year 11. One session a week at the lower end of the qualified-tutor band lands in the region of AED 600 to 1,200 a month, by the monthly estimates in Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table read in October 2026. The same table puts a budget arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more.

Hourly bands behind those figures are reasonably consistent across published UAE rate cards. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, advertises from about AED 45 an hour. A qualified subject tutor teaching online sits roughly between AED 150 and 300. An in-home one-to-one visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed, and named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 and beyond. Published monthly packages seen in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

These are market figures, quoted so you can judge any quote you receive against them. They are not IB Gram's price list, and the gap between the in-home and online bands is the part worth staring at: it is largely the cost of a car on the Mleiha road. For a Tilal City address, that premium is at the high end, because the drive is longer than the one assumed in a rate quoted from Al Majaz.

Where the money gets wasted is predictable. Two hours a week of general revision with a generalist, in a subject where the student needed four focused hours on one topic, costs more and achieves less than the opposite. So does paying a premium rate for a tutor who starts every session recapping the previous one because nothing was written down. Ask what you are buying per hour, and ask what will be different in six weeks.

sections.heading: Online lessons against an in-home visit on the Mleiha corridor
paragraphs: The comparison is usually framed as convenience against effectiveness, which is the wrong axis. The real trade is between the size of the pool you can pick from and the comfort of a person in the room. Online widens the pool to every specialist a platform can reach; in-home narrows it to whoever will make the drive.

For a district like Tilal City, that narrowing is severe. A twenty-minute radius around the Mleiha road contains a fraction of the tutors a twenty-minute radius around Al Majaz does, and almost none of the single-paper specialists. The further out a family lives, the more online buys them - which inverts the intuition that distance from the city centre makes online a compromise.

The practical objections to online are worth answering directly rather than brushed aside. A fourteen-year-old does need a quiet room and a parent walking past occasionally; a shared screen with a writing tablet does need to be set up once; and a student who will not engage with an adult on a screen is a real case, which is what the free trial lesson is for. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE - that service exists only in India - so the trial is also how a family finds out quickly whether online suits this particular child.

What online adds, beyond reach, is a record. Every annotated paper, every worked solution and every error log sits in one place instead of in a notebook that was left at school. In the final weeks before a series, that archive is the difference between revising and revising the right things.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are genuinely lost in maths, physics and chemistry
paragraphs: A school report saying 'needs to revise more' is not a diagnosis. Marks in these three subjects are lost in identifiable, repeatable places, and a tutor who can name them in the first session is worth more than one who spends a month finding out. In maths, the recurring three are algebraic manipulation under time pressure, bounds and rounding, and multi-step problems abandoned one operation early. None of those is a knowledge gap; all three respond to timed practice with immediate marking.

In physics, electricity and anything requiring a gradient read off a graph dominate the lost marks. Candidates who can state Ohm's law still mishandle a parallel branch, and students who have drawn a line of best fit in class still read a value rather than calculating a gradient over a large interval. The alternative-to-practical paper punishes students who have never narrated a method aloud, which is a teachable skill and an unglamorous one.

In chemistry, the losses cluster in three places: mole calculations where the ratio is taken from the wrong species, electrolysis where the product at each electrode is guessed rather than reasoned, and organic conditions written approximately. The extended paper also marks language precisely. Writing 'it goes cloudy' instead of 'a white precipitate forms' costs the mark even when the student knows the chemistry, and that is a writing habit, not a content problem.

The practical consequence for tutoring in Tilal City is that the first session should produce a list, not a reassurance. Our tutors mark a diagnostic paper before the trial lesson where a family can supply one, so the trial is spent on evidence rather than introductions.
bullets: Maths: bounds, rearrangement under time pressure, multi-step problems stopped early
Physics: parallel circuits, gradients from graphs, narrating practical method

sections.heading: The exam route for a Sharjah candidate, from entry to result
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series. UAE candidates sit those two. The February/March series exists, but Cambridge offers it to India only, and a page that tells a Sharjah parent to prepare for a February sitting is giving them a date they cannot use. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

Entry happens months before the paper, and it happens through the school as part of its centre registration - not through the family. That is the single most important operational fact for a parent: the deadline that matters to you is the school's internal one, which is earlier than the board's, and it is usually communicated once, by email, in a busy term. If your child might move from Core to Extended, or add a subject, the conversation with the exams officer has to happen before that internal deadline, not after the mocks that prompted the idea.

Each Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version. Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used, so the only document to work from is the one your school's exams officer issues. For Pearson, the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from a November series reach students in January - the November 2025 cohort received theirs on 22 January 2026. June Pearson results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day.

Counted backwards from any series, the shape of a sensible year is stable: topic teaching finishes roughly ten weeks out, full timed papers start about eight weeks out, and the final fortnight is error-log work on the specific question types that keep costing marks. A tutoring plan that is still teaching new content four weeks before the paper has run out of road.

sections.heading: SPEA, your child's school report and the tutor permit nobody checks
paragraphs: Private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. SPEA regulates private schools in the emirate and, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone, and it is worth knowing because it means a Sharjah school's fee structure and subject offer have been through an approval process rather than set freely.

What a school inspection report gives you is a judgement on the school, not on your child's subject. A strong overall rating is compatible with a department that has lost two teachers mid-year, and a weaker rating is compatible with excellent chemistry teaching. Read the subject-level commentary if it exists, ask the head of department how many teachers have taught the current Year 11 cohort, and treat the headline band as context.

On the tutor side, there is a rule most families never hear about. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The application route is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, through its app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow for a parent in Tilal City. First, you may ask a prospective in-home tutor whether they hold the permit; it costs them nothing to have, so a shrug is informative. Second, be wary of any offer to arrange tuition with your child's own class teacher. Abu Dhabi's regulator has published professional-ethics rules barring school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct pointing the same way. IB Gram is not described here as approved, licensed or accredited by any UAE authority - we are a tutor-matching platform, and that distinction is the point.

sections.heading: Coursework, feedback and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less coursework than it used to, but several subjects still have assessed components, and students on a British track in Sharjah often move on to A Level or an IB diploma where internally assessed work dominates. The boundary is the same across all of them, and it is simple to state: the work must be the student's own.

A tutor may teach the underlying skill, question a plan, point to a syllabus criterion, explain why a paragraph does not answer the question asked, and model an answer on a different question entirely. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit to completion any part of an assessed piece. IB Gram does not supply completed coursework, internal assessments, extended essays or any assessed writing. This is said plainly because the search results for these queries contain operations that sell exactly that, at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and a student who buys one risks a malpractice finding that no grade is worth.

There is a related boundary around materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards. We reference them and point to the official source, and your child's school is the proper route to the current version. A tutoring service that offers you a drive full of 'exclusive' board material is distributing somebody else's copyright, and in the case of unreleased material, exposing your child to a malpractice question.

Said positively: the useful thing a tutor does with assessed work is make the student better at producing it unaided, early enough that it matters. That means reading the criteria together in week one, not editing prose in the final week.

A Cambridge 0580 Extended candidate and an Edexcel 4MA1 Higher candidate need different paper strategies, and a tutor who has taught one will mislead the other about question style. faqs.question: Can I actually get an IGCSE home tutor to come to a villa in Tilal City?
faqs.answer: There are tutors in the Sharjah market who travel to homes, and in-home rates are quoted between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour once travel is absorbed. IB Gram is not one of them: we do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service we run only in India. For Tilal City families we deliver the same one-to-one teaching over live video, which lets us match your child to a tutor who has taught their specific paper rather than to whoever is willing to drive out along the Mleiha road at five o'clock.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor really knows the IGCSE syllabus my child is sitting?
faqs.answer: Ask which board and code the child is entered for, how many papers the subject has, what each paper is worth, and the three topics where candidates lose the most marks. Somebody who has taught the paper answers in specifics and often corrects your question. A generalist answers with reassurance about building confidence. You do not need subject knowledge to hear the difference, and two minutes of questions on the phone will tell you more than a CV, a degree title or a photograph of a certificate.

faqs.question: Why are there so few IGCSE specialists living near Tilal City?
faqs.answer: Tilal City is a newer residential district on the Sharjah-Mleiha corridor rather than part of the older tutoring belt around Al Majaz and Al Qasimia. Specialist tutors, the kind who have taught one subject and one board to examination depth for years, are a small population spread across the whole country. They cluster where they happen to live, not where demand appears. That is why matching by distance produces generalists almost everywhere outside central Sharjah, and why teaching over video widens the choice so sharply for families here.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tutoring cost per month for a family in this part of Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Taking Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost estimates read in October 2026 as the market benchmark, one session a week lands around AED 240 to 600 a month at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 with a qualified subject tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published packages in the market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures for comparison, not IB Gram's price list; ask us directly and start with the free trial.

faqs.question: Is my child sitting Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, and does it change who should teach them?
faqs.answer: It changes a great deal. The statement of entry or the school's exam information will carry a code: 0580 and 0620 are Cambridge, 4MA1 and 4CH1 are Pearson Edexcel. Cambridge maths uses a tiered four-paper pattern; Edexcel uses two equally weighted papers with its own question style. A tutor fluent in one board will give confident but wrong guidance about the other's papers. Send us the code and we match to it. If you cannot find it, the school's exams officer can confirm it in a sentence.

faqs.question: When do UAE students sit their IGCSE exams, and when are the results out?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For Pearson, the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from a November series reach students in January - the November 2025 cohort had theirs on 22 January 2026. Work from the timetable your school's exams officer issues, because each Cambridge centre sits in one of six zones with its own version.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10 on Core maths. Can they still move to Extended?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and for longer than most families are told, because the entry is made by the school's centre months after the course starts. The decision belongs to the school, so the conversation to have is with the head of maths and the exams officer, before the school's internal entry deadline rather than after the mocks that prompted the thought. What matters in the meantime is whether the student can handle the Extended-only topics. A tutor can test that in two sessions with past-paper questions and give you an evidenced opinion rather than a hopeful one.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 student in Sharjah usually need?
faqs.answer: One session a week per subject is the common starting point, and it is enough when the student does the work between lessons. Two becomes sensible in the final eight to ten weeks before a series, when the work shifts to full timed papers that need marking and reviewing. More than two a week in one subject is rarely useful: the limiting factor becomes the student's independent practice, not teaching time. We review at six sessions and will say if the frequency should drop as well as rise.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Sharjah need a permit, and can I ask to see it?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because the permit costs nothing, there is no good reason for a working tutor not to hold it, and asking is entirely reasonable.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my child with assessed coursework or an internal assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor will teach the skills, question the plan, explain a criterion, show why a paragraph misses the question, and model answers on different tasks. A tutor will not write, redraft or edit any part of assessed work to completion, and IB Gram does not supply completed coursework, internal assessments or extended essays. Operations selling finished assessments appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams; a student who uses one risks a malpractice finding. The useful help is early help with the criteria, not editing in the final week.

faqs.question: What does SPEA do, and does it regulate tutoring as well as schools?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private schools in the emirate, and along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge it approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. So your child's school fees and subject offer have been through an approval process. Private tutoring is a separate matter, governed federally through the MoHRE private tuition work permit. IB Gram holds no approval, licence or accreditation from SPEA or any other UAE authority, and any tutoring service claiming one should be asked to produce the permit number.

faqs.question: Can lessons be scheduled around the school run and Ramadan timings?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where online scheduling earns its place for a family on the Mleiha corridor. A slot can start as soon as your child is home rather than after a tutor's own commute, and it can move for a late school bus without losing the lesson. During Ramadan, families commonly shift sessions to after Iftar or to late morning at weekends, and shortened school days change what a weekday evening can realistically hold. Tell us the pattern you need and we schedule in Gulf Standard Time around it.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks until the papers. Is it too late to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is short but usable, provided the work changes shape. There is no time to reteach a two-year course, so the sessions should be full timed papers, marked against the published mark scheme, with an error log by question type driving what gets reviewed. That approach regularly recovers marks lost to command-word confusion, time management and presentation rather than to missing knowledge. What eight weeks cannot do is replace a year of content, and a tutor who tells you otherwise is selling you something.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Sharjah families ask for most, and which are hardest to staff?
faqs.answer: Maths, physics and chemistry at Extended or Higher level account for most requests from this part of Sharjah, followed by English first language and biology. The harder requests to fill are the narrow ones: Additional Mathematics 0606, computer science, and a specific board's business studies paper at an awkward hour. When no specialist is free at the time you need, we say so rather than putting a generalist in the slot. A clear no is more useful than a match that wastes a term.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-tilal-city.closingHeading: Start with the code, then the trial lesson
sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-tilal-city.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, take the habit of leading with the syllabus code. 'Year 11 maths' gets you a generalist; '0580 Extended, Paper 4 is the weak one, mocks in January' gets you somebody who has taught that paper and can tell you in one session what is recoverable. intro.heading: Two questions to answer before you pay for a single IGCSE hour
paragraphs: University City sits on Sharjah's eastern edge around the University of Sharjah and the American University of Sharjah, with Muwaileh next door and Al Zahia, Aljada and Al Rahmaniya within a short drive. The children of these households are schooled across a wide spread of districts and a wider spread of licences, and the practical result is that two Year 11 students living in the same building can be sitting different qualifications in the same subject. That is the first thing a tutoring plan has to establish.

Question one is the board. Cambridge IGCSE reports grades A* to G and uses syllabus numbers such as 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1 and uses codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. They are different qualifications with different papers and different mark schemes. Practising one board's past papers for the other board's examination is the most common way a Sharjah family wastes tutoring money, and it is entirely avoidable with one email to the school's exams officer.

Question two is the tier. Several Cambridge subjects are tiered: in Mathematics 0580 a Core candidate sits Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above a C, while an Extended candidate sits Papers 2 and 4 and can reach A*. Physics 0625 works the same way with a multiple-choice paper and a theory paper at each tier. Pearson's International GCSE is untiered in most subjects. A tutor who does not know which of these applies is teaching at the wrong difficulty, either wasting the student's time or demoralising them.

With those two answered, the rest is schedulable. Year 10 and Year 11 in a Sharjah school finish between about 2.30pm and 3.30pm, but a University City child bussed back from Muwaileh or across the Dubai boundary is not ready to work until considerably later. The slots that hold for a full term here are 5.30pm, 7pm and 8pm, plus weekend mornings. Choosing the slot from arrival time rather than dismissal time is the single most reliable way to make a tutoring plan last.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one tuition over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are offered only in India. For an IGCSE family in the campus belt the gain is specific: the tutor is matched to 0580 Extended or to 4PH1 rather than to a postcode, and no part of the hour is spent on the Maliha Road approach at the end of the school day. The phrase in the search is the phrase parents use, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a silent substitution: what is sold here is a live one-to-one lesson, not a visit, and the comparison later on this page sets out what each format costs and what it gives up.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-university-c.programmesIntro: Three stages matter around IGCSE in this part of Sharjah, and each needs a different kind of hour. What follows is what each stage assesses and the shape of support that works for it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Grades A* to G, with Core and Extended tiers in subjects including Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610. Sciences are completed with either Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical. Examinations run in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative timetable zones.
programmes.countryNote: In the University City belt, Cambridge entries dominate the British-curriculum schools and the tier question is where most tutoring decisions go wrong. A student sitting Core who is taught Extended content wastes the hour; a student on Extended who is drilled on Core questions never meets the demand of Paper 4. The entry list, not the textbook on the shelf, is the document that settles it.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Grades 9 to 1, untiered in most subjects, with codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry and 4EA1 for English Language A. International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and again in November, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run Pearson papers in some subjects and Cambridge in others, so a single student can be sitting both boards in the same series. That split is normal and manageable, but it makes the per-subject code list essential. For a tutor, 4MA1 and 0580 Extended are not interchangeable: the question styles, the formulae provided and the mark-scheme conventions all differ.

programmes.name: Year 9 and the pre-IGCSE foundation
programmes.description: The year before formal entry, when option choices are made and the algebra, scientific notation and extended-writing habits the IGCSE depends on are either secured or left behind. No external examination applies, which is exactly why it is the cheapest point at which to intervene.
programmes.countryNote: Families here often wait until the first Year 11 mock before asking for help, by which point a grade ceiling is already built in. An hour a fortnight in Year 9 aimed at algebraic manipulation and at writing to a command term costs a fraction of a Year 11 rescue, and it also informs the option choices that lead to the five subjects the Ministry of Education's equivalency rule counts.

programmes.name: What comes after IGCSE
programmes.description: Most students in this belt continue into A Levels or the IB Diploma. The transition is where IGCSE gaps surface: the algebraic fluency assumed in the first weeks of a Mathematics course, the practical write-up skills assumed in Diploma sciences, and the essay structure assumed in humanities.
programmes.countryNote: If the plan after Year 11 is the IB Diploma, the Mathematics route decision arrives quickly: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation. A student finishing 0580 Extended with secure algebra has both doors open. A student who scraped through on technique alone usually has one, and that narrowing happens before anybody has mentioned university.

sharjah/igcse-home-tutor-in-university-c.subjectsIntro: Each subject below names the codes a University City student is likely to be entered for, what the papers demand and the specific place marks are lost. Bring the entry list and the last marked paper and the first hour starts from evidence instead of from a conversation.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Core sits Papers 1 and 3 with a C ceiling; Extended sits Papers 2 and 4 and reaches A*. Pearson 4MA1 is untiered across two papers. Marks are lost on algebraic manipulation under time and on method marks thrown away by unshown working, both of which respond quickly to weekly timed practice.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Diploma Analysis and Approaches. Calculus and trigonometric identities are the recurring difficulty, and the paper punishes untidy working more than it punishes slow working.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Cambridge candidates sit a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper at their tier, and Paper 5 practical or Paper 6 alternative to practical. Electricity, moments and the graph-interpretation questions produce most of the requests for help in this part of Sharjah.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and the qualitative-analysis tests are reliable mark earners and reliably under-revised. Paper 6 candidates need deliberate practice at reading a method and identifying its weakness, which is a different skill from performing the experiment.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Long-answer marks depend on command terms and on correct units and scales in graph work. Transport in plants, enzymes and human physiology are where recall-based revision tends to fail against a six-mark question.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Science (Cambridge 0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Double or single award covering all three sciences in fewer papers. The content is narrower than separate sciences but the question style is identical, so tutoring works best on technique and on the topics the student's school covered quickly.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 or 0510, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: 0500 First Language and 0510 English as a Second Language are separate qualifications with separate mark schemes, and being entered for the wrong one is more common than parents expect. Directed-writing tasks reward form and audience before vocabulary.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455, 0450)
subjects.description: Both subjects reward accurate diagrams and a conclusion that answers the question set. Data-response questions are where students who have learned every definition still lose half the available marks, because the data is never used.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478, 0417)
subjects.description: 0478 requires algorithmic thinking and pseudocode discipline; 0417 is practical and assessed on efficient use of software for a documented task. Students strong at coding often lose marks on the written paper's trace tables and on precise terminology.

subjects.name: Arabic (Cambridge 0508 First Language, 0544 Foreign Language)
subjects.description: Relevant to most Sharjah students, since private schools teach Arabic alongside their licensed international curriculum. The two syllabuses differ sharply in demand, and a student placed in the wrong one spends two years either lost or unchallenged.

sections.heading: Confirming the board and the code before lesson one
paragraphs: The single most useful email a Sharjah parent can send asks the school's exams officer for three things in writing: the examination board for each subject, the syllabus code, and the tier where one applies. It takes a few minutes and it decides what every tutoring hour afterwards is worth. Families who skip it routinely pay for two or three sessions of work on the wrong paper style, which at market rates of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour is a real sum for nothing.

The reason it matters is that these are genuinely different qualifications rather than regional variants. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 both cover a Year 10 and 11 syllabus, but they present formulae differently, structure their papers differently and reward working differently. A student who has practised fifteen Cambridge Paper 4 questions walks into a Pearson paper and meets an unfamiliar layout at the worst possible moment.

A second check belongs in the same email: whether any subject is being sat in a November series rather than the main June one, and whether the school is entering the student as part of its own cohort. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That is a sentence worth repeating to a Year 11 student who has downloaded a timetable from the internet.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: Where Cambridge tiers a subject, the tier is a harder constraint than the teaching. In Mathematics 0580 a Core candidate sits Paper 1 and Paper 3 and cannot be awarded above grade C, whatever they write. An Extended candidate sits Paper 2 and Paper 4 and can reach A*, and the Extended papers contain content a Core student has never been taught. Physics 0625 follows the same structure, with a multiple-choice paper and a theory paper at each tier.

Entry decisions are made by the school, properly so, on the basis of classwork across Year 10. Where a family disagrees, the conversation to have is with the head of department in the first term of Year 11, not in the spring, because entries are filed with the exams officer months before the papers. A tutor can help by producing evidence rather than opinion: a marked Extended past paper under timed conditions says more than a parent's confidence.

The honest version of this conversation also includes the downside. A student moved to Extended who cannot cope with Paper 4 may finish with a lower grade than a secure Core C, and a student kept on Core who was capable of Extended loses access to A Level and Diploma courses that require a higher grade. The table lays the two side by side so the trade-off is visible before it is made. Two subjects deserve a particular check here. Mathematics and the sciences are where the tier most often decides a post-16 route, because A Level and Diploma courses in those areas carry grade prerequisites that a Core entry cannot reach. English and the humanities, where Cambridge does not tier, are a separate conversation entirely.

sections.heading: Paper 5 or Paper 6, and what an online science hour can really do
paragraphs: Cambridge science candidates complete their qualification with either Paper 5, a practical test taken in a laboratory, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, which is a written paper about experimental method, data and sources of error. Which one a student sits is on the entry list, and it changes what tutoring can usefully cover. A family searching for a tutor in the campus belt should establish it early.

For a Paper 6 candidate, almost all of the preparation is a desk exercise, and a video session with shared data sets is an efficient way to do it. The paper asks the student to read somebody else's method, identify the controlled variable, criticise the apparatus choice, plot data with sensible scales, calculate a gradient and comment on anomalies. Those are trainable skills with predictable question stems, and a term of weekly practice moves a grade.

For a Paper 5 candidate, the handling of apparatus belongs in the school laboratory and good tutoring says so plainly rather than pretending otherwise. What can be taught online is everything around the manipulation: planning, tabulating results before the experiment begins, significant figures, uncertainty, and the written conclusions that carry most of the marks. The distinction is worth making because it is the clearest example of where online delivery is equivalent and where it is not. One more practical point belongs with it. Science candidates in Sharjah frequently reach their final term having done the practical work but never having written about it under time, because school laboratory sessions end before the written component is practised. That gap is visible in a marked mock as a cluster of lost marks in the data questions, and it is among the quickest things a weekly hour can close.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the June series
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June series, with November available as a resit or staged route. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in those two series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so no Sharjah plan should reference it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why a tutoring page should point at the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can be revised.

The checkable past dates give a sense of the rhythm. The Pearson International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are the gaps a Year 11 family should plan around: entries filed months ahead, results arriving months after.

Working backwards produces a different spending plan from working forwards. A tutoring hour in the autumn term of Year 11 is worth more than two hours in the week before a paper, because content can still be rebuilt in October and cannot be rebuilt in May. The table sets out what should already be done at each point, and who sets each deadline, so a parent can see which items are the school's responsibility and which are the student's. Nothing in it should be acted on without the centre's confirmation, since entry deadlines and timetables belong to the school and the board rather than to a tutoring page.
