sections.heading: Command words, and why a correct answer can still score nothing
paragraphs: IGCSE questions are built on command words, and the command word is an instruction about the shape of the answer. State wants one specific thing. Describe wants features or steps without reasons. Explain wants reasons with a causal chain. Calculate wants working and a unit. Compare wants both sides addressed in the same sentence structure. Evaluate wants a judgement with support. A student who explains when the question said describe has spent time without gaining marks; a student who describes when asked to explain has capped the mark no matter how much they know.

Most students have never seen the command-word list for their own subject, and almost none have practised sorting questions by it. An effective early exercise takes a past paper and ignores the content entirely: for each question, name the command word and the mark allocation, and say in one line what shape the answer must take. Two rounds of that exercise and the category error largely disappears. It is the single cheapest intervention in the IGCSE year and it is almost never done at school, where time goes to content coverage.

The payoff compounds in the final weeks. Once a student reliably reads the command word and the tariff, every past paper they attempt becomes useful practice instead of a confidence exercise, because they can self-mark against the scheme and see what the examiner wanted. That shift, from being marked to being able to mark yourself, is what allows the last month of revision to run without a tutor present for every hour of it.
bullets: Describe wants features; explain wants reasons; the marks differ accordingly
Calculate always wants working and a unit, not only a value
Match the length of the answer to the mark allocation, not to the topic
A student who can self-mark against the scheme revises far more efficiently

sections.heading: Tiering: the entry decision that caps the grade before revision starts
paragraphs: In tiered Cambridge subjects, including Mathematics and the sciences, a candidate sits either the Core or the Extended papers, and the Core route carries a ceiling. On the A* to G scale a Core candidate can reach grade C at best; on the 9 to 1 scale the Core ceiling is grade 5. Confirm the exact ceiling in the current syllabus document for your child's series, since grading scales vary by subject and version. The decision is made by the school within the entry deadline, not by the student in the spring.

The consequence is worth facing early. If a sixth form requires a grade 6 in Mathematics for A Level study, or an IB school requires a 6 for Higher Level, a Core entry closes that route whatever happens in the exam. Families in Sharjah sometimes discover this after results, when the only remedy is a resit in a later series. The right time to ask is early in Year 10, when the school still has room to move a student between sets and tiers, and when an honest conversation about readiness is still useful.

Revision also differs between the tiers in a way that affects who to hire. Core revision is about securing the accessible marks reliably: definitions, standard methods, the question types that recur every series. Extended revision has to cover all of that and then handle the harder final questions that separate the top grades. A tutor who treats an Extended candidate as a Core candidate with extra homework will produce a solid grade 5 rather than the 7 the family was paying for, which is why the tier belongs in the first conversation rather than the fourth.
bullets: Core ceiling: grade C on A* to G, grade 5 on the 9 to 1 scale
The tier is set by the school within the board's entry deadline
Ask in Year 10, when sets and tiers can still change
Core and Extended revision are different jobs, not different volumes

sections.heading: SPEA, and what emirate-level approval means for a Sharjah candidate
paragraphs: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and its remit covers more than inspection: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A school's curriculum offer here is therefore a matter of regulatory record. What SPEA does not do is set the IGCSE syllabus or the exam timetable, both of which come from Cambridge International or Pearson, so a family tracking deadlines needs to look in two places rather than one.

Sharjah families frequently have children at schools in another emirate, which makes the national regulator map practically useful. Dubai private schools sit under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under the Department of Education and Knowledge, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. The regulator that governs term dates, inspection reports and complaints is the one where the school sits, not where the family lives.

On private tutoring itself, the UAE position is a permit rather than an accreditation. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no SPEA, KHDA or Ministry endorsement and claims none; the regulators are described so that a family can check them directly.
bullets: SPEA approves curricula, fees and assessment methods in Sharjah
The syllabus and timetable come from Cambridge or Pearson, not the emirate

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE programme
paragraphs: A Sharjah IGCSE student is rarely sitting only examined subjects. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. That requirement is the reason a Year 11 timetable in the UAE is fuller than the same year group's in the UK, and any revision plan that ignores it is planning around time the student does not have.

How the requirement is implemented in detail is set by each emirate's authority. The published Dubai guidance, issued by KHDA, is the most specific publicly available version and is useful as an illustration of what these requirements involve: it requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. It also specifies Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies.

Two further points from that Dubai guidance are worth knowing because they show the level of regulation involved: schools must ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Those specifics are Dubai's. For a Sharjah school, confirm the implementation with the school and SPEA. For planning purposes, the practical conclusion is the same: these subjects occupy real timetable and homework hours, and Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track Ministry of Education equivalency.

sections.heading: Year 10 or Year 11: when outside support actually pays
paragraphs: Timing changes what tuition can do. In Year 10 the useful work is foundational: closing a genuine gap in algebra or scientific writing, and getting the board and tier decision right while it can still be changed. Exam technique has little purchase in Year 10 because the student has not met most of the paper yet, and families who buy weekly sessions from September of Year 10 for a child tracking near target often spend two terms on reassurance.

In Year 11 the calculation inverts. By the mock window the student has seen enough of the course for technique work to pay immediately, and the marked mock script gives a tutor something concrete to target. The highest-return purchase in the IGCSE year is usually a short block straight after mocks in the one or two subjects where a required grade is within reach. That is also the point at which availability tightens, because every Year 11 family in the emirate reaches the same conclusion in the same fortnight.

The subjects to fund should be chosen by purpose rather than by weakness. Five accredited subjects need to clear grade E or 3 for British-track equivalency, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. Two or three subjects need a specific higher grade for sixth-form entry. The rest need a reasonable grade nobody will revisit. Fund the gaps of one or two grades against a real requirement, leave the secure subjects to the student's own revision, and say out loud which subject is not being rescued, because unspoken expectations cost more in morale than the grade is worth.

sections.heading: Grade boundaries, mock percentages and what a 62 per cent actually means
paragraphs: Parents often ask what grade a mock percentage corresponds to, and the honest answer is that it depends on the paper and the series. Grade boundaries are set after each series against the demand of that particular paper, so the same raw percentage can sit in different grades in different years. A school's mock boundaries are usually borrowed from a recent past series, which makes them indicative rather than authoritative. Treat a mock grade as a signal about the pattern of marks, not as a prediction.

What the percentage does tell you, read alongside the script, is where the ceiling currently sits. A student at 62 per cent who left two questions blank has a different ceiling from a student at 62 per cent who attempted everything and scored evenly. The first has marks sitting unclaimed on the page; the second needs content. That is why the script matters more than the number, and why any tutor who quotes a target grade without reading the script is guessing.

Do not expect published grade boundary tables to be supplied by a tutor. Boundaries, syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are published by Cambridge and Pearson and belong to them; the right practice is to reference and link the official pages rather than circulate copies. A tutor should be able to tell a student where the boundaries have typically sat for that paper and what that implies for how many marks are in reach, using the boards' own published material as the source.
bullets: Boundaries are set per series, so a percentage has no fixed grade
A mock grade is a signal about pattern, not a prediction

sections.heading: The east coast, and the subject your school cannot staff
paragraphs: Sharjah includes Kalba, Khor Fakkan and Dibba Al-Hisn on the east coast, where secondary provision is narrow and a school may have one teacher per science. A student wanting Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science, Accounting or a third science can find that nobody locally teaches it, and the usual options have all been expensive: take what is offered, travel, board nearer the west coast, or go without.

Online delivery changes part of that. A student in Khor Fakkan can work weekly with someone who teaches their exact syllabus code, which no travelling tutor can offer at that distance. What it does not change is the school-level provision: if the subject is not taught, tuition is carrying the whole course rather than supporting it, which needs substantially more hours, and the entry has to be arranged as a private candidate through a centre that accepts them. Those entries run to the centre's deadline rather than to the exam date, and not every centre offers every practical route in the sciences.

Availability should be disclosed rather than implied. In scarce subjects at popular hours, a slot can genuinely be unavailable, particularly in the weeks after mocks when demand across the UAE peaks at once. When that happens, the options are a different hour, a weekend slot, a tutor at a different experience tier, or waiting for a cancellation, and each gets named with its trade-off. No competitor page reviewed for this project discloses a coverage limit at all, which is itself a reason to be careful with pages promising instant matching in every subject.

process.description: Built around when your child actually gets home, including the Dubai school run from Al Nahda, with an agreed pattern for Ramadan and the weeks around mocks. Weekend mornings beat late weekday evenings for most Sharjah students in the spring.

process.title: Review against the next school assessment
process.description: The next internal test or mock is the checkpoint. If the same marks are still being lost, the options are a different tutor, a different plan or stopping, and all three stay on the table rather than being quietly dropped.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not subject name
whyPoints.description: A Cambridge 0580 candidate and a Pearson 4MA1 candidate need different past papers and different mark-scheme language. Matching on the code removes the most common source of wasted revision hours in this market, and it takes one question to get right.

whyPoints.title: Technique marks targeted first
whyPoints.description: Working, units, command words and timing are where most recoverable IGCSE marks sit, and they move within three or four sessions. Content teaching is the school's job; a session that starts with the script rather than the syllabus is the reason the hour pays.

whyPoints.title: The tier named before the plan
whyPoints.description: Core and Extended are different jobs with different ceilings, and a plan that does not name the tier can produce a competent grade 5 for a family who was paying for a 7. It is confirmed at the start rather than discovered in March.

whyPoints.title: Local load taken into account
whyPoints.description: A Sharjah Year 11 student carries Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside eight or nine examined subjects, plus a commute that for many ends after 5pm. Plans are built against that timetable rather than an idealised one.

whyPoints.description: Syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundaries are published by Cambridge and Pearson and are referenced from their own pages. Any provider circulating copies of them is taking a risk on your child's behalf that nobody asked for.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE papers does my child actually sit in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: That depends on the board, the subject and the tier, and only the school can confirm it. Cambridge subjects carry four-digit codes such as 0580 or 0625 and are often tiered Core and Extended with different papers; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look like 4MA1 or 4PH1, with Mathematics A tiered Foundation and Higher. Cambridge sciences also use either a practical test paper or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Ask the exams officer for a written list of subjects with codes, tiers and paper numbers, then check the current syllabus document on the board's own site.

faqs.question: Why do IGCSE students lose marks on questions they understand?
faqs.answer: Because mark schemes reward process, not just answers. The recurring losses are a calculation with no usable working, a value with no unit, a describe question answered as an explanation, an unlabelled graph axis, a paragraph written for a two-mark question, and blank questions at the end because the first half took too long. None of those are knowledge failures. They are habits, which is why they respond to three or four focused sessions of marked practice while the student's understanding of the subject has not changed at all.

faqs.question: What does the mark scheme mean by working shown?
faqs.answer: It means each stage of the reasoning is visible and legible. In a typical four-mark calculation, marks are available for stating the relationship, for substituting correctly, and for the final value with its unit. A student who writes only the right answer may score one mark of four; a student who makes an arithmetic slip at the end but shows every stage can score three. The practical habits are: relationship first, one step per line, units carried through, final answer stated separately and underlined. Those habits are worth a grade across a full paper.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Sharjah students most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and the three separate sciences, by a wide margin, followed by English First Language and the business-facing subjects. The reason is partly content volume and partly that these subjects carry the most technique-dependent marks: working in Mathematics, definitions and units in Physics, moles and qualitative analysis in Chemistry, technical terminology in Biology. Minority subjects such as Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 and Accounting 0452 come up less often but are harder to staff locally, particularly for families on the east coast of the emirate.

faqs.question: Does the tier my son is entered for limit his grade?
faqs.answer: In tiered Cambridge subjects, yes. A Core entry caps the grade at C on the A* to G scale and at 5 on the 9 to 1 scale, so if a sixth form requires a 6 for A Level study, Core closes that route regardless of how well he performs. Confirm the exact ceiling in the current syllabus document for his series, because scales vary by subject and version. The tier is set by the school within the board's entry deadline, so the conversation to have is early in Year 10, not in the spring of Year 11.

faqs.question: How much of the IGCSE grade comes from a single paper?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject and board, which is exactly why the weighting is worth looking up rather than assuming. In many subjects two papers carry the whole grade between them, so one weak paper can hold a student two grades below their understanding. That is the practical argument for revising the weakest paper rather than the weakest topic: a student who is strong on recall and poor on structured questions should spend their hours on structured questions. Check the weightings in the syllabus document for the series your child is entered in.

faqs.question: Does SPEA decide what my child's school teaches?
faqs.answer: To a greater extent than most parents assume. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. What it does not control is the IGCSE qualification itself: the syllabus, the series and the timetable come from Cambridge International or Pearson. If your child attends a school in another emirate, a different body applies, such as KHDA in Dubai or ADEK in Abu Dhabi, and that is the authority whose calendar and inspection reports are relevant.

faqs.question: Should we start IGCSE support in Year 10 or wait for Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the time for two specific things: getting the board and tier decision right while it can still change, and closing a genuine foundational gap, such as algebra or scientific writing, that two years of coursework will otherwise sit on top of. Exam technique has little traction in Year 10 because the student has not met most of the paper. For a child tracking near target, the better Year 10 purchase is often nothing, with the money held for a focused block after the Year 11 mocks, which is the highest-return point in the whole cycle.

faqs.question: What happens to Arabic and Islamic Education alongside IGCSE in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: They run alongside it. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations, and each emirate's authority implements that in its own way. Dubai's published guidance is the most detailed public version and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups in these subjects, with specified languages of instruction. Confirm Sharjah's implementation with your school. Note that Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track equivalency.

faqs.question: How do I compare a mock grade with the real grade boundaries?
faqs.answer: Carefully, because boundaries are set after each series against the demand of that specific paper. The same raw percentage can fall in different grades in different years, and a school's mock boundaries are usually borrowed from a recent past series, which makes them indicative rather than authoritative. Read the script instead of the number: a student at 62 per cent with two blank questions has unclaimed marks on the page, while a student at 62 per cent who attempted everything and scored evenly has a content gap. The pattern tells you what to buy; the percentage does not.

faqs.question: My daughter writes too much and still scores a 5, so what is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly the command word and the mark allocation. Writing a paragraph for a two-mark question spends time that the longer questions needed, and writing a description where the question said explain caps the mark however much content is there. The fix is mechanical: for each question, name the command word, note the marks available, and shape the answer to both. Two rounds of that exercise on a past paper, without touching the content, usually produces visible change, because her understanding was never the problem.

faqs.question: Can a tutor cover two IGCSE sciences for the same student?
faqs.answer: It is possible and often it is not ideal. Chemistry and Biology share habits of terminology and data handling, so one tutor across both can work. Physics sits further away in method and usually benefits from a specialist. The bigger constraint is the student rather than the tutor: two tutored subjects mean two sets of work between sessions on top of school and the mandatory UAE subjects, and in Year 11 that is usually the practical ceiling. If both sciences are genuinely at risk, sequence them rather than running them in parallel.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor do in the first three sessions?
faqs.answer: Session one should be the marked script: go through it question by question, name each category of lost mark, and set two or three practice questions on the most expensive category. Session two should check whether the habit transferred, in the student's own writing, and extend it. Session three should be a timed section marked live so the student sees the scheme applied to their own work. If the first three sessions are a tour of the syllabus instead, the hours are being spent on what the school already provides.

faqs.question: How many hours a week should a Year 11 student in Sharjah add?
faqs.answer: One or two in total, not per subject. A Year 11 student here carries eight to ten examined subjects plus Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, and many travel to school in another emirate, arriving home after 5pm. Adding three tutored hours produces unmarked work and a tired student. Fund one subject properly, or two if both genuinely gate the next step, and let the student's own revision carry the rest. After mocks, a short intensive block in one subject is usually better value than a thin spread across four.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson past papers interchangeable for revision?
faqs.answer: No, and treating them as interchangeable is the commonest avoidable error in IGCSE preparation. Question styles, mark-scheme wording, formula support and paper structures differ between the boards, and some content appears in one specification and not the other. Working through the wrong board's papers for six weeks produces a student well drilled for an exam they will not sit. A limited exception is using the other board's papers for extra practice on a shared topic late in revision, and even then the mark scheme to learn from is the one for your child's own board.

sharjah/igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Bring the script, the code and the tier
sharjah/igcse-tutor.closingBody: Three pieces of information turn an IGCSE plan from guesswork into arithmetic: the board and syllabus code for each subject, the tier your child is entered for, and the most recent marked mock script. With those, the recurring losses are visible within ten minutes and the number of hours worth buying is obvious. IB Gram matches Sharjah families with one-to-one tutors over live video, by code and tier, with a free trial lesson on the real paper before anything is paid. If the honest answer is a short block in one subject rather than a year in three, that is what you will be told.

intro.heading: Proximity answers a question nobody is really asking
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in Sharjah is not, on reflection, looking for the closest person. They are looking for the person most likely to move a grade, and distance has become a proxy for that because it is the only variable a map can show. The proxy is weak. It filters on a property that has nothing to do with teaching and ignores the two that decide everything: which board and tier your child sits, and whether the tutor teaches that specification often enough to know where its marks hide.

Here is how the filtering actually goes wrong. A Sharjah household in Al Qulayaah or Samnan searches, finds four tutors within fifteen minutes, and picks the one with the best reviews. Three of the four teach the subject in general terms. None of them asks for the syllabus code. The student is entered for Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher; the tutor has a cupboard of Cambridge 0580 Extended papers and uses them, because they are the papers he owns. Nothing visibly goes wrong for four months. Then the mock arrives.

Proximity also silently caps the pool in a way most families never see. A visiting tutor has to teach the right subject, know the right board, and be free in the ninety-minute window between your child getting home and losing the ability to concentrate. For Mathematics in central Sharjah, several people clear all three bars. For Additional Mathematics 0606, Accounting 0452 or Computer Science 0478, it is routinely nobody, and a parent concludes the subject is unteachable rather than that the search radius was the problem.

So this page takes the search seriously and then widens it. It sets out the five questions that distinguish a real IGCSE tutor from a directory entry, how to check the MoHRE private tuition work permit, what the Sharjah Private Education Authority does and does not regulate, which subjects have thin supply in this emirate, and what a local hour really costs once travel and cancellations are counted. All of it applies whether you hire locally or not.

Where IB Gram fits is simple enough to state in one line. Sessions for Sharjah families run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, matched on the code printed on the statement of entry rather than on a postcode. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service. If a tutor in the room is what you want, use the checks below on whoever you hire locally — they are more useful than a review score and nobody else on this page's search results will hand them to you. Read them before you call anyone, local or otherwise.

sharjah/igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Four situations account for almost every near-me search that arrives from a Sharjah address. The stage matters because it changes what a tutor can still influence: in Year 10 the tier is open, in the spring of Year 11 it is not, and after results day the conversation is about a different series entirely.

programmes.name: The two examined years
programmes.description: Years 10 and 11 end in externally marked papers, with Cambridge using four-digit codes and Pearson Edexcel using codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Several Cambridge subjects tier into Core and Extended, which sets both the paper set and the highest grade available. The decision point that matters most sits early: tiers and entries are submitted months before anyone sits anything, and the window in which tutoring can change what your child sits closes with the school's final entry deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah families frequently search in the spring of Year 11, which is the point at which the tier is already locked. Searching in Year 10 instead costs the same per hour and buys a decision that is still open. If you are reading this in February of Year 11, the first thing to establish is the school's entry deadline, because that single date governs what the next eight weeks can realistically achieve.

programmes.name: Mid-course transfer between schools or boards
programmes.description: Moving campus mid-course is common in this emirate, and it is the situation most likely to produce a hidden mismatch. A student can arrive at a new school halfway through Year 10 and find the board has changed, the tier has changed, or a subject is sequenced differently. Content overlap between boards is high, so nothing looks wrong for months. The question styles, mark schemes and paper structures differ enough that the first mock is where the gap becomes visible.
programmes.countryNote: Transfers across the Sharjah and Dubai boundary are routine, as are arrivals from other curricula. Ask the new school for a fresh statement of entry rather than assuming the old codes carried over, and give any tutor the new codes the day you have them. Replacing the stack of past papers being used is a ten-minute fix in October and a crisis in April.

programmes.name: Retaking a single subject
programmes.description: One grade short of a sixth-form requirement is the commonest reason families search at speed. Retakes are sat in the next available series, through the school where it will enter the candidate or through a registered exam centre as a private candidate. The academic work is narrow and well defined, which makes it one of the most efficient uses of tutoring money there is: a single paper, a known mark scheme, and a clear target.
programmes.countryNote: The timing trap is administrative. A November re-sit decision is effectively made in August, before the June results have been fully absorbed, because centre entry windows close early. Confirm the entry route first and the teaching plan second. Families who reverse that order arrive well prepared in October and discover the entry window shut in September.

programmes.name: AS Level, the year after
programmes.description: The destination that gives the IGCSE grades their meaning. AS Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology assume fluency with the Extended-tier content, and sixth-form entry is normally conditional on specific grades published per subject and per campus. The step up is real: students describe the first term of AS Mathematics as a different subject, which is largely why Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 exists as a bridge.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah students apply widely, including to sixth forms across the emirate boundary. Collect the published subject-by-subject entry requirements in Year 10 and work backwards from them. A tutor briefed on a target grade that exists on an admissions page is doing more useful work than one aiming at a number the household invented.

sharjah/igcse-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: The notes below say something a directory listing never will: how thin the local tutor pool tends to be for each subject, and what that means for a family searching by distance. Thin supply is a property of the subject, not a reflection on the student.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The one subject where a near-me search usually succeeds, because supply is wide across central Sharjah. The risk shifts to board mismatch instead: 0580 tiers as Core and Extended, 4MA1 as Foundation and Higher, and the past papers are not interchangeable. Ask for the code before anything else.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.levels: Extended entry only, A* to E
subjects.description: Calculus, matrices and harder trigonometry, sat alongside Extended 0580 as a bridge to A Level. There is no Core route. Local supply is genuinely thin, because teaching it weekly requires a tutor working at A Level standard. This is the clearest subject on the page where a distance filter returns nobody at all.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (Pearson Edexcel 4PM1)
subjects.description: The Pearson counterpart to Additional Mathematics, taken by students heading into demanding mathematics or engineering routes. Content and emphasis differ from 0606 despite the similar purpose, so a tutor comfortable with one is not automatically useful for the other. Supply is thinner still.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Reasonable local supply at Core level, noticeably thinner for Extended in exam term. The largest recoverable block of marks is in explanation questions, where candidates describe an observation when the command term asked for a mechanism. That is a teachable habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, balanced equations and organic naming decide the grade. Supply narrows sharply for Extended-tier work in the months before a series, which is exactly when demand peaks. Asking in October rather than March changes what is available far more than paying more does.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: Widely taught locally, so the near-me search often works. The quality variance is high, because content-heavy subjects attract tutors who revise alongside the student rather than teaching the assessment. Ask what the tutor does with a data question before agreeing anything.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Theory plus algorithms and programming. Pseudocode conventions and trace tables account for a disproportionate share of lost marks, and a tutor who codes professionally is not automatically a tutor who knows the board's pseudocode style. Local supply in this emirate is thin and unpredictable.

subjects.name: Accounting (Cambridge 0452)
subjects.description: Procedural and unforgiving: one misposted figure cascades through an entire question. Marks come from layout discipline as much as understanding. Very few tutors in any UAE emirate teach it regularly, which makes a distance-based search close to futile for this code.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Untiered, so the whole cohort sits the same papers. Diagram accuracy and command-term discipline separate grades; evaluate questions need a judgement, not a longer list. Supply is moderate locally and much better nationally, which is a straightforward argument for widening the radius.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508)
subjects.description: Sat by students who also carry the mandatory UAE Arabic requirement, which means two sets of expectations in one week. A tutor here works within the school's prescribed material rather than importing their own, because for the mandatory subjects additional content requires prior Ministry permission.

subjects.name: French (Cambridge 0520)
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking, with the speaking component administered by the centre. Local supply is reasonable but concentrated in Dubai rather than Sharjah, so near-me searches from the northern emirates often return a short list. Listening practice needs clean audio more than it needs proximity.

sharjah/igcse-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: What follows is the practical geography of a visiting tutor's evening in Sharjah: which districts a tutor can realistically cover back to back, and where the drive starts eating the lesson. It is the detail that decides whether a nearby tutor is actually available to you at the hour you need.

regions.name: Rolla
regions.note: Old central Sharjah, dense and heavily served, with several long-established schools within a few minutes. A tutor covering Rolla can fit two sessions in an evening, so earlier slots genuinely exist here. The constraint is parking and a quiet room rather than travel time.

regions.name: Al Qulayaah
regions.note: Central and close to the Rolla and Al Mujarrah school belt, with short journeys in most directions. Households here are the most likely in the emirate to find a local tutor who already covers the subject, which also makes it the place where the board-mismatch check matters most.

regions.name: Al Mujarrah
regions.note: Coastal central district with easy access to the Corniche road, which makes a tutor's route in from Dubai quicker than the map suggests. Evening slots from 5pm are feasible, assuming the student's own commute is short.

regions.name: Al Sharq
regions.note: Established eastern-central Sharjah, residential and compact. Journeys to the Muwaileh school belt are short enough that students are usually home by 4.30pm, which makes this one of the few districts where an early slot survives contact with reality.

regions.name: Samnan
regions.note: Inland of the central districts with mid-length school runs in several directions. A visiting tutor adds twenty to forty minutes of driving at each end of a session here, which is why local quotes sit at the upper end of the published range rather than the middle.

regions.name: Al Yarmook
regions.note: Residential and well connected to the inner ring, with families split between Sharjah-licensed campuses and Dubai schools. Households running two school calendars are common, and fixing each child's slot against their own timetable works better than a single family hour.

regions.name: Al Layyah
regions.note: Coastal and close to several campuses, including the creative-science group schools. Short journeys mean earlier starts, and siblings at the same campus can take back-to-back slots without the second child waiting through a drive.

regions.name: Mughaidir
regions.note: Inland residential Sharjah where in-home tutor supply drops noticeably. The subjects families here struggle to source locally are the same ones that are thin nationally, so widening the search beyond driving distance usually solves the problem outright.

schoolClusters.city: Central Sharjah: Rolla, Al Qasimia, Al Mujarrah and Al Layyah
schoolClusters.note: The oldest and densest school belt in the emirate, serving families who can reach several campuses within a short drive. Because the schools here run different boards and different tiers, two students on the same street can be sitting unrelated paper sets in the same subject.

schoolClusters.note: Students here travel further, which compresses the usable evening and shrinks the pool of visiting tutors willing to quote. These are the households for whom removing travel from the arrangement changes the economics most, not the teaching.

sections.heading: What a near-me search for an IGCSE tutor in Sharjah actually returns
paragraphs: The literal answer: a map with pins, several directory profiles, a few paid advertisements, and occasionally a tuition centre's landing page. What ranks in that list is decided by business listings, review counts and advertising budget. None of those inputs include the syllabus your child is entered for, how many times the tutor has taught it, or whether they hold the permit the UAE requires for paid private tutoring.

That is not a criticism of the search engine, which is answering the question it was asked. It is a warning about the question. Distance is a hard constraint for a visiting tutor and an irrelevance for a remote one, so a proximity search quietly restricts you to one delivery model before you have decided you want it. If you do want a tutor in the room, the list is a reasonable starting point and the checks later on this page will help you use it well.

There is also a visible quality problem in this particular market. Among the UAE tutoring pages examined for this project, review markup frequently contradicted itself: one page showed two different aggregate ratings in the same document, another claimed a rating from twenty reviews while elsewhere citing a student base in the thousands. Self-asserted ratings are not evidence, and in the UAE a commercial representation of that kind carries consumer-protection exposure as well as a structured-data penalty risk.

The practical move is to stop treating the list as a ranking and treat it as a longlist. Then apply the two filters that actually predict a good hour: the syllabus code, and five specific questions set out below. Those filters work identically on a tutor ten minutes away and a tutor who will never see your street, which is exactly why they are the right filters.
bullets: Map results rank on listings, reviews and ad spend, not on syllabus knowledge
A proximity search silently commits you to the visiting-tutor model
Self-asserted star ratings are not evidence; several in this market contradict themselves

sections.heading: The arithmetic of a local tutor pool, subject by subject
paragraphs: Every near-me search is really a question about supply, and supply varies enormously by subject. A parent looking for Mathematics in central Sharjah is choosing between several candidates. A parent looking for Accounting 0452 is often choosing between none and one, and will interpret that scarcity as bad luck rather than as the structural fact it is. Knowing which situation you are in before you start saves a fortnight of unanswered messages.

The table sets out the pattern. Thin supply clusters in two places: subjects that require the tutor to be working at A Level standard, such as Additional Mathematics 0606 and Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, and subjects that simply are not widely taught, such as Accounting 0452 and Computer Science 0478. The thickest supply sits in Mathematics and Biology, where the risk is not availability but variance in how well the assessment is understood.

Match time is the figure families most want and least often get told. It depends on the subject, the tier and the time of year, and it stretches in exam term because the same specialists are in demand everywhere at once. The honest version of that answer includes the possibility that nobody is free, which no competing page in this market discloses. Several conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking number instead.

What changes about the rate is the last column, and it is worth reading closely. A scarce subject commands a higher hourly figure in any format, so a family budgeting for 0606 at the price of 0580 is budgeting for a tutor who does not teach 0606. Published market rates in the UAE run from roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor to AED 200-450 and above for specialists, with one provider publishing AED 650 for a premium tier.

sections.heading: Five questions that separate a real IGCSE tutor from a listing
paragraphs: These five questions take four minutes and do more than an hour of reading reviews. They work on a tutor you found on a map, a tutor an agency proposed, and a tutor on this site. The point of each is to produce an answer that is checkable rather than agreeable, which is why the table includes what a weak answer sounds like. Weak answers are rarely dishonest; they are usually vague, and vagueness is the signal.

The first question carries the most weight by a long margin. A tutor who asks you for the syllabus code before quoting has already demonstrated the thing you are trying to find out. A tutor who says the content is the same across boards is technically almost right and practically wrong: the content overlaps, the question styles and mark schemes do not, and it is the question styles that produce the marks.

The permit question deserves to be asked without apology. The private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time, and the eligible categories cover school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Because it costs nothing and takes two days, not holding one is a choice. Individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

The fifth question — what a tutor will not do — is the one that separates a teacher from an essay service. The correct answer involves a clear line around work that must be the student's own: coursework is taught, reviewed and given feedback on, and no part of it is produced for the candidate. One operator in this market openly sells completed Internal Assessments. That is a malpractice trigger for the student, and a tutor who is hazy about the boundary is a risk rather than a bargain.

sections.heading: Driving radius, school-run timing and the slot that actually exists
paragraphs: A near-me search returns tutors who are near your home. What you need is a tutor who is free when your child is, and in Sharjah those are different sets. The binding constraint is almost never the tutor's address; it is the gap between when the student gets through the door and when they stop being able to think, which for a Year 11 candidate after a long commute is frequently under two hours.

This emirate has an unusual geography of commuting. A substantial number of Sharjah residents attend schools in Dubai, and the morning and evening crossings are long. A student leaving Al Nahda before six in the morning is not a candidate for a four o'clock session. A student in Al Sharq or Al Layyah, three minutes from a local campus, genuinely is. Those two households will get completely different answers from an identical search.

The table below works through the realistic earliest weekday start by district, and the last column prices the thing nobody itemises: what a visiting tutor adds to the evening before any teaching happens. Two drives of twenty-five minutes is fifty minutes of the household's evening spent on logistics, plus the tutor's willingness to accept the booking, which is where quotes from inland districts come from.

The useful conclusion is not that visiting tutors are bad. It is that the slot, not the tutor, should be chosen first. Decide the twenty-minute window in which your child is reliably capable of working, fix it weekly, and then find someone who fits it. Over video that search is national. With a visiting tutor it is a search for one person who happens to be free at 6.40pm on a Tuesday within fifteen minutes of Mughaidir, and that person may not exist.

sections.heading: Verifying the permit, and what SPEA does and does not regulate
paragraphs: Two different regulatory systems get confused in these searches, and separating them makes the verification simple. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate: it oversees the schools, and in Sharjah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a substantial remit, and it is entirely about institutions. It is not a licensing regime for the individual who comes to your home on a Tuesday.

The individual is covered federally. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation issues a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The service is listed as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' with a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

What a parent can do with that is ask, directly, whether the tutor holds one, and expect a tutor who does to answer without hesitation. What a parent should not do is accept a claim of regulator approval as a substitute. No tutoring provider is approved, accredited or endorsed by SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge simply by operating here. IB Gram holds no such approval and does not claim one; a page telling you otherwise is telling you something that is not true.

One further boundary is worth knowing. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules have been reported as barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is described in similar terms. Treat the detail as press-reported rather than quoted, and verify against the current policy. The safe rule everywhere, including Sharjah, is never to arrange paid lessons with your child's own classroom teacher.

sections.heading: Why proximity is a poor proxy for subject match
paragraphs: It is worth being specific about the mechanism, because the abstract version does not persuade anyone. Suppose a student in Al Yarmook is entered for Cambridge 0620 Extended and hires a tutor fifteen minutes away who teaches chemistry. The chemistry is fine. What the tutor does not have is the pattern recognition that comes from marking the same Extended Paper 4 twenty times: which mole question trips the cohort, where state symbols get dropped, how the organic naming marks are allocated.

That pattern recognition is the product. It is why a specialist can look at a marked script for ninety seconds and name the three habits costing the most marks, while a competent generalist works through the syllabus from the beginning and hopes to meet the problem on the way. The generalist is not doing anything wrong. They are simply solving a harder version of the problem with less information.

Proximity cannot select for it, because the number of people within fifteen minutes of any Sharjah address who teach one specific code weekly is small and, for several codes, zero. Widening the radius to the whole country raises that number by orders of magnitude. Nothing else about the arrangement changes: still one-to-one, still a fixed weekly hour, still the student's own papers on the screen.

The honest caveat is that a specialist is not automatically a better teacher. Rapport matters, particularly with a fifteen-year-old who has decided they are bad at a subject. That is what the free first lesson is for, and why a wrong match should be said out loud and changed rather than endured. The point of widening the pool is that it gives you both things to choose between, instead of forcing a trade you did not know you were making.

sections.heading: The tuition-centre option, and what group size does to an hour
paragraphs: Group classes at a Sharjah tuition centre are the other thing a near-me search surfaces, and they are a legitimate choice with a different cost structure. The family travels to the centre rather than the other way round, the per-student rate is lower, and some students work better with peers in the room. For broad content coverage in a subject a student is merely behind in, a small group can be perfectly adequate.

What a group cannot do is diagnose. In a class of four, the tutor divides attention and teaches to the middle, which means the specific habit costing your child four marks a paper never gets isolated. If the problem is that your child does not show method on calculator papers, that problem is invisible in a group and expensive to leave unaddressed. Group work addresses knowledge gaps; one-to-one addresses mark-conversion gaps, and most disappointing IGCSE results are the second kind.

An operational point about centres: a centre with premises and staff in the UAE is a different regulated entity from an individual tutor. In Dubai, for instance, a training institute requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, obtained through an initial approval and a sequence of licence steps, and renewed annually with the request submitted at least thirty days before expiry. A centre operating properly will be able to describe its own permissions. A centre that cannot is worth a second thought.

If you do use a centre, keep the group size question concrete. Ask how many students are in the class, not what the maximum is, and ask what happens to the fee if the group shrinks or grows mid-term. Published monthly package pricing in this market gives a sense of scale: around AED 799 a month has been advertised for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

sections.heading: What a near-me search cannot show you: safeguarding and your child's data
paragraphs: A map pin tells you nothing about what a provider does with information about your child, and tutoring arrangements collect a surprising amount of it: name, age, school, grades, marked work, sometimes a photograph, and in a video arrangement a minor's voice and image. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs this, and the practical standard a parent should expect is plain: what is collected, why, how long it is kept, and how to have it deleted.

A reasonable provider can answer those four questions in a paragraph. What should make you pause is a lead form asking for a child's school, grades and photograph with no stated purpose, which is a pattern this market has. If you cannot see why a piece of information is needed to arrange a lesson, ask, and treat an evasive answer as the answer. The same scrutiny applies to a local tutor collecting the same details on a messaging app.

Recording is the specific question video raises. Do not assume lessons are or are not recorded; ask, agree it explicitly, and establish who holds any file and for how long. IB Gram's own practice is that what is reliably kept from a session is the written output — the annotated script and the dated fix-list — which is more useful for revision than a recording and carries far less sensitivity. Anything beyond that should be a decision you made rather than a default you inherited.

The last safeguarding point is about where the conversation happens. Tutoring arrangements for a minor should run through the platform or through a parent, not as a private channel between an adult and a fifteen-year-old. That is a boring rule and it is the one that matters most. It applies identically to a tutor who lives on your street and a tutor who lives in another country, which is another way of saying that distance was never the safeguard anyone assumed it was.

sections.heading: What a local hour really costs once travel and cancellations are counted
paragraphs: Comparing an in-home rate with an online rate as two numbers per hour misses most of the difference. The table below puts tutoring alongside the other education costs a Sharjah family already carries, using published market figures with their source named, so the decision sits in context rather than in isolation. Every figure here is somebody else's published rate, not IB Gram's price list.

The row that changes minds is usually cancellation. A visiting tutor who cannot reschedule within the week because their route is full means a missed session is a lost session, and over a thirty-week year a handful of those is a meaningful share of the budget spent on nothing. Remote sessions reschedule more easily because there is no route to rearrange, which converts a sunk cost back into teaching.

A useful anchor for the wider budget: Dubai's regulator confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in that emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package. School costs being flat makes a tutoring decision a real choice rather than something absorbed into an unavoidable increase. It is also a reminder that the right comparison for a tutoring budget is the school fee, not the cinema.

One honest note on IB Gram's own pricing. No fixed per-hour figure is published on these pages, because the truthful number depends on subject, tier and weekly load, and a single invented figure would be less useful than none. What is fixed is that the first lesson is free and takes no card details, so the teaching can be judged before any money moves. Ask for a quote with the syllabus code in hand and you will get a specific answer rather than a range.

sections.heading: Getting started from a Sharjah address
paragraphs: The first step costs nothing and is not booking anything. Email the school and ask for the statement of entry: it lists, per subject, the board, the syllabus code and the tier. Then find the most recent marked script rather than the report card. With those two documents in hand, any tutor you speak to — local or remote — can give you a real opinion instead of a friendly one, and you can tell the difference.

The second step is to fix the slot before choosing the person. Decide the window in which your child is reliably able to work: after the commute, after food, before the point where nothing goes in. In Al Sharq that may be 4.30pm. In Al Nahda it is probably 6.30pm. Write it down and treat it as fixed, because a session that moves every week is a session that will quietly stop happening by half-term.

Then take the free first lesson. No card details are taken. It is a working session: the tutor teaches a real question from your child's own paper, usually one that lost marks, and sends a short written note afterwards saying what they saw and what they would change first. Judge the match on that note. A vague note tells you as much as a good one, and it tells you early enough to act.

The last thing to say is the thing no competing page in this market says. Some subject and tier combinations are thin, particularly Accounting 0452, Computer Science 0478 and Additional Mathematics 0606 in exam term. Where no specialist is free, IB Gram will tell you, with a realistic date, rather than substituting a generalist and letting you discover it in February. Every UAE session runs one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

process.title: Ask the school for the statement of entry
process.description: One email produces the board, syllabus code and tier for every subject. It is the single most useful document in this process and the one almost nobody requests before hiring. Send that line to any tutor you are considering and watch how they respond to it.

process.title: Decide the slot before the person
process.description: Work out the window in which your child can genuinely concentrate after the Sharjah commute, and treat it as fixed. A weekly slot that holds beats a better tutor at an hour that does not, because the second arrangement will quietly lapse by half-term.

process.title: Run the five questions
process.description: Board and code, the MoHRE permit, how week one is decided, what you receive after each session, and what the tutor will not do with coursework. Four minutes, and more predictive than any review score. Use them on local candidates too.

process.title: Take the free lesson and read the note
process.description: No card details. Your child works a real question from their own paper; you get a short written note on what the tutor saw and what they would change first. The note is the thing to judge, because vagueness in it will be vagueness in the teaching.

process.title: Review at six sessions against the scripts
process.description: Compare two marked papers rather than asking whether lessons feel better. If the same habit is still costing the same marks, the answer is a different plan or a different tutor, and saying so at week six costs far less than saying it in April.

whyPoints.title: The code is the filter, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher are different papers rewarding different habits. Matching on the code printed on the statement of entry removes the commonest silent failure in this market, which is a year of practice on the wrong question styles.

whyPoints.title: Thin subjects become available
whyPoints.description: Accounting 0452, Computer Science 0478 and Additional Mathematics 0606 frequently return nobody inside a driving radius. A national pool turns those from unteachable into bookable, without changing anything else about a weekly one-to-one hour.

whyPoints.title: The slot survives the commute
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time around when your child actually gets home, which in the border districts is after half past six. No drive has to be fitted into that evening, so the arrangement holds through the term instead of lapsing.

whyPoints.title: Checks you can run yourself
whyPoints.description: The permit question, the five screening questions and the data questions on this page work on any tutor, including ones IB Gram will never provide. They are published because a parent who can check is a better customer than one who has to trust.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: Where no code-matched specialist is free, you are given a date rather than a substitute. The month a family loses to a quietly mismatched tutor is more expensive than the lessons were, and that is the failure this policy exists to prevent.

faqs.question: Why does a near-me search for an IGCSE tutor in Sharjah return so few subject specialists?
faqs.answer: Because the search filters on distance, and distance is uncorrelated with teaching a specific syllabus code. The number of people within fifteen minutes of any Sharjah address who teach Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 or Accounting 0452 every week is small, and for some codes it is zero. Mathematics and Biology are widely taught, so a local search usually works for them. The pattern is structural rather than a reflection on where you live or on your child's subject choices. Widening the search to a national pool raises the number of genuine specialists by orders of magnitude while changing nothing else about a weekly one-to-one hour.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor from a local listing is allowed to charge for lessons?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Expect an immediate yes from anyone who does, because the permit is granted free of charge for two years and MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so disregard any page quoting a figure.

faqs.question: Does the Sharjah Private Education Authority license individual private tutors?
faqs.answer: No. SPEA regulates private education in the emirate, overseeing schools, and in Sharjah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is an institutional remit. The individual providing paid private lessons is covered federally instead, through the MoHRE private tuition work permit. The distinction matters because it tells you which question to ask of whom. It also means no tutoring provider can honestly describe itself as approved or accredited by SPEA. IB Gram holds no such approval and does not claim one; any page claiming regulator endorsement is claiming something that does not exist.

faqs.question: How long should it take to be matched with an IGCSE subject tutor?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry or Biology outside exam term, usually a few days. For a thin code such as Accounting 0452, Computer Science 0478 or Additional Mathematics 0606, longer, and in the weeks before a series it can be longer still because the same specialists are in demand everywhere at once. The answer you should insist on is a date rather than a reassurance. If nobody is free, that will be said plainly along with when it is likely to change, which is more useful than being matched quickly with someone who does not teach the code.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor who lives nearby better value than a specialist further away?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which problem you have. If your child has missed content in a widely taught subject, a competent local generalist at a lower rate is reasonable value and the proximity is a genuine convenience. If marks are leaking through unshown method, misread command terms or a tier that was set too low, you are buying pattern recognition, and that comes from teaching one specification repeatedly. Published market rates reflect this: qualified online subject tutors sit around AED 150-300 an hour while specialists run AED 200-450 and above. Read the marked script first and the price list second.

faqs.question: My daughter needs Accounting 0452 and nobody local teaches it. What now?
faqs.answer: This is the clearest case on the page for abandoning the distance filter. Accounting 0452 is taught by very few tutors in any emirate, which is why a Sharjah search returns nothing rather than something expensive. The subject itself is highly tutorable: it is procedural, the layout of financial statements carries marks on its own, and a single misposted figure cascades through a question in a way that is quick to diagnose and quick to drill. A code-matched specialist over live video solves the availability problem outright. Expect an upper-band rate, because scarcity is priced in by everyone in this market.

faqs.question: Do group classes at a Sharjah tuition centre work for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For content coverage, often yes, and the per-student rate is lower. For diagnosis, no. In a group of four the tutor teaches to the middle, so the specific habit costing your child four marks a paper never gets isolated. Group work closes knowledge gaps; one-to-one closes mark-conversion gaps, and most disappointing IGCSE results are the second kind. If you use a centre, ask how many students are actually in the class rather than the maximum, and what happens to the fee if the group changes size mid-term. Ask the centre to describe its own permissions too.

faqs.question: What information does a tutoring provider collect about my child, and can I have it deleted?
faqs.answer: You should expect a clear answer to four questions: what is collected, why, how long it is kept, and how to have it removed. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs this. Tutoring arrangements routinely gather a name, age, school, grades and marked work, and a video arrangement involves a minor's voice and image, so the standard matters. Treat a lead form asking for a child's school, grades and photograph without a stated purpose as a warning sign. Apply the same scrutiny to a local tutor collecting the same details over a messaging app.

faqs.question: How do I move my child's tutoring if we change schools mid-course?
faqs.answer: Ask the new school for a fresh statement of entry on the first week and send it to the tutor immediately. Do not assume the codes carried over: a transfer can change the board, the tier, or the sequence in which topics are taught, and content overlap between boards is high enough that nothing looks wrong for months. The first mock is usually where a mismatch surfaces, by which point a term of practice has been aimed at the wrong question styles. Swapping the stack of past papers is a ten-minute job in October and a genuine problem in April.

faqs.question: Can my son retake a single IGCSE subject in November?
faqs.answer: Usually, either through a school willing to enter him or through a registered exam centre as a private candidate. Cambridge runs June and November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May/June and November each year. The constraint is administrative rather than academic: centre entry windows close early, so a November decision is effectively taken in August before the previous results have been fully absorbed. Confirm the entry route and the component availability in writing first, then build the teaching plan. Retakes are among the most efficient tutoring purchases there are, because the target is one paper and one mark scheme.

faqs.question: We are in Rolla and my son gets home at seven. Is that too late for a lesson?
faqs.answer: No, and it is a common pattern across the border districts and the inland towns. A 7pm start works if the session is a hard 60 minutes with a clear agenda, because the useful window after a long commute is short and shrinks further if the hour drifts. What does not work is a loose ninety-minute session at that time. Over video the slot is simply booked for 7pm in Gulf Standard Time. With a visiting tutor you additionally need someone free at 7pm within a short drive of Rolla, which is a much smaller set of people than the search results suggest.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who taught at my child's school a better choice?
faqs.answer: They will know the scheme of work, which is genuinely useful, and they may know the teacher's marking habits. But there is a hard limit: never arrange paid tutoring with your child's own current classroom teacher. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules have been reported as barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is described in similar terms. Treat that detail as press-reported and verify it, but the safe rule applies everywhere including Sharjah. A former teacher at the school, not teaching your child, is a different and acceptable case.

faqs.question: What does a Sharjah tuition hour really cost once travel and cancellations are counted?
faqs.answer: More than the headline rate. Published in-home figures of AED 180-500 an hour already absorb the tutor's travel, and the household pays again in evening time: two twenty-five-minute drives is fifty minutes of logistics around a sixty-minute lesson. Cancellations are the bigger leak. A visiting tutor with a full route often cannot reschedule within the week, so a missed session is money spent on nothing, and a handful of those across a thirty-week year is significant. Remote sessions reschedule more easily because no route has to be rearranged, which converts a sunk cost back into teaching.

faqs.question: Should we start with one subject or three?
faqs.answer: One, almost always, and the exception is narrower than families expect. A single weekly slot leaves room for the homework that the tutoring generates, which is where the actual learning happens. Three subjects at once produces four or five tutoring hours a week on top of a full Sharjah school week, and it fails on fatigue rather than on teaching quality. Pick the subject where the marks are closest to moving, usually identifiable from the marked scripts rather than from which subject feels worst. Add a second after half a term if the first is holding. Reassess from scripts, not from impressions.

faqs.question: What should I do if the tutor is good but my child has stopped engaging?
faqs.answer: Say it out loud early and change the match. Rapport with a fifteen-year-old who has decided they are bad at a subject is not a secondary consideration; it is often the whole problem, and a technically excellent specialist who cannot reach your child is worth less than a merely good tutor who can. Re-matching is a routine process step rather than a complaint, and the earlier it happens the less of the term it costs. The thing not to do is persist politely until the exam, which is how families spend a full year's budget discovering something they suspected in week three.

sharjah/igcse-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Two documents, one fixed slot, then the free lesson
sharjah/igcse-tutor-near-me.closingBody: A near-me search is a reasonable place to start and a poor place to decide. Get the statement of entry so you know the board, code and tier. Find the most recent marked script so the first session diagnoses rather than introduces. Fix the weekly hour around when your child actually gets home in your district, and run the five questions on anyone you are considering, local or not. Then take the free first lesson, which takes no card details and ends in a written note you can judge. Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

None of them needs to be within driving distance of Kalba.

intro.heading: Why the east coast is a different tutoring market, and what follows from that
paragraphs: Kalba sits on the Gulf of Oman coast, part of the emirate of Sharjah but separated from the rest of it by the Hajar mountains. Fujairah city is close. Central Sharjah is well over a hundred kilometres away by road, and the journey takes considerably longer than the distance suggests because of the mountain route. The town has a corniche, the Khor Kalba mangrove reserve, a long-settled local population and a school provision that reflects its size rather than the emirate's.

That geography produces a tutoring market unlike anything on the western side. The number of people living within a reasonable drive of Kalba who specialise in, say, Chemistry at Higher Level, or who can supervise a Physics Internal Assessment against its criteria, is genuinely small. This is not a criticism of anyone; it is what population density does. A town of this size supports general teaching capacity well and specialist capacity thinly, in exactly the same way a small town anywhere does.

The consequence is that east-coast families have historically chosen between four imperfect options. Use whoever is locally available, regardless of specialism. Pay someone to drive over from Sharjah city or down from Fujairah, and accept that a meaningful share of the fee is fuel and road time. Send the child to board or to stay with relatives on the western side during term. Or do without, and hope the school's own provision covers it. Every one of those is a compromise, and three of them are expensive in money, time or both.

Delivery over live video removes the geography from the problem entirely, and it does so more decisively here than anywhere else in the emirate. A student in Kalba working with a Chemistry Higher Level specialist over a shared screen receives the same hour as a student in Al Majaz, from the same person, at the same time, with no travel in the arrangement on either side. That is not a marketing claim about technology; it is the arithmetic of a small specialist pool and a large national one.

What this page does, then, is work through the specifics the general pages skip. What distance actually does to an in-home rate out here. What the four local options cost and deliver. How exam entry works when the nearest centre is not in your town. What the school's own provision does and does not cover in a smaller cohort. And what SPEA's role is on the east coast, because the exclaves sit under the Sharjah authority rather than the federal Ministry despite their distance from the city. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.
