sharjah/maryam-island.tutorsIntro: The tutors below take most of our arriving-family enquiries: IGCSE Mathematics and the separate sciences for students joining mid-course, Diploma subjects for students arriving into DP1 from a different system, and Arabic as an additional language for children meeting the subject for the first time.

intro.heading: The arriving household on the Sharjah waterfront, and its first academic year
paragraphs: Maryam Island is a waterfront apartment development on the Al Khan side of Sharjah, the sort of address that fills with people who have been in the country for a short time. Apartment stock turns over faster than villa stock, waterfront stock turns over faster still, and the result is a resident mix weighted towards recent arrivals, young families and households whose employment brought them here within the last year or two. That demographic has an academic profile, and it is not the profile of a settled family.

A settled family's tutoring question is about a subject. An arriving family's question is about a translation. Their child has a report card from another system, a set of grades that may or may not mean what they appear to mean, and a new school that has placed them in a year group based on age rather than on what they have covered. The parent cannot tell whether a 68 per cent from the previous school corresponds to a comfortable position or a serious gap, and nor can the new teacher, who has met the student twice.

The second feature of arriving households is timing. Children do not move countries at the start of the academic year; they move when a contract starts. A student joining in January is entering an IGCSE course five or six months in, with content already covered and an exam entry already being planned. A student joining DP1 in November has missed the opening of six subjects simultaneously plus the start of the Extended Essay process. These are solvable situations, but they are solved by mapping, not by general catch-up.

The third feature is Arabic, and it arrives as a surprise more often than any other item on this page. UAE private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, which is why those subjects appear on a British or IB timetable. A child arriving with no Arabic at all meets a subject their classmates have studied for years. Nobody warns families about this before the move, and it is one of the most common first-term surprises on the waterfront.

Everything below is organised around those three features. There are subject-level transition maps from the commonest previous curricula, a first-term plan week by week, a cost-in-context table for a household budgeting its first year, and a documents list for the administrative side. Delivery is one-to-one over live video, which for an apartment household means a laptop and a corner of a room rather than a spare study. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.

sharjah/maryam-island.programmesIntro: For an arriving student, the question about each programme is not what it covers but what it assumes you have already done. That assumption is where the gap sits, and it differs sharply between programmes.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: A two-year course with content distributed across both years and an exam entry made months before the papers. Joining in the middle means arriving after specific topics have been taught and assessed. The practical difficulty is rarely the total volume; it is that the student is sitting end-of-unit tests on material covered before they arrived, which produces low marks that look like weakness rather than absence.
programmes.countryNote: An arriving family's first question should be which board and which syllabus code, taken from the new school's exam entry rather than the textbook. Cambridge and Pearson split the same subject into different papers with different tiering and practical arrangements. For Cambridge the sittings available here are the June series and the November series, and final entries for the June papers close months before the first paper - so a January arrival in Year 11 inherits a tier and a subject list the previous school has already committed to.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The Diploma assumes a particular kind of prior schooling: independent reading, extended written argument and self-managed deadlines. A student arriving from a system that assessed mainly by examination and recall meets all six subjects demanding something they have not practised, simultaneously, which is why DP1 arrivals feel harder than the subject content suggests.
programmes.countryNote: Mid-DP1 arrivals need the school's internal coursework deadline list on day one, because the Extended Essay and the first Internal Assessments are already in motion. We take that list from the student's own documents. Specific IB session and results dates are not restated here; confirm them with the school's IB coordinator against the IB's own published material.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, converted into a 1-7 grade through a school-set boundary table. For arriving students the shock is not the content but the assessment language: a child who has only ever been marked out of 100 for correctness now receives separate criterion scores for inquiry, communication and evaluation. Criterion literacy is learnable in a few sessions and is the fastest early win available.
programmes.countryNote: Children arriving into MYP from a national curriculum often read their first criterion report as a collapse in performance when it is a change in measurement. Explaining the conversion to both the student and the parent is usually the most useful thing anyone does in the first month on the waterfront.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers. For an arriving student the narrowness is an advantage, because catching up on three subjects is more tractable than on six. The disadvantage is depth: AS questions reward sustained analysis rather than recall, and a student arriving from a recall-based system can drop grades without having learned less than their classmates.
programmes.countryNote: For families thinking ahead to UAE universities, the published British-track equivalency route asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or above, or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae.

sharjah/maryam-island.subjectsIntro: The descriptions below are written for a student joining part-way through, so each one names what a late arrival has most likely missed rather than what the course contains overall.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Late arrivals most often missed transformations, the harder trigonometry and vectors, which tend to be taught early in Year 10 in many schedules. The gap is narrow and closes fast, but it affects every subsequent topic that assumes the algebra, so it is worth mapping before anything else.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: A student arriving from Cambridge material meets different question shapes in the later sections and a different paper split. The mathematics is the same; the pacing and presentation are not. A single full timed paper in the first fortnight is the quickest way to see what actually needs attention.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Arrivals often land after the electricity and electromagnetism unit, which is the heaviest in the course. The practical paper is a second, separate gap: students from systems without an assessed practical component have never written experimental method in mark-scheme language.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Reacting-mass and mole calculations are usually taught in the first year and assumed thereafter. A student who missed them can follow lessons on organic chemistry and still fail the questions, because the calculation underlies everything. This is the most common single gap in mid-course chemistry arrivals.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: The defined terminology is cumulative and the mark scheme rewards exact wording, so a student who learned the same biology in different words scores below their understanding. Rebuilding the vocabulary to the syllabus wording is unglamorous and quick.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A DP1 arrival has usually missed the opening work on functions and proof, which the rest of the course rests on. Students from systems where proof was never assessed find this the hardest adjustment, and it is worth addressing directly rather than hoping it resolves with exposure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology use is assessed, so a student arriving from a system that discouraged calculators has a specific, learnable gap in statistical functions and modelling tools. It is one of the fastest catch-ups in the Diploma because the content is not the obstacle.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: The Internal Assessment is normally introduced in DP1, so a mid-year arrival meets both the content gap and a coursework process already underway. We prioritise getting the investigation topic agreed, because a late start there costs more than a missed unit.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: Terminology volume plus data-handling technique, both cumulative. Arrivals who studied biology descriptively rather than quantitatively need graph and data-interpretation practice before content revision, because that is where the papers award marks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The hardest subject to join late, because the course works through set texts and a student cannot retroactively read and discuss what the class has analysed. Guided analysis of unseen texts, however, is a transferable skill and the sensible first focus for an arrival.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: For a child meeting Arabic for the first time, the useful early target is script, high-frequency vocabulary and the specific material the school is using, since schools must work within the Ministry's framework for these subjects. Short weekly sessions work better than long ones.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies and Moral Education
subjects.description: Content-light but unfamiliar, and taught in a different language of instruction depending on the student's stream. Arriving students usually need orientation rather than tutoring, and a few sessions settles it before it becomes a report-card issue.

sharjah/maryam-island.regionsIntro: Arriving families tend to look at several Sharjah neighbourhoods before choosing, and many move again within the emirate in the first two years. These are the areas that come up most alongside the waterfront developments.

regions.name: Al Khan
regions.note: The surrounding district, coastal and mixed between apartment towers and older villas. Many arriving households start here and it has the shortest run to the central Sharjah schools and to the Dubai boundary.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Central, apartment-dominated and popular with new arrivals for its proximity to everything. A high share of children here commute into Dubai schools, which affects both school choice and the evening timetable.

regions.name: Al Qasba and Al Taawun
regions.note: Dense towers close to the Dubai boundary, with a transient resident mix and strong demand for IGCSE support. Students here attend a wide spread of schools, so the syllabus code matters more than the neighbourhood.

regions.name: Al Nahda, Sharjah
regions.note: Right on the Dubai line and heavily built up, with the longest cross-border school commutes in the emirate. Arriving families often choose it precisely to keep a Dubai school option open.

regions.name: Aljada
regions.note: A newer mixed-use community with schooling on site, which appeals to arriving families who want to reduce the school run in their first year. Demand skews to primary and lower MYP.

regions.name: Al Zahia
regions.note: Townhouses and apartments with good access to the University City Road schools. A common second move for families who started in a central tower and want more space.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: The emirate's densest school cluster. Arriving families frequently end up with a school here regardless of where they live, which makes the afternoon return journey the main scheduling constraint.

schoolClusters.city: Central and coastal Sharjah schools
schoolClusters.note: These are the schools arriving waterfront families most often shortlist, because they are reachable from the Al Khan side without crossing the city. Curriculum menus and available year-group places change constantly, so ask the school directly about mid-year entry before assuming a place exists.
schools: Our Own English High School, Sharjah

schoolClusters.city: Muwaileh and University City schools
schoolClusters.note: The larger and more varied cluster, generally with more curriculum choice but a longer run from the waterfront. Families comparing a mid-year place here against a closer school should weigh the return journey, because it sets the earliest workable lesson time for the next two years.
schools: The American School of Creative Science, Sharjah

sharjah/maryam-island.modesIntro: Three formats cover the arriving household's first year. The first two are time-limited by design, because a transition is a project with an end rather than an ongoing commitment.

modes.title: Transition mapping block
modes.description: Four to six sessions whose only purpose is to establish, subject by subject, what the student has covered, what the new course assumed, and what the actual gap is. The output is a written map a parent can take to the new school, naming topics rather than impressions. Most families find the gap is narrower and more specific than feared, and that two subjects need work rather than six.

modes.title: Catch-up on one or two named subjects
modes.description: Weekly or twice-weekly sessions on the subjects the map identified, aimed at closing specific topics rather than re-teaching a course. Because the target is a list of named topics, progress is visible and the end point is defined. For most mid-course arrivals this runs for a term rather than a year, and it steps down to a single maintenance slot once the gaps close.

The target in year one is script, high-frequency vocabulary and classroom survival rather than fluency, which is a realistic goal and a measurable one.

sections.heading: What a Maryam Island tutoring search is usually asking for
paragraphs: Searches from waterfront addresses in Sharjah skew towards two phrases: a tutor for a specific subject, and help catching up. The second is the more honest description of what is wanted, and it is also the harder brief, because catching up is not a subject. Before any teaching happens, somebody has to establish what the student has actually covered and what the new course assumed they had, and those two lists are rarely compared by anyone.

The reason nobody compares them is that no single person holds both. The previous school knows what it taught and no longer has the student. The new school knows its own scheme of work and has met the student twice. The parent has a report card in a different format. The student, asked what they have covered, will reasonably say they do not know, because syllabus structure is not something students track. A tutor working across both is the only party positioned to build the comparison.

That is why the first product on this page is a map rather than a course. Four to six sessions working from the previous school's syllabus, the old reports and the new scheme of work produces a topic-level list of what is genuinely missing. In our experience that list is usually shorter and more specific than parents expect - two or three topics in two subjects rather than a general deficit - and it converts an anxious open-ended worry into a finite piece of work.

Because lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, an arriving family does not need to solve the logistics of a stranger visiting an apartment they have barely unpacked, and does not need a spare room. A laptop, a quiet corner and headphones is the whole requirement. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India, and we would rather state it here than let you discover it later.

sections.heading: The curriculum transition map, subject by subject
paragraphs: The table below sets out the commonest transitions into Sharjah schools and what each one actually requires. It is deliberately organised by where the student is coming from rather than by subject, because the gap depends almost entirely on the previous system's assessment style. A student arriving from a curriculum that tested recall needs technique; one arriving from a curriculum that tested extended writing needs content.

Read the fourth column carefully, because it is where families most often misjudge. The gap to close is usually not a list of topics; it is a mode of assessment. A student moving from a national curriculum into IGCSE frequently knows more content than their classmates and scores lower, because the questions ask for applied reasoning rather than reproduction. Teaching that student more content is the intuitive response and the wrong one.

The fifth column gives the support period we typically see, and it is shorter than families assume. Most transitions settle inside a term when they are mapped properly at the start. The transitions that take longer are the ones involving a new language of instruction, or a move into the Diploma from a system with no independent-research component, because those involve building a working habit rather than filling a gap.

One structural caution. A mid-year arrival into Year 11 or DP2 is a different proposition from one into Year 10 or DP1, because the exam entry and the coursework schedule are already fixed. Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series, with November as the resit route, and final entries are lodged by the centre months ahead of the June papers - the exact date comes from the statement of entry rather than from a summary. A January arrival therefore works inside entry decisions the previous school or the new one has already taken, and the useful move is to get a copy of the statement of entry in the first week rather than to assume anything can still be changed.

sections.heading: The first term, week by week
paragraphs: Arriving families usually try to solve everything in the first fortnight and then lose momentum. A sequenced first term works better, because the information needed to make good decisions does not exist on day one. The table below sets out the order we use, and the logic is simple: gather, map, target, then commit. Nothing irreversible should be bought in weeks one to three.

Weeks one and two are for watching. The student is adjusting socially as much as academically, and the first pieces of marked work are not yet reliable indicators of anything. What is worth doing in this window is administrative: getting the school's scheme of work, the syllabus codes from the exam entry, the internal coursework deadline list if the student is in the Diploma, and the previous school's final reports in a readable form.

Weeks three to six are the mapping window. By this point there is real marked work, the student has a view about which lessons are confusing, and a tutor can compare the two syllabuses meaningfully. This is where the four-to-six-session mapping block belongs. The output should be a short written document naming the topics, because a map in somebody's memory is not useful at the parent meeting in week eight.

From week seven onwards the work is targeted and measurable, and the quantity should fall rather than rise. A household that is still buying four sessions a week in March for a student who arrived in January has either misjudged the gap or never mapped it. The honest end state for most transitions is one weekly session in one subject, and then nothing.

sections.heading: Arabic, social studies and the subjects nobody mentioned before the move
paragraphs: Families relocating to the UAE research schools, fees and curricula thoroughly and almost never discover in advance that their child will study Arabic. The basis is federal: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. So a British or IB timetable in Sharjah carries those subjects alongside everything the board requires.

Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed account of how this works, and it is useful reading even for a Sharjah family because it shows the mechanics. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, permits schools to vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes. It also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited.

For an arriving child the practical consequence is that the stream matters more than the subject name. Arabic as a first language and Arabic as an additional language are different courses with different expectations, and a newly arrived non-Arabic speaker placed correctly in the additional-language stream has a manageable task. The content is also controlled: KHDA states that for these subjects the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry, is strictly prohibited, so support means working with the school's own material.

The sensible year-one target is not fluency. It is script, high-frequency vocabulary and the ability to follow the lesson, which is achievable with thirty to forty-five minutes two or three times a week. Families who attempt an intensive Arabic programme alongside an IGCSE catch-up in the same term usually abandon both. And for anyone planning ahead to equivalency: Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects on the British track, which removes one source of pressure.

sections.heading: Lessons in an apartment, and why the format suits a tower address
paragraphs: A practical section, because it is a real question on the waterfront and nobody writes about it. Apartment living changes the logistics of tutoring in ways a villa does not. There is usually no spare study. There may be a sibling doing homework at the same table. Sound carries. A visiting tutor means a stranger in a small shared space, at a time when the household is probably still unpacking and the building may still be filling.

One-to-one over live video resolves most of that quietly. The requirement is a laptop or tablet, a stable connection, headphones and a chair facing away from the room's traffic. Headphones matter more than the room does: they remove the sibling, the television and the lift lobby in one step, and they let the student speak at normal volume without the household listening. Families who set this up properly in week one rarely revisit it.

The second practical advantage for an arriving household is that the written record survives the chaos of a move. The shared board and the annotated work from each session are saved, so a student who is still finding their books can go back to a worked solution from three weeks ago. In a period when physical notes are frequently in a box somewhere, that is more useful than it sounds.

The comparison table below sets out the trade honestly, including where in-home provision is genuinely better. We would rather describe the real difference than claim the formats are identical. For a younger child in an unfamiliar country, an adult in the room has value, and our answer is to change the session shape - shorter, more frequent, parent within earshot - rather than to argue the point.

sections.heading: Budgeting the first academic year in Sharjah
paragraphs: Arriving families are making every financial decision at once, and tutoring usually gets a number attached before anyone knows what is needed. The table below puts the published market bands into the context of a first year, so the figure can be budgeted properly rather than guessed. These are market rates from the sources named, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list, and none of them is a quote for your child.

The useful framing is to treat the transition as a project cost rather than a recurring one. A mapping block plus a term of targeted catch-up in one or two subjects is a defined amount of money with an end date. An open-ended weekly commitment in four subjects, started before any mapping, is the arrangement that quietly becomes a permanent line in the household budget. Families who front-load the diagnosis generally spend less in total.

Some context for the fee side of the picture, since arriving families are usually comparing school costs at the same time. Dubai's regulator confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in that emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. That is a Dubai measure rather than a Sharjah one, where fees are approved by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, but it is the kind of published fact worth knowing before negotiating anything.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed rate card on these pages, because the figure depends on subject, level and the balance between teaching and supervision. A short consultation gives you the band before you commit, and for an arriving family we would normally recommend starting with the mapping block precisely because it is the cheapest way to find out how little or how much is needed.

sections.heading: The administrative side: documents, attestation and equivalency
paragraphs: Arriving families meet a paperwork layer alongside the academic one, and the two get confused. It is worth separating them clearly. School admission paperwork is handled by the school and the emirate's regulator. Certificate equivalency, which converts a foreign school qualification into something a UAE university or employer can accept, is a Ministry of Education process that happens at the end of schooling, not at the start.

The published British-track requirement is specific and worth knowing early, because it affects subject choices years in advance. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and must additionally show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One competitor page tells UAE candidates they need six subjects, which does not match the published clarification.

For the American track, the same clarification sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB, no points threshold appears in that source, so this page does not state one. Any figure quoted to you for IB equivalency without a Ministry page behind it should be treated as unverified.

Two boundaries. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs; no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it, and we can only tell you what the published requirement says and where to verify it. And nothing in the process requires tutoring - implying otherwise would be a false-urgency claim about a regulatory procedure. Keep original certificates safe from the moment they are issued, because they are what the process asks for.
bullets: School admission paperwork and Ministry equivalency are separate processes
British track: five IGCSE subjects at E or grade 3 or above, Arabic and Islamic education excluded
Plus one A Level at E or above, or two AS Levels at the same grade

sections.heading: Coursework support for a student who joined the course late
paragraphs: A student arriving mid-DP1 lands in the middle of a coursework process, and the temptation to find someone to accelerate it is strongest in exactly this situation. So the boundary needs stating without qualification. Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the MYP Personal Project must be the student's own work, and the student signs a declaration confirming that. One page competing for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments; buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate.

What legitimate support looks like is narrower and, for a late arrival, genuinely valuable. A tutor can teach the underlying content, explain what each criterion rewards in plain language, help narrow a research question until it is answerable inside the word limit, question whether a claim in a draft is actually evidenced, point out that data has no uncertainty treatment, and read a draft against the published criteria and name the weak criterion. For a student who missed the introduction to the whole process, that explanation alone removes most of the disadvantage.

What a tutor must not do is author any part of the submission - not a paragraph, not a methodology, not a conclusion, not a results set. We say this at the start of any supervision block and we say that anything the student did not write has to come out before submission. We also do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or boundary tables; we cite the official source and work from what the student legitimately holds through school.

The practical priority for a mid-DP1 arrival is sequencing rather than speed. Getting the Extended Essay subject and research question agreed early matters more than the writing, because a late or badly chosen question costs months. We would normally put that ahead of content catch-up in the first month, even where the content gap looks larger.
bullets: Allowed: teaching content, explaining criteria, challenging evidence, criterion feedback on the student's own draft
Not allowed: authoring any part of a submission, supplying results, rewriting to completion
Official papers, schemes and boundary tables are cited, never redistributed

sections.heading: Starting, including the case for starting before the move
paragraphs: If the move has not happened yet, the most useful thing you can do is start before it. Two or three sessions in the weeks before arrival, working from the new school's scheme of work and the student's current reports, puts the student into their first lesson knowing roughly what has been covered without them. Because lessons are delivered online, the location of the family during those sessions is irrelevant, which is one of the few genuine advantages of the format.

If the move has already happened, send the previous school's final reports, the new school's scheme of work if you have it, and the syllabus codes from the exam entry. We read those and propose a mapping block rather than a weekly commitment, because the right amount of tutoring cannot be known before the map exists. Most families are relieved to find the recommendation is less than they came expecting to buy.

The introductory session is at no charge - one per family, about thirty minutes, with the student present rather than only the parent. For an arriving student that half hour does a second job: it is a low-stakes conversation with an adult who understands the curriculum they have just joined, which is reassuring in a term when very little is familiar. If the match is not right we change the tutor rather than suggest persevering.

On availability, we tell you upfront. Mainstream combinations are almost always covered immediately. Scarce Higher Level subjects in the weeks before a written series can carry a week or two of wait, and where no UAE-based specialist is free we offer one from our wider pool, which is centred on India and includes tutors who have taught these syllabuses to international cohorts for years. Delivery is unchanged, because it was always one-to-one over live video.

process.title: Send the old reports and the new scheme of work
process.description: The comparison between those two documents is the whole of the diagnosis for an arriving student. Add the syllabus codes from the new school's exam entry, because the board determines the paper structure and nobody should be taught the wrong one.

process.title: Start with a map, not a course
process.description: Four to six sessions to establish what the student covered, what the new course assumed, and what the real gap is. The output is a written topic list you can take to the week-eight parent meeting rather than an impression nobody can act on.

process.title: Pick one or two subjects by gap size
process.description: Not four. Targeted work on the largest two gaps closes faster than thin coverage across everything, and it leaves the student enough unsupervised time to do the work the sessions set. The others usually catch up on their own.

process.title: Settle Arabic separately and early
process.description: Thirty to forty-five minutes two or three times a week, on the school's own material, with the correct stream confirmed. Dealing with it in term one prevents the report-card conversation in term two and costs far less than a rescue later.

process.title: Step the hours down, deliberately
process.description: Once the mapped gaps close, drop to a single maintenance slot and then to nothing. A transition is a project with an end. An arrangement still running at four sessions a week in March was either misjudged or never mapped.

whyPoints.title: Built for the arriving family specifically
whyPoints.description: The first product is a transition map rather than a course, because what an arriving student needs is a comparison between two syllabuses that no single school holds. Most families discover the gap is narrower and more specific than they feared.

whyPoints.title: Format suited to an apartment
whyPoints.description: A laptop, headphones and a quiet corner is the whole setup, with no visitor in a household that may still be unpacking. The shared board is saved after each session, which matters when physical notes are in a box somewhere.

whyPoints.title: Continuity through a second move
whyPoints.description: Many arriving families relocate within the emirate or across to Dubai inside two years. An online arrangement does not end when the address changes, so the student keeps the same tutor through a school move as well as a house move.

whyPoints.title: Sourced numbers only
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure carries the source that published it and the month it was read. We publish no satisfaction percentages, student counts or ratings, because the underlying data for such claims cannot be produced.

whyPoints.title: Honest on the regulatory side
whyPoints.description: We explain what SPEA, KHDA and the Ministry of Education each govern, and what the published equivalency requirement says, with links to their own pages. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from any of them and does not perform equivalency.

whyPoints.title: A clear coursework line
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own drafts, with nothing authored on their behalf. That matters most for a late arrival, who is the student most likely to be offered a shortcut by somebody else.

faqs.question: We are moving to Maryam Island in January. Can my child join IGCSE mid-year?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, subject to a place being available in that year group, which is a question for the school rather than for us. Academically the key variable is which year. Joining Year 10 in January is manageable, because there is still a full year before the papers. Joining Year 11 in January means inheriting an exam entry someone else has already made: the sitting is the June series, the centre lodged final entries months before those papers, and the November series is the resit route rather than a second chance at the same year. The tier and the subject list are effectively fixed, so the plan has to work inside them, and the first thing to ask the new school for is the statement of entry showing exactly what the student is down for.

faqs.question: How far behind will my son be if he joins Year 10 in the second term?
faqs.answer: Less than you probably fear, and the gap will be specific rather than general. In most schedules the topics taught in the first term of Year 10 are identifiable, so the shortfall is a list of three or four named units rather than half a course. The thing that tends to cause more trouble is assessment style: if his previous school tested recall and the new one tests applied reasoning, he can know the content and still score low. That is why we map before teaching.

faqs.question: What does a child coming from CBSE need to catch up on for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Rarely content. Students arriving from CBSE or ICSE frequently know more mathematics and science than their new classmates and still score lower in the first term. The gap is in how the questions work: IGCSE rewards applied reasoning, showing method rather than only answers, and precise mark-scheme wording. Science practical papers are a second gap, because they assess experimental design and error in writing. Both are technique rather than knowledge, and both usually settle inside a term once they are named.

faqs.question: Is it possible to switch from an American high school into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a common transition, but it is the one that takes longest to settle - typically two terms rather than one. What transfers well is breadth and classroom confidence. What has to be built is extended written argument, independent research and the Internal Assessment process, all of which the Diploma assumes and many American programmes do not require in the same form. The practical priority in the first month is agreeing the Extended Essay research question, because a late choice there costs more than any content gap.

faqs.question: My daughter has never studied Arabic. What happens at a Sharjah school?
faqs.answer: She will study it, because UAE private schools must offer Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed curriculum under the Ministry's general regulations. The important detail is the stream: Arabic as an additional language is a different course from Arabic as a first language, with different expectations, and Dubai's regulator requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in these subjects. A realistic first-year target is script, high-frequency vocabulary and following the lesson, which thirty to forty-five minutes two or three times a week achieves.

faqs.question: Which documents does a new arrival in Sharjah need before school starts?
faqs.answer: The school will give you its own list, and it is the authoritative one. From a tutoring point of view the documents worth securing are the previous school's final reports in a readable form, the syllabus or scheme of work the previous school was following, and once enrolled, the new school's scheme of work plus the syllabus codes from the exam entry. Keep original certificates safe from the moment they are issued, because the Ministry's equivalency process asks for them years later and replacing them from another country is slow.

faqs.question: Does a tower apartment work for one-to-one video lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the few settings where the online format is straightforwardly better than a visit. The requirement is a laptop or tablet, a stable connection, headphones and a chair facing away from the room's traffic. Headphones do most of the work: they remove the sibling, the television and the lift lobby, and let the student speak normally without the household listening in. No spare study is needed, which matters in a two or three-bedroom flat where every room is already doing a job.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for tutoring in our first year in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a project cost rather than a recurring one. Published market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 an hour and in-home provision at AED 180-500 because the rate absorbs travel. A mapping block of four to six sessions plus a term of targeted work in one or two subjects is a defined amount with an end date. Families who buy an open-ended weekly commitment in four subjects before mapping generally spend considerably more in total and finish no further ahead.

faqs.question: Will my child's previous school grades transfer to the new report card?
faqs.answer: No, and they should not be read as equivalent either. A percentage from one system, a letter grade from another and a 1-7 criterion grade measure different things against different cohorts. The new school will assess from scratch, which is appropriate but does mean the first report is a baseline rather than a verdict. The useful thing a parent can do is keep the old reports, because a tutor comparing them against the new scheme of work is how the actual topic gap gets identified.

faqs.question: Is it better to repeat a year or move up and catch up?
faqs.answer: That decision belongs to the school, which can see the cohort, the curriculum and the student's placement assessment. What we can contribute is evidence about the size and type of the gap: whether it is three named topics or a whole mode of assessment, and how long similar gaps have taken to close. As a general pattern, a content gap argues for moving up with support, while a language-of-instruction gap or a missing mode of extended writing argues for more caution.

faqs.question: How long does it take a new arrival to settle academically?
faqs.answer: For most transitions, one term with proper mapping. Two terms where the move involves a new language of instruction, or entry into the Diploma from a system with no independent-research component, because those require building a working habit rather than filling a gap. The first two weeks tell you very little, since early marks reflect disruption more than ability. The reliable signal arrives in weeks three to six, which is exactly when a mapping block is most useful.

faqs.question: Can my two children share one tutor in the first term?
faqs.answer: Not in the same session, because one-to-one means one student and the diagnosis for an arriving child is specific to them. They can certainly share a tutor across two separate slots if they are at the same stage and board, and for siblings close in age that is often efficient. Where the children are at different stages, separate specialists are better: the subject-level match matters more than the convenience, particularly if one of them is in an exam year.

faqs.question: What is the gap between IGCSE and the first term of the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Depth and independence rather than content. IGCSE rewards accurate recall and clean method; the Diploma assumes you can sustain an argument, manage your own deadlines and conduct a piece of independent research. In mathematics specifically, a student who collected top grades on Cambridge 0580 Extended often finds Analysis and Approaches assumes an algebraic fluency the IGCSE course never asked for. That gap is identifiable and closes within a term when it is addressed directly rather than waited out.

faqs.question: Do we need to pick Cambridge or Pearson before enrolling?
faqs.answer: The school chooses the board, not the family, so the practical question is finding out which one your chosen school uses before buying textbooks or starting tutoring. Cambridge and Pearson split the same subject into different papers with different tiering and practical arrangements, so teaching the wrong structure wastes the opening weeks. Get the syllabus code from the school's exam entry rather than from a textbook cover, and send it with your first enquiry to anyone you plan to work with.

faqs.question: Should we start tutoring before the move or after?
faqs.answer: Before, if there is time. Two or three sessions in the weeks before arrival, working from the new school's scheme of work and the student's current reports, mean the student walks into their first lesson knowing roughly what has been covered without them. Because lessons are delivered online over live video, where the family is sitting during those sessions is irrelevant. After the move, the better moment is weeks three to six, once there is real marked work to diagnose from rather than first-fortnight noise.

sharjah/maryam-island.closingHeading: Map it before you buy it
sharjah/maryam-island.closingBody: For an arriving family the cheapest useful step is a comparison, not a course. Send the previous school's final reports, the new school's scheme of work, and the syllabus codes from the exam entry. We will propose a short mapping block that names the actual topic gaps, then target the one or two subjects that need it and step down once they close. The introductory session is at no charge, one per family, with the student present. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, which needs a laptop, headphones and a quiet corner rather than a spare room.

sharjah/muwaileh.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are grouped by the work Muwaileh families actually buy: internal assessment supervision in Diploma subjects, and paper technique for Cambridge and Pearson candidates in Years 10 and 11. Each teaches one board and one level rather than claiming the whole range.

intro.heading: Why a good school is not the whole course
paragraphs: Muwaileh holds more international school capacity than any other district in Sharjah. Families move here deliberately for it, and the schools are generally well staffed and properly run. That is why the tutoring question in this neighbourhood is different from the one in the older coastal districts: parents here are rarely trying to compensate for poor teaching. They are discovering that good teaching covers less of the course than they assumed.

Work out the arithmetic. A Cambridge IGCSE subject gets perhaps four or five lessons a fortnight across two years. In that time a teacher has to deliver a syllabus, run practicals, set and mark assessments for a class of twenty or more, and prepare a cohort for papers written in a language of command verbs. What that timetable cannot contain is a student sitting a whole past paper under timed conditions every week for eight weeks and having each one marked individually with feedback by question type.

In the Diploma the gap is wider and more consequential, because a fifth of each subject grade comes from internally assessed work the student produces largely outside lessons. A teacher supervising thirty internal assessments can give a research question a few minutes of attention. A badly chosen research question costs marks in every criterion and cannot be rescued once the data is collected, and that is the single most common Diploma failure in this district.

There is a third, quieter gap: revision as a technique. Almost nobody is taught how to revise. Students reread notes, feel productive, and score the same mark again. Spaced retrieval, working from the mark scheme backwards, and writing answers under time pressure are learnable skills, and they belong to neither the school's timetable nor a parent's expertise.

None of this is a criticism of the schools in this district, and a page that implied otherwise would be dishonest as well as unhelpful. A teacher with a class of twenty-four and a two-year syllabus is doing the job the timetable allows. The gap is structural: it exists in Muwaileh, in Dubai, in London and in Singapore, and it is why tutoring in a well-schooled district is a supplement to good teaching rather than a substitute for bad teaching.

IB Gram addresses those three gaps with one-to-one lessons over live video. IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service run only in India. For Muwaileh that matters less for traffic than for match quality: the point of a tutor here is not another lesson on the same content, it is a specialist in the exact board, level and component where the independent work is going wrong, and that specialist does not have to live down the road.

sharjah/muwaileh.programmesIntro: Three programmes dominate enquiries from Muwaileh addresses. Each entry below names the part of the course that happens outside the classroom, because that is what tutoring in this district is actually for.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internally assessed component contributing roughly a fifth of the grade, marked by the teacher against published criteria and externally moderated. Core components can add up to three points and can also prevent a diploma being awarded.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Muwaileh have good classroom provision and almost no supervised time for internal assessment drafting. The work is produced at home across months with a handful of supervisor meetings, which is why the sessions that change a Diploma grade in this district are the early ones on question design rather than the late ones on content.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: Assessed by syllabus code, with Core and Extended tiers in sciences and maths that cap the attainable grade. Cambridge runs June and November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level. Each centre is allocated to one of six administrative timetable zones, and the school's own zone timetable is the one that applies.
programmes.countryNote: Tier is the decision Muwaileh parents hear about last and should hear about first. A Core entry caps the grade regardless of how well the candidate performs, and the entry closes months before the papers. Candidates here sit the June series, with November as the resit route, and the centre lodges final entries a long way ahead of the June papers - the exact date sits on the statement of entry rather than in a brochure, so ask the exams officer for it.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Graded 9 to 1, available in May or June and in November, with formula provision and paper structures that differ from the Cambridge equivalent in the same subject. Some qualifications are modular, which changes when revision has to peak and when a resit is possible.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson published a November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and released June 2026 results to centres on 19 August and to students on 20 August 2026. Provisional timetables are revised, so a Muwaileh family should work from the live PDF on qualifications.pearson.com rather than any date copied onto a tutoring page.

sharjah/muwaileh.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects requested most often from Muwaileh, described by the component where independent work decides the grade. Availability depends on board and level rather than on location, because lessons are delivered over video.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The internal exploration is marked against five criteria worth twenty marks in total, and most lost marks sit in reflection and personal engagement rather than in the mathematics itself. Higher Level Paper 3 needs extended unseen problem solving that no class drill reproduces.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, which hides the real demand: interpreting a result in the context of the situation modelled. A correct number with no statement of what it means for the scenario earns little, and that habit is corrected in practice rather than in lessons.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is assessed on four criteria worth twenty-four marks, and a research question that cannot generate a usable spread of data sinks all four. Energetics and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level teaching load.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circular motion defeat capable students because algebra and physical reasoning must run together. Paper 1 rewards recognising which relationship applies, which is a pattern-matching skill built through volume of practice.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A long syllabus where marks are lost to imprecise language rather than ignorance. The investigation criteria reward a controlled design and an honest evaluation of limitations, both of which are planning skills rather than content knowledge.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries based on published news articles, each with its own word limit and each requiring diagrams drawn correctly. Candidates lose marks for articles chosen badly and for evaluation that lists rather than judges.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended candidates meet functions, transformations and histograms with unequal class widths; Core candidates never see them. The tier decision sets the ceiling, and once entries close in the autumn it cannot be undone.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper is the biggest source of avoidable loss: candidates describe a method without naming a control variable or justifying a repeat reading. That is a question-type skill, not a topic.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis and the qualitative analysis tables carry the Extended difficulty. Learning the analysis tables as tables, rather than reasoning them out under time pressure, is worth several marks.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers with a formula sheet supplied, which changes what must be memorised and how time is allocated. Candidates trained only on Cambridge papers lose minutes adjusting to question order and method marks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together worth up to three points, each with its own word limit and internal deadlines set by the school. Support is question framing, criteria explanation and feedback on the student's own drafts; supplied prose is a malpractice risk, not a shortcut.

sections.heading: What class time covers, and what it hands back to the student
paragraphs: Start with an honest division of labour. A well-run Muwaileh school delivers content, demonstrates method, runs practicals, sets periodic assessments and gives whole-class feedback. That is a substantial amount, and it is not the whole course. The remainder is produced by the student outside the classroom, and the quality of that remainder is what separates a 5 from a 7.

The components that sit mostly outside class time are predictable. Timed practice on whole papers, with individual marking, is first. Internal assessment drafting is second, and in the Diploma it is the one with a fixed weighting attached. Independent revision across a two-year syllabus is third. Learning the vocabulary of command verbs is fourth, and it is almost never taught as a topic in its own right because it belongs to no topic.

A parent can test this quickly. Ask your child how many complete past papers they have sat under timed conditions this term, and how many of those were marked individually with feedback by question. The answer in most schools, in any country, is fewer than the parent assumed, and it is not a criticism of the teacher. A class of twenty-four papers marked individually every week is not a thing a timetable contains.

That test also tells you what to buy. If the answer is zero papers, the first purchase is not more teaching. It is a marked timed-paper cycle, because the content is probably already in place and the marks are being lost in the room. The table sets out the division component by component.

sections.heading: The tier decision that sets the ceiling before Year 11 begins
paragraphs: In Cambridge sciences and maths, candidates are entered for Core or Extended, and the tier caps the attainable grade. It is a decision made by the school, usually during Year 10, often on the basis of a single set of results, and it is the one Muwaileh parents most often learn about after it has already been taken.

The content difference is real rather than cosmetic. Extended maths candidates meet functions, transformations and histograms with unequal class widths. Extended science candidates meet additional topics and are examined on papers with a higher difficulty profile. A Core candidate who performs perfectly is still awarded within the Core grade range, which may not satisfy a sixth-form entry requirement two years later.

The timing is the part that catches families. Cambridge sets final entries months before the June papers are sat, so the tier is settled a long way out rather than in the run-up to the exams. Once that entry is made the tier is fixed for that series. A conversation in the autumn term about moving a child from Core to Extended is a conversation worth having; the same conversation in the weeks before the papers is mostly theoretical, and the only opening left is the November series as a resit. Get the centre own entry date from the exams officer and work backwards from it rather than from the exam timetable.

What tutoring can usefully do is provide evidence. A candidate sitting Extended past papers under timed conditions, marked honestly, produces a mark that a head of department can act on. That is a more persuasive case than a parent's conviction, and it is the right use of two or three early sessions in Year 10.

sections.heading: Internal assessment: where class time runs out entirely
paragraphs: This is the component that explains most of the gap between a Muwaileh student's predicted grade and their final one. It is produced outside lessons, it carries a fixed weighting, and it is marked against published criteria that most students never read properly.

The mark allocations are worth knowing as numbers rather than as a general idea. The Diploma maths exploration is assessed against five criteria totalling twenty marks: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics, with the last carrying the largest share. The scientific investigation in biology, chemistry and physics is assessed against four criteria totalling twenty-four marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Economics runs a portfolio of three commentaries based on published articles. Confirm every figure against the current subject guide with your school's Diploma coordinator before planning around it.

Seeing the criteria as a mark split changes behaviour. A student who knows that reflection and personal engagement carry marks stops treating them as decoration. A student who knows that evaluation is a sixth of a science investigation writes the limitations section properly instead of in the last hour. None of this is content knowledge; it is reading the assessment instrument, and it takes one session.

The failure mode is always the same and always early. A research question is chosen in the first weeks, the student collects data for a month, and the data turns out to have no usable spread or no controllable variable. By then the deadline is close and the only option is writing up a weak investigation well. Two sessions on question design before data collection are worth ten sessions of rescue afterwards.

sections.heading: Word limits, deadlines and the documents that carry them
paragraphs: The written components of a Diploma each carry a limit, and every year candidates in every country lose marks by treating a limit as a target to exceed. Collecting the limits in one place is useful because no competing page in this market does it, and because the internal deadlines that matter most are set by the school rather than by the awarding body.

The Extended Essay is normally capped at four thousand words. The Theory of Knowledge essay and the exhibition commentary each carry their own shorter limits. Internal assessments in the sciences and mathematics carry page or word guidance rather than hard ceilings in some subjects and firm limits in others, and the economics portfolio limits each commentary individually. Every one of these should be confirmed against the current subject guide through the school, because the IB revises them and a figure copied from an old page is worse than no figure.

The deadline structure matters as much as the limit. A school sets internal dates for a first draft, a supervisor meeting, a final submission and an upload, and those dates sit months before anything external. A tutoring plan built from the awarding body's calendar will always be late; one built from the school's assessment calendar will not.

Practical consequence for a Muwaileh family: ask the school for the written internal deadline schedule at the start of the Diploma year, not in the term it bites. It is the single most useful document in the house, and tutoring sessions should be positioned relative to it rather than relative to the exam.

sections.heading: The past-paper cycle, and why volume alone does nothing
paragraphs: Every family in Muwaileh has heard that past papers are the answer, and most buy the wrong version of it. Working through papers without marking them against the scheme produces confidence and no improvement, because the student grades their own answer generously on the parts they half-knew.

A cycle that works has four steps. The paper is sat to time, unaided, in one sitting. It is marked against the official mark scheme, strictly, with the marks shown. The errors are then grouped by question type and command verb rather than by topic, which usually reveals that a student losing twelve marks across a paper lost nine of them on one kind of question. Only then is anything re-taught, and only the topics the errors actually expose.

That fourth step is the one families skip and the one that saves time. A student who loses marks on every explain question does not need the whole syllabus retaught; they need to be shown that an explain answer requires a mechanism and a consequence, and then made to write six of them. The repair is narrow and fast once the diagnosis is honest.

Volume matters after that, not before. Once the technique is in place, a weekly timed paper for eight weeks before a series is the highest-value thing a candidate can do, and it is almost impossible to arrange without someone to mark it. Doing one paper properly is worth more than doing four and checking the answers.

sections.heading: What to buy first, and what it costs around Muwaileh
paragraphs: Because the problem in this district is usually independent work rather than teaching, the spending order is different from the one families assume. The cheapest effective purchase is early and narrow; the expensive ineffective purchase is late and broad.

First on the list is internal assessment supervision in a Diploma subject, bought in the first term of the course. Three or four sessions on question design and criteria interpretation protect a fifth of the grade and cost a fraction of a year of weekly lessons. Second is a marked past-paper cycle in the weakest examined subject. Third, and only third, is weekly content teaching, which is what most families buy first.

On price, market rates read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with premium examiner-experienced tutors higher. In-home visiting rates run AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, and independent home tutors up to AED 500, because those figures absorb travel. Monthly online packages of around eight sessions advertise from AED 799. None of these are IB Gram prices; IB Gram quotes after a consultation.

The useful comparison for a Muwaileh family is cost per recovered mark rather than cost per hour. Four sessions on a research question in September can protect more marks than twenty sessions of content teaching in April, and that is a pricing argument as much as an academic one.

sections.heading: Home tutoring in a school-dense district, honestly compared
paragraphs: Muwaileh is unusual in the UAE in having a genuine local supply of tutors, because the schools are here and so are the teachers and the university students. A family searching for a home tutor in this district will find one, and for primary support or homework supervision that is a reasonable arrangement.

The limits show up in two places. The first is the conflict question: the closer a tutor sits to the school, the more likely it is that they are connected to it, and an arrangement in which your child's own teacher is paid privately is the one to avoid. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi the education regulator's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Ask rather than assume.

The second is component specialism. The work this district actually needs is internal assessment supervision and marked paper cycles in specific subjects at specific levels. A local generalist can supervise homework; they cannot usually tell a Diploma candidate that their chemistry research question has no controllable variable. That is a subject-and-level match, and the pool for it is national rather than local.

IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Muwaileh families are taught one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing for papers and a shared whiteboard. What video cannot do is replace laboratory bench time, and the school holds that part; a tutor teaches method, variables, uncertainty and analysis instead.
