sections.heading: Verifying what a tutor says they are
paragraphs: Three attributes are worth verifying before money changes hands, and all three are straightforward.

The permit comes first because it is a legal requirement rather than a preference. Private tutoring in the UAE runs under a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied through the smart app, website or e-services system. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so none is quoted here. Because the permit is free, a tutor citing permit costs as a reason for their rate is telling you something they did not mean to.

Examiner experience is the second, and it is the claim most often made and least often evidenced. Treat it as unverified unless the person can say what they marked and in which series, and understand what it cannot mean. Examiner experience is not access to marking, to grade boundaries or to paper content, and anyone presenting it that way is either confused or dishonest. Where it is real, what it buys is an instinct for where marks sit on a page, which is testable in a single session on your child's own script.

The third is the school relationship, which parents often get backwards. Hiring your child's own classroom teacher privately feels like the inside track and is the opposite. Press reporting on Abu Dhabi indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also prohibits serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than exact policy wording and check the current document, but do not build a plan on it.

One more verification worth doing: ask whether the provider will hand over board materials. Published syllabus documents, past papers, markschemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards and should be referenced and linked rather than redistributed. A provider happy to send you a bundle of them is telling you how they treat rules generally.

sections.heading: Where price genuinely predicts quality, and where it does not
paragraphs: Having set out the ladder, it is worth being precise about when the extra money is the right call and when it is decoration, because the honest answer varies by component rather than by subject.

Pay up for narrowness. Higher Level components with an unusual shape — an extended problem-solving paper, uncertainty-heavy data analysis, a Diploma mathematics exploration — reward somebody who has worked on exactly that thing many times. The same is true of internal assessment supervision, where the skill is knowing which criterion is capping the mark and asking the question that makes the student see it. In these cases a specialist at the upper band does in one session what a generalist does in four, and the arithmetic favours the specialist even at double the rate.

Do not pay up for ordinary Standard Level teaching, for content recap, or for organisational support. A qualified subject tutor in the published middle band handles those entirely, and spending specialist rates on them is a transfer of money with no corresponding gain. The same applies to the first diagnostic session, which is about reading a script rather than performing virtuosity.

There is one case where the top of the market is clearly the wrong purchase: a student who is not working between sessions. No rate solves that, and buying a more expensive hour to compensate converts a motivation problem into an expensive motivation problem. The honest advice there is to fix the week before spending anything, and a provider who says so is demonstrating more about their quality than any rating could.

The general rule holds across all of it. Judge the hour by what it produced in writing, compare the same question types across six weeks, and let that decide. A page that tells you to trust its own ranking instead is asking you to accept the one thing it cannot show you.

sections.heading: What a good match looks like from this emirate specifically
paragraphs: Quality is partly an attribute of the tutor and partly an attribute of the arrangement, and in Umm Al Quwain the arrangement does more work than families expect.

Timing is the first element. A student commuting back from Sharjah or Ajman is home late and tired, and a tutor who insists on a fixed hour that happens to suit them is a poor match regardless of credentials. A good arrangement puts shorter work on weekday evenings and the long timed paper at the weekend, moves for mock weeks, and adjusts for the shortened school day during Ramadan rather than treating the timetable as fixed.

The second element is coverage honesty. No provider has unlimited specialists, and a narrow Higher Level combination in a single fixed evening slot sometimes has no match in a given week. Nobody in the researched competitor set discloses a coverage limit anywhere, and several conceal non-local delivery behind a foreign phone number. The useful behaviour is the opposite: say what is available, say what is not, and give a date. A family that knows the limit can plan around it. A family that discovers it in week three has paid for a generalist in the meantime.

The third is continuity. Expatriate households here travel, often at short notice and often in the middle of a term. An arrangement that survives a trip, because it does not depend on anybody driving anywhere, is better than one that breaks and restarts. The same property means a tutor who moves emirate or country does not end the plan.

Put together, the question for a family here is not which tutor is finest in the abstract. It is which arrangement reliably delivers a component specialist into the one hour your child is actually able to concentrate, and tells you the truth when it cannot.

sections.heading: The six-week test that settles it
paragraphs: Every argument on this page reduces to one comparison, and it costs nothing except attention. Two dated marked pieces of work on the same question types, six weeks apart, with the markscheme reference attached to both.

Set it up at the start. In the first session the tutor marks a timed piece of your child's work against a published markscheme and names two or three question types that account for most of the lost marks. Those become the targets, written down. In week four or five the student attempts the same question types again under the same conditions, and the second script is marked the same way. The comparison is at type level, not on the paper total, because totals move with paper difficulty and type-level counts do not.

Then read the result honestly. If the targeted marks moved, the match is good and the plan is right, and the next question is when to stop rather than whether to continue. If they did not move, one of three things is true: the diagnosis was wrong, the tutor is the wrong fit, or the student is not working between sessions. All three are fixable, and none of them is fixed by buying more hours from the same arrangement.

This test is also what makes rapport the secondary consideration it should be. A tutor your child likes who produces no movement in six weeks is a pleasant standing order. A tutor your child finds demanding whose targets are moving is the better purchase, provided the student is not actively avoiding the sessions. Rapport matters for attendance; evidence matters for outcome, and only one of them is measurable.

Agree the review date before the first paid session and the whole question of who is best becomes a question you can answer yourself in six weeks, with two pieces of paper, about your own child rather than about a market.

process.title: Write down what you are actually buying
process.description: Subject, level, the component where marks are going missing, and the hour your child is genuinely free. Four lines. Most enquiries contain the first two and nothing else, which is why they take longer to match and more often produce a competent generalist rather than the right specialist.

process.title: Send one marked script and the school's deadlines
process.description: A marked piece of work shows whether the losses are knowledge, method or command term. The coordinator's deadline sheet shows what the year actually looks like. Between them they remove most of the guesswork that otherwise gets charged to you in the first few sessions.

process.title: Ask the eight questions
process.description: Components, boards marked, output in writing, markscheme, the comment they would write on a weak draft, permit status, the own-school position, and what happens if nobody is free. Four minutes, and it is the single highest-return piece of diligence available in this market.

process.title: Take the trial and keep what it produces
process.description: A working session over live video, booked without card details, scheduled around the southbound commute. It should produce a marked piece of work with a markscheme reference and two named target question types. If it produces only a friendly conversation, say so, because that is the output you would be paying for.

process.title: Fix the six-week review date in advance
process.description: Two dated marked attempts on the same question types, compared at type level. Agreeing the date before the first invoice is what turns the review into a decision point. Three honest outcomes exist: continue, change the tutor or the targets, or stop because the student now works independently.

whyPoints.title: Claims limited to what a parent can check
whyPoints.description: Subject, level, components, boards whose papers a tutor has marked, permit status, and what a session produces. No self-issued ratings, no satisfaction percentages without a sample size, no accreditation anybody would have to take on trust. Everything stated is testable in one session.

whyPoints.title: Rates shown as market bands with their publishers named
whyPoints.description: The dirham figures here are published by the providers named, not invented and not borrowed and relabelled. Our own figure follows a free trial session, because before anyone has read a marked script any number would be a guess dressed up as a price.

whyPoints.title: Matching on component, which is what geography cannot give you
whyPoints.description: In the least populous emirate in the country, the resident specialist pool for one Higher Level component is close to empty. Live video replaces whoever lives nearby with whoever has done this exact thing before, which is the only version of quality that holds up at this distance.

whyPoints.title: The authorship boundary written down
whyPoints.description: The student is the author of every sentence of assessed work, drafts are dated, and no replacement text is supplied at any point. One provider in this search result sells completed internal assessments. Stating the boundary explicitly is both the rule and a real difference here.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before they bite
whyPoints.description: When no specialist is free for a narrow combination in one fixed slot you are told, with an alternative time, an adjacent specialist or a date. Nobody in the researched competitor set discloses a coverage limit at all, and discovering one in week three is what a specialist rate paid to a generalist actually buys.

whyPoints.title: A review date agreed before the first invoice
whyPoints.description: Six weeks, two dated marked attempts, compared at question-type level, with three honest outcomes including stopping. A provider willing to name the conditions under which you should stop paying them has given you the most useful quality signal on this page.

faqs.question: Is there an official ranking of IB tutors in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: No. No UAE authority inspects, scores or ranks individual private tutors. Schools are inspected and banded, and in Dubai those reports are published by the regulator, but a tutor is an individual holding a work permit rather than an institution with an inspection history. Every claim to be the finest in a city is therefore self-issued. What you can check instead is concrete: the subject and level, the components worked on, which board's papers the person has marked, whether they hold a MoHRE permit, and what their first session produces in writing.

faqs.question: What separates a tutor charging AED 400 an hour from one charging AED 150?
faqs.answer: At best, narrowness. The upper band usually means somebody who works on one component at one level repeatedly rather than covering four subjects competently, and for an extended problem-solving paper or an internal assessment that specialism genuinely saves sessions. At worst the difference is nothing but confidence, because between roughly AED 150 and AED 300 capable specialists and generalists charging specialist rates are indistinguishable by price. The discriminator is output: which markscheme was applied to your child's own work, what was annotated, and whether you keep the script.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor before paying the first invoice?
faqs.answer: Eight things. Which components of the subject they work on, named specifically. Which board's papers they have marked and when. What the first session will produce in writing and whether you keep it. Which markscheme will be applied. What comment they would write on a weak paragraph of an internal assessment draft. Whether they hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit. What happens if your child attends their school. And what they will tell you if no specialist is free in your slot. Four minutes, and it sorts a shortlist decisively.

faqs.question: Should I trust a 4.9 star rating on a tutoring website?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. In the researched competitor set one provider publishes a rating it awarded itself, another shows two different review totals on the same page, and a third shows a near-perfect score from twenty reviews alongside a claim of serving a far larger student body. Self-asserted aggregate ratings in structured data are against Google's own policy and carry a manual-action risk, which tells you something about the operation as well as the number. Named, dated, individually readable reviews are worth something. A number with no countable reviews behind it is decoration.

faqs.question: How do I check somebody is legally allowed to tutor my child here?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because it is free, nobody can honestly cite its cost as a reason for their rate.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who claims examiner experience worth the extra?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and treat the claim as unverified until they say what they marked and in which series. Where it is genuine, what it buys is an instinct for where marks actually sit on a page, which shows up immediately when they annotate your child's own script. What it must never mean is access to marking, to grade boundaries or to paper content, and a provider implying any of that has told you to walk away. Current examiner status in particular is frequently claimed across this market and rarely evidenced, so test it on output rather than on the profile.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to have taught at my child's school to be useful?
faqs.answer: No, and the assumption costs families money. What matters is component-level experience at the right level with the right board. What school familiarity genuinely helps with is the calendar, because internal assessment deadlines are set by the coordinator rather than the board, and those dates drive the plan. A tutor who asks for the school's own deadline sheet in the first conversation gets that advantage without ever having worked there. Hiring a teacher from the school itself carries its own problems and should not be the plan.

faqs.question: What does it mean if a site quotes prices in dollars or pounds?
faqs.answer: Usually that the page was not written for you. Two providers ranking for these searches quote in US dollars, and one runs a currency and phone number from another country while addressing UAE parents. It is not fraud, but it signals that localisation is cosmetic, and localisation is exactly what you need: an understanding of the school run out of this emirate, the exam centre in another one, the Ramadan timetable and the regulator that supervises your child's school. A page that cannot manage the currency rarely manages those.

faqs.question: A provider says it holds regulator approval. Should that reassure me?
faqs.answer: It should prompt one question: show me the permit number and the issuing body. Educational services permits in Dubai are granted to training institutes with premises, through initial approval, a maximum six-month window to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An online matching platform is a different kind of organisation and generally holds nothing of the sort. IB Gram does not hold such a permit and does not claim one. Implying endorsement by a regulator or an examination board is the most dangerous overreach in this market.

faqs.question: Someone offered to supply a completed Internal Assessment. What should we do?
faqs.answer: End the conversation. One provider in the researched set sells finished internal assessments at a published price of around AED 3,750. Under IB rules a candidate who submits work that is not their own faces a malpractice finding, and the consequence falls on the student, potentially across the whole Diploma rather than one subject. Legitimate support is criterion-referenced questioning on the student's own argument: which criterion is this paragraph for, what does the descriptor ask for that is missing, why was this method chosen. Every sentence stays the candidate's, and the drafts are dated.

faqs.question: How long should it take to be matched with an IB specialist?
faqs.answer: For a Standard Level subject with flexible timing, days. For Higher Level work with flexible timing, days to a week. For a narrow Higher Level combination in one fixed weekday slot, longer, and in some terms there is genuinely nobody suitable free in that hour. The useful thing is not speed but honesty about it: an alternative time, an adjacent specialist who can start now, or a date. Nobody in the researched competitor set discloses a coverage limit anywhere, which means their families find out by being given whoever was available.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is good but my child does not warm to them?
faqs.answer: Change the tutor, but check the evidence first, because the two things are often confused. A student can dislike a tutor who is demanding and still be making measurable progress, which is the arrangement working. A student can enjoy sessions with somebody producing nothing, which is a pleasant standing order. Look at the six-week comparison before deciding. Rapport matters for attendance, and attendance matters, so a genuine clash is worth fixing quickly. What should not drive the decision is a student's preference for the easier hour.

faqs.question: How do I compare two tutors who both sound convincing?
faqs.answer: Make them both produce something. Ask each for a short trial session on the same piece of your child's work, and compare the two marked outputs side by side: which markscheme was referenced, whether the annotation identifies question types or just corrects answers, and whether the named targets are specific enough to test in four weeks. Convincing is a property of conversation. Marked work is a property of competence, and it is the only comparison that does not depend on which of them is the better talker.

faqs.question: Is the most expensive tutor the right choice for Standard Level subjects?
faqs.answer: Rarely. Standard Level content teaching, timed-paper practice and technique work are handled fully by a qualified subject tutor in the published middle band, and paying specialist rates for them transfers money without buying anything. Save the upper band for narrow Higher Level components, Paper 3 style questions, and internal assessment supervision where knowing which criterion is capping the mark is the whole skill. The exception is a single stubborn component: one or two sessions at the top of the market on a specific problem can be good value precisely because it is brief.

faqs.question: Which claims on a tutoring site are actually checkable?
faqs.answer: Six of them. The subject and level offered. The components a tutor works on, if stated specifically. Which board's papers they have marked, testable on your own child's script. Permit status, which you can simply ask for. What a session produces in writing. And whether the page quotes prices with a source and a date. Everything else — rankings, satisfaction percentages, self-issued star ratings, named schools shown as clients, implied regulator endorsement — is either unverifiable or, in several cases found in this market, demonstrably inconsistent on the same page.

faqs.question: How will I know in six weeks whether I chose well?
faqs.answer: By comparing two dated marked attempts at the same question types, marked against the same published markscheme. If the targeted marks moved, the choice was right and the remaining question is when to stop. If they did not, one of three things is true: the diagnosis was wrong, the tutor is the wrong fit, or nothing is happening between sessions. Each has a different fix and none of them is more hours from the same arrangement. Agree the review date before the first invoice, and the question answers itself with two pieces of paper.

umm-al-quwain/best-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Judge the output, not the adjective
umm-al-quwain/best-ib-tutor.closingBody: Nobody can hand an Umm Al Quwain family a verified ranking of IB tutors, and the providers who imply they can are the ones whose other numbers fall apart on inspection. What you can do is convert the question into attributes, ask the eight questions, take a free trial session over live video, and keep whatever it produces. Then compare two dated marked attempts at the same question types six weeks later. That comparison is about your own child rather than about a market, it costs nothing beyond attention, and it is the only evidence on this subject that no amount of marketing can survive.

umm-al-quwain/best-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors who cover Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE for students living in Umm Al Quwain and attending schools across the northern emirates. Each one works from the syllabus code your child is entered against, not a generic maths or science outline.

intro.heading: What "best" has to mean when you can count the local options on one hand
paragraphs: Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate, and the international-school options inside its borders are thin compared with Sharjah or Dubai. Most families here who want a Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE route end up enrolled across an emirate line, which means a school day that finishes with a drive. That single fact reshapes what a good tutor looks like. The question is no longer which tutor lives nearest; there is no useful answer to that question in Al Salamah or Falaj Al Mualla. The question is which tutor can prove, quickly, that the hours your child gives up are moving marks.

So this page does not argue about adjectives. It sets out the evidence a tutoring arrangement should produce, in order, and the week it should appear. A diagnostic paper marked against the real mark scheme in week one. A per-topic error list, written down, that both you and your child can read. A revised plan in week two that names the topics being attacked and the paper they appear in. A second marked paper at week four or five against the same standard, so the comparison means something. If a tutor cannot describe that sequence before you pay, the rest of the conversation is decoration.

The reason to be strict about this in Umm Al Quwain specifically is that the fallback here is worse than in Dubai. In a dense market a weak arrangement gets replaced easily. Here, a family that loses a term to a pleasant but undirected tutor has few local alternatives and a long drive to the next one. Online delivery removes the geography from the problem: the pool is every available subject specialist rather than everyone willing to drive to the Umm Al Quwain corniche on a Tuesday, and a Chemistry 0620 specialist is a scheduling question rather than a map question.

There is also a timing problem worth naming early. A student commuting to Muwaileh, Ajman or the Ras Al Khaimah schools is often not home until well after four, sometimes closer to six if there is an activity or a bus route with several stops. An in-home tutor arriving at that point eats the only usable window in the evening with travel. A live online session can start at the moment the bag hits the floor and end before homework time collapses. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India, and on this page the comparison is made openly rather than hidden.

The other half of being useful here is honesty about what tutoring cannot do. No tutor can promise a grade, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rules do not require tutoring at all. What a tutor can do is shorten the distance between what your child half-knows and what an examiner will award a mark for, and show you that distance closing on paper. Everything below is organised around that: the evidence, where IGCSE marks actually go missing, what the exam calendar demands months before the exam, what the market charges, and where a tutor is obliged to stop and hand the pen back.

umm-al-quwain/best-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Umm Al Quwain families reach IGCSE by several routes, and the entry point changes what the first term of tutoring has to repair. These are the three stages that matter for a student sitting IGCSE from a school in the northern emirates.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE, Years 10-11
programmes.description: Two years, usually eight or nine subjects, assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings; Pearson International GCSE splits Foundation and Higher. The tier a student is entered for is decided by the school months before the exam and caps the grade available, so a tier conversation in Year 10 is worth more than any amount of revision in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: In Umm Al Quwain the practical issue is that the entry decisions are made at a school in another emirate, often communicated by email to a parent who is at work in a third. Ask the subject teacher, in writing, which tier and which syllabus code your child is entered against, and keep the reply. Tutoring built on the wrong tier teaches content the paper will never ask for.

programmes.name: Years 7-9, the run-up
programmes.description: The years where the gaps that surface in Year 11 are formed: fractions and indices in maths, balancing equations in chemistry, graph interpretation across all three sciences. Nothing here is examined externally, which is why it is easy to leave alone. A student arriving in Year 10 without fluent algebra does not have a Year 10 problem; they have a Year 8 problem being assessed at Year 10 pace.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving into Umm Al Quwain mid-cycle from a CBSE, American or MoE-curriculum school meet this most sharply, because the topic order differs and the gaps are invisible on a report card. A two-session diagnostic on arithmetic fluency and scientific notation costs very little and tells you whether Year 10 will be a build or a repair.

programmes.name: What follows IGCSE: A Level, IB Diploma or a UAE university route
programmes.description: IGCSE results decide which post-16 doors are open. A Level subject entry usually depends on the grade in the same subject at IGCSE, and the IB Diploma's higher-level choices work the same way. Students aiming at a UAE university also meet Ministry of Education equivalency rules, which count accredited subjects and grades rather than a school's own reporting.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Al Quwain students frequently continue at the same out-of-emirate school or move to Sharjah or Dubai for sixth form, which makes the Year 11 grade profile the hinge of the whole plan. Decide the post-16 target before choosing which two IGCSE subjects get the extra tutoring hours in the spring term.

umm-al-quwain/best-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Subject by subject, the marks lost at IGCSE are predictable and documented in examiner reports. These are the papers Umm Al Quwain students most often ask for, with the specific failure each one is prone to.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Method marks are the whole game. Students who write only an answer lose the working marks even when the answer is right, and lose everything when it is wrong. Extended-tier losses cluster in algebraic fractions, transformations of graphs, and the bounds-and-accuracy questions that ask for an upper or lower limit.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: The calculator-assumed syllabus with an investigation component, taken by many international schools in the northern emirates. Students trained on 0580 past papers for an 0607 entry practise the wrong paper. Graphical solution of equations and modelling from data are where 0607 marks sit.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / 0972)
subjects.description: Electricity circuits and moments cost more marks than any other topics. The common loss is unit and prefix handling: milliamps entered as amps, centimetres into a formula expecting metres. Paper 6 alternative-to-practical questions reward precise description of method and sources of error, which is a writing skill, not a physics one.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / 0971)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and the mole-ratio step are the standard pressure point, followed by organic chemistry naming and the tests for ions and gases, which are pure recall and therefore pure revision-schedule discipline. Marks also go on equations left unbalanced after a correct method.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / 0970)
subjects.description: The highest-scoring students answer the command term rather than the topic. 'Describe' and 'explain' carry different mark structures, and a correct description where an explanation was asked earns nothing. Osmosis, enzyme graphs and transport in plants generate the most dropped marks in practice.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A paper many bilingual students in the northern emirates are entered for by default. Reading marks are lost to answers that quote without selecting; writing marks are lost to register and format, because a letter, a report and an article each have a shape the mark scheme expects.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Directed-writing and descriptive tasks are marked on content, structure and style separately. The usual loss is vocabulary used imprecisely rather than vocabulary that is missing, and paragraphs with no visible argument shape. Timed practice under real conditions is the only reliable fix.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (0450 / 0455)
subjects.description: Marks concentrate in the extended-answer questions, where students describe a concept and stop instead of applying it to the case material and then evaluating. The structure is learnable in a handful of sessions, and it usually moves a grade more than content revision does.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Offered to strong mathematicians as a bridge to A Level or IB higher-level maths. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive earlier than students expect, and the pace assumes the 0580 Extended content is already fluent rather than recently learnt.

sections.heading: What a parent should ask before paying for a first session
paragraphs: The word best is unverifiable on its own, so convert it into things a tutor can either produce or cannot. Five questions do most of the work. Which syllabus code is my child entered against? Which tier, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher? What will you mark in the first week, and against which mark scheme? What will I see in writing after session one? And what happens if the specialist for this subject has no slot that fits our evening?

Each of those has a correct kind of answer. A syllabus code is a short string like 0620 or 4MA1, and a tutor who cannot name it has not read the entry. A tier answer should come with the grade ceiling attached. A marking answer should name the paper and the series, not say 'some practice questions'. The written record after session one should be short enough to read on a phone and specific enough to argue with. And an availability answer should be a date, or a plain statement that the subject is not covered this term.

The same logic applies to price. A provider who will not put a number next to an hour is asking you to decide without the one piece of information you came for. The rate table further down this page quotes what the published market charges across provider models with the month it was read, because a comparison with no sources in it is just an assertion with a table border.

Finally, ask what the tutor will refuse to do. The honest answer includes refusing to write or complete coursework, refusing to promise a grade, and refusing to carry on with weekly sessions when the marked evidence stops moving. A tutor who refuses nothing is selling hours rather than teaching a subject.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Dropped marks at IGCSE are rarely mysterious. They fall into a small number of categories that repeat across subjects and across years, and almost all of them are habits rather than knowledge gaps. This is the single most useful thing a marked paper tells you, and the reason marking has to come before teaching.

Method marks are the largest category in maths and physics. A mark scheme awards credit for a correct step even where the final answer is wrong, but only if the step is written down. Students who do arithmetic on a calculator and transcribe one number lose every available method mark on a six-mark question when they slip. The fix is mechanical and takes a few weeks of insistence rather than a term of teaching.

Command-term failures are the largest category in the sciences and in humanities. State, describe, explain, suggest and evaluate each carry a different mark structure, and an answer written in the wrong register earns nothing however accurate it is. A student who learns to read the verb first and count the marks available before writing often moves a grade boundary without learning any new content.

Then there are the quiet ones: units and prefixes, significant figures, unbalanced equations, graph axes without labels, and answers given to the wrong degree of accuracy. Individually each costs one mark. Across a paper they add up to the difference between two grades, which is why the error list is kept as a running document rather than rewritten each week.

sections.heading: The exam series, counted backwards from the date your child sits it
paragraphs: Parents usually discover the exam calendar in the wrong order: the exam date first, the entry deadline months too late. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May or June and in November each year. Which series your child sits is a school decision, and it is the fixed point everything else counts back from.

The lead times are longer than they look, and the cleanest way to see it is to take the series an Umm Al Quwain candidate can actually sit. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE written papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026; the entries that put candidates into them closed in the summer term beforehand, and the results reached students the following January. Cambridge's June series holds the same proportions: entries and forecast grades are collected well ahead of the papers, with the closing date for your centre printed on its statement of entry rather than published as one national date. The entry decision therefore lands roughly a term before the paper, which is early enough that a family planning around the exam date alone will always be planning around the wrong one.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That is a sentence worth reading twice if you are planning travel in an exam window. Ask the school which zone timetable applies before booking anything in May or November.

Pearson's recent series give concrete anchors: the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so treat any date here as a pointer to the live official timetable rather than a substitute for it.

sections.heading: Five subjects, not six: Ministry of Education equivalency for IGCSE students
paragraphs: Families aiming at a UAE university meet the Ministry of Education equivalency process, and it is widely misdescribed. For the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

Two details in that rule change how a subject list should be built. The count is five, not six, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A ranking competitor page currently tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published clarification says. If you are choosing which subjects to drop or which to support, the five-subject count is the number to plan against.

The American track is different again: English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, while mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold is published in the source we can cite, so no figure appears on this page. Verify any IB equivalency number on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority before you plan around it.

Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not a service a tutor performs. IB Gram does not submit, expedite or guarantee equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it. What tutoring can do is make sure the five subjects a family is counting on actually land at or above the grade the process needs.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach here?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a parent can check the position in a few minutes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 regarding the introduction of private tuition work permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears on this page; figures circulating online for this could not be verified against a ministry source. MoHRE's own service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

There is a separate rule parents in Abu Dhabi and beyond should know about. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on the exact wording, but the direction is clear: your child's own classroom teacher is not the right person to hire privately.

A tutoring business with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor, requiring an educational services permit from the relevant authority. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and claims none: it is an independent tutoring platform, not a licensed school or a training institute, and any provider telling you its tutors are approved by a UAE regulator is describing something that does not exist in that form.

sections.heading: Where a tutor stops: coursework, controlled assessment and honesty
paragraphs: Several providers in this market sell completed coursework. One sells finished IB internal assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach, it puts the student's whole certificate at risk, and it is worth saying plainly on a page about choosing well, because the same offer is often made quietly in a WhatsApp conversation rather than printed on a website.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the skills a piece of coursework assesses, explain the assessment criteria, model the technique on a different example, ask the questions that expose a weak argument, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, dictate, restructure or complete any part of the work that must be the student's own, and may not supply text to be submitted.

In practice the honest version is more useful anyway. A student who has had an argument pulled apart in conversation and rebuilt it themselves can defend it under questioning and reuse the skill in the exam. A student handed finished prose has learnt nothing transferable and has a document they cannot explain if asked about it.

The same restraint applies to materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and a tutor should reference and link to the official source rather than hand over reproduced copies. If a provider is distributing a library of scanned mark schemes, that is a copyright problem rather than a feature.

sections.heading: What progress looks like, week by week, and when to stop
paragraphs: Grade movement is not smooth, and a plan that promises steady weekly gains is describing something that does not happen. The realistic pattern is a flat first fortnight while habits change, then a step when the method-mark and command-term fixes start landing, then slower grinding progress on content gaps that need teaching rather than correcting. Knowing that shape in advance stops a family abandoning an arrangement in week three that was about to work.

What should be visible every week is narrower: the error list shortening in specific categories, the marked score on comparable work holding or rising, and the student able to say what they got wrong without being told. The third of those is the strongest signal. A student who can name their own failure mode has internalised the correction; a student who cannot is still being carried.

The honest reason to stop is also worth stating. If two comparable marked papers four or five weeks apart show no movement and the error list is unchanged, the arrangement is not working, and the right response is a different tutor, a different subject, or a conversation about whether the tier is wrong. No tutor can promise a specific grade, and nobody should be paying for hours that the evidence says are not landing.

This is why the evidence sequence sits at the top of this page rather than at the bottom. In Umm Al Quwain, where the nearest alternative arrangement is a long drive away, the cost of discovering a bad fit in month four is much higher than it is in Dubai. Insist on the marked paper in week one, and the decision in week five is easy.

faqs.question: How do I judge the best IGCSE tutor in Umm Al Quwain when there is almost nobody local to compare?
faqs.answer: Stop comparing by proximity and compare by evidence. Ask each tutor which syllabus code and tier your child is entered against, what they will mark in week one, and what you will see in writing afterwards. A tutor who can name 0580 Extended Paper 4 and commits to marking a real past paper against the published scheme has told you more than any amount of local reputation. Because lessons run live online, the pool is every available specialist for that syllabus rather than the handful willing to drive to Umm Al Quwain on a weekday, so the comparison is between teaching records rather than postcodes.

faqs.question: My child goes to school in Sharjah and gets home after five. Can tuition still fit on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because an online session needs no travel on either side. A slot at half past five or six works for most commuting students, and the session ends on time rather than running into dinner because the tutor arrived late. For families in Falaj Al Mualla or Al Humrah, where the drive is longest, weekend morning sessions are often steadier than weekday evenings. The practical approach is to try one weekday slot and one weekend slot in the first fortnight and keep whichever one your child actually arrives at alert, rather than defending a timetable that looked sensible on paper.

faqs.question: Which syllabus codes should I be checking on my child's IGCSE entry?
faqs.answer: Ask the school in writing for the board and the code for each subject. Common ones are Cambridge 0580 for Mathematics, 0607 for International Mathematics, 0620 for Chemistry, 0625 for Physics, 0610 for Biology, 0500 or 0510 for English, and Pearson 4MA1 for International GCSE Mathematics. The code matters because the papers differ: a student entered for 0607 who practises 0580 papers is rehearsing a different assessment. Keep the reply from the school, since tier and syllabus decisions are sometimes revised and the written record is what a tutor plans against.

faqs.question: Does my child need five or six IGCSE subjects for UAE university equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published clarification on the British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page currently tells UAE parents six subjects are needed, which does not match the source. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before building a subject list around it, because equivalency rules are revised and a tutor is not the authority here.

faqs.question: What does a marked diagnostic paper in week one actually tell you?
faqs.answer: It separates the two problems that look identical on a report card. One is not knowing the content; the other is knowing it and not converting it into marks. A properly marked paper shows which it is, question by question: method marks lost to unwritten working, command terms answered in the wrong register, units and significant figures, equations left unbalanced, and marks abandoned on the last page because of timing. The teaching plan that follows is different for each category, which is why marking comes before any teaching and why an estimate instead of a real mark scheme is close to useless.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge IGCSE exams only in June, or can my child sit them in November?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May or June and in November each year. Which series your child sits is the school's decision as the exam centre. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong timetable was used. Ask the school which zone applies before booking travel in an exam window.

faqs.question: How far before the exam is the entry deadline, really?
faqs.answer: Months. Take the Pearson November 2026 series, where every date is published and checkable: the written papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, entries had closed in the summer term before them, and results reached students in the January that followed, as November 2025 results did on 22 January 2026. Cambridge in the UAE runs a June series and a November series, and the proportions are the same: the subject list is locked roughly a term before the paper, and the exact closing date for your centre is on its statement of entry. That is why a tier or subject conversation early in the year is worth more than extra revision in the final weeks, and why any tutoring plan should name the entry deadline alongside the exam date.

faqs.question: What do private tutors in the northern emirates charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published rates across the UAE market, read in October 2026, run from roughly AED 33 to 150 an hour for budget online platforms and student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel priced in, AED 200 to 450 or more for an IGCSE, IB or A Level specialist, and AED 500 to 650 upwards for a premium named tutor. Those are market figures from providers' own pages and from a published 2026 rate table, not IB Gram's price list. For our own numbers, the route is a free trial lesson and a consultation.

faqs.question: Is online tuition a compromise for a student in Falaj Al Mualla or Al Raas?
faqs.answer: For an IGCSE student with a laptop, it is the stronger arrangement rather than the fallback. The tutor pool widens from whoever will drive inland to every available specialist for the syllabus code, the session starts on the minute, and marked papers are annotated on screen and saved so the error list persists. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. In-home does suit a younger child who cannot yet manage a screen alone, or a household with unreliable connectivity, and it is worth being honest about that.

faqs.question: Where exactly must a tutor stop on an IGCSE coursework draft?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills the task assesses, explain the assessment criteria, model the technique on a different example, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, restructure to completion or supply text for submission, and no reputable provider should offer to. Some providers in this market sell completed assessed work outright, which risks the student's certificate rather than improving it. The useful version is also the honest one: a student who rebuilt their own argument after it was questioned can defend it and reuse the skill under exam conditions.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with UAE families need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Individual private tutoring is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its app and e-services system.

faqs.question: Should I hire my child's own subject teacher for private lessons?
faqs.answer: No. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond the rules, it is a poor arrangement: the person marking your child's work internally should not also be paid to prepare it. A separate tutor gives an independent read on where marks are being lost, which is the thing you are actually buying.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 student in Umm Al Quwain usually need?
faqs.answer: One subject at one session a week is the common starting point, moving to two shorter sessions on different evenings where there is both a weak science and a maths problem. Adding a third weekly session rarely helps before the error list from the first two has shortened, because the limit is usually how much corrected practice a student can absorb rather than how much teaching they receive. In the eight to ten weeks before a series, families often switch to full timed papers instead of topic work, which changes the shape of the week more than it changes the hours.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is available for my child's subject this term?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date or a plain no, before any payment. Niche subjects at Extended tier are the usual gap, and the worst outcome is a family waiting three weeks for a slot that was never coming. Where a specialist is genuinely unavailable, the honest options are a start date, a different subject prioritised first, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. A provider that quietly substitutes a generalist for a specialist has solved its own scheduling problem rather than your child's chemistry problem.

faqs.question: How will I know whether to continue after a month?
faqs.answer: Look at three things at week five. Has the error list shortened in named categories rather than in general? Does a second comparable paper, marked under the same conditions, show movement? And can your child say what they got wrong without being prompted? The third is the strongest signal of real learning. If two comparable papers four or five weeks apart show nothing and the error list is unchanged, change something: the tutor, the subject order, or a conversation with the school about whether the tier is right.

intro.heading: Nine subjects, two budgets, one report card
paragraphs: Most Cambridge IGCSE candidates sit eight or nine subjects. Published market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run from roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with IGCSE specialists quoted higher. Multiply either figure by nine subjects and a weekly hour each, and the result is a number no family treats as a tutoring budget. It is also a number no fifteen-year-old could survive, since nine weekly sessions would leave no evening free for the independent work the sessions are supposed to prompt.

So the real question a parent in Al Salamah or Al Raas is asking is not what a tutor costs. It is where to put a finite amount of money across a crowded report card, and that is an allocation problem with a method. The method starts with the last marked script rather than with the grade column, because the grade tells you where your child is and the script tells you why.

Delivery, before the numbers. IB Gram provides tuition to this emirate as one-to-one lessons over live video. There are no home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service. On a cost page the consequence is concrete. Published data puts visiting in-home rates above online rates, and the difference is an approach drive that, to Falaj Al Mualla or Al Riqqa, is long. Removing the format removes the line rather than haggling over it, and it widens the pool from whoever teaches Chemistry nearby to whoever has actually marked 0620 papers.

Cambridge specifics then do most of the work on this page. Every subject carries a syllabus code, and the code identifies the exact paper set your child will sit: 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics, 0620 for Chemistry, 0610 for Biology. Several subjects are tiered, and the tier your child has been entered for caps the grade available to them. That decision sits behind an entry deadline months before the examination, which makes it a spending deadline as well as an academic one.

There is a second Cambridge-specific trap in this market. Families buy revision material and practice papers for the wrong board. A school on the southbound run may enter candidates with Cambridge in some subjects and Pearson Edexcel in others, and the two differ in paper structure and in how practical skills are assessed. Money spent drilling the wrong paper style is not merely wasted; it builds the wrong habits, which is more expensive than doing nothing.

What follows is the allocation method, the codes and tier ceilings, the two question types that are cheapest to fix in most Cambridge papers, the entry calendar read as a budget calendar, and the exam-day costs families here discover late because their examination centre sits in another emirate.

programmes.countryNote: A number of schools on the Sharjah and Ajman run split boards by subject, so one candidate can be a Cambridge entry in Mathematics and a Pearson entry in Physics. The entry statement is the only document that settles it, and it should be read before any revision material is bought.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The continuation route for most Cambridge IGCSE candidates who do not move to the Diploma. It matters at IGCSE stage because the subjects and tiers chosen at 14 determine which A Level routes stay open, which turns a tier decision into a longer-term cost question rather than a one-year one.
programmes.countryNote: For the Ministry's British track, equivalency requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the IGCSE requirement. That is a reason to keep a route open rather than a reason to buy tutoring, and the Ministry is where it should be confirmed.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The alternative at the same age, assessed against criteria A to D on an eight-point scale instead of whole-paper marks. Families switching a child from MYP into a Cambridge IGCSE stream mid-course face a specific gap: the student is used to criterion-referenced feedback and unused to timed papers against a markscheme.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools within reach of this emirate run MYP, so mid-course transfers happen more often here than the national average. The transfer gap is narrow and cheap to close if addressed in the first term, and expensive if discovered in a Year 11 mock.

umm-al-quwain/cambridge-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Cambridge IGCSE subjects most requested from this emirate, with the syllabus code worth confirming and the question type that most often decides whether funding that subject is worth it.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Method marks are awarded for working students routinely skip, which makes this the cheapest subject on most report cards to improve. A candidate who writes the substitution line before the answer collects marks on questions they were already getting right. Confirm whether the entry is 0580 or the alternative additional syllabus.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Graph questions and apparatus description carry independently awarded marks, and where a school enters the written alternative to practical the apparatus language has to be taught explicitly. Both are narrow, drillable and therefore good value per hour.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations and ionic equations are reliable mark sinks and respond fast to drilling. If a marked script shows most losses concentrated there, this is a short funded block rather than a year of weekly support.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Long-answer questions are marked against specific points, so a student writing three paragraphs can score two marks. Teaching the student to count the available marks and plan that many points is mechanical and visible on the next script.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading items reward exact retrieval from the text while writing tasks reward register control, and a combined mark hides which half is weak. Break the script down by component before deciding whether this subject needs funding at all.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Directed writing and comparative analysis dominate, and the common loss is a competent answer that ignores the specified audience or form. A small number of targeted sessions on task compliance is frequently all that is needed.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Application to the given context is where marks separate, and generic answers are penalised. Annotating a marked script to show where application credit was awarded is usually the fastest route from a 4 to a 6.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram labelling and evaluation carry disproportionate weight. A correct explanation with an unlabelled axis scores a fraction of the same explanation labelled, which is a mechanical fix rather than a conceptual one.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode precision and trace tables are heavily weighted, and students who code fluently often write imprecise pseudocode. Specialist supply across the UAE is thin, which pushes the rate band up for reasons of availability.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken by a minority, usually those heading for A Level Mathematics. Worth funding only once the core Mathematics entry is secure, because an extension subject rarely rescues a grade in the parent subject and competes for the same evenings.

umm-al-quwain/cambridge-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Your address, your evening window, and what both do to the bill
umm-al-quwain/cambridge-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Two area-specific factors move the cost of Cambridge support here: how long an in-home tutor would spend approaching your door, and how late your child gets back from a school in another emirate. The second one decides how much choice you have at any given rate.

regions.name: Al Salamah
regions.note: The biggest residential block and the longest average southbound commute. Students home after 17:30 land in the most contested slot of the week, which narrows specialist choice rather than raising the published rate. Weekend mornings are where the saving is.

regions.name: Al Raas
regions.note: Older housing near the creek, frequently with two IGCSE candidates in the same household. Two children in Year 10 and Year 11 is an allocation problem squared, and the usual answer is one funded subject each rather than two for the elder.

regions.name: Al Riqqa
regions.note: A longer internal drive before reaching the main road, which is why in-home quotes to this area have always sat at the top of the local range. The workable pattern is a weekend long session for full timed papers plus one short weekday follow-up.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain Marina and the corniche
regions.note: Shorter commutes toward Ajman and newer apartment stock. A 17:30 weekday start is genuinely achievable, which puts these families outside the contested band and gives real choice of specialist at the lower end of the range.

regions.name: Al Humrah
regions.note: Nearest the Ajman boundary with the shortest school run in the emirate, and therefore the widest evening window. Families here can often fund two subjects for what a contested single slot costs elsewhere in Umm Al Quwain.

regions.name: Falaj Al Mualla
regions.note: Inland, around forty minutes from the coastal strip, with no realistic weekday access to a tuition centre. The comparison here is live video against nothing at all, and any in-home quote carries the largest travel component in the emirate.

regions.name: Al Haditha and the old town
regions.note: Close to the older schools and government offices. Several families here add private Cambridge entries alongside a Ministry school, which puts entry fees and centre arrangements into the budget as separate lines from tutoring.

schoolClusters.city: Cambridge entries on the southbound run
schoolClusters.note: These are the schools most Umm Al Quwain candidates attend, and their entry statements decide which board and tier each subject is sat under. Reading that statement in the autumn term is the single cheapest piece of planning available, because it prevents an entire season of revision on the wrong paper style.
schools: Our Own English High School, Sharjah

schoolClusters.city: The northern option: Ras Al Khaimah
schoolClusters.note: A smaller group of families travel north instead. Private education in Ras Al Khaimah is regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the documentation available to a parent there differs from the Ministry-supervised position inside Umm Al Quwain.

umm-al-quwain/cambridge-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Three formats, chosen mainly by what the commute allows. The relevant comparison is not the rate but the progress produced per dirham, and for a crowded IGCSE timetable the scoped short block usually wins.

modes.title: Scoped short block, four to six sessions
modes.description: The format that suits the allocation problem best. One subject, one named question type, a fixed number of sessions, and a finish line. Used for the mechanical fixes that dominate Cambridge papers: method marks in 0580, mole calculations in 0620, graph items in 0625. Cheap, measurable, and it ends rather than renewing by default.
bullets: One subject, one question type, a fixed session count
Best fit for drillable losses on a marked script
Ends on a date, so the budget does not quietly expand

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, 60 minutes
modes.description: For a subject where the gap is genuine content rather than technique, a weekly hour across a term is the right shape. It fits a weekday evening after the southbound run and produces one marked piece of work a week. Reviewed at six weeks against the question types it was bought to fix, and stopped when they move.
bullets: Suits genuine content gaps rather than mechanical losses
One marked artefact every week, reviewed at six weeks
Workable at 18:30 even after a long commute

modes.title: Weekend long session, 90 to 120 minutes
modes.description: The only format in which a complete Cambridge paper can be sat under timed conditions and marked in one sitting, which is the single most useful thing a Year 11 candidate can do. Weekend mornings also sit outside the contested evening band, so specialist availability is better at the same rate.
bullets: Full timed paper plus marking in one session
Better specialist availability than a weekday evening
The main session for Falaj Al Mualla and Al Riqqa families

sections.heading: What a Cambridge IGCSE tutor costs here, and the nine-subject arithmetic
paragraphs: Take the market bands first. Budget online tutoring in this country starts from around AED 45 to 65 an hour at the university-student end. A qualified subject tutor working online is published at AED 150 to 300. Specialists in IGCSE, IB or A Level are quoted from AED 200 upward, with one provider in this market publishing AED 650 for premium examiner-experienced work. In-home visiting rates sit higher than their online equivalents because an approach drive is inside the hour. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150, which is a reasonable anchor for the bottom of the qualified band.

Now apply that to a report card with nine subjects. One weekly hour in each, even at the bottom of the qualified band, is a monthly figure most households in this emirate would reject outright, and it would consume every evening a Year 11 student has. The constraint is not only money. It is attention, independent study time, and a commute that already takes an hour out of each end of the day.

This is why the useful question is allocation, not price. Two funded subjects out of nine is the normal shape for a family here that is spending sensibly: one where the gap is real content, one where the loss is mechanical and cheap to fix. Everything else is handled by the school, by the student, and by the fact that fixing the mechanical problem in one subject usually improves the same behaviour in three others, because command-term discipline and writing out method travel between papers.

The table below compares the plan families imagine with the plan that actually works. Our own figure is not in it, deliberately: the honest number depends on the subject, the tier and the number of weeks before the entry series, and it is quoted after a free trial session rather than before.

sections.heading: Triage: choosing which two subjects the money goes to
paragraphs: The report card is the wrong document to choose from. It tells you which grades are low, which you already knew, and nothing about why. The right document is the most recent marked script in each candidate subject, and ten minutes with a pen will sort the whole timetable.

Go through a script and label every lost mark: knowledge, method, or command term. Knowledge means the content was not known. Method means it was known but the step that earns the mark was never written down. Command term means the student answered a different instruction from the one printed, describing where the paper said explain. Count the three totals per subject.

A subject dominated by method losses is the cheapest fix available and should be funded as a short scoped block, not as a year of weekly support. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is the classic case: marks sit on working that students skip, and a four-session block on writing out method can show up on the next marked paper unambiguously. A subject dominated by command-term losses is a reading problem rather than a subject problem, and it is the most common pattern among second-language candidates across the northern emirates. Fixing it in one subject tends to improve several, which is why it is the best-value single purchase on most report cards.

A subject dominated by knowledge losses is the expensive one, and it is the only category that genuinely needs a weekly hour across a term. Fund one of those at most. If a script shows knowledge losses in four subjects simultaneously, the constraint is study time at home rather than teaching, and more purchased sessions will not touch it; that is a conversation about the student's week.

One warning on triage. Do not choose the subject the student likes least, which is the instinctive choice. Choose the subject where the marked script shows the largest block of recoverable marks, which is frequently a subject they feel fine about.

sections.heading: Codes and tiers: the decision that caps a grade before any money is spent
paragraphs: Cambridge identifies every subject by a syllabus code, and the code is not administrative trivia. It determines the paper set, the component weightings and therefore which past papers are worth buying. A family revising Mathematics without knowing whether the entry is 0580 or an alternative syllabus is drilling the wrong question styles at full price.

Several subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, and this is the decision with the largest financial consequence on the whole page, because tier caps the grade available. No amount of tutoring lifts a candidate above the ceiling their tier sets. Before spending anything on a tiered subject, establish which tier the school has entered the student for and whether a change is still possible. If the ceiling is the problem, the purchase that matters is a conversation with the school, not a tutor.

Tier changes also have a deadline, and the deadline is the entry date rather than the examination. Once entries are final the tier is fixed for that series. This is why a diagnostic in the autumn term is worth more than the same diagnostic in the spring: the autumn version can still change what the student is entered for, and the spring one can only optimise within a decision already made.

The practical sequence is simple and almost nobody follows it. Get the entry statement from the school. Write down the board, the code and the tier for every subject. Confirm the past-paper set that matches each. Only then buy anything. That half hour routinely saves more than a term of discounted sessions.

sections.heading: Where Cambridge marks go missing, and which losses are cheap
paragraphs: Across Cambridge papers the recoverable marks cluster in a small number of places, and most of them are procedural rather than conceptual. That is good news for a family with a finite budget, because procedural fixes are fast, measurable and transfer between subjects.

Working not written down is the biggest single pool. Mathematics 0580 awards marks for intermediate steps, and candidates who can reach an answer mentally or on a calculator lose them on questions they got right. Teaching a student to write the formula before the numbers is not teaching mathematics; it is teaching exam behaviour, and it shows on the next marked script.

Command terms are the second pool, and the most transferable. Describe, explain, state, justify, compare and evaluate each ask for something different, and each is worth a different number of marks. A candidate who writes a good description where the paper asked for an explanation has produced correct work that scores nothing. One focused audit across a single marked paper usually reveals more lost marks than a parent expects, and the fix generalises across Biology, Business Studies, Economics and Geography at once.

Third is answer planning on long-response questions. Marks are allocated against specific points, so a student writing three flowing paragraphs can score two marks while a student writing six short labelled points scores six. Fourth is the practical and data cluster: graph axes, lines of best fit, apparatus description, variable control, each independently awarded, and all of it drillable. Where a school enters the written alternative to practical, this cluster has to be taught explicitly rather than assumed from lab memory.
What is not cheap is unlearnt content across a two-year syllabus, and no honest page will tell you otherwise. That requires time at home, and purchased hours cannot substitute for it.
bullets: Writing out method: the largest recoverable pool, fastest to fix
Command terms: the most transferable fix on the whole report card
Answer planning: count the marks available, plan that many points
Graphs, apparatus and variable control: narrow and drillable
Unlearnt syllabus content: slow, and not solvable by buying hours

sections.heading: The entry calendar is a spending calendar
paragraphs: Every decision on this page expires on a date set by Cambridge, and the date that catches families out is the entry deadline rather than the examination. After it, the board, the subject and the tier are fixed for that series, and the only remaining variable is performance.

Cambridge gives a UAE candidate two series and the choice between them is itself a spending decision. June is the series the cohort sits; November is the resit route, the one that lets a student retake a single subject without repeating a year, and the one almost no tutoring page mentions. Entries for either close well ahead of the papers, with forecast grades collected before the examinations begin, and the exact closing date for your child comes from the centre's statement of entry rather than from a national announcement. The February-March series is not an option here at all: Cambridge offers it to India only.

Read backwards, that imposes a budget sequence. A diagnostic that could change a tier has to happen early in the course, well before entries close for the June series. A scoped block to fix method marks is best spent in the term after entries close, when the target is fixed and the behaviour still has months to bed in. A final-stretch block in the weeks before the papers is the least efficient money of the three, because the constraint by then is revision time rather than understanding. If June goes badly in one subject, the November series turns what would have been a repeated year into a single focused block, which is usually the cheapest recovery available.

Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, so a family with children at different stages may be working to more than one calendar at once. The zone point applies to all of it: every centre sits in one of six administrative zones, the correct version of the timetable for that zone is the one to use, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Confirm the zone with the centre your child is entered at, which for most households here is in Sharjah or Ajman rather than in this emirate.
