umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Each IB programme produces a different paper trail, and knowing which one your child is inside tells you what evidence to expect from a tutor. The notes below are written from that angle rather than as a curriculum summary.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, marked out of 8, and converted to a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. Because most MYP subjects have no external paper, almost all the evidence is school-generated: task sheets with criterion strands highlighted, and teacher comments tied to descriptors rather than to percentages.
programmes.countryNote: For an Umm Al Quwain family this is the easiest programme to audit, because the task sheets come home. A tutor working with an MYP student should be able to point at a specific criterion strand and show which band the work sits in, which is a far more useful conversation than one about effort.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects graded 1-7 plus the core. Evidence splits in two: internally assessed work marked at school against published criteria and moderated by the IB, and externally examined papers marked by examiners working from a mark scheme. The two produce different documents and fail for different reasons, so a tutor should be generating both kinds of evidence.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students here are usually enrolled in another emirate, so the school's internal deadline list is the document that governs everything. Ask a prospective tutor to work from it, and ask to see how the plan maps onto it; a plan that ignores the school's own draft dates will produce evidence at the wrong time.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects and school reporting
programmes.description: Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum under the Ministry's general regulations, and they appear on the same report card as the IB subjects, often on a different scale. Parents reading a report are therefore reading two assessment systems at once, which is a common source of confusion.
programmes.countryNote: Private schools in Umm Al Quwain are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, so reporting formats vary by school rather than following an emirate template. For these subjects, additional or different content requires prior Ministry permission, so any tutoring works from the school's own scheme.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: What a marked script tells you differs by subject. The entries below describe what to look for in each one when a tutor returns work, because that is how a parent judges whether the marking is real.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A properly marked script shows method marks awarded separately from answer marks, so a student who sets up correctly and slips at the final line still scores. If every question is simply right or wrong with a tick or a cross, the marking is not following the scheme and tells you nothing diagnostic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Look for comments on reasoning around calculator results. The commonest loss in this course is a correct figure produced by technology with no mathematical justification written beside it, and a marker who does not flag that is missing the main thing the examiner will penalise.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Data questions are the tell. A real marking should name missing uncertainties, inconsistent significant figures, and conclusions stated without reference to the data. Those are the same errors the scientific investigation loses marks for, so one piece of marking should be visibly useful in two places.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The useful marking here identifies terminology precision and command-term mismatch, not content coverage. A student who wrote an accurate general account of a process and scored half marks needs the specific missing term circled, which is what a returned script should show.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Working in symbols before numbers is the habit that earns method marks, and a returned script should show whether the student has it. Unit and magnitude errors under time pressure are the other recurring loss, and they only become visible when a paper has been sat to time rather than worked through at leisure.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Marking should be annotated at sentence level: where a point was stated without evidence, where the analysis slipped into summary, where a paragraph stopped short of linking back to the question. A global comment at the end of an essay is not evidence of anything a student can act on.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: The diagnostic marks here are about use rather than recall. A good marker will show where a diagram or framework was produced but never used in the argument, and where a judgement was expected and a description was given instead. That is the difference between a middle grade and an upper one.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Marking should cover the statistics section of the experimental report line by line, because that is where students lose most, and should distinguish between listing limitations and weighing them. Both are checkable by a parent reading the annotations, with no psychology background required.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Evidence here is draft history: successive versions with the research question sharpened, and comments tied to the assessment criteria. The student writes every word, so what a parent should see is a trail of their child's own drafts improving against descriptors, dated.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the IB under the Ministry's general regulations, and reported separately. Support works from the school's own scheme of work, since the use of different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry permission is not allowed, so expect evidence that maps onto the school's material.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Where the work actually gets done in Umm Al Quwain
umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: The evidence file depends on something mundane: whether the student has a place to sit, a device and twenty uninterrupted minutes. These notes are about that, area by area, because it is the most common reason an otherwise good arrangement produces nothing.

regions.name: Al Salamah
regions.note: Mostly family villas and apartments where the usual study spot is a shared living room. A headset and a door that closes change the quality of a session more than any change of tutor, and we raise it on day one rather than after a month of distracted hours.

regions.name: Al Raas
regions.note: Larger households are common here, with several children on different school runs. Where two siblings need support, separate evenings produce better evidence than a shared slot, because marked work can be attributed to one student rather than to a room.

regions.name: Al Riqqa
regions.note: Closer to the Sharjah road, so students are often home earlier and can work before fatigue sets in. The practical gain is that written work set between sessions actually gets done, which is what makes the fortnightly marked script possible.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain Marina and the corniche
regions.note: Newer apartments with ordinary household broadband, which is sufficient for one-to-one video and screen sharing. The limiting factor is usually a quiet corner and a second device for viewing a paper while talking, not connection speed.

regions.name: Al Humrah and Al Haditha
regions.note: Nearer the Ras Al Khaimah side, with many students schooled in RAK. Printing is worth arranging here: a paper sat on screen is useful, but a paper sat on printed sheets and photographed back produces the most honest timed-conditions evidence.

regions.name: Falaj Al Mualla
regions.note: Inland and a long way from any Diploma school, so independent study time at home carries more weight than anywhere else in the emirate. A fixed weekly slot plus set work is the arrangement that holds here; anything requiring travel does not.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman and Umm Al Quwain
schoolClusters.note: The nearest IB provision for many families, and a short enough run that students arrive home with an evening intact. Report formats differ between schools, so the first thing a tutor should ask for is a copy of the most recent report rather than a description of it.

modes.description: A fixed weekly slot per subject, with a short task set at the end of each session. Alternate tasks are marked in full against the published scheme or criteria and returned with the lost marks named, so there is a dated piece of evidence in the file every two weeks rather than a verbal account at the end of term.

The tutor reads what the student has written and says where it falls short of a band. The student produces every assessed word, and the evidence is the student's own draft history.

sections.heading: What "home tutor" buys, and what it does not
paragraphs: The honest version of this comparison starts with what in-home tuition genuinely does better. A tutor in the room is harder for a teenager to ignore. Materials are physically shared, a younger child can be supervised, and some students simply settle better with an adult beside them. For a Middle Years Programme student who will not engage with a screen, that can be the deciding factor, and a family in that position should take it.

What it does not buy is evidence. The documentation a parent wants - dated marked scripts, criterion-by-criterion draft notes, an error log - is produced by a tutor's working method, not by their location. A visiting tutor who talks through homework for an hour and leaves has given you a pleasant hour and nothing to inspect. This is the substitution most families make without noticing: presence feels like proof.

It also does not buy choice. Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate and its Diploma students mostly attend school elsewhere, so the pool of adults living nearby who have taught Higher Level Chemistry or Analysis and Approaches to examination standard is very small. Filtering by driving distance first usually means accepting a generalist, and a generalist cannot mark against a scheme they have never used.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service, and there is no UAE centre. What this page offers instead is the thing the search is really after, written down: specialists matched by subject and level, and an evidence trail a parent can audit each fortnight. The table sets the two options side by side on the criteria that matter rather than on atmosphere.

sections.heading: The evidence file: what should exist after four weeks
paragraphs: A month is long enough to judge the paperwork even if it is too early to judge the grade. By the end of week four a family should be holding a small, dated set of documents, and if they are not, that is the conversation to have rather than waiting for a report card to tell you.

Week one should produce a diagnostic: a short set of questions across the syllabus areas, one piece of the student's writing marked against the criteria or scheme, and a written statement of where the marks are going. Not a grade prediction - a list of specific losses. Week two should produce the first set task coming back marked, with the lost marks named. Week three should produce a second, and the beginnings of a pattern. Week four should produce the first honest statement of which losses are reducing and which are not.

The value of writing this down is that it converts a trust problem into an inspection problem. A parent who does not teach the subject can still check that the dates are real, that the annotations refer to specific questions, that the same error is not being named for the fourth week running without a change of approach, and that the student recognises what is in the file.

It also sets up the six-week review honestly. At six weeks there is enough evidence to say whether anything is moving. If the file shows the same three error types recurring at the same rate, the arrangement is not working, and the right response is a different tutor or a different plan decided then - not a wait-and-see that consumes a term.

sections.heading: How a paper is marked the way an examiner marks it
paragraphs: Most parents have never had examination marking explained, which makes it hard to tell real marking from decoration. The core idea is that marks are allocated to parts of an answer, not to its correctness overall. A six-mark question is six separate decisions, and a student can earn four of them while reaching a wrong final answer.

Method marks are the clearest example. In mathematics and the sciences, marks are available for setting up correctly, for substituting correctly, and for the answer, so a student who rearranges an equation properly and then mis-keys a number on the calculator loses one mark rather than all of them. The related rule is error carried forward: where an earlier mistake feeds a later part, the later part can still earn full credit if the method is correct from that point. A marker who crosses out everything downstream of the first error is not following the scheme.

Accuracy conventions carry their own marks. Significant figures and units are credited or penalised explicitly in the sciences, and premature rounding inside a multi-step calculation produces an answer that is penalised even though every step was sound. In written subjects the equivalent is the mark scheme's level descriptors, where the band is set by the quality of argument rather than by counting correct points.

This is why a returned script is the most informative document a tutor produces. A parent can look at it and see whether method marks were awarded separately, whether the annotations refer to specific scheme points, and whether the comments tell the student what to do differently. Those three checks need no subject knowledge, and they separate marking from ticking.
bullets: Method marks are awarded separately from the final answer
Error carried forward keeps later parts available after an early slip
Significant figures and units carry their own marks in the sciences
Written subjects are marked by level descriptor, not by counting points
Annotations should name the scheme point, not just mark it wrong

sections.heading: Reading an Internal Assessment draft against its criteria
paragraphs: Internal Assessment criteria are published, lettered and weighted, which means a draft can be audited rather than guessed at. This is the single most useful thing a tutor does with a Diploma student, and it is entirely legitimate because the student has written the draft and will do all the revising.

The mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest allocation and the rest sitting at three or four marks each. The pattern this reveals matters: a beautifully presented exploration using mathematics below the level of the course cannot reach the top bands, while a plainer piece at the right level can. Students almost always misjudge that trade.

The sciences scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, in equal allocations. Equal weighting is the useful insight: evaluation is worth as much as design, and it is the section students write last and shortest. Economics uses a portfolio of commentaries on published articles with strict word limits; History uses an investigation with its own source-evaluation section; Psychology an experimental report whose statistics section is the main loss. Confirm all of these against your child's current subject guide, since the IB revises them on a cycle.

The method is mechanical. Take one criterion, read the top-band descriptor aloud, and ask the student to point at the part of their draft that does what the descriptor says. Where they cannot, that is the work. Where they can, move on. A tutor talks the student through it; the student makes every change.

sections.heading: What grade movement actually looks like
paragraphs: This is where most tutoring marketing becomes dishonest, so here is the plain version. Diploma subjects report on a 1 to 7 scale, and a grade is a band containing a range of marks. A student can gain real marks and stay on the same number, or sit near a boundary and move a grade on a small improvement. Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone offering a predicted score before they have seen the student's work is guessing in front of you.

What moves first is not the grade. It is the shape of written answers: command terms read correctly, conclusions actually reached, working shown, data referenced. That is visible in a marked script within two or three weeks and is why the fortnightly script matters more than a monthly grade. The second thing to move is usually accuracy under timed conditions, which needs papers sat to time rather than worked through comfortably.

Internal Assessment marks behave differently again. Because the criteria are published and the work is produced over weeks, a draft audited properly against descriptors can gain marks that are then banked, independent of examination performance. For a student who is a borderline grade, this is frequently where the movement that matters comes from, which is an argument for starting the Internal Assessment conversation early rather than at the deadline.

A realistic timescale, stated honestly: answer quality within two to three weeks, measurable change in timed-paper accuracy across a term, and Internal Assessment marks secured on the school's own deadline schedule. Mock grades are a noisy signal, because mock papers and boundaries vary by school, so read them as a direction rather than a measurement.
bullets: A grade is a band of marks, so real gains can leave the number unchanged
Answer shape improves first, usually within two or three weeks
Timed-paper accuracy takes a term of repeated practice

sections.heading: When the evidence says it is not working
paragraphs: Tutoring arrangements fail quietly, and they fail in recognisable ways. The first pattern is a file with no student work in it: sessions happen, nothing is set, nothing comes back marked. The second is a file in which the same three error types are named every fortnight at the same rate, which means the diagnosis is right and the method is not changing. The third is a student who cannot say what they are working on, which usually means the hour is being driven by whatever homework is due.

None of these requires confrontation. They require a conversation at six weeks with the file open: what has been set, what came back, what is reducing. A tutor doing the job well will have the same picture and often the same concern. A tutor who treats the question as a complaint has answered it.

The remedies differ. Where nothing is being set, the fix is usually structural: a shorter session with a task attached rather than a longer discussion. Where the same errors persist, the fix is a change of method - timed conditions instead of untimed, or one topic rebuilt from the beginning instead of papers practised across all of them. Where the hour has become homework help, the fix is to separate the two explicitly, because homework help is a legitimate service but it is not what a Diploma student losing marks on command terms needs.

And sometimes the answer is a different tutor. Subject knowledge, marking discipline and the ability to hold a sixteen-year-old's attention over video are three separate skills. A change request is a normal part of the arrangement here, and a month into a two-year programme is a much better time to make it than after the first mock series.

sections.heading: What in-home tuition costs in the northern emirates, in AED
paragraphs: Families comparing options deserve numbers rather than a brochure. These are market rates compiled from providers' own published figures and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table. They are not IB Gram's price list, and they are published here because three of the six pages ranking for UAE tutoring queries publish no price at all while the two that do quote US dollars.

An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages advertised in the market sit around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online, a budget tutor is advertised from AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, while a qualified subject tutor sits at AED 150 to 300 and Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A named IB or A-Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium examiner-marketed tutors reach AED 500 to 650 or more, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

The northern emirates distort the in-home band in a way Dubai-written pages do not mention. Umm Al Quwain sits roughly an hour from the Sharjah tutoring market in ordinary traffic, so a visiting tutor is absorbing a two-hour round trip for a one-hour booking. That is paid for either in the rate, in a two-hour minimum, or in reliability - and the cancellation always arrives in the busiest term.

Judge any quote against two questions rather than against the number alone. What comes back marked, and how often? And is the person quoting it a specialist in the course your child actually sits? A lower rate for an hour that produces no evidence is more expensive than a higher rate that produces a marked script every fortnight.

sections.heading: Reading the school report alongside the tutoring file
paragraphs: Two documents describe your child's progress and they do not agree, which confuses parents more than anything else in the Diploma. The school report carries teacher assessment, often a predicted grade, and sometimes mock results. The tutoring file carries marked scripts and draft history. Each is measuring something different, and the useful reading comes from putting them side by side rather than choosing one.

A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by the school for university applications, based on the evidence the teacher holds at that moment. It is not a forecast of the final result and it is not a ceiling. Where a predicted grade is lower than a parent expected, the productive question to the school is which evidence it rests on, because that evidence is precisely what tutoring work can add to.

Mock grades are noisier than they look. Mock papers, timing and boundaries vary between schools, and a school may set boundaries deliberately high to concentrate attention. A mock grade is therefore a direction rather than a measurement, and it is most useful when read with the actual script beside it: which questions were lost, and whether they were lost to knowledge, to timing or to command-term misreading.

Because most students here attend school in another emirate, one practical step is worth taking. Ask the school for its internal deadline list for the year - draft dates, mock windows, Internal Assessment submission points - and give it to the tutor in full. Private schools in Umm Al Quwain fall under the federal Ministry of Education while those in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah fall under their own emirate authorities, so formats vary, and a plan written from the actual list produces evidence at the moments the school is going to look.

process.title: Send a marked script, not a description
process.description: The most useful first message contains the subject, the level, and a photograph of a recent marked piece of work. For a Diploma student the school's internal deadline list is the second most useful attachment. Those two documents let a tutor say something specific before the trial session rather than after it.

process.title: A free trial that produces a document
process.description: The trial session is with the tutor who would teach. It ends with a written diagnostic: the specific marks being lost, the command terms or criteria involved, and what the first four weeks would target. You keep that document whether or not you continue, and it is the first item in the evidence file.

process.title: A plan split between internal and external assessment
process.description: Internal Assessment and examination papers fail for different reasons and have different deadlines, so the plan separates them and says which gets the hours first. Usually the Internal Assessment leads, because its deadline is earlier and its marks are banked once submitted.

process.title: Weekly sessions, fortnightly marked work
process.description: A fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, one-to-one over live video. A task is set every week; alternate tasks come back fully marked with the lost marks named and the error log updated. A short written note goes to the parent after each session, in plain language.

process.title: Open the file at six weeks and decide
process.description: At six weeks the file either shows error types reducing or it does not. If it does not, the decision is a change of method or a change of tutor, made then. Requesting a different tutor is treated as a normal part of the arrangement rather than as a complaint.

whyPoints.title: Evidence rather than reassurance
whyPoints.description: A marked script every fortnight, an error log that carries forward, and a written note after each session. A parent who does not teach the subject can still audit dates, annotations and whether the same error is being named for the fourth time without a change of approach.

whyPoints.title: Marking that follows the actual scheme
whyPoints.description: Method marks shown separately from answer marks, error carried forward applied, significant figures and units treated as the marks they are. Ticks and crosses are not marking, and a script that shows the difference is the clearest proof of a competent tutor.

whyPoints.title: Internal Assessment work kept legitimate
whyPoints.description: Criteria read aloud, descriptors matched against the student's own draft, method taught explicitly - and every assessed word produced by the student. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that transaction puts the student's qualification at risk, not the seller's.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, not the nearest available adult
whyPoints.description: In the least populous emirate, filtering tutors by driving distance means accepting a generalist. Online delivery removes geography from the match, so the tutor is chosen for the subject and level the student actually sits and has used that mark scheme before.

whyPoints.title: Honest language about grades
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no score guarantees, no claimed improvement figures. What is offered is a named weakness, a method, and dated evidence - which is both more useful than a number and the only thing anybody can honestly offer two years out from a final session.

whyPoints.title: A free trial that leaves you something
whyPoints.description: The trial is free and produces a written diagnostic you keep regardless of what you decide. That is a better basis for a decision than a profile page, and it tells you how the tutor thinks before any money moves.

faqs.question: Can we get an IB home tutor who comes to our house in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and there is no UAE office or centre; tutoring for families here is one-to-one over live video. Independent tutors in the northern emirates do offer visits, and this page publishes the market rates so a quote can be judged. Before booking one, ask the same question you would ask us: what will be set between sessions, what comes back marked, and how often. Presence in the room is not the same thing as evidence of progress.

faqs.question: What proof should I have that the tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: By the end of week four you should hold a dated file: a diagnostic from the first session naming specific mark losses, a written plan split between Internal Assessment and examination work, at least two set tasks returned with the lost marks named, and the start of an error log. By week six there should be a statement of which error types are reducing and which are not. If the file is empty and the only evidence is a verbal report, that is the problem to raise, and it is the same problem whether the tutor sits in your living room or on a screen.

faqs.question: How can I tell real marking from a tutor just ticking answers?
faqs.answer: Three checks, none of which need subject knowledge. First, are method marks shown separately from the answer, so a student who set up correctly and slipped at the end still scores? Second, do the annotations name specific scheme points, or are they general comments at the end? Third, has the error carried forward rule been applied, meaning later parts still earn credit after an early slip? A script where everything downstream of one mistake is crossed out is not following the scheme and tells your child nothing they can act on.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB mathematics exploration worth and how is it split?
faqs.answer: It is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation and the others at three or four marks each. That split explains the commonest mistake, which is a beautifully presented exploration using mathematics below the level of the course. A plainer piece pitched at the right level scores higher. Check the exact allocations against your child's current subject guide, because the IB revises subject requirements on a rolling cycle.

faqs.question: How is the sciences scientific investigation marked?
faqs.answer: Out of 24 marks across criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, in equal allocations. The equal weighting is the useful part: evaluation is worth exactly as much as research design, and it is almost always the section students write last and shortest. A tutor can read a draft against each descriptor and say where it falls short of a band, while the student does every piece of the writing and revising. Confirm the current criteria with the subject guide your child's school is working from.

faqs.question: How quickly should we expect to see a grade go up?
faqs.answer: Not quickly, and any tutor promising otherwise is guessing. A Diploma grade is a band of marks, so real gains can leave the number unchanged for a while. What moves first is the shape of written answers - command terms read correctly, working shown, conclusions reached - and that is visible in a marked script within two or three weeks. Timed-paper accuracy takes a term of repeated practice. Internal Assessment marks are the exception: audited properly against the criteria, they are secured once submitted.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a predicted grade and a mock grade?
faqs.answer: A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by the school for university applications, based on the evidence the teacher holds at that point. It is not a forecast and not a ceiling. A mock grade comes from a paper the school set and marked, often against deliberately demanding boundaries, so it varies between schools and reads best as a direction rather than a measurement. Both are most useful read with the actual script beside them, because the script shows whether marks were lost to knowledge, timing or command-term misreading.

faqs.question: Our tutor is pleasant but nothing seems to change. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Open the file at six weeks and look for one of three patterns. No student work in it means nothing is being set, and the fix is usually a shorter session with a task attached. The same three error types named every fortnight at the same rate means the diagnosis is right and the method is not changing, so switch to timed conditions or rebuild one topic from the start. A student who cannot say what they are working on usually means the hour has become homework help. If none of that shifts it, change tutor; a month in is a much better time than after the mocks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor read my child's Internal Assessment draft without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards, read the top-band descriptor with the student, discuss the research question until it is answerable, teach the method, and say where a draft falls short of a band. The student writes every assessed word and makes every change. What nobody may do is supply paragraphs, rewrite a draft into final form, or provide text submitted under the student's name. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, and the malpractice consequence of that falls on the student.

faqs.question: What does an in-home IB tutor cost in the northern emirates?
faqs.answer: Market rates for an in-home one-to-one visit including travel run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500; monthly packages of four two-hour sessions are advertised around AED 1,599 to 1,799. Add the geography: Umm Al Quwain sits about an hour from the Sharjah tutoring market, so a visiting tutor absorbs a two-hour round trip for a one-hour booking, usually paid for in the rate, a two-hour minimum, or reliability. These are market figures, not IB Gram's.

faqs.question: Does my child need a quiet room, or is a laptop enough?
faqs.answer: A door that closes and a headset change the quality of a session more than almost anything else, and in shared family spaces they matter more than connection speed. Ordinary household broadband across this emirate handles one-to-one video with screen sharing. Two practical extras help: a second device so a paper can be read while talking, and a printer, because a paper sat on printed sheets to time and photographed back produces much more honest evidence than one worked through on screen.

faqs.question: Should two children in the same house share a session?
faqs.answer: Usually not, even when they take the same subject. The marked evidence is the point of the arrangement, and work produced in a shared hour cannot be cleanly attributed to one student, which makes an error log almost useless. Separate evenings also stop the stronger child setting the pace. Where cost is the reason, a better compromise is one child at a time with alternating weeks of marked work, so each has a genuine file rather than two half-files that show nothing in particular.

faqs.question: Which schools do Umm Al Quwain IB students usually attend?
faqs.answer: Most travel out of the emirate, to Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah, because Diploma provision inside Umm Al Quwain is limited. That places them under a different authority: the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah, and both also approve fees, curricula and assessment methods, while private schools in Umm Al Quwain itself are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The practical consequence for tutoring is that the school's own internal deadline list, not a generic IB calendar, governs the plan.

faqs.question: Is the tutor legally allowed to take payment for private lessons here?
faqs.answer: They need a private tutor work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any amount quoted online is unverified. Since the permit costs nothing, a tutor who has not obtained one has simply not done it.

faqs.question: What happens in the free trial session?
faqs.answer: It is a working session with the tutor who would teach, not a sales call, and it produces a document you keep either way. The tutor sets a short diagnostic across the syllabus areas, marks a piece of the student's own writing against the criteria or scheme, and writes up the specific marks being lost along with what the first four weeks would target. You should be able to read it without a teaching background, and it should contain no predicted grade, because nobody can honestly offer one on an hour's evidence.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Ask for the file, not the promise
umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are weighing up IB support in Umm Al Quwain, judge it on paperwork. Send the subject, the level and a photograph of a recent marked script, and we will arrange a free trial session, one-to-one over live video, with the tutor who would teach. You will come away with a written diagnostic naming the specific marks being lost and what the first month would target - and you keep that whether you continue or not. Then set the standard for whoever you choose: a marked piece of your child's own work every fortnight, an error log, and an honest review at six weeks.

intro.heading: Al Raas or UAQ Marina: the comparison most parents start with
paragraphs: A family deciding where to look for a tutor usually begins by narrowing the map. Al Raas against UAQ Marina, Al Raas against Al Salamah, Al Raas against Al Riqqa. The instinct is sound for anything that has to physically arrive. It does almost nothing for tutoring, and the reason is worth spelling out, because it saves a lot of wasted searching.

Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate. Its private international school provision is small, and a small cohort cannot staff the full spread of Diploma subjects. So most internationally schooled students from Al Raas commute out: to Ajman, which is the shortest run available from anywhere in the emirate and shorter still from Al Raas, or to Sharjah, or north to Ras Al Khaimah. That is true of UAQ Marina too, with roughly fifteen minutes more driving. The practical difference between the two neighbourhoods is a quarter of an hour of evening.

Now set that against what you are actually buying. A Diploma student needs somebody who has taught their specific subject at their specific level, knows where the marks go in Paper 2, and can tell the difference between an Internal Assessment that will sit mid-band and one that will reach the top criteria. In a thinly populated emirate, the number of such people inside a twenty-minute radius of either Al Raas or UAQ Marina is very small, and for a subject like Economics HL or Environmental Systems and Societies it may be zero. Fifteen minutes of driving does not change a zero.

That is the comparison answered honestly: the two areas differ, the answer does not. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. We match your child to the specialist who has taught the course, wherever that person is, and run the session over live video on your timetable. The market does supply in-home visits across the UAE at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour on published 2026 figures, with the drive folded into the rate, and this page sets out what that premium buys so you can judge it rather than take our word.

The fifteen-minute difference is real and it is the whole of the difference. What follows is built around the comparison rather than around a sales pitch, because a parent who understands why the areas converge stops searching by map and starts searching by syllabus, which is a faster route to the right tutor and a cheaper one. There is a neighbourhood-by-neighbourhood table of what actually differs, a sourced table of UAE market rates, an online-against-in-home comparison, the Diploma year counted backwards from the May session, the regulator map across the school commute, the academic-honesty boundary on coursework, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rules your child will meet when applying to a UAE university.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-raas.programmesIntro: Three entry points bring Al Raas families to this page: a Middle Years student heading into the Diploma, a DP1 student meeting coursework deadlines, and a DP2 student in the final run-in. The comparison between neighbourhoods matters least at the top of that list.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade through subject-specific boundaries. No external paper arrives before the optional eAssessment, so a student can go years without an externally benchmarked mark. The criteria have names and the marks are awarded against them, which almost nobody teaches explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: In Umm Al Quwain the MYP to DP step often coincides with a change of school, because the local set rarely offers both. An Al Raas student may move from an Ajman school to a Sharjah one and meet a new timetable and a new teaching style at once. The spring before DP1 is the cheapest place to absorb that shock.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades run 1-7 with up to three bonus points from the TOK and EE matrix. Higher Level carries 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and in most sciences the HL extension sits on its own paper.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. For an Al Raas student the dates that bind are the coordinator's internal coursework deadlines, which fall through DP1 and into DP2 and do not move. Build the year around those rather than around the exam window, and use the terms before the pressure arrives.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Up to three points come from the TOK and EE combination, and the core is where students lose ground quietly because nothing is marked weekly. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words with a supervisor; TOK is an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. CAS is not graded but is required for the Diploma to be awarded.
programmes.countryNote: Core work needs unbroken thinking time rather than a scheduled lesson, and a commuting Al Raas student has less of it midweek than a classmate living beside the school. Weekend sessions are worth more here than midweek ones, and we schedule them on purpose rather than as an afterthought.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-raas.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects Al Raas families ask about most, with what each assesses and where marks actually go. A tutor who cannot name the paper carrying the weight has not taught the course.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-and-algebra route. HL adds complex numbers, vectors and induction, and Paper 3 is a two-problem investigation worth 20% of the HL grade. Paper 3 is where marks disappear, because students have rarely worked sustained unfamiliar mathematics without a scaffold.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with a calculator throughout. HL brings graph theory, Voronoi diagrams and matrices. The habitual loss is interpretation: a correct regression without a sentence explaining what it means collects only the calculation marks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is multiple choice under tight timing; Paper 2 is extended response, where a numerically right answer with no reasoning chain loses the explanation marks. HL adds fields, induction and quantum material on its own paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and equilibrium carry the weight in Paper 2, and organic mechanism notation is the most common hidden gap. The internal assessment rewards real uncertainty analysis; a textbook experiment written up neatly sits mid-band.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Marked as a precision subject, not a recall one. Command terms decide the mark: outline, explain, describe, suggest and evaluate each want a different answer shape. Genetics and homeostasis are the usual collapse points.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The IA is three 800-word commentaries built on news articles the student finds. Marks go on choosing an article with no usable diagram and on summarising instead of analysing. HL adds Paper 3, arithmetic under time pressure.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis against a guiding question; Paper 2 is comparative essay. The Individual Oral links a global issue to one literary and one non-literary extract. Weak IOs are weak on the global issue, not the texts.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The case study decides the grade. Candidates who revise definitions and ignore the stimulus write generic answers and score poorly on high-tariff questions. Application to the named business is the assessed skill and it is teachable quickly.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Underestimated by students who pick it as a lighter Group 4 option. It needs systems diagrams, named dated case studies and value-perspective analysis. A generic answer about deforestation scores a fraction of a specific one.

sections.heading: Why Al Raas and UAQ Marina get the same answer
paragraphs: Because the variable that decides a Diploma grade is not distance. It is whether the person teaching your child has taught that subject at that level and knows where the marks are lost. Fifteen minutes of driving changes the convenience of an in-home arrangement and changes nothing about the supply of IB Economics HL specialists in the northern emirates.

Run the numbers rather than asserting them. Take a twenty-kilometre radius from Al Raas. It contains Umm Al Quwain city, part of Ajman, and not much else. Inside that radius, count the people who have taken a cohort through IB Chemistry HL and tutor privately and are free at 17:30 on a weekday. It is a short list, and for several Diploma subjects it is empty. Draw the same circle from UAQ Marina and the contents barely change: a little less of Ajman, a little more coastline.

So the comparison between neighbourhoods is real but it is a comparison about driving, not about teaching. Where the two areas genuinely differ is the evening window, and even there the difference is a quarter of an hour. Al Raas families with an Ajman school can sometimes start a session at 17:00. UAQ Marina families with a Sharjah school are usually looking at 17:45. Both are late by the standards of the tutoring market, which assumes a 16:00 start nobody in this emirate has.

The useful conclusion is to stop filtering by area and start filtering by specification. Ask a prospective tutor which subject and level, how many cohorts, and which paper candidates lose marks on. A specialist answers in a sentence. Someone who has not taught the course redirects to their degree. That question sorts the field faster than any map, and it works identically from Al Raas, the Marina, Al Salamah or Al Riqqa.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, cheapest band upwards
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages examined for this project in October 2026 published no price at all, and two quoted in US dollars, which is not a currency Al Raas families transact in. The figures here are market rates taken from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They describe the market, not an IB Gram price list.

Reading upwards from the cheapest band makes the structure visible. Budget online tutoring with a university-student tutor runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. The step to a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300 buys subject training and familiarity with the specification. The step to a board specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above buys level-specific exam experience, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. The step to in-home at AED 180 to 500 buys travel, not teaching.

That last point is the one this page exists to make from Al Raas. The in-home band overlaps the specialist band in price, but the money is doing a different job. In an emirate where the tutor has to drive in from Ajman or Sharjah, a large part of the rate pays for the road. Monthly packaging tells the same story: published figures include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Four questions to ask any provider before accepting a quote: is the rate per hour or per session, does it include VAT, what does a cancellation inside 24 hours cost, and does the figure change closer to an exam session. The answers tell you more than a rate card does.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home visit in Umm Al Quwain
paragraphs: An in-home tutor gives you presence: somebody in the room, nothing to disconnect, a teenager who cannot quietly open another tab. For a primary-age child that presence is genuinely worth paying for. For a DP2 student failing Paper 3, it is worth much less than knowing Paper 3.

Every structural feature of this emirate works against the in-home model. The pool shrinks to those willing to drive to Umm Al Quwain, which in a specialist Diploma subject may be nobody at all. The rate carries the drive. The appointment must be fixed against a bus arrival that cannot be predicted to the quarter hour. A cancellation on either side wastes a journey and is usually billed.

Online delivery reverses each of those. The pool becomes everyone who teaches the subject at that level. The rate drops because no one is paid to drive. A late bus costs ten minutes rather than an hour. Sessions can be recorded and rewatched the night before a paper, and past papers are screen-shared and annotated live, which is closer to a desk-side explanation than most parents expect before seeing it.

IB Gram offers only the online route in the UAE, and setting out the trade-off is more useful than pretending there is none. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. If physical presence is what your child needs, the market supplies it and you now know the price.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no specific IB exam or results date, and the reason is worth stating: the IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. A date a family plans a year around must be right, so take the session dates from your child's IB coordinator, who has them directly.

The shape of the year can be planned confidently, because the school sets most of it. The Extended Essay has supervisor meetings and a school draft deadline. Each Internal Assessment has a coordinator deadline, and in the sciences and mathematics those land in DP2 while teaching is still running. TOK has an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. Mocks sit roughly a term before the papers, and predicted grades for university applications come from work completed well before that.

Counted backwards, a Diploma student has four usable blocks: the first autumn of DP1, the spring of DP1 when coursework genuinely begins, the DP2 autumn when mocks and applications collide, and the final run-in. Three of those four are better spent on content and coursework than on past papers. The families who spend least in total are the ones who use the spring of DP1, which is also the term nearly everyone treats as quiet.

For a commuting Al Raas household this is sharper rather than softer. There are fewer usable weekday hours here than for a family living beside the school, so the hours have to be spent earlier in the two years. A student starting in DP2 is attempting the same work in a smaller container.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why no tutor is approved by them
paragraphs: An Al Raas family often lives under one regulator and sends a child to school under another. Umm Al Quwain private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, as are Ajman's and Fujairah's. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, activities and assessment methods. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge on the same model. Dubai has KHDA; Abu Dhabi has ADEK. Those five bodies are the complete map for UAE private schools.

That has practical consequences. A child at a Sharjah school is in a school whose fees and curriculum were approved by SPEA, not by the Ministry covering your home address, and questions about either go to SPEA. Move the child to an Ajman school and the same questions go federal. Families who assume one national system discover this at an inconvenient moment, usually when a fee question needs answering.

None of those bodies licenses individual tutors. Private tutoring is regulated separately through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears on this page.

Two consequences follow. No provider can honestly call itself approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes with premises in Dubai, and IB Gram holds no such permit, no accreditation from any UAE authority and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. And if your child's own teacher offers private lessons, check the rules: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of their own enrolled students, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars the same.

sections.heading: Coursework: the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: This is the boundary that carries real risk for your child, and this market handles it badly. One page examined for this project sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price. The student is the one whose Diploma is at stake if submitted work is not their own, which makes that transaction considerably worse than a waste of money.

A tutor may teach. That means explaining what each assessment criterion rewards and in what proportion, reading a draft your child has written and saying where it falls short of the descriptors, pointing out a research question that cannot be answered inside the word limit, teaching the statistics a Biology investigation needs, and explaining why a Chemistry IA reproducing a textbook method sits mid-band however neatly presented. All of that is feedback on the student's own work, and it is permitted and expected.

A tutor may not write, draft, complete, ghost-produce or edit to submission standard any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay, Personal Project or coursework. IB Gram does not, and declines the request when it is made. A second and quieter line: a tutor should not hand over board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to the IB. We cite and link to the official source instead.

The parent's test is simple. A legitimate session ends with your child holding a list of changes to make. If a cleaner document arrives in the inbox instead, you have bought something that can cost a Diploma, and convenience is not worth that.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, understood early
paragraphs: A Diploma student from Al Raas applying to a UAE institution meets the Ministry of Education's equivalency process, which converts a foreign school certificate into something UAE universities and employers can read. It is worth understanding two years early, because it constrains subject choices while they are still changeable.

The published British-track rules are specific and useful even to IB families with an IGCSE history: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus either one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. The five-subject figure matters because at least one ranking competitor page publishes six, and a family planning against the wrong number makes a real error.

On the American track, English proficiency requires 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB specifically, this page publishes no points threshold. We have not read one on the Ministry's own site, and inventing a figure here is exactly what a family would plan a year around. Ask the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority directly.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a Ministry process: IB Gram does not perform it, expedite it or guarantee an outcome, and we point you to the official channel. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. A provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free, and what we say instead
paragraphs: Every provider in this market writes as though a tutor is always available. None of them is. Coverage in a niche Diploma subject at a specific level in a late-evening slot is a real constraint, and concealing it is how families end up with a mismatched tutor two weeks before a paper.

We disclose it. If a specialist in your child's subject and level is not free in the window an Al Raas school run leaves, we say so and offer the alternatives: a different evening, a specialist based elsewhere working to Gulf Standard Time, or a wait. For a subject like Environmental Systems and Societies or Economics HL, a wait is sometimes the right answer, and we would rather tell you than fill the slot badly.

The matching conversation is short. We ask for the subject and level, the school and its assessment calendar, the two or three things the student keeps losing marks on, and the hours that genuinely work after the Ajman or Sharjah run. A free trial lesson follows, so you can judge the fit rather than take our word for it. If the fit is wrong, say so: a rematch in week one costs an hour, one in week six costs a term.

One note on fallback delivery. If the specialist who fits your child is not based in the UAE, the lesson still runs over live video on your timetable, and we tell you where they are before the first session rather than after it. Two ranking competitors route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without saying so, which is the thing we are trying not to be.

process.title: Send the subject, the level and the arrival time
process.description: The useful first message names the school, the year group, the subject and level, and the hour your child actually walks through the door on a normal weekday. From Al Raas with an Ajman school that is usually around 16:00; from a Sharjah school it is later. The plan is built from that number.

process.title: Send the coordinator's deadline list
process.description: Coursework deadlines, mock windows and report dates are set by the school and bind earlier than the exam window. A tutor working without them is planning against the wrong clock, and the Internal Assessment dates in particular arrive sooner than most families expect.

process.title: Take the free trial in the slot you would really use
process.description: One session, no commitment, booked at the real hour rather than a convenient weekend one. That tests the thing most likely to fail: whether your child can concentrate after the commute. Listen for whether the tutor diagnoses or lectures in the first twenty minutes.

process.title: Hold the slot for the term, then review against marks
process.description: Keep one hour a week rather than rebooking around each week's disruption. Every six weeks, compare the plan against marked evidence: school assessments, past-paper scores by question type, coursework drafts. If nothing has moved on what you targeted, change the plan or the tutor.

whyPoints.title: The comparison answered honestly
whyPoints.description: Al Raas, UAQ Marina, Al Salamah and Al Riqqa differ by minutes of driving and not at all in the supply of Diploma subject specialists. We say that rather than writing four pages implying four different local tutor pools, because the honest answer saves you a week of searching.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the course, not the commute
whyPoints.description: In the least populous emirate, filtering by willingness to drive can leave nobody at all in a specialist Higher Level subject. Matching on subject and level first, then teaching over video, gives an Al Raas family the same access as a family living beside the school gate.

whyPoints.title: Figures that carry a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, read in October 2026, and presented as the market rather than our price. Three of six competitor pages examined published no price at all and two quoted US dollars to families who pay in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: No approval claims, no invented numbers
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval from KHDA, ADEK or SPEA, no Ministry accreditation and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We explain what each body does and link out. You will find no satisfaction percentage or star rating here, because we cannot produce the data behind one.

whyPoints.title: A firm academic-honesty line
whyPoints.description: We teach, review and give feedback on the student's own work. We do not draft, complete or produce an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay or coursework, and we decline the request. One page in this market sells finished IAs; the student, not the seller, carries that risk.

faqs.question: Is an IB home tutor in Al Raas easier to find than in UAQ Marina?
faqs.answer: Marginally, and not in a way that matters. Al Raas is nearer the Ajman road, so the pool of people prepared to drive is slightly larger and the evening starts perhaps fifteen minutes earlier. Neither change the number of local people who have taught your child's Higher Level subject, which in several Diploma subjects is zero across the whole emirate. That is why we match on the course rather than on the map and teach over live video.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send anyone to an Al Raas address?
faqs.answer: No. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The market does supply in-home tutors at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour on published 2026 figures, with the drive inside the rate. In Umm Al Quwain that drive is long and the pool willing to make it for a specialist Diploma subject is very small.

faqs.question: Which neighbourhood in Umm Al Quwain has the shortest school run?
faqs.answer: Al Riqqa and Al Raas, both close to the Ajman border, so an Ajman school is reachable fastest from there. UAQ Marina and Al Salamah add roughly fifteen minutes, and Falaj Al Mualla adds considerably more. That shapes when a session can realistically start: around 17:00 from Al Raas with an Ajman school, 17:30 to 18:00 from the Marina with a Sharjah one. It does not shape which specialists exist within reach.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for Diploma tutoring from Al Raas?
faqs.answer: Published UAE market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a board specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Unitors IB from AED 200. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure. Umm Al Quwain is not separately surveyed, so treat the national bands as a guide. These are market figures from providers' own pages, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Is paying the in-home premium sensible in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the reason is geography rather than format. A tutor driving in from Ajman or Sharjah gives up substantial time in each direction, and that time sits inside your hourly rate. The same money online buys a specialist in your child's exact subject and level. The case where presence earns its keep is a younger child who needs somebody physically there to stay on task, not a Diploma student who keeps losing marks on a specific paper.

faqs.question: Where do most Al Raas students actually go to school?
faqs.answer: Out of the emirate, in most cases. Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate and its private international school set is small, so a cohort cannot staff the full range of Diploma subjects. Families wanting a particular Higher Level combination commute to Ajman, Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah. Ajman is the shortest run from Al Raas. The consequence for tutoring is a later, shorter evening window than the market assumes when it schedules a 16:00 session.

faqs.question: If we move from Al Raas to Al Salamah, do we need a new tutor?
faqs.answer: No. The specialist is matched to the subject and level, not to the postcode, and the session runs over video, so a move inside the emirate changes nothing except possibly the start time. A move that changes schools matters far more than a move that changes address: a new school means new coursework deadlines, a possible change of regulator, and sometimes a different set of option subjects. Tell us about a school change, not a house move.

faqs.question: Which regulator covers a school my Al Raas child attends in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, activities and assessment methods. Your home emirate of Umm Al Quwain is supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, as Ajman is. So fee and curriculum questions about a Sharjah school go to SPEA rather than to the Ministry covering your address. Families who assume a single national system usually discover this at the worst possible moment.

faqs.question: Is a permit needed to tutor privately in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: Yes, across the UAE. Private tutoring is regulated through a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount quoted at you with suspicion.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether a tutor really knows the Higher Level course?
faqs.answer: Ask which paper candidates reliably lose marks on at that level, and why. A person who has taught IB Physics HL or Maths AA HL answers in a sentence, naming a paper and a failure mode. A person who has not redirects to their degree or their years of experience. Follow up with how many cohorts they have taken through it. Those two questions sort the field far faster than any filter on distance, and they cost you nothing.

faqs.question: How much Extended Essay help is a tutor allowed to give?
faqs.answer: Yes, on your child's own draft. A tutor can say where the argument fails to answer the research question, where evidence is asserted rather than shown, and where the essay has drifted outside the subject's assessment criteria. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it to standard, or supply text, and IB Gram declines that request. A legitimate session ends with your child holding a list of changes. If a finished document arrives instead, the Diploma is what is at risk.

faqs.question: When should Internal Assessment work begin for a commuting student?
faqs.answer: Earlier than for a classmate living beside the school, because there are fewer usable weekday hours. The deadlines are set by the school's IB coordinator rather than the exam board, and in the sciences and mathematics they fall in DP2 while teaching continues. The research question work belongs in the spring of DP1. Families from Al Raas who front-load into DP1 spend fewer total hours than those who start in the DP2 autumn, when mocks and applications collide.

faqs.question: Can both of our children be tutored on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in commuting households it is the arrangement we set up most often. Two consecutive video slots, each with the right specialist for that child's subject and level, occupies one evening rather than disrupting two. Nobody is travelling, so there is no second travel premium and no second arrival to coordinate. Each child gets separate session notes, which matters when one is in DP2 and the other still in the Middle Years Programme.

faqs.question: Do sessions keep running if we travel for Eid or over the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you want them to. The only requirements are a connection and an agreed hour, so a session follows a family abroad without renegotiation. A fortnightly rhythm with a past paper in between holds far more ground across a long break than it costs, and a Diploma student who loses six weeks of momentum in July pays for it in the DP2 autumn. Agree the holiday arrangement in advance rather than cancelling week by week.

faqs.question: What does a Ramadan schedule look like for an Al Raas family?
faqs.answer: Later. School days shorten, household routines invert, and the mid-afternoon hour that worked in January becomes unusable. The productive window moves to after Iftar, and a video session at 21:00 costs nobody a journey, which an in-home arrangement cannot match. Decide before Ramadan whether sessions pause, shorten or shift late, rather than renegotiating weekly. When Ramadan falls in spring it sits directly on the revision weeks before the May session.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-raas.closingHeading: Compare the neighbourhoods if you like, then compare specifications
umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-raas.closingBody: Al Raas, UAQ Marina, Al Salamah and Al Riqqa are genuinely different places to live and almost identical places to find a Diploma specialist from. The variable worth comparing is not the drive but the course: which subject, which level, how many cohorts, and which paper candidates lose marks on. Send us the subject and level, your school's coursework deadline list and the hour your child is actually home, and take the free trial lesson in that real slot. If the match is wrong, tell us in week one and we will change it.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-riqqa.tutorsIntro: The profiles below cover the Diploma subjects Al Riqqa families most often fund: Maths AA and AI, the three sciences at both levels, Economics and Business Management, plus Extended Essay and Internal Assessment coaching.

intro.heading: The number first, then what it buys
paragraphs: Of the six competitor pages examined for this project in October 2026, three published no price at all, and one of those has a frequently asked question that asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. Two of the remaining pages quote US dollars, a currency no household in Al Riqqa pays anything in. So the honest starting point for a page about hiring a Diploma tutor here is the figures, sourced, in dirhams, before any argument about quality.

Here they are. Budget online tutoring with a university-student tutor runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 survey reaching 450 or more. An in-home one-to-one visit costs AED 180 to 500, Bestimate putting it at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. Premium named tutors run AED 500 to 650 or above, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Monthly is how a family actually budgets. Published package rates include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. None of these are IB Gram prices. They are the market, published by the parties named, and quoted here so you can argue with any quote you receive.

Now the part the market does not tell you: which band is actually buying teaching. Step from budget to qualified and you buy subject training. Step from qualified to specialist and you buy level-specific and paper-specific experience, which in a Diploma subject is the thing that moves a grade. Step from online to in-home and you buy travel. Al Riqqa sits at the Ajman end of Umm Al Quwain, which is the best position in the emirate for a drive and still means a tutor coming from Ajman or Sharjah is giving up a chunk of their afternoon, and billing you for it inside the hourly rate.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. We match on the subject and level and teach over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which removes the travel line from the invoice entirely. The rest of this page prices out that comparison, sets tutoring against the other costs of a Diploma, lists the hidden extras worth asking about before you pay anybody, and names the three ways families in this emirate reliably waste money on tutoring.
