umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-riqqa.programmesIntro: The cost of Diploma support depends far more on when a family starts than on the hourly rate they pay. These are the three entry points, in ascending order of cost per point gained.

programmes.name: The year before the Diploma
programmes.description: Work done before DP1 begins is content and skill foundation: algebraic fluency, written structure, the habit of sitting a timed paper. Nothing is at stake yet, so the sessions are cheap in every sense. A student who arrives in DP1 able to work under a clock does not need the expensive intervention later.
programmes.countryNote: In Umm Al Quwain this stage is unusually valuable because the move into the Diploma often comes with a change of school, city and teaching style at once. An Al Riqqa student may go from a local school to an Ajman or Sharjah one in a single September. A term of preparation at budget or qualified rates costs a fraction of a DP2 rescue at specialist rates.

programmes.name: Diploma year one
programmes.description: DP1 carries the content load and the start of the coursework: the Extended Essay research question, the first Internal Assessments, the TOK exhibition. Nothing feels urgent and almost everything that will later be urgent is being decided. Hours spent here buy more per dirham than hours spent anywhere else in the two years.
programmes.countryNote: This is the discount nobody takes. Al Riqqa families typically call in the DP2 autumn, when mocks, coursework deadlines and university applications collide inside an evening window already shortened by the Ajman school run. The same work done a year earlier costs fewer hours because nothing has to be repaired first.

programmes.name: Diploma year two and the run-in
programmes.description: DP2 is coursework completion, mocks, predicted grades and paper technique, in that order of urgency. Tutoring here is diagnostic rather than comprehensive: find the question types where marks are reliably lost and work on those. It is the most expensive stage per unit of improvement because the cheap options have expired.
programmes.countryNote: Specialist rates apply most strongly here, because demand peaks before the May session and the available slots are the late ones a commuting Al Riqqa household already needs. Families who book in the DP2 autumn pay more per hour and need more hours. The honest advice is to call a year earlier, which is advice against our own short-term interest.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-riqqa.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects Al Riqqa families fund most often, with where the marks go. Subject choice affects cost: a subject with a heavy internal assessment needs coursework hours as well as paper hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-and-algebra route. HL adds complex numbers, vectors and induction, with Paper 3 a two-problem investigation worth 20% of the HL grade. Paper 3 is the most expensive gap to leave open, because it needs practice rather than explanation and practice takes weeks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics, calculator-permitted throughout. HL carries graph theory, Voronoi diagrams and matrices. The common loss is interpretation rather than calculation, which is cheap to fix once diagnosed and expensive to leave because it recurs on every paper.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is multiple choice under tight timing; Paper 2 is extended response where a right number with no reasoning chain loses the explanation marks. The internal assessment needs real uncertainty treatment, so budget coursework hours separately from paper hours.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and equilibrium carry the weight in Paper 2 and organic mechanism notation is the most common hidden gap. The IA rewards a genuinely personal investigation; a reproduced textbook experiment sits mid-band however neatly written, which is a costly discovery to make late.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Marked as precision, not recall. Command terms decide the mark: outline, explain, describe, suggest and evaluate each want a different answer shape. Genetics and homeostasis are the usual collapse points under timing, and both respond quickly to targeted work.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The IA is three 800-word commentaries built on news articles the student finds, and a badly chosen article wastes a fortnight. HL adds Paper 3, arithmetic under time pressure. Budget for commentary coaching as a separate line from exam preparation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The case study decides the grade. Candidates who revise definitions and ignore the stimulus write generic answers and lose the high-tariff marks. Application to the named business is the assessed skill and it is among the cheapest improvements available in the Diploma.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis against a guiding question; Paper 2 is comparative essay. The Individual Oral links a global issue to one literary and one non-literary extract. Weak IOs fail on the global issue rather than the texts, which is a planning problem and therefore inexpensive.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies must be used as evidence rather than recited: name the study, state the finding, then say what it licenses and what it does not. HL adds the extension options and a heavier research-methods load, which is where the paper separates grades.

sections.heading: Tutoring set against the other costs of a Diploma
paragraphs: A tutoring quote means nothing in isolation. Set against the cost of the two years it sits in, the decision becomes a question of proportion rather than a question of whether AED 250 an hour sounds like a lot, which it does out of context and does not in it.

Start with the anchor. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. That matters to an Al Riqqa family mainly as a benchmark: a household already paying international school fees in Ajman or Sharjah, where SPEA approves fees in that emirate, is weighing a tutoring budget against a school bill that is an order of magnitude larger.

Against that, published tutoring figures look different. A weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor at Bestimate's AED 600 to 1,200 a month is roughly the cost of one subject's worth of attention across a school year. A specialist exam-year arrangement at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month is a meaningful commitment and usually a temporary one, concentrated in two or three terms rather than spread over the full two years. The published AED 799 monthly online package for eight sessions is the cheapest structured option in the market as read in October 2026.

The table below puts the pieces together so the proportions are visible. It deliberately does not include an IB Gram price, because this page is not a price list and our own arrangements begin with a free trial lesson and a conversation. What it does is let you judge any quote you are given, from us or from anyone else, against the market and against the rest of the bill.

sections.heading: The five bands, and what the money is actually doing
paragraphs: An hourly rate is not a quality score. It is a bundle of things, and the bundles differ. Working up the bands shows what each additional dirham is buying, which is the only way to tell whether a quote is good value or merely expensive.

From AED 45 to 150 an hour you are buying availability. A university-student tutor can keep a capable child moving, explain homework, and hold a routine. What you are not buying is specification knowledge, and at Diploma level that matters, because the difference between a 5 and a 6 is usually technique against a specific paper rather than understanding of the topic. From AED 150 to 300 you are buying subject training and familiarity with the course. From AED 200 to 450 and above you are buying level-specific and paper-specific experience: someone who has taken cohorts through HL and can name the failure modes without looking them up.

From AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit you are buying presence plus travel. Presence is genuine value for a younger child. Travel is pure cost, and in Umm Al Quwain it is a large one: a tutor driving from Ajman or Sharjah to Al Riqqa gives up roughly two hours of their day to deliver one. At AED 500 to 650 and above you are buying reputation, and any claim of examiner status should be evidenced rather than accepted, because it is unverifiable from a website and is often used to imply access to marking or boundaries that nobody has.

The practical test is to ask what the rate includes and then price the pieces. If two quotes are AED 250 and AED 320 and the second includes the drive, the second is cheaper on teaching and more expensive overall. If a quote is AED 200 and the tutor teaches a different board, it is not a bargain at any price.

sections.heading: The travel premium, priced out for Al Riqqa
paragraphs: Al Riqqa is the best-placed address in Umm Al Quwain for an in-home arrangement, because it sits nearest the Ajman border. That is worth saying because it means the figures here are the most favourable version of the in-home case anywhere in the emirate, and even at their most favourable they are not compelling for an exam-year Diploma student.

Consider what the tutor is selling. One hour of teaching requires them to leave Ajman, drive north, teach, and drive back, which is somewhere between two and three hours of their working day depending on the hour. A rate that makes that worthwhile has to price all of it. That is why the in-home band at AED 180 to 500 sits above the online qualified band at AED 150 to 300 despite often being the same person: the difference is the road.

Set against that, what online delivery removes is not just the travel cost but the travel risk. The appointment no longer has to be fixed against a bus arrival time nobody can predict. A late arrival costs ten minutes instead of a wasted journey that is usually charged anyway. And because nobody is driving, an evening slot at 19:30 is as cheap as one at 17:00, which matters in a household whose child commutes out of the emirate.

The one case where the in-home premium earns its keep is a younger child who genuinely needs an adult physically present to stay on task. That is a real need and it is worth paying for. It is not the situation of a DP2 student who keeps losing marks on Paper 2 extended response, where the thing worth paying for is somebody who knows Paper 2. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.

sections.heading: The three ways families here waste money on tutoring
paragraphs: The first is paying a specialist rate for a generalist, which happens most often through the in-home route. A family pays AED 300 an hour for somebody willing to drive to Al Riqqa, and the person who arrives teaches the right subject at the wrong level, or the right level on a different board. The money was spent on willingness to travel. Nobody set out to buy that, and nobody discovers it until week three.

The second is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. Six sessions of general revision costs AED 900 to 1,800 on published market bands and changes very little, because nobody has established where the marks are actually going. Three or four sessions spent marking past papers against the official scheme and sorting the losses by cause — content not known, method not shown, command term misread, units and notation, time ran out — tells you what the next twenty hours should contain. Almost no family has seen their child's losses sorted this way, and the analysis costs less than the wasted hours it prevents.

The third is starting late, which is the most expensive of the three and the hardest to see at the time. Work done before DP1 or during DP1 is cheap: the student is not under pressure, the rate is lower because specialist exam-year demand has not kicked in, and nothing has to be repaired first. The same outcome pursued in the DP2 spring needs more hours, at higher rates, in the late slots that are hardest to book, while coursework deadlines and university applications compete for the same evenings. Families call us in the DP2 autumn and the honest answer is often that the cheap window has closed.

A fourth waste deserves naming even though it is rarer: buying assessed work. One page examined for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is not expensive tutoring, it is a transaction that puts a Diploma at risk, and the student carries the consequence rather than the seller.

sections.heading: Hidden extras: the questions to ask before paying anybody
paragraphs: A rate is only comparable if you know what it contains, and the market is inconsistent about that. Two providers quoting AED 250 can mean materially different things, and the differences are rarely volunteered. These are the questions that expose them, and they apply to us as much as to anyone else.

Is the figure per hour or per session, and how long is a session? A 45-minute session quoted hourly is a 33% increase that looks like a flat rate. Does it include VAT? We do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as a general rule because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation, but any provider should tell you plainly whether the number they quoted is what leaves your account. What happens on a cancellation inside 24 hours, by either side? Does the rate rise closer to an exam session, when demand peaks? Is there a charge for the match, for session notes, or for a progress report?

Then the questions nobody asks. What happens if the tutor turns out to teach a different board or level than your child sits? What happens if the fit is wrong in week two — is there a rematch, and is it charged? If a free trial is offered, what is the condition attached: a minimum booking, a card on file, a notice period? A conditional free trial is fine; one presented as unconditional and then revealed is not.

Our own answers, for comparison. The match is not charged. The trial lesson is free and carries no minimum booking. Session notes come with every session. If the fit is wrong, say so and we rematch rather than argue. We publish no price list on these pages because an honest one depends on subject, level and availability, and a number invented for a page is worse than a conversation.

sections.heading: What no amount of money can buy in this market
paragraphs: Some things are on sale in the UAE tutoring market that nobody can legitimately supply, and knowing what they are protects a budget as effectively as comparing rates.

Nobody can sell you regulator approval. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK; Sharjah by SPEA; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. None of those bodies approves or accredits a tutoring provider. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, requiring initial approval and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, no accreditation from any UAE authority and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no provider should imply otherwise.

Nobody can sell you a promised grade. A tutor can teach technique, diagnose losses and hold a student to a plan; the outcome belongs to the student and the examiner. Any offer of a top-grade promise, a point-gain promise or money back on results should be read as a sales device unless the exact refund terms are published and honoured. Nobody can legitimately sell you completed coursework, and nobody can sell you access to marking, unreleased papers or grade boundaries.

Nobody should be selling you the MoHRE permit either. The private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, treat any specific amount quoted at you as unverified.

sections.heading: Equivalency is free, and not something to pay a tutor for
paragraphs: A Diploma student from Al Riqqa applying to a UAE institution meets the Ministry of Education's equivalency process. It converts a foreign school certificate into something UAE universities and employers can read, and it is a Ministry process rather than a service a tutoring provider performs. Nobody should be charging you to handle it, and we do not offer to.

The published British-track rules are useful even to IB families, because most IB students in the UAE have an IGCSE history behind them: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. At least one ranking competitor page publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong and is the kind of error a family budgets around.

On the American track, English proficiency requires 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB Diploma specifically, this page publishes no points threshold, because we have not read one on the Ministry's own site. An invented figure here would be a figure a family plans two years around. Ask the Ministry, the emirate attestation authority, or your school's university counsellor.

One further caution with a direct cost implication. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. Any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process in order to sell hours, and that is a reason to end the conversation rather than to open your wallet.

sections.heading: Coursework: the only purchase that can cost more than it costs
paragraphs: Every other decision on this page is about value for money. This one is about risk. One page examined for this project sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price, and that transaction can cost a student their Diploma, which no refund covers.

What a tutor may legitimately be paid for is teaching. That means explaining what each assessment criterion rewards and in what proportion, reading a draft the student has written and saying where it falls short of the descriptors, triaging a research question that cannot be answered inside the word limit, teaching the statistics a Biology investigation needs, and explaining why a Chemistry IA that reproduces a textbook method will sit mid-band however neatly it is presented. All of that is feedback on the student's own work, and it is both permitted and worth paying for.

What a tutor may not do is write, draft, complete, ghost-produce or edit to submission standard any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay, Personal Project or coursework. IB Gram does not and declines the request. A quieter line applies too: a tutor should not hand over board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because those belong to the IB. We cite and link to the official source instead.

The test is cheap to apply and it works every time. A legitimate coursework session ends with your child holding a list of changes to make. If what arrives is a cleaner document, you have bought something whose downside is the qualification itself, and that is the one purchase on this page where the price is not the point.

process.title: Say the subject, the level and your budget shape
process.description: Tell us whether you are thinking in hours a week or dirhams a month, because the two lead to different plans. A monthly figure lets us say honestly what it will and will not cover at published market rates, rather than quoting an hourly number that sounds reasonable and then needing twice as many hours.

process.title: Buy the diagnosis before the hours
process.description: Send four marked past papers if you have them. Three or four sessions sorting lost marks by cause costs far less than twenty hours of general revision and tells you what those hours should contain. Most families have never seen their child's losses broken down this way.

process.title: Take the free trial, with no condition attached
process.description: One session, no minimum booking, no card required, at the hour you would genuinely use. Al Riqqa's position near the Ajman border often makes a 17:00 start workable. Watch whether the tutor diagnoses or lectures in the first twenty minutes, because that is what you are paying for later.

process.title: Review the spend against marked work every six weeks
process.description: Compare what you have paid against what has moved: school assessment marks, past-paper scores by question type, coursework feedback. If the numbers have not shifted on what you targeted, change the plan or the tutor. A rematch in week two costs an hour; one in week ten costs a term of fees.

whyPoints.title: The price question answered rather than deflected
whyPoints.description: Three of six competitor pages examined publish no price at all, and one asks the cost question in its own FAQ and then refuses to answer it. This page leads with sourced AED bands, names who published each one, and states plainly that they are market figures rather than ours.

whyPoints.title: The travel premium made visible
whyPoints.description: An in-home tutor driving from Ajman or Sharjah spends two to three hours of their day to deliver one, and the hourly rate prices all of it. Al Riqqa is the best-placed address in the emirate for that drive, and even here the premium buys the road rather than better teaching.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis costed before hours
whyPoints.description: Three or four sessions sorting lost marks by cause costs less than the twenty hours of general revision it replaces. We would rather sell a short diagnostic block and a precise plan than a long open-ended arrangement that nobody can evaluate.

whyPoints.title: No approval claims and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval from KHDA, ADEK or SPEA, no Ministry accreditation and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. You will find no satisfaction percentage, star rating or student count on this page, because we cannot produce the underlying data for one.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We teach, review and give feedback on the student's own work. We do not draft, complete or produce an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay or coursework, and we decline the request. It is the only purchase in this market whose downside is the qualification itself.

whyPoints.title: Advice against our own short-term interest
whyPoints.description: The cheapest Diploma support starts in DP1, when nothing is urgent and specialist exam-year demand has not pushed rates and slots. Telling an Al Riqqa family that in the DP2 autumn means selling fewer hours, and it is still the honest answer.

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in Al Riqqa charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published UAE market figures read in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500, travel included in the figure. Online, a qualified subject tutor sits at AED 150 to 300 and an IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more. Al Riqqa is the closest part of the emirate to the Ajman border, so in-home quotes here should sit at the lower end of that band.

faqs.question: Do the published monthly packages work out cheaper for us?
faqs.answer: It depends what the package contains. Published market packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is eight contact hours either way at roughly double the price for the in-home version. A package is good value if the sessions genuinely get used; it is poor value if a commuting household misses two a month. Ask what happens to unused sessions before committing.

faqs.question: Where does the money go in an in-home tutoring rate?
faqs.answer: Partly into teaching and substantially into driving. A tutor coming to Al Riqqa from Ajman or Sharjah spends two to three hours of their working day to deliver one taught hour, and a sustainable rate prices all of it. That is why the in-home band at AED 180 to 500 sits above the online qualified band at AED 150 to 300 even when it is the same person teaching. Online delivery removes the line rather than discounting it.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible way to support a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Start in DP1 and buy a diagnosis before buying hours. Work done in DP1 costs fewer hours because nothing has to be repaired first, and specialist exam-year demand has not yet pushed rates or filled the late slots a commuting family needs. Three or four diagnostic sessions, costing far less than twenty hours of general revision, tell you exactly which question types are losing marks. Fortnightly maintenance across long breaks is the cheapest insurance available.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an Al Riqqa address?
faqs.answer: No. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The market does supply in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 an hour on published 2026 figures, and this page sets out what that premium is paying for so you can judge whether it suits your child rather than taking our word for it.

faqs.question: How much should six weeks of exam preparation cost?
faqs.answer: On published bands, six weekly hours with a qualified subject tutor runs roughly AED 900 to 1,800, and with a specialist roughly AED 1,200 to 2,700 or more. Whether that is worth spending depends entirely on whether the hours are targeted. Six sessions of general revision with no analysis of where marks go changes little. Six sessions aimed at three question types identified from marked papers can move a grade boundary. Buy the analysis first.

faqs.question: Are there charges besides the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and they are rarely volunteered. Ask whether the figure is per hour or per session and how long a session runs, whether it includes VAT, what a cancellation inside 24 hours costs on either side, whether the rate rises before an exam session, and whether there are charges for matching, session notes or progress reports. Our own position: no charge for the match, no minimum booking on the trial lesson, and session notes included every time.

faqs.question: Can a provider promise a better grade if we pay more?
faqs.answer: No, and you should treat any such offer as a sales device. A tutor can teach technique, diagnose where marks are going and hold a student to a plan, but the outcome belongs to the student and the examiner. Promises of a top grade, a specific point gain or money back on results should only be considered where the exact refund terms are published and honoured on the same page. IB Gram makes no promise of that kind, because none would be honest.

faqs.question: How much does the private tutor permit cost a tutor?
faqs.answer: Nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. If anybody is charging a tutor for the permit itself, that is a fee the ministry does not levy.

faqs.question: Does tutoring cost more in exam term?
faqs.answer: In this market, often yes, because specialist demand peaks before the May session and the late evening slots a commuting Al Riqqa household needs are the first to fill. That is one more reason the DP1 year is the cheap window. Ask any provider directly whether their rate moves with the calendar, because a figure quoted in September that rises in February is a different proposition from a fixed one, and the difference is rarely volunteered.

faqs.question: Is a small group cheaper and does it work?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per student, yes, and it works for content coverage rather than for technique. A group of two to four can be taught a topic efficiently. What a group cannot do is sit with one student's marked paper and work through the specific reasons that student loses marks, which is where Diploma gains usually come from. Ask what the actual group size is, because two and six are very different products sold under the same name.

faqs.question: What should we not pay a tutoring provider to do?
faqs.answer: Four things. Do not pay for regulator approval: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA and the Ministry of Education regulate schools, not tutoring providers. Do not pay for a promise about a grade. Do not pay for completed coursework, which risks the Diploma itself and is the one purchase where the price is irrelevant. And do not pay anybody to handle Ministry of Education equivalency, which is a Ministry process that we describe rather than perform.

faqs.question: How does Al Riqqa compare with the rest of the emirate on cost?
faqs.answer: Favourably, for in-home arrangements, because it is the closest part of Umm Al Quwain to the Ajman border and therefore the shortest drive. UAQ Marina adds roughly fifteen minutes and Falaj Al Mualla considerably more, which pushes an in-home quote towards the top of the AED 180 to 500 band for identical teaching. Online rates do not vary by address at all, which is the simplest argument on this page.

faqs.question: What does school fee context tell us about a tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: It gives the proportion. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, which is a useful anchor even for a family schooling in Ajman or Sharjah, where SPEA approves fees in its emirate. Against an international school bill, a weekly hour at AED 600 to 1,200 a month is a marginal addition rather than a second school fee.

faqs.question: If we can only afford one subject, which one?
faqs.answer: The Higher Level subject with the heaviest internal assessment weighting and the weakest current marks, in that order. HL subjects carry 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level and contribute the same points, so a point gained at HL costs the same as one gained at SL and is usually harder to get unaided. Where coursework is both heavily weighted and unstarted, that is the subject to fund, because a deadline missed cannot be recovered at any rate.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-salama.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma Programme at Standard and Higher Level. Each works from the current subject guide, the published assessment criteria and your child's own drafts, and each has taught or examined the subject rather than read about it.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a published specification, so treat it like one
paragraphs: Al Salamah is the older residential core of Umm Al Quwain, and the families here running an IB Diploma timetable are a small cohort. That has one real advantage: nobody in this household is competing for a school revision club place. It has one real disadvantage, which is that there is no informal network of parents comparing notes on Higher Level Chemistry, and no cluster of DP specialists living fifteen minutes away. The gap gets filled with syllabus knowledge or it does not get filled at all.

The useful starting point is that the Diploma hides very little. Each subject has a published guide setting out the syllabus content, the assessment components and their weightings. Each Internal Assessment has criteria identified by letter with a stated maximum mark. Each paper question opens with a command term whose meaning is defined, and the mark scheme pays for that definition being met. A student losing marks is almost always losing them in a nameable place, and the first job of a tutor is to name it.

That is why a session here starts with a document rather than a conversation. A marked Paper 2 script, a first draft of the Mathematics exploration, a TOK outline, a lab report with the criterion letters scribbled in the margin by a teacher in a hurry. From those, a tutor can say that your child is not weak at Chemistry, but is losing four marks a paper by answering outline questions as though they were explain questions. That is a fixable thing. A general sense of struggling is not.

Delivery matters less than diagnosis, but it does matter, so here it is plainly. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person visits are an India-only service. Every lesson for an Al Salamah family happens one-to-one over live video, which is also what makes a Higher Level Economics specialist reachable from this address at all. A shared screen is the right surface for this work anyway: criteria and mark schemes get annotated, and the annotated version stays with your child afterwards.

One more thing is worth saying before the content starts. Diploma tuition bought as reassurance is expensive and tuition bought against a named deficit is cheap, and the difference between them is whether anybody looked at a script first. Families in the northern emirates often arrive at this search in DP2 with three subjects they are worried about and a budget for one. A marked paper in each of the three almost always reorders that list, and quite often shows that only one of them needs paying for.

What follows is subject content, not sales copy. Maths AA against AI, where marks go missing in each group, the exploration criteria letter by letter, the command terms that carry the most money, the honesty boundary around the IA and the Extended Essay, and what a genuinely useful eight weeks of past-paper work looks like.
bullets: Every DP subject has a published guide with named assessment components and weightings
The Mathematics exploration is marked against five criteria totalling 20 marks
The Extended Essay carries a 4,000-word ceiling

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-salama.programmesIntro: Al Salamah students reach the Diploma by several routes, and each route produces a different kind of gap. These are the stages we teach, framed by what the content jump actually consists of rather than by age alone.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: MYP subjects are assessed against four criteria, A to D, with descriptors rather than mark schemes. Students learn to write against a descriptor, which is a genuinely useful habit, but they are not drilled on timed recall or on the volume of content the Diploma assumes. The gap that shows up in DP1 is usually pace and retention rather than reasoning.
programmes.countryNote: In Umm Al Quwain the MYP-to-DP move frequently involves changing school as well as programme, because the campuses within commuting range that run the full Diploma are few. A student arriving in DP1 from a different campus is managing new teachers, a new cohort and a new assessment model at once.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 1
programmes.description: The year that decides the Diploma. Six subjects start at once, the Extended Essay is chosen, TOK begins, and the first Internal Assessments are set. Most of the damage done in DP1 is invisible until DP2: a Maths exploration topic chosen because it sounded interesting rather than because it allows mathematics at the right level, or a subject taken at Higher Level on the strength of an IGCSE grade.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Salamah family the DP1 priority is usually the IA calendar rather than the content. Internal deadlines sit inside the school year and cannot be renegotiated from a distance, so a student who misses the school's draft window has lost the feedback that the published criteria assume they received.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 2
programmes.description: Content finishes, Internal Assessments are submitted, predicted grades are issued and the examination session arrives. The work that moves a score in DP2 is almost entirely paper technique: reading the command term, allocating time by mark, and showing the working a mark scheme pays for. New content learned in DP2 rarely repays the hours it costs.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Al Quwain students sitting as part of a school cohort will be examined at their own campus in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah, which means the exam logistics belong to the school. The revision calendar, however, belongs to the household, and that is the part a tutor can hold.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-salama.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Al Salamah families book most often. Each entry says what the subject assesses and the specific place marks leak, because that is the information a parent cannot get from a subject brochure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic manipulation, calculus and proof, with a strong non-calculator component at both levels. Marks leak on unsimplified exact answers, on differentiation by rule where the chain rule was needed, and on students writing the answer without the line of working the mark scheme awards.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-heavy methods. The commonest avoidable loss is interpretation: a correct regression equation followed by no sentence saying what it means in context, or a hypothesis test with a p-value and no stated conclusion about the null hypothesis.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mechanism rather than recall, which is the shock for students arriving from IGCSE. Energetics, equilibrium and organic pathways carry the heaviest load. Marks go on sign conventions in enthalpy, on omitting state symbols, and on explaining a trend without naming the underlying periodic property.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The mathematics is the barrier more often than the physics. Students lose marks by quoting a formula without defining its symbols, by mishandling vector components, and by answering describe when the question said explain. Uncertainty and graph-gradient work is reliably under-practised.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A large content load assessed with precise language. Command terms distinguish state, outline, describe and explain, and the mark scheme pays by that distinction. Data-based questions reward students who quote a value with its unit from the stimulus before interpreting it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams and evaluation carry the grade. A correctly drawn and fully labelled diagram earns marks on its own; an evaluation needs a judgement supported by a stated criterion rather than a list of advantages and disadvantages. Real-world examples must be named and dated to count.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-led answers: students who reach for the right framework and apply it to the stimulus outscore students who know more theory. Marks are lost on generic answers that could apply to any firm, and on calculations presented without the formula or the units.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis of how a text produces an effect, across paper-based analysis, the individual oral and the HL essay. The commonest loss is summary dressed as analysis: a student retelling the content of a passage instead of examining the choices the writer made.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Productive and receptive skills across five prescribed themes, with a written assignment and an individual oral. Internationally schooled students often have strong spoken Arabic and weak written register, which is exactly the way round that costs marks in this subject.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-salama.regionsTitle: Umm Al Quwain districts we teach into
umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-salama.regionsIntro: Delivery is online, so the district affects when a lesson sits rather than whether it is available. These notes are about the practical shape of a Diploma week from each address.

regions.name: Al Salamah
regions.note: The established residential centre of the emirate, with the shortest run to the Ajman boundary. A DP2 student here can usually hold a 16:30 weekday slot, which matters when two Higher Level subjects both need weekly attention.

regions.name: UAQ Marina
regions.note: North of the town on the corniche side. Longer morning and evening run, so Diploma families here tend to put the heavier Higher Level session on a weekend morning and keep weekdays for shorter paper drills.

regions.name: Al Raas
regions.note: Towards the old town and the lagoon. Households here frequently split children across campuses in two emirates, so DP sessions get scheduled around a sibling's primary-school pickup rather than around the DP student's own day.

regions.name: Al Riqqa
regions.note: Inland towards Ajman, with the most forgiving commute of the main districts. Useful for the DP1 pattern of two short sessions a week rather than one long one, which suits Internal Assessment drafting better.

regions.name: Al Haditha
regions.note: On the Falaj Al Mualla road, quieter and more predictable in traffic terms. Reliable fixed slots are easier to hold here, which is the single biggest predictor of whether a DP2 revision plan survives to March.

regions.name: Al Humrah
regions.note: Southern edge of the emirate towards Sharjah. Students here often finish school earliest in practice, and can take the late-afternoon slot that Marina students cannot.

regions.name: Falaj Al Mualla
regions.note: The inland town, roughly forty minutes from the coast. For a Diploma student here online tuition is not a convenience but the only realistic route to a Higher Level specialist in a minority subject.

schoolClusters.city: Diploma campuses within commuting range
schoolClusters.note: Umm Al Quwain students taking the full Diploma almost always travel to a campus in a neighbouring emirate. Those schools are regulated by the authority of the emirate they sit in, not by Umm Al Quwain, so inspection reports and fee approvals follow the campus.
schools: American School of Creative Science, Al Layyah

schoolClusters.city: Where Umm Al Quwain itself sits
schoolClusters.note: Private schools in Umm Al Quwain are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level regulator, which is the position u.ae states for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Families moving here from Dubai or Abu Dhabi are often surprised that there is no local equivalent of KHDA or ADEK to consult.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-salama.modesIntro: Three shapes of Diploma support, each built around a different piece of the specification rather than a different length of lesson. All are delivered one-to-one over live video.

modes.title: Weekly subject teaching against the guide
modes.description: One subject, one hour a week, worked through the published syllabus content in the order the school is teaching it. The point is to stay level with class rather than to run a parallel course, because a student being taught two versions of the same topic learns neither well. Written work is set between sessions and marked.
bullets: Topic order follows the school's scheme of work
Each session ends with a set question and a deadline
Marked against the published mark scheme, not impressions
Short written note to you after every lesson

modes.title: Internal Assessment supervision, criterion by criterion
modes.description: Work on the student's own exploration, investigation or essay, read against the criteria the IB publishes and the school's internal deadlines. The tutor's job is feedback and process coaching: naming which criterion a draft is weak against and why, then letting the student rewrite it. The writing stays the student's own throughout.
bullets: Criteria named by letter with their maximum marks
Feedback on the student's draft, never text supplied for it
Planning built backwards from the school's draft deadline
Academic-honesty boundary stated at the first session

modes.title: Paper technique in the run-up to the session
modes.description: Timed papers, command-term drilling and mark-by-mark review. This is the highest-yield work in DP2 and the lowest-yield in early DP1, because a student needs the content before technique has anything to operate on. The block is sized by the diagnosis rather than by a package length.
bullets: Opens with one timed paper marked to the real scheme
Time allocated per question by marks, then practised
Command terms drilled as a separate skill
Full papers under timing in the final fortnight

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that shapes two years
paragraphs: The Mathematics route decision is made in DP1 and felt for twenty-four months, and it is the question Al Salamah parents ask most often once they understand that the two courses are not harder and easier versions of each other. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, calculus and proof route. Applications and Interpretation is the statistics, modelling and technology route. Both exist at Standard and Higher Level, and both are respectable.

The honest decision rule is prerequisite-led rather than preference-led. Engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and most economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. Medicine, biological sciences, business, psychology and design subjects are usually satisfied by either, and sometimes by Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level. Because admissions requirements differ by university and by year, the only safe approach is to read the entry requirements for two or three target courses and work backwards from them, then confirm with your school's university counsellor.

The second decision rule is diagnostic. A student who enjoyed algebraic manipulation at IGCSE and coped with surds, indices and rearranging formulae without a calculator will usually survive Analysis and Approaches. A student who understood the mathematics but relied on the calculator for every step is likely to find the non-calculator paper punishing, and will often achieve a better score, and learn more, in Applications and Interpretation at the appropriate level.

What a tutor can do with this is narrow and useful: set a short diagnostic of pre-Diploma algebra, mark it against the kind of working the Diploma pays for, and tell you honestly whether the Higher Level option is a stretch or a mistake. Changing route in DP1 is uncomfortable. Changing it in DP2 is usually impossible, which is why the diagnostic belongs in the first term.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks actually go missing, group by group
paragraphs: Ask a DP2 student why they lost marks and the answer is usually that they ran out of time or did not revise enough. Mark a script against the published scheme and the answer is almost always more specific than that, and more fixable. The losses cluster, and they cluster differently by subject group, which is why a general study-skills tutor is poor value in the Diploma and a subject specialist is good value.

In the sciences the dominant loss is explanation that stops one step short. A student names the trend but not the cause, or gives the cause but not the mechanism, and the mark scheme pays for the step that was not written. The second-largest loss is data handling: units dropped, uncertainties ignored, a gradient quoted without the two points it came from.

In mathematics the dominant loss is working. The Diploma pays for method, and a student who writes the answer alone forfeits the method marks even when the answer is right. In the individuals and societies group the dominant loss is evaluation: a developed judgement with a stated criterion earns the top band, while a balanced list of points does not. In language A the dominant loss is summary presented as analysis.

The table below is the version of this a tutor uses in a first session. It is not a promise about any particular student; it is where to look first, and it is the reason a marked script is worth more than an hour of conversation about how the term has been going.

table.caption: COMMONEST RECOVERABLE LOSSES BY SUBJECT GROUP
columns: What it looks like on a script
rows: Trend named, cause or mechanism missing
Rewrite three answers to the mark scheme's step count
Correct answer with no line of working
Re-attempt with working mandated, then compare
Add a stated criterion and a conclusion to each
Annotate a paragraph for technique before writing
Correct content in the wrong text type
Drill the conventions of each prescribed text type

sections.heading: The Mathematics exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Internal Assessment criteria are published by letter with a maximum mark attached, and almost nobody writing about IB tutoring online names a single one. That is strange, because the criteria are the whole instruction manual. For the Diploma Mathematics exploration the criteria are presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, and they total twenty marks.

Knowing the weightings changes behaviour. Use of mathematics carries the largest single allocation, which means a beautifully written exploration built on mathematics below the level of the course cannot reach the top band however polished it is. Reflection and personal engagement together carry a substantial share, which means a technically strong piece with no genuine commentary on what the student tried, abandoned and reconsidered also caps out. Students routinely over-invest in presentation, which is the smallest lever available.

The practical sequence that works is therefore unglamorous. Choose a topic that forces mathematics at or just above course level. Confirm with the teacher that the topic admits that mathematics before any writing starts. Do the mathematics first and the narrative second. Then write the reflection last, from notes kept during the work rather than invented afterwards, because invented reflection reads exactly as invented and is marked accordingly.

Other subjects use different criteria and different totals, so check your child's own subject guide rather than generalising from the Mathematics exploration. The principle transfers even where the letters do not: find the criterion with the largest maximum mark, and make sure the piece is designed to satisfy that one first.

table.caption: DP MATHEMATICS EXPLORATION CRITERIA AND MAXIMUM MARKS
rows: Padding, or a report with no visible plan

A topic lifted from a list with no personal line of enquiry

sections.heading: Command terms are worth more than content, and nobody drills them
paragraphs: Every Diploma paper question starts with a command term, and each term has a defined meaning that the mark scheme enforces. State wants a short answer with no justification. Outline wants a brief account. Describe wants a detailed account without reasons. Explain wants reasons or causes. Discuss wants a balanced review with opposing arguments considered. Evaluate wants an appraisal with strengths and limitations weighed and a judgement reached.

Students who treat these as synonyms lose marks at a steady rate across every paper they sit, and the loss is invisible to them because the content in their answer was correct. A student who explains when the question said state wastes time they then do not have at the end of the paper. A student who describes when the question said explain writes an answer that simply cannot reach the marks available, no matter how accurate it is.

Drilling this is quick and it is one of the few genuine shortcuts in the Diploma. The exercise is to take one past paper, strip the questions down to command term plus mark allocation, and write only the shape of each answer: how many distinct points, whether reasons are needed, whether a judgement is required. Twenty minutes of that is worth more in DP2 than an hour of re-reading notes.

It also disciplines timing, because the mark allocation tells a student how long a question is worth. A six-mark explain question and a one-mark state question are not both answered in a paragraph. Allocating minutes by marks, then practising inside that allocation, is the mechanical half of paper technique, and the command term is the other half.

sections.heading: The honesty line on the IA, the Extended Essay and TOK
paragraphs: This needs saying plainly because at least one site ranking for UAE tutoring queries sells completed Internal Assessments. A tutor may teach, explain, set practice, read a draft and say where it falls short of a criterion. A tutor may not write, part-write, rewrite or supply text for any piece of assessed work. The Extended Essay, the Internal Assessments, the TOK exhibition and essay must be the student's own work, and the consequence of breaching that falls on the student.

In practice the boundary is easier to hold than people expect, and the test is simple: could the student reproduce and defend every sentence in the document? Feedback that says this paragraph asserts a result you have not derived is teaching. Feedback that consists of the derivation, written out, is not. A tutor who helps a student narrow an Extended Essay research question from unanswerable to answerable has done the most valuable hour of the whole project without writing a word of it.

The Extended Essay has a 4,000-word ceiling, and the single most common structural failure is a question too broad to answer inside it. The second is a question that cannot generate argument, only description. Both are cheap to fix in week one and expensive to fix in month four, which is why a tutor's first Extended Essay session should be about the question rather than the content.

For TOK, the useful support is also upstream. The essay titles are prescribed, and the work that moves a grade is choosing the title you can argue with real examples and then finding examples precise enough to be interrogated. A tutor can press on whether a claim survives a counter-example. A tutor cannot supply the claim, and should refuse if asked.

sections.heading: What eight useful weeks of past-paper work actually look like
paragraphs: Past-paper practice is the most recommended and least well executed activity in the Diploma. Most students do papers, mark them generously, note the score and move on, which trains nothing. The version that works is slower, covers fewer papers and produces measurable movement.

Week one is a single timed paper, marked strictly against the published scheme, with every lost mark categorised: content gap, command term misread, working not shown, timing. That categorisation is the whole diagnostic. Weeks two to five attack the largest category rather than the largest topic, in question-sized pieces, with the same question type repeated until it stops going wrong. Weeks six and seven return to full papers under timing. Week eight is light, because a tired student in the examination hall loses more marks than an under-revised one.

The IB publishes its own papers, mark schemes and subject guides, and schools hold them. A tutor should reference those documents and work from the copies your child's school has provided rather than circulating them, because reproducing board material is a copyright matter. Any tutoring service offering a library of past papers as downloads is telling you something about how it handles rules generally.

One practical note for Umm Al Quwain households. The Diploma examination session UAE schools sit is the May session, and IB session and results dates are published by the IB itself and by your child's school. We do not restate them here, because this project has not been able to verify them from the IB directly, and a wrong date on a page a parent plans around is worse than no date. Ask your IB coordinator, and work your eight weeks backwards from what they tell you.

sections.heading: Who regulates the campus, and who licenses the tutor
paragraphs: Two separate questions get confused on tutoring pages. School regulation is an emirate matter and depends on where the campus sits. Tutor licensing is federal and depends on who is teaching. An Al Salamah family will usually have one of each in play, and the answers are different.

On the school side, private schools in Umm Al Quwain are supervised by the Ministry of Education, and u.ae names that supervisory role for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. If your child studies in Sharjah, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates the school and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge has the same breadth of remit. Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority oversees the quality of private education in that emirate, and Abu Dhabi's Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools there.

On the tutor side, the private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 is the instrument that matters. It is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation smart app, website or e-services, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

Two cautions follow from that. Anybody quoting you a permit fee is wrong, because the permit is free. And anybody quoting you a fine figure is going beyond the published position: the official wording is that individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no schedule of amounts published. IB Gram holds no accreditation from any of the authorities named in this section, and anyone claiming such a thing on your behalf should be asked for the permit number.

sections.heading: Arabic and the mandatory subjects a Diploma timetable still carries
paragraphs: A Diploma student in the UAE is not only doing the Diploma. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are required in UAE private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to deliver, and the federal position is that private schools must follow Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. For a DP2 student with three Higher Level subjects, that is real time out of a finite week.

The Dubai regulator publishes the most detailed version of the requirements and it is instructive even for a Sharjah or Ajman campus. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the guidance advising a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

The same guidance sets Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. It also states that using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which constrains what any tutor can legitimately offer in these subjects.

The honest tutoring position is therefore narrow. We teach Arabic B as a Diploma subject properly, and we can help a student revise the content their school has delivered in the mandatory stream. We do not offer a parallel Islamic Education or Social Studies syllabus, and we would not, because the guidance is explicit. Where the mandatory stream is squeezing a Diploma week, the useful conversation is about which Higher Level subject is actually at risk and protecting that.

process.title: Send a document, not a description
process.description: The most useful first message contains a marked script, an IA draft or a report with criterion letters on it, plus the subject, level and your child's school. From that a tutor can name the specific losses before the first lesson, which is a better use of the trial than spending it on diagnosis.

process.title: Free trial lesson at Diploma pace
process.description: The trial is a real lesson on real content at the speed the Diploma actually moves, not an introduction. You will see whether this tutor explains in a way your child follows, which is the only thing a trial can honestly test. No payment is taken at this stage.

process.title: A written diagnosis with categories
process.description: After the trial you get a short written view: where the marks are going, which category they fall into, and what the first six sessions would attack. If the honest answer is that the student needs the class teacher rather than a tutor, that is what the note says.

process.title: Weekly teaching tied to the school's scheme
process.description: Lessons follow the order the school is teaching in, not a separate course, with written work set and marked between sessions. For Internal Assessment work the calendar runs backwards from the school's own draft deadline rather than from the IB submission date.

process.title: Reviewed before each reporting cycle
process.description: We check the plan against the school's next report or mock rather than against a feeling. Where the evidence says the hours are no longer earning their keep, the recommendation is to reduce or stop, and that recommendation is made in writing.

whyPoints.title: Taught from the guide, not from memory
whyPoints.description: Subject guides change, and a tutor working from the version they themselves studied is a real risk in the Diploma. Sessions here are built from the current published guide and the assessment criteria as they stand, with your child's own school materials alongside.

whyPoints.title: Criteria named by letter
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessment feedback that says this needs more depth is useless. Feedback that says criterion E is capped because the mathematics sits below course level is actionable. Naming the criterion and its maximum mark is the difference between encouragement and teaching.

whyPoints.title: A specialist reachable from Al Salamah
whyPoints.description: The number of Higher Level Economics or Chemistry teachers living within a short drive of Al Salamah is small. Online delivery replaces local supply with national supply, which is the actual argument for the format rather than an excuse for it.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated up front
whyPoints.description: Our tutors give feedback on the student's own work and will not supply text for an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay. That is stated at the first session so nobody has to negotiate it at eleven at night three days before a deadline.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not visit UAE homes, holds no regulator or board accreditation, publishes no grade guarantee, and does not quote IB examination dates it has not verified. If a provider offers you all four of those things, ask to see the evidence.

faqs.question: Can an IB tutor come to our house in Al Salamah?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. In-person visits are a service we run in India only, and we do not send tutors to any UAE address. Independent home tutors do operate in the northern emirates and the market quotes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour for in-home one-to-one once travel is priced in. From Al Salamah the specialist pool within a short drive is small, so our view is that the same money buys a better-matched Diploma teacher online. Try a free lesson and judge it against your own child rather than against the principle.

faqs.question: Which Maths route should a DP1 student in Umm Al Quwain take?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from two or three target degree courses rather than from preference. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics courses commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level; business, psychology, biological and design subjects are frequently satisfied by either route. Then run a short diagnostic of pre-Diploma algebra without a calculator, because that is the single best predictor of whether Analysis and Approaches will be manageable. Requirements differ by university and by year, so confirm against the universities' own published entry requirements and your school's counsellor.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Maths exploration worth, and where do students lose them?
faqs.answer: The exploration is marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest single allocation at six marks, which is why a polished report built on mathematics below course level cannot reach the top band. The commonest avoidable losses are calculator notation instead of mathematical notation, reflection written after the fact rather than from notes kept during the work, and a topic chosen before anyone checked it could carry course-level mathematics.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go on the Extended Essay without crossing the line?
faqs.answer: A tutor will help him plan it, narrow the question, test whether his argument survives a counter-example and tell him where a draft falls short. A tutor will not write any part of it, supply paragraphs or rewrite his text, because the Extended Essay must be his own work and the consequence of a breach falls on him. The highest-value hour is usually the first one, spent turning a question too broad for 4,000 words into one that can actually be argued inside the ceiling.

faqs.question: What exactly is a command term and why does it keep costing marks?
faqs.answer: Every Diploma question opens with a defined instruction: state, outline, describe, explain, discuss, evaluate. The mark scheme pays for that instruction being met, so an answer that explains when the question said state wastes time, and one that describes when the question said explain cannot reach the marks available however accurate it is. Students lose marks here invisibly, because their content was correct. Twenty minutes stripping a past paper down to command term plus mark allocation is one of the few genuine shortcuts in the Diploma.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Chemistry much harder than Standard Level for a DP1 student?
faqs.answer: It is broader and it is more mechanistic, which is a different thing from harder. Higher Level adds content and expects explanation at the level of mechanism rather than recall, so energetics, equilibrium and organic pathways carry more weight and more detail. The students who struggle most are usually those who arrived on the strength of a strong IGCSE grade earned by memorisation. A short diagnostic on the first two topics, marked to the published scheme, answers this more reliably than any general advice can.

faqs.question: How should a DP2 student in Al Salamah use the last eight weeks before the session?
faqs.answer: Start with one timed paper marked strictly, with every lost mark categorised as content gap, command term misread, working not shown or timing. Spend weeks two to five attacking the largest category, in question-sized pieces, repeating the same question type until it stops failing. Return to full timed papers in weeks six and seven, then keep week eight light, because a tired candidate loses more marks than an under-revised one. Learning new content in this window rarely repays the hours it takes.

faqs.question: Does my child's Diploma school in Sharjah come under Umm Al Quwain's regulator?
faqs.answer: No. School regulation follows the campus, not your address. Private schools in Umm Al Quwain are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, as u.ae states for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A campus in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A Ras Al Khaimah campus comes under that emirate's Department of Knowledge. So inspection reports, fee approvals and complaint routes all follow the school.

faqs.question: Does a private IB tutor need a UAE permit, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation smart app, website or e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Anyone quoting you a permit fee has got it wrong.

faqs.question: How does the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education stream fit around three Higher Levels?
faqs.answer: It has to fit, because those subjects are required in UAE private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to deliver. The Dubai regulator's guidance calculates mandatory instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises at least 25 minutes for any such lesson, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. For a DP2 week the practical question is which Higher Level subject is actually at risk from the squeeze, and protecting that one deliberately.

faqs.question: Can you teach Arabic B at Higher Level for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the shape of the help is usually the opposite of what families expect. Internationally schooled students in the UAE often have fluent spoken Arabic and a weak written register, which is exactly the way round that costs marks in Arabic B. The subject assesses productive and receptive skills across prescribed themes, with a written assignment and an individual oral, and the text type matters as much as the content. Work therefore concentrates on register, text-type conventions and controlled written structures rather than conversation.

faqs.question: Do you supply past papers and mark schemes for Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: We work from the copies your child's school has provided and we reference the official sources, but we do not circulate board material. IB, Cambridge and Pearson documents are copyright, and a service handing out a library of papers and mark schemes as downloads is telling you something about how it treats rules generally. Schools hold the papers for a reason, and your child's teacher can usually release more than a family realises if asked directly for a specific component rather than for everything.

faqs.question: Why will you not tell me the exact IB exam and results dates?
faqs.answer: Because this project could not verify them from the IB directly, and a wrong date on a page a family plans around is worse than no date at all. What is safe to say is that UAE schools sit the May examination session, and that your child's IB coordinator holds the confirmed session and results dates for the current cohort. We would rather send you to the coordinator and the IB's own published calendar than restate a date we cannot stand behind for the next two years.

faqs.question: My daughter is predicted a 4 in Higher Level Economics. Is one hour a week enough?
faqs.answer: Often yes, if the hour attacks the right thing. In Economics the dominant recoverable loss is evaluation: a balanced list of points reaches a middle band, while a judgement supported by a stated criterion reaches the top one. Diagram accuracy is the second, and it is almost pure technique. Both respond fast to weekly work with written answers marked to the scheme. What one hour a week cannot do is replace missing content across the whole course, which is why the first session is a marked script rather than a plan.

faqs.question: Can we pause tuition during the school's internal assessment weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and sometimes you should. There are weeks in DP1 and DP2 when a student is carrying three internal deadlines at once and an extra hour of teaching is simply another demand. Pausing and resuming is better than cancelling week by week, because a paused plan gets reviewed and a cancelled one quietly dies. We would rather hold a fortnight and restart with a clear priority than keep billing through a fortnight nobody had capacity for.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-salama.closingHeading: Send a marked script and we will tell you what it shows
umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-salama.closingBody: If your child is in the Diploma and the grade is not moving, the fastest useful step is not a conversation but a document. Send a marked paper, an Internal Assessment draft or a report with criterion letters on it, together with the subject, the level and the school. A specialist will read it, name where the marks are going, and teach a free trial lesson in that exact area so you can see whether the explanation lands. From an Al Salamah address that lesson happens online, which is also why the tutor can be the right one rather than the nearest one.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-uaq-marin.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are the ones UAQ Marina families book most: Diploma specialists in the six subject groups, plus Internal Assessment and Extended Essay coaching for DP1 students who have just discovered how early the coursework clock starts.

intro.heading: The school run is the real constraint on a Diploma tutoring plan here
paragraphs: Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate, and its private international school provision is correspondingly thin. The practical consequence for a family in UAQ Marina is that the child is probably not schooled in Umm Al Quwain. Students sitting the IB Diploma from this part of the coast commute — south to Sharjah, west to Ajman, or north to Ras Al Khaimah — and that commute is the single fact a tutoring schedule has to be built around.

Work the timing out rather than assuming it. A Sharjah or Ajman school day typically ends somewhere between 14:30 and 15:30. Add a bus route that collects several neighbourhoods, add the Emirates Road or Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road run north in the afternoon, and a child who left school at 15:00 reaches UAQ Marina somewhere between 16:00 and 17:00. Then there is food, a change of clothes, and the small decompression a teenager needs after ninety minutes in a vehicle. The earliest honest start for a focused session is 17:30, and 18:00 is more realistic.

That compressed window is what breaks in-home arrangements in this emirate. An in-home tutor has to be told a time, and the time cannot be predicted to the quarter hour because the traffic cannot. If the tutor arrives at 17:00 and the bus arrives at 17:20, you have paid for twenty minutes of somebody sitting in your majlis. If the tutor is driving from Sharjah to reach you, they are also charging for that drive: UAE in-home one-to-one rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour on published 2026 figures, with travel folded into the number whether or not the invoice says so.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. What we do instead is start the session when your child is actually at the desk, which on a video call is a message rather than a renegotiation. A 17:45 start that slips to 18:00 costs nobody a journey, and the tutor is not watching a clock with another appointment across the emirate border.

The rest of this page is written for the Diploma specifically, because the Diploma is where the timing problem compounds. A DP student has six subjects, three at Higher Level, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, and the deadlines that bind are set by the school's own IB coordinator rather than by the exam board. There is a table of UAE market rates by format, a table of the evening window by school location, a session calendar counted backwards, the regulator map for Umm Al Quwain, the Ministry of Education equivalency rules, and a plain statement of what a tutor may and may not do with coursework.
