umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-uaq-marin.programmesIntro: UAQ Marina families arrive with one of three problems: a PYP or MYP child whose school is a long way from home, a DP1 student meeting coursework deadlines for the first time, or a DP2 student in the final run-in. The timing answer differs for each.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, organised around units rather than subjects, and it reports against learner-profile attributes rather than percentages. Parents moving from a marks-based system often cannot tell whether a child is behind. The concrete skills worth checking are number fluency, reading stamina and written structure, because those are the things a Middle Years transition exposes immediately.
programmes.countryNote: A primary-age child commuting from UAQ Marina to a Sharjah or Ajman school is tired by 17:00 in a way a secondary student is not. Short sessions work better than long ones here: thirty to forty minutes twice a week beats a single exhausted hour. For this age group a parent within earshot for the first few weeks of video lessons makes a measurable difference to focus.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade through subject-specific boundaries. There is no external paper until the optional eAssessment, so a student can go years without an externally benchmarked mark. The criteria have names — inquiring and analysing, knowledge and understanding, communicating, applying — and they are what the marks are actually awarded against.
programmes.countryNote: MYP5 into DP1 is the step that catches UAQ Marina families, partly because the local school choice is narrow and a change of school often coincides with the change of programme. A student who has never sat a timed external paper meets Paper 1 under clock pressure in DP1. The spring before DP1 is the cheapest time to fix that, and it is the term nearly everyone skips.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades run 1-7, with up to three bonus points from the TOK and EE matrix. Higher Level carries 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and in most sciences the HL extension appears on its own paper rather than being folded into the SL ones.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. For a UAQ Marina student the binding dates are the coordinator's internal coursework deadlines, which sit through DP1 and the first half of DP2 and do not move. Build the tutoring year around those, not around the exam window, and front-load the work into the terms when the evening window is least compressed.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The core is worth up to three points through the TOK and EE combination, and it is where students lose ground quietly because nothing is marked weekly. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece with a supervisor; TOK is an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. CAS is not graded but must be completed for the Diploma to be awarded.
programmes.countryNote: Core work is the part a long commute damages most, because it needs unbroken thinking time rather than a scheduled lesson. A UAQ Marina student who gets home at 17:00 has fewer usable evening hours than a classmate living near the school. Weekend sessions on the Extended Essay are worth more here than midweek ones, and we schedule them deliberately rather than by default.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-uaq-marin.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects UAQ Marina families request most, with what each one assesses and where marks reliably go missing. A tutor who cannot name the paper that carries the weight has not taught the course.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-and-algebra route. HL adds complex numbers, vectors, induction and a heavier calculus load, with Paper 3 a two-problem investigation worth 20% of the HL grade. Paper 3 is where marks vanish, because students have never worked sustained unfamiliar mathematics without a scaffolded prompt.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics, calculator-permitted throughout. HL carries graph theory, Voronoi diagrams and matrices that surprise students who chose AI expecting less work. The habitual loss is interpretation: a correct regression with no sentence saying what it means collects the calculation marks only.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is multiple choice under tight timing; Paper 2 is extended response where a numerically right answer with no reasoning chain loses the explanation marks. HL adds fields, induction and quantum material on its own paper. Students who can manipulate equations but cannot describe a mechanism plateau around a 4.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and equilibrium carry heavy weight in Paper 2, and organic mechanism notation is the most common hidden gap. The internal assessment rewards a genuinely personal investigation with real uncertainty analysis; a textbook experiment reproduced neatly sits in the middle bands however well it is written up.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Marked as a precision subject rather than a recall one. Command terms decide the mark: outline, explain, describe, suggest and evaluate each want a different answer shape, and a student who writes everything they know scores for one command and nothing for the others. Genetics and homeostasis are the usual collapse points.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The IA is three commentaries of 800 words each, built on news articles the student finds. Marks go on choosing an article with no diagram available and on summarising instead of analysing. HL adds Paper 3, which is arithmetic under time pressure rather than deeper theory.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis against a guiding question; Paper 2 is a comparative essay on studied works. The Individual Oral links a global issue to one literary and one non-literary extract and is internally assessed, externally moderated. Weak IOs are almost always weak on the global issue, not on the texts.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The case study is where the grade is decided. Candidates who revise definitions and ignore the stimulus write generic answers and score badly on high-tariff questions. Application to the named business in front of them is the assessed skill, and it is teachable in a small number of focused sessions.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be used as evidence, not recited. The strongest answers name a study, state what it found and then say what that licenses you to conclude and what it does not. HL adds the extension options and a heavier research-methods load, which is where the paper separates the grades.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: A popular Group 4 choice that students underestimate. It demands systems diagrams, named case studies and value-perspective analysis, and the exam rewards specificity about a real place. A generic answer about deforestation scores a fraction of what a named, dated case study scores.

sections.heading: What time can a session actually start in UAQ Marina?
paragraphs: Between 17:30 and 18:30 on a normal weekday, if your child attends school in Sharjah or Ajman. That is the answer, and it is more useful than any claim about availability, because the hour is the thing that decides whether a tutoring arrangement survives a term.

The arithmetic is simple and almost nobody does it. School ends between 14:30 and 15:30 depending on the school and the year group. A bus that serves multiple communities does not leave immediately and does not run a direct route. The journey north along Emirates Road or Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road in the afternoon is not the journey the map promises. Arrival in UAQ Marina somewhere between 16:00 and 17:00 is typical, and on a bad day later. Then a teenager needs food and twenty minutes of nothing, which is not laziness but the condition for being able to think.

What this rules out is the 16:00 session the entire tutoring market implicitly assumes. What it rules in is a later slot, which online delivery supplies without complaint because no tutor is being asked to drive anywhere at 18:30. It also makes the slip-tolerant start valuable: if the bus is late, a video session begins at 18:10 instead of 18:00 and loses ten minutes, while an in-home tutor standing in your hallway at 17:55 loses the lot and charges for it.

One further point specific to the Diploma. A DP2 student in the autumn is carrying coursework deadlines, mocks and university applications at once, and the evening window does not expand to accommodate them. That is the argument for front-loading content work into DP1, when the same window exists but nothing is yet urgent. Families who start in DP1 spend fewer total hours than families who start in DP2, which is the opposite of what most people expect.

sections.heading: What UAQ Marina families pay, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest option and work up, because the interesting question is not what tutoring costs but what each extra dirham purchases. Published UAE market figures as read in October 2026: budget online tutoring with a university-student tutor runs from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A board specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's survey reaching 450 or more.

Then there is the in-home band: AED 180 to 500 an hour, Bestimate putting it at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. Compare that against the online specialist band and the difference is the travel premium. In UAQ Marina it is a large premium for a small benefit, because the drive is long. A tutor coming from Sharjah to Umm Al Quwain is giving up an hour each way at the exact time of day the road is worst, and that hour is inside your rate.

Monthly packaging is the other way this market sells. Figures published in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. None of these are IB Gram prices; they are the market, cited so you can argue with a quote you are given.

The waste, in our experience of this corridor, is paying the in-home premium for a generalist. A family pays AED 300 an hour for somebody who will make the drive, and the person who arrives teaches the right subject on the wrong board, or the right board at the wrong level. The same money spent online buys a specialist in the exact specification. That is the trade this page exists to make visible.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home Diploma tutor here
paragraphs: An in-home tutor gives you presence. Somebody is in the room, there is no connection to fail, and a teenager cannot quietly open a second tab. For a younger child that presence is worth paying for. For a Diploma student eight weeks from a Paper 3 they keep failing, it is worth considerably less than knowing the paper.

Against that, every structural feature of UAQ Marina works against the in-home model. The tutor pool shrinks to people prepared to drive to Umm Al Quwain, which in a specialist Diploma subject may be nobody. The rate carries the drive. The appointment has to be fixed in advance against a bus arrival time that cannot be predicted. And if the session is cancelled on either side, a journey is wasted and usually charged.

Online delivery inverts each of those. The pool becomes everybody who teaches IB Chemistry HL, not everybody who teaches it within sixty kilometres. The rate drops because nobody is paid to drive. A late bus costs ten minutes rather than an hour. Sessions can be recorded and rewatched before a paper. Past papers are screen-shared and annotated live, which is closer to a desk-side explanation than parents expect before they have seen it.

IB Gram offers only the online route in the UAE, and we would rather set out the trade-off than pretend it does not exist. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. If physical presence is the thing your child needs, the UAE market supplies it and this page has told you what it costs.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session. We publish no specific IB exam or results date on this page, and the reason is worth stating plainly: the IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. A date a parent plans a year around has to be right, so get the session dates from your child's IB coordinator, who receives them from the IB directly.

What can be planned confidently is the shape of the year, because it is set by the school rather than the board. The Extended Essay has supervisor meetings and a school draft deadline. Each Internal Assessment has a coordinator deadline, and in the sciences and mathematics those deadlines land in DP2 while the teaching is still running. TOK has an exhibition and an essay against a prescribed title. Mocks sit roughly a term before the papers. Predicted grades for university applications are produced from work completed well before the exams. Every one of those dates is earlier than parents expect.

Counted backwards from the May session, a Diploma student has four usable blocks: the first autumn term of DP1, the spring of DP1 when coursework genuinely starts, the autumn of DP2 when mocks and applications collide, and the final run-in. Three of those four are better spent on content and coursework than on past papers. The families who spend least overall are the ones who use the spring of DP1, which is also the term almost everyone treats as quiet.

For UAQ Marina specifically, the evening window makes this more acute rather than less. There are fewer usable hours per week here than for a family living near the school, so the hours have to be spent earlier. A commuting student who starts in DP2 is trying to do the same work in a smaller container.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, from Umm Al Quwain to the school gate
paragraphs: A UAQ Marina family commonly lives under one regulator and sends a child to school under another. Umm Al Quwain private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which also covers Ajman and Fujairah. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, activities and assessment methods as well as regulating. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge on the same model. Dubai has KHDA and Abu Dhabi has ADEK. Those five bodies are the complete map.

This matters practically. If your child attends a Sharjah school, fee approval and curriculum approval for that school sit with SPEA, not with the Ministry that covers your home emirate, and questions about either go to SPEA. If you move the child to an Ajman school, the same questions go federal. Parents who assume one national system find this out at the wrong moment.

None of those bodies licenses individual tutors. Private tutoring is regulated separately through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule has been published, this page quotes no figure.

Two consequences. First, no tutoring provider can honestly describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes with premises in Dubai. IB Gram holds no such permit, no accreditation from any UAE authority, and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Second, if your child's own teacher offers private lessons, check the rules: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of their own enrolled students, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars the same thing.

sections.heading: Coursework: what a tutor may do and what nobody should offer
paragraphs: This is the boundary that carries the most risk for your child, and the market handles it badly. One page examined for this project sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price. The student is the one whose Diploma is at stake if submitted work is not their own, which makes the transaction worse than a waste of money.

A tutor may teach. That means explaining what each assessment criterion actually rewards and in what proportion, reading a draft the student has written and saying where it falls short of the descriptors, pointing out that a research question cannot be answered inside the word limit, teaching the statistics a Biology IA needs, and explaining why a Chemistry investigation that reproduces a textbook method will sit mid-band however neatly it is presented. All of that is feedback on the student's own work and it is both permitted and expected.

A tutor may not write, draft, complete, ghost-produce or edit to completion any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay, Personal Project or coursework. IB Gram does not and declines the request when it arrives. There is a second, quieter line: a tutor should not hand over board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to the IB and reproducing them is a copyright matter. We cite and link to the official source instead.

The test for a parent is simple. A legitimate coursework session ends with your child holding a list of changes to make. If what arrives in the inbox is a better version of the document, you have bought something that can cost a Diploma, and no amount of convenience is worth that.

Not permitted: drafting, completing or polishing coursework to submission standard

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, before it becomes urgent
paragraphs: A Diploma student from UAQ Marina applying to a UAE institution meets the Ministry of Education's equivalency process, which converts a foreign school certificate into something UAE universities and employers can read. It is worth understanding two years early, because it constrains subject choices at the point where they are still changeable.

The published British-track rules are specific and useful even for IB families with an IGCSE history: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus either one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That five-subject figure matters because at least one ranking competitor page publishes six, and a family planning against the wrong number makes a real mistake.

On the American track, English proficiency requires 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB specifically, this page publishes no points threshold. We have not read one on the Ministry's own site, and an invented figure here is exactly the kind of thing a family would plan a year around. Ask the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority directly.

Two cautions worth repeating. Equivalency is a Ministry process. IB Gram does not perform it, expedite it or guarantee an outcome in it; we describe it and point you to the official channel. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. A provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process, and that is a reason to walk away rather than to buy.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the UAQ Marina academic year
paragraphs: The UAE school year typically runs from late August or early September to late June or early July, with a long winter break in December and a spring break. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, and when it falls in spring it lands directly on the revision weeks before the May session.

During Ramadan school days shorten, which sounds like it should help a commuting family and in practice does not, because household routines invert at the same time. The afternoon slot that worked in January becomes the worst available hour, and the productive window moves to after Iftar. Online delivery absorbs that at no cost, since shifting a session to 21:00 asks nobody to drive anywhere. The thing to avoid is renegotiating week by week: agree before Ramadan whether sessions pause, shorten or move late.

The second calendar feature is travel. Households in this part of the coast often travel for Eid and across the summer, and a Diploma student who loses six weeks of momentum in July pays for it in the DP2 autumn. A maintenance rhythm across a long break — one session a fortnight with a past paper in between — holds far more ground than it costs. Sessions follow a family abroad without difficulty, because the only requirements are a connection and an agreed hour.

Layer that over the evening window and a planning rule emerges for UAQ Marina: use the terms where the window is widest and the pressure lowest. That is the spring of DP1 and the early autumn of DP1. It is not the DP2 autumn, when mocks, coursework deadlines and university applications arrive at once into the same two usable evening hours.
bullets: Agree the Ramadan arrangement before Ramadan, not during it
Post-Iftar sessions work; mid-afternoon sessions in Ramadan generally do not
A fortnightly session across a long break preserves more than it costs
Front-load into DP1: the DP2 autumn has no spare hours in a commuting household

process.title: Tell us the arrival time, not the school finish time
process.description: The useful first message names the school, the year group, the subject and level, and the time your child actually walks through the door on a normal weekday. From UAQ Marina that is usually an hour or more after the bell. Everything else in the plan is built from that number.

process.title: Send the IB coordinator's deadline list
process.description: Coursework deadlines, mock windows and report dates are set by the school and they bind earlier than the exam window. A tutor working without them plans against the wrong clock. For a Diploma student the Internal Assessment dates in particular are immovable and routinely arrive sooner than families expect.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson in the real slot
process.description: One session, no commitment, booked at the hour you would actually use rather than a convenient weekend one. That tests the thing most likely to fail: whether your child can concentrate at 18:30 after a long commute. Watch whether the tutor diagnoses or lectures in the first twenty minutes.

process.title: Hold one slot for the whole term
process.description: Pick an hour you can keep every week and keep it, rather than rebooking around each week's disruptions. Consistency matters more than frequency at this age, and in a household where the bus time varies, a fixed anchor in the evening is worth more than an extra session a month.

process.title: Review against marked work every six weeks
process.description: Compare the plan against evidence: school assessments, past-paper scores broken down by question type, coursework drafts and the feedback on them. If the numbers have not moved on the things you targeted, change the plan or the tutor. A rematch in week two costs an hour; one in week ten costs a term.

whyPoints.title: Built for the hour you actually have
whyPoints.description: Most of this market assumes a 16:00 session. A UAQ Marina student commuting from Sharjah is not home at 16:00. We schedule from the arrival time rather than the bell, and a video session can absorb a late bus without anyone losing an hour or a journey.

whyPoints.title: Specialists chosen by subject and level, not by drive time
whyPoints.description: In the least populous emirate, filtering tutors by willingness to drive to Umm Al Quwain can leave nobody at all in a specialist Diploma subject. Matching on the subject and level first, then delivering over video, gives a UAQ Marina family the same access as a family living beside the school.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure sourced and dated

Three of six competitor pages examined published no price at all, and two quoted US dollars to families who pay in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: No approval claims and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval from KHDA, ADEK or SPEA, no Ministry accreditation and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We explain what each body does and link to it. You will find no satisfaction percentage, star rating or student count on this page, because we cannot produce the underlying data for one.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on academic honesty
whyPoints.description: We teach, review and give feedback on the student's own work. We do not draft, complete or produce an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay or any coursework, and we decline the request. No competitor page examined for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere, and a concealed gap costs a term rather than a conversation.

faqs.question: What time should an IB home tutor in UAQ Marina start a session?
faqs.answer: Plan for 17:30 to 18:30 if your child attends school in Sharjah, and around 17:00 if the school is in Ajman. A Sharjah or Ajman day ends between 14:30 and 15:30, the bus serves several communities on the way north, and the afternoon road adds more than the map suggests. Arrival in UAQ Marina between 16:00 and 17:00 is typical, and a teenager needs food and twenty minutes of nothing before they can think. Our sessions are booked from the arrival time rather than the bell.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel out to Umm Al Quwain for lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The market does supply in-home tutors at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour on published 2026 figures, with the drive inside that rate, but the pool willing to drive to Umm Al Quwain for a specialist Diploma subject is small, and in some subjects it is empty.

faqs.question: Why do so few Diploma students attend school inside Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: Because it is the least populous emirate and the private international school set is correspondingly small. A small cohort cannot staff the full range of Diploma subjects, so families who want a particular HL combination commute to Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah. That is the fact behind this page: the school is out of emirate, the journey is long, and the evening available for tutoring is shorter than the market assumes. Planning around that honestly produces a better schedule than pretending otherwise.

faqs.question: What does Diploma tutoring cost for a family in this part of the coast?
faqs.answer: Published UAE market rates as read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a board specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Unitors IB from AED 200. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure. Umm Al Quwain is not separately surveyed, so treat the national bands as the guide. Those are market figures from providers' own pages and Bestimate's 2026 survey, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Is the in-home premium worth paying from UAQ Marina?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the reason is the geography rather than the format. A tutor driving from Sharjah or Ajman gives up an hour in each direction at the worst time of day, and that hour sits inside your hourly rate. For that money online delivery buys a specialist in your child's exact subject and level. The one case where the premium earns its keep is a younger child who needs physical presence to stay on task, and that is not a Diploma student eight weeks from a paper.

faqs.question: Which regulator covers my child's school if we live in UAQ Marina?
faqs.answer: Whichever emirate the school sits in, not the one you live in. Umm Al Quwain and Ajman private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. So a UAQ Marina family with a child at a Sharjah school takes fee and curriculum questions to SPEA rather than to the Ministry that covers their home address.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Umm Al Quwain need a licence of some kind?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring across the UAE is regulated through a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted with suspicion and check MoHRE's own service page.

faqs.question: How early does Internal Assessment work really need to start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than almost any family expects. The deadlines that bind a Diploma student are set by the school's IB coordinator, not the exam board, and in the sciences and mathematics they land in DP2 while teaching is still running. The research question work belongs in the spring of DP1. For a commuting UAQ Marina student this matters more, because there are fewer usable evening hours per week than for a classmate living near the school, so the same work has to start sooner.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on my child's Extended Essay draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, on the student's own draft. A tutor can say where the argument does not answer the research question, where evidence is asserted rather than shown, and where the essay has drifted outside the subject's assessment criteria. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it to standard or supply text for it, and IB Gram declines that request. A good session ends with your child holding a list of changes to make. If a finished document arrives instead, the Diploma is the thing at risk.

faqs.question: Does the long commute actually affect which subjects my child should take?
faqs.answer: It affects how much time the harder combinations will take, which amounts to the same thing. Three sciences at Higher Level in a household with two usable evening hours is a different proposition from the same choice in a household living beside the school. We would not tell a family to choose easier subjects, but we would tell them to make the choice with the real weekly hours written down. Front-loading work into DP1 is the practical answer rather than narrowing ambitions.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free in our late-evening window?
faqs.answer: We tell you before you commit. The late window UAQ Marina commuting forces is popular, and in a less common subject the right specialist may not have an 18:30 slot. The options are a different evening, a specialist based elsewhere working to Gulf Standard Time, or a wait, and we name which applies. We do not substitute a generalist and leave you to discover the gap in week three. No competitor page examined for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: How does the Ramadan timetable change our weekly session?
faqs.answer: It moves it later. School days shorten, household routines invert, and the mid-afternoon hour that worked in January becomes unusable. The productive window shifts to after Iftar, and a video session at 21:00 costs nobody a journey, which an in-home arrangement cannot say. Agree the plan before Ramadan begins rather than week by week: decide whether sessions pause, shorten or move late. When Ramadan falls in spring it sits directly on the revision weeks before the May session, so the decision has consequences.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same house be tutored on one evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the arrangement we most often set up in commuting households. Two consecutive video slots, each with the specialist for that child's subject and level, keeps one evening occupied rather than disrupting two. Nobody is travelling, so there is no second travel premium and no second arrival time to coordinate. Each child gets their own session notes so the two plans stay distinct, which matters when one is in DP2 and the other in MYP4.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor really knows the Diploma course?
faqs.answer: Ask which paper candidates reliably lose marks on in that subject at that level, and why. Someone who has taught IB Chemistry HL or Maths AA HL answers in one sentence, naming a paper and a failure mode. Someone who has not redirects to their degree or their years of experience. Follow it with how many cohorts they have taken through it. Those two questions sort the field faster than any filter on location, and asking them costs you nothing at all.

faqs.question: We are mid-way through DP2 and only now looking. What helps?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to change shape. In DP2 the useful work is diagnostic: find from marked papers the three or four question types where marks are reliably lost, and work on those alone. Content gaps two years deep cannot be installed in a term, and a provider promising otherwise is selling something. The coursework deadlines are usually the more urgent problem at that point, and getting those finished to a decent standard protects more points than extra past papers do.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor-in-uaq-marin.closingHeading: Start from the time the bus actually arrives

If the match is wrong, say so in week one.

intro.heading: Evidence first: what a tutor should be able to put in front of you by week four
paragraphs: Start with the honest part. IB Gram delivers tuition to Umm Al Quwain as one-to-one lessons over live video. There are no home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service, and it is stated the same way on every country page on this site. The phrase in the URL is the phrase parents type, and it describes a real need, so this page answers the home-tutoring question properly before explaining why a screen beats a car journey in this particular emirate.

Umm Al Quwain makes the case easier than most. It is the least populous emirate, and the pool of subject specialists living inside it for Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 or Diploma Chemistry HL is close to empty. A family searching for an IB IGCSE home tutor in Umm Al Quwain is realistically choosing between a generalist who can drive over and a specialist who can log in. The second option also removes the travel surcharge that sits inside every in-home quote in the northern emirates.

What replaces the reassurance of somebody sitting at the dining table is paperwork. Not a glossy monthly report with a smiley face on it, but artefacts: the script your child wrote, the markscheme the tutor applied, the mark written in the margin, the second attempt at the same question type three weeks later. A progress report is an opinion. A marked paper with a total on it is a measurement, and measurements are the only thing that tells you whether to keep paying.

Most households here are running two boards at once. An older child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE papers while a younger one is halfway through MYP criteria, or a Year 11 student is finishing IGCSEs while a sibling has just started the Diploma. The two systems produce completely different evidence. IGCSE evidence is raw marks out of a paper total. Diploma and MYP evidence is criterion letters with achievement levels. Conflating them is the single most common reason a parent cannot tell whether tuition is working.

There is a timing problem on top of that. Almost every internationally schooled child living here travels out of the emirate for school, so the day ends late and the evening available for work is short. A tuition plan that assumes a 17:00 start is a plan for a different emirate. The sessions that hold are the ones scheduled around the bus, which usually means shorter weekday blocks and the long timed paper at the weekend.

So this page is organised as a file rather than a sales argument. It sets out the artefact you should expect in each of the first six weeks, how to read a marked IGCSE past paper without a teaching qualification, what a legitimate IB Diploma exploration draft log looks like, where feedback has to stop, what the market charges, and how the Cambridge entry calendar forces the whole schedule backwards. Take the parts that apply to your child and ignore the rest.
bullets: Week one produces a marked paper, not a diagnosis delivered verbally
IGCSE progress is measured in raw marks on a named paper, not in percentages
MYP and Diploma progress is measured in criterion letters with achievement levels
Every internal assessment draft is dated and kept, so authorship is never in doubt

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Four qualification routes account for almost everything an Umm Al Quwain family needs support with, and each leaves a different paper trail. The differences below matter because they decide what you can legitimately ask a tutor to show you, and what the school keeps hold of until results day.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is examined in a June series and a November series each year, with syllabus codes that identify the exact paper set a student sits: 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics, 0620 for Chemistry. Papers are marked out of a stated total and components carry published weightings, which makes this the most measurable qualification a tutor can work on.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Al Quwain students mostly sit Cambridge papers at centres in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah, which means exam-day logistics involve a drive on a fixed morning. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the wrong zone timetable is the centre's problem, not theirs, so the school's own timetable version is the one to work from.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE runs in May/June and November series. Codes look like 4MA1 for Mathematics A and 4PH1 for Physics. Some subjects are structured differently from the Cambridge equivalent, with fewer, longer papers, so revision built on Cambridge past papers can leave a Pearson candidate under-practised on question style.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools on the Sharjah and Ajman run enter candidates with Pearson rather than Cambridge, and a few split boards by subject. The practical consequence for a family in Al Salamah or Al Raas is that the correct past-paper set has to be confirmed from the entry statement before any revision timetable is drawn up.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP subjects are assessed against four criteria, A to D, each marked on an eight-point achievement scale rather than a percentage. A student can answer more questions correctly and see no movement in the published grade, because the criterion descriptors reward different behaviour: communication, inquiry, reflection, application in unfamiliar contexts.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP schools reachable from Umm Al Quwain sit mostly in Sharjah and Ajman, and their reporting cycles differ. For a family tracking evidence, the thing to request is the task-specific clarification sheet for the assessed task, because without it a criterion level is a number with no explanation attached.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma awards up to 45 points: six subjects marked 1 to 7, plus up to three points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked against lettered criteria by the school and moderated by the IB, so part of the final grade is finished long before the examinations begin.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates in this emirate are usually enrolled in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah, and their internal deadlines are set by their own coordinator rather than by a published national calendar. Any tutoring plan has to be built around that school's dates, which is why the first session asks for the coordinator's deadline sheet.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and MYP subjects Umm Al Quwain families most often ask about, with the component where marks actually go missing. Each description names something checkable, so you can compare it against your child's last marked piece of work rather than against a claim.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, and that is where most of the damage happens. Students who can reach an answer on a graphical calculator lose method marks because the written argument is missing. Evidence of progress here is the appearance of intermediate lines of working, not a higher final answer count.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use dominate. The recurring loss is the untranslated answer: a correct regression coefficient with no sentence explaining what it means in context. Marked scripts should show whether context marks were awarded, and that is a separate column from the arithmetic.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate the biggest gaps between understanding and marks. Candidates describe a reaction correctly but omit the curly arrow or the state symbol the markscheme requires. The scientific investigation is assessed against lettered criteria and is a fixed share of the grade, so draft dates matter.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Extended-response questions reward structure over recall. Students who know the content lose marks by answering a different command term from the one printed. A useful artefact is a command-term audit across one marked paper: how many marks were lost to explain-versus-describe confusion.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Data analysis and uncertainty handling cost more marks than the mechanics content does. Graph-based questions carry marks for axis choice, line of best fit and uncertainty bars, each independently awarded. Progress shows up as fewer zeros on the graph items, not as a higher total on the recall items.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation are where the grades separate. A correct explanation with an unlabelled axis scores under half of what the same explanation scores with the axis labelled. HL adds quantitative items that reward disciplined calculation layout rather than extra theory.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and Paper 1 analysis both reward close textual evidence over general comment. Students fall back on summary under time pressure. Evidence of improvement is the density of quotation in a timed response, which is countable in a way that fluency is not.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study questions require the candidate to use the stimulus, not general knowledge. Marks vanish when an answer could have been written without reading the case. A marked script should show which answers were credited for stimulus use, since that is usually the fastest available gain.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode precision and tracing tables are heavily weighted, and candidates who code fluently often write imprecise pseudocode. The internal solution is developed over months, so a dated draft log protects the student as much as it informs the parent.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together these contribute up to three points to the Diploma total. Both are assessed on the student's own argument, which makes the supervision boundary strict: a tutor can question a claim and point at a criterion, and the words on the page must be the candidate's throughout.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE side of the same household produces a different kind of evidence: whole-paper raw marks against a published total. These are the subjects most often requested, with the syllabus detail worth confirming on the entry statement before revision starts.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge 0580 is tiered, and the tier caps the grade available, so the first question is always which tier the school has entered. Method marks are awarded for working that many students never write down, which makes the fastest early gain procedural rather than conceptual.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 differ in paper structure and in how practical skills are examined. Where a school enters the written alternative to practical, revision has to cover apparatus description and variable control explicitly rather than hoping lab memory carries it.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry
igcseSubjects.description: Mole calculations and ionic equations are the two reliable mark sinks. Both are drill-responsive, which is why they are good early targets: the second marked paper usually shows measurable movement on exactly those question types if the drilling was real.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology
igcseSubjects.description: Long-answer questions are marked against specific points, so a student writing three paragraphs can score two marks. Teaching the student to count the marks available and plan that many points is a mechanical change with a visible effect on the script.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language
igcseSubjects.description: Reading comprehension items reward exact lifting from the text, while writing tasks reward register control. The two need separate practice, and a combined mark hides which half is actually weak until the script is broken down by component.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
igcseSubjects.description: Both subjects examine application to a given context and both punish generic answers. Marked scripts should be annotated with where application credit was given, because that annotation is what turns a 4 into a 6 over a term of practice.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Distance inside this emirate is short, but almost every internationally schooled student travels out of it for school. That is what compresses the useful tutoring window. The notes below describe the real constraint in each area rather than repeating a postcode.

regions.note: The densest residential area and the one with the most Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum commuters. A bus leaving for Sharjah before seven returns late enough that a 17:00 start is optimistic and 18:30 is realistic on weekdays.

regions.name: Al Raas
regions.note: Older established housing close to the creek. Families here often run two children in two different schools, which means two different pickup times and a tutoring slot that has to be agreed around the later of them.

regions.note: Spread-out plots with a longer internal drive before the main road. The practical effect is that Thursday evening and the weekend carry the longer sessions, while weekdays carry short, tightly scoped work on one question type.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain Marina and the corniche

regions.name: Al Humrah
regions.note: Industrial and residential mix on the southern side, closest to the Ajman boundary. Students here are often in Ajman schools, so the commute is the shortest in the emirate and the evening window is the widest.

regions.name: Falaj Al Mualla
regions.note: Inland and distinctly separate, roughly forty minutes from the coastal strip. Travel to any tuition centre is impractical on a school night, which makes live video the only format that fits a weekday at all.

regions.name: Al Haditha and the old town

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every request from this emirate, and the choice is usually dictated by the commute rather than by preference. Each produces the same kind of evidence; what changes is how much of a single session is available for new teaching rather than consolidation.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, 60 minutes
modes.description: The standard arrangement for a student who is broadly on track and needs one component fixed. The hour is split: a short review of the marked work from last week, focused teaching on the weak question type, then a timed attempt that becomes next week's evidence. It fits a weekday evening even after a long southbound commute.

modes.title: Twice-weekly short blocks, 45 minutes each
modes.description: Two shorter sessions beat one long one for younger MYP students and for anyone whose commute leaves them flat by evening. Attention holds for forty-five minutes in a way it does not for ninety, and the gap between the two sessions forces independent practice that becomes the second artefact of the week.

modes.title: Weekend long session, 90 to 120 minutes
modes.description: Reserved for full past papers under timed conditions, extended-response practice and internal assessment work that needs continuous thinking. For families in Falaj Al Mualla or Al Riqqa, where weekday evenings are genuinely short, this is often the main session and the weekday slot becomes the follow-up.

sections.heading: What searching for an IB IGCSE home tutor in Umm Al Quwain actually gets you
paragraphs: The direct answer: in-home tuition exists in this emirate, it is usually delivered by a generalist, and in the northern emirates it costs more per hour than online work because the rate absorbs travel. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tuition here is one-to-one over live video, and the specialist is matched to the component your child is losing marks on rather than to a radius around your address.

That trade is sharper in Umm Al Quwain than anywhere else in the country. In Dubai a family can plausibly find a Diploma Chemistry HL specialist within a twenty-minute drive. Here, the realistic in-home candidate is somebody who teaches several subjects at several levels and happens to live nearby. The subject-specialist pool for Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL is not local, and pretending otherwise is how families end up paying for supervision rather than teaching.

There is a second practical point that nobody writing about home tutoring mentions. A visiting tutor leaves with nothing written down. The notebook stays with the student, the marking is verbal, and three weeks later there is no way to answer the question you actually care about. A session run over live video produces a file by default: the script is photographed or typed, the annotation is on the document, and the markscheme reference sits next to the mark. The evidence is a by-product of the format rather than an extra request.

None of that makes in-home tuition wrong. It makes it a different product with a different price and a different evidence profile, and a family should choose between them knowingly. What follows is the comparison a parent in Al Salamah or Al Raas actually needs, including what each option costs and what each one leaves behind.

sections.heading: The evidence file: the artefact you should be able to open in each of the first six weeks
paragraphs: A tuition arrangement that is working leaves a trail you can read without a teaching qualification. The sequence below is what a competent start looks like, and it is deliberately front-loaded: the diagnostic happens before any plan is written, because a plan written from a parent's description of the problem is a guess.

Week one is a marked paper or a marked section of one, chosen to match what the school has already taught. Not a quiz written by the tutor. A real past paper from the correct board, timed, and marked against the published markscheme with the mark written beside each item. What you receive is the script with annotations and a short note identifying the two or three question types that account for most of the lost marks. If week one produces only a conversation, the arrangement has started badly.

By week four there should be a second marked artefact on the same question types, and the comparison is the whole point. Raw marks on different papers are not directly comparable, which is why the comparison has to be type-level: six marks available on graph interpretation, two scored in week one, five scored in week four. That is a measurement. A rise in the overall paper total, on its own, could be an easier paper.

Weeks five and six are where internal assessment work starts leaving dates. Every exploration, investigation or coursework draft is logged with the date the student submitted it and the date feedback was returned. This protects the student. If a school or a moderator ever asks how a piece of work developed, a dated sequence of the student's own drafts with comments attached is the answer, and it is also the clearest possible demonstration of where the help stopped.

sections.heading: Reading a marked IGCSE script without a teaching qualification
paragraphs: Most parents are handed a marked paper and look at the total. The total is the least useful number on it. What you want is the distribution of the loss, and that is visible to anyone willing to spend ten minutes with a pen.

Work through the script and write one of three letters beside every lost mark. K for knowledge: the student did not know the content. M for method: the student knew it but did not write the step that earns the mark. C for command: the student answered a different instruction from the one printed, describing when the paper said explain, or stating when it said justify. Add the letters up. The proportions tell you what kind of help is needed, and they tell you quickly whether a tutor's diagnosis matches the paper.

A script dominated by M losses is the most encouraging result there is, because method marks are procedural. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 awards marks for working that students routinely skip, and a candidate who writes the substitution line before the answer picks up marks on questions they were already getting right. That change is teachable in weeks, and it shows up on the next marked paper unambiguously.

A script dominated by C losses points at a reading problem rather than a subject problem, and it is the most common pattern among second-language candidates across the northern emirates. The fix is a command-term drill, not more content. A script dominated by K losses is the slowest to move and the one where a weekly hour needs supplementing with real independent study, which is a conversation about the student's week, not about the tutor.
bullets: Mark every lost mark K for knowledge, M for method, or C for command term
Count the three totals before reading any comment the tutor has written

sections.heading: Two boards in one household: why the two evidence trails cannot be compared
paragraphs: A household running an IGCSE candidate and a Diploma or MYP student at the same time is the normal case in Umm Al Quwain, because families tend to pick one school run and keep both children on it. The trap is assuming the two children's progress can be read the same way.

IGCSE evidence is cardinal. A paper has a total, a script has a mark, and two marks on comparable papers can be subtracted from one another. Grade boundaries shift between series, so a raw mark does not map permanently onto a grade, but the arithmetic of improvement is straightforward and visible.

MYP and Diploma internal evidence is ordinal and criterion-referenced. An MYP criterion level of 6 out of 8 is not seventy-five per cent of anything; it is a descriptor the work matched. A Diploma internal assessment is marked against lettered criteria with separate mark allocations, and a student can write a markedly better second draft while the criterion level stays put, because the criterion that was capping the mark was never the one being improved. Parents who do not know this conclude, reasonably but wrongly, that nothing is happening.

The practical consequence is that a tutor supporting two children in one house owes you two different kinds of report. For the IGCSE child, marks by question type across dated papers. For the MYP or Diploma child, criterion letters with the descriptor band quoted and the specific gap named. Receiving one format for both is a sign that nobody has looked closely at the younger child's assessment model.

sections.heading: Where feedback on a draft has to stop
paragraphs: This is the part of the page that matters most, and it is the part competitors in this market handle worst. Some of them openly sell finished internal assessments. A family that buys one is buying an academic malpractice finding against their own child, and under IB rules that is a risk to the whole Diploma, not to one subject grade.

The boundary is about authorship, and it is simple to state. The student thinks, researches, drafts and types. The tutor asks questions, points at the criterion descriptor, identifies what is missing, and explains the underlying subject content again if the gap is a content gap. Every sentence on the page is the student's. A tutor who returns a draft with rewritten paragraphs in it has crossed the line, whatever the accompanying explanation says.

In practice legitimate feedback looks like a question or a pointer, never a replacement. Where is the control variable identified. Which criterion is this paragraph trying to satisfy. The method section describes what happened but not why that method was chosen, and the descriptor asks for justification. That kind of comment forces the student to write the improvement themselves, which is both the rule and the only thing that improves the student.

The dated draft log is what makes this verifiable rather than assertable. A sequence of the student's own files, each with a submission date and a feedback date, demonstrates development over time. If a coordinator ever queries a piece of work, that sequence is the evidence. Ask for it from the first session on any internal assessment, exploration, investigation or essay, and keep it yourself rather than leaving it with the tutor.
bullets: The student is the author of every sentence, with no exceptions
Feedback is a question or a criterion pointer, never replacement text
Drafts are dated on submission and on return, and the family keeps copies
Published syllabus documents and markschemes are linked from the official site, never redistributed
Any offer to supply finished coursework should end the conversation

sections.heading: What the market charges, and what the fee should buy in evidence
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages examined for this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. The figures below are market bands in dirhams, each attributed to the source that published it, and none of them is an IB Gram price list. For our own cost, the free trial session and the consultation are the honest answer, because the right number depends on the subject, the level and how many sessions a term actually needs.

The pattern worth noticing is the in-home premium. Bestimate's Dubai rate work puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with home tutors reaching AED 200 to 500, against qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300. In the northern emirates the gap widens rather than narrows, because the approach drive from Sharjah or Ajman is longer and somebody pays for it. The cheapest tiers, from around AED 45, are university-student tutors, and at IGCSE Extended or Diploma HL that usually buys supervision of homework rather than teaching of a component.

Judge a rate by the artefact it produces, not by the hour it fills. An hour that returns a marked script with the markscheme reference attached is worth more than two hours of homework company, at any price. The useful question to ask before paying anything is what the first session will produce in writing, and whether the family keeps it.

Monthly packages are common in this market, and the figures circulating publicly are around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Before committing to a block, check what happens to unused sessions when a school moves its mock window, because in this emirate the school calendar belongs to another emirate entirely.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the paper: entries, mocks and the dates that are actually fixed
paragraphs: Every revision plan in this emirate is built backwards from a date somebody else controls, and the date that surprises families is not the exam. It is the entry deadline, which sits months earlier and is the point after which the subject, tier and board are locked.

Cambridge publishes its key dates by series, and the series that matter here are June and November. Those are the two a UAE candidate sits for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level; the February-March series is offered to India only, and the March, May and October dates you may come across belong to Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which are not IGCSE at all. Within either series the order is what counts: entries close first, forecast grades are collected next, the papers come after that, and results and certificates follow. Entries for a June series are taken in the academic year leading up to it, well before anyone sits anything, and the exact closing date is the one on your centre's statement of entry rather than a date any page can quote for you. A decision to move a candidate from Core to Extended tier has to happen before that deadline, which means the diagnostic evidence supporting the decision has to exist earlier still, and the paragraph below shows in confirmable dates how wide that gap really is.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year, and the published pattern is useful for planning: the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the document to work from rather than any restated date, including the ones on this page.

On IB dates this page says nothing specific, deliberately. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools sit the May session, and Diploma candidates in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah work to internal deadlines set by their own coordinator. Get those dates from the coordinator's deadline sheet and treat them as the real calendar, because they are the ones that bind your child.

One logistical point specific to Umm Al Quwain: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, and will not accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after working from the wrong version. A family whose child sits papers at a centre in another emirate should confirm the zone with that centre rather than assuming the timetable a cousin abroad is using applies.

sections.heading: Who supervises the school, and what you can therefore ask to see
paragraphs: Private schools in Umm Al Quwain are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which performs the role that KHDA performs in Dubai, ADEK performs in Abu Dhabi and Ain, and the Sharjah Private Education Authority performs in Sharjah. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education there. Knowing which body holds the file matters because the published documentation differs, and a family in this emirate is often dealing with two authorities at once: the Ministry for a school inside Umm Al Quwain, and SPEA or another emirate's regulator for the school their child actually attends.

The mandatory UAE subjects run alongside whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for. Federal rules oblige private schools to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of curriculum. In Dubai, KHDA's guidance sets this out in detail: separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ; Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs; instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit with any mandatory subject lesson advised to run at least twenty-five minutes. The same guidance states that using different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, which constrains how any tutoring on them can be described.

For an evidence file, the useful implication is that these subjects sit on the report alongside the IGCSE and Diploma grades and are frequently the ones dragging an average down while nobody looks at them. They are also the subjects where a tutor has the least freedom to improvise, because the content is fixed. Support here means working through the set material and the assessment format, not supplying alternative material.

On equivalency, the Ministry route for British-track students is published and specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong. For the IB route there is no points figure published that could be verified for this project, so none appears here. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring service performs, and the official channel is where it should be confirmed.
