sections.heading: Equivalency for both routes, understood early
paragraphs: A student from Al Raas applying to a UAE institution meets the Ministry of Education's equivalency process, which converts a foreign school certificate into something UAE universities and employers can read. It is worth understanding in Year 10, because it constrains subject choices while they remain changeable, and it differs by route.

On the British track the published rules are specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. That detail is routinely got wrong, and at least one ranking competitor page publishes a six-subject requirement, which is incorrect.

On the American track, English proficiency requires 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB Diploma specifically, this page publishes no points threshold. We have not read one on the Ministry's own site, and inventing one is exactly the figure a family would plan a year around. Ask the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority directly, or your school's university counsellor.

Two cautions worth stating plainly. Equivalency is a Ministry process: IB Gram does not perform it, expedite it or guarantee an outcome, and we point you to the official channel. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. A provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process, which is a reason to leave rather than to buy.

sections.heading: What we say when nobody suitable is free
paragraphs: Every provider in this market writes as though a tutor is always available. None of them is, and concealing a coverage gap is how a family ends up with a mismatched tutor two weeks before a paper. In the least populous emirate, with an evening window compressed by a cross-emirate school run, the gap is more likely here than almost anywhere in the UAE.

So we disclose it. If a specialist in your child's board, code and level is not free in the hours an Al Raas school run leaves, we say so and offer the alternatives: a different evening, a specialist based elsewhere working to Gulf Standard Time, or a wait. For an option subject like IB Computer Science HL, a wait is sometimes the right answer, and we would rather tell you than fill the slot with somebody who will teach the wrong board competently.

The matching conversation is short and specific. We ask for the board and code or the IB subject and level, the school and its assessment calendar, the two or three things the student keeps losing marks on, and the hours that genuinely work after the commute. A free trial lesson follows so you can judge the match. If it is wrong, say so: a rematch in week one costs an hour, one in week six costs a term.

One note on fallback delivery, because some providers hide it. If the specialist who fits your child is not based in the UAE, the lesson still runs over live video on your timetable, and we tell you where they are before the first session rather than after it. Two ranking competitors route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without saying so, and one shows a Dubai address on an Abu Dhabi page. That is the standard we are trying to beat.

process.title: Say which system and which code
process.description: For IGCSE, the board code and tier from the statement of entry: 0580 Extended, 4MA1, 0625, 4PH1. For the IB, the subject and level: Chemistry HL, Maths AI SL. That single line removes most of the mismatch risk before anyone has spent an hour, and any tutor worth hiring asks for it unprompted.

process.title: Send the school's assessment calendar
process.description: Coursework deadlines, mock windows and report dates are set by the school and bind earlier than any exam window. A tutor working without them is planning against the wrong clock. For a Diploma student the coordinator's internal deadlines are the ones that cannot move.

process.title: Take the free trial in the real slot
process.description: One session, no commitment, at the hour you would genuinely use rather than a convenient weekend one. From Al Raas with an Ajman school that is often around 17:00. Watch whether the tutor diagnoses or lectures: a specialist spends the first twenty minutes finding out what the student can already do.

process.title: Hold one slot per subject for the term
process.description: Pick the hour you can keep every week and keep it, rather than rebooking around each week's disruption. In a commuting household a fixed evening anchor is worth more than an extra session a month, because consistency does the work that intensity cannot.

process.title: Review against marked evidence every six weeks
process.description: Compare the plan against school assessments, past-paper scores sorted by question type, and coursework feedback. If nothing has shifted on what you targeted, change the plan or the tutor and say so early. A rematch in week two costs an hour; one in week ten costs a term.

whyPoints.title: The distance question answered with numbers
whyPoints.description: Rather than claiming local coverage, this page shows what each radius band around Al Raas actually contains. Under five kilometres there is effectively nobody for a named code or level; the pool only grows at the Ajman edge, and growing it by driving puts the drive inside your hourly rate.

whyPoints.title: One page that serves both systems honestly
whyPoints.description: IGCSE rewards mark-scheme technique on terminal papers. The Diploma rewards getting coursework right first. Families who spend their hours in the wrong order spend more for less, and that sequencing advice is worth more than any claim about tutor quality.

whyPoints.title: Figures that carry a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, read in October 2026, and presented as the market rather than our price. Three of six competitor pages examined published no price at all, and two quoted US dollars to families who pay in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: Exam sessions that are correct for the UAE
whyPoints.description: UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June and November series; the February/March series is India-only. We also tell you that the timetable zone belongs to the exam centre, because Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong zone's version.

whyPoints.title: No approval claims, no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval from KHDA, ADEK or SPEA, no Ministry accreditation and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and is not an examination centre. You will find no satisfaction percentage or star rating here, because we cannot produce the data behind one.

whyPoints.description: If no specialist in your child's code and level is free in the window the school run leaves, we say so and name the options, including waiting. No competitor page examined for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere, and a concealed gap costs a term rather than a conversation.

faqs.question: Is there an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Al Raas, honestly?
faqs.answer: Within five kilometres, for a named board code or IB level, effectively not. Within twenty kilometres you reach Umm Al Quwain city and the Ajman edge and find a handful, mostly in Maths and the sciences. Beyond that the pool grows but the drive goes inside the hourly rate. The filter that works at any distance is the specification: who has taught Cambridge 0620 or IB Chemistry HL. We match on that and teach over live video.

faqs.question: How far would a tutor realistically travel to Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: In practice, from the Ajman edge or northern Sharjah, which is twenty to forty kilometres. That round trip costs the tutor an hour or more at the wrong time of day, and it sits inside the AED 180 to 500 hourly band published for in-home visits in 2026. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The market does supply them, and now you know what the drive is costing you.

faqs.question: My child does IGCSE and my older one does the IB. Can you handle both?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a different specialist for each, because the systems reward different things. IGCSE is won on mark-scheme technique against terminal papers; the Diploma is won by getting coursework right early and then working paper technique in DP2. We often run two consecutive video slots on one evening in commuting households, which occupies a single evening rather than disrupting two, with separate session notes so the plans stay distinct.

faqs.question: Which is the better use of money, IGCSE technique work or Diploma coursework help?
faqs.answer: Whichever matches where the student is. For a Year 11 IGCSE candidate, paper technique is the highest-yield spend: showing working, answering command terms, units, significant figures and labelled diagrams are fast to install and reliably worth marks. For a DP1 student, the highest-yield spend is a workable research question and a realistic coursework plan, because those deadlines bind earliest and a bad research question costs weeks. Spending in the wrong order is the most common avoidable waste here.

faqs.question: What do tutors charge in this part of the northern emirates?
faqs.answer: Published UAE market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, budget online tutoring from around AED 45, board specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, and in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 600 to 1,200 for a weekly hour with a qualified tutor. Umm Al Quwain is not separately surveyed, so treat the national bands as a guide rather than a quote.

faqs.question: Which exam sessions apply to a UAE candidate?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series and the November series; the February/March series is offered to India only, so ignore any page quoting a March window here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. IB schools in the UAE sit the May session. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and the zone belongs to the centre rather than to your home address.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge zone matter if we live in Al Raas?
faqs.answer: Because the zone follows the exam centre, which for most Al Raas students is their school in Ajman or Sharjah rather than anything in Umm Al Quwain. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. So the right question for the exams officer is which zone the centre sits in, not which timetable you found online.

faqs.question: Does living in a small emirate actually disadvantage my child academically?
faqs.answer: It disadvantages access to local specialists, not ability. A small cohort cannot staff the full range of Diploma subjects or guarantee a second specialist in any one of them, so a student here is more likely to need outside help than a student in Dubai with three hundred classmates. That is a supply problem with a straightforward answer: match on the specification and deliver over video. It is not a statement about what the student can achieve.

faqs.question: Who regulates the school if we live in Al Raas but study in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, activities and assessment methods. Umm Al Quwain, where you live, is supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, as Ajman is. Fee and curriculum questions therefore go to SPEA rather than to the Ministry covering your address. Families who assume one national system find this out at the point where an answer is needed quickly.

faqs.question: Do UAE tutors have to hold a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring is regulated through a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so be sceptical of any specific figure quoted at you.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on my child's Internal Assessment with them?
faqs.answer: On their own work, yes. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards, read a draft the student wrote and say where it falls short of the descriptors, triage a research question that will not fit the word limit, and teach the method or statistics required. A tutor cannot draft it, complete it or polish it to submission standard, and IB Gram declines that request. A legitimate session ends with your child holding a list of changes rather than a better document.

faqs.question: How many subjects does the Ministry count towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five, on the British track: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus either one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at E. At least one ranking competitor page states six, which is wrong. For the IB Diploma no points figure is published on this page because we have not read one on the Ministry's own site. Verify with the Ministry directly.

faqs.question: What if we need a subject nobody in the UAE covers at our hour?
faqs.answer: We tell you before you commit, and name the options: a different evening, a specialist based outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time, or a wait. For an option like IB Computer Science HL the wait is sometimes the right answer. What we will not do is substitute a generalist and let you discover the mismatch in week three. If a tutor is based outside the UAE we say so before the first session rather than after it.

faqs.question: How do we test whether a tutor really knows the course?
faqs.answer: One question does most of the work: which paper do candidates reliably lose marks on in this specification, and why. A person who has taught Cambridge 0580 Extended or IB Physics HL answers in a sentence, naming a paper and a failure mode. A person who has not redirects to their degree or their years of experience. Follow it with how many cohorts they have taken through it. Both questions are free and they sort the field faster than any map.

faqs.question: Does a Ramadan or summer break mean cancelling the whole arrangement?
faqs.answer: It should not. During Ramadan the productive window moves to after Iftar and a video session at 21:00 costs nobody a journey, so sessions shift rather than stop. Over a long summer break a fortnightly rhythm with a past paper in between holds far more ground than it costs, and it follows a family abroad because all that is needed is a connection and an agreed hour. Decide the arrangement in advance rather than cancelling week by week.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-.closingHeading: Stop measuring distance, start reading the code

intro.heading: Budget for four exam years, not for one quote
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages answer the question "what does an hour cost". That is the wrong unit for a family in Al Riqqa with a child entering Year 10, because the spending runs across four exam years and, in many households here, across two children. Judged over that span, the hourly rate is one of the smaller variables. The larger ones are when you spend, how precisely you spend, and how much of what you buy is travel rather than teaching.

The sourced figures first, so the rest has something to stand on. Published UAE market rates read in October 2026: budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270; in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500; and premium named tutors at AED 500 to 650 or above, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Monthly, which is how households plan: published packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. These are market figures published by the parties named. IB Gram does not publish a price list on these pages, because an honest number depends on subject, level and availability.

Now the structural point. IGCSE and the Diploma have different cost profiles. IGCSE money is best spent on mark-scheme technique in the final year, because the assessment is terminal and predictable and the gains are fast. Diploma money is best spent early, on coursework and research questions in DP1, because those deadlines bind first and a bad research question costs weeks that no hourly rate recovers. Households that spend in the wrong order on each pay more and get less, and that single observation is worth more than any rate comparison.

The geography matters only in one respect. Al Riqqa is the closest part of Umm Al Quwain to the Ajman border, so it is the cheapest address in the emirate for a visiting tutor. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. We match on board, code and level and teach over live video, which removes the travel line from the bill entirely. The rest of this page prices the four-year view, names where households here overspend, and lists what nobody should be charging you for at all.

This is the year where money converts to marks fastest.

The same work a year earlier needs fewer hours because nothing has to be repaired.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: No coursework component, so the whole budget goes on paper technique. Marks are lost on transformations, bounds and the final part of multi-step problems where method marks were available for working that was never written down.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (IB)
subjects.description: Carries an internal exploration as well as papers, so budget two lines rather than one. Paper 3 at HL is a two-problem investigation worth 20% of the grade and the most expensive gap to leave open, because it needs practice rather than explanation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation (IB)
subjects.description: Also carries an exploration. The recurring loss is interpretation rather than calculation: a correct regression with no sentence explaining what it means collects only the calculation marks, which is cheap to fix once somebody has diagnosed it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: At IGCSE the practical or alternative-to-practical paper is a separate preparation cost from the theory papers. At IB level the internal assessment needs real uncertainty treatment, which is coursework coaching rather than subject teaching and should be budgeted as such.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1
subjects.description: Cambridge 0620 Paper 6 rewards apparatus precision no textbook summary supplies. The IB internal assessment rewards a genuinely personal investigation, and discovering late that a reproduced textbook experiment sits mid-band is one of the costlier surprises in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1
subjects.description: Command terms decide the mark in both systems: describe, explain, suggest, compare and evaluate each want a different answer shape. Genetics and homeostasis are the usual collapse points, and both respond quickly enough to be cheap to fix.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The IB IA is three 800-word commentaries on articles the student finds, and a badly chosen article wastes a fortnight of unpaid student time plus paid coaching time. At IGCSE, careless diagrams cost marks that cost almost nothing to recover.

subjects.name: Business
subjects.levels: IB Business Management HL and SL · Cambridge 0450
subjects.description: The case study decides the grade in both systems, and application to the named business is the assessed skill. Among the cheapest improvements available, because candidates who revise definitions and ignore the stimulus are losing marks for a habit rather than a gap.

subjects.name: English
subjects.levels: IB English A HL and SL · Cambridge 0500 and 0990 · Pearson 4EA1
subjects.description: At IGCSE, directed writing is marked on audience and form as much as content. At IB level the Individual Oral is internally assessed and externally moderated, and weak ones fail on the global issue rather than the texts, which is a planning cost rather than a teaching cost.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The subject where local supply most often fails in a small emirate, so the realistic cost is an online specialist at the qualified or specialist band. At IB level the internal assessment needs a real client and documented testing, not a working program alone.

sections.heading: The four-year view, priced
paragraphs: A household in Al Riqqa with a child entering Year 10 is looking at four exam years. Pricing that properly changes the decisions, because it shows that the expensive years are the ones where help is bought reactively and the cheap years are the ones most families skip.

The pattern is consistent. Year 10 is cheap and high-leverage: a short diagnostic block settles the Cambridge tier question, which fixes the grade ceiling for two years. Year 11 is where money converts to marks fastest, because the assessment is terminal and the losses are diagnosable from past papers. DP1 is the cheap window in the Diploma, when coursework decisions are made and nothing is urgent. DP2 is the expensive year, because specialist exam-year demand peaks, the late slots a commuting household needs fill first, and anything left undone has to be repaired rather than built.

Set against published monthly figures, a household that funds a weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor across the parts of those four years where it matters is spending in the AED 600 to 1,200 a month band during those terms, not continuously. A household that funds nothing until the DP2 spring is spending AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month, for more hours, in worse slots. The second household pays more in total for less.

sections.heading: What the wrong decision costs, in dirhams
paragraphs: Hourly rates are visible and decisions are not, which is why households optimise the first and ignore the second. Yet almost every large tutoring bill in this market traces back to a decision rather than a rate.

Take the Cambridge tier. A capable student entered for Core is capped at grade C for two years, and no amount of tutoring lifts a Core paper above its ceiling. The cost of that decision is not an hourly rate at all; it is a grade band, and it may close a sixth-form or degree route. Conversely a student entered for Extended who cannot complete a paper under timing scores below their Core potential, and the remedial hours bought in the final term are at the top of the market.

Take the board mismatch. A tutor who teaches Cambridge 0620 competently, hired for a Pearson 4CH1 candidate, delivers chemistry rather than specification. At AED 250 an hour over a term that is a four-figure spend on the wrong mark scheme, and it is the single most common avoidable waste we see in the northern emirates, usually arriving through an in-home arrangement where availability drove the choice.

Take the Diploma Higher Level choice and the research question. Three sciences at HL in a household with two usable weekday evening hours is a workload decision with a price attached. A research question that cannot be answered inside the word limit costs weeks of a student's time and then has to be rebuilt under deadline pressure with paid help. Both are cheap to get right in advance and expensive to fix afterwards, which is the whole argument for buying a diagnosis before buying hours.

sections.heading: One-to-one, group or package: comparing like with like
paragraphs: Three products are sold at very different prices in this market and they are not substitutes. Knowing which one a quote describes is the difference between a fair comparison and a false one.

One-to-one is attention plus specificity. The whole hour is spent on one student's losses, which is why it costs most and why it is the only format that reliably moves a grade in the final year. Small group, typically two to four students, is cheaper per student and works for content coverage: a topic can be taught to four people as easily as to one. What a group cannot do is sit with one student's marked paper and work through why that student loses marks, which is where most of the recoverable marks are. Ask what the group size actually is, because two and six are sold under the same word.

Packages are a pricing structure rather than a product. Published examples include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is the same eight contact hours at roughly double the price for the in-home version. A package is good value if the sessions get used and poor value if a commuting household misses two a month, so the question to ask is what happens to unused sessions.

The fourth option deserves naming because it is free and under-used: the school. Teachers run clinics, departments publish past papers, and coordinators will explain deadlines to a parent who asks. None of that costs anything, and a household that exhausts it first buys fewer paid hours. A provider who never mentions the school as a first resort is selling you hours you may not need.

sections.heading: Where households in this emirate overspend
paragraphs: Four patterns account for most of the waste, and all four are specific to a small emirate with a cross-emirate school run rather than being general advice.

The first is paying the travel premium and receiving availability. The in-home band at AED 180 to 500 overlaps the specialist band at AED 200 to 450, so a household can pay specialist money for a tutor selected because they were willing to drive to Al Riqqa. Al Riqqa is the shortest drive in the emirate, which makes this the cheapest version of the mistake, and it is still a mistake for an exam-year student.

The second is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. Six sessions of general revision at published mid-band rates is roughly AED 900 to 1,800 and changes little, because nobody established where the marks were going. Three or four sessions marking past papers against the official scheme and sorting losses by cause — content not known, method not shown, command term misread, units and notation, time ran out — tells you what the next twenty hours should contain. The analysis costs less than the hours it saves.

The third is funding exam technique while a coursework deadline is unmet. In the Diploma the coordinator's internal deadlines bind before the May session, and a missed internal deadline cannot be bought back at any rate. Paper practice funded ahead of an unfinished Internal Assessment is money spent in the wrong order. The fourth is running two children on separate in-home arrangements at two travel premiums when two consecutive video slots on one evening would do the same work for less and disrupt one evening rather than two.

sections.heading: What nobody should be charging you for
paragraphs: Several things are for sale in this market that cannot legitimately be supplied, and recognising them protects a four-year budget more effectively than haggling over an hourly rate.

Regulator approval is not for sale. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK; Sharjah by SPEA; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. None of those bodies approves or accredits a tutor or a tutoring platform. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, requiring initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, no accreditation from any UAE authority and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

The MoHRE private tuition work permit is not for sale either. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any specific figure quoted should be treated as unverified.

Nor should anybody be charging for a promise about a grade, for completed coursework, for board syllabus documents and mark schemes as downloads, or for handling Ministry of Education equivalency. The first is not deliverable, the second risks the qualification itself, the third belongs to the boards, and the fourth is a Ministry process that we describe and point you to rather than perform.

sections.heading: Two calendars, and what each one costs to get wrong
paragraphs: A household running an IGCSE candidate and a Diploma student is running two calendars at once, and a missed date is the most expensive thing on this page because it cannot be repurchased.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting a March window to an Al Riqqa family is quoting the wrong country, and that is a date a parent would act on. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The zone belongs to the centre, which is usually the school in Ajman or Sharjah.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those past dates show the pattern — a November series means January results — which has a cost attached if a sixth-form or university application depends on them. Pearson publishes provisional timetables and revises them, so work from the live official timetable.

For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session, and this page publishes no specific IB exam or results date. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a wrong date is one a family plans a year of spending around. Ask your child's IB coordinator, and build the budget around the school's internal coursework deadlines, which bind earliest.

sections.heading: Equivalency: free to understand, and worth understanding in Year 10
paragraphs: A student from Al Riqqa applying to a UAE institution meets the Ministry of Education's equivalency process, which converts a foreign school certificate into something UAE universities and employers can read. It costs nothing to understand and understanding it early prevents expensive subject-choice mistakes.

On the British track the published rules are specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. At least one ranking competitor page publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong, and a household budgeting for a sixth subject's tuition on that basis is spending money for no reason.

On the American track, English proficiency requires 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB Diploma specifically, this page publishes no points threshold, because we have not read one on the Ministry's own site. An invented figure would be one a family plans two years of spending around. Ask the Ministry, the emirate attestation authority or your school's university counsellor.

Two cautions with direct cost implications. Equivalency is a Ministry process that IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee, so nobody should be charging you for it. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. A provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process in order to sell hours.

sections.heading: Coursework: the one purchase where price is irrelevant
paragraphs: Every other decision on this page is a value judgement. This one is a risk judgement. One page examined for this project sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price, and that transaction can cost a student their qualification, which no refund addresses.

What a tutor may legitimately be paid for is teaching. Explaining what each assessment criterion rewards and in what proportion. Reading a draft the student has written and saying where it falls short of the descriptors. Triaging a research question that cannot be answered inside the word limit. Teaching the statistics a Biology investigation needs, or the testing documentation a Computer Science solution needs. All of that is feedback on the student's own work, and it is worth paying for.

What a tutor may not do is write, draft, complete, ghost-produce or edit to submission standard any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay, Personal Project or IGCSE coursework. IB Gram does not and declines the request when it arrives. A second line applies too: a tutor should not hand over board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because those belong to the boards. We cite and link to the official source.

The test is free to apply. A legitimate coursework session ends with your child holding a list of changes to make. If a cleaner document arrives in the inbox instead, you have bought something whose downside is the qualification, and that is the one line in a four-year budget where the number does not matter.

process.title: Tell us the year, the code and the monthly shape
process.description: Which exam year the student is in, the IGCSE board code and tier or the IB subject and level, and whether you are thinking in hours a week or dirhams a month. A monthly figure lets us say honestly what it will and will not cover at published market rates instead of quoting an hourly number that needs twice the hours.

process.title: Buy the diagnosis first
process.description: Send four marked past papers if you have them. Three or four sessions sorting lost marks by cause costs far less than twenty hours of general revision and determines what those hours should contain. Most households have never seen their child's losses broken down this way, and the breakdown is usually lopsided.

process.title: Exhaust the free options before the paid ones
process.description: School clinics, departmental past papers and a conversation with the coordinator about deadlines cost nothing, and a household that uses them first buys fewer paid hours. We would rather say that than sell hours you did not need, because the four-year relationship is worth more than the first invoice.

process.title: Take the free trial with no condition attached
process.description: One session, no minimum booking, no card required, at the hour you would genuinely use. From Al Riqqa with an Ajman school that is often around 17:00. Watch whether the tutor diagnoses or lectures in the first twenty minutes, because that is what the later hours are paying for.

process.title: Review the spend against marks every six weeks
process.description: Compare what has been paid against what has moved: school assessment marks, past-paper scores by question type, coursework feedback. If nothing has shifted on the things you targeted, change the plan or the tutor and say so early. A rematch in week two costs an hour; one in week ten costs a term.

whyPoints.title: Costed across four years, not one quote
whyPoints.description: IGCSE money works best late and Diploma money works best early, and a household funding both needs to know which. Sequencing advice is worth more than a rate comparison, and no competitor page examined for this project offers any.

whyPoints.title: The decisions priced, not just the hours
whyPoints.description: A wrong Cambridge tier caps a grade for two years. A board mismatch buys a term of the wrong mark scheme. A research question that cannot be answered costs weeks. Those are the large numbers in a tutoring budget, and they are all cheap to get right in advance.

whyPoints.title: The free options named first
whyPoints.description: School clinics, departmental past papers, the board's own published materials and a conversation with the coordinator cost nothing. We name them because a household that uses them buys fewer paid hours, and because a provider who never mentions them is selling hours rather than outcomes.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure sourced and dated
whyPoints.description: The bands here are attributed to the provider or survey that published them, read in October 2026, and presented as the market rather than our price. Three of six competitor pages examined published no price at all and two quoted US dollars to families who pay in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: No approval claims and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval from KHDA, ADEK or SPEA, no Ministry accreditation and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and is not an examination centre. You will find no satisfaction percentage, pass rate or star rating here, because we cannot produce the data behind one.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We teach, review and give feedback on the student's own work. We do not draft, complete or produce an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay or coursework, and we decline the request. It is the only purchase in this market whose downside is the qualification itself.

faqs.question: What should an Al Riqqa household budget across IGCSE and the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Think in terms per exam year rather than a single figure. On published 2026 bands, a weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month during the terms where it matters, and specialist exam-year support AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. The cheaper path funds Year 10 diagnosis, Year 11 technique and DP1 coursework, and needs far fewer hours than the path that starts in the DP2 spring at peak rates.

faqs.question: Which costs more to support, an IGCSE candidate or a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: The Diploma, usually, and for a structural reason. IGCSE is assessed by terminal papers, so the spending concentrates in the final year and converts to marks fast. The Diploma carries internal assessment in nearly every subject plus the Extended Essay and TOK, which means two budget lines rather than one: coursework coaching and exam technique. Funding them in that order matters, because a missed internal deadline cannot be recovered at any hourly rate.

faqs.question: Is a tutor near Al Riqqa cheaper than one further away?
faqs.answer: For an in-home arrangement, yes: Al Riqqa is the closest part of Umm Al Quwain to the Ajman border, so it is the shortest drive in the emirate and the lowest in-home quote. For an online arrangement the address is irrelevant and the rate is identical from anywhere. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, so the travel line does not appear on the bill at all.

faqs.question: How do we avoid wasting money on the wrong tutor?
faqs.answer: Confirm the specification before the first session. For IGCSE that is the board code and tier from the statement of entry, 0580 Extended or 4MA1; for the IB it is the subject and level. A tutor who teaches the subject competently but not the specification delivers a term of the wrong mark scheme, which at AED 250 an hour is a four-figure mistake. It is also the most common one in the northern emirates, usually arriving through an availability-driven choice.

faqs.question: Is a group class a reasonable way to cut the bill?
faqs.answer: For content coverage, yes. A topic can be taught to four students as efficiently as to one, and the per-student cost drops accordingly. What a group cannot do is sit with your child's marked paper and work through the specific reasons marks were lost, which is where most recoverable marks sit in an exam year. Ask what the actual group size is, because two and six are sold under the same label and behave very differently.

faqs.question: What do the published monthly packages actually include?
faqs.answer: Market examples read in October 2026 are AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Both are eight contact hours, at roughly double the price for the in-home version because the drive is inside it. The question worth asking before committing is what happens to unused sessions, since a commuting household that misses two a month has quietly changed the effective hourly rate.

faqs.question: Should we spend anything in Year 10?
faqs.answer: A small amount, on a decision rather than on hours. For Cambridge subjects the Core or Extended tier is settled in Year 10, Core caps the grade at C and Extended reaches A*, and the decision stands for two years. Three or four sessions of Extended-standard questions under real timing, marked against the official scheme, produces evidence the school will take seriously. That is the highest return available anywhere in the four-year run.

faqs.question: Can we fund just one subject if the budget is tight?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the choice should follow weighting rather than difficulty. For the Diploma, fund the Higher Level subject with the heaviest unstarted internal assessment and the weakest current marks, because HL and SL points are worth the same and a coursework deadline missed cannot be recovered. For IGCSE, fund the subject where marked past papers show the largest cluster of technique losses, since those convert to marks fastest.

faqs.question: Does the rate go up before exams?
faqs.answer: In this market it often does, because specialist demand peaks before the May session and the June series, and the late evening slots a commuting Al Riqqa household needs are the first to fill. That is one more reason the early years are the cheap window. Ask any provider directly whether their rate moves with the calendar, because a September figure that rises in February is a different proposition and the difference is rarely volunteered.

faqs.question: What free help are we probably not using?
faqs.answer: School clinics, departmental revision sessions, past papers the department holds, the board's own published materials, and a direct conversation with the IB coordinator or exams officer about deadlines and the Cambridge zone. All of it is free, and a household that exhausts it first needs fewer paid hours. A provider who never mentions the school as a first resort is selling you hours rather than outcomes.

faqs.question: Is there any charge for being matched with a tutor?
faqs.answer: Not with us. The match is not charged, the trial lesson is free with no minimum booking and no card required, and session notes come with every session. We publish no price list on these pages because an honest figure depends on subject, level and availability, and a number invented for a web page is worse than a conversation. Ask any other provider the same questions: matching fees, report fees and notice periods are the usual hidden lines.

faqs.question: How much does the tutor's permit cost, and should it affect the rate?
faqs.answer: It costs nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. So a tutor cannot reasonably attribute a higher rate to licensing costs. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can a provider sell us regulator approval?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer of it should end the conversation. KHDA oversees private education quality in Dubai, ADEK handles licensing and accreditation in Abu Dhabi, SPEA regulates Sharjah, the RAK Department of Knowledge regulates Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. None approves tutors. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes with premises, which IB Gram does not hold.

faqs.question: Which exam sessions apply, and what does a wrong date cost?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series; the February/March series is India-only, so a page quoting a March window here is quoting another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. IB schools sit the May session. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong zone's timetable, which is the most expensive error available.

faqs.question: Two children, two systems. What is the efficient arrangement?
faqs.answer: Two consecutive video slots on one evening, each with the right specialist for that child's board and level. One evening is occupied rather than two, nobody travels so there is no second travel premium, and each child gets separate session notes so an IGCSE plan and a Diploma plan do not blur. In a commuting Al Riqqa household this is the single most efficient structure we set up, and it is also the easiest to review every six weeks.

intro.heading: Why the near-me question has the same answer in every district here
paragraphs: A near-me search assumes a dense local market, and that assumption holds in Dubai Marina and fails in Umm Al Quwain. This emirate has the smallest school-age population of the seven, and its internationally schooled students are distributed across campuses in Sharjah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah rather than concentrated at home. The practical result is that the pool of qualified Diploma or International GCSE specialists living near Al Salamah is not small in a relative sense. It is small in an absolute sense, measured in individuals rather than dozens.

That changes what the search is really asking. A parent typing tutor near me wants someone who can be in the room with their child during the evening, which sounds like a geography question and is actually a scheduling question. Once lessons are delivered over live video, the room is solved and the geography disappears, leaving only the two things that were always the real variables: whether the tutor knows this exact syllabus, and whether the time works after the school run.

The comparison this page makes is therefore between districts, and it is deliberately unflattering to the premise. Al Salamah has a shorter outward commute than UAQ Marina and a longer one than Al Riqqa. Al Raas households are more often splitting children across two emirates. None of those differences changes which Higher Level Economics teachers exist, and none of them changes what a Cambridge 0620 specialist needs to do with a marked script. The differences are real and they are about timetable, not about supply.

Stated plainly, because it is the thing most providers blur: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-person visits are an India-only service. There is no circumstance in which we would tell an Al Salamah family that a tutor will arrive. What we will do is put a specialist in front of your child one-to-one over live video, in a slot timed to Gulf Standard Time, and let the trial lesson settle whether that format works for this particular teenager.

The rest of the page is the comparison in detail: the districts side by side, what to judge instead of distance, how the two boards sit in one household, which regulator governs which campus, what a near-me listing cannot tell you about permits, and what we do when nobody at all covers a requested subject. That last one is a question no competitor in this market answers in public. One thing is worth settling before any of that: private schools in Umm Al Quwain sit under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate regulator such as KHDA or ADEK, so an Al Salamah parent checking a campus inspection record or a curriculum approval is reading a national file, not a local dashboard, and the same is true of any complaint they ever need to file.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-.programmesIntro: An Al Salamah household running both boards is common, usually because one child is mid-International GCSE while an older sibling is in the Diploma. These are the stages involved and what each demands of a week.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, eight or nine subjects, assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both operate here with different paper structures and tiering rules for identically named subjects, which is why the syllabus code matters more than the subject title when you book anyone.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Al Quwain candidates are entered through their campus in a neighbouring emirate, so the internal entry cut-off and the mock calendar belong to that school. What belongs to the household is the revision calendar, and that is the part a weekly slot holds together.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and creativity, activity and service. Assessment combines examinations with internally assessed work marked against published criteria identified by letter, each with a stated maximum mark.
programmes.countryNote: The number of campuses within commuting range of Al Salamah that run the full Diploma is short, so Diploma families here often choose a school for the programme and accept a longer journey. That journey is what compresses the evening a tutor has to fit into.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 1 to 5
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment against four criteria per subject, with descriptors rather than mark schemes. Students become good at writing to a descriptor and less practised at timed recall, which is the gap that surfaces when they meet Diploma or International GCSE papers.
programmes.countryNote: Households with one child in MYP and another in Year 11 are juggling two assessment cultures at once. The useful tutoring decision is usually to leave the MYP student alone and concentrate resources on the examined year, which is the opposite of what anxiety suggests.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Al Salamah families ask for across both boards, with the level and the thing that actually costs marks in each. The same tutor rarely covers both boards in a science, and we do not pretend otherwise.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, calculus and proof with significant non-calculator assessment. Marks are forfeited on omitted working, since the Diploma pays for method, and on exact answers left unsimplified when the scheme demands the exact form.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-led methods. The dominant loss is interpretation: a correct regression or hypothesis test followed by no sentence stating what it means in context or what happens to the null hypothesis.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers, no coursework. Core caps the grade available under Cambridge, which makes the tier decision as consequential as any teaching. Most recoverable marks here are presentation and method rather than understanding.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: At Diploma level the subject turns on mechanism, where International GCSE treats much of the same ground as recall. Students arriving with a strong 0620 grade earned by memorisation are the ones who struggle most in DP1.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mathematical handling is the barrier more than the physics. Formulae quoted without defined symbols, vector components mishandled, graph gradients given without the points they came from. Uncertainty work is reliably under-practised at both levels.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A heavy content load assessed through precise language, where command terms separate state, outline, describe and explain and the scheme pays by that separation. Data questions reward quoting a value with its unit before interpreting it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy earns marks on its own at both levels, and evaluation earns the top band only with a judgement supported by a stated criterion. A balanced list of advantages and disadvantages reaches the middle and stops there.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis of how a text produces its effect, across paper work, the individual oral and the Higher Level essay. The recurring failure is summary dressed as analysis, where the content is retold and the writer's choices go unexamined.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading comprehension, a summary under a strict word allowance and extended writing judged on register. Fluent speakers often underperform because they write the way they talk, and the summary task punishes that harder than anything else.

sections.heading: Al Salamah against the districts next door, honestly
paragraphs: The premise of a near-me search is that the next district over might have a better answer. Here it does not, and it is worth showing the working rather than asserting it. The four main residential districts of Umm Al Quwain differ in commute direction and journey length, which changes when a lesson can sit. They do not differ in the number of Diploma Chemistry specialists resident within a short drive, because that number is close to zero in all of them.

What does differ is useful to know anyway, because it determines which slot to ask for. Al Riqqa, inland towards Ajman, has the shortest outward commute and the most usable weekday evening. Al Salamah sits a little further out and typically supports a 16:30 start. UAQ Marina, north on the corniche, has the longest return journey and works better with a weekend morning for the heavy session. Al Raas households are most often splitting children between campuses in two emirates, which makes the constraint a sibling's pickup rather than the candidate's own finish time.

The table sets this out with indicative times. They are indicative because school finish times vary by year group, and because traffic on the Emirates Road and the Sharjah ring roads shifts with term, prayer timing and the weather. Treat them as a starting point for a conversation about which slot to book rather than as a schedule.

The conclusion is the uncomfortable one for a near-me query. Moving the search two kilometres does not improve the shortlist. Changing the variable you are searching on does, and that is what the next section is about.

sections.heading: Distance is the wrong variable, so compare these five instead
paragraphs: If proximity cannot sort the shortlist, something has to. The five variables below are the ones that actually predict whether tuition works, and they are all checkable before you pay anything. None of them appears in a map-based search result, which is the structural weakness of searching this way.

The first is syllabus-code match. Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are both International GCSE Physics and are not the same teaching job; Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are both Diploma Mathematics and are not interchangeable. Ask which code the tutor has taught most recently and how many times. A vague answer is itself an answer.

The second is what happens in the first session. A tutor who opens with a marked script or a draft is diagnosing. A tutor who opens with a conversation about confidence is deferring. The third is what you receive afterwards: a short written note naming what was covered and what was set, or nothing. The fourth is the permit position, which is a legal question covered later on this page. The fifth is what happens when the match is wrong, and whether that costs you anything.

Running those five against a candidate takes about ten minutes and protects you from the two expensive mistakes in this market, which are paying for proximity and paying for reassurance. The table puts them next to the question to ask and the answer that should worry you. Ask all five in one written message rather than across a week of phone calls, because a tutor who answers all five in writing has already shown you how the session notes are going to read.

sections.heading: Running both boards in one household
paragraphs: Families comparing options in Al Salamah frequently have both qualifications live at once, and the two assessment cultures pull in different directions. International GCSE is terminal: almost everything rests on written papers in a single series, and technique under timing is the dominant skill. The Diploma distributes risk across internally assessed work, orals, essays and papers, and the dominant skill is working accurately to published criteria over months.

That difference changes what tuition should look like. For the International GCSE child, the highest-yield hours sit in the eight weeks before the series and consist of timed papers and command-term discipline. For the Diploma child, the highest-yield hours sit far earlier, around the exploration topic, the Extended Essay question and the Higher Level subject choice, because those decisions are cheap to change in month one and nearly impossible in month twelve.

It also changes who you hire. A tutor fluent in Cambridge mark schemes is not automatically fluent in Diploma criteria, and the reverse is equally true. Asking one person to carry both children is tempting on cost and usually a false economy. If the budget only stretches to one, the evidence should decide which child gets it, and the evidence is the marked scripts rather than the volume of complaint.

sections.heading: Five regulators, and which one your household is actually under
paragraphs: Comparing schools is harder from Umm Al Quwain than from Dubai, because this emirate has no local education authority of its own to publish inspection reports. Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae identifies as holding that role for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Families arriving from Dubai often look for an equivalent of the Knowledge and Human Development Authority and find nothing, which is not an oversight but the actual structure.

The complete map has five bodies. Dubai is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education covers the remaining three emirates.

The remit is wider than inspection in some cases, which is worth knowing when you compare fees. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. So a fee increase at a Sharjah campus is an approval question in Sharjah, while the equivalent conversation in Dubai runs through a different authority with a different inspection framework behind it.

For an Al Salamah household the consequence is simple and often missed. Your regulator is the one covering your child's campus, not the one covering your address. Two neighbours on the same street can sit under two different authorities. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or approval from any of the five, and any tutoring provider claiming such a thing should be asked to produce the specific permit it refers to.

sections.heading: What a near-me listing cannot tell you: the permit question
paragraphs: A map search shows you distance and, sometimes, a self-reported rating. It does not show you whether the person is permitted to tutor in the UAE, and that is the one item on the list with a legal answer. Private tutoring here is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years.

The eligibility list is broader than most parents expect. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 may all apply. The route is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation service named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Two claims should end a conversation. One is that a permit costs money, because it does not. The other is that a permit is unnecessary, or that private tutoring is unregulated: the published position is that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, so a figure circulating online should be treated as unverified rather than quoted back to you as a threat.

There is a related point about who you should not hire. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. Beyond the rules, an independent tutor gives you something a school teacher cannot: a second opinion on the predicted grade with no stake in the school's own marks.

sections.heading: What happens when nobody covers the subject
paragraphs: No competitor in this market publishes an answer to this, which is why it is here. Sometimes a family asks for a combination nobody on the platform covers that week: Higher Level Film, a minority language B, Design Technology at Diploma level, a Pearson code in a subject where our depth is in Cambridge. The honest options are to wait, to be matched with a strong adjacent specialist, or to be told no.

Being told no is a real outcome and we would rather say it than take a booking that will disappoint. The commonest version is a minority Diploma subject in a narrow window before the examination session, where a general subject teacher cannot usefully teach criteria they have never marked against. In that case the better advice is usually the school's own subject teacher plus a study-skills structure at home, and we say so.

Where an adjacent match is genuinely useful, we say which part is adjacent. A Chemistry specialist can carry the physical-chemistry half of a Diploma course convincingly and should not pretend to carry the organic half with the same authority. A Mathematics specialist can support Physics mathematics without teaching Physics. Naming the boundary is what makes the match honest rather than optimistic.

sections.heading: Online against in-home, priced from published figures
paragraphs: The last comparison is the format itself, and it deserves numbers rather than adjectives. Published market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors quoting International GCSE from AED 150 and Diploma work from AED 200. The specialist band runs about AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase at around AED 270 and the top of the reported range reaching AED 650 at BartyED.

In-home one-to-one is quoted separately because the extra money buys travel rather than teaching. Bestimate's Dubai rate work puts in-home visits at roughly AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in this market run about AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Those Dubai-derived figures understate the position from Al Salamah. The drive is longer, the specialist pool within reach is smaller, and the number of candidates willing to make that drive on a weekday evening is smaller again. So the in-home premium here is larger and buys less choice, which is the opposite of what a premium is supposed to do.

Every figure above is another provider's published rate, cited so you can calibrate a quote from anyone, including us. It is not an IB Gram price list, and we do not offer home visits in the UAE at any price. What we offer is a free trial lesson in the slot you would actually use, after which the number of hours worth buying becomes a discussion based on evidence rather than on anxiety.

process.title: Say which board, which level, which code
process.description: The first message that saves the most time contains the board, the subject code, the level and the year group for each child involved. From Al Salamah the other useful fact is the time the school run gets home, because that decides whether a weekday slot exists at all.

process.title: A free trial in the real slot
process.description: The trial runs at the time you would book rather than at a convenient demonstration hour, so you find out whether your child can concentrate after the commute. No payment is taken and there is no obligation afterwards.

process.title: A written view, including no
process.description: After the trial you get a short note: what the script or draft showed, what the first sessions would attack, and how many are justified. Where the honest answer is that no tutoring is needed, or that we cannot cover the subject, the note says that instead.

process.title: Allocate between children deliberately
process.description: Where two children are in play and the budget covers one, we recommend which one on the evidence rather than splitting the hours. Splitting feels fair and reliably produces two plans that are too thin to move anything.

process.title: Rematch early if it is wrong
process.description: A mismatch shows up inside two sessions: the student goes quiet, the written work stops, the tutor is pitching at the wrong level of abstraction. Say so and we change the match. Waiting eight weeks to be polite about it costs you the eight weeks.

faqs.question: Why does a tutor near me search return so little in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: Because the market is genuinely thin rather than badly indexed. This is the least populous emirate, and its internationally schooled students are spread across campuses in Sharjah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah instead of being concentrated locally. The number of people living within a short drive of Al Salamah who can teach Higher Level Chemistry or Extended-tier Cambridge Physics is countable on one hand. A map search is therefore sorting on the one variable that cannot be improved, which is why it produces a disappointing list.

faqs.question: Would I get a better shortlist from Al Riqqa or UAQ Marina?
faqs.answer: No. The districts differ in commute length and therefore in when a lesson can sit, not in which specialists exist nearby. Al Riqqa has the shortest run towards Ajman and the most usable weekday evening, Al Salamah typically supports a 16:30 start, and UAQ Marina works better with a weekend morning for the heavier session. Those are scheduling facts. The supply of Diploma or International GCSE specialists within driving distance is close to zero across all four districts.

faqs.question: What should I judge a tutor on if not distance?
faqs.answer: Five things, all checkable in about ten minutes. Which syllabus code they have taught most recently and how often. What happens in the first session, where the right answer is a marked script or a draft rather than a conversation about confidence. What you receive in writing after each lesson. Whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit and how you can verify it. And what happens, at no penalty, if your child does not get on with them.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle my Year 11 and my Diploma student together?
faqs.answer: It is tempting on cost and usually a false economy. International GCSE is terminal and rewards timed technique and command-term discipline; the Diploma distributes risk across internally assessed work, orals and essays marked to published criteria. A tutor fluent in Cambridge mark schemes is not automatically fluent in Diploma criteria. If the budget stretches to one child only, let the marked scripts decide which, rather than the volume of complaint at home.

faqs.question: Which education authority covers a family living in Al Salamah?
faqs.answer: For your home address, the federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae identifies as supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. For your child's school, whichever authority covers that campus: the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority in Dubai, or the Department of Education and Knowledge in Abu Dhabi. Two neighbours on one street can sit under two different authorities depending on where their children study.

faqs.question: Do online tutors need the UAE private tuition permit too?
faqs.answer: The permit requirement is not waived because a lesson happens over video, and anyone telling you it is should not be hired. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation smart app, website or e-services, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: What do you do if no tutor covers my child's Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you, which is apparently unusual in this market. The honest options are a short wait, a match with an adjacent specialist whose boundary we name explicitly, or a refusal. Minority Diploma subjects close to the examination session are the commonest refusal, because a general subject teacher cannot usefully teach criteria they have never marked against. In that case the better advice is the school's own subject teacher plus structure at home, and we would rather say so than take the booking.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor worth the extra money from an Al Salamah address?
faqs.answer: The arithmetic is worse here than in Dubai, which is where most published figures come from. In-home one-to-one is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's Dubai rate work and AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. From Al Salamah the drive is longer, so the premium is larger, and the pool of people willing to make it on a weekday evening is smaller. You pay more and choose from less. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at any price.

faqs.question: Is online tuition actually effective for a Diploma student here?
faqs.answer: It works when the session is structured and the student has a quiet surface and a charged device, and it is particularly well suited to this subject matter. Criteria, mark schemes, drafts and past papers are documents, and annotating a document on a shared screen leaves the annotated version with the student afterwards. What breaks it is a phone within reach, a bedroom door open to younger siblings, and a slot placed before the student has eaten after a long commute.

faqs.question: Which child should get the tuition if we can only fund one?
faqs.answer: The one whose marked scripts show the most recoverable marks in the nearest examined year, which is frequently not the child generating the most anxiety at home. Ask both schools for annotated papers rather than grades, categorise the losses, and spend the money where the categories are technique and presentation rather than missing content. We will give you that recommendation in writing after a short second-opinion block, and sometimes the recommendation is to wait a term.

faqs.question: Can we book a tutor for a three-session second opinion only?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for comparison purposes it is often the most efficient thing to buy. Three or four sessions aimed at one question, whether the predicted grade is right, whether a Higher Level choice is sustainable, whether an exploration topic can carry course-level mathematics, costs far less than a term and frequently settles the decision. It opens with a marked script or a draft and ends with a written view, which can perfectly well be that no further tuition is needed.

faqs.question: Does the tutor follow my child's school scheme or run a separate course?
faqs.answer: The school's scheme, in the order the school teaches it. A student being taught two versions of the same topic by two people learns neither well, and the second version arrives with different notation and different emphasis at exactly the wrong moment. The exception is deliberate retrieval of material taught months earlier, which is the single most under-used technique available. Internal assessment work runs backwards from the school's own draft deadline rather than the board's submission date.

faqs.question: How quickly can a match happen from Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics, the sciences and English at either board, usually within days, because depth is good and the constraint is your evening rather than our supply. Individuals and societies subjects can take up to a week. Minority Diploma subjects sometimes cannot be matched at all, and we say so rather than holding a family in a queue. Online delivery is what makes those timescales possible from this emirate; an in-home requirement would stretch them considerably or make them impossible.

faqs.question: What if my child does not get on with the first tutor?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week two rather than week eight. A mismatch is visible early: the student stops talking, the written work stops coming back, or the tutor is explaining at a level of abstraction this child does not use. None of that improves by waiting and none of it reflects effort on either side. We rematch rather than defend the pairing, and the free trial exists so the first pairing is an informed guess instead of a blind one.

Send us the board, the level and the subject code for each child, plus the time the school run gets home, and we will tell you who is a genuine match, how quickly, and where our coverage is thin. A specialist then teaches a free trial lesson in that real slot, online, and you decide afterwards with a written view in front of you rather than a sales call behind you.
