intro.heading: What an hour of IGCSE or IB teaching actually costs a family in UAQ Marina
paragraphs: A parent in UAQ Marina typing "IB IGCSE tutor near me" into Google is usually holding two numbers in their head: the rate a neighbour mentioned, and the rate a Dubai agency quoted on the phone. Those two numbers are often three times apart, and nothing on the first page of results explains why. This page explains why, prints the bands, names who publishes each one, and then says plainly what IB Gram does differently with them.

The published market in this country splits into five tiers. A university-student tutor working online advertises from AED 33 to 65 an hour; EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing from AED 150 for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel folded in, is quoted between AED 180 and 500, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. A named IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650.

Read those five tiers side by side and one thing becomes obvious: the in-home band overlaps almost exactly with the specialist band, but it buys a different thing. In-home money buys a car, fuel and forty-five minutes of unpaid driving. Specialist money buys someone who can look at a Paper 2 script and tell you which command term the student misread. For a family in UAQ Marina, where the pool of tutors willing to drive is small and mostly lives in Sharjah or Ajman, those two purchases are not available at the same price.

Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate, and most internationally-schooled children here commute out to Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah for school. That commute compresses the evening. A child back home at 4.30pm, fed and settled by six, has a workable window between 6.30pm and 8.30pm on a school night. A tutor who has to drive into Al Salamah or UAQ Marina for that window will quote for 90 or 120 minutes, because a 60-minute booking does not cover the trip. The minimum booking size is the cost nobody quotes you, and it is where a UAQ Marina budget leaks first.

Online one-to-one over live video removes that leak. A 60-minute lesson is economically viable for the tutor, so it is available to you, and the tutor can be the Chemistry HL specialist who happens to be free at 7pm rather than the generalist who happens to live twenty minutes away. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. That is a limit worth stating in the first two hundred words rather than burying, and the rest of this page argues the case on cost, tutor pool and continuity instead of pretending the limit is not there.

Everything below is organised around money. What the market charges, what each tier buys, where families overpay, what a month costs instead of an hour, what you can verify before you pay, and what happens to the price when the specialist you need is not free. The exam calendar, the permit rules and the academic-honesty boundary all appear, because each one has a direct effect on what you should be willing to spend and when.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-.programmesIntro: Four programme routes cover nearly every Umm Al Quwain family who searches this phrase. The cost of teaching each one differs, because the assessment load differs, so each entry below notes what drives the hours as well as what the programme is.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked A to D on an eight-point scale and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. There is no external paper until the optional eAssessment, so the grade a student carries is built entirely from internally marked tasks. Families usually seek help when criterion marks stop moving despite effort, which is a rubric-literacy problem rather than a content problem.
programmes.countryNote: MYP places in and around Umm Al Quwain mean a commute, most often to an IB continuum school in Ajman or Sharjah. Teaching hours for MYP tend to be cheaper than Diploma hours because the work is criterion coaching rather than paper technique, and one hour a fortnight is often enough. Spending Diploma-level money on MYP 3 is the single most common overspend we see from this emirate.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly 20 to 25 per cent of the grade, and the external papers sit in the May session for schools in this region. The Diploma is the most expensive thing to tutor because HL depth and IA supervision are two different skills and the same person needs both.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student commuting from UAQ Marina loses an hour a day to the road, which is why Diploma families here are the most likely to buy long in-home blocks they do not need. The cheaper structure is a weekly 60-minute online slot in term time, stepped up to twice weekly for six to eight weeks before the series, with IA work booked as discrete sessions around the school's own draft deadlines.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subjects are coded and the code decides the paper structure: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, English Language 0500. Most sciences split Core and Extended tiers, and the tier caps the grade. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, so the timetable version matters as much as the date.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the February/March series is offered in India only, and a page that tells an Umm Al Quwain parent otherwise is handing them a wrong deadline. Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so confirm your child's zone with the school's exams officer rather than with a tutor.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other IGCSE board in common UAE use, with its own codes: Mathematics 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language 4EA1. Papers are available in a May/June window and in November. Some Pearson qualifications are modular, which changes when a student can bank a result and therefore when tutoring is worth buying.
programmes.countryNote: For the November 2026 series the Pearson final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results follow in January: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson revises provisional timetables, so work from the live official timetable rather than from a figure on any tutoring site.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-.subjectsIntro: Not every subject costs the same to tutor, because not every subject has the same failure mode. The ten below are what Umm Al Quwain families ask for most, with the specific thing that eats marks in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-heavy IB maths route. Marks go on unjustified steps in calculus and on the HL proof and complex-number work in Paper 3. An IGCSE maths tutor cannot teach this; it needs someone who works at HL regularly, and that is a different hourly band.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with a graphic display calculator throughout. The common loss is interpretation: a correct regression with no sentence explaining what it means in context scores the calculation mark and nothing else. Calculator fluency is cheap to fix and worth fixing first.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The Extended tier reaches A*, the Core tier caps at grade C, and a student entered on the wrong tier is paying for teaching that cannot reach the grade they want. Check the tier on the entry before buying hours. Algebraic fractions and bounds are the recurring Extended losses.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetic induction carry the heaviest mark loss, followed by anything asking for a method. Paper 6 alternative-to-practical questions reward precise apparatus language and nothing else, which is why a tutor who only teaches theory leaves marks on the table.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic reaction pathways are where Extended candidates lose most. The qualitative-analysis tables are learnable in two sessions and often the cheapest grade movement available in the whole subject.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Content volume, not difficulty, is the problem. Students lose marks on extended-response questions by listing facts without using the command term. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance diagrams account for a large share of dropped marks.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: HL adds depth across energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms, and the Internal Assessment demands a research question narrow enough to control. The IA is where a tutor is most useful and most constrained: feedback on the student's own design and analysis, never drafting.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: Data-based questions and the statistical treatment in the IA are the two reliable mark sinks. Students who can recite a process often cannot read an unfamiliar graph under time pressure, and that is a trainable skill rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: English Language and English A
subjects.description: At IGCSE the loss is structural: directed writing that ignores audience and form. At IB the Individual Oral and Paper 1 guided analysis both reward a line of argument rather than feature-spotting. Both are coachable without any writing being done for the student.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides IB Economics marks more than prose quality does, and the IB commentaries need real published articles chosen early. IGCSE Business Studies rewards applied answers tied to the case material rather than textbook definitions.

That is a scheduling fact with a price attached, so each area below carries its own timing note.

regions.note: Waterfront villas and apartments on the Khor Al Beidah side, popular with families who commute to Sharjah or Ajman schools. A 6.30pm to 8.30pm online slot is the realistic school-night window once the drive home is done.

regions.name: Al Salamah
regions.note: One of the emirate's main residential districts, close to the corniche and the older town. Families here often run two children on different school buses, which makes staggered online slots cheaper than a single long in-home block.

regions.note: Established housing near the old town and the UAQ lagoon. Shorter internal journeys than the newer developments, so an earlier 5.30pm start is sometimes possible for a primary-age MYP student.

regions.note: On the Sharjah side of the emirate, which cuts the Sharjah school commute noticeably. Families here are the most likely to be offered an in-home visit, and therefore the most likely to be quoted the travel premium.

regions.note: Industrial and mixed-use with residential pockets, close to the Emirates Road corridor. Convenient for a Sharjah or Dubai commute, inconvenient for a tutor who then has to drive back through it at 9pm.

regions.note: Inland residential area with federal and private schooling nearby. Internationally-schooled children usually travel out, so weekend morning sessions work well here for IGCSE past-paper practice.

sections.heading: What a UAQ Marina parent is really asking when they search for a tutor near them
paragraphs: The honest answer to "is there an IB IGCSE tutor near me in UAQ Marina" is that proximity is the wrong variable. There are specialists who teach Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and IB Chemistry HL every week of the year; almost none of them live in Umm Al Quwain, and the ones who would drive here are charging you for the drive. The question that gets a parent a better outcome is "who is free at 7pm on a Tuesday and knows this paper", and that question has a much larger answer.

This matters more in this emirate than almost anywhere else in the country. Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate, and the researched competitor corpus for UAE tutoring mentions it almost nowhere — the content that ranks for these searches was written about Dubai and had the place name swapped. A page that tells you an in-home IGCSE maths tutor is readily available in UAQ Marina at Dubai rates is describing a market that does not exist here.

What does exist is a short list of generalist tutors who work across the northern emirates, a longer list of Sharjah-based tuition centres, and the whole online market. The first group is convenient and expensive per useful hour. The second means another drive at the end of an already long day. The third is where the subject depth is, and it is the only one of the three where a UAQ Marina family and a Dubai family can buy the same tutor at the same rate.

So this page answers the search literally and then reframes it. Below you will find the market bands, the places the money goes wrong, a monthly rather than hourly view of cost, what you can verify about a tutor before paying, how the exam calendar should shape when you spend, and what we tell a family when the specialist they need genuinely is not free. IB Gram delivers all of it as live online one-to-one teaching.

sections.heading: The published AED bands, and what each tier of money actually buys
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. That is useful to know before you accept a number over the phone, because it means the going rate is not something you can easily check. The table below gathers what providers have actually published, with the provider named against each band, so you can see where a quote you have been given sits.

Read it as a ladder of purchases rather than a ladder of quality. The bottom tier buys supervision: someone sitting with a student while homework gets done, which has real value for a disorganised MYP 3 student and almost none for a DP2 candidate six weeks out from a Chemistry paper. The middle tier buys paper literacy — a teacher who can look at a script and name the lost mark. The top tier buys scarcity, and scarcity is worth paying for only when the subject genuinely is scarce.

The in-home row is the one to study. It overlaps the specialist band almost exactly, but the overlap is not like-for-like: a tutor quoting AED 300 for an in-home hour in Umm Al Quwain is pricing in a round trip that a tutor quoting AED 300 online is not. Somewhere between AED 30 and AED 200 of that hourly rate is the car. You are entitled to ask a prospective tutor to separate the two, and a reluctance to do so tells you something.

One caution on every figure here: these are market rates published by other providers on the dates recorded in our research, not IB Gram prices. If you want our number for your child's subject and level, the free trial lesson and the consultation that follows it is where you get it, and the trial is free with no card details taken.

sections.heading: Five ways an Umm Al Quwain family overpays without noticing
paragraphs: Overspending on tutoring rarely looks like a high hourly rate. It looks like a sensible rate attached to the wrong structure. The five patterns below account for most of the wasted money we see from families in this emirate, and each one is fixable in a single conversation before the first invoice.

The first is the minimum-booking trap. A tutor who travels needs 90 to 120 minutes to make the trip worthwhile, and a twelve-year-old does not concentrate for 120 minutes. You are buying attention you cannot use. The second is paying specialist rates for generalist work: AED 300 an hour to supervise MYP homework is a real invoice someone pays every month. The third is buying hours for six subjects at once, which produces a timetable no child follows and a bill nobody wants to look at.

The fourth is spending in the wrong eight weeks. Money spent in the two months before a June or November series does measurably more than the same money spent in September, because that is when timed papers and mark-scheme work actually bite. The fifth is paying for a tutor whose permit position you never checked, which is a risk rather than a waste — the UAE private tuition work permit exists and is issued free of charge, so there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one.

The underlying fix is boring: name the syllabus code, name the paper, name the grade you are trying to move, and buy the smallest structure that could plausibly move it. Then review after six weeks against the school's own assessment data rather than against a feeling. Almost every family who does this spends less in the first term than they expected to.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor who drives to Umm Al Quwain

A home tutor in UAQ Marina is a real option; it is simply an expensive one here, for reasons that have nothing to do with the tutor's ability. The table sets the two side by side on the dimensions that change a monthly bill.

The tutor-pool row is the one that decides outcomes. Umm Al Quwain cannot supply a Chemistry HL specialist, an Economics HL specialist and a 4MA1 Mathematics specialist within driving distance on the same weekday evening. Online, that constraint disappears entirely, because the only question is who is free in the Gulf Standard Time evening window. Families who insist on proximity end up with a generalist teaching three subjects, which is the compromise that quietly costs a grade.

The lost-time row matters almost as much. A round trip from Sharjah or Ajman into UAQ Marina on a weekday evening is 45 to 90 minutes, and someone pays for it: either the tutor absorbs it and raises the rate, or the family absorbs it by accepting a 9pm start. Neither is good for a fifteen-year-old with a mock the following week.

To be explicit, because the URL you arrived on says "tutor near me": IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Umm Al Quwain or anywhere else in the UAE, and no in-person session is available here. In-home teaching is a service we run only in India. What a UAQ Marina family gets instead is one-to-one teaching over live video with screen-sharing and a shared whiteboard, from a tutor chosen for the syllabus rather than for the drive.

sections.heading: Think in months, not hours: four spending patterns and what each one fixes
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how tutoring is sold and monthly totals are how families actually experience it. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session put a budget tutor at AED 240 to 600 a month, a mid-range tutor at AED 600 to 1,200, and a specialist in an exam year at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Packaged offers circulate too: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Converting to monthly figures changes decisions. An AED 650 premium hour looks unthinkable until you notice that one such hour a fortnight is AED 1,300 a month, which is roughly what the in-home package costs — and the in-home package includes travel you are not using. Equally, a cheap AED 60 hour looks like a bargain until a parent realises they are buying eight of them a month to produce the same effect one specialist hour would.

The right pattern depends on the year, not on the family's means. In MYP 3 or Year 9, light maintenance is usually correct and anything heavier is money held in reserve badly. In Year 10 or DP1, weekly mid-range teaching builds the habits that matter later. In the final IGCSE or Diploma year, specialist money in the eight weeks before the series is the highest-return spend available, and that is also the period when good tutors have no free slots left.

One structural point about packages: a monthly bundle buys a number of sessions, not a specific person at a specific time. If having the same tutor in the same slot every week matters to your child — and for an anxious student it usually does — check that the package actually commits to it before you buy the discount.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit, and what a parent can check before paying anything
paragraphs: Private schools in Umm Al Quwain, Ajman and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae describes as playing a central supervisory role for private schools in those three emirates. Dubai has KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. If your child commutes to Sharjah, both the federal rules and SPEA's requirements are in play — SPEA approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods in that emirate.

None of those bodies accredits private tutors, and no tutoring provider in this market can honestly describe itself as approved by any of them. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, partnership or licence, and neither do the sites that imply otherwise. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific document issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai; it is not something an online platform or an individual tutor has.

What does apply to individual tutors is the permit. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page, "Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services. Anyone tutoring privately without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any specific figure you read as unverified.

A separate rule is worth knowing before you ask about a school teacher tutoring privately. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff being barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct covering similar ground. Confirm the current wording with the authority before relying on it, but the practical advice is clear: do not arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them for money.

sections.heading: Reading the exam calendar backwards, and why it decides when you spend
paragraphs: The single most expensive mistake in tutoring budgets is spreading money evenly across a year. Assessment does not work evenly, so spending should not either. Working backwards from results day rather than forwards from September tells you which weeks matter.

For Cambridge IGCSE, UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered in India only, and a parent in Al Riqqa who acts on an India date will miss an entry. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam when the wrong one was used. The school's exams officer, not a tutoring site, is the source for your child's zone.

For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, papers run in a May/June window and in November. The dated evidence is instructive about lead times: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Final entries close months before a paper is sat, which is why a decision to resit in November is really a decision made in late summer. Pearson publishes provisional timetables that it revises, so always work from the live official timetable.

For the IB Diploma, schools in this region sit the May session. We do not publish IB session or results dates on these pages, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than no date. Confirm every IB deadline with your school's Diploma coordinator. The budgeting rule survives the uncertainty: load the eight weeks before the papers, keep term time light, and book Internal Assessment sessions against the school's internal draft deadlines rather than the external ones.
bullets: UAE Cambridge candidates: June and November only
Pearson International GCSE: May/June and November, results in August and January respectively

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, an Extended Essay or IGCSE coursework
paragraphs: This boundary is worth more to a family than any discount, because getting it wrong costs the qualification rather than the fee. Some sites in this market sell completed Internal Assessments outright — one advertises them at AED 3,750. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller.

A tutor can do a great deal inside the line. They can teach the assessment criteria and what each criterion letter rewards. They can push a research question until it is narrow enough to be answerable with the equipment a school actually has. They can explain why a data set needs error bars, read a student's own draft and say which criterion is underserved, model an analysis on a different data set, teach referencing conventions, and rehearse an oral. All of that is teaching.

What a tutor cannot do is produce any part of the work. No drafting, no rewriting a paragraph into its final form, no supplying data, no editing to completion. IB Gram tutors give feedback on the student's own work and nothing beyond it, and they say so in the first session. If a tutor offers more than that, the correct response is to end the conversation, because the offer tells you what else they are willing to do.

The practical structure that respects the line also happens to be cheaper. Three or four discrete sessions timed around the school's own draft deadlines — scope, method, analysis, criterion review — does more than a weekly open-ended slot in which a student slowly hands over ownership. It also leaves a visible trail of the student's own drafts, which is exactly what a school asks for if a question about authenticity is ever raised.
bullets: Inside the line: criteria teaching, question scoping, feedback on the student's own drafts, oral rehearsal
Outside the line: drafting, rewriting, supplying data, editing to completion

sections.heading: When the specialist you need is not free: what we say instead of a waiting list
paragraphs: No tutoring platform has every subject at every level free at 7pm Gulf Standard Time, and the ones that imply otherwise simply put a generalist in front of your child. For a family searching for an IB tutor in UAQ Marina, the subjects most likely to be unavailable at short notice are Chemistry HL, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, Physics HL and the smaller Group 3 options.

When that happens, you get told. The options we put in front of a family are a different time slot with the right specialist, a different day of the week, a short-term match with a strong non-specialist for foundational work while the specialist slot is held, or a plain recommendation to wait two weeks rather than start badly. Nobody is charged for a match that does not happen, and no slot is confirmed against a tutor who has not agreed to it.

The trial lesson exists for this reason as well. One free lesson, no card details taken, with the actual tutor proposed for the actual subject, tells you in sixty minutes what a profile page cannot. If the fit is wrong, say so and the match changes; it costs nothing and it is a far better test than a review score of unknown provenance. Several providers in this market publish star ratings they cannot evidence, which is a reason to trust a trial lesson over a number.

The last thing worth saying about availability is that it is seasonal in a predictable way. The six weeks before a June series are when specialist slots vanish, and the families who get the tutor they wanted are the ones who asked in March rather than in May. If your child is sitting papers in the June series, the cheap time to buy is earlier than it feels.

faqs.question: How much should a UAQ Marina family budget for an IB or IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Work from published market bands rather than from a single quote. A qualified online subject tutor sits at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. A named specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home one-to-one is quoted AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside the rate. Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 plus for an exam-year specialist. Those are market figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB IGCSE tutor near me in UAQ Marina, or do they all live in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate and the pool of IB and IGCSE specialists physically based here is very small. Most tutors willing to travel live in Sharjah or Ajman and price the drive into their hourly rate. That is why we deliver one-to-one teaching over live video instead: the constraint becomes who is free at your slot rather than who lives within range. A UAQ Marina family and a Dubai family see the same specialists at the same rates, which is not true of in-home provision here.

faqs.question: Why does an in-home rate in Umm Al Quwain sit above an online rate for the same teaching?
faqs.answer: Because a round trip into UAQ Marina from Sharjah or Ajman takes 45 to 90 minutes on a school night and somebody has to pay for it. Published bands show the effect plainly: AED 180 to 500 for in-home against AED 150 to 300 for a comparable online subject tutor. The second cost is subtler. A travelling tutor needs 90 or 120 minutes to justify the trip, so the minimum booking grows, and you buy attention a teenager cannot sustain. Online, a 60-minute weekly session is viable, which keeps the monthly figure low.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible way to start IGCSE support from this part of the emirate?
faqs.answer: One 60-minute online session a week in a single subject, with the syllabus code and tier confirmed first. Add a free trial lesson before any payment so you are not buying on a profile page. Keep term time at that level and hold the money back for the eight weeks before the June or November series, where timed-paper work and mark-scheme drilling do most of the grade movement. Resist starting three subjects in the same month: it produces a schedule no child follows and a bill that makes the whole thing feel like a failure.

faqs.question: Does a tutor charging AED 60 an hour ever make sense for my child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on what the problem is. The budget tier, advertised from AED 33 to 65 by providers such as Tutopiya and EdFlik, buys supervision and worked examples. For a disorganised MYP 3 student who simply does not start the homework, that is a reasonable purchase. For a DP2 candidate who needs someone to read a Paper 2 script and name which command term was misread, it is not, and four cheap hours will not add up to one capable one. Match the tier to the failure mode rather than to the budget.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with Umm Al Quwain families need a permit from the authorities?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which u.ae states is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring privately without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published, so treat any specific figure you read elsewhere as unverified.

faqs.question: Which authority oversees the private schools that children from UAQ Marina attend?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the school is. For schools inside Umm Al Quwain, Ajman and Fujairah, u.ae describes the federal Ministry of Education as holding the supervisory role. Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge. Since many UAQ Marina children commute to Sharjah, SPEA is often the relevant body in practice, and it approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods rather than merely inspecting.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge IGCSE exam series do candidates in Umm Al Quwain actually sit?
faqs.answer: The June series and the November series. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so any site quoting a February or March exam window or a late-November entry deadline to a UAE parent is giving you the wrong country's calendar. One further detail matters: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge says it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong one was used. Get the zone from the school's exams officer.

faqs.question: When do Pearson Edexcel International GCSE results arrive after a November sitting?
faqs.answer: In January. The dated evidence from Pearson's own timetable pages: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. For the summer route, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. The practical consequence for budgeting is that a resit decision is effectively made in late summer, because final entries close months ahead of the papers. Pearson revises provisional timetables, so work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does UAE Ministry of Education equivalency count for the British track?
faqs.answer: Five. Gulf Today's reporting on the clarified requirements states that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or better, or two accredited Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. No IB points threshold should be trusted unless you have read it on moe.gov.ae or the attestation authority's own page.

faqs.question: Can a UAQ Marina tutor help with my daughter's Internal Assessment without crossing an academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach what each criterion rewards, narrow a research question until it is answerable with the school's equipment, explain uncertainty and error treatment, read your daughter's own draft and say which criterion is underserved, model an analysis on different data, and rehearse an oral. A tutor cannot draft, rewrite, supply data or edit to completion. Some sites in this market sell finished Internal Assessments outright; buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student. Keep the student's own draft history as the authenticity record.

faqs.question: Is tutoring priced per hour or per lesson, and does a longer session cost more per hour?
faqs.answer: Across this market it is usually priced per hour and billed per session, which is why session length changes your monthly total more than the headline rate does. A tutor who travels needs a 90 or 120 minute booking to make the trip pay, so the hourly rate may look reasonable while the monthly figure is double what you planned. Packaged offers behave differently again: market bundles seen online include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Check what a package commits to before buying the discount.

faqs.question: What happens to the cost if no Chemistry HL specialist is free for our evening slot?
faqs.answer: You are told, and nothing is charged for a match that does not happen. The options are a different time in the Gulf Standard Time evening window, a different day, a short-term match with a strong non-specialist for foundational work while the specialist slot is held, or a recommendation to wait rather than start badly. Chemistry HL, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, Physics HL and the smaller Group 3 subjects are the ones most often unavailable at short notice, and availability tightens sharply in the six weeks before a series.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan without a rescheduling charge?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the clearer practical advantages of online delivery for families in this emirate. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the useful study window shifts late, so sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot or to early morning. Because nobody is planning a drive to UAQ Marina, moving a slot costs nothing and is usually agreed a week ahead. A travelling tutor has to re-plan a journey for every change, which is why in-home arrangements tend to lose weeks during Ramadan and the early revision period after it.

faqs.question: What should I check about a tutor before I pay anything at all?
faqs.answer: Four things. Ask which syllabus code and tier they teach most, because "IGCSE Chemistry" alone tells you nothing about 0620 Core against 4CH1. Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free, so there is no reason not to. Ask them to separate teaching from travel in any in-home quote. Then take a trial lesson and watch whether they identify something specific in your child's marked work within the hour. Treat unevidenced star ratings and unsourced success percentages as what they are: marketing, not information.

intro.heading: Without a percentage, what counts as proof the hour is working?
paragraphs: Middle Years Programme reports do not behave like the ones most parents grew up with. There is no 68 per cent, no class rank and often no exam. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, and each criterion is awarded an achievement level from 1 to 8 by best fit against a published descriptor. Those four levels are then converted, using the school's grade boundaries, into a single subject grade from 1 to 7. A parent reading that report cannot tell from the numbers alone whether anything improved.

This is the real problem an MYP tutor is hired to solve in a household here, and it is why this page is built around evidence rather than around subject content. If you cannot see a percentage move, you need something else you can read: the marked task with the criterion levels shown, the task-specific clarification the teacher used, the redraft, and the next task marked the same way. Four weeks of that is readable by a parent who has never taught the subject. Four weeks of a tutor saying sessions are going well is not.

The second thing worth saying plainly is that MYP marking is not arithmetic. A level 5 on criterion B is a band, not a score out of eight, and the descriptors are written as holistic statements. A teacher judges which descriptor the work best fits. That means a student can write more, work harder and produce a longer piece without moving a single criterion, because the thing that moves a level is usually a specific missing move: an evaluation that was never attempted, a variable that was never controlled, a source that was never questioned.

Families in Umm Al Quwain are also solving a logistics problem at the same time. Most internationally schooled students here commute to Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah, and an MYP 2 or MYP 3 student is often home later and more tired than their own parents expect. An hour that starts at 7.30pm after homework is an hour spent on a child with nothing left. Some of the practical sections below are about where in the evening a session should sit, and when a shorter one twice a week is the better purchase.

Everything described here is delivered online, one to one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we offer only in India. For an MYP student the online format has a specific advantage beyond the tutor pool: criterion-marked work is shared, annotated and redrafted on screen, so the marked evidence accumulates in one place instead of in the bottom of a school bag.

umm-al-quwain/ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes sit around an MYP student: the Primary Years Programme behind them, the Middle Years Programme itself, and the Diploma ahead. The notes below are about how each one behaves for a family based in this emirate, where the school is usually in a neighbouring one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria on an eight-point scale. Learning is organised into units built on a statement of inquiry, key and related concepts and a global context. Approaches to learning skills are taught deliberately and reported on. In the final year every student undertakes a Personal Project, and some schools enter candidates for on-screen eAssessment leading to the MYP certificate.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision reachable from Umm Al Quwain sits mostly in Ajman and Sharjah, which means the commute shapes the week for a child aged 11 to 16 who is not yet managing their own time. It also means two households in Al Salamah can be on different term dates and different assessment calendars, so a session plan has to follow the school rather than a generic UAE calendar.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry organised around six themes, finishing with the exhibition. Assessment is formative and descriptive rather than graded, so a student arriving in MYP 1 may never have sat anything resembling a timed task. The habits the PYP builds, which are questioning, research and reflection, are the ones MYP criteria B and D reward most directly.
programmes.countryNote: Students moving from a PYP school into MYP 1 locally usually change school as well as programme, often crossing an emirate boundary in the process. The first MYP report is where families here most often ask for help, because the criterion-level format is unfamiliar and a grade 4 on a 1 to 7 scale reads worse than it is.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment combines terminal examinations with Internal Assessment marked against criteria lettered A onwards. The MYP is the better preparation for the Internal Assessment half of that; it is weaker preparation for the timed-paper half, which is where most MYP 5 students feel the step up.
programmes.countryNote: Post-16 IB provision is thin in the northern emirates, so Diploma students from Umm Al Quwain generally travel further than they did in MYP or board weekly. Families planning that move usually want the MYP 4 and 5 years used to build timed-writing stamina, because the Diploma adds examinations that the MYP has not required.

umm-al-quwain/ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: MYP subjects are grouped rather than listed as separate qualifications, and each group has its own four criteria. The notes below say what each group's criteria actually reward and where levels are most often lost, which is the detail a school report leaves out.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. Levels are lost most often in B, where the hypothesis has no scientific reasoning behind it and variables are listed without being controlled, and in C, where data is presented but not evaluated.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. B is the criterion most students have never been taught to attack: it wants a general rule, tested and justified, not a table of values. C costs marks when working is correct but unexplained.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: A analysing, B organizing, C producing text, D using language. The recurring loss is in A, where a student retells the text rather than analysing how the writer achieves an effect, and in D, where register and control are assessed separately from ideas.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: A listening, B reading, C speaking, D writing, with phase bands rather than year groups. Students placed in the wrong phase are the commonest cause of a puzzling grade: a capable speaker in a high phase can score below a weaker student placed in a lower one.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. D is where the grade is usually decided, and it needs sources weighed against each other, not described. Referencing is part of C and is lost through carelessness rather than ignorance.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. The design folder is where levels live: a strong product with a thin folder scores poorly, because three of the four criteria are about the process rather than the object.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: A investigating, B developing, C creating or performing, D evaluating. As in design, the process journal carries most of the assessment. Students who make good work and document nothing are the ones whose reports surprise their parents.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting and improving performance. Only one of the four is about physical performance, so a sporty student with no written reflection can sit on a grade 4 indefinitely.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed on its own criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesis and reflection. Students treat these units as a double dose of two subjects, which is exactly what the criteria do not reward: the marks are for integrating the two disciplines into one explanation.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: A planning, B applying skills, C reflecting, assessed through the process journal, the product and the report. It is the one piece of MYP work with a formal academic-honesty dimension, and the boundary between supervision and interference matters here more than anywhere else in the programme.

sections.heading: What an MYP tutor is hired to do when there is no past paper
paragraphs: The direct answer: an MYP tutor's job is to make the criteria legible and then teach the specific moves a criterion rewards. There is no bank of past papers to grind through, because most MYP assessment is task-based and set by the school. What exists instead is a published set of criteria per subject group, a task-specific clarification per unit, and whatever your child's teacher wrote on the last piece of work.

That changes the shape of a session. A tutor working on IGCSE physics can sit a Paper 4 and mark it. A tutor working on MYP sciences has to start from the marked task and the criterion that cost the most: usually B, inquiring and designing, where the student wrote a hypothesis with no scientific reasoning and listed variables without saying how they would be controlled. The teaching is then narrow and specific. Write three hypotheses with reasoning. Identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables in each. Redraft the method so another student could follow it.

The second part of the job is translation for the parent. You are entitled to know which criterion is holding the grade, what the next band up actually requires, and what evidence will show it has moved. In practice that means a written note after the first few sessions saying something like: criterion D in individuals and societies is sitting at 4 because sources are described rather than weighed, and here is the redraft where it was done properly.

The third part is restraint. A great deal of MYP work is coursework-shaped, and the temptation to improve it directly is constant. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own writing. A tutor does not write, redraft or substantially edit it. That boundary is not a formality in the final year, where the Personal Project carries an academic-honesty requirement that the student signs.

sections.heading: Criteria A to D: the four questions every MYP task is really asking
paragraphs: Each MYP subject group has four criteria, and they are not interchangeable between subjects. A student who has worked out what criterion B rewards in mathematics has learned nothing about criterion B in sciences, because one is about investigating patterns and the other is about designing an investigation. Parents are rarely given this map, and without it a report is four unexplained numbers.

Learning the map takes a quarter of an hour and changes how you read everything that comes home. It tells you, for instance, that three of the four design criteria are about the folder rather than the product, which explains why a beautifully made object scored a 4. It tells you that only one of the four physical and health education criteria is about performing, which explains the sporty child on a grade 4. It tells you that in language acquisition the four criteria are the four skills, so a confident speaker can be carried by criterion C while B and D sit low.

The map also tells you where a tutor can help quickly and where they cannot. Criteria that reward a written move, such as evaluating, justifying or weighing sources, respond fast to teaching because the student usually knows the content and has never been shown the move. Criteria that reward sustained independent work, such as the design folder or the arts process journal, need habit change over a term rather than a technique taught in an hour.

The table below sets out the four criteria for each subject group. The published subject guides on the IB's own site are the authority, and your child's school issues a task-specific clarification for each unit which is more precise again. Ask for it; most schools provide it on request and some print it on the task sheet.

sections.heading: Why a 6 is not 75 per cent: how criterion levels become a grade
paragraphs: Each criterion is awarded an achievement level from 1 to 8. Those levels are not percentages and they are not added up as marks. The level is chosen by best fit: the teacher decides which descriptor band the work as a whole most closely matches, which is why a piece can contain one excellent paragraph and still sit in a lower band. At the end of a reporting period the four levels are combined and the school applies published grade boundaries to produce a subject grade from 1 to 7.

Two consequences follow that parents here ask about constantly. The first is that a student can improve visibly without the grade moving, because they have gone from the bottom of a band to the top of the same band. That is real progress and the report hides it. This is exactly why the marked task matters more than the report: the annotation shows the movement that the number does not.

The second is that the fastest route to a better grade is usually the lowest criterion rather than the one the student likes. A student sitting at 7, 7, 6, 3 does not need more content teaching. They need the one criterion nobody has taught them, and in most subject groups that is the reflective or evaluative one. Chasing the strong criteria higher is both harder and worth less.

The table below describes what each band usually looks like in the work and what the next band typically requires. The exact wording of every descriptor is published in the IB subject guides, and the school's own task-specific clarification is what was actually applied to your child's task, so both are worth having in front of you.

sections.heading: Four weeks in: what a parent should be able to read
paragraphs: This is the part of the page that matters most for a programme with no percentages. If you are paying for an hour a week, there should be something on paper at the end of each week that you can read without knowing the subject. Not a report that the session went well. A marked piece of your child's own work, with the criterion named, the level the tutor would award, and the specific sentence or omission that holds it there.

Week one should produce a diagnosis: the marked school task reviewed, the lowest criterion identified, and a short written note of what the next band requires. Week two should produce a redraft of one section of that task, done by the student, annotated by the tutor. Week three should produce a new piece of work on a different unit, marked the same way, which is where you find out whether the move has transferred or was only copied. Week four should produce a comparison between the two markings.

That sequence is deliberately boring and it answers the question parents cannot otherwise answer: is this working. If the criterion level on the new task is the same as on the old one, you have learned something useful for the price of four hours, and the honest options are a different tutor, a different subject or stopping. If it has moved, you know which criterion to target next. Either way the decision is based on your child's marked work rather than on anyone's impression.

One caveat for MYP specifically. Some criteria cannot show movement in four weeks because the school only assesses them once a unit. Design folders and arts process journals are the clearest cases. Where that is true, the evidence becomes the journal entries themselves, written weekly by the student and reviewed rather than written by the tutor.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, the process journal and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: In MYP 5 the Personal Project is assessed on its own criteria: planning, applying skills and reflecting. The product itself is not marked directly, which surprises almost every family. What is marked is the process: the goal set and justified, the criteria the student defined for their own success, the skills applied and evidenced, and the honest reflection on what the project became. The process journal is the evidence base for all of it.

That makes the Personal Project the single most common place where well-meant help becomes malpractice. A parent or tutor who tidies the report, suggests the reflection or writes the success criteria has not helped; they have contaminated the only thing being assessed. The student signs an academic-honesty declaration and the supervisor confirms it. A finding here is a serious matter for the student and no tutoring provider should be anywhere near it.

What legitimate support looks like is narrower and more useful than most families expect. A tutor can explain what the criteria ask for. A tutor can ask the questions that make a student's own reflection sharper: what did you try, what failed, what did you change, how do you know. A tutor can teach a skill the project needs, such as how to structure a report or how to reference a source. A tutor can read a draft the student has written and say where criterion C is thin. The student makes every change.

Practically, the Personal Project is also a project-management problem, and that is where a weekly session earns its place for a student in this emirate. Deadlines sit months apart, the journal is supposed to be kept continuously, and a commuting student with a full MYP 5 timetable will leave it until the last fortnight unless something external paces it. A standing weekly slot that reviews dated journal entries solves that without touching the content.

sections.heading: From MYP 5 into the Diploma, or sideways into IGCSE
paragraphs: Two routes lead out of MYP 5 for families here, and they need different preparation. The first is into the IB Diploma, which is the continuation the programme was designed for. The second, common in the northern emirates because post-16 IB provision is limited, is sideways into an IGCSE or A-Level stream at a school in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah. Students do both successfully. They fail to prepare for either in the same way.

The Diploma gap is mostly about examinations. MYP assessment is task-based and criterion-marked, with time to draft and redraft. The Diploma adds terminal papers sat under time pressure with mark schemes that reward precision and penalise vagueness. A student who has spent five years writing considered responses can be genuinely shocked by a six-mark question that wants three short points. The MYP 4 and 5 years are the right place to build timed-writing stamina, and the Internal Assessment half of the Diploma is where MYP habits pay off handsomely.

The IGCSE gap is the sharper one. IGCSE marking is by mark scheme rather than by best fit, command terms carry specific meanings, and method must be visible to earn method marks. A student moving from MYP 5 into Year 11 mid-cycle also arrives at a tier decision, Core or Extended, that was made for a cohort they were not part of. That is worth raising with the receiving school in writing before the entry deadline rather than discovering it on a statement of entry.

For either route, the useful preparatory work is narrow. Three timed pieces marked against an external standard tell you more than a term of general revision. If the move is to IGCSE, ask the new school for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for each subject, because those three facts decide which past papers are worth sitting at all.

sections.heading: An MYP week in Umm Al Quwain, after the bus
paragraphs: A twelve year old who leaves Al Salamah at 6.40am and gets home at 4.15pm has already done a long day before anyone opens a book. Where the session sits in the remaining hours decides what it produces. New or difficult work needs the first slot while attention holds. Practice of something half-learned can go later. Anything mechanical, such as writing up a journal entry or copying a results table properly, belongs last.

For MYP 1 to MYP 3 students the better purchase is usually two shorter sessions rather than one hour. Attention at that age does not hold for sixty minutes at the end of a commuting day, and two contacts a week keeps the gap between being taught something and practising it under three days. From MYP 4 onwards, with longer tasks and the Personal Project running, a single weekly hour makes more sense, with a longer weekend block when a deadline is close.

Ramadan reorganises the week completely. School days shorten, which frees the afternoon, and the evening rearranges around iftar. Sessions that move to a late-morning slot on a shortened day, or to a post-iftar hour, keep continuity through a month that otherwise interrupts everything. It needs booking a fortnight ahead, because every family in the Gulf wants the same post-iftar slots.

One more local point. Schools in different emirates publish different term dates and different unit deadlines, so two MYP students living on the same street in Al Riqqah can have assessment weeks a fortnight apart. A session plan that follows your child's own school calendar, rather than a generic UAE one, is the difference between arriving before a task is due and arriving after it has been marked.

process.title: Send the marked task, not the report
process.description: The school report gives four numbers. The marked task gives the reason. Send the most recent piece of work with the teacher's annotation and the task sheet, plus the task-specific clarification if the school issued one. That is enough to identify the criterion holding the grade before anybody is paid for an hour.

process.title: Free 45-minute trial, no card details
process.description: A tutor in that subject group works through the marked task with your child and writes you a short note: which criterion is lowest, what the next band requires, and how many sessions the gap realistically needs. Nothing is charged and no payment details are taken first. You are told who the tutor is beforehand.

process.title: Agree the shape to the child's age and bus
process.description: Two short sessions for a younger MYP student, a weekly hour from MYP 4, a longer weekend block when a project deadline is near. The slot is fixed in Gulf Standard Time and held, and the Ramadan rearrangement is agreed in advance rather than improvised in the first week of the month.

process.title: Build the evidence file week by week
process.description: Every session leaves something readable: an annotated draft, a redraft by the student, a new task marked against the criteria, a dated journal entry with comments beside it. After four weeks you can compare two markings of the same criterion and decide on evidence rather than impression.

process.title: Review at the reporting point and decide again
process.description: The school's next report is the decision point. Continuing, switching subject group, changing tutor and stopping are all offered. If no specialist is free in a niche subject at the only time your family can manage, we say so rather than filling the slot with a generalist.

whyPoints.title: The criteria are explained to you, not just to the student
whyPoints.description: You get the four criteria for your child's subject group in plain words, which one is holding the grade, and what the next band requires. A parent who has never taught sciences can still check whether criterion B has moved between two marked tasks, which is the only honest basis for deciding whether an hour a week is worth buying.

whyPoints.title: Marked work against the published criteria, every week
whyPoints.description: Sessions produce annotated drafts and criterion levels, not progress summaries. For a programme with no percentages this is the only readable evidence there is, and it is also what makes stopping a reasonable decision rather than a difficult conversation.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is drawn before the first session
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the skill, asks the questions and comments on work the student has written. A tutor does not write, redraft or substantially edit a Personal Project, a design folder, a process journal or any assessed task. The student signs the honesty declaration, so the boundary protects them.

whyPoints.title: Session shape set by the child's age and the commute
whyPoints.description: Two forty-minute sessions suit an MYP 2 student home at quarter past four far better than one hour at half past seven. We set the shape around the bus and the bedtime rather than selling a standard hour, and we will say when a weekend block is the better buy.

whyPoints.title: A subject-group specialist, not whoever is nearby
whyPoints.description: Within a twenty-minute drive of Al Salamah there may be nobody who teaches MYP design or language acquisition at the phase your child is in. Over a video link, the pool is everyone who teaches it. That is the practical argument for online delivery in the least populous emirate.

whyPoints.title: The plan follows your child's school calendar
whyPoints.description: Unit deadlines, assessment weeks and term dates differ between schools in Sharjah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah. Sessions are planned against your child's own school calendar, so support arrives before a task is submitted rather than after it has come back marked.

faqs.question: What do criteria A to D actually mean on my child's MYP report?
faqs.answer: They are four separate assessment strands, and they differ by subject group. In sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In mathematics they are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Each is awarded a level from 1 to 8. Knowing which letter is low tells you what to work on, because the remedies are completely different: criterion A usually means content, while a low final criterion usually means a reflective or evaluative move the student has never been taught.

faqs.question: Is an achievement level of 6 out of 8 the same as 75 per cent?
faqs.answer: No. The level is a band chosen by best fit against a published descriptor, not a mark out of eight. A teacher reads the work as a whole and decides which descriptor it most closely matches, so a piece containing one excellent paragraph can still sit in a lower band. Levels are not added up as marks either; the school combines the four criteria and applies published grade boundaries to produce a subject grade from 1 to 7. Treating a level as a percentage leads parents to conclusions the marking does not support.

faqs.question: Why has my child improved but the MYP grade has not changed?
faqs.answer: Usually because they have moved from the bottom of a band to the top of the same band. The descriptors are broad, so real progress can happen entirely inside one level and the report will not show it. This is the strongest argument for keeping marked tasks rather than relying on reports: the annotation shows movement the number hides. It also points to where the next gain is, which is normally the lowest criterion rather than the strongest one. Chasing a 7 higher is harder and worth less than taking a 3 to a 5.

faqs.question: What is a task-specific clarification and should I ask to see it?
faqs.answer: It is the version of the criteria your child's teacher wrote for that particular task, turning general descriptors into what this piece of work specifically required. Schools often print it on the task sheet and will usually provide it on request. It is the most useful single document in MYP assessment, because it tells you what the marking was actually measuring rather than what the subject guide says in general. A tutor working from the generic descriptors alone is guessing at the thing your child's teacher applied.

faqs.question: How is the MYP Personal Project marked, and is the product graded?
faqs.answer: The Personal Project is assessed on its own criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. The product itself is not marked directly, which surprises most families. What is assessed is the process: the goal and its justification, the success criteria the student set, evidence of the skills applied, and the quality of the final reflection, all evidenced through the process journal and the report. A well-made product with a thin journal scores poorly. A modest product documented honestly and reflected on properly can score very well.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Within a clear boundary, yes. A tutor can explain what each criterion asks for, teach a skill the project needs such as structuring a report or referencing properly, ask the questions that make a student's own reflection sharper, and read a draft the student has written and say where it is thin. A tutor must not write, redraft or substantially edit any part of it, suggest the reflection, or compose the success criteria. The student signs an academic-honesty declaration and a supervisor confirms it, so the consequence of crossing that line falls on your child.

faqs.question: What is MYP eAssessment and does my child have to sit it?
faqs.answer: In the final year of the programme, schools may enter candidates for on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP certificate. It is not universal: many schools complete MYP 5 without it, and the decision belongs to the school rather than the family. Ask your child's MYP coordinator directly whether the school offers it and in which subjects. If it does, the preparation is genuinely different from ordinary MYP coursework, because it introduces timed on-screen response for students who have spent five years drafting.

faqs.question: My child writes carefully but keeps scoring 3 on criterion B in sciences. Why?
faqs.answer: Criterion B is inquiring and designing, and careful writing is not what it rewards. It wants a hypothesis with scientific reasoning behind it, the independent, dependent and controlled variables identified, and a method precise enough for someone else to repeat. Most students who sit at 3 or 4 have written a sensible prediction with no science attached and listed variables without saying how any of them would be held constant. It is one of the fastest things to fix, because the content is usually already known and only the structure of the design is missing.

faqs.question: How is MYP mathematics different from the IGCSE maths my older child does?
faqs.answer: The content overlaps heavily; the assessment does not. IGCSE mathematics is marked against a mark scheme where method marks are awarded for visible working and answers need stated precision. MYP mathematics adds criterion B, investigating patterns, which asks the student to find a general rule, test it and justify it, and criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Neither of those appears on an IGCSE paper. A student strong at IGCSE-style questions can sit at 4 in MYP because nobody has taught them how to write an investigation.

faqs.question: What should the first four weeks of MYP sessions actually produce?
faqs.answer: Something readable each week. Week one, a written note naming the lowest criterion and what the next band requires. Week two, one section redrafted by the student with the tutor's annotation beside the original. Week three, a new task on a different unit marked the same way, which shows whether the move transferred. Week four, a comparison of the two markings and a revised target. If after four weeks there is nothing but a tutor's impression that things are going well, you have no basis for continuing and should ask for marked work.

faqs.question: How long does it take for an MYP criterion level to move?
faqs.answer: For criteria that reward a specific written move, such as evaluating or justifying, a level can move on the next assessed task once the student has been shown the move and practised it. For criteria that reward sustained independent work, such as a design folder or an arts process journal, change takes a term because it is a habit rather than a technique. Nobody can promise a grade. What a tutor can promise is that each marked task will show whether the level moved, which is a check you can apply yourself.

faqs.question: Does the MYP prepare a student for Diploma Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: For the Internal Assessment half of the Diploma, it prepares them well. Investigating, designing, processing data and reflecting are exactly what MYP criteria have been training for five years, and MYP students often handle their first Diploma investigation more confidently than students arriving from exam-only systems. The weaker half is examinations. The Diploma adds terminal papers under time pressure where precision is rewarded and length is not, and that is the gap worth working on during MYP 4 and 5 rather than discovering in the first Diploma mock.

faqs.question: We are moving from MYP 4 into an IGCSE stream in Sharjah. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Three things. Marking changes from best fit against descriptors to a mark scheme where method must be visible and command terms carry fixed meanings. Content changes, because IGCSE syllabuses examine a defined list that MYP units may have covered in a different order or not at all. And there is a tier decision, Core or Extended on many Cambridge subjects, which sets the highest grade available and was made for a cohort your child was not part of. Ask the receiving school in writing for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject.

faqs.question: Is a full hour too long for an MYP 2 student after the bus home?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. A student who left Al Salamah before seven and got home after four has limited concentration left, and an hour at five o'clock can produce less than forty minutes would. For MYP 1 to MYP 3 we usually suggest two shorter sessions a week instead: attention holds, and the gap between being taught something and practising it never grows past three days. From MYP 4 onwards, with longer tasks and the Personal Project running alongside, a single weekly hour makes more sense, with a longer weekend block before a deadline.

faqs.question: Do approaches to learning skills and service as action affect the subject grade?
faqs.answer: Approaches to learning skills are taught and reported on, and they shape the criteria indirectly because research, communication and self-management are what the investigative and reflective criteria actually measure. They are not a separate grade in themselves. Service as action is a programme requirement reported separately rather than a graded subject component. Ask your child's coordinator how the school reports both, because practice varies between schools in Ajman, Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah, and a parent comparing two reports from two schools is often comparing two reporting conventions.

umm-al-quwain/ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Bring the marked task and we will tell you which criterion is holding the grade
umm-al-quwain/ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: An MYP report gives you four numbers and no reasons. The marked task, the task sheet and the task-specific clarification give you all of them. Send those over and a tutor in that subject group will teach a free 45-minute trial with your child, identify the lowest criterion, and write you a short note saying what the next band requires and how many sessions the gap genuinely needs, including when the answer is none. Lessons run one to one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, in a slot built around the bus rather than around a standard hour.
